title: Exploring personal and contextual factors influencing pre-service English teachers' willingness to integrate AI into their future teaching practices
abstract: Despite the transformative potential that AI promises for English language teaching (ELT), there remains a paucity of inquiry into the readiness of pre-service English teachers (PSETs) to integrate AI into their future instructional practice, particularly within the Chinese educational context. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Social Cognitive Theory (SCT), this study examines the personal and contextual predictors shaping PSETs' willingness to integrate AI (WIAI) into their future ELT endeavours. A questionnaire was administered to 306 PSETs, investigating the interrelationships among perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEU) of AI, AI-specific technological pedagogical content knowledge (AI-TPACK), AI language technological knowledge (AIL-TK), AI technological pedagogical knowledge (AI-TPK), AI self-efficacy (AISE), peer support (PS), and university support and resources (USAR) in relation to PSETs' WIAI. Structural equation modelling analysis substantiated 15 of the 21 hypothesised relationships. The complex interrelations were mapped to offer stakeholders with a theoretically grounded framework for supporting PSETs' WIAI in Chinese and other similar educational contexts.

title: When customers cross the line: how anger and emotional intelligence shape service sabotage
abstract: Purpose Frontline service employees are increasingly exposed to customer aggression, yet existing research continues to portray emotional intelligence (EI) as an inherently protective personal resource against destructive employee responses. This assumption remains theoretically incomplete, as high EI does not necessarily preclude employees from engaging in service sabotage. Drawing on Frustration–Aggression Theory (FAT) and Affective Events Theory (AET), this study aims to examine employee anger as the emotional mechanism linking customer aggression to service sabotage, while investigating whether EI consistently functions as a protective resource. Design/methodology/approach Multisource data were collected from 267 employees and 25 supervisors working in 25 five-star hotels in Vietnam. Employees provided information on customer aggression, anger and EI, while supervisors assessed employees’ service sabotage. To reduce potential bias, social desirability was controlled for in both employee and supervisor responses. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4.1.1.8. Findings Customer aggression increased employee anger, which, in turn, promoted service sabotage. More importantly, the findings challenge the dominant “EI-as-panacea” perspective. Instead, EI may function as a double-edged resource: although it weakens both th…

title: Faktor-Faktor Yang Berhubungan dengan Kinerja Tenaga Kesehatan dalam Pelaksanaan Standar Pelayanan di Puskesmas Rantau Durian
abstract: Pendahuluan: Kinerja tenaga kesehatan merupakan salah satu komponen penting dalam menjamin terlaksananya standar pelayanan dan mutu pelayanan di Puskesmas sebagai fasilitas kesehatan tingkat pertama. Kinerja dapat berkaitan dengan karakteristik individu maupun faktor organisasi, seperti pengetahuan, motivasi, kepemimpinan, supervisi/pengawasan, dan beban kerja. Tujuan: Menganalisis hubungan faktor individual dan organisasi dengan kinerja tenaga kesehatan dalam pelaksanaan standar pelayanan di Puskesmas Rantau Durian, Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ilir, tahun 2026. Metode: Penelitian kuantitatif analitik dengan desain cross-sectional melibatkan 56 tenaga kesehatan yang memenuhi kriteria penelitian. Pengambilan responden dilakukan menggunakan total sampling. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner terstruktur yang mencakup karakteristik responden, pengetahuan, motivasi kerja, kepemimpinan, supervisi/pengawasan, beban kerja, dan kinerja. Analisis dilakukan secara univariat dan bivariat menggunakan uji Chi-Square pada α=0,05. Hasil: Mayoritas responden berusia 20–35 tahun (75,0%), perempuan (76,8%), berpendidikan D3 (67,9%), berprofesi sebagai bidan (58,9%), dan memiliki masa kerja <5 tahun (39,3%). Pengetahuan baik sebesar 75,0%, motivasi 87,5%, kepemimpinan 75,0%, supervisi/pengawasan 87,5%, dan beban kerja kategori baik 75,0%. Kinerja baik ditemukan pada 40 responden (71,4%). Tidak terdapat …

title: الثقافة التنظيمية وأثرها في تحسين جودة خدمات الرعاية الصحية (من وجهة نظر مقدمي الخدمة الصحية بمركز علاج وغسيل الكلى الرئيسي ببلدية بمصراتة)
abstract: هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى تحديد أثر الثقافة التنظيمية على جودة الخدمات الصحية من وجهة نظر مقدمي الخدمة الصحية بمركز علاج وغسيل الكلى الرئيسي ببلدية بمصراتة، اعتمد الباحث على المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، مستخدماً استمارة استبانة أعدت كأداة لجمع وتحليل البيانات لمجتمع الدراسة البالغ عددهم (70) مفردة، وكانت عدد الاستبانات الصالحة للتحليل (63) مفردة. وتم تحليل بيانات الدراسة واختبار فرضياتها من خلال تطبيق بعض أدوات التحليل الإحصائي الوصفي التحليلي الأكثر ملاءمة لطبيعة تلك البيانات، ولتحليل البيانات التي تم جمعها من مجتمع الدراسة ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة؛ تمت الاستعانة بالحاسب الآلي واستخدام برنامج الحزمة الإحصائية للعلوم الاجتماعية والمعروف اختصارا (SPSS). حيث استخدام الباحث الاختبارات الإحصائية المناسبة التي تتلائم مع طبيعة الدراسة بناءً على تحليل البيانات الكمية للدراسة، كما تم استخدام معامل الانحدار لقياس أثر الثقافة التنظيمية على جودة الخدمات الصحية بمركز علاج وغسيل الكلى الرئيسي ببلدية بمصراتة قيد الدراسة. فقد خلُصت هذه الدراسة إلى مجموعة من النتائج أهمها ما يلي: 1. يوجد أثر إيجابي للثقافة التنظيمية على جودة الخدمات الصحية لدى مقدمي الخدمة الصحية بمركز علاج وغسيل الكلى الرئيسي ببلدية بمصراتة قيد الدراسة. 2. وجود علاقة طردية بین الثقافة التنظيمية وجودة الخدمات الصحية، أي أنه كلما زادت الثقافة التنظيمية زادت جودة الخدمات الصحية بمركز علاج وغسيل الكلى الرئيسي ببلدية بمصراتة الدراسة. 3. شعور أفراد مجتمع الدراسة بوجود ثقافة تنظيمية في المراكز ووحدات غسيل الكلى قيد الدراسة من خلال مصادر الثقافة …

title: Understanding sustainable mobility services: a customer-dominant logic perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to advance sustainability-oriented service research by examining how customers make sense of sustainability and integrate sustainable mobility services into their everyday use. Applying customer-dominant logic, it examines why sustainability matters to customers, how they pursue sustainability-related goals through everyday practices, with whom these efforts are coordinated across social and service actors, and when sustainable practices are enacted and embedded over time. Design/methodology/approach Using a sequential mixed-methods design, we first conducted in-depth interviews with customers of a German mobility provider (n = 20). Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using interpretive thematic analysis. Open coding generated first-order concepts, which were iteratively clustered into second-order themes. A subsequent hermeneutic interpretation revealed latent factors capturing how customers integrate sustainable mobility services within their personal ecosystems, identified interrelationships among these factors, and developed measurement scales for these factors. The research model was tested using an online survey (n = 278) and structural equation modeling. Findings The findings show that the integration of sustainable mobility services within customers' ecosystems is driven by the perceived intra- and interconnectivity of the provider's mobilit…

title: Ready on Paper? Functionality of Disaster Preparedness Strategies for Service Continuity at Julius Nyerere International Airport, Tanzania
abstract: Abstract Purpose: This study assessed the functionality of existing disaster preparedness strategies, namely early warning systems and resource preparedness, for maintaining service continuity at Julius Nyerere International Airport (JNIA), Tanzania’s busiest aviation hub. Design/methodology/approach: A mixed-methods, cross-sectional descriptive design guided by High Reliability Theory, the Resource-Based View and Crisis Management Theory was used. Questionnaires were completed by 187 respondents, including Tanzania Airports Authority managers, air traffic controllers, security, fire and rescue and operational staff and frequent passengers, and 14 key informants were interviewed. Incident reports, safety committee minutes and policy documents were reviewed. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. Findings: Early warning systems were moderately effective (M = 3.39): radar and communication redundancy (M = 3.46) and scheduled testing (M = 3.44) were rated high, but simultaneous alert dissemination (M = 3.35), failure logging (M = 3.35) and backup communication (M = 3.32) lagged. Resource preparedness was the weakest construct (M = 3.06), with dedicated and consistently disbursed budget lines rated lowest of all items (M = 2.99). Interviews revealed postponed testing, fragile backup communications, deferred maintenance and recurring causes of inciden…

title: Quantitative analysis of urban underground drainage pipeline service status under rainstorm disaster
abstract: Abstract Underground drainage pipeline (UDP) system is critical infrastructure for urban flood control and drainage. During extreme rainstorms, rainfall infiltration can alter pore-water pressure and soil-pipe interaction in the surrounding soil. These changes may affect the structural safety of buried pipelines under traffic load. To investigate the structural responses of buried pipelines during extreme rainstorms and provide a basis for emergency assessment, this study integrates full-scale mechanical test, finite element simulation, historical rainstorm scenarios, and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) data agent model. Firstly, full-scale pipeline mechanical tests are conducted, and test results are used to calibrate material parameters in numerical simulations; on this basis, a pavement-pipeline coupled numerical model is established to evaluate UDP structural responses under normal service state. Secondly, based on time-series rainfall data from historical rainstorm disaster in Beijing, China, 20 numerical working conditions are established to investigate the effects of pipe voids, burial depth, subgrade soil permeability, and pipeline diameter on structural responses under the coupled action of rainstorm and vehicle load. Finally, a dataset containing 2370 samples is used to develop the 1D-CNN model; this model achieves an MSE of 0.0003 and an R² of…

title: Determinants of Cayenne Pepper Production, Farm Income, and Extension Service Effectiveness in Mimika Regency
abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes production factors, farmer income, and the effect of agricultural extension services on cayenne pepper cultivation in Muare Village, Mimika Regency, where local production potential remains constrained by dependence on external supplies. Research Methodology: A census method was applied to 48 cayenne pepper farmers in Muare Village. Three analytical approaches were used, including Cobb–Douglas production function with robust standard errors, farm income analysis (TR−TC), and simple linear regression to assess agricultural extension effects on farmer interest. Classical assumption tests included normality and multicollinearity assessments. Results: The Cobb–Douglas model was significant (F=20.11; p=0.000; R²=0.6569). Seeds (β=1.1927; p=0.037) and capital (β=2.0968; p=0.004) positively affected production, while fertilizer showed a negative significant effect (β=−0.8136; p=0.025). Other production factors were insignificant. The Return to Scale value of 3.50 indicated increasing returns. Farmers achieved average revenue of IDR 103 million, costs of IDR 41.1 million, and net income of IDR 63.5 million per season. Agricultural extension services significantly influenced farmer interest (β=1.0191; p=0.000; R²=0.8233). Conclusions: Cayenne pepper farming is economically viable and can be expanded through optimized input management and strengthened extensi…

title: Reassessing the workplace incivility scale in restaurant service encounters
abstract: Purpose This study provides a context-specific psychometric examination of a Chinese-translated and customer-adapted workplace incivility scale used to assess customer-to-employee incivility in restaurant service encounters. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative field survey was conducted with 873 frontline restaurant employees in Zhuhai, China. The original English-language measures were translated into Chinese using translation and back-translation procedures. The analyses included the general partial credit model within an item response theory framework, confirmatory factor analysis, internal-consistency reliability analysis, local-independence diagnostics and preliminary criterion-related testing using matched customer-satisfaction indicators. Findings In the present sample, the seven response categories showed poor differentiation and unusually high inter item correlations. After category consolidation and item reduction, the candidate four-item version with four categories showed clearer category functioning, better model fit, no substantial local dependence and a stronger but still modest negative association with customer satisfaction. These findings are context specific and do not establish a universally superior WIS. Research limitations/implications The findings show that scale properties may change after translation and contextual adaptation. Independent replic…

title: Optimized Cloud Service Ranking through PCA-based Dimensionality Reduction and BOM Weight Synthesis
abstract: Selecting a cloud service from many competing providers is a multi-criteria decision problem in which the Quality of Service (QoS) criteria are often strongly correlated. Methods such as AHP, BWM and TOPSIS treat these criteria as independent and need many pairwise comparisons. An earlier study by the authors combined Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with a two-level Best-Only Method (BOM), in which an expert also compared every provider under every criterion, at a cost of 95 judgements for eight criteria and twelve providers. The present paper keeps the PCA stage, the BOM weighting of the criteria and the variance-weighted utility of that study, and removes the provider-level elicitation. BOM weights are applied directly to the standardised QoS data, so only n − 1 judgements are needed (7 instead of 95) and the effort no longer grows with the number of providers. The two versions are compared on the same twelve QWS services and under the same two preference profiles. Under the reliability-focused profile of the earlier study, both select the same three leading services, and their rankings are significantly correlated (Spearman's ρ = 0.80); under the response-time profile, the agreement is weaker (ρ = 0.56). In all four common-basis sensitivity settings, the single-level version is the more stable (mean ρ 0.93–0.98 against 0.82–0.94). Its ranking also agrees with PCA-BWM (ρ =…

title: Cyclic-frequency-constrained time–frequency masking for fault feature extraction and diagnosis in rotating machinery
abstract: Abstract Accurate fault feature extraction is essential for analyzing rotating machinery measurement signals, especially when fault signatures are masked by strong noise and multi-source interference. In practical measurement scenarios, different bearing faults may excite adjacent resonance bands, while isolated impulsive disturbances may occur in the same carrier-frequency band as the target fault. These effects make it difficult for time–frequency methods to distinguish fault-related impulses from non-target components. To improve the selectivity of periodic transient extraction, this paper proposes a cyclic-frequency-constrained time–frequency masking (CFC-TFM) method. The cyclic modulation spectrum is first used to identify the target fault cyclic frequency and its associated carrier-frequency band. A cyclic modulation frequency mask (CMFM) is then constructed to constrain the resonance band, and a cycle-consistent time gate (CCTG) is developed to retain impulse instants consistent with the target fault periodicity. The CMFM and CCTG are then combined to form the final CFC-TFM. This combined mask selectively enhances fault-related impulsive features while suppressing same-band isolated interference and adjacent fault components. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that CFC-TFM produces clearer periodic impulse sequences and more distinct fault characteristic fre…

Beyond affective coping and use frequency: academic rumination, generative AI dependency, and two dimensions of perceived cognitive debt
abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support learning and emotion regulation, yet frequent or coping-oriented use does not necessarily constitute difficult-to-regulate dependency. It remains unclear how academic rumination and affective coping are positioned relative to dependency and whether dependency is differentially associated with perceived costs to knowledge internalization and independent reasoning. This study examined these distinctions within a single educational psychology model. Methods A cross-sectional survey included 611 current GenAI users recruited through university settings in Tianjin, China (91.7% first-year students). Dependency was a continuous, nonclinical tendency. Ordinal CFA and WLSMV SEM evaluated a prespecified partial association model. Covariate adjustment, four alternative measurement specifications, an AR-score hybrid, and observed-score regressions assessed sensitivity. Results In the reference model, academic rumination was associated with affective coping (β = 0.283), and both were associated with dependency (β = 0.187 and 0.555). Dependency was associated with perceived internalization/memory debt (β = 0.550) and independent-reasoning debt (β = 0.644); their standardized difference was 0.095 (95% Monte Carlo CI [0.032, 0.157]). The corresponding observed-score coefficients were 0.413 and 0.518, with a difference of 0.105 …

title: Professional Standards and Self-Regulation in Coaching and Consulting Associations
abstract: Coaching and consulting form a large international field of practice, with an estimated 122,974 coach practitioners worldwide in 2025. In the six jurisdictions covered by a recent sector review, no statute was identified that reserves the title of coach or licenses the practice of coaching. Professional associations therefore carry much of the responsibility for defining competence, ethical conduct and client protection. This conceptual paper asks how associations can establish credible standards, ethical accountability and quality assurance when statutory regulation is limited or fragmented. Drawing on a structured review of association standards, sector reports and the literature on professions, information asymmetry and industry self-regulation, it distinguishes statutory licensing, individual credentialing, programme accreditation and association self-regulation, and examines ethics codes, competence and continuing development requirements, complaints and disciplinary procedures, and conflicts of interest. In the sources reviewed, standards are more developed for declared inputs than for verifiable outputs, and voluntary self-regulation is exposed to commercial interests, certification without effective control and limited independence. As its original contribution, the paper proposes the Credibility of Professional Self-Regulation (CPSR) framework, which assesses an associ…

title: AI governance as co-regulation: a practitioner-informed framework for defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how practitioners supporting defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) place artificial intelligence (AI) governance within the coregulatory regime of National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-171, the cybersecurity maturity model certification program, contracts and assessors. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory survey of 38 practitioners, recruited through a public LinkedIn post, combined a risk-to-control-family mapping task, artifact feasibility ratings and open-ended responses. Analysis was descriptive, with exploratory correlations adjusted for multiplicity and one researcher coded the open text. Findings Respondents concentrated AI risk on a few evidence-bearing control families, led by audit and accountability, risk assessment, access control and system and information integrity. Perceived compliance strain was high and readiness low. Artifacts resembling existing evidence, such as audit trail exports, were rated most feasible. Guidance ambiguity was the leading barrier. No exploratory association survived adjustment for multiplicity. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample and self-reported perceptions support pattern identification, not population estimates or claims about implementation outcomes. Practical implications Assessors and prime contractors could reduce SME …

title: Acceptability and preferred frequency of syphilis-focused SMS reminders for syphilis testing among men who have sex with men in Melbourne, Australia
abstract: Background Regular screening is important for syphilis control. We assessed acceptance of syphilis-focused SMS reminders for syphilis testing and preferred reminder frequency among men who have sex with men (MSM) attending a sexual health clinic in Australia. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of MSM attending the Melbourne Sexual Health Centre, Australia, between April 2024 and August 2025. Clients were presented with a proposed message describing syphilis epidemic among MSM, modes of transmission and asymptomatic infection, and then asked whether they would accept an SMS reminder for syphilis testing and their preferred reminder frequency (3-, 6-, or 12-monthly). Logistic and multinomial logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with reminder acceptance and preferred reminder frequency. Results Among 6752 MSM, 56.4% (n = 3805) accepted SMS reminders. Overseas-born (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.07, 95% CI: 1.81–2.36) and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander MSM (aOR 1.88, 95% CI: 1.10–3.22) were more likely to accept reminders, whereas PrEP users were less likely (aOR 0.74, 95% CI: 0.63–0.86). Among those who accepted reminders, 81.9% preferred reminders every 3 months, 16.1% every 6 months and 1.5% every 12 months. Older MSM were more likely to prefer less frequent reminders, whereas overseas-born MSM and PrEP users were more likely to pr…

title: Emerging roles of circular RNAs in bovine mastitis and mammary immune regulation: mechanisms, networks and translational potential
CHALLENGES AND PROSPECTS OF THE LEGAL REGULATION OF REAL-WORLD ASSET TOKENIZATION IN RUSSIAN LAW
abstract: The article examines the challenges and prospects of the legal regulation of the tokenization of real-world assets under the Russian jurisdiction. It analyzes the possibilities of tokenization through digital rights in light of the ongoing digital assets market reform and the Concept for the Tokenization of Real Sector Assets of the Russian Economy. The study concludes that these transformations remove a number of barriers but contain critical contradictions. It identifies challenges including the duplication of the intermediary-based securities market model, the conflict between the reform and the Concept, and the unsuitability of digital rights for tokenizing absolute rights.

title: Ccf-net: weakly supervised camouflaged object detection via consistency prior and frequency-domain enhancement
Prior-guided dual stream time–frequency meta learning network for few-shot cross-domain fault diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Drastic fluctuations in fault feature distributions under large-span variable speeds, compounded by target domain label scarcity, severely degrade the generalization performance of diagnostic models. To address these challenges, a prior-guided time–frequency dual-stream meta-learning network (PR-TFML) is proposed in this paper. By leveraging the deeply decoupled synergy between mechanistic knowledge and data-driven learning, PR-TFML constructs a multimodal feature extraction architecture composed of complementary time-domain and time–frequency branches. The time-domain branch employs large-receptive-field convolutions to capture nonstationary transient impact characteristics, while the time–frequency branch extracts high-dimensional evolutionary features through an embedded short-time Fourier transform layer. Building upon this, a physical prior mapping branch is introduced to construct a compact hybrid prior by combining macroscopic operating conditions (e.g. rotational speed) with intrinsic statistical and energy-based descriptors (e.g. kurtosis, envelope energy, and wavelet energy). This prior is transformed into domain-invariant semantic anchors, enabling adaptive calibration against distribution shifts. Furthermore, guided by physical priors, an explicit alignment-enhanced meta-optimization strategy couples Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning with Correlation Alignment c…

title: Penerapan Senam Kegel untuk Menurunkan Frekuensi Berkemih pada Ibu Hamil Trimester III dengan Inkontinensia Urin
abstract: Pendahuluan: Inkontinensia urin merupakan salah satu keluhan yang dapat dialami ibu hamil trimester III akibat pembesaran uterus yang memberi tekanan pada kandung kemih dan perubahan fungsi otot dasar panggul, sehingga kondisi ini dapat meningkatkan frekuensi berkemih, mengganggu kenyamanan serta gangguan aktivitas sehari hari. Salah satu upaya nonfarmakologis yang dapat dilakukan untuk mengatasi keluhan tersebut adalah dengan senam Kegel, yaitu latihan yang bertujuan untuk memperkuat otot dasar panggul sehingga membantu meningkatkan control berkemih. Tujuan: Mendeskripsikan penerapan senam Kegel terhadap penurunan frekuensi berkemih pada ibu hamil trimester III dengan inkontinensia urin di wilayah kerja Puskesmas Telaga Dewa Kota Bengkulu tahun 2026. Metode: Penelitian deskriptif dengan pendekatan studi kasus pada dua ibu hamil trimester III yang mengalami inkontinensia urin. Senam Kegel dilakukan dua kali sehari selama tujuh hari. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara, observasi, pemeriksaan fisik, dan kuesioner International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-SF), kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil: Setelah intervensi, frekuensi berkemih menurun pada kedua partisipan. Ny. S mengalami penurunan dari 12 menjadi 8 kali pada siang hari dan dari 4 menjadi 1 kali pada malam hari, sedangkan Ny. title: Legal Regulation of the Principles of Bioethics and Biolaw in the Republic of South Africa
abstract: The article consideres reconstruction of the stages of formation of legal regulation of biolaw and bioethics in the Republic of South Africa over the past forty years, characterization of the current system and determination of its development prospects. Regulation has evolved from fragmented apartheid-era legislation and discriminatory voluntary guidelines to a constitutionally grounded statutory system (section 12(2)(c) of the 1996 Constitution, National Health Act of 2003); decisions of research ethics committees are binding in the administrativeregulatory sense yet subordinate to legislation and judicial review; the current stage constitutes a reflexive restructuring with a reform agenda concerning minors’ consent, heritable genome editing, end-of-life decisions and artificial intelligence.

title: Genome-wide identification of the GRAS transcription factor family and regulation of metabolites under drought and salt stress in Isatis indigotica
abstract: Introduction Isatis indigotica is a traditional medicinal and food homology plant in China, and its cultivation is frequently limited by drought and salt stress. The GRAS transcription factor family plays a critical role in plant development and stress adaptation. However, its regulatory network in medicinal plants remains largely uncharacterized. Methods In this study, we performed a genome-wide analysis to identify IiGRAS genes in I. indigotica , followed by phylogenetic and synteny analyses, promoter cis-element analysis, and integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. Results We identified 39 IiGRAS genes in I. indigotica . Phylogenetic and synteny analyses indicated that the gene family expanded via tandem and segmental duplications, and all duplicated gene pairs were subject to strong purifying selection (Ka/Ks < 1), suggesting functional conservation. Promoter analysis identified stress-responsive cis-elements linked to abscisic acid, jasmonic acid, and drought signaling. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that IiSCL genes are co-expressed with AP2 , bZIP , WRKY , and HLH transcription factors and are correlated with metabolites implicated in osmotic balance, membrane stability, and oxidative defense. Discussion These findings establish a molecular framework for SCL-mediated stress regulation in I. indigotica and highlight potential ca…

title: A buffer-capacity-constrained integrated scheduling model for automated container terminals
abstract: Purpose This study investigates an integrated scheduling problem in automated container terminals (ACTs) for export loading, jointly coordinating quay cranes (QCs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and automated stacking cranes (ASCs). It explicitly models two practical buffering resources: limited-capacity block buffer zones at yard blocks and quay-side buffer lanes/buffer locations for AGV queuing. The objective is to minimize total QC idle (waiting) time while satisfying realistic constraints, including equipment non-blocking, handover time windows, predetermined QC loading sequences, exclusive buffer-location occupancy, buffer-location assignment, and the rule that each AGV may park on buffer lanes at most once per job transport. Design/methodology/approach A comprehensive mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) (M1) is formulated to capture ASC retrieval, AGV transport with buffer-lane parking, buffer-location assignment, and QC loading interactions under finite buffer capacities. An equivalent reformulation (M2) replaces the max-type QC idle objective with a QC waiting-time-based objective to improve computational efficiency. Given NP-hardness, an improved genetic algorithm (GA) is developed with long- and short-chromosome (SC) random-key encodings and a model-based evaluation method (MEM) that enforces feasibility via time-window calculations and resource exclusivity ch…

title: Towards high-capacity and robust free-space optical communications
Economic capacity of territorial communities and its restoration in the post-war period
abstract: The full-scale war has increased the financial, infrastructural and energy vulnerability of territorial communities of Ukraine, making the issue of their ability to maintain economic activity and form the resource base for future recovery more urgent. The combination of fiscal sustainability, investment opportunities and energy security is of particular importance. The purpose of the study is to determine the financial, economic, investment and energy factors of the economic capacity of territorial communities of Ukraine; the object is the process of forming the prerequisites for their post-war recovery. The methodology is based on a comparative documentary and statistical analysis of data for 2021, 2023–2025 for a matched sample of 1,314 communities using descriptive statistics, the Wilcoxon test, Spearman correlation and documentary analysis. Non-linear dynamics of financial capacity have been established: subsidy, transfer dependence, local taxes and capital expenditures changed along different time trajectories. In all annual sections, a negative relationship was found between transfer dependence and the share of capital expenditures, most pronounced in 2023. The share of local taxes and fees had a weaker relationship with development expenditures, which limits its use as an independent criterion of economic capacity. Documentary analysis allowed us to single out fiscal cap…

title: A PSO-Optimized Non-Linear Channel Capacity Enhancement Framework for CSI-based and MIMO Wireless Communications
abstract: Optimization of channel capacity in Channel State Information (CSI)-assisted Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems is a critical need for beyond 5G and future 6G wireless communication systems, in which non-linear propagation and time-varying fading channels significantly affect the channel capacity. Traditional approaches based on linear channel models and complex optimization algorithms often face challenges in terms of robustness, Scalability, and global optimality. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-optimized non-linear channel capacity enhancement scheme by incorporating Monte Carlo-based stochastic channel modeling, polynomial analysis of Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-capacity trends using K-fold cross-validation, and evolutionary optimization. Simulations performed in a realistic fading channel environment strongly validate the existence of a strong non-linear SNR-capacity trend and statistical channel stability. The baseline Monte Carlo simulation model establishes a channel capacity prediction of approximately 1.3×108 bps when operating at an SNR value of 20 dB. The PSO-optimized approach results in a channel capacity increase to 3.79 × 10⁸ bps, representing an approximately 2.91-fold increase over the baseline system. The proposed scheme demonstrates superior performance through simulation tests against Single …

title: Predictive Model for Ammonia Absorption Capacity of Deep Eutectic Solvents Using Rough Set Theory
abstract: Abstract The direct emission of ammonia (NH 3 ) into the atmosphere from process waste gas streams brings environmental and health risks. This can be mitigated through absorption using solvents. Deep eutectic solvents (DES) were introduced as green absorption solvents with advantages including wide liquid range, high thermal stability and simple synthesis. Experimental studies indicate that NH₃ absorption capacity improves with acidic DES, higher hydrogen bond donor (HBD) to hydrogen bond acceptor (HBA) ratio, controlled water content, lower temperature and higher pressure. However, the exhaustive number of possible DES combinations formed by varying HBAs, HBDs, molar ratio and water content, makes it difficult to evaluate each combination experimentally. This combinatorial complexity together with the influence of process conditions, makes determining the optimal ranges of these variables through trial-and-error experiments resource-intensive and time-consuming. While predictive modelling offers a solution, most existing models are black-box approaches that lack interpretability, providing limited insights into how each variable affects NH 3 absorption performance. This limits their application in guiding solvent and process design. Therefore, this work developed an interpretable predictive model for NH 3 absorption in DES using rough set machine learning (RSML). RSML applies …

title: Digital, AI-enabled marketing and the competitiveness of trade services: a sociological perspective on labor transformation, social inclusion and organizational capacity
abstract: Research on digital and AI-enabled marketing explains how channels, data, and algorithms create value for firms, while the sociology of digital labor explains how the same technologies reorganize work and access. Neither explains why trade-service firms adopting near-identical tools reach very different competitive outcomes, a question that matters most for small firms in emerging and transition economies. This conceptual Perspective proposes a model of socially mediated competitiveness in which the adoption of digital and AI-enabled marketing, treated as one continuum from basic digital channels to generative-AI content, customer response, and targeting, affects competitiveness through three mechanisms. Labor transformation reallocates marketing tasks between automation and human judgment, strengthening competitiveness where workers can direct AI tools and weakening it where work depends on platform and algorithmic control. Social inclusion, through access, skills, and autonomy of use, decides how many firms and which social groups can contest a digitally mediated market. Organizational capacity, through routines for sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring human-machine practices, decides whether adoption becomes durable advantage. The theoretical novelty is threefold: the model joins mechanisms usually studied apart, treats job quality and inclusion as conditions of competitivene…

title: Pengaruh Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) Terhadap Kapasitas Paru Pada Pasien Multi Drug Resistance Tuberculosis (MDR-TB)
abstract: Pendahuluan: Multi Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) merupakan penyakit menular yang dapat menyebabkan kerusakan jaringan paru sehingga berdampak pada penurunan kapasitas paru. Kondisi ini dapat diperberat oleh ketegangan otot pernapasan dan gangguan psikologis pasien. Selain terapi farmakologis, diperlukan terapi non-farmakologis sebagai pendukung, salah satunya Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) yang bertujuan meningkatkan relaksasi otot pernapasan dan memperbaiki kapasitas paru. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh PMR terhadap kapasitas paru pada pasien MDR-TB di Poli MDR-TB Rumah Sakit Ibnu Sina. Metode: Penelitian ini menggunakan desain pre-eksperimental dengan pendekatan one group pretest-posttest. Populasi penelitian berjumlah 74 pasien. Sampel berjumlah 20 pasien MDR-TB yang dipilih menggunakan teknik accidental sampling. Intervensi PMR diberikan 2x seminggu selama satu bulan dengan durasi 20 menit setiap sesi. Pengukuran kapasitas paru dilakukan menggunakan spirometri. Analisis data menggunakan uji Mc Nemar. Hasil: Hasil penelitian Sebelum intervensi, sebagian besar pasien memiliki kapasitas paru tidak normal 15 (75%). Setelah intervensi, sebagian besar pasien memiliki kapasitas paru normal 14 (70%). title: Mechanism and Kinetics of Nucleation and Growth in Amine Aerosols for Post-Combustion Carbon Capture
abstract: Abstract As the major component of organic amine emission, amine aerosol can generate the substantial secondary pollutants, posing serious environmental impacts and hindering the large-scale deployment of absorption carbon capture. The existing studies have proposed several end-of-pipe strategies to achieve 99% removal within a reasonable cost range while it is still challenging. It is necessary to elucidate the nucleation and growth mechanisms of amine aerosols. Herein we investigate the mechanism and kinetics of amine nucleation and growth by molecular dynamics simulation, quantum chemistry calculation, and experiment. Molecular dynamics simulation results show that the aerosol nucleation process follows a typical growth pathway characterized by mutual attraction, collision-coalescence, and nucleation. The results show that, compared with the nucleation process without chemical reactions, the reaction energy barrier of the rate-determining step in the nucleation process involving chemical reactions is reduced by 16.56 kJ/mol, reaching 11.55 kJ/mol. The reaction rate of the rate-determining step is 1.214 × 10–9 s–1, which is 3 orders of magnitude higher than that of the nonreactive reaction. This finding is further verified by structural characterization using FTIR experiments. It is expected to provide further mechanistic insights into the removal of amine aerosols.

title: Defense of the Defendant in Civil Proceedings: Issues Regarding the Application of the Counterclaim Mechanism Institution
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the problems related to legal regulation and practical implementation of the counterclaim institution in Russian civil proceedings. The author examines existing discrepancies between formally established legal norms that provide defendants with the opportunity to file a counterclaim and actual conditions under which this norm is implemented in practice. Special attention is given to key issues associated with determining deadlines for filing counterclaims, establishing criteria for their acceptance by judicial bodies, as well as negative phenomena arising from improper use of this procedural right by certain participants in litigation processes. Modern trends in court practice are analyzed, characterized by insufficient consideration of these factors, making it difficult to effectively utilize the counterclaim as an effective means of protecting the defendant’s interests. Based on the analysis results, specific amendments and additions to current legislation are proposed aimed at overcoming existing legal uncertainty and achieving optimal balance of interests among parties involved in civil proceedings.

title: Suspension of Disposal of Digital Currency in Criminal Proceedings: The Procedural Mechanism and Judicial Practice
abstract: The article, drawing on Russian judicial practice and the doctrine of criminal procedure, examines the suspension of disposal of digital currency as a form of seizure of property. The analysis highlights the specific features of digital currency as an object of seizure and confiscation and explores the relationship between Articles 111 and 115 of the Criminal Procedure Code of the Russian Federation and special legislation on digital assets with law-enforcement decisions in cases involving illicit drug trafficking and the laundering of criminal proceeds. The article further examines the significance of Federal Law No. 38-FZ of February 20, 2026, which recognized digital currency as property for the purposes of criminal law and established special rules for its seizure (Parts 7.1–7.2 of Article 115 of the Criminal Procedure Code of the Russian Federation) and the procedure for its seizure during investigative actions (Article 164.2 of the Criminal Procedure Code of the Russian Federation). The paper describes models of digital currency flows in criminal cases, the procedural steps taken by investigators and courts when preparing and considering motions for seizure, as well as the set of technical actions and practical guidelines for cooperation between investigative authorities, courts, Rosfinmonitoring, credit institutions and operators of exchange services.

title: ReaxFF Molecular Dynamics Simulation Study on the Microscopic Mechanism of the Synergistic Effect of an Oscillating Electric Field and SiO2 Catalyst on Oil Shale Pyrolysis
abstract: Abstract The synergistic effect of microwave catalysts can significantly enhance the pyrolysis efficiency and product selectivity of kerogen, but the microscopic mechanisms at the molecular scale have yet to be elucidated. In this study, reactive force field molecular dynamics (ReaxFF-MD) simulations are employed to elucidate the synergistic effect of an oscillating electric field (OEF) and SiO2 catalyst on oil shale pyrolysis. Nonisothermal simulations show that the synergistic condition reduces the initial decomposition temperature from 1700 to 1150 K and the activation energy from 140.8 to 25.1 kJ/mol. Isothermal simulations further confirm that the synergistic condition significantly enhances light oil yield, exceeding the arithmetic sum of the individual OEF and catalytic conditions. Mechanistically, the OEF induces dipole orientation polarization of polar functional groups (e.g., hydroxyl, carboxyl, carbonyl, and ether bridges), generating intramolecular stress that weakens chemical bonds and enhances atomic mobility (diffusion coefficient (D) increased from 0.233 to 0.453 Å2/ps). SiO2 exhibits selective cleavage of C–O bonds. The synergistic mechanism originates from mutual promotion: the enhanced molecular motion induced by the OEF strengthens the interaction between kerogen and SiO2, accelerating bond cleavage. The polar intermediates generated subsequently undergo fur…

title: Transformation of the Legal Mechanism for Managing Digital Risks in the Context of Countering External Economic Threats
abstract: The restructuring of economic relations, driven by the transformation of data into a key production resource, requires a revision of established approaches to risk management. The article examines managerial and legal relations arising in the course of transforming digital risk management mechanisms under the influence of external economic threats. The methodological basis of the study comprises formal legal analysis, systems analysis, the comparative legal method, and legal modeling. As a result of the study, a conceptual model has been developed for integrating the risk management system into data processing processes; key determinants of the transformation have been identified, including a paradigm shift regarding the object of risk, the external economic determinant, and the juridification of technological procedures. The author substantiates the conclusion that the effectiveness of countering external economic threats in the digital sphere depends on a transition from fragmented regulation to the creation of a holistic digital risk management ecosystem embedded in the management decision-making loop.

title: Possible aescin–rowachol interaction presenting as acute watery diarrhea: a case report and proposed mechanism
abstract: Abstract Background Drug-induced acute diarrhea is a common adverse effect, but its occurrence due to interaction between herbal medicinal products is rarely documented. We describe a case of acute watery diarrhea developed shortly after Reparil ® (aescin) was added to chronic Rowachol ® (terpene-based) therapy in a patient with cholelithiasis, raising the possibility of a drug interaction. Case presentation A male patient in his thirties, who had been receiving Rowachol ® for symptomatic cholelithiasis for three months, developed watery acute diarrhea within hours of initiating aescin (for acute hemorrhoidal attack). Vital signs were within normal limits. Routine stool testing was unremarkable except for the presence of mucus, and fecal calprotectin was within normal limits. Fecal bile acids were not measured. Given the suspicion of a drug interaction, the Drug Interaction Probability Scale (DIPS) was applied, yielding a score of 4, corresponding to a possible interaction. Symptomatic treatment was provided, and the diarrhea resolved after aescin was discontinued, while Rowachol ® was continued unchanged. The following day, Daflon ® (diosmin/hesperidin) was initiated, and no further gastrointestinal complaints were reported. Conclusions This case describes acute watery diarrhea shortly after the addition of aescin to chronic Rowachol therapy, with rapid resolution following ae…

title: Outsourced social media marketing transformation: an agency-side mechanism framework for agency–client coordination
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how agency professionals describe the structuring, governance and coordination of outsourced social media marketing transformation (SMMT) across the agency-client boundary. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research approach was used, involving 16 semi-structured interviews conducted with professionals from digital agencies. The interview guide focused on two primary themes: the initiation of client–agency relationships and the diagnosis of outsourced SMMT needs; as well as the implementation, validation and management of social media strategies and communities. Findings The analysis develops an agency-side mechanism framework of outsourced SMMT. The framework links reciprocal knowledge asymmetry with resource complementarity, distributes decision rights through role allocation, locates client brand control in validation and feedback and connects operational evidence with strategic adaptation through reporting. Across repeated engagements, governance may move from formal controls toward more relational coordination as trust develops. Originality/value The study conceptualizes governed complementarity as the condition in which cross-boundary specialization simultaneously creates value potential, mutual dependence and a need for control. The framework explains how role allocation, boundary validation, feedback and performance learning or…

title: Mechanism-guided large-grain design of Sc–Ce co-doped BaCoO 3 dual-phase oxygen electrodes for protonic ceramic cells
abstract: Abstract Conventional oxygen electrode designs for protonic ceramic cells (PCCs) predominantly rely on the empirical notion that maximizing specific surface area inherently enhances electrochemical performance. However, this paradigm overlooks the critical mismatch between the electrode microstructure and the intrinsic rate-determining step (RDS) of the proton-coupled oxygen-reduction reaction (PC-ORR). In this study, we present a mechanism-driven microstructure engineering strategy that deliberately favors large-particle architectures over nanoscale morphologies to optimize performance when proton transport, rather than surface reaction kinetics, governs the electrode process. By employing Sc–Ce co-doping in BaCoO3, Sc stabilizes the cubic perovskite lattice, while supersaturated Ce induces spontaneous in situ phase reconstruction, yielding a dual-phase composite electrode composed of ~80 wt% Co-rich cubic catalytic framework and ~20 wt% BaCeO3-based nanoscale proton-conducting fillers. Comprehensive electrode reaction pathway analysis reveals that Ce doping shifts the proton migration mechanism from hydration-dehydration to hydrogenation-dehydrogenation, thereby repositioning the RDS to be proton transport-dominated rather than surface-ORR-controlled. Guided by this insight, micrometer-sized particles are employed to establish continuous proton conduction channels. The optimi…

title: The Personal Fund as a Mechanism for Family Business Succession in Russia
abstract: The article studies the impact of the personal fund structure on ensuring family business succession and transforming traditional approaches to succession planning. The conclusion is substantiated that transferring key assets to an independent legal entity enables the founder, during their lifetime, to establish a stable governance model for the family business, define the procedures for asset utilization, and secure the financial interests of family members after their death. The significance of a personal fund is examined in terms of preserving unified corporate control, preventing the fragmentation of ownership interests and shares among heirs, mitigating the risk of inheritance and corporate disputes, and maintaining the continuity of a family business. Particular attention is paid to separating the functions of business management from the receipt of economic benefits: heirs and other family members can act as beneficiaries of a personal fund without being directly involved in managing the company. The article analyzes the specific features of the legal status of beneficiaries and separately examines the property qualification of 100 million rubles established by the civil law which is required for the creation of a lifetime personal fund. The conclusion is made that the high qualification amount limits the accessibility of this structure for small and medium-sized enterpr…

title: Mechanism-Embedded Machine Learning for Predicting Barite Induction Period Using Effective Interfacial Energy
abstract: Abstract Barite is a common inorganic scale in oilfield and is difficult to remove. Accurate prediction of the induction period is important for the safe and efficient operation of gathering and transportation systems. However, machine-learning-based prediction studies of the induction period of barite in systems containing scale inhibitors remain limited. In particular, few existing prediction methods explicitly incorporate information on nucleation mechanisms. Therefore, in this study, an effective interfacial energy descriptor was constructed based on Smoluchowski theory and introduced into the optimized support vector regression model to establish a mechanism-embedded model. The results showed that incorporating effective interfacial energy into the support vector regression (SVR) model improved its predictive performance. Specifically, the test-set R2 increased from 0.8364 to 0.857, while the RMSE decreased from 0.2853 to 0.2321 and the MAE decreased from 0.2082 to 0.1592. Meanwhile, the training-set R2 increased from 0.9286 to 0.949, while the RMSE decreased from 0.1768 to 0.1493 and the MAE decreased from 0.1054 to 0.0672. Further statistical analysis supported the rationality of using effective interfacial energy as an embedded descriptor and showed that it could provide complementary physical information for the model. These results indicate that the mechanism-embedded…

title: Disentangling weak spatial priors from generic local context in radiographic abnormality detection: a controlled mechanism audit
abstract: Abstract Background. Improvements from spatially guided crops may reflect generic local context, optimization or operating-point selection rather than informative spatial guidance. Purpose. To assess whether a coarse foreground guidance map improves radiographic abnormality discrimination beyond non-prior local controls. Methods. We audited original frozen DenseNet121 pipelines and conducted a revision-stage matched experiment using five seeds, patient-disjoint development partitions, and prior-guided, centered and random-position crops. Crops retained 90% of image width and height. The primary revised comparison used a common eight-epoch local budget and study ROC-AUC. Validation-selected checkpoints and fixed 50:50 global–local fusions were secondary. Evaluation used 1199 studies from 783 patients, with paired patient-cluster bootstrap intervals. This cohort had already been evaluated in the original study. Results. At the common final epoch, mean ROC-AUC was 0.892 269 for prior-guided, 0.891 573 for centered and 0.892 221 for random-position crops. Mean paired AUC differences were +0.000 696 (seed SD 0.002 757) versus centered and +0.000 048 (SD 0.002 693) versus random. All ten primary per-seed 95% intervals included zero. title: Speciation Distribution, Valence Transformation, and Immobilization Mechanism of Cr during Portland Cement Hydration
abstract: Abstract Chromium (Cr) immobilization pathways in Portland cement may vary with cement-matrix characteristics. In this study, representative 32.5- and 42.5-grade cements (C3-3 and C4-2) were compared using controlled Cr(III)/Cr(VI) addition and multiscale characterization. XPS showed partial reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) during hydration, while XAFS and 29Si NMR indicated Cr(III) association/incorporation with C-(A)-S-H-related structures. In C3-3-Cr, TEM, and SEM-EDS further revealed localized CaCr2O4 nanocrystals, indicating a combined structural association/incorporation–precipitation pathway. In C4-2-Cr, Cr was more diffusely distributed, and no resolvable Cr-bearing nanocrystals were observed in the examined TEM regions, indicating predominantly structural association/incorporation. These differences were associated with the higher hydration reactivity and more homogeneous C-S-H-rich microstructure of C4-2. The results demonstrate that cement-matrix hydration characteristics regulate the relative contributions of established Cr immobilization pathways, providing a mechanistic basis for the selection of cementitious matrices for Cr stabilization.

title: A hidden jet emission component revealed by the anomalous X-ray low state of 1ES 0229+200
abstract: Abstract In August 2021, simultaneous Swift-XRT and NuSTAR observations caught the extreme high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lac object 1ES 0229+200 in an exceptionally faint X-ray state. The spectrum was concave, showing tentative hardening above ∼ 25 keV. We investigate three representative interpretations within a common decelerating-jet framework: a one-zone hybrid electron–proton syn-chrotron model (Model A), and external-Compton (EC) and pure synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) realizations of a two-zone leptonic model (Model B). All three reproduce the simultaneous X-ray spectrum. In Model A, electron synchrotron emission accounts for the soft X-rays, while proton synchrotron emission produces the hard component. In both realizations of Model B, a compact inner zone produces the hard component through EC or SSC emission, while an outer zone approximately describes the historical broadband emission. The three solutions therefore lead to the same observational inference: the low state reveals an additional radiative component that is normally hidden beneath the dominant soft-X-ray continuum. The present data do not determine whether this component arises from a second particle population in one zone or from a distinct dissipation region. Simultaneous hard-X-ray, MeV, GeV, and VHE observations will distinguish these possibilities.

title: Fractal Modeling of Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Medium-Carbon Steel St6 Based on Fractal Dimension
abstract: This study examines the relationship between cooling conditions after austenitisation and the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties of medium-carbon steel St6. Samples were cooled in air, oil, Water-Polymer Solution (WPS) medium, and water following heating at 830 °C for 10 minutes. The Hausdorff (fractal) dimension of the obtained ferrito-pearlitic, bainitic, and martensitic structures was determined from optical micrographs at ×1000 magnification. Significant correlations were identified between the fractal dimension and hardness (HRB), ultimate tensile strength (s B ), and yield strength (s T ). Regression equations were developed that allow accurate prediction of the steel’s mechanical characteristics directly from the fractal dimension of its microstructure. The results indicate that a reduction in fractal dimension, which reflects increased structural ordering, leads to substantial improvements in strength and hardness. The fractal approach offers a promising non-destructive method for evaluating and optimizing heat treatment processes in structural steels.

title: PkM KTH Wana Mertha melalui Manajemen Ekowisata Mangrove Berbasis Blue Carbon di Desa Budeng
abstract: Ekowisata mangrove merupakan instrumen vital bagi keberhasilan konservasi karbon biru dan pemberdayaan ekonomi pesisir. Namun, kelompok berbasis masyarakat sering menghadapi tantangan terkait manajemen pariwisata konvensional, pemantauan karbon yang belum terstandarisasi, serta integrasi teknologi yang terbatas. Program pengabdian masyarakat ini bertujuan memberdayakan Kelompok Tani Hutan (KTH) Wana Mertha di Desa Budeng, Kabupaten Jembrana, melalui pengembangan ekowisata mangrove berbasis karbon biru. Program ini menerapkan pendekatan Participatory Action Research (PAR) melalui lima tahapan sistematis: perencanaan, persiapan, implementasi solusi multidisiplin, pemantauan dan evaluasi, serta pengelolaan keberlanjutan. Intervensi multidisiplin tersebut mencakup tiga pilar utama: manajemen ekowisata, restorasi mangrove, dan penerapan teknologi informasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan peningkatan signifikan di seluruh sektor (p < 0,001). Pengetahuan mitra dalam manajemen ekowisata meningkat dari 49,05% menjadi 89,00%, disertai dengan pembentukan paket wisata edukasi yang terstruktur serta diversifikasi empat produk hasil hutan bukan kayu (HHBK) dengan branding modern/kekinian. Pada pilar restorasi, tingkat pemahaman meningkat dari 72,00% menjadi 93,50%, didukung oleh penanaman berbasis spasial, modul pemantauan karbon terstandarisasi, dan papan informasi edukatif luar ruang. Selain i…

title: Biogenic Carboxylation of Granular Activated Carbon via Citrus aurantiifolia Juice for Fluoride Removal
abstract: Abstract Excess fluoride (F⁻) in potable water matrices poses a critical global public health threat, including endemic dental and skeletal fluorosis across vulnerable populations. Conventional defluoridation techniques like electrocoagulation and ion exchange are frequently constrained by prohibitive operational cost, complex synthesis protocols, and infrastructure limitations in decentralized settings. Herein, we demonstrate a surface functionalization approach for granular activated carbon (GAC) using raw Citrus aurantiifolia (lime) juice as a naturally derived, citric-acid-rich modifying agent. The procedure employs food-grade, non-hazardous materials as an alternative to conventional analytical-grade chemical reagents. Following modification, surface carboxyl-group concentrations increased from 1.26 mmol/g for GAC to 1.98 mmol/g for lime-modified GAC (LGAC) and 1.85 mmol/g for citric acid modified GAC (CAGAC). XPS showed a corresponding increase in surface oxygen content, from 5.92 at% (GAC) to 12.29 at% (CAGAC) and 21.28 at% (LGAC), with distinct C–O and O–C = O contributions on LGAC. Despite a 47% reduction in BET surface area, LGAC exhibited an empirical maximum monolayer adsorption capacity (q max ) of 1.63 mg/g, making its thermodynamic performance statistically identical ( p > 0.05) to CAGAC (1.65 mg/g) and yielding > 85% enhancement over unmodified GAC (0.88 mg/g). …

title: First observation and interpretation of ion cyclotron emission from energetic ions accelerated by lower hybrid waves in a tokamak plasma
abstract: Abstract We report the first observation of ion cyclotron emission (ICE) from a tokamak plasma during lower hybrid wave (LHW) injection and electron cyclotron resonance heating. Using a novel approach derived from linear kinetic theory, we infer key parameter values for the LHW-accelerated fast-ion distribution which drives the observed ICE spectra, and for the bulk plasma. These ICE spectra from deuterium plasmas in the EAST tokamak exhibit peaks at successive deuterium cyclotron harmonics, consistent with the collective relaxation of energetic deuterons through the magnetosonic cyclotron instability (MCI). By carrying out a multi-dimensional parameter scan of MCI growth rates in high-resolution two-dimensional ( k ∥ , k _ b o t ) wavenumber space, we obtain best-fit values for: the magnetic field; plasma density; background electron and ion temperature; and the concentration of fast deuterons, together with their energy, pitch ( u ∥ / | u | ) and thermal spread. We find that the observed ICE spectrum is likely driven by 770 keV deuterons, plausibly accelerated through LHW–ion interactions, which then undergo the MCI. The assumptions of the linear analytically based model include an infinite homogeneous plasma, and a ring-beam distribution of fast deuterons. Our results demonstrate a new scenario in which ICE serves as a passive diagnostic of energetic ion populations, and inv…

title: Green Light-Active Carbon Dots as Photoredox Catalysts for Atom-Transfer Radical Addition
abstract: Abstract Phenol-rich carbon dots were employed as efficient, metal-free photoredox catalysts for the atom-transfer radical addition reaction across multiple substrates. Their photocatalytic activity proved superior under green light compared to shorter-wavelength visible light, affording milder reaction conditions, fewer side products, and easier scalability.

title: A Molybdoenzyme Mediates Carbon–Sulfur Bond Making and Breaking in Ergothioneine Biosynthesis
abstract: Abstract The molybdopterin-dependent ergothioneine synthase (MES) from Caldithrix abyssi is the first molybdoenzyme known to catalyze the formation of carbon–sulfur bonds. To complete its catalytic cycle, this bifunctional enzyme desulfurates l-cysteine at a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate binding site and transfers the harvested sulfur atom (S0) to the molybdenum center of a bis-molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide cofactor more than 50 Å away. Subsequently, the sulfurated Mo-center transfers the labile sulfur atom onto the imidazole ring of Nα-trimethyl histidine (TMH). Combining experimental observations from cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, sequence-activity correlation, and substrate-specificity studies, we delineate the structural basis for long-distance sulfur transfer via a persulfide relay, the identity of the imidazole sulfurating species, and key sequence motifs that are indispensable for activity. Furthermore, the reversibility of MES-mediated sulfurization of TMH under physiological conditions suggests that ergothioneine may serve as a soluble reservoir of oxidizing equivalents, supporting anaerobic metabolism in deep-branching bacteria such as C. abyssi.
