title: Oxidase-mimicking bimetallic doped carbon quantum dots for mechanistically resolved dual-mode determination of tert-butylhydroquinone in edible oils
Carbon dioxide mineralised iron tailings powder for high-performance mortar
abstract: This study evaluates carbon dioxide (CO2) mineralised iron tailings powder (C-ITP) as a supplementary cementitious material for eco-friendly high-performance mortar (HPM). Accelerated carbonation (15% carbon dioxide, 0.5 MPa, 60°C and 70 ± 5% relative humidity for 48 h) was employed to modify raw ITP. Crucially, the treatment passivated and partially consumed reactive free oxides, particularly free calcium oxide (CaO), thereby mitigating soundness risks. Unlike raw ITP which impairs workability, C-ITP reduced the yield stress of fresh mortar, creating a ‘ball-bearing’ effect by way of surface passivation. An optimal replacement ratio of 15% C-ITP yielded a 28-day compressive strength of ∼115 MPa, comparable to the control, while higher dosages maintained high-performance standards. Microstructural characterisation (X-ray diffraction, thermogravimetry-derivative thermogravimetry and scanning electron microscopy) demonstrated that carbonation weakened calcium oxide-related reflections, produced only limited crystalline calcite and improved the particle–matrix interface, thereby enhancing durability against chloride ingress and freeze-thaw damage. While the quantitative carbon dioxide uptake was 0.175%, the primary value lies in overcoming the technical barriers of volume instability and poor rheology. By enabling 15% cement substitution, this chemo-physical modification strategy …

title: Plume emission rate estimation using Gaussian plumes in remote imaging spectroscopy with SPIIRE
abstract: The detection and quantification of methane and other trace gas emissions using remote sensing with imaging spectroscopy is an increasingly important tool for understanding local, regional, and global emissions. Traditional algorithms for quantifying the emission rate often rely on user-determined, instrument-dependent parameters and arbitrary plume boundaries. In this paper we present a new algorithm to estimate the emission rate based on a statistical inversion of a physical, Gaussian plume model that does not depend on such parameter choices or plume boundaries, termed SPIIRE. The method fully exploits instrument noise models, incorporates surface-albedo and atmospheric effects present in gas enhancement imagery, and is well suited for operational use. We present simulation results showing improved noise resilience, demonstrate performance against controlled-release experimental data using AVIRIS-3 and EMIT, and provide multiple examples using EMIT. The controlled-release results show improved performance of SPIIRE relative to an IME-based method. We then show how the model can be extended to complex scenes having overlapping plumes and to spatially-distributed sources like landfills.

title: Investment Decisions in Trading Card Game (TCG) Cards: The Roles of Self-Control, Financial Literacy, Financial Attitude, and Income
abstract: This study aims to empirically examine the effects of self-control, financial literacy, financial attitude, and income on investment decisions involving Trading Card Game (TCG) cards. The study is motivated by the rapid growth of investments in unconventional assets, such as TCG cards, which have attracted increasing interest from investors beyond traditional investment instruments, such as stocks or bonds. A mixed-methods approach employing an explanatory sequential design was adopted, with quantitative analysis serving as the primary method and qualitative inquiry providing complementary insights. The sample was selected using purposive sampling from members of TCG communities in Indonesia who had engaged in collecting, trading, or investing in TCG cards. Primary data were collected through an online questionnaire followed by semi-structured interviews. The quantitative data were analyzed using SmartPLS 4, while the qualitative data were examined through thematic descriptive analysis. These findings indicate TCG investment decisions are driven by income and restrained by conservative financial attitudes. Literacy and self-control have no significant effect, overridden by community dynamics.
venue: Dinasti International Journal of Economics, Finance & Accounting

title: The impact of green funds on the carbon emission intensity of listed companies
abstract: Background As the global climate change crisis intensifies, advancing the low-carbon transition has become a core strategy for sustainable development. Green finance is increasingly a key driver of corporate pollution reduction and carbon mitigation, yet how equity-based green funds shape corporate carbon emission intensity remains underexplored. Objective This paper investigates the impact of green fund shareholdings on the carbon emission intensity of listed companies, and examines the underlying mechanisms, heterogeneity and boundary conditions. Methods Using data from China’s A-share listed firms over 2010-2022 (3,299 firms; 17,943 firm-year observations) sourced from the CSMAR database, we employ firm and industry-by-year fixed-effects regressions, a battery of robustness checks, instrumental-variable (2SLS) and lagged-variable endogeneity treatments, as well as heterogeneity and mechanism analyses. Results Green funds significantly reduce corporate carbon emission intensity, a finding that remains robust after a series of alternative measures and endogeneity treatments. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that this emission-reduction effect is more pronounced among firms in non-heavily polluting industries, regions with stringent environmental regulations, growth-stage enterprises, and industries with low concentration. Mechanism analysis suggests that green funds curb carbon …

title: Decoding heritage buildings’ microclimate-behavior nexus: coupling fenestration light-ventilation performance with visitor behavior and perception
Triphenylphosphine Oxide-Enabled Nickel-Catalyzed Electrochemical C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling of Challenging Heteroaryl Electrophiles
abstract: Abstract We report a practical electrochemical decarboxylative cross-coupling enabling direct C(sp3)-C(sp2) bond formation between redox-active esters (RAEs) and recalcitrant (hetero)aryl electrophiles. The transformation is enabled by the use of triphenylphosphine oxide (TPPO) as an additive in the synergistic Ag–Ni electrocatalytic system reported previously. Critically, TPPO acts as a cooperative ligand additive that enables efficient coupling of heteroaryl scaffolds previously inaccessible under state-of-the-art electrochemical cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) conditions. Notably, this strategy accommodates nitrogen-rich heterocycles, including pyrazoles, pyrimidines, quinazolines, and indazoles, despite their frequent failure in existing methodologies and their importance as key medicinal chemistry scaffolds. This advance represents a qualitative expansion of the accessible chemical space, rather than an incremental extension of substrate scope. The protocol operates under mild conditions using an ElectraSyn setup, inexpensive Ni sources, and stoichiometric AgOTf, without strict exclusion of air or moisture, and has been validated at gram scale.

title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
abstract: Abstract Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Modelling the circular economy–renewable integration nexus: a cross-national empirical analysis of smart-technology adoption, territorial CO₂ emissions, and the material footprint
abstract: Climate neutrality relies on two levers usually examined separately: circular-economy (CE) practices and renewable integration. Drawing on ecological modernization theory and the environmental Kuznets curve (EKC), we regress per-capita carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in 20 European Union member states over 2014–2023 ( N = 200) on the circular material use (CMU) rate and the renewable energy (REN) share, with smart-technology adoption [ST; internet penetration and research and development (R&D) intensity] as a moderator. The pooled ordinary least squares (OLS), two-way fixed-effects (FE), and random-effects models use cluster-robust standard errors and a wild cluster bootstrap. A 1-percentage-point rise in the renewable energy share is associated with approximately 0.9% lower per-capita emissions in the baseline FE model ( p = 0.095) and 0.95% in the moderated model ( p = 0.030; bootstrap p = 0.048). CMU has no significant unconditional association with emissions in the levels models, and income exhibits concave curvature, although the implied EKC turning point lies above the sample maximum. The CMU × ST interaction is positive and significant ( β = 0.0065, p = 0.009; bootstrap p = 0.033) and is robust across all 20 leave-one-country-out subsamples: the circularity–emissions slope becomes less favourable as adoption rises, with the estimated interaction coefficient larger for…

title: Confinement-Driven Selectivity for Alkanol Dehydration in Ti-BEA Zeolites
abstract: Abstract Zeolite catalysts offer unique opportunities for tuning catalytic behaviors through modifications to both the active site and the surrounding pore environment. Although confinement effects in zeolites have been investigated, their specific contributions—particularly in Lewis acid catalysts—remain difficult to isolate from active-site chemistry and diffusive limitations. Here, we use density functional theory combined with microkinetic modeling to demonstrate confinement effects on the dehydration of ethanol, n-propanol, and n-butanol to alkene and dialkyl ether products catalyzed by Ti-BEA zeolites. Dehydration mechanisms are proposed over “closed” heteroatom-substituted sites, partially hydrolyzed “hydroxy-open” sites, and “alkoxy-open” sites formed through the dissociative adsorption of an alkanol. Closed-site dehydration dominates both alkene and ether formation at low alkanol partial pressures in the absence of co-fed water. Dispersion stabilization increases with alkanol size, decreasing the ratio of alkene-forming reactant-state coverages relative to ether-forming states. For alkanols that are smaller than the surrounding zeolite framework, dispersion stabilizes the closed-site alkene transition state, resulting in similar alkene selectivities for EtOH and n-PrOH. Repulsive interactions between the n-BuOH backbone and the framework raise the closed-site alkene fo…

title: Oil Recovery from Micropores in Heterogeneous Tight Conglomerate Rocks Using a Diluted Rhamnolipid Microemulsion
abstract: Abstract Oil recovery from micropores in heterogeneous tight conglomerates is limited by pore-scale heterogeneity and surfactant retention. This study evaluates a diluted rhamnolipid microemulsion (DME) in Mahu conglomerate cores with permeabilities of 0.01–1.6 mD using interfacial measurements, dynamic adsorption, coreflooding, NMR, and CT. DME has a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 7.7 nm. At 0.1 wt % DME, the oil–water interfacial tension is 1.2 mN/m, and the aqueous-phase contact angle decreases from 109° to 60° after treatment of an oil-wet surface. At the same working formulation concentration of 0.1 wt %, DME exhibits 78–80% lower cumulative adsorption than RL in two cores. This formulation-dose result does not establish intrinsic adsorption reduction at equal active-RL concentration. DME increases oil recovery by 8–14 percentage points relative to RL in three cores with permeabilities of 0.01–0.03 mD. Dynamic NMR indicates an earlier small-pore response with DME while large-pore oil production continues. Cumulative NMR analysis gives lower equivalent mobilization cutoff radii, and CT-derived estimates support a more uniform axial sweep. Fracture-network microfluidics provides qualitative supporting evidence. Together, these results suggest that lower adsorption losses, alongside improved interfacial and wetting properties, contribute to recovery and small-pore oil mobiliza…

title: Life cycle assessment of retail store interiors identifies environmental hotspots and the potential of furniture recycling and energy recovery at end of life
The Two-Dimensional Infinite Heisenberg Classical Square Lattice: Exact Free Energy and Specific Heat
Commercial nail polish-based single-electrode triboelectric nanogenerator for mechanical energy harvesting and water droplet energy conversion
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have brought new opportunities to realize relevant low-frequency mechanical energy self-powered systems, it is still a challenge and holds back the development of simple, low-cost, and scalable triboelectric materials. In this work, a triboelectric layer is made of commercially available nail polish used to fabricate a single-electrode TENG (abbreviated as N-TENG). The device was driven in single-electrode mode and exhibited an open-circuit voltage of 195 V, short-circuit current of 1300 nA, and maximum output power of 51.09 μW at an external load resistance of 500 MΩ. The electrical performance illustrates how nail polish acts as a feasible triboelectric material used for energy conversion, especially due to its availability. The practical applicability was validated through powering a commercial calculator, and other experiments proved that the device could harvest energy from free-falling water droplets under gravitational potential, indicating further applications for rain-energy harvesting. With the advantages of simple fabrication process, low-cost materials and acceptable electrical performance, the proposed N-TENG is practical for self-powered electronics and environmental energy harvesting.
venue: Journal of Metals, Materials and Minerals

title: Alkali-metal Na2LiXH6 (X = Al, In and Ga) complex hydrides as prospective materials for solar energy conversion and hydrogen storage applications
Effect of Acute Coffeeberry Extract on Self-Reported Mental Energy and Physical Performance Following a Fatiguing Cognitive Task: a Randomized, Double-Blind Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Objectives To assess the acute effects of two doses of coffeeberry (CB®) extract use on (i) mental energy and fatigue-related feelings (primary outcomes) and (ii) cycling performance (exploratory outcome). Methods Twenty-eight adults completed a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, cross-over experiment. Treatments were a base beverage supplemented with a CB® extract at doses of 100 mg (CB®100) and 300 mg (CB®300). The base beverage alone was the placebo (PL) and the base beverage with 75 mg caffeine (CAFF) was the positive control. Participants consumed one of the four beverages during four separate visits. Before (BL) and one-hour post-treatment (Post 1), cognitive tests and scales assessing the mood states of alertness, energy and fatigue were completed, taking 55-min. Two-hours post-treatment, a 20-min-high intensity interval cycling protocol was performed followed by a 3-min all-out time trial. Treatment effects on primary outcomes were tested using repeated measures ANOVAs. Cycling performance outcomes were tested using dependent t-tests. Results There was a significant Beverage x Time interaction for alertness ( p = 0.008), mental energy ( p = 0.009), and mental fatigue ( p = 0.008). Post-hoc analysis showed significant improvements from BL to Post 1 in the CAFF condition for alertness ( p = 0.002); and mental energy ( p = 0.006). Conclusions Beverages …

title: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry -derived adiposity and retinal arteriolar structure in men with hypogonadism: an exploratory cross-sectional pilot study
abstract: Introduction Previous studies showed correlations between body mass index (BMI) and microvascular remodeling. Materials and methods Using Adaptive Optics, we assessed the retinal arteriolar morphology of men with hypogonadism undergoing a dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and an endocrinological evaluation. Obesity was defined according to total body fat (BF [%]) ≥ 30%. Results We recruited 43 men; 46.5% were people with obesity. People with obesity had a higher arteriolar wall thickness (WT) (12.87 µm vs 11.98 µm, p=0.025) and wall cross-sectional area (WCSA) (4558.46 µm2 vs 4006.76 µm2, p=0.022). WCSA and WT resulted directly associated with waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR); their association with BMI was not significant (p=0.052 and p=0.053). WT and WCSA were significantly associated with BF (%), Fat mass/height 2 , Estimated visceral adiposity mass. Wall-to-lumen ratio (WLR) was directly associated with global adiposity distribution indices like Android to gynoid ratio and % Fat trunk/% Fat legs. Conclusions People with obesity showed hypertrophic remodeling. WHR, WHtR and actual adiposity indices from DXA displayed numerically more robust associations with retinal parameters compared to BMI, which may not fully capture such vascular impairments. The alterations of retinal microcirculation could be differently influenced by the extension and di…

title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
abstract: Abstract Establishing autonomous and energy-efficient feedback control at the hardware level remains challenging because conventional systems rely on centralized processing and continuous external computation, increasing energy consumption and system complexity. Here we show a neuromorphic autapse-inspired system that enables localized and bidirectional feedback control, using thermoregulation as a representative application. An autapse is a self-synaptic connection in which a neuron feeds its output back to its own synaptic input, enabling intrinsic feedback modulation. The system integrates a solid electrolyte-based synaptic transistor capable of multiplexing multiple inputs and a bidirectional leaky integrate-and-fire artificial neuron. By feeding the neuronal output back to an additional synaptic gate, excitatory and inhibitory feedback loops are realized within a compact architecture. Using an artificial thermoregulation platform, temperature-dependent inputs bidirectionally modulate neuronal firing frequency, demonstrating biologically inspired feedback control with a compact set of neuromorphic devices for autonomous and energy-efficient systems.

title: Integration and investigation of spatial and time diversity techniques in underwater wireless optical communication
Channel-Aware Hybrid Precoding and Gaussianized Companding for Energy-Efficient PAPR Reduction in Next-Generation Multicarrier Waveforms
abstract: Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) remains a major limitation in multicarrier communication because large waveform peaks reduce power-amplifier efficiency and may degrade reliability and spectral containment while increasing energy consumption. This paper presents a Channel-Aware Hybrid Precoding and Gaussianized Companding (CA-HPGC) framework for energy-efficient PAPR reduction in OFDM, UFMC, and OTFS waveforms. The framework observes channel-state information, Signal-to-Noise Ratio, Doppler condition, modulation order, power-amplifier headroom, and quality-of-service requirements to select SRC, DCT, DHT, or hybrid precoding. It then applies selective Gaussianized companding only to statistically dominant envelope samples. A multi-objective controller jointly considers PAPR, bit-error rate, error vector magnitude, out-of-band emission, energy per bit, and latency. In the simulation-based evaluation, CA-HPGC reduces PAPR to 6.50 dB for UFMC and 6.10 dB for OTFS at CCDF of 10-3. At 20 dB SNR, the proposed OTFS achieves BER of 2.8×10-4, EVM of 2.40%, and OOB power of -45.10 dBm. Energy efficiency reaches 2.17 Mbit/J with 0.46 μJ/bit. These findings indicate that adaptive signal shaping can reduce peaks while preserving reliability and transmitter energy efficiency.
venue: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering

title: The integration of persons with disabilities in municipal empowerment programmes: Lepelle-Nkumpi Municipal Area
abstract: Background: Despite South African government introducing anti-discrimination policies, persons with disabilities experience exclusion in municipal economic programmes and face disparities in participating in economic and social initiatives. Aim: This study aims to investigate the integration of persons with disabilities within economic empowerment programmes in Lepelle-Nkumpi Municipal Area. Methods: The study adopted a qualitative approach with in-depth interviews conducted with 15 participants within an area of Lepelle-Nkumpi Local Municipality (LNLM). Data were analysed through thematic content analysis and ATLAS.ti. Results: The findings revealed that disability integration in local government is constrained by inadequate disability promotion; poor understanding of persons with disabilities; deficient representation of persons with disabilities; limited recruitment; non-participation in local economic development forums; and capacity constraints. Conclusion: Municipalities are unable to integrate persons with disabilities in the implementation programmes and policies because of fragmented knowledge on disability. Contribution: The study is expected to add to knowledge on disability inclusion in local government. It aims to support the participation of persons with disabilities in decision-making and empowerment, leading to better governance and greater social justice.
venue: Journal of Local Government Research and Innovation

title: Idealizing energy democracy in the European semi-periphery: lithium mining, solar energy and fiction
abstract: Abstract Background The EU Green Deal aims to turn Europe into the first carbon neutral continent by 2050. However, criticisms of the hegemonic versions of this energy transition have focused on the top-down, asymmetric and corporate dimensions that often view local communities as barriers to the swift implementation of renewable energy infrastructures. Indeed, current scholarship argues that the energy transition is only maximizing the contradictions of neoliberal capitalism as the rapid rollout of green technologies increases North/South asymmetries, thereby fostering capital accumulation, green grabbing and ecocide. Research findings have furthermore argued that semi-peripheral countries such as Portugal are disproportionately affected by these negative impacts of the EU Green Deal. This paper explores two of the leading environmental controversies in the Portuguese context stemming directly from the prevailing energy transition – lithium mining in northern Portugal and plans to construct a large solar power plant in the Alentejo. Results The controversial lithium mining and solar energy projects prioritise corporate ownership, the centralization of renewable energy production, the marginalization of local communities as well as producing large green sacrifice zones and raising issues around energy democracy. This paper explores the role of fiction in the idealization of cou…

title: Visible-Light-Driven Dearomatization via Electrocyclic Ring Expansion for Solar Energy Storage
abstract: Abstract Molecular solar thermal (MOST) energy storage compounds capture solar photon energy in the strained chemical bonds of metastable photoisomers and release it on demand as heat, yet simultaneously achieving visible-light absorption and high energy storage density has remained a persistent challenge. Here we introduce 9-aryl acridine N-oxides as MOST compounds based on visible-light-driven dearomative ring expansion. Irradiation at 470 nm, near the solar irradiance maximum at 482 nm, quantitatively converts these compounds to metastable 1,2-oxazepines, which thermally revert to the parent N-oxides and discharge the stored energy. The system achieves energy storage densities of up to 0.54 MJ/kg, comparable to Dewar anthracenes, while absorbing substantially more red-shifted light and offering nearly 3 orders of magnitude longer storage lifetimes of up to 1.4 years in the solid state. The thermal half-lives of the 1,2-oxazepines are tunable through para-substitution on the aryl ring and solvation, enabling up to a 1,300-fold reduction in half-life. Crucially, the 9-aryl substituent biases the transient oxaziridine intermediate toward selective reversion to the N-oxide over competing decomposition pathways, overcoming the limitations of other acridine N-oxides reported to date. This work establishes light-induced ring expansion as an effective strategy for MOST and expands t…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Biogas Production by Co-Digestion between Food Waste and Watermelon Rind on Biochemical Methane Potential and Pilot-Scale
abstract: This research aims to study the biogas production potential from anaerobic co-digestion of food waste (FW) and watermelon rind (WR) in biochemical methane potential (BMP) batch scale and semi-continuous pilot scale. At first part, BMP assay was conducted under mesophilic conditions (35 ± 2 °C) for 30 days. Substrate mixture between FW and WR were digested at different proportions of 1:1, 1:3, and 3:1. Cow manure was used as inoculum and substrate-to-inoculum ratio (SIR) was fixed at 1:2 on a VS basis. All conditions of co-digestion, the FW1:WR3 ratio achieved the highest cumulative biogas production (812.18 ± 24.42 NmL g-1VSadd) and methane content (62.0 ± 2.0%). At the second part, based on the findings obtained from the BMP tests. The FW1:WR3 ratio was test in a pilot-scale semi-continuous anaerobic digester (total volume: 1,000 L; working volume: 800 L) at an organic loading rate (OLR) of 1 kgCODm⁻³d⁻¹ and a hydraulic retention time (HRT) of 30 days. The system achieved stable biogas production, with a cumulative yield of 8,322.86 L and an average methane concentration of approximately 57%. The VFA/ALK ratio remained below 0.30, indicating stable process performance. In summary, the results demonstrated that co-digestion of FW and WR has potential for decentralized renewable energy generation and sustainable organic waste management in the future.
venue: Journal of Renewable Energy and Smart Grid Technology

Bridging textile design and AI: An innovative methodological approach for the Ghanaian Textile Designer
abstract: Purpose: The study aimed to investigate the feasibility of employing selected artificial intelligence (AI) software to generate contemporary textile designs. Focusing on bridging textile design and AI, with a methodological approach for the Ghanaian Textile Designer. With AI emerging as a transformative force in multiple industries, including textiles, the research sought to assess its capacity to enhance design processes and meet consumer preferences. Methodology/Design: Three AI software programs, including Playground, Leonardo, and Lexcia, were selected for the study. Each was provided with identical prompts to generate contemporary textile designs. The outputs were then systematically analysed to identify similarities, differences, and overall design quality. Findings: The results showed that while the software received identical prompts, the generated designs displayed notable variations, alongside some shared visual features. The AI-driven process proved significantly faster and more efficient than traditional methods and yielded designs consistent with consumer specifications. Practical and Social Implications: The findings suggest that AI tools can substantially improve productivity, creativity, and responsiveness in textile design. Introducing AI-based design tools to textile designers in Ghana could enhance competitiveness, foster innovation, and better align producti…

title: MVMamba-Seg: a precise multimodal segmentation method for tomato disease monitoring via efficient Vision Mamba
abstract: Introduction Accurate segmentation of tomato leaf lesions is essential for disease diagnosis, severity assessment, and precision crop protection, yet field images contain complex backgrounds, diverse lesion appearances, irregular boundaries, and confusing foreground-background transitions. Methods We propose MVMamba-Seg, a text-guided multimodal Vision Mamba network that couples CNN and Vision Mamba streams with BERT-encoded expert descriptions for efficient global modeling. Dynamic Difference-Driven Feature Enhancement (DDFE) explicitly models foreground, background, and uncertainty branches, while the SSM Spatial Reweighting Attention Module (SSM-SRAM) refines skip connections and suppresses background noise. Results On a self-built dataset, MVMamba-Seg achieves 94.32% Dice and 89.26% mIoU using expert text; in cross-domain evaluation on PlantVillage, it achieves 81.82% Dice and 69.24% mIoU with 21.89M parameters. Compared with a Transformer-based counterpart, the Vision Mamba variant reduces parameters by approximately 31%, FLOPs by 42.8%, and improves inference speed by 60.1%. Discussion Through efficient global modeling with Mamba and the integration of expert disease descriptions with visual features, the framework delineates lesion contours and spatial distributions to support tomato disease monitoring and targeted crop protection.

title: Humidity and light control methacrolein dry deposition to vegetation: measurements and model implications
abstract: Introduction Volatile organic compounds (VOC), especially isoprene oxidation products such as methacrolein (MACR), contribute significantly to tropospheric ozone and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. While VOC emissions are well studied, their dry deposition to vegetation remains poorly understood and is often misrepresented in atmospheric models, owing to the scarcity of dry deposition data. Methods We conducted controlled twin-chamber experiments to quantify the dry deposition velocity (Vd) of MACR to coniferous (Scots pine, white spruce), deciduous (birch) and evergreen (English ivy) species, each in three biological replicates, under varying temperature, relative humidity (RH) and light, with concentrations measured by PTR-ToF-MS. The resulting vegetation-specific, RH- and light-dependent parameterisations were implemented in two independent chemistry-transport models, GEOS-Chem and EMEP, within the Wesely (1989) resistance-in-series scheme. Results MACR dry deposition was significantly higher under light, with Vd showing strong RH dependence during illuminated periods and much lower, RH-independent values in the dark. The response varied by species: conifers displayed higher deposition rates and greater RH sensitivity than the deciduous broadleaf birch. Compensation points remained near zero, consistent with active uptake involving stomatal control and/or metaboli…

title: Proteomic responses to elevated CO2 in wheat flag leaves are largely cultivar- and year-specific
abstract: Increasing atmospheric CO 2 concentrations are expected to alter carbon and nitrogen metabolism in C 3 crops such as wheat ( Triticum aestivum ), affecting not only grain yield and quality but also source tissues involved in assimilate supply. Among these, the flag leaf plays a central role during grain filling. Here, we investigated the effects of elevated CO 2 on protein content and protein composition in flag leaves of ten winter wheat cultivars grown under ambient (≈420 ppm) and elevated (≈600 ppm) CO 2 during the 2021 and 2022 growing seasons. To establish a robust proteomic workflow, four protein extraction methods were compared, identifying filter-aided sample preparation as the most suitable, followed by combined extraction, phenol extraction, and trichloroacetic acid/acetone precipitation. An SDS concentration of ≈0.5% was optimal, whereas higher concentrations markedly reduced protein identifications. Protein content ranged from 1.8 to 3.9% of fresh weight. Three-way ANOVA showed significant cultivar effects and a significant year × CO 2 interaction, but no overall CO 2 main effect, indicating strong environmental modulation of protein responses. Quantitative proteomics confirmed this pattern, with principal component analysis separating samples primarily by year rather than CO 2 treatment or cultivar. Only 22 proteins in 2021 and six proteins in 2022 were significant…

title: Multi-omics dissects long seed dormancy dynamics during wheat maturation
abstract: Seed dormancy is a critical adaptive trait conferring resistance to pre-harvest sprouting (PHS) in wheat, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying long dormancy remain elusive. This study integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses of developing seeds from the long-dormant Yunnan hulled wheat variety YT34 and the non-dormant variety ‘Huapei 5’ at 10, 20, 30, and 40 days after anthesis (DPA), with three biological replicates per time point. Germination assays confirmed that YT34 exhibited significantly deeper dormancy than Huapei 5, with final germination percentages of 15.3% ± 2.1% versus 96.7% ± 1.5% (P<0.001). Genotype was the primary driver of differences of omics differences, with developmental stage playing a secondary role. We identified 156 core differentially accumulated metabolites in YT34, primarily organic oxygen compounds, fatty acyls, and carboxylic acid derivatives. Exogenous application of these metabolites at multiple concentrations, individually or in combination, did not significantly reduce germination (P>0.05), indicating that single metabolites are insufficient to induce deep dormancy. Transcriptome analysis revealed 1,798 shared differentially expressed genes as a core regulator, with downregulated genes outnumbering upregulated genes at 40 DPA, reflecting a transcriptional suppression during dormancy establishment. GO and KEGG enrichment analy…

title: ASIA: adaptive single-diffusion-stage inference acceleration for diffusion-based virtual try-on
abstract: Abstract Virtual try-on synthesises an image of a person wearing a chosen garment. Diffusion models give the most realistic results, but remain too slow for interactive use. The leading method, TPD, runs its diffusion network twice: a first pass predicts a pair-specific mask locating where the garment belongs, and a second pass renders the garment into that region. Each pass takes about 100 denoising steps, so one image needs roughly 200, half of them producing only a binary shape. This first stage does not justify a diffusion model. We propose Adaptive Single-Diffusion-Stage Inference Acceleration (ASIA), which replaces diffusion-based mask generation with a lightweight convolutional network. Using DensePose and the flat garment mask as structural priors, ASIA predicts the pair-specific mask in one forward pass, reducing that stage from seconds to milliseconds. Try-on then needs a single diffusion stage, whose input block alone is finetuned to the new mask distribution. On VITON-HD, inference falls from 15.4 to 7.5 seconds per image, a 2.05-fold speedup. Under a controlled reproduction of TPD, paired structural (SSIM) and perceptual (LPIPS) similarity both improve while the Fréchet Inception Distance rises slightly (9.04 against 8.78). Removing an entire diffusion stage thus trades a small FID increase for a large speedup and improved paired fidelity.

title: Joint Clustering, Association, and Power Allocation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO-NOMA
abstract: This study revisits the joint design of user clustering, Access-Point (AP) association, transmit-antenna selection, and power allocation in downlink cell-free massive MIMO with Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA). A rigorous Monte-Carlo evaluator with pilot contamination, Minimum Mean-Square-Error (MMSE) channel estimation, maximum-ratio transmission, and Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) scores every candidate configuration consistently under common random numbers. A central methodological point is emphasized: prior clustering-centric comparisons hold AP association and power fixed, which conflates the clustering effect with an unoptimized association budget. When all schemes are granted an identical association/antenna/power search-a matched-scope comparison over 40 independent topologies—a clear and statistically significant ordering of resource levers emerges: AP association is dominant (+20.2 bps/Hz), clustering optimization is a significant second lever (+13.0 bps/Hz), the clustering algorithm itself contributes a small but significant increment (+4.1 bps/Hz), and transmit-antenna selection is spectrally neutral, all under the parameter regime investigated (Table 3); the ordering is not asserted to hold universally across every cell-free massive MIMO-NOMA configuration. A block-coordinate joint optimizer is proposed and shown, by exhaustive enumeration on small…

title: The effects of visual and auditory presentation styles on learning outcomes and emotional responses in virtual cultural heritage experiences
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly used to present and teach cultural heritage. However, systematic guidance for designing combinations of visual and auditory elements remains limited, and potential interactions between these modalities across different dimensions of user experience have often been overlooked. To address this gap, we conducted a 2 × 2 × 2 within-subjects experiment examining visual style (Realistic 3D vs. Stylized 3D), voice type (Standard Voice vs. Emotional Voice), and ambient background soundscape (Absent vs. Present). Seventy-two university students experienced narrated VR presentations of Sanxingdui bronze artifacts through a head-mounted display. User engagement, perceived presence, emotional responses, and immediate cultural knowledge acquisition were assessed. The results revealed outcome-specific differences across audiovisual presentation factors. Realistic 3D was associated with higher perceived presence and Dominance, whereas Stylized 3D was associated with higher Valence and immediate learning scores. Emotional Voice was associated with higher perceived presence, Valence, and Arousal. Background Soundscape was associated with higher engagement, perceived presence, and Arousal but lower immediate learning scores. No significant interactions were observed for engagement, whereas perceived presence, emotional responses, and learning outcomes exhibit…

title: Effects of menstrual cycle phase on straight punch performance and explosive power in elite female boxers
abstract: Purpose To compare straight punch performance and explosive power across the early follicular, ovulatory, and mid-luteal phases of the menstrual cycle in elite female boxers, and to examine the relationship between hormone changes and performance changes. Methods Twenty-four national first-class female boxers participated in a prospective longitudinal repeated-measures design. Cycle phases were verified using basal body temperature, urinary luteinizing hormone testing, and salivary hormones. Lead and rear straight punch peak force and peak velocity were measured, along with countermovement jump relative peak power, rotational medicine ball throw distance, and bench press throw relative peak power. Salivary estradiol, progesterone, and free testosterone were measured using LC-MS/MS. Repeated-measures ANOVA was used to compare phases, with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons and partial η² reported. Individual response proportions and correlations between hormone changes and performance changes were calculated. Results All punch performance and explosive power variables peaked during the ovulatory phase, with large effect sizes (partial η²=0.175–0.451). No significant differences were observed between the early follicular and mid-luteal phases. Salivary estradiol, progesterone, and free testosterone exhibited expected cyclic fluctuations, confirming valid phase classificatio…

Microencapsulation of Bacillus subtilis BS9 in an alginate-chitosan matrix for the management of fusarium wilt in Bengal gram
Advancing Alzheimer’s Therapy Through Nanobotanicals: Metallic Nanoparticles and Plant-Derived Neuroprotectants
Multifaceted characterisation of Bipolaris maydis isolates causing maydis leaf blight of maize in India
abstract: Maydis leaf blight (MLB), caused by Bipolaris maydis, is a major foliar disease of maize in India, causing yield losses ranging from 20 % to 85 %. Its prevalence has increased with rising temperature regimes. The present study characterised the cultural, morphological, pathogenic and molecular variability among 22 isolates of B. maydis collected from five agro-climatic zones across India. Radial growth on potato dextrose agar (PDA) ranged from 49.00 to 90.00 mm and the growth rate from 4.9–9.0 mm day-1. Colony colour varied from creamy white to black and texture from smooth to rough. Conidial length and width ranged between 36.62–72.12 µm and 9.45–14.45 µm, respectively, with the number of septa varying from 5 to 9. Significant positive correlations were observed among conidial length, width and septation (r > 0.80, p < 0.01). All isolates were pathogenic, showing considerable variation in virulence. The incubation period varied from 39.6 to 57.6 hr and the latent period from 67.2 to 91.2 hr across genotypes. Mean lesion length ranged from 14.34 to 19.35 mm and lesion breadth from 2.45 to 2.90 mm. Disease severity ranged from 5.3 to 7.5 on a 1–9 scale. Isolate Bm-7 (Pantnagar-2) was the most virulent, with the highest disease score (7.5), shortest incubation (39.6 hr) and latent (67.2 hr) periods and longest lesion length (19.35 mm). It formed a distinct cluster in pathogenic g…

title: Collaborative governance under power asymmetry: co-opted agility in NGO resource mobilisation during the 2021 Henan flood
abstract: Purpose This study introduces the concept of co-opted agility to explain how non-state organisations maintain operational speed within state-dominated emergency governance systems. Focusing on a government-affiliated foundation responding to the 2021 Henan floods in China, the study examines how power asymmetry shapes collaborative governance in centralised disaster regimes. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a qualitative case study of a government-affiliated foundation with a specialised relief unit and pre-positioned supplies. The evidence includes 11 semi-structured interviews with 10 people: 5 foundation staff members, 3 representatives of peer organisations and 2 sector experts. One participant was interviewed during both the acute response and the recovery period. Internal documents and media reports provided additional context. The analysis used the material through iterative coding informed by the Gioia methodology. Findings The analysis shows how the foundation remained quick without becoming independent of the state. Its internal procedures buffered operational decisions from external pressure. Established ties with logistics providers and peer organisations allowed staff to mobilise before formal coordination was fully in place, although this created duplication and coordination costs. Learning was uneven. Staff adjusted operations rapidly, but politica…

title: QTL mapping and transcriptome analysis reveal genetic loci and candidate genes associated with drought-related traits in maize (Zea mays L.)
abstract: Drought is a major abiotic constraint on maize growth and productivity worldwide. Elucidating the genetic basis of drought-related traits is essential for developing drought-tolerant maize cultivars. In this study, a recombinant inbred line (RIL) population derived from a cross between the drought-sensitive inbred line ZhengA88 and the drought-tolerant line ZhengT22, was used to identify quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for plant height (PH), ear height (EH), plant-to-ear height ratio (PEH), ear tip-barrenness length (ETL), and kernel ratio (KR) under well-watered (WW) and water deficit (WD) conditions at the flowering stage over two summer maize growing seasons. A total of 125 QTLs were detected, each explaining 1.55%–19.65% of the phenotypic variation. Of these QTLs, 78 (62.4%) were associated with drought tolerance and 5 showed significant QTL-by-environment interactions (QEI) effects. Fifty-one QTLs were located in overlapping genomic regions, forming 18 QTL clusters. Integrating QTL mapping with transcriptome profiling of the parental lines under drought stress identified 235 drought-responsive differentially expressed genes (DEGs) within nine genomic regions encompassing seven QTL clusters and two major-effect QTLs. Based on these genes expression patterns and reported functional annotations, eleven genes were predicted as candidate genes for drought tolerance: Zm00001d0057…

title: Pembelajaran Virtual dalam Perspektif Teori Behaviorisme, Kognitivisme, dan Konstruktivisme
abstract: Virtual learning enables students to participate in learning activities online without face-to-face meetings with teachers in the classroom. Its implementation requires an appropriate foundation in learning theory to align instructional strategies with the intended objectives. This study aims to examine the concept and characteristics of virtual learning, analyze the application of behaviorism, cognitivism, and constructivism, and explain the implications of integrating these three theories into virtual learning. The study employed a qualitative approach through a literature review using descriptive-critical analysis and conceptual synthesis. The review findings showed that behaviorism emphasizes practice, reinforcement, and feedback; cognitivism focuses on information processing and conceptual understanding; and constructivism emphasizes experience, interaction, and problem solving. The synthesis yielded a conceptual matrix linking the three theories to learning objectives, learning activities, interaction, feedback, and assessment. The review concludes that the three theories can be used in complementary ways according to learning needs. The study contributes a conceptual framework that helps educators select and align virtual learning strategies with learning objectives and learner characteristics.

title: Rhizosphere microbiome-mediated adaptation to soil nutrient stress under organic substitution: implications for kiwifruit productivity and metabolic quality
abstract: Introduction Intensive perennial orchards frequently suffer from soil nutrient imbalance marked by accumulated legacy nutrients and insufficient bioavailable nutrient pools, which acts as a major abiotic stress limiting kiwifruit productivity. In this study, we adopted an isosynthetic-nutrient experimental design with rapeseed-cake substitution gradients to disentangle organic carbon effects from macronutrient inputs, and investigate how organic amendments remodel rhizosphere microbiomes in association with kiwifruit acclimation to soil nutrient stress. We hypothesized that suitable organic substitution would reshape rhizosphere microbial composition and co-occurrence patterns linked to balanced soil nutrient supply and enhanced fruit performance, without inferring causal microbial functions. Methods Based on a five-year field trial involving two commercial kiwifruit cultivars (‘Donghong’ and ‘Jinyan’), we implemented equal-nutrient fertilization treatments with 25%, 50%, and 100% rapeseed cake replacing mineral fertilizer. By combining high-throughput amplicon sequencing and PLS-SEM modeling, we uncovered correlative, non-causal pathways within the “soil-microbe-fruit” continuum. Results The 100% rapeseed-cake treatment (T1) showed the best overall performance among the tested treatments, depleting legacy soil N and P. This treatment enriched key microbial taxa including Stero…

title: Legal Regulation of the Use of Information and Digital Technologies in the Exercise and Guaranteeing of Reproductive Rights and Reproductive Health
abstract: As part of the work, a comprehensive analysis was conducted of the legal regulation of the use of information and digital technologies in the field of implementing and guaranteeing reproductive rights and reproductive health. The introduction of digital technologies in the field of reproductive health affects not only the rights and dignity of an individual but can also have a comprehensive impact and change social roles of parents and social relations. Options for using digital technologies in the field of reproductive health, as well as the legal and ethical problems associated with such use, were examined in order to develop a comprehensive and systematic approach to legal regulation, taking into account bioethics and bioconstitutionalism.

title: The Precautionary Principle in UNESCO International Biolaw and Its Promotion through State Action
abstract: This research article examines the legal nature, content, and significance of the precautionary principle in international biolaw, as well as its promotion through the activities of UNESCO and sovereign states. It identifies challenges in the legal regulation, interpretation, and application of the precautionary principle in the context of scientific and technological progress, biotechnology, and scientific advances. The author concludes that this principle should not be pitted against technical progress, scientific advances, or technological innovation. Its purpose is to promote the prevention of unnecessary risks and the search for “alternative development paths” that may be considered safer or more environmentally friendly technologies.

title: Molecular Characterization of Polarity-Based Fractions of Bamboo Tar: Implications for Upgrading Challenges
abstract: Abstract Bamboo tar, produced from bamboo pyrolysis, is a promising renewable feedstock for fuels, chemicals, and carbon materials. However, its complex chemical composition—particularly the presence of highly oxygenated polar compounds—poses significant challenges for efficient upgrading and high-value utilization. In this study, five distinct polarity fractions of bamboo tar were separated by column chromatography and investigated using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) and Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS). The results revealed that the moisture content and oxygen content of bamboo tar were 15.70% and 28.43%, respectively. Besides, the yields of non/weakly polar fractions (F-I, F-II, F-III) and polar fractions (F-IV and F-V) were 8.16% and 35.82%, respectively. GC–MS analysis of the non/weakly polar fractions revealed phenolics (24.08%), furans (15.99%), and methoxyphenols (13.10%) as the predominant volatile compounds, which hold promise for applications in biofuels, biochemicals, and biobased materials. FT-ICR MS analysis of the polar fractions uncovered a dominance of O4–O6 class compounds, primarily polycyclic aromatic structures enriched with oxygen-containing functional groups, concentrated in the lignin-derived region of van Krevelen diagrams (0 ≤ O/C ≤ 0.6, 0.5 ≤ H/C ≤ 2.0). The high abundance of polyoxygenated aromati…

title: Molecular Evolution, Heteroatom Transformation, and Asphaltenes Formation during Controlled Autoxidation of Vacuum Residue: Insights from Complementary Atmospheric Pressure Photoionization and Electrospray Ionization Fourier Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometry
abstract: Abstract Controlled autoxidation induces substantial molecular evolution in vacuum residue (VR) through oxygen incorporation and molecular restructuring, yet the associated heteroatom transformations remain insufficiently understood. In this study, complementary atmospheric pressure photoionization (APPI(+)) and electrospray ionization (ESI(±)) Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) were employed to characterize the structural evolution of vacuum residue and its derived asphaltenes during controlled autoxidation, with and without tetralin. APPI-MS revealed an increase in the relative abundance of oxygen–sulfur (OSx) molecular classes from 6.10% in vacuum residue-derived asphaltenes (VR-Asph) to 14.76% in asphaltenes derived from oxidized vacuum residue (VR-ox-Asph), consistent with oxygen-containing transformations involving sulfur-bearing molecular populations. Complementary ESI-MS analyses showed substantial transformation of nitrogen-containing molecular populations, with nitrogen-only species decreasing while nitrogen–oxygen species increased in both positive- and negative-ion modes. Together, the APPI and ESI results reveal oxygen-containing molecular transformations together with changes in molecular unsaturation and composition that are consistent with molecular-restructuring pathways. Oxygen incorporation is reflected by increased relati…

title: Deep spiking Q-networks for turn-based game environments: encoding choices and energy trade-offs
abstract: Abstract Deep reinforcement learning has achieved remarkable success across various domains but at the cost of substantial energy consumption. Spiking neural networks (SNNs), inspired by biological neural processing, offer a promising solution through event-driven, sparse computations. To evaluate the capability of SNNs in discrete, strategic decision-making settings, we adopt the deep spiking Q-network (DSQN) framework, whose viability has been established in foundational studies. However, these prior works predominantly restricted DSQN’s application to reactive control tasks and high-frequency visual environments such as Atari games, leaving its efficacy in deliberate, long-horizon strategic reasoning and discrete turn-based environments unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by evaluating the DSQN architecture against traditional deep Q-networks (DQN) to investigate whether spike-based value estimation can achieve comparable performance in turn-based strategic tasks. To enable this comparison, we adopt two well-established open-source turn-based environments: Tic-Tac-Toe (TTT) as a baseline micro-benchmark for turn-based structures, and Connect 4 to assess architectural scalability under complex game environments. Within this framework, we then systematically analyze six distinct SNN input encoding methods: Population, Count rate, time-to-first-spike (TTFS), rank order co…

title: ANN–GA based adaptive predictive energy management for renewable energy optimization in solar-diesel hybrid systems
abstract: The intermittent nature of solar energy continues to constrain the effective utilization of photovoltaic (PV) systems in solar-diesel hybrid energy systems, particularly in tropical semi-arid regions where solar irradiance fluctuates considerably throughout the day. This study proposes a predictive energy management framework that integrates artificial neural network (ANN)-based irradiance forecasting with genetic algorithm (GA)-based optimization to support adaptive selection of energy sources between PV systems and diesel generators. Environmental data, including air temperature, relative humidity, and solar irradiance, were collected at the Badan Perakitan dan Modernisasi Pertanian (BRMP, Agricultural Assembly and Modernization Agency) experimental field in Naibonat, Kupang Regency, Indonesia. A multilayer perceptron ANN was developed to forecast short-term solar irradiance, and its predicted output was subsequently adopted as the fitness function for the GA to identify the optimal operating condition using an irradiance threshold of 300 W m−2. The ANN produced reliable short-term irradiance predictions, while the GA converged to a stable solution within approximately 15 generations, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed predictive energy management framework. The developed approach achieved a renewable energy utilization rate of 75.0%, reduced diesel fuel consumptio…

title: Tailoring energy storage properties of epoxy composites using ferroelectric, anti-ferroelectric particles and hybrid ceramic fillers
abstract: Epoxy-based dielectric composites reinforced with ferroelectric BaTiO3 and antiferroelectric AgNbO3 were fabricated and comprehensively evaluated to investigate the influence of filler type and composition on dielectric and energy storage performance. Structural, spectroscopic and microstructural analyses confirmed the successful incorporation of the ceramic fillers within the epoxy matrix. BaTiO3/epoxy composites exhibited markedly enhanced dielectric permittivity and polarization, resulting in a maximum recoverable energy density of 134.4 mJ·cm‒3, albeit with moderate charge-discharge efficiency due to hysteresis-induced energy loss. In contrast, AgNbO3/epoxy composites displayed lower permittivity but significantly reduced dielectric loss and excellent efficiency, reaching up to 96.7%, owing to low remanent polarization and a highly reversible dielectric response. Building on these complementary characteristics, hybrid BaTiO3-AgNbO3/epoxy composites were developed and found to provide complementary improvements in dielectric and energy-storage performance. The optimal hybrid formulation (15 wt% BaTiO3/30 wt% AgNbO3) achieved the highest recoverable energy density of 155.8 mJ·cm‒3, while the equimolar hybrid (22.5/22.5) provided exceptional efficiency of 99.06% with minimal energy loss. These enhancements arise from the complementary dielectric responses of the two ceramic fi…

Mechanistic Insights into Biosurfactant-Mediated Microbial Enhanced Oil Recovery under Reservoir Conditions: Ex Situ and In Situ Core Flooding Using Bacillus subtilis SN1
abstract: Abstract Microbial enhanced oil recovery (MEOR) has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional recovery methods for mobilizing trapped oil through biosurfactant-mediated interfacial interactions. Herein, a facultative anaerobic strain, Bacillus subtilis SN1 was isolated from refinery sludge, which produced diverse lipopeptide biosurfactant mixture comprising surfactin, iturin, and fengycin. The SN1 strain reduced the surface tension (ST) and interfacial tension (IFT) to 28.8 and 0.71 mN/m, respectively, with a crude biosurfactant yield of 6.15 g/L and critical micelle concentration (CMC) of 320 mg/L. The strain remained metabolically active under elevated salinity (10%), temperature (70 °C), and crude oil concentration (10%). It also produced ∼1.81 g/L of crude biosurfactant under anaerobic reservoir-simulated conditions at 60 °C. Additionally, biosurfactant retained structural stability and surface activity at high temperature (90 °C), salinity (10%), and pressure (3000 psi). The produced biosurfactant exhibited shear thickening behavior (n = 1.17) with a viscosity of 1.20 mPa.s. Core flooding experiments under reservoir-simulated conditions demonstrated additional oil recovery (AOR) of ∼15.6% through ex situ biosurfactant (1 CMC) flooding, while in situ flooding using SN1 culture with 5-day shut-in period showed ∼9.6% AOR. A cyclic huff-and-puff strategy further imp…

title: Physics–informed deep learning for soliton dynamics and energy flow control in nonlinear physical systems
abstract: Abstract Nonlinear field equations that model high-energy physical systems are frequently hampered by limited integration of deep learning frameworks and the absence of robust hybrid analytical-computational methodologies. In the current research, we overcome such challenges by examining the complex coupled Higgs field equations by using a novel combination of analytical and deep learning methods. First of all, the Kumar–Malik (KM) approach is used to obtain exact traveling wave solutions such as bright, dark, singular, and periodic soliton structures. These solutions are graphically visualized using high-resolution three-dimensional surface plots, two-dimensional cross-sectional profiles, and full heatmap representations, all generated in a Python computational environment. Subsequently, for the first time, an inverse KM physics-informed neural network (IKM-PINN) is proposed for identifying unknown physical parameters and reconstructing soliton dynamics in an inverse-learning setting. The proposed hybrid model incorporates physics-based constraints, analytical soliton profiles, and data-driven learning processes, resulting in highly accurate recovery of bright soliton solutions. A quantitative comparison between the KM solutions and predictions of the IKM-PINN demonstrates excellent agreement resulting in a mean squared error (MSE) of 2 × 10 − 8 and mean absolute error (MAE) o…

Agro-processing value chains and SMME participation in South Africa: insights from Johannesburg and the Gauteng city-region - a scoping review
abstract: Agro-processing is increasingly recognised as a strategic sector for promoting inclusive urban economic development, SMME growth, and employment creation within sustainable food systems. This study examines SMME participation and employment outcomes within Johannesburg’s urban food system, drawing on evidence from Gauteng Province and South Africa more broadly. A scoping review design was adopted, using structured searches of Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar for literature published between 2020 and 2025. Eligible sources included peer-reviewed articles, government policy developments, and institutional reports addressing agro-processing, value chains, and SMME development. Of the 40 evidence sources included (28 peer-reviewed articles, eight government policy developments, and four institutional/grey literature reports), 12 focused specifically on Johannesburg, 10 on the wider Gauteng City Region, and 18 provided national or international perspectives. Findings indicate that agro-processing has considerable potential for enterprise development and employment creation; however, SMMEs face persistent constraints in finance, food safety compliance, infrastructure, logistics, and market access. Opportunities exist through niche urban markets, supplier development programmes, shared infrastructure, and cooperative business models. The evidence base remains uneven, with a p…

title: Current Collector Augmented Reductive Dissolution of Spent Li-Ion Battery Black Mass for Regeneration of NMC622 Cathode
abstract: Abstract Overcoming reliance on strong acid and external reductants in the hydrometallurgical recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) offers a promising pathway toward an environmentally benign and cost-effective strategy. In this study, we developed a current collector augmented reductive dissolution strategy using a mild phosphorus oxoacid as the hydrometallurgical leaching medium. The process utilizes aluminum current collector already present in the spent LIB black mass as an in situ reducing agent. Importantly, the proposed system addresses two key limitations of previously reported aluminum-assisted leaching processes, i.e., reliance on strongly acidic conditions and sluggish leaching kinetics, by operating under milder acidic conditions while exhibiting accelerated leaching kinetics. At optimized conditions, the process achieved maximum leaching efficiencies of approximately 94%, 89%, and 91% for Ni, Co, and Li, respectively. This reductive pathway lowered the leaching activation energy to below 13 kJ mol–1, indicating favorable dissolution kinetics. The transition metals are selectively retrieved as oxalates by means of chemical precipitation with more than 98% yield and subsequently used as precursors to synthesize LiNi0.6Mn0.2Co0.2O2 (rNMC). rNMC exhibits a well-ordered layered hexagonal structure with minimal cation mixing and successfully emulates the electr…

title: Regulatory conformity as a foundation for revenue performance: Property tax (PBB-P2) administration in Bitung City, Indonesia
abstract: Rural and Urban Land and Building Tax (PBB-P2) is a key local tax, yet many local governments fall short of their collection targets after its administration was devolved to the regions and local tax rules were restructured by Law No. 1 of 2022 on Fiscal Relations between the Central Government and Regional Governments. This study analyzes the PBB-P2 collection system and procedures at the Regional Revenue Agency (BAPENDA) of Bitung City and assesses how procedural conformity relates to revenue performance in 2021–2025. Using a qualitative descriptive single-case design, primary data came from semi-structured interviews with three purposively selected BAPENDA officials, complemented by regulations, target–realization records, and Tax Payable Notice (SPPT) data. Each procedural stage was compared with Bitung City Regional Regulation No. 1 of 2024 and Mayoral Regulation No. 63 of 2017. All stages are carried out formally, but registration, assessment, and billing conform only with qualifications and data collection is only partly evidenced: mass collection was skipped in some years for lack of budget, and billing relied on notification rather than graded enforcement. Revenue realization never reached the target, ranging from 75.19% (2023) to 95.64% (2025), and only 42.30%–57.53% of SPPT issued were paid each year. Regulatory conformity is a necessary foundation but does not by it…

title: Understanding VAT Revenue Potential in Bangladesh: A Comparative Assessment of Public Evidence on Tax Expenditure and Revenue Administration
abstract: Value-added tax (VAT) is an important source of domestic revenue in Bangladesh, yet concerns remain about the size of tax concessions, the effectiveness of revenue administration, and the extent to which potential revenue is translated into actual collections. This article examines publicly available evidence on Bangladesh's VAT revenue potential through a comparative documentary analysis of the National Board of Revenue's (NBR) VAT Expenditure Study Report, a 2025 presentation by the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), and earlier methodological work on measuring the VAT gap. The analysis distinguishes tax expenditure estimates from potential-versus-actual VAT calculations and from comprehensive VAT-gap measurement. The NBR report estimates total VAT tax expenditure for 2022 at BDT 1,295,701.35 million, equivalent to 3.26% of GDP, compared with net VAT revenue of 2.63% of GDP. CPD's calculations for FY2022–23 report a VAT gap of BDT 188,080.546 crore under an effective-rate scenario of 11.73%. Under a separate 15% standard-rate scenario, potential VAT is reported at BDT 409,357.335 crore; subtracting actual collections produces an arithmetic difference of BDT 277,320.445 crore. However, inconsistencies within the published presentations require caution. These estimates are not directly interchangeable and do not establish how much additional revenue could necessarily be collecte…

title: Large-Area Marine Surface Current Measurement Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle-Based Optical Flow Mosaicking Without Ground Control Points
abstract: Abstract Nearshore ocean currents are characterized by complex structures and spatial heterogeneity. Conventional measurement techniques are either inefficient or offer low spatial resolution, while image velocimetry (a low-cost, high-resolution method) is limited in marine applications due to the trade-off between large-area coverage and high resolution, as well as the lack of ground control points for calibration. To address these issues, this study proposes a current field mosaicking method. By maintaining the camera in constant-speed motion, the distance differences between consecutive image frames are converted into row offsets using the interframe time interval and image resolution, thereby expanding the velocimetry observation range through stitching. An adaptive thresholding method combining sun-glint identification and cropping is also developed. Results show that the picture range increases from 60 to 350 m, enabling large-area optical-flow velocimetry, and that the sun glint removal technique effectively reduces interference without additional quality degradation or artificial signals. This approach solves key constraints of image velocimetry in large-scale marine environments.

title: Pragmatic strategy use in English as a lingua franca in academic settings: evidence from Chinese learners in English for academic purposes
abstract: Abstract The internationalisation of higher education has consolidated English as a lingua franca in academic settings (ELFA) as a principal medium of academic intercultural communication. Research on ELFA interaction increasingly demonstrates that communicative effectiveness depends less upon conformity to standardised linguistic norms than upon speakers’ adaptive deployment of pragmatic strategies to negotiate meaning and sustain interactional coordination in multilingual communication. These interactional realities challenge dominant English for academic purpose (EAP) pedagogies, which continue to privilege form-focused and norm-oriented models of academic communication despite the fluid and collaboratively negotiated character of ELFA interaction. Drawing on approximately 30 h of naturally occurring ELFA study-group discussions involving Chinese MA students and peers from diverse linguacultural backgrounds at a UK university, this study employs conversation analysis supplemented by semi-structured interviews to examine both the situated deployment and developmental trajectories of pragmatic competence in interactions in academic settings. The findings demonstrate that participants effectively mobilised a range of strategies to negotiate understanding, manage communicative contingency, and sustain interactional alignment in real time. Importantly, participants attributed the…

title: Green and simple rrs spectroscopic strategy based on xanthene-based dye; Acid Red 51 for eletriptan quantification in pharmaceuticals and biological samples
abstract: Abstract Eletriptan tablets are a targeted pharmaceutical agent that acts as an agonist for the 5-hydroxytryptamine1 receptor subclassification, mostly employed to alleviate acute migraine episodes. As a member of the triptan class, Eletriptan functions by constricting cerebral blood vessels and decreasing the release of chemicals that cause light and sound sensitivity, nausea, and headache discomfort. Its efficacy in alleviating migraine symptoms makes it a valuable option for individuals seeking rapid and effective relief. A sustainable, rapid, one-pot resonance Resonance Rayleigh Scattering spectrometric technique was created for estimating out Eletriptan in pharmaceutical tablets and biological matrices. Upon mixing Eletriptan with the fluorescent ligand Acid Red 51 in an acidic buffer, a marked increase in resonance Resonance Rayleigh Scattering intensity was immediately observed. This phenomenon was ascribed to the selective formation of an ion-pair complex between the cationic Eletriptan drug and the anionic dye, which amplified the Resonance Rayleigh Scattering signal through enhanced scattering interactions. The RRS intensity showed a straight-line connection with Eletriptan concentration between 50 and 1500 ng/mL, allowing for accurate measurement. Key experimental parameters, including pH, ligand concentration, and buffer volume, were systematically optimized to maxi…

title: Integrating Traditional Occupations into Tertiary Institutions Curricula: A Strategy for Addressing Unemployment and Contemporary Societal Challenges in Nigeria
abstract: Societal challenges such as unemployment, cultural erosion, food insecurity, urban migration, and loss of indigenous knowledge have intensified in the 21st century. This paper examine tertiary institutions curricula and the integrating of traditional occupations such as farming, blacksmithing, weaving, fishing, carving, pottery, farming, dyeing, herbal medicine, as a way to address unemployment and societal problems. The objectives of this study were to; study the conceptual basis for harmonization, proposes four models for integration and to analyzes how such approach addresses unemployment, food insecurity, healthare gap social, identity loss, cultural erosion, loss of indigenous craft, rural-urban migration and loss of indigenous knowledge and skill. Nativism theory propounded by William and Laura is adopted for this research. This paper argues that integrating traditional occupations with tertiary institution curriculum is an act of epistemic decolonization and a pragmatic strategy for solving contemporary societal challenges. Findings shows that traditional occupations that was included in national institutions curricula has been replaced with formal education and is causing alot of societal problems among the youth. The paper concludes that curriulum reform grounded in hybridity and self-determination is necessary for tertiary institutions to become engines of locally rel…

Who Perceives Work Performance Improvements from Generative AI Use in Government, Early-Stage Diffusion? Exploring the Roles of Organizational Power and Motivation on Work Performance
abstract: Abstract This study examines which civil servants perceive performance improvements from using generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and why, drawing on the Ability-Motivation-Opportunity theory and the reinforcement politics model. Using the Korea Institute of Public Administration survey data, we analyzed responses from 1,608 Korean civil servants. Results indicate that civil servants who frequently use generative AI and are intrinsically motivated perceive greater benefits from AI-assisted work than those with organizational power. These findings suggest that, early in the adoption of generative AI tools in government, these tools influence performance by shaping motivation and usage, not hierarchy.

title: Genetic Sovereignty within the System of Functions of Public Authorities: A Doctrinal Model and Transboundary Reality
abstract: This article demonstrates the qualitative impact of the development of genomic technologies on national security, which is leading to the emergence of new functions for government agencies. It is argued that the accumulation of human genetic data, its use for various social purposes, and the growing dependence of personalized medicine on information about human biology have led to the transition of genetics from a fundamental science to a critical factor in state sovereignty. The specific aspects of the sovereignty of human genetic data are highlighted. A comparative legal study of the concept of genetic sovereignty is conducted (using the examples of Mexico and China).

title: Reproductive Rights in Russian Law: The Legal Nature, Classification, and Constitutionalization Issues
abstract: This article examines doctrinal approaches to the concept of reproductive rights and freedoms existing in Russian law. The author analyzes the legal nature of this group of rights and classifies these subjective rights according to various criteria. The article emphasizes the need for specialized legislative regulation of reproductive rights at the level of a consolidated federal law and considers the possibility of constitutionalization through amendments to the Russian Constitution.

title: Issues of the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Analysis and Editing of Genetic Information: Law, Ethics, and Technology
abstract: The article examines legal and ethical aspects of using artificial intelligence (AI) for genome editing, using the example of generating proteins used in genome editing using the CRISPR‑Cas method. It is shown that such proteins can be superior to natural ones, but they contain hundreds of mutations and insertions whose function is unknown, which creates unpredictable risks when they are used in medical practice. The author analyzes possible legal consequences: the liability of medical organizations to patients, the absence of recourse requirements for developers of AI products, the inadequacy of the existing regulation in Russia, and the need to strike a balance between innovation and safety. Measures to minimize risks are proposed, including independent testing, expanded informed consent, the creation of compensation funds, and data transparency.

title: Effects of plyometric training with and without external load on neural adaptations and lower-limb power in male collegiate sprinters
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to explore whether plyometric training with 10% body-mass external load can enhance the intensity of eccentric contractions, induce neuromuscular adaptations, and improve lower-limb power among male collegiate sprinters. Methods Twenty-three male collegiate sprinters were randomly assigned to a weighted plyometric training group (PG-Load, n=8), a bodyweight plyometric training group (PG-BW, n=8), and a control group (CG, n=7) over an 8-week intervention. Both training groups completed 8 weeks of plyometric training (two sessions/week) in addition to regular sprint training, while CG maintained regular training only. The Hoffmann (H-) reflex and M-wave tests, isokinetic strength, tendon elastography, rate of force development (RFD) and 30-m sprint performance were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Results Significant group-by-time interactions were found for Mmax, Hmax/Mmax, H-reflex threshold, M-wave threshold, hamstring concentric/eccentric torque and RFD (all P<0.05). Post-hoc tests showed larger gains in these outcomes within PG-Load relative to PG-BW and/or CG. Quadriceps thickness, patellar tendon stiffness, jump performance, vertical stiffness and 30-m sprint performance improved significantly over time across all groups (all P<0.05). Conclusion Eight weeks of plyometric training improved neuromuscular function and lower-limb power…
