Liquidity And Capital Structure As Determinants Of Profitability (Case Study of Retail Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange 2020-2025 Period)
abstract: Profitability is a key indicator for assessing a company's ability to generate profit. A company's profitability level can be influenced by various factors, including liquidity and capital structure. This study aims to determine the simultaneous and partial effects of liquidity and capital structure on the profitability of retail companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) from 2020 to 2025. A quantitative method with a causal approach was employed. The sample was selected using a purposive sampling technique from retail companies listed on the IDX during the 2020–2025 period; based on established criteria, 14 companies were selected as the study sample. Secondary data obtained from company financial statements were used. Data analysis techniques included descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, panel data regression analysis, the coefficient of determination, t-tests, and F-tests, utilizing EViews 12 software. The results indicate that liquidity and capital structure have a significant simultaneous effect on profitability. Liquidity also has a significant partial effect on profitability. Similarly, capital structure has a significant partial effect on the profitability of retail companies listed on the IDX during the 2020–2025 period. These findings demonstrate that a company's ability to manage liquidity and its capital structure composition influence it…

title: A Multimetallic Single-Atom Catalyst on a Defective Graphene Support toward Methanol Oxidation and Oxygen Reduction Reactions: Density Functional Theory, Machine Learning, and Experiments
abstract: Abstract Multimetallic single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as promising candidates for electrocatalytic reactions. However, identifying bifunctional multimetallic SACs capable of efficiently catalyzing both the oxygen reduction and methanol oxidation reactions (ORR and MOR), applicable to direct methanol fuel cells, remains challenging due to the vast compositional design space. Here, we propose a defective graphene-supported multimetallic SAC (M1M2M3M4M5-SAC) incorporating Mn, Pt, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cu for simultaneous MOR and ORR catalysis. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations along with machine learning (ML) predictions reveal that the Co active site in PtFeNiCoCu-SAC delivers the most favorable performance, exhibiting ORR and MOR overpotentials of 0.47 and 0.46 V, respectively. Guided by these insights, we synthesized PtFeNiCoCu-SAC and a nitrogen-doped sample, confirming their atomic structures using X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Electrochemical measurements validate the theoretical predictions: PtFeNiCoCu-SAC achieves an experimental ORR overpotential of 0.30 VRHE and a Tafel slope of 114 mV/dec at –1 mA/cm2, along with a half-wave potential of 0.86 VRHE. This catalyst also demonstrates good MOR activity, with a pronounced oxidation peak at 0.97 VRHE. Therefore,…

title: TRACE-Net: A Physics-Inspired Geometric Deep Learning Framework for Antibody–Antigen Docking Ranking
abstract: Abstract Elucidating antibody–antigen interactions at atomic resolution is fundamental for therapeutic antibody design. However, accurately discriminating near-native conformations from massive decoy pools remains a critical bottleneck for current high-accuracy structure prediction, as existing scoring functions often fail to capture complex interfacial interactions and monomeric deformation. To address this challenge, we present TRACE-Net, a physics-inspired geometric deep learning framework. TRACE-Net introduces three innovative modules: Context-Aware Edge Feature Recalibration (CEER), Internal Deformation-Aware Gated Fusion (IDGF), and Top-Weighted Combined Ranking Loss (TWCRL). Trained on a comprehensive data set of 1442 complexes, the model effectively reduces geometric noise and quantifies spatial divergence as a structural indicator of localized geometric deformation forced during flexible interface adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that TRACE-Net effectively mitigates the severe ranking inversion of near-native decoys, yielding a competitive improvement in the Top-1 success rate, particularly on challenging targets. Overall, this framework offers a sensitive and informative scoring strategy for assessing predicted structures and advancing computational immunology.

title: Digital storytelling as a tool for social communication in the process of learning English language and literature
abstract: The aim of the study was to identify and theoretically substantiate the socio-communicative potential of digital storytelling in the process of learning English language and literature, taking into account the linguistic, collaborative, multimodal and narrative mechanisms of its pedagogical application. The study was carried out in the format of a structured literature review with a qualitative thematic synthesis. The search for scientific publications was carried out in March–May 2026 in international bibliographic databases with additional verification of bibliographic data and digital identifiers of publications. From 286 initially identified records, after removing duplicates, screening of titles and annotations and full-text evaluation, a corpus of 25 peer-reviewed works from 2022–2026 was formed. Thematic coding revealed that 72.0% of the publications covered language production, 68.0% – socio-communicative interaction, 64.0% – multimodal and narrative mediation, while only 16.0% directly integrated literary material. It was determined that the socio-communicative potential of digital stories is formed through interconnected language production, narrative structuring of content, collective agreement of meanings, multimodal recoding and audience orientation of the message. It was found that the linguistic and collaborative aspects have a much broader evidence base than the…

title: Motivational impact of the OSCE on students’ learning, preparation, and professional development—a qualitative study
abstract: Background The Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) is widely used in nursing education to assess clinical competence, yet its influence on students’ learning processes remains insufficiently explored. Aim This study aimed to explore how first-year nursing students and nurse educators perceive and experience the OSCE's motivational impact on students’ learning, preparation, and professional development. Design The study has an exploratory–descriptive qualitative design with a hermeneutic approach. Method Data were collected at Oslo Metropolitan University (OsloMet) through eight focus group interviews with 41 first-year nursing students, conducted between March and June 2025. In addition, 17 nursing educators who had served as OSCE evaluators participated in individual semi-structured interviews conducted between August and September 2025. All participants had experience as evaluators in one or more OSCE sessions during the 2024–2025 academic year. The analysis was informed by Kvale and Brinkmann's three contexts of interpretation: self-understanding, critical understanding, and theoretical understanding. Results Participants perceived the OSCE as a strong motivator for systematic preparation, repeated skills practise, and engagement with theoretical knowledge and practical procedures. Three main themes were identified: (i) OSCE as a motivator for active preparation…

Characterizing University Students’ Geometric Thinking Through Dialogues with Generative Artificial Intelligence in Geometry Transformation Learning
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has emerged as a promising technology for supporting mathematical dialogue, feedback, and reasoning in mathematics education. However, research has paid limited attention to how university students’ geometric thinking develops through sustained interaction with GenAI, particularly in geometry transformation learning. This study aims to develop a Dialogic Geometric Thinking Framework that characterizes the dimensions and progression of university students’ geometric thinking during sustained dialogue with ChatGPT. A qualitative exploratory design was employed involving undergraduate mathematics education students enrolled in a Geometry Transformation course at an Indonesian public university. Data were collected from student–ChatGPT dialogue transcripts, students’ written solutions, and reflective interviews. The data were analyzed thematically using reflexive thematic analysis to identify recurring characteristics and relationships among dimensions of geometric thinking and to synthesize them into an integrated framework. The findings identified five interrelated dimensions of geometric thinking: conceptual reasoning, representational coordination, procedural justification, reflective regulation, and mathematical elaboration. These dimensions illustrate how students progressively articulate mathematical concepts, coordinate representat…

title: Pengembangan Komponen Modul Ajar Berorientasi Project Based Learning pada Materi Diagram Batang Kelas IV SD
abstract: A needs analysis based on interviews with the fourth-grade teacher at SD Negeri 31 Pontianak Utara indicated that approximately 40% of 27 students had not met the criteria for learning objective attainment (KKTP) and had difficulty distinguishing between the x and y axes when constructing bar charts. This study aims to develop a teaching module oriented toward Project-Based Learning (PjBL) on bar charts and assess the validity of its components. The study employed a research and development method using the 4-D model, limited to the definition, design, and development stages. Data were collected through teacher interviews and validation questionnaires. Quantitative data were analyzed using feasibility percentages, while qualitative data were used to explain needs and inform product revisions. The first validator’s assessment yielded a mean feasibility score of 87%, with percentages of 92% for the general information component, 70% for the core component, and 100% for the appendices. The product was then revised in terms of time allocation, prompting questions, and the alignment of learning activities with the PjBL syntax. The second validator’s assessment yielded a mean feasibility score of 97%, with all components categorized as valid. This study concludes that the components of the PjBL-oriented teaching module met the validity criteria based on the validators’ assessments. T…

title: The Effectiveness of Conventional and Digitally Modified Problem-Based Learning (PBL) on Students’ Understanding of Disaster Mitigation Concepts
abstract: This study aimed to analyze students’ understanding of disaster mitigation concepts through conventional Problem-Based Learning (PBL) and digital media-based modified PBL, as well as compare the effectiveness of both learning models. This quantitative research employed a quasi-experimental method with a nonequivalent control group design involving 60 eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 1 Banawa. Class VIII-B served as the experimental group, while class VIII-C served as the control group. Data were collected using a 40-item concept understanding test, observation, interviews, and documentation. Data analysis involved the Mann-Whitney U test, ANCOVA, Two-Way ANOVA, and N-Gain analysis. The results showed that the control group's mean score increased from 47.67 to 71.67, with an N-Gain of 0.46, while the experimental group's mean score increased from 48.58 to 81.83, with an N-Gain of 0.65. The posttest scores revealed a significant difference between the two groups (U = 149.000; p < 0.001). This difference remained significant after controlling for students' initial abilities (F = 30.70; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.350). Furthermore, the interaction between learning model and measurement time was significant (F = 25.48; p < 0.001). These findings indicate that digital media-based modified PBL is more effective than conventional PBL in improving students' understanding of disaster mitigati…

Assessing learners’ attitudes toward meme-based learning through the technology acceptance model
abstract: Introduction In an era when learners are immersed in a fast-evolving digital culture, education should adopt practices that resonate with learners' characteristics. There is a growing need to examine how emerging tools can support the current generation's learning styles. In this context, internet memes offer a potentially engaging resource for language learning. This study investigates learners' acceptance of meme-based learning in English language education by applying an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Methods A quantitative research design was employed, with data collected from 238 undergraduate ESL learners through a structured questionnaire. The instrument assessed five constructs: perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, attitude towards use, behavioural intention, and positive learning experience. Reliability and regression analyses were performed using SPSS version 25 to examine the proposed relationships among these constructs. Results The findings indicate that all hypothesised relationships are statistically significant. Perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness emerge as significant predictors of learners' attitudes towards meme-based learning. Attitude is significantly associated with behavioural intention, which, in turn, significantly predicts positive learning experience. The findings further indicate that learners perceive memes as meaning…

title: An interpretable machine-learning model for Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome differentiation in ischemic stroke using integrated disease–syndrome features
abstract: Objective To develop and internally validate an interpretable machine-learning model for traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndrome differentiation in ischemic stroke by integrating modern clinical characteristics with TCM-related features. Methods A total of 616 patients with ischemic stroke from a tertiary TCM hospital in Sichuan Province, China, were included. Fifty-one candidate predictors covered demographics, stroke severity, laboratory indices, infarction characteristics, medical history, TCM symptoms, tongue features, and pulse characteristics. Five TCM syndrome classes were considered. Patients were stratified into a training set (n = 495) and a held-out test set (n = 121). Grouped multinomial least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used for feature selection. Random forest (RF), support vector machine with a radial basis function kernel (SVM-RBF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were trained using identical stratified 10-fold cross-validation partitions. Performance was assessed using accuracy, Cohen’s κ, Macro-F1, macro balanced accuracy, Macro AUC, and Hand-Till multiclass AUC, with 95% confidence intervals estimated by 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Model calibration and TreeSHAP-based interpretability were further evaluated for the final model. Results At λ1se = 0.0281, 33 encoded features were retained. In the held-out test set, RF ach…

title: Implementing game-based and quest technologies in secondary school geography: a quasi-experimental study of 7th-grade learning outcomes in Kazakhstan
abstract: The modernization of school education in Central Asia has placed innovative learning technologies at the center of national education policy, yet evidence on how such technologies perform in ordinary classrooms remains scarce. This study examined whether the systematic use of game-based and quest technologies in Grade 7 geography lessons is associated with higher student achievement than conventional instruction. A quasi-experiment with a repeated cross-sectional design was conducted over three academic years (2017–2020) in two state secondary schools in the Zhambyl region of Kazakhstan: a new Grade 7 cohort was assessed in each school at a baseline stage and at two formative stages. The experimental group ( n = 45 per stage, School No. 28 named after A. Moldagulova, Taraz) studied geography through a program of didactic games, educational quests, and interactive tasks embedded in short-term lesson plans, while the control group ( n = 55 per stage, A. Makarenko Secondary School, Zhambyl district) followed the standard curriculum. Achievement was taken from criterion-based assessment and classified into low, medium, and high levels. At baseline the achievement distributions of the two groups were similar [χ 2 (2) = 0.42, p = 0.809]. Across stages, the share of high-achieving students in the experimental group rose from 20.0% to 35.5% (two-sided p = 0.099) and changed little in t…

title: A CNN-LSTM-based Hybrid Deep Learning Model Enhanced with PSO-GA Optimization for Accurate Code Clone Detection
abstract: Code clone analysis is needed when software repositories contain multiple implementations of the same or closely related functionality. Such duplication can make later maintenance harder because a change made in one fragment may not be reflected in another. This paper presents a hybrid CNN–LSTM framework in which PSO and GA are used to refine the feature representation before classification. The workflow consists of source-code preparation, feature construction, optimization, and clone classification. CNN is used to learn local patterns from the code representation, whereas LSTM models dependencies that extend across the sequence. The optimized representation is evaluated on BigCloneBench, Google Code Jam, and a Java repository. The reported experiments show that the combined model provides higher recall, accuracy, and precision than the comparison models. The findings indicate that optimization-assisted deep learning can provide a practical route toward more reliable clone analysis in software repositories.

title: Enhancing DeepIRT through counterfactual item-invariance regularization and joint learning
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) models are widely used in adaptive learning systems to estimate students’ evolving knowledge states. Despite recent advances in deep KT models, many approaches exhibit poor probabilistic calibration, producing overconfident predictions that misrepresent students’ knowledge. This paper presents Counterfactual Item-Invariance Regularized Knowledge Tracing (CIR-KT), a bias-aware approach for calibrated knowledge tracing. For each interaction the method constructs an item-level counterfactual, substituting the presented item while holding the observed response fixed, and enforces consistency between the factual and counterfactual latent states through a regularization objective. By reducing the model’s reliance on item-identity shortcuts, the framework improves probability calibration without altering the underlying KT architecture. On a severely miscalibrated private College of Engineering (COE) subset, counterfactual regularization substantially reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier score and improves ranking (AUC and PR-AUC) relative to the DeepIRT backbone, while on already well-calibrated public benchmarks its effect on discrimination and calibration is small. Skill-level analyses show that the calibration gains are broad-based across knowledge components rather than driven by a few items. These results indicate that item-level counterfactua…

title: A review of predictive maintenance strategies for Industry 5.0: AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to provide a comprehensive review of predictive maintenance (PdM) strategies within the emerging Industry 5.0 paradigm, emphasizing the shift from automation-centric maintenance to human-centric, collaborative systems. The study aims to synthesize model-based, data-driven, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled and hybrid PdM approaches, examine the role of key enabling technologies such as digital twins and edge computing and highlight human–machine collaboration in maintenance decision-making. By proposing a unified taxonomy, the article seeks to identify research gaps and guide the development of resilient, sustainable and explainable PdM systems. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a structured systematic review methodology to analyze PdM strategies in the context of Industry 5.0. Peer-reviewed journal articles, standards and authoritative reports were identified through major scientific databases using predefined keywords related to PdM, condition-based maintenance, AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration. The selected literature was critically examined and classified based on maintenance approach, enabling technologies, deployment architecture and degree of human involvement. Comparative analysis was employed to identify research gaps, challenges and emerging trends, culminating in the development of a novel taxonom…

title: Aprendizaje cooperativo y habilidades sociales en Educación Física escolar: una revisión sistemática
abstract: Physical education has traditionally been conceived as a subject focused on physical performance; this approach creates competitive environments that can lead to exclusion and uncooperative behavior. Recent studies indicate that cooperative learning promotes communication, empathy, and group cohesion which are essential aspects of social skills and has thus become established as an active methodology that places the student at the center of the educational process. This systematic review aimed to analyze the scientific literature on cooperative learning and social skills in school physical education, in order to identify predominant patterns and findings in the literature. The methodology followed the PRISMA guidelines and included studies published between 2021 and 2026 in the following databases: Scopus, ERIC, Redalyc, Scielo, Web of Science, and Dialnet. A total of 175 records were identified, of which 19 studies met the eligibility criteria following the screening and methodological evaluation process. The findings indicate that cooperative learning improves students’ social skills, self-esteem, and emotional well-being. It also promotes educational inclusion, enhances motor and academic performance, and strengthens students’ sense of belonging. In conclusion, cooperative learning represents a promising pedagogical strategy for holistic human development, although experimen…

title: Introduction of Songket Motifs from Four Regions Using Inception V3 Image Embedding and Machine Learning in Orange Data Mining
abstract: Background: Manual identification of songket motifs is time-consuming and requires specialized expertise, limiting the cataloging and documentation of regional textiles. Objective: To develop a songket motif classification system using image embeddings extracted with Inception v3 and machine learning algorithms implemented in Orange Data Mining. Methods: The research dataset comprised 200 images of songket fabrics representing four regional motif categories: Balinese songket, Lombok songket, Palembang songket, and Riau songket, with 50 images per category. Image embeddings were extracted from all images using Inception v3, and the resulting embeddings were used as inputs for several classification models. The classification algorithms evaluated in this study were Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and Neural Network. Results: Logistic Regression achieved the best overall classification performance, with an accuracy of 75%, an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.905, and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.667. Confusion matrix analysis further revealed that Palembang and Riau songket motifs had per-class recall values of 88% and 84%, respectively, whereas Balinese and Lombok songket motifs had the lowest per-class recall values, at 62% and 66%, respectively. Exact prevalence regions: finite-sample uncertainty quantification, threshold decisions, and monitoring for class-prevalence analytics under prior probability shift
abstract: Abstract Many analytics decisions consume class prevalences rather than individual labels: the market share of a sentiment, the case burden of a disease, the drift state of a deployed model. Quantification methods estimate the prevalence vector of an unlabeled batch under prior probability shift, but they return point estimates, and their uncertainty companions, resting on large-sample approximations, resampling, or a prior, carry no finite-sample frequentist guarantee. I introduce exact prevalence regions (EPR): confidence regions obtained by inverting exact Monte Carlo two-sample tests against reference samples drawn from held-out, class-conditional calibration pools. Because prior probability shift makes each null hypothesis exactly simulable, the region is finite-sample valid for any classifier, any permutation-symmetric statistic, and any sample size, marginally over calibration sampling; the exchangeability the test uses is derived from the sampling assumptions, and the cost of its failure under within-batch dependence is measured. The same construction yields exact one-sided tests for threshold decisions and a day-over-day monitoring workflow whose representability alarm flags batches that leave the label-shift family. Across 18 datasets and more than 300,000 evaluation bags, against audited bootstrap, delta-method, and Bayesian baselines, EPR held its nominal level wher…

title: Integrated Technoeconomic Analysis of CO2-EOR from Industrial Sources: Source Comparison, Tax Incentive, and Uncertainty Assessment
abstract: Abstract This study develops an integrated technoeconomic analysis (TEA) framework that places industrial CO2 capture, supercritical-phase pipeline transport, CO2-enhanced oil recovery (CO2-EOR) operations, permanent-storage accounting, and the Section 45Q tax credit on a common CO2 mass basis. A discounted cash flow (DCF) approach is used to calculate the net present value (NPV) of a 25-year project life. Unlike approaches that treat delivered CO2 as a single cost input, the model separates source-dependent capture capital and operating costs, transport infrastructure, gross recycling, net storage, field development, and time-dependent revenues. Reservoir performance is represented for project screening using field-validated performance metrics such as oil recovery ratio, response time, gross-to-net CO2 utilization, and water-alternating-gas (WAG) assumptions rather than compositional reservoir simulation. Following deterministic discounted cash flow (DCF) analysis, the model incorporates one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analysis that quantifies the effects of technical, economic, market, and policy inputs on NPV. The most influential inputs are then propagated through 20,000 Monte Carlo trials using truncated normal distributions to estimate source-specific NPV ranges and probabilities of positive NPV. Performance-Driven Generative Design for Daylighting Optimization in a Tangerang Aerotropolis Office Building
abstract: Daylighting in tropical climates may increase glare risk in office buildings. This issue is particularly relevant in the Tangerang Aerotropolis area, where humid tropical conditions and airport operational safety regulations constrain building development. This study optimized daylighting performance in an office building using a Performance-Driven Generative Design approach. The workflow integrated Rhinoceros 3D, Grasshopper, ClimateStudio, and Galapagos to evaluate six envelopes and building mass variables. The optimization evaluated 950 design alternatives across 18 generations using UDI₁₀₀–₃₀₀₀ as the objective function. A maximum UDI₁₀₀–₃₀₀₀ of 95.5% was achieved with a WWR of 0.47, window height of 2.53 m, shading spacing and depth of 0.40 m, building width of 12 m, and orientation of 76°. Best-performing configurations converged within WWR 0.40–0.47, window height 2.50–2.60 m, shading spacing 0.30–0.50 m, shading depth 0.30–0.40 m, building width 12–13 m, and orientation 72°–84°. The results identified a high-performing configuration and recurring parameter ranges among the best-performing solutions.

Optimization of the SCL-90 scale using machine learning: a novel approach to mental health assessment
abstract: Background Mental health assessment is critical for early intervention and treatment, yet traditional tools like the Symptom Checklist-90 (SCL-90) suffer from redundancy and high respondent burden. This study aims to optimize the SCL-90 using machine learning to enhance assessment efficiency while maintaining agreement with the full-scale SCL-90 screening classification. Methods Nine machine learning algorithms were evaluated via 10-fold cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to rank item importance, and the optimal item count was determined experimentally by a pre-specified one-standard-error rule, yielding a 44-item subset; hyperparameters were tuned with metaheuristic optimization algorithms. All feature-selection and tuning steps were evaluated under a leakage-free nested cross-validation protocol, complemented by a stratified hold-out evaluation, head-to-head comparison with established SCL-90 short forms, and psychometric analyses. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, and f1 score. Results The baseline LGBM model achieved the highest F1 score of 0.9413. Under the original full-data evaluation protocol, the GWO-optimized SHAP-XGB model reached an F1 of 0.9501. title: Ergonomic chair parameter optimization based on user prototype recognition and improved genetic algorithm
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop a data-driven ergonomic chair design framework that improves multi-parameter chair design for user groups with heterogeneous anthropometric characteristics. Design/methodology/approach Large-scale anthropometric data from the Anthropometric Survey of US Army Personnel (ANSUR) II database are clustered using K-means to identify representative user prototypes. Prototype-specific ideal seat parameters are then de-rived according to ergonomic principles. To solve the resulting multi-prototype optimization problem, an improved genetic algorithm (IC2GA) is proposed by integrating a clearing mechanism and a crowding replacement strategy, enabling joint optimization of multiple chair parameters while preserving solution diversity. Findings The proposed method achieved a mean comfort score of 74.00 ± 0.02 across multiple independent repeated experiments, and showed a computational efficiency of 18.89 ± 8.41 s. Ablation analysis shows that introducing prototype identification increased the comfort score from 64.96 ± 0.49 to 73.46 ± 0.06, indicating that modelling user diversity was the primary reason for the performance improvement. Prototype matching analysis further demonstrates that the mean own-other difference is 21.38, confirming that continuous improvement at the individual level is stable. An Optimized Ensemble Intrusion Detection Framework with Hybrid Feature Selection and Multi-Dataset Validation
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) play a vital part in protecting modern communication networks against many classy cyberattacks. But the existing intrusion detection methods suffer from problems including data imbalance, redundant features, and poor performance in various network environments. Hence, this work presents a optimized ensemble Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on comprehensive data preprocessing, hybrid feature selection, and ensemble learning techniques to improve intrusion detection performance. To enhance the data quality and class balance, the proposed framework includes missing value handling, outlier removal, noise filtering and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). A hybrid feature selection method, which combines the Mutual Information (MI) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), is used to identify the most useful network traffic features. Then, an attack classification ensemble model is constructed using Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). This framework is tested on the CICIDS2017 and UNSW-NB15 datasets via 5-fold cross-validation, and its performance is measured by standard classification metrics. Additionally, explainability using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is integrated to enhance the interpretability of the model prediction. The experimental results show that the p…

title: TPU Accelerated Multi-Resolution and Occupancy based Performance Analysis of Embedded Real-Time Traffic Sign Detection on Raspberry Pi 5
abstract: Embedded traffic-sign detection must balance accuracy against the compute, memory and power limits of the target platform. This study evaluates YOLOv8n on TT100K at six independently trained input resolutions (640×640, 512×512, 480×480, 320×320, 224×224 and 160×160) and on three platform configurations: an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 laptop GPU, a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU and a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Google Coral USB Edge TPU. Validation accuracy decreased monotonically from 0.812 mAP@50 at 640×640 to 0.088 at 160×160. By contrast, measured Edge TPU throughput remained between 87.70 and 89.33 FPS, so downsampling produced no meaningful throughput gain on the evaluated configuration while substantially reducing accuracy. Normalized sign occupancy was then related to recall for all 7,471 annotations in the test subset. Recall increased from 20.50% below 0.005% occupancy to 98.17% above 0.10%, with a transition region between approximately 0.02% and 0.05% observed for this dataset and model configuration. The combined analysis provides a platform-specific basis for selecting input resolution and camera geometry.

Multi-cohort and single-cell multi-omic analyses reveal multicellular mechanotransduction–immune remodeling in rheumatoid arthritis synovium
abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovitis integrates immune-cell recruitment, stromal remodeling and persistent inflammation, but its relationship with tissue mechanotransduction remains unclear. We investigated whether RA involves coordinated remodeling of multicellular mechanotransduction–immune programs. Methods We constructed a 327-gene mechanotransduction compendium and used GSE89408 synovial transcriptomes from healthy controls (n = 28), patients with osteoarthritis (n = 22) and patients with RA (n = 152) for discovery. Candidates prioritized through RA-versus-Healthy and RA-versus-OA contrasts were evaluated in three patient-independent cohorts using validation-only random-effects meta-analysis. Co-expression networks, consensus clustering, locked external mapping, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell–cell communication inference, virtual knockout and single-cell chromatin-accessibility analyses (11 RA donors and one OA reference; no healthy controls) resolved network, cellular and regulatory contexts. Selected gene-expression findings were examined by quantitative PCR in independent healthy (n = 20) and RA (n = 25) synovial tissues and by overexpression and siRNA-mediated knockdown in synovial fibroblasts. title: Study on teaching practices of etiquette education: fostering cultural sensitivity among multi-ethnic college students
abstract: The increasing ethnic and cultural diversity of higher education requires pedagogical approaches that develop not only knowledge but also cultural sensitivity and ethical cross-cultural interaction. This study examined teaching practices in etiquette education and changes in students' cultural sensitivity during participation in a general education course at a multi-ethnic higher education institution. The study employed a single-group pre-test–post-test design integrating quantitative data with reflective qualitative evidence. A total of 82 undergraduate students participated in the course, while the paired quantitative analysis included 32 students with complete and matchable pre-test and post-test questionnaire data. Qualitative data were obtained through structured interviews with 12 participants, learning documents, student reflections, and mind maps produced at the beginning and end of the course. The data were analyzed using thematic and content analyses, natural language processing for concept visualization, descriptive statistics, and paired-samples t-tests . The findings showed that students reported higher post-test scores across all questionnaire items, with statistically significant changes primarily in intercultural interaction skills, communication confidence, sensitivity to subtle social implications, and positive feedback. The qualitative evidence also indicate…

In what ways does general practice align with trauma-informed care: a multi-method qualitative study
abstract: Abstract Background Healthcare policies and guidelines recommend implementing trauma-informed care, but how best to embed it in general practice is not yet known. General practice readiness to implement trauma-informed care depends on whether this can fit into the existing ways of working. This study aimed to explore where general practice is regarding trauma-informed care implementation and what are the enabling and constraining factors. Methods Informed by the frameworks for trauma-informed care and implementation, we conducted an exploratory qualitative study in four general practices in southwest England. Data from 17 documents, 12 hours of observations, and 43 semi-structured interviews with patients and healthcare providers were analysed thematically. Results We developed four themes: realise, recognise, respond, resist retraumatisation; safe physical and psychological environments for all; opportunities for choice and collaboration; empowering patients. The focus of trauma-informed care on addressing structural and systemic violence matched general practice’s mission of supporting disadvantaged communities and commitment to social justice. We found examples of trauma-informed care implemented by individual providers and at a clinic for patients with multiple disadvantage. However, these examples existed alongside individual providers, services and organisations that had …

title: In-transit temperature deviations and arrival quality in the South Africa–Middle East orange export cold chain
abstract: Background: Temperature fluctuations during refrigerated transport accelerate citrus deterioration, increasing physiological damage, decay and quality loss. Controlled studies may not capture cumulative commercial exposure and disruption. This study examines associations between historical in-transit temperature deviations and arrival quality in a commercial export corridor. Objectives: The study characterised in-transit temperature deviations and their association with arrival quality in the South Africa–Middle East orange export corridor. Method: A quantitative retrospective design linked 2023–2025 proprietary shipment data, container temperatures and receiver-reported quality outcomes for 252 export containers. Logistic regression assessed associations between in-transit deviations and arrival quality, with alternative model specifications used as robustness checks. Results: Peel pitting increased from 24.1% in 2023 to 71.3% in 2025, whereas rind breakdown and decay declined. Peel pitting was consistently associated with year, departure-port group and transit duration. Temporal and port factors largely explained rind breakdown; temperature effects were inconsistent. Decay remained prevalent, although model instability constrained inference. Transit duration was the most reliable positive predictor. Extended analyses confirmed these patterns. Conclusion: Operational condition…

title: Redefining senior workforce management: challenges, opportunities and strategic pathways
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify and analyse the emerging challenges that will shape the development of senior talent in the coming years and, crucially, to provide a multi-level and context-sensitive framework for interpreting these challenges responsibly. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative–computational design combining collective artificial intelligence (CAI) with a two-stage analytical process involving 306 Spanish management staff. A theoretical framework integrates structural, organisational and individual perspectives (theory of ageism, human capital theory, theory of social capital, theory of cognitive ageing and a variety of psychosocial approaches). CAI algorithms (conceptual stratification, semantic clustering, hybridisation and pairwise comparison) enable the aggregation, synthesis and prioritisation of expert judgements. Findings The findings reveal two main areas of challenge: (1) ensuring that senior employees adapt and remain essential in organisational transformation – addressing issues of strategy, motivation, roles, digitalisation and humility – and (2) enabling them to feel valued and to pass on their legacy, which involves addressing knowledge transfer, recognition, ageism, rewards and work–life balance. This study highlights the most widely supported initiatives and the differences found based on gender, age and professional pro…

First-line management of post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathic pain: objective consensus analysis reveals marked heterogeneity among international expert centers
abstract: Background: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathic pain (PTNP) lacks disease-specific treatment guidance, and how experienced clinicians select first-line management remains unclear. We aimed to quantitatively characterize real-world decision-making for first-line treatment of PTNP in patients meeting International Classification of Orofacial Pain criteria. Methods: Nineteen experts from dedicated secondary and tertiary care centers worldwide were invited; 13 provided detailed management strategies. Their responses were converted into anonymized decision trees and analyzed using the Objective Consensus Method, which compares recommendations across all possible combinations of predefined clinical parameters. Similar criteria and treatments were grouped into broader categories to enable cross-comparability. Results: Thirteen decision-criteria categories were identified. Comparison of all submitted strategies yielded 35 distinct clinical scenarios. Limited agreement (54%) was reached in only 6 scenarios, whereas no agreement was observed for the remaining scenarios. Topical treatment was favored in selected patients without imaging evidence of injury and with superficial, localized pain, whereas a slight majority of experts chose surgical intervention for selected patients after mandibular third molar surgery with imaging evidence of nerve injury and a positive diagnostic block. title: Human-centred lean management practices, employee involvement and innovative performance in SMEs: evidence from an emerging economy
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to evaluate how small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies continue to face pressure to innovate due to intense competition, changing customer expectations and resource constraints. Although lean management practices are widely adopted to improve operational efficiency, their role in enhancing innovative performance remains insufficiently understood, particularly in SMEs where human and organisational factors are often overlooked. This study examines the relationships between human-centred lean management practices (HLMPs) and innovative performance and the mediating role of employee involvement among employees in Nigerian SMEs. Design/methodology/approach Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 314 employees across 45 SMEs and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings Customer focus, employee training and small group problem solving are significantly and positively associated with innovative performance, whereas top management leadership shows no significant direct association with innovative performance. All four HLMPs are significantly associated with employee involvement, with employee involvement mediating the relationships between top management leadership and small group problem solving with innovative performance. Practical implications The findings suggest that SMEs seeking to st…

Ultra-high voltage transmission and corporate ESG performance: evidence from Chinese A-share listed firms
abstract: Whether large-scale clean-energy infrastructure can alleviate the trade-off between economic growth and environmental degradation is central to environmental regulation under China's dual-carbon goals. This study examines the relationship between ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission access and corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance using firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed companies with valid Sino-Securities ESG ratings from 2009 to 2022. We estimate a two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences model with firm and year fixed effects, complemented by the Callaway–Sant’Anna staggered DID estimator. Firms gaining UHV access exhibit higher ESG scores, with the largest point estimate observed for the environmental dimension and smaller positive estimates for the social and governance dimensions. The positive UHV-ESG association persists after accounting for local carbon-market exposure and is also observed under alternative ESG specifications and propensity-score-matched DID estimation. Mechanism estimates are consistent with production resilience, including liquidity buffers, and reduced transition risk as two potential channels. Subgroup estimates are larger for smaller firms and firms in other classified industries, with formal coefficient-difference tests indicating cross-group variation, while positive relationships are observed in…

title: Literary Stylistics of Mother-Daughter Trauma Transmission in Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen and Eniola Lateefat's A Broken Bird
abstract: Female gender, whether young or adult, married or single experiences trauma in various facets of their lives; research has established that they even transmit it to unborn generations. In a bid to wade into the root cause and profer possible solutions on how to manage it, this study examines the representation of the intergenerational transmission of trauma through the mother-daughter dyad in two Nigerian novels: Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen and Eniola Lateefat's A Broken Bird. Employing a qualitative content analysis approach informed by feminist trauma theory and African feminist criticism as pronounced by Herman (1992) and Brown (1995), the study analyses twenty purposively selected textual samples (ten from each novel) that represent emotional and mental traumatization. The trauma areas investigated include shame, grief, cognitive dissonance, and suicidal ideation. The analysis revealed that both texts represent the mother-daughter relationship as a primary vector for the transmission of trauma across generations, through mechanisms including maternal socialisation into gendered inferiority, the internalisation of maternal judgment, and the failure of substitute mother-figures. The study also identified moments of resistance and potential interruption of the intergenerational cycle. In conclusion, the experiences of protagonists Adah and Bola in the two novels are …

title: Insider threat detection: a socio-technical analysis of behavioural pathways in malicious insider fraud
abstract: Purpose Cybersecurity is inherently interdisciplinary, yet insider threats are often examined through technical or behavioural lenses in isolation. This paper aims to focus on fraud committed by malicious insiders and aims to improve the understanding of how such attacks develop, thereby enhancing detection and prevention. Design/methodology/approach A novel methodological approach is adopted, integrating grounded theory (GT) with behaviour sequence analysis (BSA) to examine socio-technical events. This enables identification of key indicators and the temporal pathways leading to insider fraud. Findings The findings caution against assuming a single, distinct fraudster profile. Within the cases examined, individuals involved in fraud sometimes engaged in other forms of insider misconduct, including intellectual property theft. The results question established frameworks, such as the fraud triangle, by demonstrating the complexity and dynamic nature of insider fraud. In several cases, information concerning offending or intent was communicated through online or face-to-face interactions. The pattern warrants further investigation, as a potential source of detection using natural language processing methods. Practical implications Drawing on situational prevention theory, the paper offers recommendations for organisations, including strengthening access controls and promoting tra…

title: The reasons for the self-control bias of investors in the Pakistan stock exchange and the degree of its growth
abstract: Purpose This study is conducted with the purpose of investigating the causes of investors’ self-control bias in Pakistan’s stock market and to build a scale on it so that the research can be operationalized in the future. The study aims to identify potential precursors of self-control bias and to characterize the extent to which each precursor contributes to its development among Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) investors during the investment decision-making process. The self-control bias is a state in which people show a lack of ability to control their emotions. The study’s first section consists of semi-structured interviews with stock market experts. Expert responses based on semi-structured dialogues with investors are then approved, and NVivo is used on the main findings to create a word cloud that can be used to identify specific self-control bias precursors. The measures’ context and content validity are also checked by having five language experts and five market experts approve each measure in turn. In Section 2, the self-developed scale is floated to perform the following tests: the Bartlett’s sphericity test to verify item correctness; the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) test to assess sample size; an exploratory factor analysis to reduce overloading items based on outlier detection; and a check for outliers. To examine the inter-item association between items and create a m…

title: Evaluating the Impact of Non-Financial Incentives on Employee Productivity in Nigeria's Manufacturing Industry
abstract: Non-financial incentives remain underexplored as productivity drivers in Nigeria's manufacturing sector, where wage-based interventions have produced inconsistent outcomes. This study examines how employee recognition, training and skill development, participative decision-making, and work environment quality influence employee productivity, with job security as a moderating variable. Existing literature concentrates on banking, education, and public administration, leaving manufacturing-specific empirical evidence scarce and cross-construct moderating analysis largely absent. A quantitative cross-sectional survey collected data from 302 employees across ten Lagos State manufacturing firms, analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling. Training and skill development exerted the strongest effect on productivity (β=0.267, p<0.001), followed by work environment quality (β=0.213), employee recognition (β=0.184), and participative decision-making (β=0.156). Job security significantly moderated all relationships, with the model explaining 62.7% of productivity variance. Manufacturing firms should prioritise structured capability development programs within stable employment frameworks to achieve sustainable productivity gains. Therefore, Manufacturing firms should invest in structured training programs and transparent recognition systems, supported by stable emp…

title: Financial Management Practices of Micro and Small Business in Laoag City
abstract: This study determined the financial management practices of micro and small businesses in Laoag City in terms of financial planning, financing decision, working capital management, and capital budgeting. It also tested whether practices differ significantly between micro and small businesses and proposed strategic recommendations. A descriptive quantitative design was used, with business owners selected through convenience sampling. Data were gathered using a survey questionnaire patterned after Parilla (2013) and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and a t-test. Most of the businesses were small enterprises (90.9%), and most were sole proprietorships (85.6%) that had operated for one to three years (68.2%). Micro businesses highly practiced financial management overall (mean = 3.26), but only moderately practiced financing decision (3.12) and capital budgeting (3.14). Small businesses highly practiced all four areas (overall mean = 3.51). The difference between the two groups was significant (t = -3.56, p = .001), which the authors attribute to small businesses’ greater manpower, assets, and income. The study recommends financial literacy training and orientation for owners, and the adoption of sound, computer-aided accounting practices.

title: Alaali Investment Risk-Return Model (AIRRM): An Integrated Multi-Dimensional Measure of Risk-Adjusted Investment Performance
abstract: Introduction: Conventional risk-adjusted performance measures provide transparent mechanisms for relating investment returns to risk but typically represent risk through selected dimensions such as total volatility or systematic market exposure. Although subsequent literature has incorporated additional dimensions, including downside and liquidity risks, these developments remain distributed across specialized measurement approaches. This leaves an integration gap concerning the joint representation of market, liquidity, operating, financial, and macroeconomic risks within a single performance measure. Methods: This study develops the Alaali Investment Risk-Return Model (AIRRM), a multidimensional risk-adjusted performance measure integrating market exposure, liquidity risk, earnings instability, financial leverage, and macroeconomic risk. Heterogeneous inputs are transformed into bounded and comparable components and aggregated using a transparent baseline equal-weight specification. The model is examined through an illustrative numerical application, comparison with conventional risk-adjusted measures, and sensitivity and stress analysis. Results: The numerical application demonstrates that AIRRM generates differentiated investment rankings when multiple risk dimensions are considered simultaneously. Stress analysis shows internally consistent behavior: increases in individua…

title: Patent Foramen Ovale in Adults With Right-to-Left Shunting: Clinical Significance, Diagnosis, and Contemporary Management
abstract: During fetal development, the foramen ovale is an important component of normal fetal circulation, allowing oxygenated blood to bypass the nonfunctional fetal lungs and supporting fetal growth and development. After birth, incomplete fusion of the septum primum and septum secundum may result in a persistent patent foramen ovale (PFO), which is present in approximately 25% of adults. Although most individuals remain asymptomatic, PFO has been recognized as an important contributor to paradoxical embolism and cryptogenic ischemic stroke. The clinical significance of PFO depends not only on its presence, but also on patient characteristics and anatomical features that influence the likelihood of right-to-left shunting and embolic events. High-risk morphology characteristics, including a large interatrial communication, elongated tunnel length, and prominent Eustachian valve or Chiari network, are associated with increased embolic potential. Advances in multimodality imaging, particularly contrast transesophageal echocardiography, have improved the diagnosis and anatomical characterization of PFO, while risk stratification tools such as the Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (RoPE) score and the PASCAL classification are important tools when determining whether a PFO is likely to be causally related to ischemic stroke. Treatment options for PFO are also largely related to the risk and mo…

title: Auditing information leakage and predictive signal in financial machine learning: a controlled study
abstract: This study audits a financial machine learning pipeline designed to detect information leakage, the absence of predictive structure, and the recovery of a known signal. The evaluation uses a controlled financial benchmark comprising 1,304 business-day dates, nine sector-specific asset series, and seven economic indicators generated through a prespecified GARCH-like conditional-variance process with controlled factor exposures. Three base models, a long short-term memory network (LSTM), a simplified attention model, and XGBoost, together with a fixed-weight ensemble are evaluated after correcting an initial configuration in which contemporaneous predictors were mechanically related to the target. All cross-model comparisons use a common sequential asset-date test subset ( N = 1, 476). Under the leakage-free, null-signal condition, the evaluated configurations yield mean R 2 values between −0.0052 and 0.0000 and directional accuracies between 49.53 and 49.95%. Moving-block bootstrap intervals for directional accuracy, based on blocks of consecutive test dates while retaining all assets within each sampled date, include both the balanced 50% reference and the observed majority-class rate for all evaluated models. Explicit sample accounting distinguishes the raw tabular test partition ( N = 1, 755 asset-date rows), the complete-case tabular sample used for XGBoost/SHAP analysis ( N…

Tail risk spillover asymmetry across global financial markets: a quantile connectedness approach
abstract: Cross-market tail risk spillovers threaten global financial stability, yet most studies examine risk contagion within individual asset classes or a limited set of markets. This study investigates tail risk spillover effects across five major financial market categories—equities, bonds, commodities, foreign exchange (FX), and money markets (short-term interbank interest rates)—in 12 economies from 2 January 2008 to 31 December 2024. Principal Component Analysis is first applied to reduce high-dimensional market data into representative factors, which are then modeled using Quantile Vector Autoregression to estimate spillover intensity at different conditional quantiles ( τ = 0.05 , 0.50 , 0.95 ) . The results reveal a clear asymmetry: under normal conditions ( τ = 0.50 ) , cross-market spillovers remain weak (total connectedness index around 16%), whereas under extreme downside conditions ( τ = 0.05 ) , spillover intensity rises sharply (total connectedness index exceeding 87%). Bootstrap inference shows that the money market’s net absorber position under extreme downside conditions and the commodity market’s net transmitter position under extreme upside conditions are the only market-level net positions statistically distinguishable from zero, whereas the difference between the two tail connectedness levels is not. In contrast, during extreme upside conditions ( τ = 0.95 ) , th…

title: From Resource Allocation to Mobility Outcomes: Examining the Role of Strategic Financial Configuration in Nairobi’s Urban Transport System
abstract: Effective urban mobility requires more than the availability of financial resources; it also depends on how funds, grants and debt are planned, allocated, monitored and aligned with transport priorities. Anchored in the Resource-Based View and complemented by Resource Orchestration Theory, this study examined the association between strategic financial resource configuration, defined as the deliberate structuring of fund, grant and debt resources, and perceived urban mobility outcomes (safety, reliability and efficiency) in Nairobi City, Kenya. A positivist, cross-sectional descriptive correlational survey design was used. The target population comprised 765 organisational actors in 25 public, private and international development institutions. A sample of 263, computed with Yamane’s formula, was allocated proportionally across the three stakeholder strata, and respondents within strata were selected purposively. Of 220 returned questionnaires (83.7%), 214 usable responses were analysed in SPSS version 30 using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple linear regression. Financial resource configuration showed a moderate-to-strong positive association with urban mobility outcomes (r = .635, p < .001) and accounted for 40.4% of their variance, F(1, 212) = 143.42, p < .001; B = 0.352, 95% CI [0.295, 0.409]. Planning, allocation, accountability and monitoring practice…

title: Financial Inclusion and Financial Empowerment among Women in Baringo County, Kenya
abstract: Financial inclusion is gaining consideration for its possibility to foster financial development and promote inclusive growth and income equality. New financial services designed specifically for women are frequently the focus of efforts to reduce gender disparities in financial inclusion. Women's contact to high-quality financial services is critical to economic growth because it enables families to improve their standard of living. This study’s purpose was to examine the connections amongst women's financial empowerment in Baringo County, Kenya, financial access, the qualityand the use of financial services. Using a descriptive research design and a positivist philosophy, Economic and system theory were used to. Women who were registered with women's groups and key informants like representatives from financial institutions, area chiefs, and the Baringo County Social Services department made up the target population. Information was gathered utilizing organized polls and key witness interviews, utilizing straightforward irregular testing to choose members. The aim of the research was academic, and participants participated voluntarily. Information investigation included information altering, coding, order, classification, and show involving Measurable Bundle for Sociologies (SPSS). Descriptive statistics likefrequency distributions, percentages, and proportions were used to s…

title: The Impact of Big Data Technology on Financial Performance through Operational Efficiency of Telecommunication Companies
abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of Big Data Technology on financial performance, its impact on operational efficiency, the influence of operational efficiency on financial performance, and the role of operational efficiency in mediating these relationships. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing secondary data specifically financial statements, annual reports, and stock price data from four telecommunications companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2019 -2024 period. Sampling was conducted using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics and Partial Least Squares -Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. The results indicate that Big Data Technology has a positive and significant impact on operational efficiency, with a coefficient of 0.920 and a p-value below 0.001. However, the impact of Big Data Technology on financial performance is not significant (p-value 0.626), nor is the influence of operational efficiency on financial performance (p-value 0.848). The indirect effect of Big Data Technology on financial performance through operational efficiency is also statistically insignificant (p-value 0.849). This study concludes that while Big Data Technology is associated with operational efficiency, its role in enhancing financial performance either directly or through a mediating mechanism has …

title: Keeping community sport afloat: a national survey of the costs and financial strain of Australian community sports clubs
abstract: Introduction Community sport clubs are central to participation systems, yet tight fiscal environments may constrain their ability to deliver affordable sport. The “cost of sport” is often examined from the participant perspective, however less is known about the cost of delivering community sport and financial strain of clubs. Research question: What are the costs to deliver local community sports clubs in Australia? Methods Clubs reported financial position, income sources, expenditure categories, perceived cost pressures, recent changes in operating costs, registration fee options, volunteer and participation trends, and the presence of paid staff and player payments. The resource and capacity theories—Capacity to Serve, Resource-Based View, and Resource Dependency Theory were used as a lens for investigation and discussion. An online survey was conducted in collaboration with the Australian Sports Commission between October and December 2024. The survey was sent to National Sporting Organisations and National Sporting Organisations for people with a disability encouraging distribution to their associated community sports clubs and advertised through social media and a marketing campaign. Results A total of 2,659 clubs from all eight Australian States and Territories and 83 different sports were represented. Overall, 28% of clubs reported operating at a deficit, with deficit…

title: Financial strength and ESG participation: evidence from Thailand's tax-incentivized ESG policy
abstract: Purpose This study reconceptualizes the environmental, social and governance (ESG)–finance nexus from an outcome-driven to an enabler-driven perspective by examining financial capacity as a boundary condition for sustainability participation. Using Thailand's 2023 tax-incentivized ESG policy as a natural experiment, the paper argues that institutional incentives alone are insufficient to drive adoption if firms fall below a critical financial resource threshold. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on institutional and resource orchestration theories, the study investigates the relationship between financial performance indicators and ESG rating attainment for 610 Thai publicly listed firms. Using Welch's analysis of variance and regression models, it identifies specific financial gatekeepers – grouped into valuation, profitability, liquidity and asset management dimensions – that determine a firm's ability to achieve recognition under the Stock Exchange of Thailand ESG (SETESG) rating framework. Findings The results show that firms with stronger profitability and valuation metrics – particularly return on assets, earnings per share and price-to-book value – were significantly more likely to obtain ESG ratings. Financially weaker firms remained largely excluded, revealing a sustainability gap that highlights the unequal effects of market-based policy interventions. Practical imp…

title: A hybrid graph attention network and proximal policy optimization framework for adaptive fog-cloud offloading and frameproof-based secure IoT data transmission
abstract: Introduction Internet of Things (IoT) applications require secure, low-latency data transmission in resource-constrained environments. Conventional cryptographic security is computationally intensive, and static scheduling adapts poorly to changing IoT-Fog-Cloud conditions. Methods A hybrid Graph Attention Network-Proximal Policy Optimization (GAT-PPO) framework is proposed. The IoT-Fog-Cloud infrastructure is modeled as a dynamic graph, from which GAT learns topology-aware node embeddings. A PPO agent uses these embeddings, together with task urgency, battery level, resource availability and task sensitivity, to select fog or cloud nodes for offloading. For high-sensitivity tasks, a lightweight frameproof combinatorics-based verification mechanism integrated with SHA-256 hashing is activated, and its outcome is incorporated into the PPO reward. The framework was implemented in Python and evaluated in a simulated fog-cloud environment using tasks derived from TON_IoT network traffic, over 10 independent runs. Results The framework achieved an average latency of 68.2 ± 0.7 ms, energy consumption of 31.5 ± 0.4 mJ/task, throughput of 912 ± 9.8 tasks/s, packet delivery ratio of 98.7 ± 0.3% and security success rate of 98.9 ± 0.2%, outperforming the Without GAT, GCN-PPO and GAT-DQN configurations (Welch's t-test, p < 0.001). Under representative attacks, the false acceptance rate…

title: Systematic Evaluation of Membrane Materials and Process Design Trade-offs for Hydrogen Deblending
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen can play an important role as a fuel or feedstock in various industries, but transportation of hydrogen is challenging. Hydrogen blending with natural gas in existing natural gas pipelines can leverage the existing infrastructure to expand access to hydrogen for unconventional end uses. However, this approach would require on-point separation technologies to deblend the hydrogen from natural gas. This study evaluates the performance of 224 membrane materials, including polymers and carbon molecular sieves, for purity and required area in a single-stage system for hydrogen deblending. A two-stage membrane cascade is optimized for recovery of a target purity, and the costs of hydrogen recovery are estimated. We demonstrate that fuel-grade A hydrogen can be deblended at $0.320 kg–1 H2, but with a recovery of 84%. The costs are found to be most sensitive to the electricity cost and the cost of annualization of capital expenditures. Compared with other hydrogen transport options, the blending–deblending approach is economically favorable for long-distance H2 delivery.

title: Absent Partners – Artificial Allies
abstract: Collaboration between researchers and practitioners is central to Educational Design Research (EDR). However, epistemic-temporal misalignments as well as power-dependency relations frequently impede such collaboration, particularly in projects addressing technology-rich educational contexts. This paper examines these collaboration challenges as a constitutive part of EDR rather than as contingent implementation problems. Drawing on Actor-Network Theory (ANT), the paper reconceptualises collaboration as an emergent effect of socio-material networks where technologies are not treated as neutral tools but as actors. Against this backdrop, it explores how generative artificial intelligence (genAI) might strengthen research-practice interactions by assuming specific collaborative functions in situations where human participation is constrained or unevenly resourced. Through two constructed scenarios situated in school contexts, the paper illustrates how genAI could formalise tacit knowledge or provisionally represent absent stakeholders within EDR networks. Rather than positioning genAI as a substitute for human collaboration, the paper argues that genAI-enhanced collaboration may contribute to the stabilisation and extension of collaborative relations within EDR networks. In doing so, it advances a theoretically grounded and methodologically transferable perspective on AI integrati…

title: Stakeholder influence on cost performance of riverine construction projects in the Nigerian Niger Delta: evidence from completed public intervention projects
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how stakeholder actions influence the cost performance of riverine construction projects in Nigeria’s Niger Delta region, with emphasis on governance practices, contractor conduct, environmental disturbances, community engagement, and broader contextual risk management. The research makes a clear distinction between cost performance and cost overruns by defining cost performance as the degree to which actual expenditure aligns with the approved budget, while cost overruns specifically refer to expenditure that exceeds the approved completion estimate or baseline. The assessment is based on archival project records comparing initial and final project costs, as well as documentary evidence linking the relationship between stakeholder actions and observable cost outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative archival research design drawing on documentary evidence from 48 completed public intervention projects carried out by intervention agencies as well as stakeholder-related data involving 57 stakeholders. Project cost records, attendance sheets, and meeting reports were carefully analyzed to determine how stakeholder actions such as contract re-awards, redesigns, pending payments, contractor conduct, and community disruptions influenced project cost performance. The analysis combined archival cost data with stakeholder documentation u…

title: Design, Synthesis, and Herbicidal Activity of Coumarin-3-Acetamide Derivatives as Potential Transketolase Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract Transketolase (TKL; EC 2.2.1.1) has been confirmed to be a promising new herbicide target. In this study, two series of the coumarin-based compounds 12a–12j and 13a–13m were designed and synthesized based on TKL as the new target. Among them, compound 12c could significantly inhibit the activity of SvTKL (IC50: 0.96 μmol/L) in vitro. Notably, compound 12c exhibited inhibitory effects of over 90% against D. sanguinalis and A. retroflexus higher than those of the positive control (inhibition < 80%) at 375 g a.i./ ha via the pot spraying method. Additionally, compound 12c exhibited good safety (injury rate <10%) for wheat and maize at 375 g a.i./ha. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation studies indicated that compound 12c has a strong binding ability and dynamic stability with SvTKL. Furthermore, ARG598 may contribute to the stabilization of 12c within the SvTKL active pocket. These findings establish coumarin-fusaric acid derivatives as promising leads for new herbicide development.

title: Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation to Multicarbon Products: Mechanisms, Catalyst Design, and Scale Demonstration
abstract: Abstract Photothermal CO 2 hydrogenation to multicarbon products presents a promising route to mitigate global climate change while simultaneously generating valuable C 2+ products for industrial use. However, realizing high activity and selectivity toward multicarbon products remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the intricate nature of reactant activation and the inherently sluggish kinetics of C−C coupling. This review elucidates the fundamental principles of photothermal catalysis, with a particular focus on the synergistic interplay between light and thermal energy. In addition, the activation pathways of CO 2 to C 1 intermediates and the subsequent mechanisms of C−C bond formation leading to multicarbon products are systematically examined. On this basis, catalyst design and modification strategies are categorized to enhance reactant activation and facilitate efficient C−C coupling. Furthermore, recent progress in pilot-scale demonstrations is highlighted to showcase the potential for scalable and sustainable CO 2 hydrogenation technologies. By addressing the current challenges and outlining future research directions, this review aims to accelerate the development of efficient photothermal processes for CO 2 valorization.

title: Field-evaluated constitutive modeling of Nanning silty clay for excavation above existing metro tunnels: implications for resource-efficient design
abstract: Reliable prediction of soil and structural deformation is important not only for safety but also for resource-efficient underground construction. Excessively conservative constitutive modeling may lead to unnecessary use of retaining, bracing, and cementitious ground-improvement materials, whereas underestimated deformation can result in infrastructure damage and resource-intensive remediation. In this study, parameters for the Modified Cam-Clay (MCC), Hardening Soil (HS), and Hardening Soil with small-strain stiffness (HSS) models were determined for silty clay sampled at the investigated site in Nanning, China, using laboratory tests on undisturbed samples, in situ shear-wave velocity measurements, and empirical correlations. The three parameter sets were then implemented in PLAXIS 2D to simulate a representative excavation section above existing twin metro tunnels, and the calculated responses were compared with field monitoring data. The MCC and HS models reproduced the overall deformation patterns of the retaining system and tunnels but systematically overpredicted tunnel heave. The HSS model provided closer predictions of tunnel vertical displacement and central-column rebound than the MCC and HS models at the final excavation stage, although the agreement varied with monitoring location and excavation stage. For tunnel sidewall displacement, however, the HSS model tended…

title: Legal Certainty and the Protection of Online Motorcycle Taxi Drivers after Indonesia's Labour Law Reform
abstract: The year 2026 marked a major shift in the regulation of platform work in Indonesia. Presidential Regulation No. 27 of 2026 affirms online motorcycle taxi drivers as partners and caps platform fees at 8%, while the Labour Protection Law passed by the House of Representatives on 6 October 2026 grants platform workers the right to fair income, occupational safety, and protection from unilateral account deactivation, still within a partnership framework. This article examines whether these reforms produce real legal certainty and how the partnership relationship should be reconstructed. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches, it reaches three findings. First, the 2026 reforms deliver certainty of label without certainty of protection: partner status is now formally settled, yet criteria distinguishing genuine partnership from disguised employment remain absent. Second, affirming status through a presidential regulation raises a hierarchy problem, since it cannot displace the statutory elements of an employment relationship where the facts of performance satisfy them. Third, Nonet and Selznick's theory of responsive law is often invoked as a slogan in Indonesian scholarship, although it presupposes an achieved stage of autonomous law that the ride-hailing regime has not reached, and itself warns of the erosion of institutional integrity…
