Molecular Differentiation of Bipolaris oryzae and Nigrospora oryzae Associated with Brown Spot Symptoms in Rice
Energy security in the Age of Electricity
abstract: Abstract The global energy system is being reshaped by a second major supply shock in five years, surging electricity demand and intensifying competition over the technologies needed to meet it. In today’s more uncertain geopolitical landscape, energy security and electrification should not be seen as competing priorities – instead, they are deeply intertwined. Electrification can allow countries to make greater use of their domestic resources, reduce dependence on imported fuels and lower emissions. But these benefits will not be realised automatically. Grids, flexibility, resilient supply chains, access to finance and modern energy services must advance alongside innovation in electric technologies. The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, in November 2026 offers an opportunity to translate these priorities into tangible progress, with a proposed global ambition to raise electricity’s share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, while recognising different national circumstances and starting points.

title: Species composition, purity and safety concerns of edible insects in a Cambodian market
abstract: Abstract Insects are increasingly recognised as sustainable protein sources amid rising global food demand and the environmental impacts of conventional livestock production. However, although entomophagy is widespread in Southeast Asia, empirical information regarding Cambodia is limited. In this study, we investigated the composition and handling of insect-based food items sold at Skun Market in Kampong Cham Province, Cambodia, through surveys conducted in September and December 2022 and March 2023. Mixed fried assortments were purchased, sorted and taxonomically identified and the proportions of each group were quantified. Crickets, mainly Brachytrupes portentosus and Gryllus bimaculatus , were sold in high purity (mean 87.9%), whereas water beetles showed low purity (mean 79.0%) and frequently contained non-target taxa, including Diplonychus rusticus . A variety of additional insects, including mole crickets, ground beetles, cicadas, grasshoppers and dung beetles, were also detected in the cricket samples. Harmful or potentially toxic insects are occasionally mixed into assortments, raising concerns similar to those raised by contamination issues reported in other processed animal products. In the water beetle samples, vendors appeared to distinguish between Dytiscidae and Hydrophilidae and higher proportions of Dytiscidae were associated with higher prices, suggesting poss…
venue: Journal of Insects as Food and Feed

title: Regulatory compliance and quality of veterinary oxytetracycline injections in Zambia: findings from post-market surveillance
abstract: Objective Substandard antimicrobials affect the One Health ecosystem comprising both human and animal health, food production and food security, driving up Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) rates. This study assessed compliance with regulatory and quality specifications of oxytetracycline injection marketed for veterinary use in Zambia. Methods Between August 2023 and December 2023, a total of 48 samples of assorted marketed brands of oxytetracycline injection for veterinary use on the Zambian market were collected and analyzed for conformity to marketing authorisation terms on labeling and quality parameters, including identification, assay, and pH tests at the National Drug Quality Control Laboratory, Lusaka, Zambia. Results Conformity to labeling for information such as product name, active pharmaceutical ingredient, dosage form, batch number, expiry date, manufacturer, and container description were assessed at 100%. However, compliance with storage conditions and product registration numbers was assessed at 95.8% and 43.8%, respectively. All samples met requirements for specific quality tests such as identification, assay, and pH. Conclusion Although the sampled oxytetracycline injections met some labeling requirements and specific quality parameters, essential factors for effective disease treatment and combating AMR, the low rate of product registration compliance indicated…

title: The innovation and development of capital theory under the conditions of socialist market economy
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to deepen the comprehensive and accurate understanding of the essence, types, characteristics, laws of motion and functions of capital in the socialist market economy, explore policies for rationally regulating and guiding the sound development of various forms of capital and thereby to uphold the basic socialist economic system, advance high-quality development and common prosperity and modernise and sinicise Marxist political economy. It systematically addresses why China has innovated and developed capital theory, what the new capital theory contains and in what respects it innovates upon and develops Marx's theory of capital and the capital theory of mainstream Western economics. Design/methodology/approach Adopting materialist dialectics and a problem-driven comparative approach, the paper first reviews and synthesises the main content of Marx's theory of capital and of mainstream Western capital theory, identifying the historical and practical limitations of the former and the fundamental defects of the latter. It then examines the new perspectives on capital theory advanced in China since the reform and opening-up and, grounded in the reality of China's primary stage of socialism, constructs and expounds the new capital theory of socialist political economy with Chinese characteristics and demonstrates its scientific validity through theoretical r…

title: Credibility displacement in algorithmic financial reporting: a critical review of AI, disclosure credibility and capital-market consequences
abstract: Purpose This review examines how financial-reporting credibility is shaped when algorithmic systems enter the reporting chain. It asks where credibility is produced, tested and understood when artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, large language models, eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) analytics and related tools affect reporting information. Design/methodology/approach The paper combines a search and screening procedure informed by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) with a concept-centric synthesis. The evidence base comprises a 226-paper curated core and a 144-paper close-synthesis subset. Sensitivity analyses re-examine the 39-record outlet boundary and the close-synthesis threshold. Findings The evidence remains dispersed across research on textual disclosure and natural language processing (NLP), audit analytics and assurance, structured reporting using XBRL, market interpretation, accounting information systems (AIS) implementation and AI governance. Across these streams, algorithms can improve reporting processes but may also alter the grounds on which reporting assertions are accepted. We describe the latter possibility as credibility displacement: model-related output, provenance or validation partly substitutes for scrutiny of the underlying assertion or for identifiable professional and institutional…

title: The Impact of 2022 Electricity Tariff Increases on Household Electricity Consumption: An Econometric Analysis of Kalmunai Municipal Council
abstract: Electricity tariffs aim to promote efficiency, equity, and financial stability. Ceylon Electricity Board increased the tariffs after making losses in 2022. The research is meant to establish whether there is any correlation between electricity tariffs and consumption. Data were collected over three years, from 2022 to 2024, using 101 households in each year. The same number of households were observed in each year, totaling 303 samples (101 households × 3 years). This research examines any changes in households' electricity consumption using the data collected over these three years. Random Effects regression analysis model has been used to analyze the data collected using Stata software. According to the results of the analysis, electricity consumption is associated with electricity tariffs and electricity expenditure. From the data collected, it is clear that there is a correlation between household electricity consumption and electricity tariff, income, and number of appliances. There is a positive correlation between electricity tariff and consumption. This is contrary to expectations but can be attributed to economic performance in the post-COVID era, increases in income levels, and use of appliances during the sample period. However, the application of modern technology, like solar panels, shows an inverse relationship with the use of electricity. This research recommends…

title: Optimalisasi Monitoring Service Level Prosedur Melalui Penyusunan Instrumen Monitoring dan Prioritisasi Prosedur Berbasis Risiko di PT. Pelindo Multi Terminal
abstract: PT Pelindo Multi Terminal mengelola 182 prosedur aktif, namun monitoring service level masih terbatas, manual, berbasis audit, dan belum mempertimbangkan prioritas risiko sehingga belum optimal sebagai instrumen pengendalian proses bisnis. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengoptimalkan monitoring service level melalui prioritisasi prosedur berbasis risiko dan pengembangan instrumen monitoring yang terstruktur. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan applied research dengan metode kualitatif deskriptif-evaluatif. Data dikumpulkan melalui studi dokumentasi, wawancara terstruktur, diskusi teknis, dan expert judgment dari Divisi Sistem Manajemen, Business Process Owner, dan Divisi Manajemen Risiko, sedangkan tahap pengujian instrumen melibatkan 9 partisipan pada level Officer dan Vice President. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan content analysis, Criticality Analysis berbasis ISO 31010, serta Framework Maturity Assessment Model melalui tahap scope, design, populate, dan test. Dari 182 prosedur, 169 memiliki service level; 92 tergolong moderate to high dan high, kemudian 33 prosedur ditetapkan sebagai prioritas setelah proses scoping. Instrumen yang dikembangkan dinilai layak, mudah digunakan, dan mampu mendukung evaluasi secara konsisten. Penelitian ini menghasilkan model monitoring berbasis risiko yang memperkuat pengendalian proses bisnis dan efektivitas manajemen operasional.

title: EDITORIAL VOL. 11 2026 – Evolución tecnológica al servicio de la comunicación científica. MOJP 4.0 y una nueva etapa de desarrollo editorial
abstract: This editorial presents MOJP 4.0, a technological evolution of the editorial infrastructure of the Peer-Reviewed Scientific Journal of the MenteClara Foundation, developed by Oscar R. Gómez and his engineering team on the basis of OJS 3.5.0.5. It describes its main innovations: optimization of the metadata architecture, implementation of interoperable semantic schemas, improved identification of authors and institutions through persistent identifiers, expansion of OAI-PMH services, and integration of XMP metadata into PDF documents. It also presents Custom Head Injector, a native MOJP 4.0 module compatible with OJS 3.5.0.5 and later versions, which expands the possibilities for customizing and integrating metadata, semantic schemas, and external services into the HTML header of editorial platforms. The editorial also introduces the XMP-PDF Module, a technology designed to enrich scientific documents with structured information about their bibliographic identity, editorial provenance, rights, and other relevant data. These developments are part of an institutional trajectory of innovation, technological autonomy, and commitment to the principles of openness, interoperability, and the circulation of scientific information.
venue: Revista Científica Arbitrada de la Fundación MenteClara

title: The Role of Pre-Service Teachers’ Reflective Journals in Authentic Assessment
abstract: This study explored how pre-service teachers used reflective journals during an Authentic Assessment Intervention Program in Educational Test and Measurement. The study formed part of an explanatory sequential mixed-methods project involving 42 BEd Fourth Year (Second Semester) pre-service teachers at Yangon University of Education. This study focuses on qualitative evidence from journals completed throughout the intervention. Seven journal questions, organised around pre-topic and post-topic reflection, invited participants to record prior knowledge, feelings, participation, learning difficulties, beliefs about authentic tasks, and suggestions for instruction. The entries indicated that journal writing helped participants review and evaluate their learning, recognise strengths and weaknesses, monitor participation and collaboration, express affective responses, and connect course concepts with real-life situations and future teaching. The journals also gave the teacher timely formative evidence about misconceptions, readiness, learning needs, and requests for clearer explanations, realistic examples, additional feedback, and more time for discussion. Reflective journaling therefore served a dual purpose within authentic assessment: it supported learner self-monitoring and reflective thinking while also informing responsive instructional adjustment. These findings suggest that …

Evolutionary drivers of China’s interprovincial healthcare service network: a temporal exponential random graph analysis of provincial panel data
abstract: Background High-quality healthcare resources remain unevenly distributed across China, while cross-provincial care seeking, teleconsultation, and regional medical collaboration are increasingly common. Existing studies have mainly explained regional disparities in terms of resource endowments, geographic proximity, and spatial accessibility, with less attention to network structure, tie formation and persistence, and changes during public health crises. Methods Using panel data for 31 provincial-level administrative units in mainland China from 2009 to 2023, we constructed a directed interprovincial healthcare service association network with a modified gravity model. Social network analysis, temporal exponential random graph models (TERGMs), and separable temporal exponential random graph models (STERGMs) were used to examine network structure, endogenous mechanisms, sender and receiver effects, and differences before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Results The network shifted from expansion and integration toward contraction and differentiation. The number and density of ties increased from 2009 to 2013, declined after 2014, and fell markedly in 2019, while rising hierarchy indicated stronger core-periphery differentiation. Beijing, Shanghai, and Jiangsu formed the core of tie reception and path control; Zhejiang, Fujian, Henan, and Guangdong served as regional bridges; and…

title: Imagining the child’s perspective: pre-service social studies teachers’ visual representations of childhood vulnerability, empathy, and moral meaning
abstract: This study examined how social studies teacher trainees construct meanings of childhood vulnerability through visual and written representations, with particular attention to empathic perspective-taking and moral meaning-making. Rather than conceptualising vulnerability as individual fragility, the study examined how children were positioned in relation to voice, agency, rights, and structural conditions. An interpretative qualitative design integrating art-based inquiry, multimodal visual analysis, and reflexive thematic analysis was employed with 51 fourth-year social studies teacher trainees at a state university in Türkiye. During a 14-week Art and Museum Education module, participants produced visual works addressing childhood vulnerability and accompanying reflective texts, generating 51 paired visual–textual units. Analysis identified three interrelated patterns: the paradox of visibility, in which children were made visually salient yet remained discursively silent ( n = 20); the construction of vulnerability through enclosure, fragmentation, and control ( n = 17); and a shift from emotional response towards an ethical encounter grounded in empathy, rights, and professional responsibility ( n = 14). Frequencies indicate the dominant theme of each unit; many units also carried features of the other themes. Because the production guidelines explicitly invited participants…

title: Digital transformation of service ecosystems: an orchestration perspective
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital transformation unfolds within logistics service ecosystems and how inter-actor operational connections and coordinating roles change over time from an orchestration perspective. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted a case study of three international inland ports in China. Data were triangulated through interviews, observations and documents to capture ecosystem-level orchestration practices and transformation evolution. Findings The authors developed a process model that identifies three evolutionary stages of the digital transformation of service ecosystems: developing digital connectivity, tapping digital service potential and co-creating digital value. The model demonstrates how actors employ resource and network orchestration at each stage. The analysis reveals how these two forms of orchestration interact and how orchestration dynamics change over time. Originality/value This study shifts the focus of digital transformation research from a few focal firms to service ecosystems overall. It theorizes a three-stage transformation process, reveals the evolving interplay between resource and network orchestration, shows that different actors can assume orchestration leadership, and provides actionable recommendations for managers seeking to digitally transform logistics and supply chain service ecosystems.
venue: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Exploring attentional bias in posttraumatic stress disorder: insights from police officers with service dogs
abstract: Introduction PTSD is characterized by hypervigilance and attentional bias to threat, which can severely interfere with daily functioning. Stress exacerbates this bias by increasing amygdala activity and depleting prefrontal resources, reducing attentional control. The presence of a dog may help regulate attention by reducing stress. Methods This study investigates attentional bias to emotional faces in police officers with PTSD and examines whether the presence of their service or companion dog diminishes this bias by mitigating stress-related cognitive depletion, using a within subject design. Police officers with ( n = 24) and without PTSD ( n = 24) completed the dot-probe task with angry and happy faces in the presence and absence of their dog. Reaction times and event-related potentials (ERP) were analyzed to assess attentional bias. Results Officers with PTSD showed a greater trial level bias score but no consistent bias direction. The P3 amplitude indicated no differentiation between happy and angry faces in the PTSD group, unlike the control group. The VPP amplitude was higher in the PTSD group when the dog was absent, suggesting increased early-stage attention to faces without the dog. Officers with PTSD showed also slower reaction times when their dog was absent. Discussion The findings suggest that PTSD is associated with a reduced ability to selectively allocate atte…

title: From Learner Modeling to Human–AI Co-Regulation: A Systematic Scoping Review of Adaptive Generative AI in Personalized Learning
abstract: Abstract* Background Adaptive generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to personalize learning, yet evidence remains fragmented across system design, human–AI co-regulation, self-regulated learning (SRL), sustained behavioral outcomes, and ethics. This systematic scoping review mapped these dimensions in a single synthesis. Methods We searched Dimensions, ERIC, IEEE Xplore, Lens, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science on 5 May 2026. Of 3,084 records identified, 95 journal articles published between 2023 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. Evidence was synthesized using descriptive mapping, form–function co-occurrence analysis, and qualitative comparative synthesis. Results Adaptive GenAI was most commonly instantiated as conversational tutors, generative content personalizers, and hybrid feedback systems, with adaptive feedback, content adaptation, diagnostic analysis, scaffolding, and progress tracking emerging as the dominant functions. Conceptualizations of human–AI co-adaptation were less mature: most studies framed AI primarily as a responsive regulator, with feedback-loop acceleration and metacognitive prompting more frequently articulated than internalization, behavioral reinforcement, or social modeling. Empirical effects were concentrated in proximal SRL outcomes, particularly forethought and performance, while evidence for self-reflection, affectiv…

title: Early evaluation of the effectiveness of final income tax expenditure for MSMEs as a public policy instrument
abstract: This study conducts an early policy evaluation of Indonesia's final income tax expenditure for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) following Government Regulation No. 20 of 2026. Publicly available secondary data up to 13 August 2026 are assessed using the OECD-DAC criteria, while causal evidence is classified using an adapted Maryland Scientific Methods Scale. In 2024, the expenditure reached IDR 27.551 trillion for 543,908 beneficiaries, or an arithmetic mean of IDR 50.65 million per taxpayer, although beneficiary-level distribution is unavailable. A benchmark simulation for an individual taxpayer with IDR 1.5 billion turnover shows tax expenditure of IDR 25.90 million at a 20% profit margin, IDR 3.40 million at 10%, negative IDR 3.95 million at 5%, and negative IDR 5.00 million at a 2% margin or loss. Thus, benefits rise with profitability and resemble an upside-down subsidy, while low-margin firms may face negative tax expenditure. The option to elect ordinary taxation mitigates this problem but shifts the constraint toward tax literacy and bookkeeping costs. Policy relevance and simplicity are only partially supported: tax is not identified as the primary MSME constraint, and expanded turnover aggregation and cumulative threshold tracking add administrative complexity. The shared IDR 4.8 billion income-tax and value-added-tax threshold also creates a double notch.…

A catalogue of solar rotation-scale variations in the first Schumann resonance frequency at high latitudes, 2004–2024
abstract: Abstract Schumann resonances (SR) are extremely low-frequency (ELF) electromagnetic resonances of the Earth–ionosphere cavity, excited primarily by global lightning activity. Their modal frequencies can vary with the effective electrical properties and dimensions of the cavity, including lower-ionospheric conditions. Solar-rotation-scale variability has been reported in SR parameters, but its appearance in long-term SR frequency time series has not yet been systematically studied. We analyzed daily peak-frequency measurements of the first-mode SR (F1) from Hornsund (Svalbard), Ivalo, and Rovaniemi (both in northern Finland) from 2004/2005 to 2024. The north–south and east–west component time series were examined for time-localized wavelet power in the predefined 25–29-day, 12–15-day, and 8–11-day bands. Temporally overlapping detections in the same target band were grouped across the six F1 time series and labeled as events. Events detected at two or more stations were defined as multi-station events. For these events, we estimated band-limited F1 amplitudes and examined their relationships with solar-wind speed, geomagnetic indices, solar-radiation proxies, and lightning counts using the cross-wavelet transform and wavelet coherence. We identified 8, 29, and 68 time-localized events in the respective bands, of which 2, 4, and 25 were multi-station events. The 25–29-day activit…

title: Pithecellobium clypearia ameliorates ulcerative colitis through regulation of purine metabolism and gut microbiota
abstract: Background Pithecellobium clypearia (PC) is a traditional Chinese medicine with anti-inflammatory effects. However, the preventive efficacy and underlying mechanisms of PC in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain unclear. Objective This study applied an integrated microbiome-metabolomic approach to investigate PC’s pharmacological mechanisms against UC. Materials and methods A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced UC model was established, and the preventive efficacy of PC was evaluated using the disease activity index (DAI), histopathology, inflammatory cytokines, and tight junction proteins. Subsequently, 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics were performed to analyze alterations in the gut microbiota composition and colonic metabolic profiles. Results PC significantly ameliorated DSS-induced weight loss, reduced DAI scores, prevented colon shortening, and alleviated mucosal damage. Furthermore, PC decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β), increased anti-inflammatory IL-10, and restored tight junction expression. The 16S rRNA sequencing showed PC restored gut dysbiosis, enriching beneficial Bacteroides while reducing pathogenic Escherichia-Shigella. Metabolomics indicated PC modulated colonic purine metabolism, normalizing key metabolites like xanthylic acid and aminoimidazole ribotide. Correlation analysis confirmed a strong crosstalk between these purine metabol…

title: Combined effects of concurrent motor imagery and high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on human motor performance and corticospinal excitability
abstract: Introduction Combined therapeutic maneuvers may be more effective for improving motor dysfunction than single interventions. Although motor imagery (MI) and high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) each may enhance cortical excitability and/or motor performance, whether simultaneous application yields superior effects remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate behavioral and neurophysiological changes induced by HF-rTMS applied concurrently with MI. Methods Participants underwent four modulation procedures in a crossover design: MI of a typing task alone, 5-Hz rTMS over the left primary motor cortex alone, concurrent MI with 5 Hz rTMS, and a control condition. Before and after each intervention, motor performance was evaluated by means of actual and imagined movement time, error rate, MI vividness, and surface electromyography of intrinsic and extrinsic hand muscles. Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) elicited by single-pulse TMS were also recorded at rest, during MI, and actual movement. Results No significant changes in motor or MI performance were observed following any intervention. Task-related corticospinal excitability, expressed relative to resting MEP amplitude (%rest), decreased during actual movement after concurrent MI with HF-rTMS compared with the control and MI-alone conditions. MEP persistence in the agonist muscle remained stable …

title: Self-differentiation, adult attachment, and difficulties in emotion regulation among undergraduate nursing students
abstract: This study examined self-differentiation, adult attachment, and difficulties in emotion regulation among undergraduate nursing students in China and identified significant differences, relationships, and predictive influences among the variables to inform the development of a university-based mental health education program. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 500 undergraduate nursing students selected through stratified random sampling. Data were gathered using the Differentiation of Self Inventory-Revised (DSI-R), Adult Attachment Scale-Revised (AAS-R), and Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS). Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, an independent-samples t-test, a one-way ANOVA, a Pearson correlation, and a multiple regression analysis. Findings revealed that the respondents demonstrated a lower level of differentiation of self, a moderate level of adult attachment, and a high level of difficulties in emotion regulation. Significant differences were observed in differentiation of self and emotion regulation by place of origin, whereas adult attachment differed significantly by year level. Pearson correlation analysis indicated no significant relationship between differentiation of self and adult attachment. However, differentiation of self-exhibited a significant weak negative relationship with difficulties in emotion…

title: Electron temperatures derived from low-frequency radio observations of planetary nebulae
abstract: Planetary nebulae are formed around low- and intermediate-mass stars after the asymptotic giant phase and before the extinction of thermonuclear reactions. Chemical abundances and electron temperatures of planetary nebulae show a dichotomy known as an abundance and temperature discrepancy. Collisionally excited lines show higher temperatures and lower abundances compared to recombination lines. This is explained by the presence of two ionised components: a hot ionised gas and clumps of a cold, metal-rich gas of unknown origin. We sought to map radio free-free emission in order to determine electron temperatures across a sample of planetary nebulae. We compared these temperatures with those derived using other methods to investigate whether the radio emission traces the hot or cold component. Our aim was also to verify the lower radio extinction from the radio data compared to extinction determined from the Balmer decrement. We cross-matched the LoTSS-DR3 catalogue with existing catalogues of Galactic planetary nebulae as well as with archival radio and optical surveys. We fitted free-free and power law spectra to the radio spectra. Determining the electron temperatures required observation of low-frequency turnover, which marks the transition from optically thin to optically thick emission. To derive the radio extinction, we combined our radio observations and optical emission …

title: Anticompetitive Practices of Marketplaces and the Experience of Their Regulation by Antitrust Authorities in Russia and China
abstract: The volume of the global e-commerce market is 5.31 trillion dollars, an increase of 8.6% per year by 2024, which accounted for a quarter of total retail sales. With a significant positive effect, the rapid development of marketplaces is accompanied by the risk of monopolization by individual platforms of traditional and electronic value chains, which can lead to abuse of market power and the creation of conditions that form extreme negative processes in the system of interaction of all stakeholders of the digital platform. To prevent platform monopolism, various approaches to regulating their transactional and behavioral characteristics are being developed in different countries of the world. The proposed article examines the general characteristics of anticompetitive practices by marketplaces in Russia and China, describes the experience of China's antitrust authority regarding their actions, and presents a list of decisions by the Russian FAS in connection with the anticompetitive business policies of platforms. The author's view and experience of Chinese regulatory practice for Russia are presented. This article is a logical continuation of a previously published article by I. Knyazeva "Features of the Functioning of Marketplaces in the Context of the Requirements of Competition Law", published in no. 5, 2025, of the Journal of Modern Competition.

Habitual social media use as everyday information behavior: interruption, refusal and self-regulation among older adults
abstract: Purpose This article examines habitual social media use among older adults as everyday information behavior, focusing on how repeated use reaches closure, remains renewable or becomes interrupted. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods study combined a survey of 198 Taiwanese adults aged 55 and above with ten follow-up interviews. Motivation composites, Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS) scores and interview accounts were analyzed around the Hook cycle. Findings Self-validation and relaxation were more closely associated with problematic-use tendency than information learning. Learning-oriented use usually ended when a question was answered or a task could continue; recognition and relief were easier to renew through replies, likes, recommendations and temporary escape from worry. Participants limited use through filtering triggers, pacing action, sorting rewards and refusing investment. Research limitations/implications The sample was recruited largely through libraries and community learning settings, so findings are best read as showing how structured everyday settings shape interruption rather than as population estimates. Originality/value The study extends information behavior research by treating interruption and refusal as information judgments within habitual social media use.

title: Macro–Micro Synergistic Design Driven by Interlayer Electric Field Load Regulation: All-Organic Sandwich Dielectrics for High-Temperature Energy Storage Applications of PMMA
abstract: Abstract To address the severe performance degradation of polymer dielectric capacitors under extreme high-temperature and high-field conditions, this study proposes a layered dielectric electric-field reconstruction strategy. An all-organic PC/PMMA/PC (CMC) sandwich-structured composite film was fabricated via layer-by-layer solution casting, utilizing polycarbonate (PC) as the outer buffer layer and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) as the functional core. The dielectric mismatch between layers induces intrinsic electric-field redistribution, allowing the low-dielectric PC outer layers to sustain higher local fields and dissipate stress, thereby reducing the electric-field load on the high-dielectric, wide-bandgap PMMA core. This architecture circumvents the high-temperature breakdown of PMMA while fully exploiting its polarization capability, synergistically optimizing polarization and breakdown strength. Additionally, deep traps at heterogeneous interfaces effectively suppress carrier transport and reduce conduction loss. At 100 °C, the CMC film achieves a breakdown strength of 630 MV/m, a discharged energy density of 8.50 J/cm3, and an efficiency of 88%, significantly outperforming single-component polymers. By integrating macroscopic electric-field modulation with microscopic band-structure engineering, this study elucidates the regulatory mechanisms of the layered stackin…

title: Increased frequency of dislocation following total hip arthroplasty for trauma
abstract: Aims The purpose of this study was to compare surgical techniques and postoperative outcomes in an age- and sex-matched cohort of patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) for neck of femur fracture (#NOF) and for osteoarthritis (OA). Methods A single-centre, consecutive series of patients at minimum one-year follow-up following THA for #NOF were compared with a 1:1 age- and sex-matched cohort of patients following THA for osteoarthritis from the same institution. The primary outcome measure was frequency of dislocation at one year postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included rates of all-cause revision, infection, periprosthetic fracture, and mortality at one year and medium-term postoperatively. Cox regression compared medium-term outcomes between groups, accounting for unequal follow-up duration. Results A total of 722 patients were included, with 361 in each group. BMI was greater in the OA group (28.9 kg/m 2 vs 24.7 kg/m 2 ; p < 0.001). Sex, age, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, and comorbidity profile did not differ between groups (p > 0.247). Overall, 151 patients (41.8%) in the #NOF group received dual-mobility implants, compared with eight (2.2%) in the OA group (p < 0.001). Femoral offset was similar between groups (42.6 mm and 42.7 mm, p = 0.892). Dislocation rates were greater in the #NOF group than the OA group at one-year (4.4% vs 1.1%; p = 0.01…

Annual sampling frequency and false-negative probability in water-quality threshold-exceedance detection: an exact conditional analysis of the Buranhém River, Bahia, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Routine monitoring captures conditions present during sampling, so sparse schedules may fail to encounter threshold exceedances recorded at other times in the same year. Using 106 Class 2 freshwater campaigns from five Buranhém River sites during 2015–2024, the analysis examined seven water-quality parameters and a composite any-exceedance outcome within site-years. Exact finite-population probabilities were calculated for each positive annual reference set to determine whether hypothetical schedules of one to four campaigns would include at least one recorded exceedance. Fixed common support defined the primary one- to three-campaign comparison, requiring at least three classifiable results for the target outcome; Monte Carlo simulation and independent enumeration served only as computational verification. Across 20 positive common-support site-years, mean conditional detection probabilities for the composite outcome were 58.3%, 87.9%, and 95.8% for one, two, and three campaigns, corresponding to conditional false-negative probabilities of 41.7%, 12.1%, and 4.2%. Annual simple random sampling yielded 53.9%, 79.5%, and 94.3%, indicating that temporal allocation affected the magnitude of the estimates but not the observed increase with sampling frequency. Twelve of the 20 site-years contained exactly three classifiable campaigns, so finite-population exhaustion partly i…

Early change in serum prealbumin adds predictive value for Day-7 enteral nutrition response in critically ill adults: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background and aims Single serum prealbumin (PAB) measurements are difficult to interpret during critical illness because they are strongly influenced by inflammation and disease severity. We investigated whether early changes in PAB after enteral nutrition (EN) initiation were associated with an operationally defined Day 7 EN response and added predictive value to that of routinely available clinical variables. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study screened 341 critically ill adults. The primary cohort comprised 263 patients with PAB measured at baseline, Day 3, and Day 7; an expanded sensitivity cohort comprised 271 patients with baseline and Day 3 PAB and ascertainable Day 7 EN outcomes, irrespective of Day 7 PAB availability. Day 7 EN response required energy target achievement ≥70%, protein delivery ≥1.0 g/kg/day, no gastrointestinal (GI)-related EN interruption >24 h, and no supplemental parenteral nutrition (PN) before assessment. We used multivariable logistic regression analyses, component-specific analyses, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration, decision-curve analysis, restricted cubic splines, and 2,000-resample bootstrap validation. Results In the primary cohort, 154 of the 263 patients (58.6%) were responders. Each 10 mg/L increase in Day-3 ΔPAB was independently associated with higher odds of response (adjusted odd…

title: Seasonal response of sea surface salinity to sea ice retreat and polynya opening in the Ross Sea
abstract: Antarctic sea ice extent increased gradually over recent decades but has declined rapidly since 2016, including in the Ross Sea. Because sea ice melt alters the freshwater budget and sea surface salinity (SSS), understanding SSS variability is essential for interpreting recent hydrographic changes in the Ross Sea. Here, we reconstruct SSS for 1999–2023 using in-situ observations and a Random Forest (RF) model. The RF-based SSS (SSS RF ) shows high accuracy (R 2 = 0.80, RMSE = 0.10 psu) and captures spatial variability more consistently with in-situ observations than existing satellite- and model-based SSS products. Regime shift analysis of sea ice concentration anomalies using the Sequential t-Test Analysis of Regime Shifts (STARS) identifies three distinct periods: Regime 1 (R1; 1999–2004), Regime 2 (R2; 2004–2016), and Regime 3 (R3; 2016–2023), corresponding to high, moderate, and low sea ice conditions, respectively. During the recent low-sea-ice regime (R3), SSS RF initially decreases as sea ice retreats, then rises after the opening of the Ross Sea Polynya, as exchange with relatively saline waters intensifies. Cross-correlation analysis further shows that changes in open-water area precede SSS variations by approximately one month. These results demonstrate that the recent decline in sea ice does not simply drive surface freshening. Instead, the observed seasonal evolutio…

title: Quantifying the near-term response of the ocean CO 2 sink to reduced atmospheric carbon concentrations
abstract: The ocean plays a critical role in sequestering carbon, yet how the air–sea carbon sink will respond to rapid reductions in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations remains a key uncertainty for climate mitigation and carbon accounting. In this study, we utilize the ECCO-Darwin ocean biogeochemistry model to simulate the ocean's response to a range of near-term CO 2 mitigation scenarios which are simulated with reduced atmospheric carbon concentrations. Our results demonstrate an immediate but spatially heterogeneous weakening of the ocean carbon sink following reduced atmospheric forcing. Global air–sea carbon uptake decreases substantially within the first several years of mitigation, with the magnitude of the reduction scaling with the strength of the mitigation scenario. We find that the mitigation signal is primarily confined to the upper-500 m, reflecting dominant decadal-scale ventilation pathways. The most pronounced reductions in uptake occur in subtropical thermocline regions, western boundary currents, and the subpolar North Atlantic – regions characterized by intense ventilation and rapid air–sea equilibration. These findings align with recent CMIP-based long-term projections and observation-based inversions, confirming that the areas currently dominating anthropogenic carbon uptake are also the most sensitive to atmospheric forcing changes. Our results sug…

title: Macro-level determinants of rail freight demand and implications for sustainable transport: evidence from Sri Lanka
abstract: Purpose This article empirically examines the macro-level determinants of rail freight demand in Sri Lanka, given the persistent decline in rail modal share and the need to support sustainable transport objectives. Design/methodology/approach Rail freight tonne-kilometres are used as a measure of rail freight demand, and the relationships with rail freight rates, fuel prices, gross domestic product growth and trade intensity are examined. The autoregressive distributed lag bounds-testing approach and the error-correction model (ECM) are employed to estimate long-run relationships and short-run dynamics among the variables, complemented by the Toda–Yamamoto Granger causality test. Findings Rail freight rates and trade intensity are identified as significant long-run determinants of rail freight demand. In the short run, the ECM indicates significant lagged adjustments and a negative, statistically significant error-correction term. The Toda–Yamamoto analysis shows no evidence of predictive Granger causality from the selected macroeconomic variables to rail freight demand. The findings suggest that macroeconomic growth and price-based measures alone are unlikely to generate a sustained recovery in rail freight demand, highlighting the need to consider service quality, infrastructure capacity, multimodal connectivity and institutional constraints when developing sustainable transp…

title: Comparative constitutive modelling of anisotropy, pore-pressure response and strain localization in Opalinus clay
abstract: Abstract Several countries are considering argillaceous rocks as host formations for the geological disposal of radioactive waste. These rock types possess favourable properties for the retardation of radionuclide migration from the deep geological repository (DGR), including very low permeability, low molecular diffusivity, high sorption capacity and self-healing characteristics. However, several internal and external events and processes, such as excavation of the DGR, thermal loading from the waste, and gas generation, can mechanically disturb the host rock and might adversely affect its favourable properties. The assessment of the host rock performance as a barrier to radionuclide migration necessitates the development of robust constitutive models. In the present paper, constitutive models developed by six research teams of the international DECOVALEX project are presented and compared. The models were developed using a comprehensive experimental database from laboratory tests performed on Opalinus Clay, an argillaceous host rock formation in the Swiss DGR concept. The laboratory tests consist of uniaxial compression tests, Brazilian tensile tests, and consolidated-undrained (CU) triaxial tests with pore pressure measurements, followed by microscopic observations of the deformation and failure modes. The models reproduced the main features of the experimental observations,…

title: Genome-wide identification of CDPK genes in Ricinus communis L. and functional characterization of RcCDPK18 in osmotic stress response
EFFECT OF ARB AND HIGH-TEMPERATURE ANNEALING ON THE MICROSTRUCTURAL EVOLUTION AND MECHANICAL RESPONSE OF Cu–Al–Ag SHAPE MEMORY ALLOYS
abstract: This work employs accumulative roll bonding (ARB) to generate ultrafine-grained Cu–Al–Ag laminates prior to annealing. Subsequent high-temperature annealing produces the coarser microstructures required for martensitic phase development. High-purity aluminum and copper strips were combined with silver particles as the starting materials. The aluminum level was kept constant at 15[Formula: see text]wt.%, while the silver content was adjusted to 2.5, 5, and 7.5[Formula: see text]wt.%. After ARB processing, the multilayered composites were annealed for one hour at 700–[Formula: see text]C and then quenched to room temperature. The study focuses on how silver concentration and annealing temperature influence the resulting microstructure. All processed samples developed refined grains and elevated dislocation densities. Heat treatment produced new intermetallic compounds. Alloys containing 2.5[Formula: see text]wt.% Ag mainly formed Cu 9 Al 4 , whereas those with 5–7.5[Formula: see text]wt.% Ag stabilized orthorhombic Cu 3 Al martensite. The presence of martensite increased strength and microhardness at room temperature. The highest martensite content appeared in the 900–[Formula: see text]C annealing range. The annealed and quenched composites demonstrated strong shape memory performance at ambient conditions.

title: BRD4 c.1213-1 G > T, BRD4-S loss, and NHWD-870 response: Evidence from a NUT carcinoma case and an isogenic lung squamous cell model
Case Report: Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis in HER2-low breast cancer: near-complete response to multimodal management and trastuzumab deruxtecan
abstract: Background Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis (ISCM) is a rare neurological complication of breast cancer. While trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) demonstrates robust central nervous system efficacy in HER2-low metastatic disease, real-world evidence regarding its specific activity against ISCM remains exceedingly limited. Case presentation A patient initially diagnosed in 2021 with hormone receptor-positive (HR+), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low (1+) breast cancer with sternal metastasis presented in July 2025 with severe right upper extremity weakness (Medical Research Council [MRC] grade 3/5). Cervical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a C2 intramedullary lesion, prompting immediate surgical resection and laminoplasty. Pathological evaluation of the spinal lesion confirmed breast cancer-derived ISCM, revealing a HR-negative (ER 0%, PR 0%), HER2-low (1+) profile with a high Ki-67 index (70%). Two months post-surgery, follow-up spine MRI detected a 9-mm C2 nodule, designated as radiologically suspected local recurrence or residual disease. Guided by the identified HER2-low target, the patient received T-DXd therapy concurrently with intensity-modulated radiation therapy to the C1-C4 cervical spine (30 Gy in 10 fractions). Follow-up imaging demonstrated a near-complete radiological resolution of the spinal nodule, accompanied by substantial neurologi…

title: Synchronizing nitrogen supply with crop demand through postponed and reduced topdressing improves nitrogen use efficiency and maintains yield in wheat
abstract: Abstract Background Nitrogen (N) management is essential for wheat productivity; however, the traditional practice of excessive N fertilization frequently leads to low N use efficiency and increased environmental risk. Although numerous studies have shown that postponed or split N topdressing can enhance wheat production, it remains unclear whether it is possible to maintain grain yield and increase N use efficiency by moderately reducing N fertilizer input when coupled with postponed N topdressing. Results A two-year field experiment was carried out during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons. Seven N fertilizer treatments were established: a conventional N treatment (NS37: basal + topdressing at 3‑leaf stage and 7‑leaf stage), basal N only (NS), zero‑N control (N 0 ), a postponed N topdressing treatment (NS58: basal+ topdressing at the 5‑leaf stage and 8‑leaf stage), and three postponed‑reduced N topdressing treatments (NS5 R 8: basal + 50% N at the 5‑leaf stage + full N at the 8‑leaf stage; NS R 5 R 8: 50% basal N + 50% N at the 5‑leaf stage + full N at the 8‑leaf stage; NS 0 5 R 8: no basal N + 50% N at the 5‑leaf stage + full N at the 8‑leaf stage). Grain yield, tiller traits, spike characteristics and grain quality were measured. N 0 and NS treatments significantly reduced grain yield, total tiller number, effective spike number and grain quality parameters. In contrast, the…

title: Depressive symptoms are associated with poor prognosis and lower pathological complete response in triple-negative breast cancer: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Depressive symptoms are common in patients with cancer, but their associations with survival and treatment response in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain uncertain. Methods This single-center retrospective study screened 19,335 patients with breast cancer treated during 2015–2025 and included 4,060 patients with TNBC. A single baseline Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) assessment classified patients into normal/mild (score <10; n = 3,666) and moderate/severe (score ≥10; n = 394) symptom groups. Survival analyses included 3,878 patients without baseline distant metastasis; pathological complete response (pCR) analyses included 1,689 neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) recipients with available response data. Cox and logistic regression models adjusted for recorded clinicopathological variables. An exploratory cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2009–2018 was conducted separately. Results In the TNBC cohort, moderate/severe baseline depressive symptoms were associated with differences in T-stage and Ki-67 distributions and a higher frequency of baseline distant metastasis. N-stage distributions did not differ significantly (P = 0.059). Among patients without baseline distant metastasis, adjusted hazard ratios were 1.626 for overall survival (OS; 95% CI: 1.301–2.033; P < 0.001) and 1.439 for disease-free survival (DFS; 95% CI: 1.170–1.770; P < 0.001). …

title: Modelling of an imprecise production inventory problem with interval-valued demand and semi-Type-2 interval-valued inventory costs: Its optimality via parametric optimization technique
abstract: In real-life production inventory systems, decision-makers often struggle to estimate demand rates, production rates, and inventory costs because of market volatility, limited historical data, and unstable economic conditions. While traditional interval-based models have some usefulness, they do not properly address uncertainty in cost estimates. This study proposes a new production inventory model that includes interval-valued production rates, interval-valued demand that depends on both time and selling price, and semi-Type-2 interval-valued inventory costs for ordering, holding, and production. The semi-Type-2 interval method keeps one boundary fixed and lets the other vary, more accurately reflecting cost uncertainties caused by inflation, supply chain disruptions, and market fluctuations. The model uses interval differential equations and parametric interval mathematics. To study the optimal policy of the proposed model, we derive the parametric form of the semi-Type-2 intervals and an optimization technique for the semi-Type-2 interval-valued average profit function. Three numerical examples show how to determine the optimal policies. A sensitivity analysis is performed to show the effects of known system parameters on the optimal policy. The numerical results show that allowing the flexible upper bound of cost estimates can improve decision-making and increase profitabil…

title: Cross-border disaster victim identification after the Struma Motorway bus fire: operational response and element-by-element comparison with the INTERPOL DVI Guide
abstract: Abstract Background Mass-fatality road incidents with severely burned victims require integration of scene recovery, post-mortem examination, ante-mortem information and reconciliation. In the Struma Motorway bus fire in Bulgaria on 23 November 2021, all victims were nationals of the neighbouring country. This report presents the findings from all 45 decedents, describes the local workflow assembled out of necessity, and compares it element by element with the INTERPOL Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) Guide. It is a retrospective review of the judicially mandated medico-legal investigation, based on the scene, autopsy, toxicology and DNA records, the ante-mortem material from North Macedonia and the identification outcomes. Carboxyhemoglobin and recovery position were transcribed from the annotated scene schematic, and 33 Guide elements were extracted before scoring and assigned one of five descriptors, from fulfilled to not fulfilled. Results The first search did not clear all compartments of the vehicle; when reconciliation showed one passenger unaccounted for, a repeat examination recovered the 45th decedent, a child, from a luggage hold. DNA profiles from all 45 sets of remains were compared with those of 34 relatives sampled in North Macedonia; DNA and dental analysis resolved a dizygotic twin pair and two sibling groups. All 45 victims were identified within 10 days. …

title: Pooling hospital resources to enhance resilience and sustainability under concurrent supply and demand shocks
abstract: Introduction Recent health crises have highlighted the structural vulnerability of hospital operations, pushing operational resilience and social sustainability to the forefront as organizational imperatives. While healthcare supply chain literature extensively addresses safety stock management, demand forecasting, and supplier diversification as resilient strategies, less attention has been given to internal hospital resource reorganization as a resilience strategy during crises. Managers lack evidence-based tools to adapt internal operations when facing distinct or simultaneous supply and demand shocks. Consequently, crisis management still relies on rigid trade-offs, often resulting in substantial delays or postponement of elective surgical care. To address this gap, this study evaluates internal cross-departmental resource pooling as an operational resilience strategy to mitigate surgical delay and preserve service continuity across mixed patient pathways. Methods A discrete-event simulation model was developed to compare two organizational configurations within a mixed-flow (emergency and elective) surgical environment: a siloed versus a pooled organization. The model incrementally tests three distinct crisis scenarios: a demand shock, a supply shock, and a simultaneous dual shock. These scenarios were applied to a real-world case study at the Fez-Meknes Regional Hospital …

title: Development of An IoT-Based Smart Home Security System Using Laser Beams and LDR Sensors
abstract: This study to analyze the design and performance evaluation of an Internet of Things (IoT) based home security prototype combining RFID access authentication with laser light dependent resistor (LDR) intrusion detection. The prototype employed an Arduino Uno, RFID RC522, laser emitter, LDR voltage divider, relay-controlled solenoid door lock, buzzer, and ESP32-CAM for image acquisition and Telegram notifications. Engineering research involved system design, prototype construction, and subsystem and integrated testing. Across 13 alarm test observations, LDR analog-to-digital converter readings ranged from 56 to 1004, a threshold of 850 distinguished the nine interrupted-beam observations from four uninterrupted-beam observations under the tested lighting conditions. RFID card were detected at distances of 1–6 cm but not at 7–9 cm. Registered credentials activated the door lock, whereas unregistered credentials were rejected. In 30 response-time tests, the buzzer responded in 120.87 ± 4.25 ms (mean ± standard deviation); Telegram transmission required 2290 ± 75.20 ms. The results demonstrate the functional integration of local authentication, beam-interruption detection, actuation, image capture, and remote notification. The findings apply to the tested prototype and environmental and network conditions.

title: AgriTech: Foundations, Emerging Technologies, System Architectures, and Deployment Readiness—A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: Agricultural technology (AgriTech) is transforming agricultural production through advances in artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, robotics, remote sensing, digital twins, and intelligent decision-support systems. Despite these developments, the transition from technological innovation to effective agricultural deployment remains constrained by technical, operational, economic, and institutional challenges. Existing research frequently emphasizes individual technologies, applications, or performance indicators, providing limited integration of system architectures, operational reliability, affordability, interoperability, and deployment readiness. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of AgriTech foundations, enabling technologies, architectural approaches, agricultural applications, and performance evaluation methods. It examines centralized, distributed, cloud, edge, and hybrid architectures alongside intelligent agricultural systems and autonomous technologies. A comparative analysis identifies their capabilities, limitations, infrastructure requirements, and operational trade-offs. The survey further investigates agricultural data quality, environmental variability, cybersecurity, maintenance, financial sustainability, digital inclusion, and governance challenges affecting practical implementation. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes the Integrated …

title: Walk the talk: how procurement professionals' interpretations shape social sustainability cascading
abstract: Purpose Procurement professionals shape how firms translate their commitments to social sustainability into supplier-facing governance, which can vary markedly, even within the same firm. This study explains this variation by theorizing how procurement professionals interpret their role and translate engagement with suppliers into governance practices. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on constructivist grounded theory and interviews with 27 professionals across organizational contexts. The analysis combines iterative coding, constant comparison, theoretical sampling, and abductive engagement with sensitizing literature. Findings The study develops a process model that explains cascading depth from a people-centric perspective. The interviewed procurement professionals differed on whether they construed their remit to include social sustainability, whether supplier-facing action appeared worth pursuing, and whether more improvement-oriented engagement appeared feasible. This situated judgment shaped whether cascading is enacted predominantly through procedural compliance or through more generative supplier-facing practice. Prospective paradoxical sensemaking helped explain how more generative supplier-facing responses could remain actionable under competing commercial demands, as professionals saw anticipated social and commercial consequences as relevant to their jud…

title: Understanding and managing the human side of acquisitions
abstract: Orientation: The persistently high failure rate of mergers and acquisitions (M&As) remains a major concern for economic growth and corporate development. Many failures stem from poorly managed people transitions, leading to severe negative social consequences for employees, families and communities. Effective human resource management is essential to minimise these outcomes. Research purpose: This study identifies specific challenges faced by human resource (HR) specialists and managers during people transfers in acquisitions, critically evaluates existing scholarly frameworks and proposes a strategic model for successful human transitions. Motivation for the study: Acquisition research typically lacks longitudinal, insider perspectives, yielding fragmented insights. This work fills that gap by providing a rare, in-depth insider view of human dynamics in M&A processes. Research approach/design and method: Using a qualitative auto-ethnographic approach, the study draws on nine detailed vignettes from Swart’s experiences as both an acquirer and an acquiree, supplemented by field notes, minutes and emails. Two additional cases were corroborated through interviews and documents. Critical event analysis identified participant themes, which were synthesised with scholarly constructs from the organisation, management, social change, commerce and legal literatures. Analytic induction a…

title: When bots act like us: the role of social media accounts' human-likeness in opinion polarization
abstract: Purpose As social bots penetrate social media, social media accounts with different human-likeness interact with each other, with opinion polarization as one of the results. This study investigates the impact of human-likeness of social media accounts on opinion polarization on social media. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the social validation principle and its intersections with the optimal distinctiveness theory as the theoretical foundation, this study applies empirical analysis with a dataset of 2,034,201 replies from Weibo to examine the proposed model. Findings An inverted U-shaped relationship between human-likeness of social media accounts and opinion polarization in replies mediated by their social validation and moderated by information valence. Originality/value Our findings advance understanding of human–bot interaction dynamics, highlighting how bot human-likeness relates to opinion polarization at the community level. This study provides actionable measures for stakeholders: bot developers should carefully calibrate human-likeness, platforms should implement graded indicators on human-likeness of social media accounts and users must critically evaluate information sources to mitigate polarization.

title: A systematic review on emerging technologies for cardiovascular disease management
Negotiating Chinese scientific power in multipolar global science: an exploration of STEM international doctoral students’ glonacal learning experiences in China
abstract: Abstract China’s rapid ascent as a scientific superpower has disrupted the Euro-American duopoly in global science, attracting a growing number of STEM international doctoral students, particularly from the Global South. However, the intricate global-national-local (glonacal) power dynamics that pose unique challenges to these students’ learning remain understudied. Through interviews with 20 STEM international doctoral students from the Global South, this narrative inquiry examined how glonacal powers influenced students’ learning experiences and how students negotiated the powers. Framed by theorisation of global-national-local imbrications and the notion of ‘in-between agency’, findings revealed that students navigated triple-dimensional power tensions, caught among enduring hegemony of Western academia, China’s national scientific ambitions, and ‘local’ supervisors as gatekeepers of STEM knowledge and networks. These power tensions led to an ambivalent positioning that marginalised international students across the local laboratory, national and global scientific communities. Yet, students enacted in-between agency to negotiate glonacal power tensions, by bridging local lab resources, China’s research training, and global knowledge production. This study contributes to the literature by integrating glonacal and agency perspectives to illuminate STEM international doctoral s…

title: Perioperative anesthetic management of a patient with narcolepsy: a case report
abstract: Introduction and importance: Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that disrupts sleep–wake regulation and poses unique challenges in perioperative anesthetic management. Presentation of case: We report the successful perioperative management of a 21-year-old man with type 1 narcolepsy, accompanied by mild obstructive sleep apnea with an apnea–hypopnea index (AHI) of 14.3 events per hour, who underwent uvulopalatopharyngoplasty. Clinical discussion: Short-acting agents (propofol, remifentanil, and sevoflurane) were administered under continuous bispectral index (BIS) monitoring. Multimodal analgesia with sufentanil, flurbiprofen, and ropivacaine was used to optimize pain control and minimize respiratory risk. The patient recovered without delayed awakening after the primary anesthesia or worsening of narcolepsy symptoms, despite a postoperative bleeding episode requiring reoperation. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of individualized anesthetic strategies for patients with narcolepsy, emphasizing BIS-guided anesthetic depth control and multimodal analgesia to ensure safe perioperative outcomes.

title: Dynamic modeling and structural dynamic analysis of a laminated casing system with bolted connections at both ends
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to analyze the vibration behavior of a cylindrical shell model with bolted ends under different influence factors, and to provide a reliable theoretical prediction for the study of bolted casing. Design/methodology/approach Based on love theory, the vibration differential equation of laminated cylindrical shell is derived by using orthogonal polynomials as axial modal functions, combined with the boundary conditions of bolted joints and Lagrange equation, and the theoretical model of laminated cylindrical shell connected by bolts at both ends is established. By comparing the theoretical model with the finite element analysis results, the accuracy of the model established in this paper is verified. The influence of the number of bolts on the natural frequency and mode shape of the cylindrical shell and the influence of the axial, torsional, tangential and radial connection stiffness on the natural frequency of the cylindrical shell are analysed in detail. Findings The different number of bolts has a great influence on the natural frequency and mode shape of cylindrical shell. The axial connection stiffness, tangential connection stiffness and radial connection stiffness have significant effects on the natural frequency of cylindrical shells, while the torsional connection stiffness has little effect on the natural frequency. Originality/value…

title: Design and Implementation of an Integrated Academic Affairs Management and Faculty Evaluation System at Faryab University
abstract: Universities increasingly require integrated digital systems to manage academic affairs, faculty evaluation, institutional planning, and quality assurance. In resource-constrained higher education institutions, fragmented administrative records and paper-based procedures can complicate academic monitoring, reporting, and decision-making. This study presents the design and implementation of an Integrated Academic Affairs Management and Faculty Evaluation System for Faryab University, Afghanistan. A design-oriented research approach was adopted, with system requirements identified through the analysis of official institutional forms and administrative procedures. The system was developed using Laravel (PHP), Filament, and MySQL, following a three-layer architecture. Its integrated components support academic personnel management, academic rank tracking, operational planning, course administration, faculty evaluation, quality assurance, document management, and administrative reporting. The implementation demonstrates how institution-specific administrative requirements can be translated into interconnected software modules and database structures. The study contributes a context-specific implementation case for integrating academic administration and quality assurance processes within a unified information system. Although the application has been developed, formal user-based eva…
