title: Credit Default Risk Assessment of Listed Real Estate Firms Using the KMV Model
abstract: This study examines the credit default risk of Chinese listed real estate firms using the KMV structural credit risk model, with particular attention to market-based risk assessment and the limitations of conventional credit ratings. Drawing on data from 261 real estate firms listed on mainland China's A-share markets and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange between 2010 and 2023, the study estimates distance to default (DD) from equity market information and financial statement data. A logistic regression approach is employed to translate DD into estimated default probabilities, while receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and firm-level case studies are used to evaluate risk discrimination and early-warning performance. The results reveal a substantial deterioration in the creditworthiness of mainland-focused property developers during the industry downturn, particularly in 2022–2023, alongside pronounced differences between mainland and non-mainland firms. The DD measure achieves an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.760, indicating moderate discriminatory ability within the evaluated sample. Comparative case studies further suggest that market-based risk indicators can provide more frequent signals of financial deterioration than conventional credit ratings, although their predictive reliability depends on appropriate calibration and validation. The findings highlight …

title: Influence of digital work platforms on working conditions in the tourism sector: a system dynamics model
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the System Dynamics (SD) model developed within a research project focused on the phenomenon of platformisation of services in tourism and its impacts on the labour market, i.e. wages, working conditions and unionisation of tourism workers. Through consultations with domain experts, we have developed a causal loop diagram representing the relationships between stakeholders and other influential factors and used it as the starting point for the development of a System Dynamics (SD) model. The SD model aims to provide insight into the tourism labour market dynamics in Slovenia through the interplay of a set of variables representing the tourists, employers and workers in tourism industry. The model is based on previous research, consultation with labour market experts, public data on collective bargaining coverage, public statistical data on labour market and tourism industry from SiStat, Eurostat and OECD, and reports from Hotels, Restaurants & Cafés in Europe association (HOTREC) and European Working Conditions Surveys (EWCS).
venue: Central European Journal of Operations Research

title: Psychological contract breach and diminished organisational citizenship behaviour: the mediation of employee knowledge hiding
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the relationship between psychological contract breach and diminished organisational citizenship behaviour in Southern Nigeria through the mediation of knowledge hiding. Design/methodology/approach The design was a cross-sectional survey. A structured questionnaire served as the instrument for data collection from the respondents. The authors constructed and validated the research instrument. The authors also tested the instrument's reliability. The study used structural equation modelling to analyse the data with a specific focus on the path diagram technique. Findings The results show that an organisation's breach of the relational psychological contract significantly influences employees' knowledge hiding behaviour; employee knowledge hiding behaviour significantly stimulates diminished organisational citizenship behaviour. In addition, employee knowledge hiding significantly mediates the relationship between psychological contract breach (relational, implicit, balanced) and diminished organisational citizenship behaviour. Research limitations/implications A major limitation of the study is the use of a cross-sectional survey design, which is constrained for inferring causality. Nevertheless, the significance or non-significance of the associations between variables in a cross-sectional design is instructive about the hypothesised relations…

title: Same Pressure, Different Outcomes? Land-System Change and the Divergence of Water Quality in São Paulo State (Brazil) and Europe
abstract: Abstract Evidence that land-use change degrades surface water comes almost entirely from single-jurisdiction studies, which cannot ask whether the same land-system pressure is associated with the same water-quality outcome elsewhere. This study combines 41 years of annual MapBiomas land-cover data for six monitored water-management units (UGRHIs) in São Paulo State, Brazil, with a harmonised land-cover and water-quality panel for 179 European NUTS2 regions (LUCAS, cross-checked against Corine Land Cover for 2018, $$r=0.92$$ ). A within/between panel decomposition shows that within-unit increases in artificial land share are associated with lower nitrate (NO 3 –N) in São Paulo ( $$\beta =-0.210$$ standard deviations per percentage point, mixed-model $$p<0.001$$ ) and essentially unrelated to nitrate in Europe ( $$\beta =0.004$$ , 95% CI $$-0.026$$ to 0.034). The São Paulo estimate is stable across data-handling choices and precipitation adjustment, but it is not significant under cluster-robust or wild-cluster-bootstrap inference with six clusters ( $$p=0.23$$ and 0.43) or under a time-series-preserving permutation test ( $$p=0.30$$ ); it disappears when one unit is omitted, when unit-specific trends are allowed, and when land cover is measured over each station’s upstream drainage area ( $$\beta =-0.027$$ ). Biochemical oxygen demand and total phosphorus show no reliable within…

title: Relative efficacy of 25-hydroxycholecalciferol supplementation on growth parameters, bone quality, and plasma concentration in broilers
abstract: Abstract Among metabolites of vitamin D 3 , 25-hydroxycholecalciferol (25-(OH)D 3 ), also referred to as 25-hydroxyvitamin D 3 , is recognized for its bioavailability and utility in poultry rations. This four-arm randomized controlled trial evaluated the outcomes of three commercial products of 25-(OH)D 3 with varying active concentration on growth performance metrics, bone mineralization, and plasma 25-(OH)D 3 levels in broilers relative to an unsupplemented control. A total of 1,500 Ross broiler chicks were allocated to four treatments with 15 replicate pens of 25 birds in each replicate floor pen. Dietary treatments included: T1 - Basal diet (2000 IU/kg of finished feed) + 0 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 , T2 – Basal (2000 IU/kg) + Product A (69 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 ), T3 - Basal (2000 IU/kg) + Product B (69 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 ), and T4 – Basal (2000 IU/kg) + Product C (34.5 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 ). Performance parameters were recorded during starter (day 0 to 14), grower (day 14 to 28) and finisher (day 28 to 43) phases. Tibia mineral contents and plasma 25-(OH)D 3 were measured on day 21 and 43. Feed intake did not differ significantly during starter, grower, and finisher phase ( P > 0.05). Body weight gain was higher in Product A birds compared to Product B and Product C from 0 to 43 days ( P < 0.05). There were no differences between groups in tibia b…

title: Machining performance of flax-reinforced polylactide biocomposites using high-power picosecond lasers
A 1 km gridded dataset of Northern Hemisphere permafrost active layer thickness (2000–2024)
abstract: Active layer thickness (ALT) is a key indicator of permafrost change, with important implications for soil hydrothermal conditions, carbon feedbacks, ecosystem processes, and cold-region infrastructure. However, hemispheric-scale ALT mapping remains challenging because field observations are sparse and unevenly distributed, while thaw depth is controlled by complex and nonlinear environmental interactions. Here, we developed a LightGBM–XGBoost ensemble framework to reconstruct annual ALT on a 1 km grid across the Northern Hemisphere permafrost region from 2000 to 2024. Spatial block cross-validation yielded an R 2 of 0.720 and an RMSE of 39.47 cm, while complementary leave-one-site-out cross-validation achieved an R 2 of 0.780 and an RMSE of 34.98 cm. Temporally blocked validation using all withheld observations from 2021–2024 achieved an R 2 of 0.693 and an RMSE of 26.36 cm, improving to an R 2 of 0.826 and an RMSE of 19.74 cm when evaluation was restricted to previously observed sites. Across 60 long-term monitoring sites, the observed and reconstructed mean ALT series showed close temporal agreement ( r =0.954), although site-specific year-to-year variability was substantially smoothed, with predicted detrended variability reaching only about 64 % of the observed amplitude. The reconstructed ALT showed an overall long-term increase during 2000–2024, together with pronounced …

title: Perceptions of innovation in Brazil and Sweden: A cross-cultural comparison and its implications for human capital development and organizational management
abstract: Although the literature widely explores innovation, it remains under-researched from a cross-cultural perspective that considers associations between national cultures and values, attitudes, and behaviors. Most studies also rely on objective indicators such as patent counts, research and development investments, and university quality. While relevant, these metrics do not fully capture the subjective dimensions of innovation. Focusing on citizens from a developing country and a developed country, this study explored differences in perceptions of innovation between Brazilians and Swedes, discussing them in light of cultural characteristics, human capital development, and organizational management. The sample included 1,486 Brazilians and 1,206 Swedes, and the authors analyzed the data using correlation and comparison methods. Innovation variables included creativity, science, and technology, while Hofstede’s six dimensions characterized national cultures. Sex was the sociodemographic characteristic most frequently associated with positive perceptions of innovation, with men in both countries holding more favorable views. Higher levels of education and income were also associated with more positive perceptions. Swedes held more positive perceptions of innovation than Brazilians. Overall, the results suggested that Brazil’s and Sweden’s cultural characteristics align with their ci…

title: Gender diversity and corporate governance: Effects during the COVID-19 pandemic
Stakeholder relationships and environmental outcomes in natural resource management: a systematic review of mechanisms and governance conditions
abstract: Abstract This systematic review synthesizes 62 empirical studies published between 1996 and 2025 to examine how organizational stakeholder relationships relate to environmental outcomes across emission reduction, resource efficiency, ecological governance, and natural resource stewardship. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches covered Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO Business Source Complete, and ProQuest Business Collection, with explicit coverage of environmental science, ecology, and sustainability subject areas. The natural resource-based view provides the primary theoretical anchor, complemented by environmental governance theory and the community-based resource management literature. Six mechanisms organize the evidence: environmental sensing and early warning, green supply chain co-development, regulatory co-evolution, community-based ecological stewardship, environmental legitimacy accumulation, and collective environmental action. Three boundary conditions qualify the evidence: the association between engagement depth and environmental performance is non-linear; cooperative supply chain programs without credible enforcement show no measurable environmental improvement; and stakeholder selection driven by economic salience may underweight communities most dependent on affected ecosystem services. The evidence base documents eco-efficiency more consistently than ecolog…
authors: M. A. M. L. de Oliveira

title: Tillage and integrated cover crop management effects on soil microclimate, root traits, and winter wheat productivity
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of tillage systems (conventional ploughing, shallow harrowing, and no-tillage) and agricultural technologies (traditional and integrated) on winter wheat root traits, grain yield, soil microclimate, and soil CO 2 efflux over three growing seasons (2022–2024) in a temperate agroecosystem. Root length density (RLD), root diameter, grain yield, soil temperature, volumetric water content, and soil CO 2 efflux were assessed, and relationships among root traits, soil microclimatic conditions, and CO 2 efflux were examined. Integrated technology significantly increased RLD by 6% in 2022 and 13% in 2023, whereas the difference was minimal in 2024. No-tillage produced higher RLD than harrowing and conventional ploughing in 2022 and 2023, whereas tillage effects were not significant in 2024. Grain yield varied markedly among years, coinciding with contrasting seasonal climatic conditions. Integrated technology increased yield by 12% in 2022, whereas no-tillage significantly reduced yield in 2024. Soil CO 2 efflux declined from 2022 to 2024 and was highest in 2022, which had the greatest May–July precipitation, indicating an association between seasonal water availability and soil respiration. Relationships between root traits and soil CO 2 efflux were weak and inconsistent across years, indicating that variation in total soil respiration could not be expl…

title: Groundwater sustainability in hyper-arid regions: Integrated groundwater modeling of Qatar’s aquifers under climate change and management scenarios
Navigating cross-cultural dynamics in European multinational firms: How acculturation strategies influence African indigenous employee outcomes
abstract: Purpose: This research examines how acculturation strategies impact employee restiveness, internal legitimacy and job satisfaction among local workers in European multinational firms in Africa. Design/methodology/approach: Utilising a quantitative research design, the study uses a structured questionnaire to draw data from 515 indigenous employees in German-owned and French-owned multinational firms. The hypothesis was tested using structural equation modelling. Findings/results: Contrary to expectations, the results suggest that integration strategy significantly addresses employee restiveness, internal legitimacy and job satisfaction in German-owned and French-owned multinational firms in Nigeria. Conversely, assimilation, separation and marginalisation acculturation strategies were found to have insignificant influence on internal legitimacy, employee restiveness and job satisfaction among the employees. Practical implications: The outcomes of this study will enable managers to understand the appropriate acculturation strategy that can help foreign firms to gain internal legitimacy and address employee restiveness and job satisfaction in Africa. The findings will also motivate foreign firms to provide support to local employees to adopt the beneficial acculturation strategy for the overall benefit of the organisation and the employees. Originality/value: This study makes two…

title: Low-Power Ultrasound-Assisted Methanesulfonic Acid–Formic Acid Pretreatment Coupled with Simultaneous Saccharification and Fermentation for Bioethanol Production from Sugarcane Leaves
abstract: This study investigates an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable approach to enhancing bioethanol production from sugarcane leaves through synergistic pretreatment using low-power ultrasound and an organic acid co-solvent system. To reduce the energy demand and environmental impact associated with conventional pretreatment methods, methanesulfonic acid (MSA) and formic acid (FA) were combined under low-power ultrasonic conditions. A Box–Behnken design (BBD) based on response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to optimize the FA concentration, ultrasonication time, and ultrasound power. The optimal conditions were identified as 29.17% FA, 18.70 min of ultrasonication, and an ultrasound power of 16.61 W, with the MSA concentration maintained at 5%. These conditions promoted the disruption of the lignocellulosic structure through acoustic cavitation and acid-assisted modification, thereby enhancing cellulose accessibility while minimizing energy consumption. Subsequent simultaneous saccharification and fermentation (SSF) using Saccharomyces cerevisiae at 32 °C with an enzyme loading of 50 FPU/g achieved an ethanol yield of 73.22% of the theoretical yield (on a cellulose basis), corresponding to an ethanol concentration of 12.602 mg/mL after 48 h. Extending the fermentation time to 72 h resulted in only a marginal increase in ethanol yield of 0.8%, suggesting that a …

title: ANALISIS PERFORMA MODEL CNN MELALUI EVALUASI EKSTERNAL PADA SISTEM KLASIFIKASI CITRA MAMMOGRAFI BERBASIS WEBSITE LOKAL
abstract: The performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for mammographic image classification needs to be evaluated using data that were not involved in model development to assess its ability to generalize to data from different sources. This study aims to analyze the performance of a CNN model through external evaluation on a local web-based mammographic image classification system. The method involved applying the previously developed EfficientNetB2 model to 15 clinical mammographic images as external data. Each image was entered into the system to obtain its classification result, which was then compared with the diagnostic label in the original data. During the model development stage, the EfficientNetB2 model achieved an accuracy of 72%, precision of 67%, recall of 96% and an F1-score of 79%. The external evaluation results showed that 13 out of 15 images produced predictions consistent with their diagnostic labels, while 2 images produced inconsistent predictions, resulting in a prediction agreement rate of 86.67%. Based on the confusion matrix, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.67%, precision of 80%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 88.89%. The external evaluation provides an overview of the model’s generalization capability when applied to data outside its development environment through a local web-based system.

title: Fluctuation in China’s liquefied natural gas import prices and risk transmission mechanism: an empirical study from the perspective of the eco-environment-oriented development model
abstract: Introduction This study is an exploratory analysis. From the perspective of the Eco-environment-oriented Development (EOD) model, this study constructs a three-dimensional transmission model of “international oil prices–geopolitical risk–environmental policy” to explore the drivers and risk transmission paths of China’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) import price fluctuations. Methods Using monthly data (September 2021 to September 2024) on China’s LNG import prices, international oil prices (Brent and WTI), the Geopolitical Risk (GPR) Index, and the Environmental Policy Index (EPI), we conduct a dynamic empirical analysis via a vector autoregression (VAR) model. Results The research findings indicate that, based on asymptotic standard error statistics, the bootstrap robustness check reveals that only the contribution of GPR (22.81%, 95% Bootstrap CI: 3.04%–42.59%) is statistically significant, making it the only robust driver of price fluctuations within the sample period. The contributions of international oil prices (Brent point estimate 13.54%, WTI point estimate 10.05%) and environmental policy (EPI point estimate 11.38%) do not reach statistical significance under bootstrap inference; their point estimates are provided only as directional references and require further validation with larger samples. Discussion The study suggests possible transmission pathways of “internatio…

title: Research on the Construction Mechanism of Enterprise Flexible Supply Chain Management and Competitive Advantage in Platform Economy
abstract: The platform economy uses data connections and rule collaboration to reshape supply chain organizations. Demand fluctuations and external disturbances make traditional chain management slow to respond and resources rigid. This article uses literature review and theoretical analysis to conduct research around enterprise flexible supply chain management and competitive advantage construction under the platform economy. First, define the organizational characteristics of the platform economy, flexible supply chain dimensions and the logic of competitive advantage formation; secondly, analyze demand fluctuations and forecast deviations, cross-subject collaboration and data barriers, platform dependence and risk transmission and other practical constraints; then build a "data perception - resource orchestration - collaborative performance - value feedback" mechanism framework, and propose an implementation path from the aspects of unified and scalable platform architecture, supplier portfolio and flexible operations, risk governance and performance evaluation, etc., and use organizational structure and talent capabilities, platform governance and interest coordination as guarantees. The study believes that the advantage of flexible supply chain is not the result of a single resource or technology, but the linkage effect of demand identification, resource reorganization and ecologica…

title: Bidentate Chelation-Driven Selective Depression of Pyrite: Adsorption Mechanism and Flotation Application of an N-Heterocyclic Carboxylic Acid Depressant
abstract: Abstract The selective flotation separation of chalcopyrite and pyrite constitutes a core bottleneck in the comprehensive utilization of copper–sulfur ores. Given the proneness of pyrite to copper activation and pipeline scaling defects induced by the conventional high-alkaline lime depression process, novel organic depressants with outstanding selectivity under weak alkaline media are urgently required to be developed. In this study, 3-hydroxy-2-pyridine carboxylic acid (3-HPA) was adopted as a novel eco-friendly organic depressant to realize the selective flotation separation of chalcopyrite from pyrite under weakly acidic conditions (pH = 6). The selective depression mechanism of 3-HPA against pyrite was systematically investigated via microflotation assays, multiscale surface characterizations, and first-principles theoretical computations. Flotation experimental data verified that 3-HPA is capable of selectively depressing pyrite floatability while maintaining excellent floatability of chalcopyrite, with a maximum recovery gap of 92.71% observed between the two minerals. Collectively, 3-HPA serves as an efficient and highly selective organic depressant for pyrite. On pyrite surfaces, 3-HPA undergoes bidentate chelation with surface iron active sites: the nitrogen atom on its pyridine ring and the oxygen atoms of the carboxyl group coordinate with Fe atoms to generate stabl…

title: Low-carbon city pilot policy, carbon emission reduction effect of agricultural inputs, and transmission pathways: evidence from a quasi-natural experiment at the prefecture level in China based on multi-period DID
abstract: Introduction Low-carbon city pilot policies constitute an important institutional practice for advancing the green and low-carbon transition of agriculture and achieving the “Dual-Carbon” goals. Scientific assessment of the agricultural emission-reduction effects of this policy is critical for land and food security. Methods Based on prefecture-level panel data of China spanning 2005–2024, this paper adopts a multi-period staggered Difference-in-Differences (DID) model to systematically examine the impacts of low-carbon city pilot policies on carbon emissions associated with agricultural inputs, and provides associational evidence on the transmission mechanisms. Given that the conventional two-way fixed-effect multi-period DID may yield potential bias under strong heterogeneity, this study further employs the Callaway-Sant’Anna staggered DID (CS-DID) to estimate the dynamic treatment effects for different cohorts. Multiple robustness strategies including PSM and placebo tests are also applied to validate regression results and improve the credibility of causal inference. Results The study finds that low-carbon city pilot policies significantly reduce regional Agricultural input-related carbon emissions mainly through three pathways: optimizing agricultural factor allocation, forcing the low-carbon transformation of agricultural industrial structure, and improving agricultural e…

title: Spillover effect between oil prices, climate risks, and carbon prices in China: dynamic effects and key drivers
abstract: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and volatile international oil markets, the interdependence among energy prices, climate-risk information, and carbon markets has become increasingly prominent. Clarifying their dynamic spillover patterns is important for climate governance, energy security, and carbon-market risk management. This study examines the dynamic interactions among decomposed oil price shocks, physical and transition climate-risk indices, and China’s regional carbon price represented by the Guangdong pilot market. The research design is structured in three stages. First, oil price fluctuations are decomposed into supply, demand, and risk shocks following Ready (2018), and a time-varying parameter vector autoregressive (TVP-VAR) model is employed to capture evolving spillovers. Second, the Baruník–Křehlík (2018) frequency-domain spillover framework is used to distinguish short- and long-horizon connectedness. Third, the XGBoost–SHAP framework is used as a post-estimation predictive complement to identify nonlinear feature contributions to changes in spillover intensity; the resulting SHAP values are interpreted as feature-association evidence rather than structural causal estimates. The results show that: (1) oil price shocks, carbon prices, and climate risks exhibit substantial volatility spillovers, with short-term spillovers considerably stro…

Sedimentary organic carbon contents control the nitrate reduction potential in a Holocene aquifer: Evidence from batch incubations
abstract: Abstract Groundwater quality is increasingly threatened by nitrate (NO 3 − ) contamination from agricultural activities. In many aquifers, NO 3 − is attenuated through microbially mediated reduction coupled to the oxidation of reduced constituents in the aquifer matrix. However, predicting NO 3 − turnover at the aquifer scale remains difficult because electron donors such as organic carbon and reduced sulfur species are heterogeneously distributed and reliable proxies for NO 3 − reduction potential are lacking. To address this challenge, batch experiments were conducted using eight facies types from a previously characterized tufaceous Holocene aquifer in southwestern Germany. The facies exhibited a wide range of solid-phase organic carbon contents (SOC 0.5–40.1 wt.%). NO 3 − reduction in batches was assessed by monitoring temporal changes in NO 3 − , sulfate (SO 4 2− ), and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentrations. NO 3 − reduction followed a two-phase pattern: An initial rapid, nonlinear decrease likely driven by readily bioavailable DOC, followed by a linear decline consistent with zero-order kinetics. Long-term NO 3 − reduction rates showed a strong positive relationship with solid phase organic carbon (SOC) ( R 2 = 0.69) across all microcosms ( n = 40) and facies ( n = 8). Experimental reduction rates were combined with facies-specific horizontal groundwater flow velo…

title: Mediation of soil aggregate stability and carbon sequestration by meadow steppe soil microorganisms under long-term nitrogen and phosphorus nutrient additions
Explainable machine learning identifies a one-carbon–epigenetic axis associated with sperm DNA fragmentation in reproductive-age men with cancer: a retrospective translational cohort study
abstract: Background Cancer can perturb systemic metabolism, redox homeostasis, and germ-cell genomic integrity before gonadotoxic therapy. Homocysteine (Hcy), a central intermediate of one-carbon metabolism, links methyl-donor balance, oxidative stress, and DNA methylation. We investigated whether serum Hcy was associated with sperm DNA fragmentation in reproductive-age men with cancer and whether explainable machine learning could integrate clinical, semen, and molecular features to characterize a candidate one-carbon–redox–epigenetic axis associated with high DNA fragmentation index (DFI). Methods This retrospective translational cohort included men referred for fertility preservation before systemic therapy or radiotherapy. The primary outcome was high sperm DFI (≥30%). Multivariable logistic regression and three machine-learning algorithms were evaluated using a 70% development/30% hold-out split. An archived-sample substudy assessed oxidative stress, global sperm DNA 5-methylcytosine, and MTHFR- and DNMT3A-related expression as candidate readouts of one-carbon and epigenetic regulation. Results Among 286 men, high DFI occurred in 26.2%. Serum Hcy correlated with DFI (Spearman ρ = 0.476, P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, BMI, smoking, varicocele, recent fever, and cancer type, each 5-µmol/L increase in Hcy was associated with higher odds of high DFI (adjusted OR 7.10, 95% CI …

title: Bio-inspired interfacial engineering of carbon fabric@ZIF-67@cobalt phytate towards enhanced fire safety and mechanical properties of epoxy composites
abstract: Abstract Carbon fabric-reinforced epoxy composites (EP/CF) are vital structural materials for engineering fields, but the intrinsic trade-off between fire safety and mechanical properties restricts their high-end applications. Inspired by the hierarchical structure of stylophora pistillata, a bio-inspired, interfacially-engineered carbon fabric@ZIF-67@cobalt phytate hybrid (CF@ZIF-67@CoPhy) was synthesized via in-situ ZIF-67 growth and subsequent phytate coordination. Systematic characterizations via Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed the successful fabrication of micro-nano hierarchical interfacial structure on the tailored hybrid. The as-synthesized CF@ZIF-67@CoPhy was incorporated into EP to fabricate advanced composites. The resultant composites exhibited prominently enhanced fire safety, with the limiting oxygen index (LOI) of 35.6%, UL-94 V-0 rating, and 63.4% reduction in peak heat release rate (PHRR). Such outstanding flame-retardant enhancements stemmed primarily from the synergistic catalytic carbonization of ZIF-67 and CoPhy during combustion. Meanwhile, the modified composites achieved significant mechanical reinforcement. Specifically, the tensile strength, flexural strength and impact strength were increased by 35.0%, 30.9% and 54.6%, re…

title: Synthesis and characterization of diglycidyl methacrylamide epoxy resin as a corrosion inhibition performance for carbon steel in 1.0 M HCl solution: experimental, DFT calculations, and molecular dynamics simulation
Income differences in high-carbon activities, climate perceptions and behavioral willingness: an exploratory analysis of a UK survey
abstract: Introduction Radical actions across all sectors of the economy are necessary to meet stringent carbon emission reduction targets, which requires the widespread adoption of low-carbon technologies as well as significant lifestyle changes. However, carbon emissions are not evenly distributed across households—both globally and within countries—indicating that different income groups have unequal responsibilities for reducing emissions. Policy directed at higher-income households therefore rests on untested assumption that those who contribute more feel more responsible and are more ready to act given their greater resources. Method As an initial step, this exploratory study uses secondary data from a survey conducted in October and November 2023 in the UK, which oversampled higher-income respondents, to examining income-based differences in activities associated with high-carbon consumption, climate perceptions, and willingness to engage in pro-environmental behaviors. Results Results show that higher-income groups are more likely to engage in activities associated with high-carbon consumption, as indicated by their flying, car ownership, and recent purchases of household items. However, income groups in the UK do not differ significantly in their climate perceptions, including concern about climate change, feelings of guilt, or a sense of personal responsibility to take climate …

title: Database-driven divergence in carbon footprint estimates for Chinese refined copper supply chains
abstract: Refined copper is critical to the global energy transition, yet carbon footprint estimates for Chinese primary production vary because background databases represent concentrate supply, electricity systems, and process conditions differently. Using 2025 operational data from two Chinese smelters, this study developed cradle-to-gate inventories for Ausmelt-based and double-flash production systems and evaluated them across five software-database-modeling configurations. Across these configurations, the observed Ausmelt case yielded 5.9-7.1 t CO2e/t Cu, whereas the double-flash case yielded 4.6-6.3 t CO2e/t Cu. Because feed composition and operating conditions were not normalized, this contrast represents the sampled plant systems rather than an intrinsic technology effect. Upstream concentrate production was the main source of inter-configuration divergence. A controlled parameter-transfer check reproduced the SimaPro result in OpenLCA within 0.008%, indicating transfer fidelity rather than native cross-software equivalence; the estimated OpenLCA-ecoinvent 3.11 result was 1.31% lower than the reconstructed ecoinvent 3.10 case. Paired Monte Carlo analysis confirmed the case-level ordering and showed that inter-configuration dispersion exceeded within-configuration parameter uncertainty. After consistently rebasing the electricity-factor trajectory, combined process-efficiency imp…

title: Engineered interface in sunlight-driven non-oxidative ethane dehydrogenation
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic reactions powered by solar energy are essential for capitalizing on renewable solar resources. However, efficiently utilizing the entire sunlight spectrum for reactions with high activation energy, such as alkane dehydrogenation, poses a major challenge in catalyst design. In this research, we propose a surface modification strategy that generates abundant interfacial sites on the TiN surface while preserving strong light absorption, promoting interfacial electron-hole recombination, and supporting catalytic reactions across the full spectrum. Through a combination of spectroscopic, theoretical, and experimental investigations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of this catalyst design in enhancing solar energy utilization. We have successfully developed a SrTiO3/SrOx-TiN catalyst that significantly enhances the activity of non-oxidative ethane dehydrogenation by 11.7-fold under solar photocatalysis. The strategy revealed in this work, which involves constructing abundant reaction sites with enhanced interfacial electron-hole recombination, is vital for developing advanced heterogeneous solar photocatalytic systems.

title: Experimental investigation and parametric analysis of laser-based fusion bonding of polyamide 6 to AISI 1018 low-carbon steel
abstract: Abstract This study investigates laser-assisted metal–plastic (LAMP) joining of polyamide 6 (PA6) to AISI 1018 low-carbon steel using a 1 kW fibre laser system. The individual and interaction effects of four key process parameters, laser power, scanning speed, defocus distance, and number of scans, on joint quality are examined using a central composite design of the response surface method. An empirical model is developed to correlate lap-shear strength with these parameters and validated through analysis of variance and additional experiments, confirming predictive reliability. Careful control of process conditions ensures balanced heat input and laser interaction time, enabling enhanced interfacial adhesion while limiting polymer degradation and thereby improving joint performance. A maximum lap-shear strength of 45.86 N mm −1 for the AISI 1018/PA6 joint, about 66 % of the tensile strength of 2 mm-thick PA6, is achieved using 900 W laser power, 35 mm s −1 scanning speed, 40 mm defocus distance, and two scan passes. Post-shear analysis reveals PA6 residues and elongated fibrils on the steel surface, confirming strong interfacial adhesion and load transfer. Failure modes exhibit both adhesive and cohesive characteristics, influenced by process parameters. These findings confirm LAMP joining as a reliable method for fabricating durable AISI 1018/PA6 hybrids with adequate joint …

title: Defect-Tolerant Conduction Band Formation in SrBi3O4Cl3 through Interlayer Bi 6p Orbital Coupling
abstract: Abstract The control of defect-induced electron trap levels is crucial for regulating the reactivity of photogenerated charge carriers. Although electron trapping can suppress rapid electron–hole recombination, excessive deep trapping lowers the energy and mobility of photogenerated electrons, thereby reducing their reactivity. Thus, controlling trap depth is essential for improving photocatalysts and other photofunctional materials. However, rational design principles remain limited. Here, we compare two layered bismuth oxychlorides, SrBiO2Cl and SrBi3O4Cl3, using time-resolved absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. These materials consist of stacked fluorite-like oxide slabs separated by chloride layers: SrBiO2Cl contains [SrBiO2]+ slabs, whereas SrBi3O4Cl3 contains Bi-rich regions in adjacent slabs that face each other across a single chloride layer. This structural contrast provides a suitable platform to examine how interlayer Bi 6p coupling modifies the conduction band minimum (CBM) and affects defect-induced electron trapping. Transient absorption measurements revealed that photogenerated electrons in SrBiO2Cl are predominantly trapped in deep defect states, whereas SrBi3O4Cl3 retains a substantial population of free and/or shallowly trapped electrons in the microsecond time region. DFT calculations indicated that, in SrBiO2Cl, the abse…

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Water Security in Western Rajasthan: A Study of Selected Renewable Energy Companies
abstract: The western parts of Rajasthan experience water scarcity owing to the arid nature of the climate and low amount of rainfall in the area. As such, the CSR programs of renewable energy companies have immense importance in conserving the water resources as well as uplifting the rural population. This research analyzes the water-based CSR initiatives of Suzlon Energy Limited and Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) in western Rajasthan. Using the descriptive research methodology, the paper is based only on corporate annual reports and any other available corporate public reports. The analysis is conducted by classifying and examining company's interventions in pond construction, desilting, and construction of water infrastructure. It is found that both the companies have carried out many water projects; however, type of activities and places have varied in different financial years. Furthermore, it is found that there is a serious lack of information in the corporation's reports, especially about the number of beneficiaries and project viability in the long run. It is concluded that the water projects by CSR programs have great potential to increase water security of rural areas provided they are monitored constantly.

AI Integration in Automotive Packaging Engineering for Multi-Constraint Component Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a framework for the packaging of components in a vehicle's threedimensional structure that is grounded in evidence and reproducible when taking advantage of the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The public OSU–Honda CarHoods10k dataset provides over 10,000 3D hood-frame designs based on 109 parameterized designs, along with design parameters and finite element (FE) performance data. The data package is about 45.66 GB, including design parameters and finite-element (FE) performance data. This dataset is not a multi-component vehicle-layout dataset and can't be used for a complete validation of a vehicle packaging optimizer: thermal, service access, or assembly data of the vehicle are not available at the component level. The studies of published adjacent work have shown that an improved solution with 3 times less computational budget could be offered, a result specific to this study but not predicted for automotive packaging. The proposed framework formalizes the placement variables, geometric constraints, engineering constraints, a model of screening by an artificial neural network (ANN), and a genetic search by NSGA- II, where the two objectives change. It also defines a controlled validation protocol to manual and rule-based baselines. There are no new vehicle-program performance gains since no proprietary vehicle-program layout dataset, e…

title: Tunable crystallinity in cellulose nanofiber-polyethylene oxide electrolyte films for stable quasi-solid-state lithium-metal batteries
abstract: Solid-state lithium-metal batteries are promising next-generation energy storage systems owing to their high energy density and enhanced safety. However, conventional polyethylene oxide (PEO)-based solid polymer electrolytes have low ionic conductivity at room temperature, poor Li+ transference numbers, and unstable electrode interfaces, which hinder their practical deployment. Herein, we report quasi-solid polymer electrolyte (quasi-SPE) films prepared by blending cellulose nanofiber (CNF) with PEO in various ratios (0.50:0-0.50:2.0), incorporating 1 M Lithium bis(trifluoromethane)sulfonimide (LiTFSI) in 1,3-Dioxolane (DOL):1,2-Dimethoxyethane (DME) (1:1 vol%) with 1 wt.% LiNO3. Structural analyses [X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy] revealed that moderate PEO incorporation disrupted CNF crystallinity and generated amorphous domains that enhanced polymer chain mobility and Li-ion transport, whereas excessive PEO promoted recrystallization. Within the composition range of 0.50-1.50, ionic conductivity reached ~10-4 S·cm-1 at room temperature. Notably, CP-1.00 emerged as the balanced formulation for lithium-metal battery applications, achieving a Li+ transference number of 0.46 and a wide electrochemical stability window of 4.68 V vs. Li+/Li…

title: Accelerating the transition: a policy and practice review of alternative vehicle adoption and infrastructure readiness in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Transport decarbonization in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) requires approaches that reflect differences in vehicle use, electricity systems, financing, industrial priorities and institutional capacity. This Structured Policy and Practice Review synthesizes research and policy/practice evidence on alternative vehicle pathways and infrastructure readiness through four purposively selected country cases: Rwanda, Kenya, South Africa and Nigeria. It considers electric two- and three-wheelers, electric buses and minibuses, passenger electric vehicles, battery-as-a-service (BaaS), charging and battery swapping, renewable energy integrated charging, compressed natural gas (CNG), and emerging hydrogen applications. Across the cases, adoption is shaped by upfront costs, foreign exchange exposure, electricity access and reliability, local distribution network capacity, charging and refueling availability, battery lifecycle management, and the design and implementation of policy. The evidence suggests that high-utilization commercial fleets may offer early electrification opportunities where duty cycles, financing and charging arrangements are suitable; this is not a universal conclusion, and passenger electric vehicles, public transport electrification and alternative fuels may be relevant in other contexts. Solar plus storage, managed charging, time-of-use tariffs and vehicle-to-grid services…

title: Image reconstruction based on FWHM-energy joint weighting for magnetic particle imaging
abstract: Abstract Objective. Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) enables high-sensitivity quantitative imaging by detecting the nonlinear magnetization response of superparamagnetic nanoparticles. field-free-point (FFP)-gridded MPI has been developed to reduce system complexity, and its multi-harmonic extension exploits harmonic-dependent information to balance spatial resolution and SNR. However, an appropriate weighting strategy is required to utilize complementary information across harmonics. We propose an image reconstruction method based on full width at half maximum (FWHM)-energy joint weighting, which combines PSF-derived FWHM with either L2-norm harmonic energy or noise energy to achieve a favorable trade-off between spatial resolution enhancement and reconstruction stability. Approach. In the FFP-gridded multi-harmonic fusion framework, the 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th harmonic components are jointly used for image reconstruction. Since different harmonics exhibit distinct characteristics in signal intensity, noise level, and spatial resolution, optimizing their weights is essential for improving reconstruction quality. Traditional weighting strategies based on amplitude, signal energy, and noise characteristics were implemented as comparison methods. On this basis, two FWHM-energy joint weighting strategies were developed: L2-norm energy-FWHM weighting for balancing resolution improvem…

title: Oral health integration in antenatal care: knowledge, attitudes and practices of practicing gynecologists and obstetricians in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan – a multicenter cross-sectional study
Assessing Total Heat Load as a Proxy for Optimising Operating Specifications in Extractive Distillation
abstract: Abstract In this work, it is assessed whether the total heat load of the two-column extractive distillation system is a useful proxy for determining the optimal number of stages in systems that use cooling water in the condensers and steam in the reboilers. Thereafter, the optimal operating specifications of the extractive distillation column must be updated accordingly. The heuristic method features a straightforward, sequential, iterative optimisation approach for theoretical designs of a two-column extractive distillation sequence, developed using a process simulator. Four case studies are optimised to demonstrate the methodology’s suitability. The results were compared against simulated annealing, full total annual cost sweeps and data available in the literature. In all four cases, the proxy guided the choice of reflux ratio, and total annual cost determined the stage count. The operating specifications were then refined. Essentially, the proxy is utilised to identify the trend in total annual cost with the stage number of the extractive distillation column; therefore, the location or region where the optimal number of stages exists can be rapidly identified. Due to its efficiency, the proposed approach can theoretically be utilised to determine the optimal system specifications, using more complex modelling approaches, such as rate-based simulations.

title: APPLICATION OF DEEP ESN NETWORKS AND WAVELET DECOMPOSITION FOR ENERGY CONSUMPTION FORECASTING IN BUILDINGS
abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the application of deep Echo State Networks (DeepESN) combined with wavelet decomposition for short-term forecasting of daily natural gas consumption in a building. The proposed approach includes extracting the temperature-related component using linear regression, wavelet decomposition of the residual signal, and independent forecasting of the resulting components using NAR, ESN, and DeepESN models. The experimental study was conducted using real data on natural gas consumption and outdoor air temperature from eleven heating seasons. The last season was used exclusively as an independent test set. Forecasting accuracy was evaluated using RMSE and MAE. The results showed that, among the investigated models, DeepESN provided the best forecasting performance for the complete time series, achieving an RMSE of 92.17 m³/day and an MAE of 55.52 m³/day. The results demonstrate the applicability of combining wavelet decomposition with DeepESN for short-term natural gas consumption forecasting.

title: Energy transfer in shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interactions
abstract: Abstract The energy transport and exchange processes among the mean kinetic energy (MKE), turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), mean internal energy and turbulent internal energy in a shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interaction (SBLI) are quantified using direct numerical simulations. By analyzing the transport budgets of mean and fluctuating energy modes, the primary mechanisms governing energy transfer cycles within the interaction region are identified. Results show that energy transfer is dominated by three key processes: turbulence production ( $$P_k$$ P k ), which transfers energy from the mean flow to turbulence, mean pressure dilatation ( $$\Phi^{pm}$$ Φ pm ), which mediates the compressibility-driven energy exchange between MKE and mean internal energy, and viscous dissipation ( $$\varepsilon$$ ε ), which irreversibly converts TKE into mean internal energy. The effects of variable density and terms related to turbulent internal energy are found to be negligible. The present work clarifies the essential energy transfer pathways in SBLI, offering valuable insights for the development of improved turbulence closure models and the design of effective flow control strategies.

title: Solar photovoltaics and hydrogen energy as pathways to a sustainable future
From wound to essence: a hypothesis and theory article proposing the Integrative Emotional Alchemy Framework for psychotherapy integration and transformation
abstract: Contemporary psychotherapy suffers from paradigm fragmentation: affective neuroscience, depth psychology, and evidence-based interventions (EFT, IFS, mindfulness) operate in disciplinary silos without a unifying theory explaining why diverse methods converge on similar therapeutic outcomes. We propose the Integrative Emotional Alchemy Framework (IEAF), a three-stratum theory positing that emotional suffering and transformation operate through nested architecture: (1) Six Wounds of Humanity (Repression, Denial, Shame, Rejection, Guilt, Separation) as ontological core; (2) Eleven Emotion Families as phenomenological middle stratum; and (3) a preliminary taxonomy of Sixty-Four Shadows as behavioural surface patterns. We hypothesise that transformation follows a Shadow→Gift→Essence trajectory, potentially instantiated through reconfiguration of the Default Mode, Executive Control, and Salience Networks, culminating in Fundamental Peace—a dynamic capacity characterised by flexible attentional control, emotional coherence, reduced self-referential rigidity, and compassionate self-awareness. The framework draws on Perceptual Control Theory to provide the functional architecture through which regulation is understood, and synthesises evidence from more than 80 sources across affective neuroscience, psychotherapy research, and contemplative science. A seven-movement clinical protocol (D…

COVID-19 impact on households’ energy poverty and clean energy transition in China
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound yet understudied impact on energy poverty and clean energy transition among households. Using at least 6000 and up to 12,000 household longitudinal data from the China Family Panel Studies from 2014 through 2022, this study implements multiple empirical strategies to assess these effects on urban and rural Chinese households. Our findings reveal that the pandemic disrupted the pre-existing trend of rising electricity usage and exacerbated energy inequality, as indicated by shifts in the Lorenz curves of household energy expenditure. In particular, the energy poverty of rural households increased more rapidly than that of their urban counterparts in the post-pandemic era. Moreover, the growth rates of energy poverty incidence, depth, and intensity decelerated following the outbreak, suggesting a partial regression of energy poverty alleviation interventions, particularly in western and certain central regions compared to the more developed eastern Chinese provinces. Finally, the pandemic shock further intensified household energy poverty, whereby structurally advantaged households demonstrated resilience, but marginalized households experienced deepened deprivation. These insights highlight the urgency of implementing affordable, equitable, and resilience-based clean energy policy interventions in and beyond China.

title: Two Years of the Journal of Geo-Energy and Environment: Progress and Future Directions
abstract: Founded in 2025, the Journal of Geo-Energy and Environment (JGEE) provides a forum for research on geo-energy and the environmental issues associated with its development. In its first two publication years, 2025 and 2026, the journal published six issues containing 30 articles. It is now indexed by Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) and has become a Partner Journal of the International Mine Safety and Emergency Rescue Association. Two Honorary Editors-in-Chief have been appointed, and the editorial board has been restructured. This editorial reviews the journal's progress over this period and summarizes the main findings reported in its published articles. It then outlines future research directions in geothermal energy, hydrogen energy, subsurface energy storage, and geological carbon storage. Academic quality, open scholarly exchange, and international collaboration remain the priorities that will guide the journal's development and its contribution to geo-energy and environmental research.

title: Design for care and connection: consideration for how spatial and sensory factors in care home dayrooms influence social interaction
abstract: This article examines how architectural design decisions in care home dayrooms shape social interaction possibilities for residents. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork conducted in a care home in South Wales, the research reveals persistent contradictions between spatial patterns and lived realities. While care home dayrooms are theoretically positioned as domestic spaces supporting connection and well-being, institutional imperatives and regulatory compliance generate environments that can inadvertently undermine the social interactions they intend to enable. The study employs layered floor-plan analysis to document how residents navigate sensory conditions (lighting, acoustics, temperature), negotiate territorial claims and adapt spaces through micropractices of occupation. Findings demonstrate that dayrooms function as ‘unnatural third spaces’ performing third-place functions within institutionally constrained and spatially mandatory settings that lack the neutral ground, accessibility and playful atmosphere that characterise authentic third places. As residents’ lifeworlds contract, from public to institutional realms, these communal areas become sole arenas for casual encounters, yet their design often reflects assumptions divorced from empirical understanding of spatial experience. The article contributes detailed ethnographic evidence to debates on institutional space, sp…

title: Permit-Ready by Design: A Quantitative Checklist Framework to Reduce Municipal Water/Wastewater Resubmittals
abstract: Municipal water and wastewater projects must be submitted with comprehensive, coordinated, and traceable documents, but no readily available pre-submission quality-control metric exists. This research introduces a 30-item Permit Readiness Index (PRI) with six different weighted domains that are based on the primary needs and requirements of agencies in the United States as well as water utilities. This study compared the feasibility of analyzing public records and is a source-linked, purposive audit of 20 completed water-supply construction permits from Iowa and 20 water or wastewater correction comments received by the City of Tucson. The median interval from receipt to review was 30.5 calendar days (interquartile range [IQR] 22.75–51.00), and the median interval from receipt to finalization was 53.0 days (IQR 27.75–99.75). The study categorized significant comments into eight preestablished deficiency categories, and the number of comments in each category was illustrative only because the categories were intentionally diversified. In an ancillary analysis limited to pumpers living within the treatment and water-main boundaries in Iowa, the odds ratio for treatment water versus the combined treatment+storage/pumping cohort for finalization on the 60-day treatment time was 6.00 (95% Wald CI 0.81–44.35; p = 0.079). title: Food as Medicine: Design and Implementation of a Produce Prescription Program at Federally Qualified Health Centers
abstract: Background: The Bronx faces high food insecurity rates. Previous health center–based programs to improve fruit and vegetable intake and address food insecurity showed limited provider engagement and participant uptake. To address these gaps, we implemented a redesigned Food as Medicine Produce Prescription program at federally qualified health centers in New York City. Methods: We enrolled adults (≥18 years) screening positive for food insecurity. Provider engagement was measured through Best Practices Advisory alerts and direct referrals; participant uptake was tracked by enrollment and retention (January 2023–April 2024). Results: By April 2024, 1790 Best Practices Advisory generated 911 expressions of interest and 34 direct referrals, leading to 395 enrollments. Of these, 145 completed 6 months, 202 dropped out, and 48 remained active. Completers attended 10 of 12 distributions on average; 315 participants joined 35 food demonstrations. Conclusions: Provider input and engagement were critical to successful recruitment and retention.

title: PENGARUH PRODUCT DESIGN DAN BRAND IMAGE TERHADAP PURCHASE INTENTION KONSUMEN PADA TOKO BINTANG TAS SUKAREGANG GARUT
abstract: This study examines the standing of product design, brand image, and purchase intention among customers of Toko Bintang Tas Sukaregang in Garut, alongside the extent to which product appearance and brand perception contribute to consumers’ willingness to buy. A quantitative design was employed under a descriptive-verificative framework. Data were elicited through Likert-scale questionnaires completed by 100 customers and visitors recruited using purposive sampling. The responses were subsequently examined through descriptive statistics, classical assumption checks, and multiple linear regression using SPSS version 20. The assessment indicated that all three variables occupied a moderate level. Partially, product design exerted a significant effect on purchase intention (t = 8.082 > t table = 1.985; sig. 0.000 < 0.05) and emerged as the most influential determinant, while brand image also showed a significant influence (t = 3.527 > t table = 1.985; sig. 0.001 < 0.05). Simultaneously, both predictors significantly explained 46.8% of the variation in purchase intention (F = 42.733 > F table = 3.09; sig. 0.000 < 0.05). The novelty of this study lies in examining the effects of product design and brand image on purchase intention within the retail trade of local leather products in the Sukaregang Garut industrial cluster, a highly competitive business environment that has received l…

Rethinking Design Skill Formation in Fashion Design Curricula Under Outcome-Based Education: A Document Analysis Approach
abstract: Outcome-based education increasingly requires fashion design programs to demonstrate how professional competencies are developed and assessed. This study examines the 2025 Bachelor of Fashion Design curriculum at Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology and Education, Vietnam, to investigate the distribution, integration, and formal documentation of professional competencies. A qualitative document analysis was conducted using the curriculum framework, program learning outcomes, course learning outcomes, course syllabi, outcome mapping matrices, and quality assurance documents from the 2021–2025 review cycle. A deductive framework was used to analyze three domains: Design Thinking, Technical–Technological Competency, and Professional Practice. Technical–Technological Competency represents 48.1% of the 131 curriculum credits, followed by Professional Practice at 27.5% and Design Thinking at 24.4%. Design Thinking is integrated into 42 of 65 courses (57.3%), but is less consistently articulated in written course learning outcomes, particularly in technical courses. The findings identify an Outcome-Based Education Documentation Gap between competencies enacted through learning activities and those explicitly represented in formal outcome mapping and assessment. The study proposes a competency-oriented framework for improving outcome articulation, competency progression, assessmen…

title: Modification to Improve the Structural Performance of Hybrid Reinforcements Made of GRP and Naval Aluminum for Ship Design
abstract: The study analyzes the mechanical behavior of Omega type reinforcements in a hybrid configuration of GFRP and naval aluminum, evaluating their structural feasibility in naval applications. The specimens were manufactured by manual lamination of fiberglass with palatal resin. In the hybrid specimens, 1.1 mm and 2 mm aluminum sheets were incorporated in the upper area of the reinforcement, proportionally reducing the GFRP layers. Performance was determined by threepoint bending tests, recording force-displacement curves to obtain maximum load, deformation and failure modes. The comparative analysis showed variations in stiffness, crack initiation and structural collapse between conventional and hybrid specimens, highlighting the influence of metal thickness on the progression of damage. An 11% similarity in strength was achieved with respect to conventional specimens, despite having 23% less GFRP. These results demonstrate the potential of hybrid frames to reduce weight and optimize structural efficiency placed on top of the reinforcement allowing uniformity in bending.

Transmission patterns and future forecasting of mpox: a review of mathematical modelling approaches for prediction and public health preparedness
abstract: Abstract Mpox has shifted from a disease mainly associated with zoonotic spillover in Central and West Africa to a recurrent global public-health threat involving sexual-contact networks, household transmission, international mobility, ecological persistence and clade-specific uncertainty. Mathematical models have clarified important mechanisms in the 2022 clade IIb outbreak, including the role of heavy-tailed sexual-contact distributions, behavioural adaptation, vaccination and case isolation. However, the literature remains less mature in one respect that is essential for preparedness: the conversion of transmission insight into reliable, setting-specific forecasts. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed modelling evidence on mpox transmission patterns and evaluates the extent to which existing compartmental, stochastic, network, agent-based, phylodynamic and time-series models support future outbreak prediction. The review identifies four recurring gaps: insufficient prospective validation, weak integration of spatial and cross-regional lags, limited clade-specific parameterization for clade I/Ib risk, and inadequate incorporation of immunity, reporting delay and surveillance uncertainty. We propose a forecasting-oriented framework that links epidemiological state variables, contact structure, population immunity, mobility, interventions and uncertainty quantificati…

abstract: The article assesses the impact of inbound tourism on the national economy using Tourism Satellite Account indicators and develops a probabilistic forecast up to 2030. It argues that gross value added of tourism industries must be distinguished from tourism direct gross value added: in 2024 their ratio was 3.8. A formula for the effect of extending the length of stay is proposed; extending the stay by one night raises inbound tourism consumption by UZS 3.19 trillion (9.4%). Because the annual national series is short and has structural breaks, a dynamic panel gravity model based on 2,134 observations for 194 countries is used. Out of sample, the model with an error of 1.0% outperformed ARIMA (33.6%) and a random walk with drift (5.4%). The number of inbound tourists is forecast to reach 18.9 million in 2030, and the probability of achieving the target of 20 million tourists is 47.6%.

title: From Price to Value: How Procurement Practices Reshape Competition in Medical Device Markets
abstract: Procurement affects both the prices paid for medical devices and the conditions under which suppliers compete. Broader value-based assessment may reward clinical performance and life-cycle savings but may also raise bidding costs and favor incumbents. This conceptual study examines that tension through a focused, non-systematic review of economic theory, peer-reviewed studies, and public procurement documents. It develops four conditional propositions on aggregation, verifiable quality, contractual governance, and evidence-related entry barriers. The framework separates static purchasing efficiency from dynamic market contestability, including supplier entry, switching, and innovation. Evidence from U.S. group purchasing, Canadian tenders, Dutch purchaser interviews, UK experiments, and European procurement frameworks is compared according to the claims each design can support. Available evidence identifies specific expenditure and decision-process effects but does not establish a universal causal impact of value-based procurement on long-run competition. The paper argues for independently verifiable criteria, proportionate evidence requirements, workable contract exit, and continuing opportunities for qualified suppliers. Price-based awards may remain suitable where products are genuinely comparable and downstream differences are small.

title: Conventional Preoperative Prediction of MASLD-Compatible Histologic Abnormality, Fibrosis, and Higher-Grade Steatohepatitis, and Exploratory Machine-Learning Classification of MASH Severity in Patients Undergoing Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass
abstract: Abstract Introduction Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent in patients with severe obesity undergoing metabolic/bariatric surgery. Noninvasive preoperative stratification of histologic liver abnormalities remains incomplete. We evaluated conventional regression models and a separate exploratory machine-learning analysis of MASH grade 1 versus grades 2/3. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort included patients undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass between March 2000 and March 2025. Of 1,350 surgical patients, 745 underwent intraoperative wedge liver biopsy and 375 had complete data for conventional modeling. Conventional endpoints were MASLD-compatible histologic abnormality, any documented fibrosis, and higher-grade steatohepatitis, defined as biopsy-reported grades 2/3. The machine-learning analysis included 284 patients with steatohepatitis and used routine preoperative variables, ultrasound-reported steatosis, NFS, the AST/ALT ratio, and FIB-4. Model development used RandomizedSearchCV and repeated stratified cross-validation within the training set, followed by training-based threshold selection and held-out test evaluation. Prediction of long-term mortality in maintenance hemodialysis patients using machine learning survival models: a prospective multicenter study with SHAP-based interpretation
abstract: Background Accurate and interpretable prediction of long-term mortality in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate machine learning survival models integrating clinical, nutritional, inflammatory, and anthropometric predictors. Methods This prospective multicenter cohort included 1,129 MHD patients from eight dialysis centers in China. Patients were allocated to training ( n = 645), internal validation ( n = 274), and independent external test ( n = 210) cohorts. Predictors were selected using LASSO–Cox regression and Survival Boruta. Five survival machine learning models were developed and evaluated for discrimination, prediction error, calibration, and clinical utility. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to interpret model predictions. Results During a median follow-up of 4.53 years, 603 patients died. 14 predictors were selected for model development. In the external test cohort, gradient boosting survival analysis (GBS) achieved a C-index of 0.748 (95% CI, 0.705–0.790), a 5-year time-dependent AUC of 0.799 (95% CI, 0.726–0.861) and the lowest integrated Brier score (0.141) among the five models. GBS also demonstrated reasonable calibration, although its discrimination was not significantly superior to that of random survival forest. title: Improved Hybrid DBN-HEVA Framework for Accurate Prediction and Multi-Objective Optimization of Die Sinking EDM Performance
abstract: Electrical discharge machining (EDM) has made it possible to cut conductive metals that are either uncut or difficult to cut using standard machining techniques. In this EDM process, an accurate and flexible prediction and optimization model is required to evaluate this process and increase machining efficiency and surface quality. This study develops a novel adaptation of an improved Attention-Guided Deep Belief Network integrated with an Adaptive Human Eye Vision Algorithm (AG-DBN-AHEVA) for accurate prediction of EDM performance characteristics. Using an experimental dataset of 81 runs for accurate performance prediction, this work also examines the impact of EDM input parameters on material removal rate (MRR), tool wear rate (TWR), and Surface roughness (SR). To ensure high data quality and better generalization capability, pre-processing techniques including outlier detection, normalization, correlation analysis, and SMOTE-based regression augmentation were applied. The results showed that the suggested model outperformed the existing models, achieving the lowest prediction errors (MAE [Formula: see text] 0.007, RMSE [Formula: see text] 0.010) and the greatest [Formula: see text] value of 0.994. Integrated imaging, body composition, and systemic immune-inflammatory profiling for non-invasive prediction of HER2 status in endometrial cancer
abstract: Objectives Preoperative evaluation of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status in endometrial cancer (EC) is clinically important for molecular stratification and treatment planning. This study aimed to develop a non-invasive predictive model integrating functional MRI-derived tumor characteristics, CT-derived body composition, and systemic immune-inflammatory markers for identifying HER2-positive EC. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 75 patients with pathologically confirmed EC (41 HER2-positive, 34 HER2-negative) who underwent preoperative 3.0 T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), including amide proton transfer–weighted (APTw) imaging and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) diffusion-weighted imaging, and chest CT between August 2019 and June 2026 were evaluated. Quantitative MRI parameters, including APT values, the slow apparent diffusion coefficient (D), fast apparent diffusion coefficient (D*), and perfusion fraction (f), and CT-derived body composition, including visceral adipose tissue (VAT), subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT), skeletal muscle (SM) and intramuscular adipose tissue (IMAT), were extracted. Systemic immune-inflammatory parameters including neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte to lymphocyte ratio (MLR), platelet to lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated. title: Prediction of Acid-Base (Polar) Component Free Surface Energy in Dispersion-Filled Polymer Composites
abstract: The paper develops a predictive model to determine the influence of the magnitude of the acid-base (polar) component of the free surface energy (FSE) of polymers and fillers, as well as the volume fraction of fillers on the acid-base (polar) component of the FSE of a polymer composite. Mathematical equations and graphical relationships illustrating these relationships are presented. The model is based on the assumption that in composites the magnitude of the FSE is partially determined by acid-base (polar) interactions between functional groups at the “polymer−filler” interface. Using the predictive model, it was established that knowing the acid-base characteristics of the polymer and filler, it is possible to predict what kind of surface character a particular filled composite will have − acidic, alkaline, or predominantly neutral. Based on the results obtained, it can be argued that the acid-base (polar) component of the free surface energy (FSE) can be a reflection of the properties of polymer composites, namely, resistance to the action of aggressive media, such as water, aqueous solutions of acids and alkalis, polar organic and inorganic solvents, etc. To verify the proposed model, the energy characteristics of the surfaces of epoxy composites based on epoxy oligomer with diethylenetriamine and mineral fillers of different chemical nature – rutile and bentonite – were exp…

title: HEALTH PREDICTION FOR RURAL OLDER ADULTS BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DEEP NEURAL NETWORK
abstract: With the intensification of global population aging, health management for the elderly in rural areas faces challenges such as insufficient medical resources, outdated service facilities, and inadequate professional capacity. Against this backdrop, the early warning of health risks primarily related to hypertension and cardiovascular chronic diseases, as well as the real-time assessment of health status based on multi-source physiological data, have become urgent issues to address. To address this challenge, this study proposes an artificial intelligence-driven deep neural network (AI-DNN) health prediction model designed for rural intelligent elderly care scenarios. This model fuses multi-source heterogeneous physiological and behavioral data. It adopts an improved residual gated recurrent unit combined with a two-level attention mechanism for health risk perception to jointly model key time segments and high-risk physiological indicators. Meanwhile, an adaptive feature reweighting module is designed to dynamically adjust feature contributions according to individual health status. This enhances the model’s representation capability and predictive performance for sparse, noisy, and heterogeneous health data. On the large-scale real-world rural health monitoring dataset covering 2158 elderly residents in several administrative villages in three provinces, the AI-DNN model achie…
