title: Agricultural Information Networks, Information Needs and Risk Management Strategies among Smallholder Farmers in Southeast Nigeria
abstract: This study examined agricultural information networks, information needs, and risk management strategies among smallholder farmers in Southeast Nigeria using the Diffusion of Innovation Theory. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS Version 21 with descriptive statistics including means, frequencies, rankings, and standard deviations, while qualitative data from focus group discussions were examined thematically using Braun and Clarke’s six-step framework. Findings show dominance of farmer-to-farmer networks, traditional knowledge systems, and kinship ties as the most trusted sources of agricultural information, while institutional and digital platforms were least utilized. Major information needs centred on disease and pest management, climate-related risks, fertilizer use, and improved seed varieties, reflecting farmers’ vulnerability to environmental and production uncertainties. Within Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovation Theory, interpersonal communication channels such as peer networks significantly influenced awareness and adoption of agricultural practices. The study concludes that strengthening farmer-led networks and improving access to credible institutional information sources can enhance risk management and innovation adoption among smallholders in the region. Implications suggest that extension agencies and development actors should leverage existing social structu…

title: Evaluation of the Quran literacy program at Muhammadiyah Simpang Empat Junior High School using the CIPP Model
abstract: Low Qur’an reading proficiency among junior high school students from general education backgrounds poses a unique challenge for Islamic-based schools. This study aims to evaluate the Qur’an Literacy Program at Muhammadiyah Simpang Empat Junior High School using the CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product) evaluation model. This study used a qualitative approach, with data collection methods including in-depth interviews, structured observations, and document analysis. The evaluation results at the context stage showed that this program arose from a real need and is highly relevant to the school’s vision and mission. The evaluation at the input stage indicated that, despite limitations in the number of teachers and financial support, the program was designed and implemented efficiently, realistically, and collaboratively. The process stage revealed that program implementation was consistent with the plan, student participation was high, and regular monitoring and improvements were conducted. In the product stage, the program proved successful in improving students’ ability to read the Qur’an, fostering religious attitudes, and having a positive impact on students’ self-confidence. This program also has strong potential for replication in other schools.
venue: International research journal of management, IT and social sciences

title: Decoupled vegetation structure and composition in a mangrove–apicum ecotone in Northeastern Brazil
abstract: Abstract Mangrove–apicum ecotones are heterogeneous transition zones in which woody colonization need not follow a single age-ordered trajectory. We reanalysed an author-validated area-level matrix from ten successional mangrove patches in the Barra de Gramame estuary, northeastern Brazil. Five patches belonged to a 6–10-year and five to an 11–15-year site-history category inherited from the original survey. Individuals of Avicennia schaueriana , Laguncularia racemosa and Rhizophora mangle were classified into two height-defined structural strata (< 1 m and >1 m) and counted over 225 m2 per patch; a single 900 m2 reference stand was used descriptively. Hierarchical Bayesian modelling, fully enumerated exact permutations, Bray–Curtis and Aitchison analyses, beta-diversity partitioning and leave-one-area-out diagnostics were applied. The <1 m stratum contained 7,439 individuals, compared with 1,898 individuals in the >1 m stratum. Posterior density ratios (< 1 m/>1 m) were 2.73 (95% credible interval: 1.46–5.12) in 6–10-year areas and 3.64 (1.94–6.73) in 11–15-year areas, whereas site-history effects remained uncertain. Abundance-sensitive assemblage structure differed significantly between height strata (Bray–Curtis R2 = 0.213, exact P = 0.00195), whereas relative species composition did not clearly differ under Aitchison geometry (R2 = 0.029, P = 0.105). Long-haul L + S-band WDM transmission over a 1052-km dispersion-shifted fiber link with inter-band nonlinearity management
abstract: We demonstrated long-haul inline-amplified wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) transmissions with 10.8-THz signal bandwidth in the L and S bands over a 75.2-km-span dispersion-shifted fiber (DSF) link. In L + S-band DSF transmission, where the signal is allocated on both sides of the zero-dispersion wavelength, some S-band channels and L-band channels can become group-velocity matched, leading to strong inter-band Kerr nonlinear interactions. In addition, the edge-to-edge bandwidth of the L + S-band WDM signal exceeds the peak Raman-shift frequency in the silica-core fibers, resulting in significant power transfer due to inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS). We investigated the feasibility of L + S-band long-haul coherent transmissions over DSF links by optimizing the launch power for each band. We also evaluated a band-wise bidirectional transmission configuration in which the S-band and L-band signals propagate in opposite directions to avoid inter-band phase matching. Highly efficient parametric waveband converters based on periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides were employed for the generation, reception, and amplification of the S-band signals. title: Blockchain Technology and Financial Services Transformation: Evidence from Institutional Cryptocurrency Adoption
abstract: Introduction/Main Objectives: The advent of blockchain technology has introduced a new paradigm in the financial landscape through decentralization, immutability, transparency and enhanced efficiency in financial services. This study focuses on institutional cryptocurrency adoption and its implications for financial services transformation in the blockchain era. Background Problems: Most studies have focused on the institutional adoption of one cryptocurrency or one institutional investment channel. This study focuses on institutional cryptocurrency adoption via three distinct institutional investment channels for Bitcoin and four other key cryptocurrencies. Novelty: There have been some limited studies that have attempted to quantify the various institutional channels for investing alongside the key cryptocurrencies. This study set out to fill this gap through a thorough empirical assessment of institutional cryptocurrency adoption. Research Methods: The study adopted a quantitative method and secondary data was obtained from credible databases and market reports on cryptocurrencies. Descriptive analysis and comparative concentration of ownership analyses were used on the basis of participation of institutions, geographical coverage, institutional holdings, CR5, CR10, Herfindahl Hirschman Index (HHI) and Gini coefficient. title: Financial Leverage and Financial Performance in Emerging Tourism Economies: Empirical Evidence from Sri Lanka’s Listed Hotel Sector
abstract: Financial leverage plays a critical role in shaping a company’s performance, particularly as businesses strive to reduce their overall cost of capital. Thus, this study investigates the relationship between financial leverage and financial performance among high market-capitalized hotels listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) over the period of 2015–2024. Drawing on trade-off, pecking order, and agency theories, this study investigates the effect of two key financial leverage indicators, debt ratio and debt-to-equity ratio, on financial performance using measures such as return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE) while using firm size as the control variable. Using panel data, the study covers 18 listed hotels and 180 firm-year observations and employs regression analysis. The findings reveal that the debt ratio has a significant positive effect on ROA, supporting the trade-off theory's notion that moderate debt enhances asset utilization and operational efficiency. Conversely, debt-to-equity ratio shows no significant impact on ROA. Regarding ROE, the debt-to-equity ratio and debt ratio demonstrate a significant positive effect, suggesting that higher leverage can improve shareholder returns under prudent management. The study enriches the limited empirical literature on capital structure within Sri Lanka’s tourism sector and offers practical insights for hotel mana…

title: Digital Financial Literacy, Technology Trust, and Financial Attitudes: MSME Financial Well-Being in Pangkalpinang
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital financial literacy, trust in technology, and financial attitudes on the financial well-being of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) owners in Pangkalpinang City.Methodology: This study employs a quantitative approach using multiple linear regression analysis, along with t-tests and F-tests, to examine the impact of digital financial literacy and trust in technology on the financial well-being of MSME owners in Pangkalpinang City. The sample consists of 107 respondents selected via purposive sampling. Following data transformation, data from 100 respondents were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS version 32.Results: Digital financial literacy has a significant negative effect on financial well-being, whereas trust in technology and financial attitudes have significant positive effects. These three variables explain 86% of the variation in financial well-being.Conclusions: Digital financial literacy, trust in technology, and financial attitudes collectively influence the financial well-being of MSME owners in Pangkalpinang City.Limitations: The study is geographically limited and utilizes non-probability sampling, which restricts the generalizability of the findings.Contribution: This study provides empirical evidence regarding the application of Consumer Financial Well-Being Theory and the Theory…

title: Financial Performance Implications of Capital Structure Choices: Evidence from Listed Non-Financial Companies in Sri Lanka
abstract: Capital structure decisions are considered as critical in the present highly competitive financial world, as firms strategically adopt them to accomplish their goals. The composition of a firm’s capital influences its overall cost of financing and value. Particularly, firms need to cautiously evaluate the advantages of debt financing in contrast to the potential costs of insolvency and financial distress. The primary objective of the study is to examine the extent to which capital structure choices influence the financial performance of non-financial companies in Sri Lanka. This study includes the independent variables of the Debt-to-Equity Ratio and Debt to-Total Assets Ratio, reflecting the proportion of debt and equity used to finance operations and growth and the dependent variables are Return on Equity (ROE) and Return on Assets (ROA), which measure financial performance. Under the stratified random sampling method 70 non-financial companies were selected and the relevant data of the sample companies were collected for the period from 2020 to 2024 from the audited annual financial statements of the companies. The statistical techniques of Pearson’s correlation and panel data regression were used to analyse the association between the capital structure decisions and the financial performance. title: The Right to Disconnect in Modern Employment: Protecting the Boundary Between Work and Personal Life in the Digital Era
abstract: Digital transformation has changed the way humans work, especially regarding time and space. Smartphones, emails, instant messaging applications, and collaborative work platforms allow employers to contact employees almost anywhere and at any time. The boundary traditionally established by labor law between "working hours" and "rest periods" is therefore increasingly eroded. This article examines the right to disconnect as a new legal institution designed to protect that boundary. The study uses qualitative methods: textual analysis, comparative jurisprudence, historical analysis, synthesis, logic, and descriptive statistics based on secondary data. The article systematizes international scientific literature, compares representative legal models (France, Spain, Belgium, Portugal, Ireland, Ontario, Chile, Australia, and the European Union), and then juxtaposes them with current Vietnamese law. The results show that the right to disconnect has evolved from a bargainable declaration into an enforceable legal obligation backed by sanctions. Meanwhile, Vietnam's Labour Code of 2019 is still designed according to the logic of physical time and lacks legal instruments to regulate out-of-hours digital communications. Guided by the directives of the Documents of the 14th National Congress of the Party on human development, digital transformation, and the building of harmonious, stable,…

title: Qashqadaryo viloyatida moliyaviy xizmatlardan foydalanish imkoniyatlarini baholash va hududiy tafovutlarni qisqartirish yo'llari
abstract: В статье рассматриваются подходы к оценке доступности финансовых услуг в районах и городах Кашкадарьинской области и меры по сокращению территориальных различий. В качестве основных показателей используются обеспеченность точками банковского обслуживания, объёмы кредитов и вкладов в расчёте на душу населения, а также уровень использования цифровых платежей. Сопоставление районов и городов по этим показателям позволяет выявить территории с ограниченным доступом к финансовым услугам. Для сокращения территориальных различий предлагаются меры по расширению охвата банковскими услугами, развитию инфраструктуры цифровых платежей и повышению финансовой грамотности населения.

title: Financial Performance and Firm Value: The Moderating Role of ESG Disclosure in Indonesian Mining Firms
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether Return on Assets (ROA) affects firm value (Tobin’s Q) and whether Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure moderates this effect in Indonesian mining firms.Methodology: An explanatory quantitative design with secondary data was applied to nine mining firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange that issued complete annual and sustainability reports in 2021–2025 (45 firm-year observations). ESG disclosure was scored by content analysis of the 30 indicators of the National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations (NASDAQ) ESG Reporting Guide 2.0. Moderated panel regression was estimated in EViews, and the Chow and Hausman tests selected the fixed effect model.Results: ROA has a positive but insignificant effect on Tobin’s Q (coefficient 0.433, p = 0.176). The ROA × ESG interaction is positive (3.722) but not significant at the 5% level (p = 0.070). The model is jointly significant (adjusted R² = 0.809), largely because of firm fixed effects.Conclusions: The evidence is insufficient to conclude that ROA influences firm value or that ESG disclosure alters that influence at the 5% level.Limitations: The sample is small, the period is short, no control variables are included, and the binary disclosure index varies little across firms.Contribution: The study tests ESG disclosure as a moderator, not a direct predictor, wi…

title: The Mediating Role of Digital Literacy Between Financial Literacy and Investment Scam Awareness
abstract: This study analyses whether digital literacy mediates the relationship between financial literacy and investment scam awareness. Despite the rapid expansion of digital financial services, there remains limited knowledge of whether financial and digital literacy interact to shape resistance to online investment scams. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among undergraduates who were selected through stratified random sampling in Sri Lanka. Financial literacy is measured through budgeting skills, financial attitude, financial product literacy and risk awareness. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied to estimate the direct effects and mediating effects. Budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness enhance digital literacy, while financial attitude shows no meaningful effect. Digital literacy exhibits the strongest direct influence on investment scam awareness. Mediation analysis confirms that digital literacy transmits the effects of budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness to scam awareness, whereas financial attitude remains non-significant. The study conceptualizes digital literacy as a coping appraisal mechanism that enables individuals to operationalize financial knowledge in digital financial environments. Guided by Protection Motivation Theory, the study interprets financial literacy as supporting threat appraisal…

Inverse design of terahertz metasurface polarization converters based on generative adversarial networks
abstract: A reflection-type broadband terahertz metasurface polarization converter with a three-layer structure—comprising a patterned metal layer, a dielectric layer, and a metallic ground plane—is inversely designed based on a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP). By incorporating the Wasserstein distance and a gradient penalty term, the WGAN-GP effectively overcomes the training instability inherent in conventional generative adversarial networks, thereby enabling the construction of an end-to-end mapping model from target spectra to metasurface structural parameters. The results demonstrate that the WGAN-GP achieves efficient and high-accuracy inverse design, with a single inference time of only 30 ms and a mean absolute error of structural parameter prediction as low as 0.1263. The optimized metasurface polarization converter exhibits a consistently high polarization conversion ratio exceeding 0.8 over the 3–7.5 THz frequency range, corresponding to a relative bandwidth of up to 86%, and maintains excellent angular stability within an incidence angle range of 0° to 50°. This work not only verifies the efficiency and reliability of WGAN-GP in the inverse design of complex electromagnetic devices, but also provides an effective solution for the development of high-performance terahertz metasurfaces, with the potential to accelerate device innovati…

title: RECONSTRUÇÃO ESTÉTICA DE SOBRANCELHAS EM PACIENTES COM ALOPECIA NÃO CICATRICIAL: UMA ABORDAGEM COMBINADA ENTRE DESIGN E ESTÍMULO COSMÉTICO
abstract: A alopecia não cicatricial caracteriza-se pela perda parcial ou total dos pelos sem destruição definitiva do folículo piloso, podendo acometer diferentes regiões do corpo, incluindo as sobrancelhas. Essa condição pode causar impactos estéticos, emocionais e psicossociais significativos, comprometendo a autoestima, a autoimagem e a qualidade de vida dos indivíduos. Nesse contexto, a tricologia e a estética associada desenvolveram abordagens não invasivas voltadas à recuperação funcional e estética dos pacientes acometidos por essas alterações capilares. O presente trabalho teve como objetivo analisar a reconstrução estética de sobrancelhas em paciente com alopecia não cicatricial por meio de uma abordagem combinada entre design de sobrancelhas e estímulos cosméticos, considerando seus possíveis benefícios estéticos. Tratou-se de um estudo descritivo, de caráter qualitativo, realizado por meio de relato de caso clínico, com avaliação estética, registros fotográficos e análise da evolução do tratamento. A associação entre estímulos cosméticos e técnicas de design de sobrancelhas foi utilizada com o propósito de contribuir para o estímulo ao crescimento dos fios e a melhora da harmonia facial. O trabalho também permitiu discutir a atuação da estética e da tricologia no manejo das alopecias não cicatriciais, destacando a importância de abordagens humanizadas e integrativas na reabil…

title: Design, Implementation, and Empirical Evaluation of a Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model in Higher Education
abstract: AI-supported assessment increasingly enables adaptive tasks, automated analysis, and personalized feedback, yet their integration into coherent, human-supervised formative assessment remains insufficiently established. This study developed and evaluated the Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model (HA-CAAM) using Design and Development Research structured through the ADDIE framework. Implemented in a higher-education Media Education course, the model employed performance-responsive task adaptation using predefined thresholds, rubric-guided AI-assisted scoring, formative feedback, and instructor verification. Five experts validated the model, 148 students provided quantitative and qualitative implementation feedback, and 50 student responses were independently assessed by two human raters and AI. Expert validation provided initial evidence of content validity (mean Aiken's V = 0.818). Students reported generally favorable experiences, particularly regarding clarity and feedback usefulness, although Learning Support and Overall User Experience received comparatively lower ratings. AI-generated scores demonstrated strong agreement with human-reference scores (ICC = 0.898), despite individual discrepancies. These findings provide initial evidence of content validity, positive implementation experiences, and scoring agreement, rather than demonstrated improvements in learnin…

Intergenerational Effects of Türkiye’s Education Reform on Children’s Academic and Health Outcomes
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the intergenerational effects of Türkiye’s 1997 compulsory schooling reform, which increased mandatory schooling from five to eight years. Drawing on a novel dataset from the nationally representative 2022 Turkish Child Survey, we use a regression discontinuity design (RDD) to identify the effect of mothers’ exposure to the education reform. We find that the reform significantly increased maternal educational attainment and, in turn, improved children’s performance in Turkish, while having no statistically significant effect on mathematics achievement. Maternal exposure to the reform also had positive effects on children’s mental health, increasing happiness and reducing anxiety, but did not affect their general health status. These effects are heterogeneous by child gender, with boys benefiting more than girls. Analysis of potential channels shows that increased parental investment may be one relevant channel explaining the observed effects, while reduced child work appears to play a limited role.

title: Collision Dynamics in Thermally-Controlled Ball Milling in Rh(I)-Catalyzed C−H/C−N Bond Activation: Mechanism and Hot−Spot Activity
abstract: Abstract Mechanochemical activation represents a powerful concept to harness mechanical force and drive chemical transformations in a solid state. Herein, we report a framework to determine the effect of temperature increase on mechanochemical ball milling in Rh(I)-catalyzed C−H/C−N activation. By using collision dynamics, we provide a model to determine the effect of ball size, milling frequency, internal jar length, velocity, material, and internal curvature during the collisions. By conducting computational studies, we investigate the reaction mechanism and the role of thermal mechanochemical collisions on C−H/C−N bond activation steps. Taking the solution-phase mechanism as a working hypothesis, the observed ball-milling acceleration is consistent with a proposal combining local temperature elevation at impact sites, estimated at up to 83.5 K above the bulk temperature, and modest, step-dependent mechanical modulation of selected transition states, while the rate-determining step is not significantly affected by compression. These results suggest that mechanical force can lower selected transition-state barriers at hot spots, offering a promising strategy for mechanochemical synthesis.

title: Integration of Solar and Wind Energy With Electrolyzers and Fuel Cells to Generate Green Hydrogen and Electricity in Valparaíso
abstract: The energy transition toward renewable sources and the decarbonization of the power sector represent both a strategic challenge and an opportunity for Chile due to its outstanding solar and wind resources. This study evaluates the technical and economic feasibility of hybrid renewable energy systems integrated with hydrogen technologies under a Small Distributed Generation Means (SDGM) scheme, where grid injection is limited to 9 MW. A photovoltaic–wind (PV-WT) system combined with electrolyzers (Proton Exchange Membrane Electrolyzer, PEME, and Alkaline Water Electrolyzer, AWE) and fuel cells (Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell, PEMFC, and Alkaline Fuel Cell, AFC) is analyzed for green hydrogen production and utilization. Hourly simulations in Python model renewable generation, grid injection constraints, hydrogen production, storage, and reconversion. The complementarity between solar and wind resources improves generation stability and hydrogen production. Among the evaluated configurations, the PV-WT-AFC-AWE system in the coastal region achieved the best economic performance, with an LCOE of 106.29 USD/MWh, an LCOH of 7.60 USD/kg, an NPV of −3.7 million USD, and an IRR of 7.6%. In contrast, configurations including fuel cells (PV-WT-PEMFC-PEME) exhibited the poorest economic performance, indicating that hydrogen reconversion into electricity is not economically viable under …

title: Cross-Zonal Short-Term Load Forecasting in Resource-Constrained Distribution Grids: A Multi-Model Benchmarking Study
abstract: Accurate short-term load forecasting is essential for modern power distribution, yet selecting optimal predictive architectures across diverse feeder profiles remains a key challenge for local grid operators. This paper presents a multi-feeder comparative evaluation of machine learning architectures using hourly load data (January 2024–April 2026) from six distribution feeders within two operational zones under the Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board. The evaluated models include statistical baselines (ARIMA, SARIMA), linear regression, tree ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), and recurrent architectures (LSTM, GRU). Feature engineering includes cyclical temporal encodings, weather parameters, and temporal lags. Experimental results demonstrate that tree-based ensembles consistently outperform both statistical baselines and recurrent neural networks across all feeders. Random Forest achieved the highest performance, with a Mean MAPE of 2.35%, and individual feeder errors reaching as low as 0.83% MAPE and 0.02 MW MAE. Meanwhile, LightGBM demonstrated superior operational deployment efficiency, delivering a highly comparable Mean MAPE of 2.56% with the lowest inference time of 0.55 s, and a minimal memory footprint of 1.2 MB. These findings highlight that feature-engineered tree ensembles provide an optimal balance of predictive performance, scalability, and computat…

title: Fallas de mercado y Derecho continental
abstract: Este artículo propone emplear la noción económica de «falla de mercado» como criterio dogmático —operado a través de la teoría de las cláusulas generales— para reforzar la comprensión del contrato y, de manera más intensa, en la protección del consumidor. La propuesta adopta una concepción restringida de la falla de mercado y desarrolla un test operativo de identificación y de selección de remedios, orientado a reducir discrecionalidad judicial y a evitar riesgos de sobreintervención, manteniendo como criterio de control la reducción de pérdidas sociales. El objetivo último de este trabajo es determinar cómo se puede aplicar el AED al Derecho continental.

title: First Report of Leaf Spot Caused by Alternaria alternata on Rice in Korea
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is the most important cereal crop in Korea. In 2025, a survey of symptomatic rice plants in Haenam, Jeollanam-do, recovered Alternaria spp. at a high frequency. The isolates were not identified to species level, and pathogenicity was not examined (Kim et al. 2025). Leaf spot symptoms were observed in July 2025 in a rice field in Haenam, Jeollanam-do, Korea. Approximately 5% of plants showed symptoms. Lesions initially appeared as small dark-brown flecks that enlarged into circular or irregular spots with dark margins and pale gray to brown centers. As lesions expanded, adjacent lesions frequently coalesced and caused extensive blighting. Small pieces of tissue excised from lesion margins were surface-disinfested, plated on water agar amended with streptomycin (100 μg/ml), and incubated at 25°C. Thirty fungal isolates were recovered, and three representative Alternaria isolates (SYP-2629, SYP-2649, and SYP-2659) were selected for further analyses. Colonies grown on PDA for 14 days were dark olive-brown in the center with grayish margins. Conidia were light brown, ellipsoid to obclavate, with roughened walls and 1–5 transverse and 0–3 longitudinal septa, measuring 11.9–56.0 × 5.9–16.4 μm (mean 25.6 × 10.9 μm, n = 100). These characteristics agreed with published descriptions of A. alternata (Woudenberg et al. 2015). The ITS, gapdh, tef1, rpb2, Alt a1, endoP…

title: The Effect Of Service Quality And Price On Consumer Satisfaction (Case Study Of Consumers At Sukajaya Store, Ciawi Market, Tasikmalaya Regency)
abstract: This study aims to determine and analyze the influence of service quality and price on customer satisfaction at Toko Sukajaya, Ciawi Market, Tasikmalaya Regency, both simultaneously and partially. The study employs a quantitative approach with a causal research design. The population consists of all Toko Sukajaya customers, while the sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 100 respondents. Data were collected via questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive analysis, validity and reliability tests, the Method of Successive Intervals (MSI), classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, correlation coefficient analysis, the coefficient of determination, the F-test, and the t-test. The results indicate that service quality and price simultaneously have a positive and significant influence on customer satisfaction. Partially, service quality has a positive and significant influence on customer satisfaction. Similarly, price has a positive and significant influence on customer satisfaction. The coefficient of determination (R²) is 0.620, indicating that 62% of customer satisfaction can be explained by service quality and price, while the remaining 38% is influenced by other variables not examined in this study.

title: Social Influence as a Moderator of Cognitive Biases and Market Sentiment in Digital Gold Investment: Tring! Users in Denpasar
abstract: Digital gold micro-investment platforms have made gold accessible to retail investors, yet investment decisions on these platforms are not driven by rational fundamentals alone. This study examines the effect of heuristic behavior, market sentiment, and overconfidence bias on digital gold investment decisions, and tests whether social influence moderates these relationships among Tring! application users in Denpasar. A quantitative, causal-associative design was applied using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire distributed through an online survey to respondents selected by purposive sampling (domiciled in Denpasar, active Tring! users for at least six months, and with a steady income). The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The results show that heuristic behavior, market sentiment, and overconfidence bias each have a positive and significant effect on digital gold investment decisions, and that social influence significantly strengthens all three relationships. The model explains 67.3% of the variance in investment decisions and shows strong predictive relevance (Q²predict = 0.588). These findings highlight the role of the social environment in amplifying the psychological drivers of investment behavior in digital micro-investment ecosystems.

Avaliação de estudos com PLS-SEM na pesquisa em inovação: um protocolo estruturado para revisores em contextos de mercados emergentes
abstract: Objetivo do estudo: Propor um protocolo estruturado para apoiar a avaliação de estudos que utilizam PLS-SEM na pesquisa em inovação, especialmente em contextos de mercados emergentes. Metodologia/abordagem: O estudo adota abordagem teórico-metodológica baseada em revisão crítica da literatura sobre PLS-SEM, sistematizando orientações práticas para avaliação de estudos quantitativos. Originalidade/Relevância: A ampla difusão do PLS-SEM na pesquisa em inovação tem sido acompanhada por críticas relacionadas ao uso mecânico do método, com foco excessivo em métricas estatísticas e menor atenção à coerência entre teoria, operacionalização e inferências. Em mercados emergentes, limitações de dados, uso de proxies e desafios de mensuração ampliam essa complexidade. Principais resultados: O artigo organiza critérios de avaliação distribuídos ao longo das principais etapas de estudos com PLS-SEM, desde a justificativa do método até a interpretação dos resultados, apresentando checklists avaliativos para apoiar revisões metodológicas mais consistentes. O protocolo incorpora recomendações metodológicas atuais, como a avaliação da capacidade preditiva fora da amostra (PLSpredict/CVPAT) e o diagnóstico de viés de método comum por colinearidade total (full collinearity VIF). title: Persistent Firm Performance and ESG Ratings: A Chronologically Separated Evaluation in the Korean Capital Market
abstract: This study examines whether a persistent firm-specific component of financial performance, estimated only from a 2011–2017 training window, remains informative out of sample and whether it is associated with later ESG ratings in Korean listed firms. The component (PFPC) is the firm fixed effect from a two-way fixed-effects model. In a chronologically separated 2019–2025 holdout, PFPC outperforms firm-mean benchmarks and, for Tobin’s Q, a training-fitted covariates model, but not that model for ROA, and it does not outperform the latest observed outcome for either measure; Tobin’s Q holdout accuracy decays to zero by 2022–2025. Using one observation per firm, mean ESG is negatively associated with ROA-based PFPC and positively associated with Tobin’s Q-based PFPC (one-standard-deviation differences of −0.21 and +0.48 standard deviations of PFPC). Two-stage firm-bootstrap intervals exclude zero for Tobin’s Q, whereas the ROA interval includes zero at its upper end and the ROA sign reverses under alternative winsorization. Because the data are current-vintage extracts, the exercise is a chronological holdout, not a real-time forecast. The evidence supports a bounded evaluation framework, not a universal predictive or causal ESG claim.

title: An Assessment of Market Research Effectiveness in Strategic Marketing Decision-Making at Grand View Research Inc.
abstract: India’s research and insights industry reached approximately Rs. 29,008 crore (USD 3.5 billion) in FY2025, growing 10.9 per cent from Rs. 26,300 crore, according to the Market Research Society of India (MRSI). This paper assesses how effectively market research supports strategic marketing decision-making at Grand View Research Inc. (GVR). A descriptive, quantitative design was used, with primary data from 50 GVR employees collected through a structured 20-question questionnaire using convenience sampling and analysed through frequency, percentage and mean scores. Perceptions were positive: average mean scores were 3.91 for Market Research Effectiveness, 3.66 for Strategic Market Understanding and 3.90 for Strategic Marketing Decision-Making, and 94 per cent agreed that effective market research contributes significantly to better strategic marketing decisions. Timeliness (mean 3.60), changing market conditions and a lack of actionable insights were the main concerns. Keywords: Market Research, Market Intelligence, Strategic Marketing Decision-Making, Market Orientation, Grand View Research

title: Make Do or Renew? How Market Turbulence Reshapes the Sources of Competitive Advantage in Pakistan's Textile Industry
abstract: The exporters of textiles from Pakistan have to compete on value as they have to deal with record energy costs, new tariff barriers, and fluctuating demand from buyers. This study is about what resource-deployment practices (innovation, knowledge management and entrepreneurial bricolage) generate a competitive advantage for these firms. It also poses the question of how two factors affect those effects: absorptive capacity (internal) and market turbulence (external). The model is an integration of the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities perspective and contingency theory. A total of 113 bed-linen and upholstery manufacturers' owners and senior managers responded to the survey. Systematic random sampling was used to select the firms from a population of 362 members of the association. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and 5000 bootstrap subsamples were used to test the hypotheses. Entrepreneurial bricolage had the most significant impact on competitive advantage (β = 0.338, p = .001), with innovation being the second most significant impact (β = 0.172, p = .038). There was no significant direct effect of the knowledge management. Absorptive capacity did not moderate any of the three relationships. Market turbulence took a dual impact on the market. It increased the innovation–advantage relationship (β = 0.212, p = .047) and significantly reduced…

title: Scenarios for Angola’s Electricity Transition: Generation Capacity, Electricity Production, and Environmental Sustainability
abstract: This paper presents a prospective multivariate analysis of Angola’s electricity sector over the period 2024–2050, assessing the economic, demographic, and environmental impacts of three energy transition pathways: Baseline, Green Transition, and Restricted Development. Using energy system optimization models complemented by parametric robustness tests, the study projects a rapid increase in electricity demand, driven by population growth, with Angola’s population expected to reach approximately 86 million by 2050. Under the Green Transition Scenario, electricity demand reaches 283 TWh, corresponding to a per capita consumption of 3350 kWh. Although large-scale hydropower remains the backbone of the electricity system, accounting 37–51% of total generation, solar photovoltaics emerge as the leading technology for capacity expansion, accounting for up to 33% of installed capacity and achieving the lowest levelized cost of electricity, ranging from 19.2 to 25.5 EUR/MWh. By contrast, diesel generation and new hydropower plants exhibit substantially higher generation costs. In isolated rural grids, diesel–solar hybrid systems reduce electricity generation costs by more than 50% while significantly lowering carbon intensity. Sensitivity analysis shows that overall system costs are strongly influenced by the discount rate and macroeconomic assumptions but remain comparatively robust t…

title: Horizon-Aware Forecasting of Hypertension Prevalence and Mean Total Cholesterol in Chinese Men: Retrospective Leakage-Controlled Benchmark Study Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, and Neural Models
abstract: Abstract Background Forecasts of population-level cardiovascular risk factors can support surveillance and planning, but annual country-level health series are often short. With only 30 or 39 annual values per target, model flexibility can outpace the information available for training, making leakage control, repeated temporal evaluation, and comparison with simple baselines essential. Objective The aim of this study is to compare statistical, classical machine-learning, and neural forecasting models for age-standardized prevalence of hypertension (ASPH) and mean total cholesterol (MTC) in Chinese men and to test whether attention or substantially greater neural capacity provides consistent predictive benefit. Methods The authors analyzed 2 officially sourced annual series: ASPH for Chinese men aged 30 to 79 years (1990‐2019; 30 observations) and MTC for Chinese men aged 18 years or older (1980‐2018; 39 observations). No series was interpolated, extrapolated, imputed, smoothed, spliced, or synthetically extended. Leakage-controlled expanding-window evaluation began after 21 observations and assessed 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons. Classical machine-learning and neural models used a fixed primary lookback of 3 (L=3), with nested lookback selection disabled; neural models used 10 fixed seeds. Performance was assessed with root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error, mean abs…

title: A Multi-Graph Diffusion Mamba Framework for Ultra-Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting
abstract: Accurate ultra-short-term wind power forecasting is critical to grid security and economic dispatch. However, existing methodologies are constrained by two fundamental gaps: rigid topologies that fail to balance physical and data-driven information, and decoupled architectures that process spatial and temporal features separately. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a novel Multi-Graph Diffusion Mamba (MGDM) framework. A multi-graph architecture is introduced to decouple the dependencies among wind turbines into a physics-informed Meteorological Causal Graph (MCG) that captures directional wind propagation, and a learnable Systemic Adaptive Graph (SAG) that encodes unobserved operational constraints. A dynamic gated fusion mechanism adaptively balances the two graphs through a real-time confidence factor, and the fused representation is finally fed into a topology-aware Mamba module, where graph diffusion convolutions are embedded into the selective scan process, achieving joint spatio-temporal modeling. The results demonstrate that the MGDM outperforms all baseline models for 15 min, 1 h, 2 h, 3 h and 4 h ahead forecasts, and achieves improvements in accuracy of 3.59–4.81% across the forecasting horizons over the best benchmark model. Moreover, ablation studies demonstrate that the multi-graph topology and the selective scan mechanism are indispensable for robust foreca…

Residual Diffusion-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Network for Human Mobility Forecasting in Disaster Scenarios
abstract: Forecasting human mobility during disasters is essential for emergency response but remains challenging because disasters cause abrupt, uncertain, and context-dependent deviations from regular mobility patterns. Deterministic models capture dominant spatio-temporal patterns but tend to underrepresent these deviations, whereas diffusion-based models characterize predictive uncertainty but may generate forecasts inconsistent with historical mobility dynamics. To overcome these limitations, we propose ResDiffNet, a residual diffusion-enhanced spatio-temporal network that decomposes mobility dynamics into a regular trend and a residual deviation. This decomposition enables a principled integration of deterministic and diffusion modeling: a deterministic base predictor first learns the stable mobility trend using a hypergraph convolutional network, and a residual conditional diffusion module (RCDM) subsequently models disaster-induced stochastic residuals through a conditional diffusion process. Guided by historical trend signals and disaster-related semantic information extracted from social media, the RCDM refines residual predictions in a context-aware manner, mitigating the excessive randomness of standard diffusion models. Experiments on two real-world disaster-related mobility datasets show that ResDiffNet reduces RMSE and MAE by 4.5–7.0% and 5.2–9.0%, respectively, relative t…

title: Improving Energy Price Forecasts: Autometrics With Indicator Saturation
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we evaluate Autometrics, an automated model selection method with controls for outliers and location shifts, against artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests for six monthly energy price series (WTI, Brent, Dubai, US and Russian gas, Australian coal) from IMF data. Autometrics generally delivers lower RMSE/MAPE and higher directional accuracy than the ANN and random forest specifications considered here, particularly in the more volatile oil and coal markets. Autometrics also has the benefit of being interpretable in a familiar regression context as opposed to more “blackbox” machine learning. The CARDt method often delivers predictive accuracy which is not statistically different from Autometrics, but there is some evidence that simple model averaging of the two with intercept‐corrected Autometrics yields further gains relative to either alone.

title: Unveiling the Price Tag on Unpaid Labour: Decoding Gender Disparities in Time Allocation among Married Women and Men in Kollam District, Kerala
abstract: In today’s dynamic and competitive world, women’s workforce participation will not only result in economic development but also help them achieve financial independence. Providing better educational opportunities for women has helped them break the social, economic and political glass ceiling. However, education in itself cannot bring them into the workforce. The state of Kerala in India is often celebrated for its high literacy rate and progressive stance on gender equality. According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (2021–2022), the female workforce participation rate of the state was only 32 per cent. One important reason for India’s low female labour force participation is mainly rigid societal norms that obligate women to undertake unpaid care work at home, over and above their interests and passions. This study found that married women in Kollam district spent two and a half times more time on unpaid work as compared to married men. JEL Codes: D13, J12, J16

title: A Review of Trustworthy Deep Learning for Renewable-Rich Distribution Smart Grids: Forecasting, Resilience, and Operation
abstract: This PRISMA-informed structured review examines trustworthy deep learning for low- and medium-voltage distribution feeders and coordinated multi-feeder systems, from standard test feeders to utility networks; it does not assume one fixed bus count. Renewable generation, electric vehicles, flexible demand, storage, and digital monitoring create nonlinear, temporal, spatial, and probabilistic decision problems. We organize the evidence through a task–data–model–risk–validation pathway that links each operational task to its data structure, defensible model family, principal trustworthiness risk, and minimum deployment evidence. Common mathematical formulations provide shared evaluation criteria for forecasting, state estimation, reliability, resilience, control, and deployment. Reported results are interpreted only within their stated datasets and test conditions. Compact temporal models are defensible first-line baselines for moderate-horizon forecasting; topology-aware and physics-informed models are suited to tasks where network structure and feasibility matter; and deep reinforcement learning is a candidate for sequential control only when constraints and fallback behavior are tested. Exact database search dates and retrieval counts were not retained, so the review does not claim exhaustive systematic coverage or a quantitative meta-analysis.

title: Short-Term Multi-Energy Load Forecasting Based on Multiscale Spatial-Temporal ChebyNet
abstract: The accurate prediction of multi-energy loads is of crucial importance for the optimisation, scheduling and economic operation of integrated energy systems. However, current multi-energy load forecasting methods still suffer from insufficient capture of the complex coupling between multi-energy loads and meteorological features, as well as inadequate extraction of short-term characteristics and periodic patterns. In response to the aforementioned issues, we propose a Multiscale Spatial-Temporal ChebyNet model that learns directed signed graph structures from both dynamic and static views, aggregates node information over them through a role-lifted Chebyshev spectral filter, and uses a multiscale forward attention mechanism and gated dilated convolutions to capture short-term and periodic temporal dependencies. Experiments on two public datasets show that MST-ChebyNet outperforms ten baseline networks in forecasting electricity, cooling, and heating loads. Compared with the representative adaptive graph based spatiotemporal models Graph WaveNet and MTGNN, it reduces load MAPE by 0.54–1.40% on the Arizona dataset and by 0.59–1.53% on the Eagle dataset.

title: The Asymmetric Effects of Oil-Price Shocks on Inflation in Cambodia: A Nonlinear Autoregressive Distributed Lag Model
abstract: In this study, a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) was used to analyze asymmetric effects of oil-price shocks on consumer prices. The Augmented Dickey–Fuller test results indicate that consumer price index (CPI) shocks, positive and negative oil-price shocks, and the broad money supply ar I(1), whereas the foreign exchange rate is I(0), thereby favoring the use of the NARDL framework. The bounds test asserts that there is a statistically significant long-run relation between the variables at a 5% level. Diagnostic tests provide additional evidence that the estimated model is free of serial correlation and heteroskedasticity with normally distributed residuals that are stable over the sample period. The error-correction coefficient estimation is −0.122 and significant, which means that approximately 12.2% of the short-run disequilibrium is corrected per period. Over the long run, the CPI is affected to a significant degree by positive oil-price shocks, with a 1% cumulative rise in oil prices resulting in an approximate 0.053% increase in the CPI. On the contrary, a negative oil-price shock has no statistically significant impact. The existence of cointegration between oil-price increase shocks and inflation is a necessary but only partial condition for the presence of asymmetry under such conditions, and a Wald test provides evidence that long-run asymmetries, in …

title: Fourier dynamic hypergraph interaction network for traffic flow forecasting
IoT-Based Residential Energy Forecasting with Explainable Feature Selection for Sustainable Building Management in the Industry 5.0 Era
abstract: Buildings are a key application domain for improving energy efficiency and sustainability, while Industry 5.0 emphasizes sustainable and human-centric digital transformation. This study presents a comparative framework for IoT-based residential energy consumption forecasting, combining time-series models with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based feature analysis. Using a publicly available dataset from a residential building in Leicester, United Kingdom, the study predicts the next-hour total power consumption of six monitored appliances using a 24-h historical window and measurements available at or before the forecast time. Ridge Regression, conventional machine learning models, iTransformer, and TimeFilter are evaluated using 993 out-of-sample observations. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) support feature analysis and selection. With all features, Ridge Regression achieves an RMSE of 35.869 W, an MAE of 23.261 W, and an R2 of 0.265. Feature selection has varying effects across models and evaluation metrics and does not necessarily improve predictive performance. Persistence and 24-h seasonal-naïve methods serve as baselines. The findings assess explainable IoT-based forecasting without requiring a full Digital Twin infrastructure and may offer insights relevant to Industry 5.0-oriented building managem…

title: Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

Applicability-Aware Reliability Scoring and Prediction of EMS Patient-Care Records for Trustworthy Smart Ambulance AI
abstract: This study presents the EMS Record Reliability Index (EMS-RRI), which measures how completely selected fields are documented in an emergency medical services encounter, when applicable. Using National Emergency Medical Services Information System (NEMSIS) data, we analyzed 200,000 records from 2024 and 500,000 from 2025. The basic score measured the percentage of applicable elements documented, while a domain-weighted version adjusted for differences in the number of elements across documentation domains. The two scores showed high agreement in both years. We labeled records at or below the basic EMS-RRI cutoff, defined by the 20th percentile of 2024 training scores, as low reliability. To predict this label, we developed and internally tested classifiers using 2024 records, then evaluated them on the full 2025 dataset without refitting. The final XGBoost model performed well, with ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, and F1 values of 0.9079, 0.8594, and 0.7637 on the 2024 internal test set and 0.8846, 0.8270, and 0.7319 on the 2025 test set. Most missed low-reliability records had scores near the cutoff, and performance varied across subgroups. In a separate retrospective analysis of high-acuity patient prediction, adding the EMS-RRI slightly improved the ROC-AUC and PR-AUC but showed no clear improvement in F1 score. Records flagged by the primary EMS-RRI cutoff did not have a higher downstream …

title: Early-Stage Prediction of Lithium-Ion Battery RUL and Capacity Degradation Trajectory Using CNN-LSTM and Stretched Exponential Model
abstract: Sustainable development in the energy storage sector requires batteries to be graded before leaving the factory so that their performance matches the requirements of intended applications, thereby maximizing service potential and minimizing resource waste caused by premature retirement. However, conventional grading relies primarily on initial performance and does not account for the future capacity degradation trajectory or service life, and limited early-cycle data are typically available. This paper therefore proposes a method that uses only two early aging cycles to estimate both the capacity degradation trajectory and the remaining useful life (RUL). The proposed method, termed CNN-LSTM-SE, combines a convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture with a stretched exponential (SE) model. The network takes the resampled voltage-capacity curves obtained during the constant-current charging segments of the first and third cycles as input and estimates the parameters of the SE model. The predicted parameters are then used to reconstruct the capacity degradation trajectory, from which the battery RUL is estimated. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 5.06% and 0.73% for RUL estimation and capacity degradation trajectory prediction, respectively, with corresponding root mean square erro…

title: Evaluation and Analysis of a Novel Fugitive Road Dust Collector and Its Prediction Using Machine Learning Models
abstract: This research paper presents the conceptual design, development and performance evaluation of a compact fugitive vehicular dust collector to control and mitigate air pollution resulting from increased particulate matter on roadways. The developed dust collector is designed to work with two-wheeler automobiles, having a length 0.3 m, 0.15 m in diameter, and weight 2Kg, was experimentally tested on the gravel, asphalt, and concrete road at different speed of the vehicle. Results show distinguished dust collection efficiencies of 67.29% for gravel road, 65.65% for asphalt road, and 33.26% for concrete road, with dust collection increasing proportionally with speed of vehicle and maximum dust collection of 480 g at 80 km/h. The aerodynamic study verifies that dust jet length and mudguard dust area circumference expand as speed increases. The dust angle of attack increases from 220 at 20 km/h to 300 at 80 km/h, representing the direct relationship between speed of vehicle and dust dispersion pattern. The mathematical models were developed for gravel, asphalt and concrete road, reaching high correlations (R² > 98%), and machine learning approaches (Random Forest and XGBoost) further validated the accuracy of dust collection predictions. Relative assessment shows that gravel roads produce the more capturable dust, nearly 3% more than asphalt road and 35% more than concrete road. The d…

title: The impact of elderspeak on dementia care: a comprehensive review of its influence and underlying mechanism
abstract: Background The global prevalence of dementia is rising in the context of an aging population. The quality of communication plays a crucial role in influencing the emotions and psychological well-being of individuals with dementia, and the effects of elderspeak on these patients are bidirectional. Aim This study aims to examine the definitions, characteristics, and underlying mechanisms of elderspeak within dementia care settings, while summarizing its impact on patient behaviors and the quality of care. Design A scoping review. Data sources A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, ProQuest, Cochrane, Embase, and CNKI for studies addressing the effects of elderspeak in dementia care. Review methods Studies that focused on elderspeak in dementia care were included, while those that solely analyzed its linguistic features without a nursing or management perspective were excluded. Two researchers independently performed data screening and extraction. Results This analysis encompasses 295 articles, of which 19 studies specifically examine the effects of elderspeak on dementia care. Elderspeak is characterized by the use of simplified language, a higher vocal pitch, and terms of endearment. Caregivers utilize elderspeak with the intention of conveying care and enhancing older adults' comprehension of information, however, it often leads to unintended negative cons…

title: Electric-field-assisted interfacial rubrene self-assembly for continuous tuning of liquid crystal pretilt angles
abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates a contact-free, low-temperature strategy for continuously tuning the pretilt angle of nematic liquid crystals (LCs) via electric-field-assisted capillary filling combined with rubrene self-assembly. By applying an AC electric field (0–5 V) across unrubbed, polyimide-free indium tin oxide (ITO) cells during LC injection, the pretilt angle of a rubrene-doped nematic LC mixture can be continuously programmed from approximately 3° (near-planar) to 90° (homeotropic). Contact-angle analysis reveals that increasing the filling voltage dramatically alters the interfacial interaction from a polar-dominated surface to a nonpolar, high-dispersive regime, resulting in a gradual transition from planar to homeotropic LC alignment. Electro-optical and dielectric measurements confirm stable, uniform LC alignment and customized threshold responses across cycles. This field-imprinted interfacial assembly method eliminates mechanical damage and high-temperature thermal processing, offering a scalable route for next-generation flexible, wearable, and tunable photonic devices

title: Philanthropic Engagement and Eco-Friendly Vehicle Purchase Intention in Seoul’s Urban Mobility System: The Moderating Role of Descriptive Social Norms
abstract: Understanding the social antecedents of eco-friendly vehicle purchase intentions is essential for advancing the transition toward sustainable urban mobility. From a socio-technical systems perspective, vehicle adoption depends not only on technologies and infrastructure but also on the social contexts in which users make decisions. Drawing on behavioral spillover theory and the theory of normative social behavior (TNSB), this study examines whether philanthropic engagement, namely charitable donation and volunteering, is associated with eco-friendly vehicle purchase intentions, and whether descriptive social norms (measured as perceived compliance with everyday civic rules) moderate these associations. Using weighted binary logistic regression with design-based standard errors and data from the 2024 Seoul Survey (n = 36,280), we found that charitable donation was positively related to purchase intention, whereas volunteering showed no significant overall association in the main-effects model. Descriptive norms moderated both associations: the association of donation was positive and significant at moderate-to-high norm levels, whereas the association of volunteering changed from negative at low norm levels to positive at high norm levels. The findings were robust to alternative specifications, although the norm-conditioned association of donation was concentrated in hybrid vehi…

title: Assessing the Impact of Solar-Powered Electric Motorcycles on Household Petrol Expenditure in Kano Metropolis, Nigeria
abstract: The removal of Nigeria’s petrol subsidy in May 2023 raised pump prices from about ₦200 to well over ₦1,000 per litre, straining household transport budgets in Kano Metropolis, where motorcycles are the dominant mode of private and commercial mobility. Solar-powered electric motorcycles (SPEMs) are a potential alternative, but their effect on household petrol expenditure has not been documented with household-level data. This study assessed the effect of SPEM adoption on household petrol expenditure in Kano Metropolis. A descriptive survey of 384 motorcycle-owning household heads, selected by stratified random sampling across the eight local government areas of the metropolis, was conducted with a structured questionnaire (Cronbach’s α = 0.78). Data were analysed with paired-samples t-tests, correlation, and simple and multiple regression at the 0.05 level. Of the respondents, 31.5% (n = 121) had adopted SPEMs. Among adopters, mean monthly petrol expenditure fell from ₦30,200 to ₦0, t(120) = 31.42, p < 0.001, d = 2.86. Adoption was a significant negative predictor of petrol expenditure (β = −0.641, R² = 0.411) and was associated with a lower transport cost burden (r = −0.492). High acquisition cost, limited charging infrastructure, unreliable grid supply and concerns about battery quality significantly constrained adoption, whereas awareness and maintenance skills did not. title: Coordinated Control of Hydraulic Distributed Drive in an All-Terrain Tracked Vehicle Under Articulated Steering Constraints
abstract: Coordinating four independent hydrostatic circuits in a dual-body articulated all-terrain tracked vehicle requires track-speed allocation accommodating articulation kinematics and propulsion-load distribution. Geometric speed matching alone can concentrate propulsion loads on the front body, induce rear-body drag and track slip, and elevate circuit pressure differences. This study proposes differential-projection coordinated control (DPCC) to address this coupling. Nominal four-track speeds incorporating body sideslip are derived from articulation-point velocity compatibility, and circuit pressure deviations drive load redistribution through bounded zero-sum projection. Conditions for conservation of the target track-speed sum and bounded differential-speed deviations are established, elucidating load imbalance under geometric matching and load redistribution through small track-speed adjustments. Simulations at 0–30° show that DPCC reduces peak circuit pressure difference and root-mean-square (RMS) slip ratio at all six nonzero steady-state articulation angles relative to conventional geometric differential control. At 30°, peak pressure difference decreases from 34.16 to 15.55 MPa, RMS slip ratio from 0.59% to 0.40%, and RMS vehicle-speed error by 74.05%, while average rear-body drag becomes forward propulsion. Limits of Curtailed Wind Utilization by Ferry-Borne Tourist Electric Vehicles: A Milos Island Case Study
abstract: Islands without a grid connection to the mainland should meet their energy requirements with limited local resources. On the tourist islands, curtailed wind energy is often proposed for charging the electric vehicles (EVs) that visitors bring by ferry, but this share has rarely been measured against ordered curtailment. This paper estimates its limits for the autonomous Milos system in Greece, whose operator publishes hourly curtailment set-points. Hourly operating records for 2023–2025 are combined with an open trip-level series of ferry vehicle arrivals and a cohort-based Monte Carlo model of the tourist fleet. A transport-problem ceiling and a weekly mixed-integer linear program solved under perfect foresight are evaluated for the 2025 shoulder season and the full year. At a battery electric vehicle (BEV) share of 6.2%, smart charging meets 1.6–1.8% of curtailed wind energy, against 0.4% under uncontrolled charging; at 30%, it meets 5.3–6.9%, against 1.7–1.9%, and 14–17% if every EV could charge at a controllable point. Meeting 10% requires a BEV share of 29–41% under the wind-conditional measure and at least 83% under the conservative one. A generic pumped hydro facility uses 80–100% of the curtailed energy; once it is installed, the additional diesel saving from smart charging falls by 38–57%.

title: From passenger perception to vehicle-level requirements: A state-of-the-practice review and roadmap for NVH, ride comfort, and motion sickness in electrified and automated vehicles
abstract: Passenger comfort has become an increasingly important consideration in automotive development, particularly as electrification and automated driving reduce traditional powertrain noise and shift passenger attention toward vibration-, noise-, and motion-related discomfort. Existing comfort evaluation methods span both vehicle-perspective approaches based on objective measurements and passenger-perspective approaches relying on subjective assessment, biosignals, and surveys. However, the relationship between these perspectives and their respective roles in practical vehicle development are often unclear. This paper reviews comfort evaluation methods from both vehicle- and passenger-perspective viewpoints, with emphasis on buzz, squeak, and rattle (BSR), structure-borne road noise, ride comfort, odor, fatigue, and motion sickness. The strengths and limitations of each class of methods are discussed in the context of automotive engineering practice. The review focuses on linking passenger-perceived discomfort to objective, repeatable vehicle-level metrics that can inform subsystem requirements. A requirements-oriented framework is presented to link subjective complaints to surrogate evaluation indices, test protocols, and subsystem-level design targets for vehicle development. From National Climate Strategies to Local Response
abstract: National adaptation strategies have become the principal instrument through which governments organize their response to climate risk, yet their effectiveness ultimately depends on delivery at the local level. This article examines whether Canada’s 2023 National Adaptation Strategy (NAS) and its accompanying federal action plan truly prepare municipalities to adapt to climate change in a timely and sustainable manner. Drawing on publicly available policy documents, academic literature, and international reports, it analyzes how responsibilities, financial resources, and decision-making authority are distributed across the federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal orders of government. The analysis identifies structural misalignments in vertical and horizontal governance, and a municipal fiscal position that is poorly suited to financing long-term adaptation. These misalignments are treated as a form of unseen unsustainability: an architecture in which ambitions are set nationally, implementation burdens are carried locally, and financial capacity is concentrated elsewhere. The experience of three flood-affected British Columbia (BC) municipalities, Abbotsford, Princeton, and Merritt, illustrates how competitive, merit-based funding can leave high-risk communities without a realistic pathway to implementation. title: Secondary stroke prevention strategy addressing dual mechanisms in a patient with concurrent atherothrombotic and cardioembolic risk
abstract: Introduction: Etiological classification forms the basis of treatment strategy in ischemic stroke. In older patients with vascular risk factors, cardioembolic and atherothrombotic mechanisms can coexist. In strokes with mixed mechanisms, a single-target treatment approach may not adequately reduce the risk of recurrent ischemic events. This report presents the management of a mixed-mechanism stroke in a patient with atrial fibrillation (AF), severe left ventricular dysfunction, and critical carotid atherosclerosis, and a left atrial appendage (LAA) closure approach for secondary prevention.Case: An 81-year-old woman was evaluated with a history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, heart failure (EF: 28%), and AF. She weighed 55 kg, and her creatinine was 1.47 mg/dL. Her CHA₂DS₂-VASc score was calculated as 8 and her HAS-BLED score as 3. She developed an acute ischemic stroke while taking apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily, a dose appropriate to the dose-reduction criteria. Neurological examination: oriented and cooperative, GCS 15, cranial nerve examination normal, pupils isocoric, and eye movements full in all directions. Deep tendon reflexes and pathological reflexes were normal. Muscle strength was 4+/5 in the right extremities and full in the left extremities; there was no sensory deficit or cerebellar sign. title: Cubicost's Implementation Strategy in Construction Services Companies in Bali
abstract: Five-dimensional Building Information Modeling (5D BIM) software, such as Cubicost, can improve the speed and accuracy of quantity takeoff and cost estimation; however, its adoption among construction companies in Bali remains limited. This study aimed to identify and prioritize the driving and restraining factors influencing Cubicost implementation in medium-sized and large construction companies in Bali and to formulate appropriate implementation strategies. A mixed-methods research design with a predominantly descriptive quantitative approach was employed. A total of 25 factors, comprising 10 driving factors and 15 restraining factors identified through a literature review and preliminary interviews, were evaluated using a questionnaire with established validity and reliability. Data were collected from 72 practitioners selected through purposive sampling, and the factors were ranked using the Relative Importance Index (RII). The five highest-ranked factors in each category were subsequently assessed by five key informants using Force Field Analysis (FFA). All driving factors were classified as important to very important (RII = 0.794–0.836), with perceived ease of use and ease of updating quantity takeoffs receiving the highest rankings. THE EFFECT OF THE POST-BRANNAN STRATEGY ON ACHIEVEMENT AND SYSTEMIC THINKING AMONG MIDDLE SCHOOL GIRLS IN BIOLOGY
abstract: The study aims to identify the effect of the post-Brannan strategy on achievement and systemic thinking among middle school female students. The research sample consisted of 72 students from one of the schools under the General Directorate of Education in Maysan for the academic year 2024–2025. The experimental group consisted of 36 students who were taught using the post-Brannan strategy, and the control group consisted of 36 students who were taught using the traditional method.The researcher ensured the equivalence of the two groups in variables such as intelligence, prior achievement in science, and prior knowledge. The researcher also prepared two tools: the first was an achievement test composed of 24 multiple-choice questions with four options, and the second was a systemic thinking test composed of 30 multiple-choice questions with four options. The researcher verified the validity and reliability of both tools. After applying the experiment and analyzing the data statistically using the T-test, the results showed significant differences between the experimental and control groups in both the achievement test and the systemic thinking test, in favor of the experimental group.

title: Gestão de estoque no comércio varejista: mapeamento e análise do giro de produtos de brinquedos em uma empresa de Manaus.
abstract: In retail, inventory directly impacts business efficiency, as it determines how much and when to buy, whether merchandise will be on the shelf when the customer looks for it, and to what extent the operation functions without waste. Based on this issue, this study analyzed the toy department of a retail store in Manaus, Amazonas, aiming to understand which products had lower turnover and where processes could be improved. The research is applied, descriptive, and exploratory, with a qualitative-quantitative approach, following a case study design. To gather data, technical visits and interviews with managers were conducted, alongside the analysis of records for ten toy groups during 2024, 2025, and 2026. The high-turnover and low-turnover groups showed distinct performance patterns. Among the five lowest-turnover groups, sales fell from 102 units in 2024 to 37 in 2026, with 450 units remaining slow-moving in stock. Consequently, more effective inventory tracking, increased dialogue between the departments involved, and commercial actions to clear non-moving merchandise are recommended. The company already possesses much of the required data, and using it systematically can improve purchasing, replenishment, and control decisions.

title: Apathy to the power of 3 — the government, judiciary, and pharma companies on patented drug pricing
Legitimacy Strategies for Animal Welfare in Dyadic Supply Chains: An Evidence‐Based Business Strategy Typology
abstract: ABSTRACT Firms at food supply chains have increasingly been concerned with their environmental and social business strategies, such as animal welfare adoption. However, we know little about how to set boundaries to manage these strategies. This article thus explores how buyer–supplier relationships build market legitimacy in the cage‐free table egg supply chain. Grounded on legitimacy theory, a case study was conducted through six buyer–supplier relationships. Data were collected from a table egg supplier, retailers, hybrid wholesale‐retailers, a certifier, and a nongovernmental organization over a 1‐year timespan and then codified using an inductive content analysis. Our results reveal three objects formed from supplier's and buyers' legitimacy strategies (animal welfare scheme, certification, and product mix), with only the first one being successfully adopted across all dyadic relationships analyzed. Our analysis led to an evidence‐based business strategy typology for legitimacy organized into four quadrants (i.e., sleeper, explorer, passenger, and driver). This study builds theory on how dyadic supply chains legitimize animal welfare practice and offers the concept of object legitimation . By doing so, we explain why and how the legitimacy‐as‐process leads to shift from actions (legitimacy strategies) to outcomes (types of legitimacy) in the cage‐free table egg supply chain…

title: The role of the state in industrial policy
Studying implementation strategies in the field: the Veterans Affairs Quality Enhancement Research Initiative implementation strategy tracking and dissemination (I-STRAND) project
abstract: Introduction The Veterans Affairs Quality Enhancement Research Initiative funds program centers to implement evidence-based practices (EBPs) with operational partners. Prior work has highlighted the importance of using standardized tools to describe how strategies for improving uptake of EBPs are operationalized. Methods We developed an electronic form based on Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change groupings and survey questions. Prior to fielding in May-June 2024, we iteratively reviewed the form with experts. We determined strategy frequencies and identified correlations between strategy groupings. We also determined how frequently evaluation designs and frameworks were used to test strategies. Results There were 54 projects across 17 centers. The most common implementation strategy groupings selected were “Education” (94.4%), “Interested Parties” (90.7%), “Assistance” (87.0%), “Tailoring” (87.0%), and “Evaluation” (87.0%). The most common individual strategies selected were “Assess for Readiness and Identify Determinants” (81.5%), “Facilitation” (79.6%), and “Distribute Educational Materials” (75.9%), with more than half (57.4%) selecting all three. Most projects reported using CFIR or RE-AIM frameworks (CFIR only 22.6%; RE-AIM only 34.0%; both 24.5%) and hybrid implementation-effectiveness designs (64.2%). Nearly all projects indicated that the form was able to cap…
