title: Single-Actuator Driven Symmetric Five-Bar Mechanism for Producing Reciprocal Rectilinear High-Deflection Motion for Pumping Bag-Valve-Mask (BVM)
Adverse Reaction Mechanism and Optimization Strategy of Therapeutic Vaccines for Glioblastoma
abstract: This paper focuses on glioblastoma therapeutic cancer vaccines as the research subject, introducing the mechanisms of action and side effects of therapeutic vaccines. Regarding local, systemic, nervous, and immune-related adverse reactions occurring in vaccine clinical applications, the article analyzes the core causes and solutions for adverse reactions from four aspects: improper antigen selection, imbalance in immune activation levels, the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment of the glioblastoma, and the overlap of side effects from multimodal combination therapies. At the same time, the paper looks ahead to the development direction of this field, pointing out that personalized vaccine development, combined application of vaccines with immune checkpoint inhibitors, and conducting larger-scale clinical trials are future research priorities. Therapeutic vaccines are an important means of precision treatment for glioblastoma, but they still face limitations such as adverse reactions. Balancing anti-tumor efficacy with therapeutic safety is the core key to future vaccine optimization and clinical translation

title: Digital Marketing and Inclusive Finance: A Mechanism Analysis from the Perspectives of Cost Optimization, Efficiency Enhancement, and Resource Allocation
abstract: Inclusive finance has long been limited by information asymmetry, insufficient physical branch coverage, and the "80/20 rule" mindset, which has left long-tail customer segments underserved. The spread of digital technology offers a possible way to ease these problems. Drawing on long-tail theory, market efficiency theory, and capital cost theory, this study employs a theory-driven literature review to examine how digital marketing supports inclusive finance, focusing on its pathways, main mechanisms, and practical limits. The review indicates that digital marketing changes traditional financial service models in three main ways: it reduces information asymmetry, extends service reach, and improves resource allocation. In practice, these effects come mainly from lower costs (reducing information costs, outreach costs, and customer acquisition costs) and higher efficiency (improving information matching, operational efficiency, and customer lifecycle management). Besides, the high initial customer acquisition cost (CAC), the structural mismatch between the cost and return when providing services to low-income groups (long-tail customers) on a large scale through low-profit products, as well as the weak business sustainability, still pose significant limitations to this model. This study has constructed a comprehensive theoretical framework to understand how digital marketing sup…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Resilience in the quiet months: an anticipatory reconstruction capacity framework and its diagnostic application to cyclone Ditwah, Sri Lanka
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to specify and apply a framework linking capacities built before a hazard to the outcomes that follow it, running from the immediate impact and response to the quality of eventual reconstruction. Using Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka, set against two South Asian cases, it argues that durable resilience accumulates in the quiet months between disasters. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper synthesises pre-disaster recovery planning, disaster risk reduction mainstreaming and build back better into one construct, anticipatory reconstruction capacity, expressed as testable propositions. It is applied to cyclone Ditwah using secondary data and probed through a structured comparison with Odisha and coastal Bangladesh. Findings The framework links three measurable capacities, namely, risk literacy, institutional integration and anticipatory investment, to a chain that runs from disaster impact through response to reconstruction. The present evidence bears on the first link: for Ditwah, impacts tracked weaknesses in these capacities rather than the hazard’s rarity and in the comparison, mortality from similar storms fell sharply where capacity had been built deliberately, though life-safety gains outpaced asset protection. Evidence on reconstruction quality itself awaits the maturing of recovery and is framed as a proposition for future testing. Researc…
venue: International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment

title: Research on the Impact of Digital Inclusive Finance on Corporate Financing Cost: Theoretical Mechanism and Empirical Test
abstract: Based on the data of A-share non-financial listed companies from 2011 to 2023, this paper matches the Peking University prefecture-level city digital inclusive finance index with corporate financial data, and empirically examines the impact of digital inclusive finance on corporate financing cost and its mechanism of action. Financing cost is measured by the financial expense ratio, and the industry and year fixed effects model is used for estimation. The study finds that the increase of the regional digital inclusive finance development level significantly reduces corporate financing cost; the mechanism analysis shows that digital inclusive finance plays its role by improving the external information environment of enterprises and raising analyst following and research report coverage. The heterogeneity analysis shows that this effect is more obvious in non-state-owned enterprises, the eastern region and larger-scale enterprises. The study provides an empirical basis for improving digital financial infrastructure, optimizing corporate credit information governance and differentiated credit pricing.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Legal Implications of Heir's Incompetence and Violation of Legitime Portie on the Will Reduction Mechanism
abstract: Testamentary deeds made by testators under curatorship raise questions about legal capacity and the protection of heirs' absolute share (legitime portie) under the Indonesian Civil Code. This study analyzes the validity of a will made by a testator under curatorship, comparing the requirements of a valid agreement with will formalities, and evaluates inkorting as a remedy for wills that infringe the legitime portie of Class I heirs. The research employs a normative juridical method with statute and case approaches, using the Civil Code and court decisions as primary legal materials and literature as secondary materials. The findings indicate that curatorship does not automatically render a will null and void; it remains valid if the formalities are fulfilled and no defect of consent, such as duress, fraud, or mistake, is proven. Infringement of the legitime portie does not nullify the entire deed but is resolved through proportional reduction until the absolute share of Class I heirs is met. The study concludes that disputes must distinguish defects in the validity of the deed from violations of the legitime portie, thereby ensuring legal certainty and protecting the rights of heirs.

title: From participation to data: collaborative mapping in the context of natural hazards and risks
Pore Structure and Sodium Storage Performance of Sodium-Ion Battery Anodes
abstract: Pore structure affects ion transport and interfacial reactions in sodium-ion battery anodes and provides space to accommodate volume changes. This paper focuses on hard carbon, alloy anode and conversion composite materials, discusses the role of pore size, connectivity, pore opening and internal voids in the sodium storage process, and analyzes the advantages and limitations of different pore structures. The article also compares the synthesis strategies such as template method, activation method, carbonization control, dealloying and composite precursor derivatization, and explains how these methods shape the pore structure. Studies have shown that the sodium storage process and failure mechanism of different anode materials are very different, and the functional requirements of the pore structure are also different. The formation of pores is often accompanied by changes in phase composition. The contribution of pore structure cannot be evaluated only by capacity. The evaluation should also consider the sodium storage mechanism and failure process of the material under comparable electrode preparation and test conditions.

title: English immersive game participation and attention, emotional health, and cognitive function in children: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Screen exposure is an important issue for children’s health. The existing research pays more attention to the duration of use, but not to the content type and immersion experience. English immersion game integrates language learning and game mechanism, which belongs to educational digital behavior. This study analyzes the daily English game duration, immersion and English integration of children aged 6–14, and their relationships with attention, working memory, executive function and emotional behavior. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 215 children. Based on the parents’ questionnaire, the data of English game participation were obtained: daily duration, 1–5 immersion self-evaluation, and English integration. The outcome includes all kinds of attention, working memory, executive function, emotion and ADHD symptoms. Multivariate linear regression controls total screen time, sleep, physical activity, age, gender and family SES. CPT, Flanker and Corsi were the main outcomes, and after Bonferroni correction, the four executive function and behavior indicators were set as exploratory outcomes, which were not corrected. Results English game time is positively correlated with selective attention ( β = 0.218, p = 0.001). It is significantly different from the primary analysis of working memory, and its effect size fell below the minimum-detectable-ef…

title: Framing the harvest: advertising message framing, perceived benefits and consumer participation in adoption agriculture
abstract: Purpose This study examines how advertising message framing influences consumer participation in adoption agriculture, an emerging agri-food service model. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on message framing theory and the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, we developed a mediation model with regulatory focus and context-specific trust as two proposed moderators. A one-factor between-subjects experiment was conducted with Chinese consumers after pretesting stimuli. Hypotheses were tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) and bootstrapping, with artificial neural network (ANN) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analyses for robustness. Findings Gain-framed ads outperform loss-framed ads on short-term, long-term and recommendation intentions, with small-to-moderate effect sizes. Functional and emotional-social benefits jointly mediate this relationship. In addition, a post-hoc exploratory analysis suggests a positive association between functional and emotional-social benefit appraisals. The proposed interactions of regulatory focus and context-specific trust are not significant. However, context-specific trust has a strong positive main effect on perceived benefits, suggesting a general positive association with benefit appraisals rather than a framing-specific moderating effect. Research limitations/implications This study has several limitations. It …
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Machine learning prediction of energy band gaps in curcumin derivatives
abstract: Machine learning (ML) regression models using SMILES-encoded molecular fingerprints were developed to predict the band gaps of 19 synthesized curcumin derivatives. The goal was to develop a ML-based framework capable of estimating the band-gap values prior to synthesis, thereby guiding chemists in their experimental effort. Training data for the model were obtained from the Harvard Clean Energy Project (HOPV-15), restricted to 52,000 non-fullerene acceptor (NFA) organic molecules with density functional theory (DFT)-calculated band gaps. Multiple fingerprinting schemes, including Morgan fingerprints, MACCS keys, atom-pairs, and FCFP, were used to train a pool of regression models. These models were then applied to the 19 curcumin derivatives for band-gap prediction and compared to DFT simulation calculations. The accuracy of the predictions was enhanced by using the Most Common Substructure (MCS) approach, narrowing it to molecules sharing key curcumin motifs. This refinement reduced the average predictive error by 30% compared with using the full HOPV-15 dataset, highlighting the benefit of targeted feature selection. Finally, the model was applied to virtually generate and evaluate 1,225 unsynthesized curcumin derivatives by permuting side groups on the BF2-curcuminoid backbone, identifying ten candidates with predicted band gaps above 3.2 eV, which were selected as a proof-o…
venue: Journal of Metals, Materials and Minerals

title: Optimization of Local Revenue Through Collaborative Governance of the Tourism Sector in Bandung Regency
abstract: Tourism growth presents opportunities to increase local government revenue; however, its fiscal contribution depends on effective linkages among tourism activities, local enterprises, and revenue administration systems. This study examined how collaborative governance could support the optimization of tourism-related revenue in Bandung Regency, Indonesia. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, drawing on Ansell and Gash's collaborative governance framework to examine initial conditions, institutional design, facilitative leadership, and collaborative processes. The analysis was based on policy documents, regulatory frameworks, and administrative statistics related to tourism, taxation, and enterprise development. The findings revealed that tourism-related tax revenue increased from IDR 46.12 billion in 2021 to IDR 95.31 billion in 2024, while the number of microenterprises increased from 15,790 in 2021 to 72,731 in 2025. Existing regulations, interagency coordination forums, infrastructure development, tourism promotion, and capacity-building initiatives provided institutional foundations for collaboration. Nevertheless, challenges persisted, including limited accessibility, insufficient stakeholder capacity, inconsistent coordination, and inadequate integration between tourism activities and local revenue administration systems. The available evidence demonstrated go…

title: Consumer Perceptions and Behaviour in the Transition from Internal Combustion Engine Vehicles to Battery Electric Vehicles
abstract: In recent years, the world has been accelerating the development of electric vehicles, but the response of consumers is not consistent. This study focuses on how economic cognition, safety beliefs and technical knowledge affect consumers' willingness to shift from fuel vehicles to pure electric vehicles, and examines how these effects differ across income levels and household car scenarios. The study surveyed 296 car owners. The results showed that cost savings and driving experience were the main driving factors, while battery decay and endurance anxiety were the main obstacles. Regression analysis found that electric vehicle knowledge is the strongest predictor of purchase intention, economic factors and safety factors also have a significant positive effect. Different consumer groups have different preferences: people with higher incomes pay more attention to technology and performance, while buyers with limited budgets pay more attention to total cost of ownership. In addition, pure electric vehicles as a second commuter car are more acceptable than as the main household car. These results suggest that in order to accelerate the popularity of electric vehicles, not only price incentives, but also targeted consumer education and marketing for different usage scenarios are needed.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Engineering dislocations in δ-MnO2 to boost Zn2+ diffusion kinetics for high-performance zinc-ion storage
Political connections and revenue-expense matching: evidence from Malaysia
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the association between political connections and revenue-expense matching. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of 465 Malaysian listed firms from 2000 to 2022, Dichev and Tang’s (2008) revenue-expense matching model is used to assess the impact of political connections. Findings Politically connected firms (PCFs) exhibit weaker contemporaneous revenue-expense matching, driven by both accrual and cash flow channels. This pattern persists across PCF types, with variation in magnitude across connection forms. Following Malaysia’s 2018 regime change, PCFs rely more on past expenses and reduce forward-looking matching, indicating diminished discretionary reporting. Originality/value Using a sample of 465 Malaysian listed firms over the period 2000-2022, this study employs Dichev and Tang’s (2008) revenue-expense matching model to examine the impact of political connections on revenue-expense matching.

title: Design and Optimization of Non-Isolated Cuk-Boost Converter with Solar Photovoltaic/Battery in Plug-in Electric Vehicles
Electrode Modification and Fluoroethy Lene Carbonate Additive Optimization for Ultra-Low Temperature Sodium Storage
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to the low cost and abundance of sodium, but their ultra-low-temperature application is hampered by sluggish Na+ kinetics, unstable electrolyte interfaces, and severe capacity decay. In this work, Al-doped Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 with carbon coating was prepared, and FEC additive was introduced to optimize the electrolyte interface. The modified electrodes were tested from −60 to −80°C. The average capacity decay reaches 0.3%, 0.4%, and 0.6% per cycle at −60, −70, and −80°C, respectively, indicating that the target of ≤0.3% decay per cycle below −40°C is not achieved. Nyquist analysis shows that rising charge-transfer resistance and restricted Na+ diffusion dominate the failure. This work reveals the ultra-low-temperature failure mechanism and offers guidance for designing durable low-temperature SIBs.

title: Research Progress on the Applications of Solid-Waste-Based Nanomaterials in Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage Technologies
abstract: With the continuous advancement of the "Dual Carbon" strategic goals, coupling solid waste resource utilization with carbon emission reduction has become a practical demand in the environmental field. This paper systematically reviews the types, preparation methods and functional properties of solid-waste-based nanomaterials, and summarizes their technical characteristics and current applications across the main stages of CCUS, including CO₂ capture, utilization and storage. Practical bottlenecks in preparing various solid-waste-based nanomaterials, improving their performance, and adapting them to actual operating conditions are analyzed. From the perspective of life-cycle assessment (LCA), the environmental benefits and burdens are discussed. The reviewed literature shows that improved material performance does not necessarily lead to lower overall environmental impacts, as activation and modification may require additional energy and chemicals. Future research directions are also proposed, providing a theoretical basis for developing low-cost solid-waste-based functional nanomaterials for CCUS with low environmental impacts, as well as for integrating solid-waste recycling with carbon emission reduction.

title: Pedagogical Experiences, Challenges, and Ethical AI Use in Peer Writing Tutoring: Insights from the Azcapotzalco Writing Center (CEAZ)
abstract: El presente artículo busca reflexionar sobre los retos encontrados en la práctica del modelo de tutorías entre pares, en el Centro de Escritura Azcapotzalco (CEAZ), durante mi trayectoria como voluntario en el programa de tutores de escritura del 2024 al 2025, centrando la atención en los desafíos y usos éticos de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en los procesos de escritura, las aportaciones de la pedagogía de Paulo Freire en este modelo de aprendizaje y acompañamiento así como los desafíos de la aplicación del modelo con tutorados universitarios de distintas áreas del conocimiento.

title: "We are all alone together": male loneliness, relational recognition, and peer support in YouTube public discourse
abstract: Introduction Male loneliness has emerged as a significant public health concern, yet men's experiences of disconnection remain underexplored in naturalistic digital settings. This study examines how male loneliness is described and publicly negotiated in a large YouTube comment corpus. Methods Data were drawn from the comment section of The Male Loneliness Epidemic, which had generated 57,359 comments and more than five million views at extraction. Following cleaning, 45,807 comments were analysed using computational methods to examine sentiment, emotion-related language, recurring concerns, and differences between parent comments and replies. Reflexive thematic analysis was conducted on a purposive subsample of 654 comments. Results The comments contained expressions of distress alongside encouragement, care, and solidarity. Five qualitative themes showed that commenters frequently described loneliness not simply as a lack of social contact, but as feeling unseen, unheard, or emotionally unsupported. They discussed difficulties expressing vulnerability, the dismissal or misunderstanding of men's emotional needs, pressures associated with masculine and provider expectations, and the importance of being acknowledged by others. Replies were less negative and contained more trust-related language than parent comments. Some replies offered validation, encouragement, and recognition…

title: Dynamic Evolution of Minimum Miscibility Pressure in CO2–Crude Oil Systems: A Review
abstract: Abstract In the context of the rapid advancement of carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) technologies, CO2 flooding has garnered considerable attention owing to its dual benefits in boosting oil recovery and enabling geological carbon sequestration. Maximum oil displacement efficiency can be achieved when CO2 achieves miscibility with crude oil. Minimum miscibility pressure (MMP) is a pivotal criterion for determining oil-gas miscibility. Field operations demonstrate that the miscibility state between CO2 and crude oil varies spatially and temporally within reservoirs during flooding processes, which manifests the dynamic evolution of MMP. Precise determination of MMP has remained a key research focus. This paper reviews experimental protocols and theoretical prediction models for MMP, and clarifies the potential of various approaches for studying MMP evolutionary behavior. The underlying mechanisms and evolutionary rules of MMP are elaborated in terms of component interaction, reservoir conditions and displacement parameters. Meanwhile, practical MMP applications are analyzed based on two representative CO2 flooding pilot projects. Finally, current research outcomes are concluded and prospective research trends are proposed. This Review systematically demonstrates that MMP dynamic evolution arises from the coupling effect of multiple factors, providing essential theo…

title: Energy-saving optimized parameters for 3D selective laser melting using dimensionless model and ANN surrogate mapping
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify energy-efficient selective laser melting (SLM) parameters that achieve high relative density and mechanical performance while reducing trial-and-error experiments. Design/methodology/approach The proposed workflow integrates dimensionless process mapping, an analytical melt-pool geometry model, specific energy consumption (SEC, Es) evaluation, and an artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate map. For Ti6Al4V, the selected parameter set was further evaluated by increasing hatch spacing based on powder-entrainment and melt-pool-width considerations, followed by density and tensile tests. The same SEC-guided screening strategy was also applied to an IN718 dataset to check cross-material applicability. Findings For Ti6Al4V at 80 µm hatch spacing, the optimized condition achieved 99.98% relative density, 1201 MPa tensile strength and 8.2% elongation. The experimentally assessed 120 µm energy-efficient hatch-spacing extension reduced model-estimated SEC by 36.2% while maintaining 99.95% relative density. Tensile strength increased to 1299 MPa, whereas elongation decreased to 6.22%, indicating a strength–ductility tradeoff. Originality/value This work proposes a physics-informed and data-assisted optimization workflow linking dimensionless modeling, melt-pool geometry screening, SEC-based energy evaluation, ANN surrogate mapping and experimental tes…

title: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO2 emissions to peak and decline
abstract: Abstract Global fossil fuel CO 2 emissions have grown 0.8% per year on average between 2019 and 2025. Here we project a decrease of 0.4% in 2026, probably as a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power offset about 64–79% of increasing emissions from demand growth through 2028; acceleration in clean technology deployment is needed to guarantee emissions peak and subsequent decline.

title: Nanostructure Engineering of Silicon-Based Anodes for High-Energy Lithium-Ion Batteries: Strategies, Performance, and Practical Challenges
abstract: Because its theoretical capacity is significantly higher than that of traditional graphite, silicon is a desirable anode material for high-energy lithium-ion batteries. However, severe volume change, particle fracture, repeated disruption of the solid-electrolyte interphase, low electrical conductivity, and significant irreversible lithium loss limit its practical application. This paper investigates how nanostructure engineering and associated interface strategies address these coupled mechanical and electrochemical constraints. Stress accommodation, transport behavior, interfacial stability, and electrode packing are compared between low-dimensional silicon, porous and hollow particles, and core-shell or yolk-shell architectures. The complementary methods of surface coatings, artificial interphases, silicon/carbon composites, binder and electrolyte design, and prelithiation are then evaluated. Although areal loading, tap density, volumetric energy density, manufacturing yield, and compatibility with current electrode-processing techniques also affect practical performance, representative studies show that nanoscale control can significantly improve cycling stability, Coulombic efficiency, and rate capability. The analysis suggests that a multiscale design incorporating controlled internal void space, stable interfaces, conductive carbon networks, and manufacturable secondary …

title: Machine learning–driven stability and power quality assessment in renewable-integrated power systems
abstract: Stability and power quality assessment are critical for the effective and reliable operation of hybrid renewable power grids, where the intermittency of solar and wind generation can lead to significant voltage and frequency fluctuations. This study proposes a framework that integrates an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) with a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to simultaneously estimate system states, evaluate dynamic stability, and monitor power quality. The UKF provides accurate voltage and frequency estimation under various disturbances, while the GNN predicts the operating states: stable, marginal, and unstable. The framework is validated under multiple scenarios, including nominal operation, high-load conditions, renewable intermittency, faults, measurement noise, and extreme disturbances. The results demonstrate low estimation errors, with voltage RMSE ranging from 0.008 to 0.06 pu, and frequency RMSE ranging from 0.01 to 0.08 Hz, depending on the operating conditions. The GNN achieves classification accuracy above 94% in most scenarios, reaching up to 98%–99% under nominal conditions. Furthermore, multi-scenario heatmaps and standard power quality indices, such as voltage sag/swell, frequency deviation, and total harmonic distortion (THD), are employed to verify robustness and consistent performance under simulated conditions of the proposed approach. THD remains below 2% under n…

title: Two-Stage Fault Management Framework for IoT-based Wireless Sensor Network through Resilient and Energy-Efficient Approach
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is built on the foundation of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), which is the technology that provides a smooth connection and real-time data transmission in smart cities and industrial settings. Nevertheless, IoT-based WSNs are prone to several challenges due to hardware, software, and time-related faults, which affect stability and reliability. In the research, a two-step fault management system is proposed to improve fault detection, classification, and resilience in IoT-based WSNs. At the initial step, the identification of faulty nodes in heterogeneous environments is done with a Siamese-Residual Attention Convolutional Neural Network - Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (SRA-CNN-BiLSTM) model. Next, the second step used a Self-Learning Residual Shrinkage Network (SLRSN) to categorize the types of faults effectively. The optimization of the model parameters is performed using a new Clan Cooperative Crested Porcupine-based Optimizer (3CPO) that guarantees high accuracy and convergence rate. Python simulations indicate a 0.98% increase in the accuracy of fault detection and significant energy savings. The framework is therefore a reliable and scalable system of fault management of IoT-enabled WSNs.
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: Factors Influencing Corn Futures Prices and Derivative Trading Strategies: A Literature Review
abstract: Corn is an important agricultural commodity used primarily for animal feed and industrial processing. Corn futures prices are influenced by a range of interconnected factors, including weather conditions, supply and demand fundamentals, exchange rate movements, geopolitical events, and trade policies. Although previous studies have examined these factors separately, relatively few provide an integrated review linking market fundamentals, multiple sources of risk, and related derivative trading strategies. This paper reviews the existing literature on the major factors affecting corn futures prices and discusses commonly used trading and risk management approaches. It examines global corn supply and demand, including the role of substitute grains such as wheat and sorghum. It also discusses climate and extreme weather risks, exchange rate risks, and geopolitical and policy risks, and reviews derivative strategies including weather-related option strategies, inventory-based trading, exchange-rate hedging, and cross-commodity arbitrage. The literature suggests that corn futures price movements are shaped by the interaction of fundamental, macroeconomic, weather, and policy factors rather than by a single dominant variable. The review also identifies limitations in the existing literature, particularly the reliance on historical data and the limited attention paid to trader behavio…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: A digital twin of the heat supply network in managing domestic energy demand
abstract: With its production of 440 million metric tons and exports of 211.2 million metric tons in 2025, Russia’s coal industry remains unprofitable; therefore, stability of the domestic demand for thermal coal is of critical importance. This article presents a quantitative assessment of the thermal component in the domestic coal market, as well as a systematic error of the current normative method for planning fuel requirements for heat supply, and the economic benefits of transitioning to adaptive forecasting of heat consumption based on a digital twin of the heating network and AI-simulated climate scenarios. Based on the assessment results, the domestic heat demand amounted to 30.2 million metric tons of coal equivalent, or 50.2 million metric tons of natural coal, which corresponds to 28.2% of the domestic market and 11.3% of the annual production. The weather-related variation in coal demand was calculated to be 2.4 million metric tons with a standard deviation, which is comparable to the effects of the price and logistical factors. It was found that the current normative planning method systematically overestimates the calculated load. The average absolute percentage error of the normative method was 8.2%, compared to 4.3% for the inertial method. Transition to adaptive forecasting based on a digital twin of the heating network will reduce the planning error by at least twofold …

title: Global energy transition: the role of hydrocarbons
abstract: This article examines the role of hydrocarbons in conditions of global energy transition against a backdrop of rising demand, geopolitical instability, sanctions, and accelerated development of the renewable energy sources. The author argues that the energy transition does not cancel out the strategic importance of fossil fuels, but rather alters the nature of competition by shifting the focus from physical volumes to logistics, technology chains, currency mechanisms, and the state’s ability to ensure long-term sustainability. A “balance-based realism” approach is proposed, in which decarbonization scenarios are correlated with actual balances and infrastructure costs. The value of the proposed approach lies in integration of the resource, technological, financial, and geopolitical analyses, while the global energy sector will maintain a mixed balance with hydrocarbons retaining their system-defining role. Russia’s strategic objective is to use its resource base to develop industrial processing and logistical alternatives, preventing ideologically driven energy transition scenarios from undermining the existing energy base.

title: Available technologies for improving energy efficiency and safety in rock blasting
abstract: Based on the research performed, a set of methodological and engineering solutions has been proposed, which aims to introduce automation in blasting operations performed in particularly challenging conditions and to enhance workplace safety. The novelty and relevance of the proposed solutions are confirmed by patents and test results. This article presents: (1) a robotic technology to form borehole charges with variable energy density and sensitivity; (2) a methodology for creating digital twins of simulation composite models of the blasted media, test bench charge configurations, and blasting conditions at the test site. The developed methodology makes it possible to analyze various methods used to redistribute the harmful energy of the blast impact on the environment into useful forms of energy that can be utilized. Studies were conducted using physical tests and a modified (extended) smoothed particle method to assess the patterns of change in the stress state parameters of the blasted media, as well as the processes of pre-failure and fragmentation. The research revealed fundamental relationships between the displacement velocity vector of the rock fragments and the explosive properties of the rock disintegration means. It was established that the relationship between the rock displacement velocity and the explosive energy of the charge is polynomial in nature. This article…

title: Metal Powder-Filled Ceramic Heating Tube for High-Voltage Molten Salt Thermal Energy Storage
Efficient Dynamically Regularized Lagrange Multiplier Schemes with Energy Dissipation for Pitting Corrosion
abstract: In this paper, a series of efficient decoupled dynamically regularized Lagrange multiplier schemes with guaranteed energy dissipation are developed for phase-field modeling of pitting corrosion coupled with ionic concentration, and their energy-dissipation properties are rigorously analyzed. The proposed method requires only the solution of a few constant-coefficient elliptic equations and a single nonlinear algebraic equation per time step, resulting in a significantly reduced computational cost for the coupled system. The resulting system preserves the discrete energy decay unconditionally at each time step. An adaptive space-time finite element algorithm is employed to efficiently resolve the evolving corrosion front and steep concentration gradients. Combined with a decoupled iterative solver and a mass-lumped finite element method, the scheme achieves high computational efficiency and robustness. Numerical results confirm that the scheme not only reliably captures pit nucleation and evolution with substantially reduced computational cost but also exhibits strong overall applicability to real-world challenges.
venue: East Asian Journal on Applied Mathematics

title: A strategy for astrometric quasar selection with Gaia DR3 and its application to discover new luminous z>2 quasars
abstract: We provide a cookbook for a purely astrometric selection of quasars with Gaia DR3 and provide an example of its use for the identification of very luminous z>2 quasars. We analysed the Gaia DR3 astrometry of confirmed quasars and stationary sources. The proper motion signal-to-noise ratio μ/σ_μ follows a Rayleigh-like distribution. We also show the importance of properly taking the correlation between proper motions in right ascension and declination into account, as well as the non-linear error propagation. We adopted the Mahalanobis distance to the null proper-motion hypothesis. A scaled ̧hi^2 distribution with k=2 and scale s=1.1485 was fitted to Gaia-CRF3; the corresponding pm2σ Gaussian-equivalent threshold is D^2_ M(μ) <7.097. The final criteria combine this with the parallax condition and mathrm ruwe <1.4. When we applied the new criteria to the SDSS DR16Q confirmed quasars, the recovery rate was 90.25%. The suggested purely astrometric selection significantly improves completeness and purity compared to other strategies used in the literature, reaching a quasar purity of approximately 95% (sim2σ Gaussian-equivalent). It can be used to improve the selection purity and completeness for future quasar surveys. As an example, we used the suggested strategy to locate 24 very bright z>2 quasars without redshifts in the literature. Our proposed astrometric selection strategy re…

title: The diagnosis-delivery gap: when evidence cannot become differentiated commitment
abstract: Purpose This paper examines why organizations can generate highly differentiated diagnostic evidence yet make undifferentiated resource commitments. It asks how strategically meaningful distinctions are lost as evidence moves from diagnosis and recommendation through allocation, commitment and delivery. Design/methodology/approach Theory building. The diagnosis-delivery gap is developed by integrating research on resource allocation, strategy implementation, evidence-based management, organization design and organizational justice. A descriptive audit of 200 administrative records from a capability development program illustrates the data conditions required to trace conversion. The extract is not used to test the propositions. Findings Four mechanisms compress resolution: delivery indivisibility, allocation legitimacy, split authority and horizon mismatch. The paper distinguishes diagnostic, recommendation, allocative and delivery resolution and separates variety, alignment and fidelity as components of each. In the administrative extract, ten diagnostic dimensions are complete for all 200 participants while allocation, commitment and delivery fields are unpopulated, so the record cannot establish whether diagnosis altered provision, or whether individualization was genuine or symbolic. Practical implications Senior leaders should assess delivery modularity, decision rights, a…

title: Modelling leadership capital and expenditures from a cybernetic perspective – monitoring, intervention, and contradiction under conditions of complexity
abstract: Purpose From a cybernetic perspective, leadership can be approached as informed practices of status monitoring and intervention. This paper aims to use this approach to describe leadership capital and expenditures in complex-adaptive systems, addressing the efforts to keep an organization in the state of boundary stability between order and chaos. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on recent works on complexity leadership, the authors capture two different monitoring and intervention activities. One is directed at the creation of order, the other at its disturbance. A combination of both is needed to avoid both stagnation and complete disintegration. In consequence, it also becomes necessary to spend effort on handling contradictions resulting from this combination. To illustrate the validity and relevance of their approach, the authors discuss its application to (1) identify leadership capital and expenditures (2) understand implications of different leadership styles. Findings The model distinguishes three types of issues that leadership must address to enable successful management, which can be further broken down to monitoring, intervention and processing contradiction. This leads to a radically different account of leadership capital and expenditures than elsewhere in organizational studies. Requisite variety in the organization emerges as a critical factor regarding the …

title: Single-atom silver decorated MoS2-PEG nanoparticles as a novel antibacterial and immunomodulatory therapy for periodontitis: a catalysis-inspired nanotherapeutic strategy
Traditional Chinese Cultural Branding and Premium Positioning: A Critical Evaluation of CHAGEE's Marketing Strategy
abstract: China's freshly brewed tea market is growing rapidly, making cultural branding a key differentiator. This study explores how CHAGEE leverages traditional Chinese culture to build a premium brand position. It addresses three questions: (1) How cultural branding shapes its segmentation, targeting, and positioning, (2) How positioning is executed through the marketing mix—product, price, place, and promotion, and (3) What challenges threaten brand authenticity, perceived customer value, and message consistency. Using a qualitative single-case study approach, the research analyzes CHAGEE's official materials, industry reports, and academic literature. Findings show that CHAGEE targets urban consumers who prioritize tea quality, convenience, and brand experience. Its premium positioning is built through origin-sourced leaf tea, culturally resonant product names, heritage-inspired packaging, minimalist-store aesthetics rooted in Chinese design principles, and digital storytelling that modernizes tea culture. These elements jointly deliver both functional value (e.g., freshness, taste) and symbolic value (e.g., identity, tradition)—anchored firmly in tea itself as the core product. However, "premium" positioning alone does not automatically translate into higher willingness-to-pay, repeat purchases, or loyalty. Rapid physical expansion, inconsistent service quality across stores, and …
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Genetic Algorithm-Optimized LQR Control Strategy for Boosting Ethanol Production and Minimizing Control Effort
abstract: This paper presents a novel control strategy for the dynamic optimization of ethanol fermentation using a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) whose gains are tuned via Genetic Algorithm (GA). The fermentation process, characterized by nonlinear and time-varying dynamics, demands advanced control strategies for optimal performance to maximize the production of ethanol and to minimize its environmental impact. A procedure for controlling the bioreactor's temperature is created because it is a crucial component of an effective process. Multiple evaluations conducted using genuine computational simulations are provided to confirm the efficacy of controlling techniques. A GA is employed to optimize the LQR's cost function matrices Q and R, aiming to minimize a composite performance index based on tracking error and control energy. The fitness function evaluates each candidate based on performance of various criteria such as Integration of Absolute Errors (IAE), Integral Time Squared Error (ITSE), Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE), and Integration of Square Errors (ISE). The simulation results demonstrate that the GA-optimized LQR outperforms conventionally tuned controllers in terms of ethanol yield, disturbance rejection, and system stability. This approach shows promise for scalable implementation in industrial biochemical process control.
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: Stakeholder Engagement: Sustainable Tourism Development Strategy in Pati Regency
abstract: Tourism is a leading sector that makes a significant contribution to the national economy. Therefore, tourism management is directed towards sustainability with stakeholder synergy. The main problem in the tourism sector is the lack of synergistic, comprehensive, integrated, and sustainable integration or collaboration between stakeholders. Structural egos between parties are still high, and overlapping duties and functions often become obstacles faced, especially in the development of Indonesian tourism. The urgency of this research is the realization of a sustainable tourism development strategy model by collaborating with all stakeholders. The purpose of this research is to conduct a study and compile stakeholder engagement: a sustainable tourism development strategy in Pati Regency that is dynamic, humanistic, comprehensive, integrated, sustainable, and continuous. The research methodology uses a mixed methods approach, namely qualitative and quantitative through mapping and analysis of stakeholder roles/interactions using MACTOR (Matric of Alliance, Conflicts, Tactics, Objectives, Recommendations). The results show that the role of actors The Office of Youth, Sports and Tourism of Pati Regency with Tourism of Pati Regency has the highest level of convergence. The main focus of the objective is Environmentally Based Sustainable Tourism (Sustainable).

title: A review-based guide to selecting an appropriate strategy for transgene-free genome editing in plants
abstract: Abstract The field of plant genetic engineering has advanced considerably since the development of the first transgenic crop plants, and even though transgenic varieties of various crops are now commercially available, consumer reluctance and environmental concerns over transgene escape pose limits on their expansion. Gene editing offers the opportunity to selectively and precisely alter DNA sequences without reliance on stably integrated transgenes, assuaging both concerns. Considerable progress has been made with the advent of programmable nucleases such as Cas9 and its derivatives. The transgenes encoding the gene editing components can be expressed transiently without integration in the plant's genome or removed from the genome via outcrossing or haploid induction to result in gene-edited plants that are no longer considered transgenic. Nonetheless, gene editing systems remain challenging to implement in some plant species, notably those that have long generation times or are vegetatively propagated, precluding the removal of editing tools through crosses. In these cases, a transgene-free method for introduction of all components needed to enable gene editing will bring the promise of modern breeding tools within reach. Transgene-free genome editing can be accomplished through the delivery of editing components as DNA, RNA, or ribonucleoproteins with delivery via Agrobacter…

title: AI-Assisted Adaptive Interface Design for Lowering Entry Barriers in Real-Time Strategy Games
abstract: Real-time strategy (RTS) games require players to make strategic decisions while executing numerous commands. This paper presents a qualitative synthesis of recent academic research on game accessibility, human–Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistance, interface design, and community content. Six design directions are examined against accessibility, strategic depth, long-term engagement, and practical value. A layered control model is proposed with beginner, traditional, and competitive profiles sharing the same strategic rules. Routine automation requires player approval and remains visible and reversible, while tutoring uses information available to the player. Cooperative practice, hybrid interactions, and community content are considered as supporting design contexts. A conceptual mission walkthrough examines how the model could separate repeated operations from consequential decisions. The analysis yields design requirements and testable hypotheses; no prototype or new participant experiment was conducted. Controlled player studies, including unassisted transfer tasks and return-session measures, are needed to determine whether the model lowers entry barriers while preserving strategic depth.

title: Power Unit Garima Distribution: Properties, Comparison of Estimation Procedures and Diverse Applications
abstract: Summary This paper derives the power unit Garima distribution (PUGD), which is an extension of the unit Garima distribution (UGD) obtained through a power transformation. Properties of this new model, among which are mode, moments, moment generating function, entropies, extropy, and Bonferroni and Lorenz curves, are studied in detail. The relationship between the PUGD and the Garima distribution is established mathematically. Additionally, several estimation techniques for the parameters of the PUGD are examined through a Monte Carlo simulation procedure, including maximum likelihood, ordinary least squares, weighted least squares, and the Anderson–Darling and Cramer–von Mises methods. The simulation results obtained are favorable to the maximum likelihood approach. Both the observed and expected information matrices are discussed. The goodness of fit of the distribution to three data sets relating to various fields is determined relative to that of the unit power Lindley, UGD, Kumaraswamy and beta distributions. Among the distributions considered, the PUGD proved to be the best in modeling the data.

title: Beyond Ultrasound Power: Acoustic Cavitation, Nucleation Kinetics and Polymorphic Control in Palm Oil Crystallization-A Critical Review
abstract: Ultrasound-assisted crystallization offers a route to manipulate the microstructure and functional properties of palm-based fats, yet acoustic, thermal, and hydrodynamic mechanisms are frequently conflated. This critical qualitative literature review synthesizes journal evidence published in 2020–2026 concerning acoustic cavitation, nucleation kinetics, polymorphic transitions, analytical characterization, and engineering translation. Direct palm-oil studies are differentiated from related work on cocoa butter, milk fat, coconut oil, and general sonocrystallization. The literature indicates that treatment position, subcooling, agitation, lipid composition, and emulsion architecture strongly moderate the observed response. Faster crystallization and smaller crystals do not necessarily predict higher hardness, greater solid fat content, or more stable emulsions. Nominal ultrasound power also provides an incomplete description of the actual acoustic field. A multiscale attribution framework is proposed that links acoustic forcing and energy dissipation to local temperature and flow, nucleation and growth, evolving polymorphs, crystal-network architecture, and application-specific performance. The review recommends thermal-history-matched controls, characterization of delivered acoustic energy, time-resolved scattering and NMR measurements, and transparent system-level energy balan…
venue: Journal of Advanced Physics and Interdisciplinary Science

title: Recent advances and challenges in autonomous wireless implantable neurologgers for animal studies: neural recording, power supply, and data transmission technologies
abstract: Abstract Objective . Wireless implantable neurologgers are emerging as miniature autonomous systems for long-term, untethered neural recording in animal studies. However, their development remains constrained by critical engineering bottlenecks, including neural recording, power supply, and data transmission. Approach. This review systematically summarizes representative commercial neurologgers and state-of-the-art research advances. Recent progress in three key engineering areas is then reviewed, covering high-performance electrode technologies, efficient wireless power transfer strategies, and advanced communication technologies. Main results. The critical trade-offs among energy efficiency, bandwidth, transmission distance, and system complexity are identified. Furthermore, the influence of diverse application environments on system-level design and the practical implementation of neurologgers is analyzed from a new perspective. Significance. This review discusses the remaining technical challenges and future research directions, providing guidance for the development of fully autonomous wireless implantable neural recording systems for animal studies.

title: Design of Residential Photovoltaic Power Generation Systems for Low-Carbon Buildings
abstract: Decarbonising residential buildings is a combination of energy demand reduction on the demand side and renewable electricity generation on the supply side. In Shanghai, rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation could be a viable option to reduce household electric power consumption for detached residential buildings, provided PV array sizing, design of power conversion, grid-filtering and control strategy are tailored. In this paper a preliminary electrical design of a grid connected PV power generation system is based on the low carbon residential building to provide the annual electricity balance is developed. Given a winter design demand of 17.8 kWh/day, an effective sunshine duration of 3.8 h/day and a system-loss coefficient of 1.8, the PV capacity is found to be 8.43 kW. A 10.08 kWp array is selected for use, which consists of 24 mono-crystalline silicon modules, and an estimated module area of 48.0m2. The design is also specified by the direct current (DC) bus voltage of 400 V, the frequency of the DC-DC boost converter of 10 kHz, the frequency of the single-phase sinusoidal pulse-width modulation (SPWM) inverter of 20 kHz, and an inductor-capacitor-inductor (LCL) grid filter. A hybrid constant-voltage and perturb-and-observe maximum power point tracking (MPPT) strategy is employed to enhance the PV operating point tracking under the condition of irradiance change. The simula…

title: PENGARUH KUALITAS LAYANAN TERHADAP KEPUASAN PELANGGAN MELALUI HASIL LAYANAN DAN KEPERCAYAAN PELANGGAN PADA PERUSAHAN RETAIL
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of service quality on customer satisfaction through service outcomes and customer trust as mediating variables among AEON Jakarta Garden City customers. This research uses a quantitative approach with purposive sampling. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 151 respondents who met the research criteria. Data analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that service quality does not significantly affect customer satisfaction or service outcomes. However, service outcomes positively and significantly affect customer satisfaction. Service quality also positively and significantly affects customer trust, while customer trust positively and significantly affects customer satisfaction. The mediation analysis reveals that service outcomes do not mediate the relationship between service quality and customer satisfaction. In contrast, customer trust significantly mediates this relationship. These findings suggest that customer trust plays an important role in connecting service quality with customer satisfaction in the retail industry. Therefore, retail companies should consistently improve service quality to strengthen customer trust and enhance the overall shopping experience. By building reliable services and maintaining customer confidence, com…

title: Social media platforms and innovation in UK fashion retail firms: a TOE–affordance explanation
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how UK fashion retail firms use social media platforms to inform product and process innovation. Integrating the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework with affordance theory, it examines how platform-generated information is interpreted and applied to innovation-related decisions and the organisational conditions associated with these activities. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an abductive qualitative design drawing on 60 semi-structured interviews with marketing managers across 12 UK fashion retail firms, conducted between June 2023 and April 2024. Interview evidence was supplemented by 328 archival artefacts, including company websites, online catalogues and social media content. Iterative qualitative coding, informed by Gioia et al. (2013), was used to develop empirical themes and theoretical interpretations. Findings The findings show how managers reported using social media information for product refinement, collaborative product development and changes to operational routines. These reported practices are examined through four analytical categories: product-incremental, product-radical, process-incremental and process-radical innovation. Incremental changes are more directly supported by the available evidence, while the magnitude of potentially radical changes remains uncertain. Platform features, including pol…

title: Blockchain-Enabled Coordination and Pricing Optimization in Closed-Loop Supply Chains under Information Asymmetry
abstract: This paper examines the effects of blockchain technology on pricing, recycling, and coordination decisions in a closed-loop supply chain under information asymmetry. A two-echelon model consisting of one manufacturer and one retailer is constructed, with the manufacturer acting as the Stackelberg leader. The main decisions concern the wholesale price, retail price, recycling transfer price, and consumer buy-back price, while market demand and return quantity are determined endogenously. By comparing four models—traditional decentralized decision-making, centralized decision-making, blockchain information sharing, and blockchain-enabled coordination—the study finds that recycling-information asymmetry reduces the buy-back price and return quantity, while decentralized decision-making causes double marginalization. Blockchain enhances the transparency and verifiability of recycling information, but information sharing alone cannot eliminate incentive conflicts between supply chain members. Introducing a coordination contract can reproduce the centralized optimal decisions. Blockchain-enabled coordination increases total supply chain profit only when its implementation cost does not exceed the critical value K ∗ . Under this condition, a fixed transfer payment can achieve a Pareto improvement. These findings provide practical guidance for firms in evaluating blockchain investment,…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: LASSO Regression on Asset Pricing Factor Selection
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of redundant factors in asset-pricing models. The excessive inclusion of factors may result in model overspecification and multicollinearity, thereby increasing estimation uncertainty and reducing the accuracy of asset-return predictions. To address this issue, the study proposes a factor-selection procedure based on the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression model. The LASSO objective function imposes a penalty on model complexity, discouraging the inclusion of redundant factors and shrinking the coefficients of irrelevant or weakly informative factors toward zero. The proposed procedure was evaluated using monthly data from the Chinese A-share market and successfully selected seven factors from a set of 29 commonly used factors. Nevertheless, in predicting the absolute levels of individual stocks' excess returns for the following month, the model did not significantly outperform the naïve historical-mean benchmark, as indicated by an out-of-sample R-squared value slightly below zero. However, the positive mean rank information coefficient (Rank IC) suggests that the LASSO model retains some ability to identify cross-sectional differences in expected stock returns. Therefore, although its point forecasts remain limited, the model may still provide useful information for stock ranking, portfolio construction, and i…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The Belgian Prosecutorial Strategy in Foreign Terrorist Fighters Cases and the Emergence of European Joint Investigation Teams: Moving Beyond Participation-Based Terrorist Liability?
abstract: Abstract The prosecution of Belgian foreign terrorist fighters linked to the Syrian-Iraqi conflict illustrates how evidentiary constraints can shape the development of counterterrorism criminal liability. Faced with persistent difficulties in proving terrorist offences and international crimes committed abroad, Belgian judicial authorities relied on the offence of participation in the activities of a terrorist group. Belgian courts progressively adopted an interpretation of terrorist participation encompassing organisational, logistical and ideological forms of support. The development of European Joint Investigation Teams, battlefield evidence-sharing practices and cooperation through Eurojust and Europol strengthened the capacity of national authorities to investigate conduct committed in Syria and Iraq. These developments facilitated prosecutions extending beyond participation-based terrorist liability towards more serious terrorist offences and, in certain cases, genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes. The Belgian experience demonstrates how enhanced EU and International judicial cooperation may contribute to overcoming evidentiary constraints that favoured participation-based prosecutions in foreign terrorist fighter cases.
venue: European Journal of Crime, Criminal Law and Criminal Justice

title: Risk-Adjusted Returns in S&P 500 with Long-Only Cross-Sectional Momentum Strategy
abstract: Cross-sectional momentum has been used widely, but there are few researches to find the impact of portfolio concentration to long-only momentum strategy. This Paper examines how varying the number of stocks affects the performance of long-only momentum strategy in S&P 500 universe from 2000 to 2026. This study uses the standard 12-month period and skip the recent month to filter out the microstructure noises. Through picking the top n historical winners, the results show a significant balance between risk and return. Considering that evidence indicates that concentrated portfolios carry distinct trade-offs, a highly concentrated portfolio may have the highest return but also the risk of large drawdowns and elevated volatilities. However, the study may indicate that when the size of portfolio increases to n=6, the strategy could reach the optimal balance between the momentum premium and the diversification benefits. Additionally, this strategy reaches the highest Sharpe Ratio of 1.04 and shows a significant alpha of 30.84%. Therefore, these findings show that for the institutional investors who use long-only strategies, mechanically picking the extreme winners is not the best option, rather, changing the portfolio to a proper size may be the key to maximize the risk-adjusted returns.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: To What Extent Has Congestion Charging Contributed to Sustainable Urban Environmental Governance? Evidence from London and Stockholm
abstract: This paper examines the progress of congestion charging in promoting sustainable urban environmental governance in London and Stockholm. A comparative case study of traffic demand, environmental results, equity and acceptance, and long-term institutions. Both schemes reduced the amount of traffic entering the paid area significantly and permanently altered people's travel behaviour. A drop in demand did not result in a reduction of long-term congestion or air pollution because both were also influenced by capacity, growth, fleet structure, weather and traffic diversion. The schemes achieved stability through different paths: London was led by politics and administration; Stockholm was a trial run by the public and a referendum. Equity effects were determined by car dependence, alternatives and revenue utilisation. Congestion charging will thus have a relatively small and uneven effect. It is recommended that one of the first devices to be used for demand-fluctuation regulation is selected to reduce congestion and pollution.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: A Cost-Effective Object-Oriented Approach for Multiple Vehicle Tracking using Optical Flow: Comparative Review and Insights
abstract: Intelligent and dynamic traffic management is the key component for smart city development. Vehicle tracking plays a vital role in providing enhancements in urban mobility and city planning for smart city development. Real-time tracking helps authorities to manage the traffic flow, to estimate the speed of vehicles, to maintain dynamic traffic control systems, etc. Computer Vision transforms the way traffic surveillance is conducted from manual to automatic, also by making the process static and automatic. This paper provides a video processing technique to track multiple vehicles using Computer Vision.
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: Integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and the Theory of Planned Behavior to Explain Electric Vehicle Purchase Intention Through Willingness to Pay
abstract: This study examines the determinants of electric vehicle (EV) purchase intention in Indonesia by integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) through attitude and willingness to pay (WTP) as sequential mediating mechanisms. Addressing inconsistent empirical findings in prior literature regarding ease of use, infrastructure, and green lifestyle, this research offers novelty by combining psychological evaluations and financial commitments into a unified framework. A quantitative approach was applied using purposive sampling, collecting primary data via an online survey targeting Indonesian individuals aged 17 and older who are familiar with EVs and possess potential purchase interest. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) via SmartPLS 4. The model demonstrates strong predictive power, explaining variance in attitude (R2 = 0.631), WTP (R2 = 0.628), and purchase intention (R2 = 0.707) The main findings reveal that attitude and WTP significantly drive purchase intention. Subjective norm, perceived usefulness, and battery warranty positively shape attitude, while price perception and perceived behavioral control enhance WTP. Conversely, perceived ease of use and charging infrastructure show no significant direct impacts, whereas green lifestyle and battery warranty negatively affect WTP. The…

title: Space Electric and Magnetic Sensor (SEAMS) phase I: a pathfinder mission for low-frequency radio astronomy
Real-world analysis of machine learning and Pi-model techniques for SoC prediction in urban electric buses
abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of the State of Charge (SoC) of electric vehicle (EV) batteries is important for efficient energy management, battery safety, and reliable range prediction. This is particularly challenging for urban electric buses, where battery operation varies continuously with changing driving and operating conditions. Conventional model-based methods can face difficulties in such conditions because of parameter variations and limited adaptability to real-world operation. In this study, six months of real-world operational data from PMI electric buses running on the Meerut–Sardhana route in India are used to evaluate different approaches for SoC estimation. A Battery Equivalent Circuit (BEC) Pi-model is developed and its performance is compared with six machine learning approaches: Random Forest, XG Boost, Light GBM, Support Vector Regression, Linear Regression, and a hybrid K-Means-assisted regression approach. The models are evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), coefficient of determination (R 2 ), and correlation coefficient. The results show that the Pi-model and the ensemble-based ML models provide accurate SoC estimates under real-world operating conditions. Among the methods studied, the Pi-model provides the best overall performance while also offering better physical interpretability and a closer connection to the act…

title: Adaptive Measurement of Portfolio Downside Risk Based on Quantile Machine Learning
abstract: The risk of downside of the portfolio depends on volatility, drawdown, asset dependence, and regime in a nonlinear way which undermines the stability of risk measurement with fixed distribution. In this paper, we propose a machine-learning based adaptive downside risk measure that utilizes LightGBM quantile regression to predict the conditional tail of the portfolio made up of equally-weighted eight ETFs. The data is composed of daily SPY, IWM, EFA, EEM, TLT, GLD, DBC, and VNQ during the period of 2010 to 2025, and features are constructed by rolling window volatility, semivariance, drawdown, dependence, and market state. Conditional quantiles between 0.25% and 2.50% are forecast and used to construct one-day ahead 97.5% VaR and Expected Shortfall. The adaptive LightGBM in the out-of-sample test produces a pinball loss of 0.0187±0.0011, a VaR violation ratio of 1.04±0.08, and an ES backtest score of 0.021±0.006. Its joint tail loss score significantly outperforms Historical Simulation, Gaussian GARCH, and linear Quantile Regression. When the regime is volatile, the forecast improvement is still significant. Feature ablation suggests that downside-history and asset dependence variables contribute most.

title: Deep learning-driven multiclass groundwater water quality index assessment using attention mechanisms
Work–family conflict and motivation: the mediating role of perceived visionary leadership and insights from explainable machine learning
abstract: Introduction Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) and Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study examines the relationships among work–family conflict (WFC), perceived visionary leadership (VL), employee age, and motivation, focusing on the mediating role of perceived VL and the direct and moderating role of employee age. Methods Using survey data from 232 employees across various sectors, we employed a hybrid explanatory–predictive quantitative framework combining Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with six supervised machine learning (ML) algorithms (Ridge, Lasso, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost) and explainable ML techniques. Model generalizability was further assessed using repeated and nested cross-validation. Results PLS-SEM indicated that WFC was not directly associated with employee motivation, whereas a statistically significant indirect association emerged through perceived VL. Age was associated with motivation and moderated the relationship between WFC and motivation. The predictive analyses provided complementary rather than confirmatory evidence. Within the LightGBM explainability analyses, perceived VL emerged as the most influential predictor, while WFC and age also contributed to prediction. The explanatory and predictive analyses showed partial convergence, particularly regarding the prominence of perceived VL, w…

title: Community of Inquiry in Technology-Mediated Collaborative Learning: A Bibliometric Analysis (2021-2025)
abstract: Background and Aim: Technology-mediated learning has attracted growing interest in higher education, including applications of the Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework. This study mapped publication trends, contributors, bibliographic relationships, and research themes in this field between 2021 and 2025. Materials and Methods: Bibliometric data were retrieved from Dimensions AI on 22 July 2026. Article selection was reported using PRISMA 2020. The initial 37,715 records were filtered by publication year, publication type, research field, Sustainable Development Goal, open-access status, and selected source titles, yielding 278 open-access journal articles. Performance analysis, bibliographic coupling, and keyword co-occurrence analysis using VOSviewer examined publication patterns, citation impact, contributing authors, organizations, countries, sources, and thematic associations. Results: Annual output increased from 37 articles in 2021 to 67 in 2023, declined to 55 in 2024, and reached 69 in 2025. China and the United States contributed 32 and 31 publications, respectively. A study by Ayanwale received the most citations (291), while Education and Information Technologies demonstrated the highest citation impact among the analyzed sources. Bibliographic coupling identified publication groups sharing reference structures. Keyword co-occurrence revealed three thematic clusters…

title: Selecting Translations for Young Readers: An Educational Framework for Reading Foreign Literary Works
abstract: Background and Aims: Selecting suitable translations of foreign literature for young readers requires attention not only to textual fidelity but also to accessibility, aesthetic quality, age appropriateness, and educational purpose. However, teachers often lack a systematic basis for comparing editions. This conceptual article proposes an educational framework for selecting Chinese translations of foreign literary works and reinterprets translation principles for literary education. Methodology: The framework was developed through pedagogical reflection, illustrative comparison of Chinese translations, and engagement with scholarship on translation, children’s literature, and literary education. Chinese versions of The Little Mermaid, The Happy Prince, and The Little Prince were used as illustrative cases rather than as an empirical sample. Results: The proposed framework comprises three stages: preliminary screening of translators and editions, professional educational evaluation, and reader-oriented validation. Yan Fu’s principles of faithfulness, expressiveness, and elegance are reformulated as knowledge, language, and aesthetic engagement. The illustrative comparisons demonstrate how textual completeness, lexical choice, readability, imagery, rhythm, tone, and literary style can shape educational suitability. The framework encourages teachers to consider both source-text re…

title: Discrepancies between simulation and clinical practice: Implications for self-directed learning in nursing education
abstract: Background: Self-directed simulation learning (SSL) is increasingly recognised as an essential approach in nursing education, empowering students to identify their own learning needs, practice skills and build confidence. Despite its benefits, inconsistencies between the simulation and clinical practice environments hinder the effective use of SSL. Aim: This study explored student nurses’ experiences with SSL, focusing on the impact of discrepancies between simulation and clinical environments on their learning. It further explored strategies to enhance the effectiveness of SSL in nursing education. Setting: The research was conducted at a public university in South Africa within the Faculty of Health Sciences, where the Department of Nursing shares a simulation laboratory with 11 other health science disciplines. Methods: Using a qualitative, exploratory and descriptive design, 19 third-year nursing students were purposively sampled. Data were gathered through four online focus group discussions and analysed thematically following Tesch’s method. Results: Participants reported that the self-directed simulation-based learning often felt unrealistic and discrepant from clinical practice. They described differences in how procedures were demonstrated across the two contexts, which led to confusion, reduced confidence and decreased motivation to use SSL. Conclusion: The simulation…

Generative AI Misuse and Rule Compliance Among University Students in Bhutan: Implications for Assessment and Institutional AI Policy
abstract: Background and Aim: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) use is expanding in Bhutanese universities while institutional policies remain under development. Guided by an extended Theory of Planned Behavior, this study examined factors associated with unauthorized AI use and intention to comply with institutional AI policies. Materials and Methods: An anonymous, cross-sectional survey was conducted in June 2026 among a convenience sample of 713 Bhutanese university students. Seven-point Likert-type responses were analyzed using factor analyses, reliability assessments, correlations with false discovery rate correction, multiple and moderated regression, and bootstrapped indirect association tests. Robustness checks included robust standard errors and demographic controls. Results: The models explained 24.5% of variance in AI misuse and 19.6% in compliance intention. Approximately 29% of respondents endorsed at least one misuse item. Misuse was associated with misuse acceptability, AI familiarity, academic pressure, moral rationalization, rule clarity, subjective norms, and learning impact. Compliance intention was associated with subjective norms, rule clarity, behavioral control, productive AI use, institutional enforcement, and moral rationalization. Institutional enforcement showed a small independent association with compliance intention (β = .086). Compliance intention was…
