title: A machine learning-based model for predicting 5-year conditional survival in patients with colon cancer: a development and validation study
abstract: Background Most prognostic models for colon cancer are not tailored to the Chinese population or implemented clinically. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for five-year conditional survival and compare conventional logistic regression with machine learning models to develop an optimal predictive model. Methods This retrospective study included 430 newly diagnosed colon cancer patients from Suzhou Municipal Hospital (2015–2022). Clinicopathological data and dynamic tumor markers—carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9)—were collected. Patients were randomly split 70:30 into training (n=301) and validation (n=129) sets. This study employed a dual feature selection strategy combining the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and Boruta algorithms. One conventional logistic regression model and six machine learning models (including XGBoost) were built. Performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score, and F1 score, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) employed for model interpretability. Results Nine core predictors were selected: clinical stage, differentiation, distant metastasis, surgery, targeted therapy, and baseline and 12-month CEA and CA19–9 levels. The XGBoost model performed best, achieving an AUC of 0.955, the highest F1 score (0.904), and the…

title: Exploring Kindergarten Teachers’ Experiences in Using Teacher-Made Interactive Reading Materials
abstract: Background and Aim: Teacher-made interactive reading materials can provide context-responsive opportunities for early literacy instruction. This study explored kindergarten teachers’ experiences in developing and using these materials in Tubod, Lanao del Norte, Philippines, focusing on preparation, instructional use, perceived benefits, challenges, and coping strategies. Materials and Methods: A qualitative single-case study involved seven purposively selected public-school kindergarten teachers with relevant experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, field notes, artifact analysis, and document review and analysed thematically. Triangulation and member checking supported credibility. Classroom observations were not conducted. Results: Teachers developed three main categories of materials: flash cards and charts, multisensory and hands-on resources, and materials informed by the Marungko Approach and Claveria Technique. Preparation reflected learning objectives, learner readiness, and available low-cost resources. Teachers integrated the materials into guided instruction, scaffolding, questioning, modelling, repeated practice, and play-based activities. They reported increased attention and participation, as well as support for letter–sound recognition and foundational reading skills. Financial constraints, preparation demands, and limited durability co…

Generative Artificial Intelligence in High School Science Education: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, Pedagogical Strategies, and Critical Thinking Development
abstract: Background and Aim: Evidence on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in secondary science education remains limited. This systematic review examined students’ conceptual understanding and engagement, teachers’ pedagogical strategies and challenges, and students’ critical thinking and scientific inquiry. Materials and Methods: Following PRISMA 2020, ERIC, Scopus, and Lens.org were searched for peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2022 and 2026. Two authors independently screened 187 unique records (Cohen’s κ = .78), identifying 20 eligible studies. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Framework synthesis integrated findings, informed by Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK). Results: Seven studies assessed AI capabilities rather than classroom implementation. Only two compared learning outcomes across conditions; none employed a randomized controlled design. Student perceptions and engagement were generally positive, whereas learning outcomes were mixed. A chatbot supporting self-regulated learning outperformed a rule-based chatbot, but ChatGPT-4o yielded smaller gains than peer collaboration. Teachers reported concerns regarding content accuracy, assessment reliability, and instructional readiness. Generative AI matched or exceeded student performance on structured examinations but demonstrated lower grading r…

title: Bridging Cultures through Brushstrokes: A Framework for Chinese Calligraphy Transmission in Thai Educational Contexts
abstract: Background and Aim: Chinese calligraphy embodies philosophy, aesthetics, and historical memory. Thailand’s longstanding ties with China, Chinese community, and expanding digital infrastructure offer opportunities for its transmission, yet pathways into formal education remain underexplored. This study develops a localized framework for teaching calligraphy to Thai Generation Z learners. Materials and Methods: A qualitative thematic synthesis examined nine curated references published from 2022 to 2025 and retrieved through CNKI, Thai-Journal Online, and Google Scholar. Following Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis, the study triangulated Chinese scholarship on international calligraphy communication, Thai research on youth media use and primary-level teaching, and international research on digital-native engagement with traditional culture. This targeted corpus does not constitute a systematic review. Results: Four interconnected pillars emerged: reciprocal cross-cultural communication; a three-tier curriculum adapted to Thai learners; promotion through classroom instruction, digital media, and cultural activities; and institutional support. Five barriers were identified, with inadequate standardized curricula and qualified teachers posing the greatest challenges. The proposed Cultural Resonance Zone identifies shared Buddhist values, indirect communication styles, and aesthet…

title: Decoding Configurational Populations and Temperature of Flexible Chiral Molecules from Chiral Optical Spectra with Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Quantitative determination of configurational populations in flexible chiral molecules is challenging due to spectral overlap, conformational averaging, and random noise. Here, we present a multitask residual network that integrates quantum chemical calculations, spectral simulation, and deep learning to achieve configurational inversion from spectroscopic data. As a proof-of-concept study, the neural network uses DFT-computed ultraviolet–visible absorption and electronic circular dichroism spectra as input to simultaneously predict the populations of configurational isomers and the thermodynamic temperature of the system. Demonstrated on the flexible chiral drug molecule labetalol, the method achieves high accuracy: under 10% spectral noise, the root-mean-square error for configurational populations is about 8.2%, and the temperature error is below 3.4 °C. The successful inversion demonstrates that machine learning can effectively bridge spectroscopic observables and statistical thermodynamics, providing a rapid, data-driven paradigm for resolving structural distributions in complex flexible chiral systems.
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C

title: Application Patterns and Educational Effects of Intelligent Tutoring Systems for Memory Learning in K-12 Education
abstract: It is crucial for K-12 students to find a way to remember the information they have learned, particularly when working with an intelligent tutoring system. In order to learn more about how intelligent tutoring systems can assist them in this process, the literature review was conducted in relation to documents that were published between the dates of January 1st 2018 and August 31st 2026. The methods that were studied include spaced practice, AI-based question creation, visual flashcards, and gamification. Various outcomes were obtained from the studies; the textbooks that were studied on the subject of spaced practice and visual flashcards offered information on retaining vocabulary, while studies examining the art of question formulation provided information about the practice of retrieval and feedback technique. However, investigations into the gamification of intelligent tutoring systems mainly examined how effective the system is in terms of how engaged learners were with the learning material. Therefore, all of the studies were conducted with different samples and settings. In the general sense, it can be said that using computer-assisted instruction properly is one of the most effective methods of memory retention learning in K-12 education, which provides the strongest effectiveness in the area of vocabulary retention.

title: A study into the seismic settings and rock-bump hazard at the Kukisvumchorr apatite-nepheline deposit at the deep +10 m level
abstract: This article presents the results of studying seismic activity with increasing mining depth using the Kukisvumchorr apatite-nepheline deposit (the Khibiny Mountain Range) as a case study. The study is based on a statistical assessment of the seismic settings of the deposit as a whole and a predictive assessment of the state of Block 9/12 at the deep +10 m level. The following main seismicity levels were used to describe the dynamics of the seismic settings: extremely high, high, elevated background, average background, and reduced background. Geomechanical situation in adjacent Blocks 12/15 and 15/18, where mining operations are underway, was analyzed to forecast the condition of Block 9/12. Zones with higher seismic activity and a high level of stress-and-strain state in the boundary part of the mass at deep mining levels (+25 m; +50 m; +75 m; +10 m) were identified using the methods of regional rock-burst hazard forecasting, i.e. analytical (numerical) stress state modeling, visual inspection of the mine workings, and the results of continuous seismic monitoring. A visual inspection of the mine workings confirmed the development of localized areas showing signs of rock pressure. A spatiotemporal assessment of the seismic anomalies has shown that seismicity moves along with the advance of the mining front, including the depth changes. Significant geodynamic phenomena have been…

Tourism uncertainty and the behaviour of travel and leisure stocks in Europe, the UK and the USA
abstract: Purpose This study investigates whether tourism uncertainty predicts the behaviour of travel and leisure (T&L) stocks in Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States of America. Specifically, it examines the predictive role of the Tourism Uncertainty Index for realised volatility and risk premia while assessing whether tourism uncertainty provides additional forecasting information beyond geopolitical risk. Design/methodology/approach The study uses the Westerlund–Narayan feasible generalised least squares (FGLS) predictability framework, which accounts for persistence, endogeneity and conditional heteroskedasticity. The study conducts both in-sample predictability and out-of-sample forecasting analyses, employing the Clark–West test to evaluate forecast improvements. Tourism uncertainty is examined alongside geopolitical risk for the UK, Europe, the USA and additional regional market classifications. Findings Our findings show that tourism uncertainty significantly and increasingly predicts realised volatility and risk premia in Europe and, to a lesser extent, in the UK, indicating that tourism-specific uncertainty may be priced differently across these markets. Out-of-sample results show that tourism uncertainty consistently improves volatility forecasts and enhances risk-premia forecasts, particularly for Europe and the USA, beyond the information contained in geopoliti…

title: The Behaviour of Gold Prices During Periods of Economic Uncertainty
abstract: Gold is generally regarded as a safe-haven asset, but its price behavior differs in the different phases of a crisis. This paper investigates the co-movement of gold prices with economic policy uncertainty, market risk sentiment, and key financial market variables using monthly data from January 2006 to December 2025 and compares gold price performance during the 2008 global financial crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic. Descriptive statistics, trend comparison and case analysis are used to investigate the variations of the Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index (GEPU), VIX, the US Dollar Index, the US 10-year real interest rate and the S&P 500 Index. The analysis reveals that gold prices do not always move together with risk indicators. Gold might be under some pressure at first as the US dollar strengthens and liquidity pressures build up in the early stages of a crisis, but gold prices may rise again as real interest rates fall and the financial market environment changes. Gold's function as a safe-haven asset was phased and conditional in both crises.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Leading Through Uncertainty: How Leadership Agility Influences Organizational Resilience and Performance
abstract: Organizations facing uncertainty must interpret incomplete information, coordinate responses and protect performance while preserving their capacity to adapt. This conceptual paper develops a framework explaining how leadership agility may contribute to organizational resilience and performance. A focused, non-systematic synthesis integrates selected leadership, resilience and dynamic capabilities literature, comparing concepts, findings and contextual limitations. The framework proposes that leaders’ sensing, revisable decisions, coordination and learning may become shared organizational routines supporting anticipation, coping and adaptation. Organizational resilience may connect leadership agility with performance, while a direct leadership–performance pathway remains possible. Six propositions address these relationships, differences across performance outcomes and time horizons, and the roles of environmental uncertainty and resource availability. The paper contributes a leader-to-collective explanation of resilience and distinguishes continuity during disruption from recovery and longer-term renewal. Practical implications concern decision authority, information sharing, routine development and balanced performance assessment. The study collects no primary data and does not test causal effects; its propositions require longitudinal and multilevel investigation. Purposive …

title: An uncertainty-aware deep learning-based registration model for adaptive lung cancer radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Objective . To develop a deep learning (DL) based probabilistic 3D deformable image registration framework for uncertainty-aware dose accumulation in magnetic resonance imaging-guided radiotherapy of lung cancer. Approach . We propose TransMorph-prob (TM-prob), a variational Bayesian model that predicts the voxel-wise mean and variance of dense displacement fields (DDFs). Two TM-prob models were trained on an internal computed tomography dataset (725 patients) and a low-field MR-linac dataset (102 patients), and benchmarked against Monte Carlo dropout TransMorph (TM-MCD) and DIRUncertainty with B-spline initialization (ASDIR) on the deformable image registration laboratory (DIRLAB) 4DCT dataset (10 patients, 3000 landmarks), and an annotated MR-linac dataset (16 patients, 107 image pairs, 227 landmarks) with target and seven organ-at-risk contours. Both datasets contained an additional 1239/13 289 algorithm-generated landmarks. Performance was evaluated using target registration error (TRE), Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), landmark- and voxel-wise expected calibration errors (LECE/ECE), and dose distributions derived from 2000 DDF samples per patient. Main results . On the DIRLAB dataset, TM-prob achieved a median TRE of 1.8 mm/2.8 mm on manual/algorithm-generated landmarks, versus 1.3 mm/2.4 mm for ASDIR and 2.1 mm/3.0 mm for TM-MCD. On the MRI dataset, TM-prob ach…

title: Depression, anxiety, stress, and intolerance of uncertainty during the COVID-19 pandemic by considering the impact of pre-existing mental health issues
abstract: Purpose This research was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study aims to investigate self-reported mental health issues in a public sample, including depression, anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty about the future. Design/methodology/approach A public sample (N = 313) was obtained through social media, and collected using an online survey. Participants completed a series of demographic questions including disclosure about previous mental health issues, the depression anxiety stress scale (DASS) and the intolerance uncertainty scale (IUS). Findings There was a strong positive relationship between elements of the DASS and IUS. Having previous mental health issues were strongly associated with higher scores across all measures. Originality/value Evidence is provided to support the notion that additional stress, anxiety and fear is experienced by people with pre-existing mental health issues during unprecedented times. This research offers a unique insight into the mental health of the general public during a global pandemic.

title: Enhancing stiffness and flexural properties of dissimilar friction stir welding between 3D-Printed PLA/TiO 2 and PEEK/CNT nanocomposites: parametric optimization using Taguchi method
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive parametric analysis and optimization of friction stir welding (FSW) for dissimilar joining of additively manufactured nanocomposites: polylactic acid reinforced with TiO 2 nanoparticles (PLA/TiO 2 ) and polyether ether ketone reinforced with carbon nanotubes (PEEK/CNT). The main focus is to evaluate the effects of welding parameters – rotation speed, traverse speed, and tool tilt angle – on the flexural strength and elastic modulus of the welded joints. The experiments were designed using the Taguchi method, and the grey relational analysis (GRA) technique was used to determine the optimal conditions for maximizing both flexural strength and elastic modulus. Signal to noise (S/N) analysis revealed that rotation speed exerts the most significant influence on both flexural strength and elastic modulus, followed by traverse speed. The optimal parameter combination was 1,500 rpm rotation speed, 10 mm/s traverse speed, and 2° tilt angle, under which elastic modulus and flexural strength improved by 11 % and 32 %, respectively. Under these optimized settings, the welded joint achieved 80 % of the elastic modulus and 75 % of the flexural strength of the weaker base nanocomposite (PLA/TiO 2 ). Microstructural analysis confirmed that adequate heat input at 1,500 rpm promoted smooth flow lines and a dense, defect-free interface, while excessiv…

title: Analysis and Optimization of Flow Characteristics in Hollow Microneedle Lumen Based on Poiseuille's Law
abstract: Microneedle patches represent an innovative transdermal drug delivery technology that offers painless administration and improved patient compliance. An in-depth understanding of the hydrodynamic characteristics in microneedle channels is crucial for optimizing drug delivery efficiency. This paper explores the flow characteristics of drug solutions within microneedle channels, focusing on the applicability of Poiseuille's law and the influence of geometric parameters on flow rate. Based on Poiseuille's law, an analytical flow model of microneedle array is established in this study. The results show that the inner lumen radius is the most critical parameter ( S R =4), significantly higher than those of pressure and needle length. When R = 35μm, L = 250μm, ΔP = 30kPa, the optimal design can achieve a maximum flow rate of 4741 μL/min. This study provides a theoretical basis and rapid design methodology for geometric parameter optimization of microneedle patches, offering valuable reference for advancing transdermal drug delivery technology.

Phase 1/2 trial of Evomela for autologous transplant in myeloma: schedule optimization and matched comparison with MEL200
abstract: Abstract Melphalan 200 mg/m2 is the standard conditioning regimen for autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT) in multiple myeloma, but further dose escalation is limited by toxicity. Evomela, a propylene glycol–free melphalan with enhanced stability, enables safer dose intensification and pharmacokinetic (PK) optimization. We conducted a prospective phase 1/2 trial to optimize Evomela dosing and infusion schedule in patients with newly diagnosed myeloma undergoing ASCT. Primary objectives included dose/schedule optimization using a Bayesian design and PK characterization; secondary objectives included minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative complete response (CR) at day 90, toxicity, and progression-free survival (PFS). Sixty patients were randomized to short (30-60 minutes) or long (8-9 hours) Evomela infusions at 200 or 225 mg/m2. No grade ≥4 nonhematologic toxicities or day-100 nonrelapse mortality occurred. MRD-negative stringent CR (sCR)/CR at day 90 was 45% (43% in the short-infusion arm and 47% in the long-infusion arm), with similar toxicity and PFS between the schedules. A higher melphalan area under the concentration–time curve (AUC) was strongly associated with MRD-negative sCR/CR (posterior probability of benefit [PBE] of 0.99) without increased toxicity but not with PFS. In propensity-matched comparisons, Evomela was associated with longer PFS tha…

title: Harris Hawks Optimization–Optimized Explainable Quality Index for Tomato Grading
abstract: Automated tomato ripeness and quality grading is essential for precision agriculture and industrial packing lines, replacing slow, subjective manual sorting. Most reported systems, however, rely on heavy deep networks or a single accuracy figure without ablation, statistical validation, or an explicit accuracy–interpretability–latency trade-off. This study proposes HHO-XQI, a Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO)-optimized Explainable Quality Index that fuses interpretable color-statistical features into a continuous Tomato Quality Index for four-class grading (Damaged, Old, Ripe, Unripe). The framework extracts 125 RGB/HSV/Lab colorstatistical descriptors, fuses four base learners (logistic regression, random forest, extra trees, k-nearest neighbors) via HHO-optimized soft voting on 7,226 images, and is benchmarked against a fine-tuned ResNet18 CNN with Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). Evaluation combined held-out accuracy/macro-F1, repeated cross-validation with Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests, feature- and ensemble-composition ablation, HHO sensitivity/convergence analysis, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attribution, and latency/training-time profiling. title: An Integrated Framework for Fair and Interpretable Predictive Modeling in Educational Analytics
abstract: As learning analytics becomes more widely used in education, there is a need to develop predictive models that account for a range of real-world factors. However, existing predictive systems emphasize model performance more than the design of transparent, trustworthy models. This study combines model performance, fairness, and interpretability in a single pipeline. The integrated predictive framework evaluates five classification models under stratified cross-validation on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD). Two data files are selected from the dataset for model development. The processed data comprises 32,593 merged records with demographic and behavioral features of the learners. SVM-RBF and gradient boosting classifiers show similar, high predictive performance in mean Accuracy, AUC, and F1-score. Fairness is assessed using gender as the sensitive attribute. Random forest shows the lowest group disparities, with a mean Demographic Parity Difference (DPD) of 0.1147 and an Equalized Odds Difference (EOD) of 0.1610. Statistical analysis further identifies significant classifier differences in all metrics except DPD; however, pairwise tests show no significant difference for any metric. SHAP provides feature importance plots for model interpretation based on the sensitive attribute. They show that the behavioral features contribute more to predictions than de…

Neuroendocrine neoplasms of the digestive system: challenges of biopsy diagnosis
abstract: Abstract The diagnosis of digestive neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) is increasingly being made on endoscopic biopsies and endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration/biopsy (EUS-FNA/FNB) or ultrasound biopsies taken from metastases. Although current classification systems provide a robust and elaborate framework for categorizing NENs, their application to limited tissue biopsy samples often remains challenging. A major challenge is the accurate distinction between well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), which is essential because of their markedly different prognostic and therapeutic implications. Additional challenges include reliable Ki-67 assessment, recognition of intratumoral heterogeneity, and identification of mixed neoplasms, including mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) and amphicrine-like carcinoma (ALC)—a recently introduced and still poorly characterized category—and assignment of the primary site in metastatic disease using organ-associated immunohistochemical markers. Site-specific differences in morphology and immunophenotype further complicate biopsy interpretation and require integration of histological, immunohistochemical, clinical, and radiological findings. Although morphology remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, molecular testing is increasingly used in dif…

title: De-dollarization: Drivers, Institutional Constraints, and the Evolution of the International Monetary System
abstract: The inherent contradictions of the dollar-centered international monetary system have become increasingly prominent in recent decades, compounded by geopolitical tensions and fluctuations in US monetary policy. These developments have intensified efforts by some countries and emerging economies to reduce their dependence on the US dollar, contributing to structural adjustments in the international monetary system. This paper examines the global de-dollarization trend and systematically analyzes its realistic drivers and institutional constraints through literature review, mechanism analysis, and comparative research. The study finds that the evolution of the Triffin dilemma under the dollar standard, the weaponization of dollar-based financial tools, and deepening monetary cooperation among emerging economies jointly constitute the realistic drivers of de-dollarization. However, institutional constraints, including currency network externalities, lock-in effects of global settlement infrastructure, and developmental limitations of alternative currencies, determine that de-dollarization will be a long-term, gradual process. In the long run, the international monetary system may become more multipolar, and currencies of emerging markets can enhance their international influence through continuous institutional improvement.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Characterizing the post-marketing safety profile of duvelisib: a comprehensive pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA adverse event reporting system
abstract: Introduction Duvelisib, a dual phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-δ/γ inhibitor, is used for relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), but serious safety concerns warrant continued post-marketing surveillance. Methods We analyzed the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from the third quarter of 2018 through the second quarter of 2026. Duvelisib-associated adverse events (AEs) were evaluated using disproportionality analysis and clinical priority scoring. Serious vs. non-serious AE patterns, subgroup differences, factors associated with serious AE (SAE) reporting, and comparative reporting disproportionality vs. ofatumumab were also assessed. Results Among 11,580,309 FAERS reports, 703 duvelisib-associated reports were included. Death was the only strong-priority signal, while pneumonia, sepsis, enterocolitis, colitis, and diarrhoea were classified as moderate-priority signals. Infectious enteritis showed the highest disproportionality (ROR025 = 49.63) but was based on only six reports and received weak clinical priority. Among reports with death recorded as an outcome, significant SAE signals included colitis, stomatitis, dehydration, hepatic failure, diarrhoea, and pneumonia. Subgroup analyses showed disproportionate SAE reporting among patients aged <65 years, reports from North America, T-cell lymphoma, and no…

title: Acute Total Ammonia Nitrogen Exposure in Pacific White Shrimp ( Litopenaeus vanname i): Physiological and Multi-Omics Responses Associated with Tissue Semicarbazide
abstract: Abstract Acute total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) exposure may impair shrimp health, while the interpretation of semicarbazide (SEM) in crustaceans remains uncertain. We examined physiological, histological, omics, and SEM responses to a 96 h toxicity assay and a 48 h graded TAN challenge (0–20 mg/L), with end point hepatopancreas metabolomics and transcriptomics in the control and 20 mg/L groups. The 96 h LC50 was 24.43 mg/L TAN. High TAN caused gill and hepatopancreas lesions, increased apoptosis, and altered amino acid, purine, energy, lipid, and immune-related profiles. SEM was detectable in shell and gill, including control shell, but not in muscle or hepatopancreas under the analytical conditions used. Shell SEM was associated with several stress indices, and nor-NOHA treatment and in vitro oxidation provided exploratory evidence consistent with a possible role of arginine-related metabolism. These data are consistent with a transition from adaptation to injury and endogenous SEM formation under acute TAN stress.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Hidden-genes multi-dimensional archive of phenotypic elites: a quality-diversity algorithm for conditional search-space problems
abstract: Abstract The preliminary design and optimization of engineering systems requires to make architectural and technological choices that can be represented by design variables called conditional variables. They are acting on the structure of the optimization problem (e.g., number of design variables and constraints) along the iterations. In the early design phases, the decision makers may be interested in obtaining a set of valuable solutions presenting a diversity of characteristics. Quality-Diversity (QD) is an optimization paradigm tailored for providing optimal solutions with respect to an objective function and diversified with respect to feature functions. Multi-dimensional Archive of Phenotypic Elites (MAP-Elites) is a popular QD algorithm which explores the design space using evolutionary operations. This work extends the MAP-Elites algorithm to deal with conditional variables by developing an adapted mutation mechanism. The performance of the proposed method is assessed on four test-cases of increasing complexity. Three of them are analytical and the last one is an engineering representative problem dealing with the design of a sounding rocket.

title: Exploring user perceptions of customer-centricity in chatbot interactions: a multi-method study in the healthcare sector
abstract: Purpose The advent and integration of technology have reshaped the interaction between customers and service providers across the customer journey. In the healthcare sector, chatbots are increasingly being adopted by service providers. Despite their growing usage, the perceived effectiveness of these tools depends on how users evaluate their customer-centricity. This paper investigates the user perceptions of customer-centricity in chatbot interactions. The study focuses on the healthcare sector. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory sequential multi-method approach was adopted, combining Grounded Theory and Total Interpretive Structural Modelling for this study. Findings The findings identify that perceived customer-centricity and customer satisfaction are driven by factors like digital empathy, trust, anthropomorphism, perceived usefulness, perceived control and perceived ease of use. The findings will help healthcare providers in designing more human-centric and emotionally intelligent chatbot systems. Originality/value The study contributes to the understanding of AI-mediated healthcare interactions by highlighting different aspects of chatbot experiences and their structural influence on customer-centricity.
venue: International Journal of Health Care Quality Assurance

title: Multi-dimensional signal exploration on the effect of tremor interventions
abstract: Background Machine learning in tremor time-series analysis has so far been applied to differentiate tremor disorders. Respective analytical approaches can similarly be geared to explore therapeutic interventions, which conventionally are assessed by their induced amplitude changes. This may overlook subtle signal alterations. Feature-based machine learning offers the potential to explore much more granular tremor signal changes induced by therapeutic interventions. Objective To investigate multidimensional time-series signal changes associated with tremor-modulating interventions, and to identify shared and distinct intervention-specific patterns across tremor conditions. Methods Sixty-six participants (Essential Tremor (ET): propranolol n = 13, deep brain stimulation (DBS) n = 10; Parkinson’s Disease (PD): levodopa n = 23; enhanced Physiological Tremor (ePT): caffeine n = 20) were assessed in therapeutic OFF and ON states using high-resolution tri-axial accelerometry. In addition to established tremor characteristics, advanced time-series features were extracted from raw recordings. Machine Learning (ML) approaches, including ensemble classification and Principal Component Analysis (PCA), were applied to detect intervention-related changes. title: ST-M 2 EDA: spatio-temporal metric-guided multi-stream expert domain adaptation network for fatigue monitoring
abstract: Abstract In the human-machine collaboration paradigms of Industry 5.0, the intrinsic non-stationarity and domain drift of electroencephalogram signals pose significant challenges to fatigue monitoring. Consequently, achieving accurate and robust cross-subject fatigue detection is paramount for workplace safety. This paper proposes a Spatio-Temporal Metric-Guided Multi-Stream Expert Domain Adaptation Network. The framework initially employs Singular Value Decomposition-based signal reconstruction to attenuate non-stationary noise, followed by Mixup data augmentation to enhance and smooth the feature space distribution. Furthermore, a hybrid architecture integrating Domain-Specific Batch Normalization with a ResNet-Transformer backbone is constructed to precisely decouple statistical discrepancies between domains. Finally, Multi-Kernel Maximum Mean Discrepancy is introduced as a dynamic routing criterion to facilitate fine-grained, adaptive decision-making for target samples. The baseline experiments on the SEED-VIG dataset yield a subject-wise mean accuracy of 90.54% across all 23 subjects, including S15. Visual analysis of brain topography confirms that the model successfully aligns distributional shifts caused by individual heterogeneity—specifically correcting for specific frontotemporal lobe activation observed in subject S7—and establishes distinct decision boundaries. Thes…

title: Multi-band localized surface plasmon enhanced terahertz biosensor chip with electrostatic and acousto-optic active tuning
abstract: Introduction Terahertz (THz) biosensing can read biomolecular vibrations without labels, yet two practical problems limit its sensitivity: sub-wavelength biological samples interact only weakly with the radiation, and 1/f noise dominates slow readouts. Methods We propose a multi-band localized surface plasmon (LSP)-enhanced THz biosensor chip in which a gold metasurface of nine spectrally isolated cross-resonator sub-arrays sustains LSP resonances at 0.1–0.9 THz, concentrating the field in deep-sub-wavelength hot spots at the resonator arm ends and gaps. An in-plane electrostatic bias tunes any resonance by up to 7.5%, and a 60 MHz surface acoustic wave (SAW) modulates the transmitted signal so that lock-in readout can reject roughly 15 dB of low-frequency noise. Coupled-mode theory was used to compute the transmission, near-field enhancement, tuning, and detection-limit improvement; the same array supports two readout modes, broadband THz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and direct THz-induced micro-current detection. Results The calculations give a field enhancement of 17–33×, per-band redshifts of 1.6–2.8% that vary by band and can be read as a nine-point spectral pattern against calibration spectra, and a 39.6–45.4 dB improvement in detection limit over bare THz-TDS, corresponding to a 95–186× reduction in the minimum detectable amplitude. Discussion The intended analytes…

title: Addressing the Diglossic Gap in Arabic audio deepfake detection with a multi-dialect benchmark and multi-representation fusion detector
abstract: Abstract Arabic audio deepfake detection is challenged by the interaction of within-language dialectal variation, prosody, recording conditions, codec history, and rapidly evolving synthesis technologies. We characterize this compound target-domain shift through the Diglossic Gap , a structured taxonomy spanning dialectal/phonetic, prosodic, channel/acquisition, and synthesis-source variation. We introduce DeepShield, a 5030-file Arabic audio corpus comprising 2375 genuine and 2655 synthetic recordings spanning voice cloning, text-to-speech, and voice conversion. The experimental protocol uses a balanced 1600-file target-adaptation partition and a locked, file-disjoint 2089-file independent test partition, with an additional 1341 recordings reserved outside the active protocol. DeepShield Fusion integrates SincNet/ECAPA-TDNN, wav2vec 2.0, and EfficientNetV2-S + BiGRU evidence through validation-locked score fusion and achieves 91.00% accuracy, 9.20% equal error rate (EER), and 0.9652 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) using the opening 4 s of each recording. A duration-stratified ablation further verifies the contribution of padding-aware Smart Attention-Mask Pooling, reducing wav2vec 2.0 EER from 17.90% to 17.25%. Comprehensive comparative evaluation against RawNet2, WavLM-Base+, and LFCC-LCNN yields EERs of 8.31%, 6.49%, and 5.19%, respectively. Buil…

title: Genetic structure, inbreeding and effective population size in an endangered island cockatoo, following management-led recovery
abstract: Abstract Island populations are particularly vulnerable to genetic risk. The glossy black-cockatoo Calyptorhynchus lathami halmaturinus has been restricted to Kangaroo Island, South Australia, since the mid-20th century and had declined to a few hundred individuals before management-led recovery. To understand how this population bottleneck might have affected population structure, genetic diversity and inbreeding, we analyzed single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), principally generated from feather samples collected from nestlings during two breeding seasons. We investigated differences in genetic variability between population ‘flocks’ across the island. Overall F IS was 0.02 and mean allelic richness was 1.84. Low pairwise F ST values (-0.001-0.04) indicated genetic connectivity between the flocks, however, genetic differentiation (P ≤ 0.004) between all but the two eastern flocks suggests some limitations to gene flow. Seventeen per cent of individuals were highly inbred, with more than a third of these individuals from the most eastern flock. While there was no substantial population structure, analysis indicated some differentiation of the currently expanding eastern flock. Spatial autocorrelation found stronger than random relatedness amongst nestlings in nesting clusters, confirming suggestions from previous studies. The estimated effective population size ( N e ) was …

title: ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ КАК ФАКТОР ТРАНСФОРМАЦИИ ТЕХНОЛОГИЧЕСКОЙ ЭКОСИСТЕМЫ КАЗАХСТАНА: МЕТОДОЛОГИЯ УПРАВЛЕНИЯ РЫНОЧНОЙ КОНВЕРСИЕЙ ИННОВАЦИЙ
abstract: Цель исследования — обосновать методологию управления развитием технологической экосистемы Казахстана в условиях распространения искусственного интеллекта. На основе теоретического синтеза концепций инновационных систем, предпринимательских экосистем и динамических способностей предложена модель способности к рыночной конверсии (MCC). Она рассматривает развитие технологических компаний как последовательность переходов от разработки к пилотному внедрению, оплачиваемому контракту, экспорту и масштабированию. Функциональная модель GICTM описывает доступность управления и регулирования, инфраструктуры, капитала, кадров и рынков, а вектор TPV — вероятность, продолжительность и качество рыночного перехода. Предложен алгоритм диагностики ограничений и адаптивного выбора инструментов поддержки. Специфика искусственного интеллекта раскрывается через требования к данным, вычислениям, надежности моделей, безопасности и промышленной интеграции. Применение подхода к институциональной среде Казахстана представлено как проектная управленческая схема. Исследование носит теоретико-методологический характер; эмпирическая проверка модели не проводилась.
venue: Central Asian Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Management Studies

title: Patient journey mapping-guided intervention improves metabolic markers and self-management in young and middle-aged adults with hyperuricemia: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Hyperuricemia (HUA) is increasingly prevalent among young and middle-aged adults, who often demonstrate poor illness perception and low treatment adherence. Patient Journey Mapping (PJM) offers a patient-centered approach to identify unmet needs, but its application in HUA management remains unexplored. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a PJM-based multiphase health behavior intervention for this population. Methods This single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial recruited 150 young and middle-aged HUA patients randomly assigned to intervention (n=75) or control (n=75). The intervention group received a PJM-based multiphase intervention across three stages: symptom awareness, diagnosis and early treatment, and long-term self-management. The primary outcome was the serum uric acid (SUA) level at 6 months; secondary outcomes included SUA target achievement, BMI, illness perception (BIPQ), and self-management (AHSMSRS), assessed at baseline and 1, 3, and 6 months. Results Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significantly lower SUA levels and higher SUA target achievement rates at 1, 3, and 6 months, significantly lower BIPQ scores at 1, 3, and 6 months, and significantly higher AHSMSRS scores at 3 and 6 months. A supportive observed complete-case analysis also showed lower BMI at 6 months. At 6 months, the intervention gr…

title: The Introduction, Survival and Development of Public REITs in China
abstract: Public real estate investment trusts provide a capital-market mechanism for converting income-producing assets into liquid and tradable investment vehicles. China launched its pilot programme for publicly offered infrastructure REITs in 2020, and the first nine products began trading on the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges on 21 June 2021, raising approximately RMB 31.4 billion. Over the subsequent five years the market evolved from a narrowly focused pilot into a multi-asset platform covering infrastructure, affordable rental housing, consumption facilities and commercial real estate. By mid-June 2026 the number of listed public REITs had reached 86, with cumulative capital raised of RMB 245 billion. Expansion offerings became operational, creating a dual mechanism of primary issuance and follow-on fundraising. This paper examines the policy origins, market expansion trajectory, operating performance and principal constraints facing Chinese public REITs. Drawing on exchange statistics, regulatory notices and secondary-market data, the analysis shows that the sector has achieved substantial scale and institutional completeness. Nevertheless, limited secondary-market liquidity, valuation dispersion across asset classes and an institutionally concentrated investor base continue to constrain market depth. Sustained development will depend on further improvements in market mic…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Factors Driving and Inhibiting Consumer Purchase Intention on Livestream E-commerce Platforms in the Influencer Economy: A Case Study of East Buy
abstract: Livestream e-commerce now comprises a large share of China's online shopping, but the purchase intention it generates depends on a delicate balance between what supports buying and what dissuades it. How these forces operate together inside a single company, and not as separate variables in one survey model, is yet to be fully understood, and that is important for the long-term success of the business model. Drawing on East Buy as an example, this paper analyses how streamer expertise, real-time interaction and perceived value can help drive purchase intention, and how over-reliance on key livestreamers, negative online information and product uncertainty can undermine it. Professional knowledge, social presence, trust and multiple dimensions of consumption value are associated with a higher willingness to buy. On the other hand, heavy reliance on individual hosts and negative online comments weakens consumer confidence and increases the firm's operational and reputational risk. This paper suggests four managerial responses: cultivating brand-level customer relationships, tightening public-opinion monitoring and response, ensuring product quality control and information disclosure, and aligning knowledge-based content, interaction and value delivery more closely. The results provide practical advice for livestream retailers who are looking to keep customer trust while managing …

title: Costs and benefits of digital twin adoption in UK construction: a statistically tested stakeholder perception study
abstract: Purpose There is limited quantitative data on the weighting of costs and benefits of digital twin (DT) for stakeholders in the UK and this paper re-tests sub-group differences from a 2022 survey. Design/methodology/approach The 74 members of DTHub rated 15 benefits and 10 costs (scale of 0–4) and ranked both by Relative Importance Index (RII) (full sample) as well as two experience-based sub-samples (Group A n = 17; Group B n = 57). Corrected Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis H tests were used to explore differences and Spearman correlations were used for rank agreement. Findings Operational benefits (Lean Construction, Effective Data Sharing, Improved Decision Making, Construction 4.0) topped net-zero and United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) benefits. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Components, Skilled Personnel and IoT Devices/Systems were the top-rated costs. There were no significant differences between sub-groups after correction (groups shared similar priorities of benefits, but not costs). Research limitations/implications Due to the small, self-selected sample (n = 74; Group A n = 17), this limits the power of the study and null results are not confirmatory. Larger replication (mixed methods) across contexts is recommended. Practical implications Operational benefits should be the main consideration for a new DT framework. For the dominant costs, coordina…

title: The Impact of Work–Life Balance and Organizational Support on Job Satisfaction: The Mediating Role of Psychological Well-Being
abstract: The present study attempts to examine the relationship between job satisfaction (JS) of bankers in Bangladesh and work-life balance (WLB) and organizational support (OS), with the mediating role of psychological well-being (PWB). Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model, Work-Life Balance Theory, and Social Exchange Theory, the study provides a holistic understanding of how personal and organizational factors shape satisfaction differences in high-demand service environments. A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted using convenience sampling, with data collected from 201 bankers across 19 commercial banks in Bangladesh via a structured questionnaire. The data were analysed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling (SEM). Results show that WLB and OS have significant positive effects on PWB, which in turn has a positive effect on JS. The mediation analysis indicated that PWB partially mediated the relationship between WLB and JS, and also partially mediated the relationship between OS and JS. The findings emphasize the importance of psychological health in translating a positive work environment and work-life balance into job satisfaction. Theoretically, the study contributes to the research on WLB and OS by adding insights from the context of a developing country. Practically, it offers implications for HR managers aiming to imple…
venue: Journal of Management, and Development Research

title: The Influence of Business Owner Leadership on Employee Productivity Through Financial Literacy in MSMES In Medan City
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of business owner leadership on employee productivity, either directly or through financial literacy as a mediating variable, in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Medan City. The study used an associative quantitative approach with a survey method of 175 MSME employees in various sectors (culinary, fashion, handicrafts, and retail trade) who were selected using purposive sampling techniques. Data were collected through a 5-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using the Structural Equation Modeling approach based on Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS) with the help of SmartPLS 4. The results of the study showed that the leadership of business owners had a positive and significant effect on financial literacy (β = 0.412, p < 0.001), financial literacy had a positive and significant effect on employee productivity (β = 0.358, p < 0.001), and business owner leadership had a positive and significant effect on employee productivity directly (β = 0.276, p < 0.01). The results of the mediation test showed that financial literacy partially mediated the influence of business owner leadership on employee productivity (indirect effect = 0.148, p < 0.01; VAF = 34.9%). This finding confirms that increasing the leadership capabilities of business owners needs to be accompanied by strengthening employee financial literacy so that the p…

title: What Drives Bank Financial Performance? The Role of Liquidity, Leverage, and Asset Efficiency in Indonesian Banking
abstract: This study examines the relationships of liquidity, leverage, and asset efficiency with financial performance in five Indonesian listed banks BNI, Mandiri, BRI, BTN, and BCA over 2018-2022 (25 bank-year observations). Using the original multiple linear regression results, liquidity (CR) and asset efficiency (TATO) show positive associations with return on investment (ROI), while leverage (DER) shows a negative association. The joint model is statistically significant in the reported SPSS output. The study contributes a focused comparison between four state-owned banks and one major private bank across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and recovery periods, bringing together three balance-sheet and activity dimensions in a single empirical framework. For bank managers, the findings underscore the need to balance short-term liquidity, funding structure, and revenue-generating use of assets rather than optimize any ratio in isolation. Because the sample is limited and the design is observational, the results describe sample-specific associations rather than causal effects or the banking industry as a whole

title: Econometric modeling of financial risks and credit space of small and medium-size mining businesses
abstract: In current conditions of high volatility of the global commodity markets, increasing uncertainty and stricter requirements for financial stability of companies, the task of assessing the financial risks and credit space of small and mediumsize companies operating in the mining industry is becoming particularly relevant. The article is dedicated to an empirical study of the financial risk factors and credit space of small and medium-size mining businesses. The study formed a dedicated industry sampling of 9,901 companies and applied a comprehensive econometric approach that takes into account statistical financial indicators and dynamic changes in revenues, assets and profits. The purpose of the study is to identify the most significant balance sheet, operational and dynamic factors that determine the level of financial risks and the probability of the company’s shifting into the high-risk category. The results show that negative equity remains the dominant risk factor for the small and medium-size mining businesses: in the basic financial risk index model their coefficient is 38.816 points, and in the high-risk logit model, the odds ratio is 15.561. The dynamic variables have a more accurate interpretation, i.e. in the working capital model the revenue growth is associated with an increase in the financial risk index, whereas the profit growth statistically reduces the risks. title: A study on the sources of HIV-1 transmission in Haikou, China: insights from molecular genetics and field epidemiological investigations
abstract: Objective This study aimed to integrate molecular network analysis, Bayesian phylogenetic modeling, and field epidemiological investigation to systematically trace the sources of HIV-1 transmission in Haikou, China. Design A longitudinal molecular surveillance program was implemented between 2021 and 2024, combined with a cross-sectional field epidemiological investigation. Methods Subtype-specific local sequence databases were constructed from nationwide sequences. Molecular clusters containing both local and external sequences were subjected to phylogeographic analysis under a Bayesian relaxed molecular clock and a Skygrid model to infer transmission origins. Complementing the molecular analyses, field epidemiological investigations were carried out among a subset of participants to assess self-reported transmission sources. Results Among the 1,125 pol sequences, CRF01_AE (35.64%), CRF07_BC (38.58%), CRF65_cpx (7.20%), and CRF55_01B (4.53%) were the four most prevalent subtypes, with local clustering rates of 36.65%, 33.64%, 86.42%, and 54.90%, respectively. Phylogeographic analysis identified Guangdong as the primary origin of HIV-1 introductions into Haikou for all four subtypes, followed by Beijing (CRF01_AE_C1 and CRF65_cpx) and Shanghai (CRF07_BC). CRF01_AE showed bidirectional transmission between Haikou and Sanya, and between Haikou and Dongfang; CRF07_BC and CRF65_cpx…

title: The Impact of Digital Financial Inclusion on Household Consumption Upgrading: Empirical Evidence from Provincial Panel Data in China
abstract: Whether digital financial inclusion can push household consumption toward higher-quality categories, and through what channels, remains an open empirical question in the context of domestic demand expansion. This study combines the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index with provincial macroeconomic statistics to build a balanced panel covering 31 Chinese provinces over 2013-2022, and estimates two-way fixed effects models that identify the aggregate impact, its regional variation, and the underlying transmission channels. Three findings emerge. First, digital financial inclusion exerts a significant positive influence on consumption upgrading: raising the aggregate index by 1% is associated with an increase of roughly 0.23 percentage points in the share of development- and enjoyment-oriented spending, a result that survives alternative dependent-variable definitions and a one-period lag of the core regressor. Second, the effect is geographically uneven — clearly present in eastern provinces but not yet detectable in central and western ones — which indicates that turning financial supply into actual consumption behavior requires complementary conditions in income, logistics, and consumption scenarios. Third, channel tests lend preliminary support to the digital credit route but not to the payment convenience route, and coverage breadth proves to be the dominant su…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The Effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on The Financial Sustainability Of MSMES in Medan City
abstract: This study examines the effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on the Financial Sustainability of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Medan City. An associative quantitative design was applied to a survey of 120 MSME owners and managers in the culinary, fashion, retail trade, and service sectors, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected with a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met all validity and reliability criteria. Fintech Adoption had a positive and significant effect on Financial Sustainability (β = 0.412; t = 4.873; p < 0.001), and Digital Accounting also had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.358; t = 4.126; p < 0.001). Together, the two variables explained 43.4% of the variance in Financial Sustainability, with medium effect sizes (f² = 0.236 and 0.178, respectively). The findings suggest that digital financial services and digital bookkeeping reinforce MSME financial sustainability, so support programs in Medan should promote both together rather than treating them as separate agendas

title: Perceived Risk and Finfluencers as Determinants of Stock Investment Intention among Generation Z Employees at Universitas Negeri Padang: The Moderating Role of Financial Literacy
abstract: This study examines the relationships between perceived risk, finfluencers, and stock investment intention among Generation Z employees at Universitas Negeri Padang, with financial literacy serving as a moderating variable. A quantitative approach with a causal research design was employed. The study involved 104 respondents selected through purposive sampling, comprising Generation Z employees who met the research criteria. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with IBM SPSS Statistics. The results show that perceived risk is negatively associated with stock investment intention, whereas finfluencers are positively associated with stock investment intention. However, financial literacy does not significantly moderate either relationship. These findings indicate that although perceived risk and finfluencers are relevant to understanding stock investment intention, financial literacy does not significantly alter the strength of these relationships in the studied context. This study contributes empirical evidence to the investment literature by examining these relationships among Generation Z employees in a public university setting, including lecturers and educational staff. The findings highlight the importance of rational risk assessment and critical evaluation of financial information f…

title: Gender and respect in leadership: voices from ExCo women in the financial sector
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to explore the role gender plays in the respect accorded to women leaders in the financial sector. Furthermore, the article seeks to identify ways in which disrespect is related to systemic legitimacy deficits experienced by women leaders in the sector. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a qualitative research design. Fieldwork gathered data through twenty in-depth semi-structured interviews with senior women leaders in a range of financial sector organisations. Fifteen interviews were conducted with UK leaders with remaining interviews conducted with leaders in the United States, Belgium, Brazil and The Channel Islands. Findings In a sector historically constructed as masculine terrain, findings show that women leaders in finance experience gender based (dis)respect, both overt and systemic, in ways that are related to conditional and contingent legitimacy. Women in senior leader positions are often positioned as “space invaders” to the sector. Strategic interrogation of respect and legitimacy cultures can be initiated through a systems approach. Originality/value This study frames the under-researched issue of gendered respect in leadership as a consequential construct, substantively linked to leadership legitimacy. It suggests that the notion of respect can be leveraged and embedded in the systems, structures and shared values …

title: The Potential Risk Factors of Hantavirus Transmission to Humans from Infected Rodents in Malaysia
abstract: Zoonotic hantavirus is a negative single-stranded RNA virus from the family Bunyaviridae which is known to cause two significant rodentborne diseases in humans namely hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), affecting about 30 000 people worldwide each year. HFRS is a disease found endemically in Asia and Europe with case fatality rates varying from <1% to 12%, while HPS which has a higher mortality rate of approximately 40% occurs within the American continent. Many countries in Southeast Asia unaware the public health implication of Hantavirus infection despite favorable ecological conditions include rich rodent species diversity, urbanisation and high human-wildlife interface that serve as ecological condition that could support the virus persistence and transmission. Since humans serve as spillover hosts who are infected largely by inhalation of infected rodents’ excreta, it is crucial to fill in the research gap by identifying the risk factors for human hantavirus infection. This paper provides a review of the potential risk factors associated with hantavirus transmission to humans from infected rodents in Malaysia focusing on behavioral, occupational, urban, and environmental. Other pieces of knowledge such as hantavirus virological properties, the geographical distribution with its respective role as a reservoir, clinical feat…
venue: Pertanika Journal of Veterinary Medicine and Science

title: From Innovation to Affordability: A Conceptual Framework Linking Insurtech Capability to Patient Financial Outcomes
abstract: Healthcare affordability remains a significant concern because insured patients may still face substantial out-of-pocket (OOP) expenses arising from deductibles, copayments, uncovered services, and complex billing. This conceptual study develops a framework explaining how Insurtech Capability may contribute to Patient Financial Outcomes through Patient Financial Navigation and Benefit Optimization. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Information Systems Success Model, Service-Dominant Logic, and the financial toxicity perspective, the framework defines Insurtech Capability through five dimensions: data integration and interoperability, analytics and decision support, process automation, digital financial engagement, and privacy, security, and governance. Interoperability and Organizational Integration are treated as enabling conditions, while Health-Insurance Literacy is a patient-level boundary condition. Six propositions describe the proposed direct, mediated, and moderating relationships. The framework distinguishes actual OOP expense reduction from cost predictability, reduced administrative burden, and reduced financial distress. It also recognizes that plan design, provider prices, network restrictions, and clinical requirements may constrain savings. The contribution is an integrated, patient-centered explanation of how digital insurance resources might translate…
