title: Counseling on Household-Scale Pharmaceutical Waste Disposal at Talise Public Health Center
abstract: Improper disposal of pharmaceutical waste can harm the environment and public health. Public knowledge regarding appropriate household-level drug disposal remains limited. This community engagement aimed to improve the knowledge, attitudes, and behavior of residents regarding the handling of expired and damaged medicines. The activity was conducted at Bumi Roviga Sub-Public Health Center, a unit under Talise Public Health Center, Palu City. A total of 24 respondents, selected randomly among parents attending child health checks or antenatal care, participated in the program. The counseling was delivered face-to-face and supplemented with printed educational flyers. A pre-test was administered at the location, while the post-test was distributed via WhatsApp using Google Forms one week later. Shapiro-Wilk normality tests indicated non-normal data distribution. Paired t-tests showed significant improvements (p<0.05) in knowledge (p=0.000), attitude (p=0.000), and behavior (p=0.000) scores, indicating the effectiveness of the intervention. This activity demonstrates that brief counseling supported by print media can effectively enhance public understanding of safe drug disposal at the household level. As a recommendation, household-level pharmaceutical waste education should be integrated into routine health promotion activities at community health centers, with periodic follow-up…

abstract: This study examines the development of Uzbekistan’s public service delivery system using secondary administrative data for 2017–2024. Descriptive statistical, comparative, and dynamic analyses were applied. From 2018 to 2024, the number of services offered through Public Service Centers (PSCs) increased from 63 to 403, while services available via the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (UPIPS) rose from 83 to 717. By 22 October 2024, automated services had increased from 10 to 186 and BPM-based services from 24 to 494. The findings show broader service coverage and greater automation; the article compares these trends by delivery channel and automation type

title: Universal design for learning in general chemistry: a pre-post study of inclusive teaching competence in pre-service teacher education
abstract: Abstract Inclusive STEM education places distinct demands on prospective chemistry teachers, owing to the discipline’s high cognitive load, the need to organize practice-oriented activities safely, and the requirement to ensure fair assessment in the context of diverse learners’ educational needs. The present study examined changes in inclusive chemistry teaching competence during a semester-long intervention grounded in Universal Design for Learning (UDL). A single-group pretest-posttest intervention design was implemented in the General Chemistry course (6 credits; 180 academic hours) at Zhanibekov University. The sample comprised 106 first-year university students. Over a 15-week semester, the UDL approach was embedded into the course through a sequence of design-based assignments targeting multiple means of engagement, representation, and action and expression. The course instructor served as the intervention implementer (teacher effect). Data collection included pre- and post-measures using self-report scales (knowledge, self-efficacy, attitudes, and intention to implement UDL), a case-based knowledge test, and the evaluation of student-generated pedagogical artifacts at two time points (T1 and T2) using a study-specific eight-criterion UDL design rubric (0–3 per criterion; total score 0–24). Data were analyzed using paired pre-post comparisons, effect size estimation, and…

title: Esco2 restrains pathological endothelial-mesenchymal transition through hidden isoform regulation in a Roberts syndrome model
abstract: Roberts syndrome is caused by biallelic ESCO2 pathogenic variants, but the mechanisms linking ESCO2 loss to embryonic endothelial failure remain poorly defined. Endothelial cells must maintain identity and resist endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), yet conventional transcriptomics measures gene abundance rather than isoform composition. Here, using endothelial-specific Esco2 deletion in a mouse model relevant to Roberts syndrome, we show that Esco2 loss causes yolk sac vascular remodeling failure, pathological EndMT, diversion from hemogenic endothelial fate, hemogenic endothelial depletion, impaired hematopoietic output, and embryonic lethality. Short-read single-cell RNA-seq revealed broad endothelial reprogramming, whereas single-cell long-read isoform sequencing uncovered a hidden layer of isoform dysregulation that conventional gene-level analysis failed to resolve. Esco2-deficient endothelium exhibited transcriptome-wide isoform switching, disruption of a multi-tier splicing-factor network, and predicted broad loss or rewiring of protein-coding output. Chromatin occupancy profiling localized Esco2 to exonic regions near alternatively spliced loci, supporting a cotranscriptional route to spliceopathy. Whole-genome sequencing showed that local DNA variation was insufficient to explain these changes, supporting a predominantly posttranscriptional mechanism. These fin…

Enhanced output voltage regulation in a seven-level inverter with minimal active power switches for renewable energy applications
abstract: Smart inverters are a prevalent solution in renewable energy applications due to their capacity to provide output voltage with minimal harmonic distortion and ease of control and operation. This trend has driven the rapid growth of power converters in various renewable energy applications. This research aims to design a strategy and implementation technique for a single-phase seven-level (SPSL) inverter that can control output voltage accurately. This research is innovative because it constructs an SPSL inverter with six active power switches and a new control strategy. This inverter comprises two active power switches that operate as a three-level direct current (DC) voltage shaper and four active power switches for polarity inversion. This inverter is controlled using advanced sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) methods. The inverter SPSL was selected because it can produce smoother sine waves with a total harmonic distortion (THD) less than the IEEE standard. The SPSL inverter's power circuit is controlled by a microcontroller-based control system, which enables the inverter to dynamically adapt to changes in load and operating conditions. This study performed simulations and verified the design performance via hardware implementation. The results from the simulations and lab tests indicate that the inverter works well with a THD of 4.16%; the SPSL inverter created in t…

title: Digital leapfrogging or digital divide? Internet penetration and structural transformation in Africa
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether digitalization accelerates structural transformation in African economies or reinforces existing structural inequalities. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data on African countries and a rigorous fixed-effects framework, complemented by dynamic System GMM estimation, the analysis provides a direct test of the digital structural transformation hypothesis. Findings The results show a strong and robust positive effect of internet penetration on structural transformation, even after controlling for key macroeconomic and demographic factors. Sectoral evidence reveals a clear mechanism: increased internet access reduces the share of agriculture while significantly expanding the services sector, confirming that digitalization actively reallocates economic activity across sectors. Crucially, interaction results show that the impact of internet penetration is stronger in slower-growing, less advanced economies, providing compelling evidence in favor of the digital leapfrogging hypothesis rather than the digital divide. Originality/value These findings establish digital infrastructure as a central driver of modern structural change and suggest that expanding internet access can serve as a powerful policy tool for accelerating inclusive development in Africa.

title: Regulations, infrastructure and financial efficiency: evidence from 101 economies
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether regulatory quality or information infrastructure better predicts financial system efficiency and investigate the pathway through which regulation translates into operational outcomes across 101 economies. Design/methodology/approach The World Bank B-READY 2025 data set is used to separately measure regulatory framework quality and public-service infrastructure as predictors of operational efficiency. OLS with HC3-robust standard errors is estimated across eight institutional variables and four income groups, with formal mediation analysis and robustness checks including region fixed effects and principal component digital infrastructure. Findings Payment interoperability rules and credit registry accessibility are the institutional variables most robustly associated with efficiency. Information infrastructure transmits approximately 29% of the total regulatory effect, consistent with partial mediation. A steep income gradient persists after controlling for all institutional variables. Decomposing efficiency reveals distinct channels: credit registry accessibility is associated with credit efficiency; payment interoperability rules are associated with payment efficiency. title: Decoupling growth from degradation: a fractional frequency Fourier analysis of India's aviation sector and the environmental Kuznets Curve
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India's aviation sector from 1970 to 2021. Using the ecological footprint as an indicator and a novel fractional frequency Fourier approach, it tests the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. The results reveal a U-shaped relationship, contradicting the EKC, and highlight the negative environmental impact of increased air freight. However, financial development supports sustainability by enabling cleaner technologies. The study aims to inform policy by proposing strategies such as carbon pricing, renewable fuel adoption, and green logistics to decouple aviation growth from environmental harm. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a fractional frequency Fourier approach to examine the long-run relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India from 1970 to 2021. The ecological footprint is used as a comprehensive measure of environmental impact. This advanced econometric method captures structural breaks and nonlinearities more effectively than traditional models. Factors associated with severe COVID-19 among children aged <12 years in Fuzhou, China: a frequency-matched case-control study
abstract: Background Evidence on social, preventive, and clinical factors associated with severe pediatric COVID-19 remains limited in regional Chinese surveillance settings. We evaluated these factors among children aged <12 years in Fuzhou. Methods We conducted a frequency-matched case-control study of 347 severe cases and 694 non-severe controls identified from sentinel hospitals and the China Disease Prevention and Control Information System between January 2020 and August 2025. Controls were sampled at a 1:2 ratio by broad onset period, geographic sampling stratum, and parental education level. Group differences were assessed using Pearson&apos;s chi-square test. Given frequency matching without individual matched sets, unconditional multivariable logistic regression was used. Concurrent clinical manifestations were interpreted as warning indicators rather than antecedent etiologic risk factors. Results The selected sample comprised 1,041 children (347 severe cases and 694 non-severe controls). Severe disease was positively associated with male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.897, 95% CI 1.451-2.481), age <=5 years (aOR 1.578, 95% CI 1.209-2.061), home-based/preschool care (aOR 2.771, 95% CI 2.033-3.776), rural residence (aOR 2.470, 95% CI 1.858-3.283), delayed consultation of &gt;2 days (aOR 1.902, 95% CI 1.388-2.605), obesity (aOR 2.028, 95% CI 1.398-2.941), chronic…

title: Process optimization of spray-dried buffalo milk Bubalus bubalis bubalis (Linnaeus, 1758) using response surface methodology
abstract: Buffalo milk has higher fat and solids-not-fat contents, consisting mainly of proteins, carbohydrates, and minerals, making it more nutritious than cow’s milk. However, its composition also makes the product more perishable. Thus, preservation techniques like spray drying must be employed to extend its shelf life and facilitate efficient transportation and distribution. Spray-drying conditions for cow's milk have already been established. However, because of differences in physicochemical properties and composition, these conditions may not be applicable to buffalo milk. Therefore, optimizing the processing conditions for buffalo milk is necessary. This study aimed to optimize the spray-drying conditions for buffalo milk to produce an acceptable milk powder. Response surface methodology was used to evaluate the effects of three key variables: maltodextrin (10-20%w/w), feed pressure (8-12Hz), and inlet temperature (190-210°C). The goal was to determine their effects on the response variables, including moisture content, water activity, hygroscopic moisture, and insolubility index. The optimal spray-drying conditions were obtained at a maltodextrin concentration of 20% (w/w), a feed pressure of 12 Hz, and an inlet temperature of 210°C. The Calculus of Quick Commerce: Demand, Pricing, Elasticity and Profit Optimization in India
abstract: The fast-paced evolution of digital retail requires the enhanced application of quantitative analysis of decisions related to pricing, demand forecasting, inventory control and fulfillment. In this paper, there is a mathematical treatment of the modern business model of quick commerce and how the tools of calculus and business mathematics can be employed in order to analyze the decisions related to it. For this purpose, a linear inverse demand function is constructed that sets the connection between price and quantity. Using this connection, a quadratic function of revenue is developed and then marginal revenue is found out via differentiation. Further, a nonlinear cost function that reflects the fixed operating cost, variable costs and increasing marginal cost is constructed. Using the profit function, its first derivative is found in order to find out the stationary level of output and the second derivative helps in defining the characteristics of this point. Moreover, price elasticity is computed in order to measure the degree of sensitivity of demand to the price change. The numerical values are fictional and are used for the purpose of demonstrating the process of mathematical analysis. abstract: Background Drug resistance remains a key barrier to durable remission in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). A central but poorly resolved question is whether AML cells resistant to mechanistically distinct drugs converge on shared downstream survival dependencies, and whether those dependencies can be exploited therapeutically. Methods We compared transcriptional reprogramming across 3 independent resistance models derived from the FLT3-ITD-positive MV4-11 cell line: midostaurin-resistant cells, sorafenib-resistant cells, and a novel venetoclax-resistant line generated in our laboratory. Differential expression analysis, protein -protein interaction network analysis, hub-gene prioritization across multiple network centrality algorithms, and pathway enrichment analyses were performed on shared upregulated genes. Ketone monoester supplementation during a live high – train low training camp does not yield an additional adaptive response
abstract: Recent evidence indicates that oral ketone monoester (KE) intake acutely increases blood [EPO] following exercise in normoxia and improves endurance performance following an exercise training program. Therefore, we investigated whether post-exercise and pre-sleep KE supplementation may improve performance and hematological adaptations to an altitude training program. Eighteen recreational cyclists (9 male, 9 female) performed a five-week, live-high, train-low (LHTL) program, involving progressive normobaric hypoxia (2000-3000m) and 4–7 training sessions per week, followed by a one-week tapering period under normoxic conditions. Throughout the six-week period, subjects received either 25g KE (n=9) or an isocaloric placebo (CON; n=9) both post-exercise and pre-sleep for a total daily dose of 50g. Experimental measurements were performed before (PRE) and after (POST) LHTL, and after the subsequent taper (POST + 7), and included a 30-minute time trial (TT30), maximal oxygen uptake rate (VO 2 max) test, determination of gross mechanical efficiency, repeated sprint performance, measurements of hemoglobin mass, blood draws and muscle biopsies. A weight loss fibrotic response in visceral fat is driven by defective lysosome-dependent collagenolysis
abstract: Obesity induces pathological remodeling of white adipose tissue (WAT), including chronic inflammation and fibrosis, which drive metabolic dysfunction. Although weight loss (WL) is the cornerstone of obesity treatment and improves systemic metabolic health, its effect on WAT remodeling remains incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of diet-induced obesity followed by nutritional WL, we show that visceral WAT (vWAT) failed to fully recover despite normalization of body weight and marked metabolic improvement. Notably, vWAT fibrosis persisted and continued to progress after WL. This occurred while extracellular matrix (ECM) production by adipose progenitor cells was markedly reduced following WL, explaining why pharmacological inhibition of ECM synthesis fails to prevent fibrosis during WL. Instead, we observed impaired collagen degradation by both progenitor cells and macrophages, along with lysosomal dysfunction, during WL. This suggests that defective ECM degradation, rather than continued ECM production, underlies fibrosis persistence and aggravation during WL. Together, these findings identify impaired collagenolysis as a critical barrier to adipose tissue recovery after WL and suggest that enhancing ECM clearance, rather than inhibiting ECM synthesis, may represent a more effective therapeutic strategy to restore adipose tissue function.

title: Aerobic exercise for depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms and perceived stress in university students: a systematic review and dose–response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Abstract Objective To assess the effects of aerobic exercise on depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms and perceived stress in university students and to identify potential exercise prescription and dose–response patterns. Methods PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, PsycINFO and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception to August 15, 2026. Eligible studies were English language, peer reviewed RCTs in university students (≥ 18 years) comparing aerobic exercise with a control condition. Random effects meta-analyses used standardized mean differences (SMDs) based on change scores. Subgroup analyses examined baseline depression, intensity, session duration and intervention length. Dose–response associations (METs·min/week) were modelled using restricted cubic splines. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, and publication bias was explored using funnel plots and Egger test. The review was retrospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261473381). Results Fourteen RCTs ( n = 982) were included. Aerobic exercise reduced depressive symptoms (13 RCTs; n = 717; SMD = − 0.88, 95% CI − 1.35 to − 0.41), anxiety symptoms (10 RCTs; n = 579; SMD = − 0.59, 95% CI − 0.92 to − 0.26) and perceived stress (7 RCTs; n = 353; SMD = − 0.68, 95% CI − 1.20 to − 0.16). Assessing demand-side policy impacts on US urban passenger transport
abstract: Abstract Demand-side policies could significantly mitigate energy use and carbon emissions of urban passenger transport. However, previous integrated assessment modeling studies often failed to fully evaluate their mitigation potential in the absence of explicit representation of urban transport dynamics. Here we adjust the global integrated assessment model GCAM to disaggregate passenger transport in the US region into the urban and inter-city subsectors. We analyze the impacts of transformative demand-side policies on US urban passenger transport service demand, mode share, energy use, and carbon emissions. We consider six demand-side policies (compact urban development , speed limit, shared mobility, remote working, fuel tax, and congestion fee) as well as a technology policy of vehicle electrification. We find that all demand-side policies could collectively reduce urban transport energy use and carbon emissions by approximately 60% from the baseline in 2050 by shifting and reducing transport demand. We also find that demand-side policies could deliver strong synergies with electric vehicle (EV) deployment. Under ambitious EV deployment, although most direct urban passenger transport emissions are mitigated, electricity demand would increase by 718 TWh from 2021 to 2050, as much as 16% of current US total electricity consumption. title: Beyond the basics: how digital transformation, orientation and competence fuel SME performance through resilience in the manufacturing sector
abstract: Purpose In emerging economies such as Pakistan, SMEs have a high failure rate, underscoring the need to understand what drives SME performance. This paper fills a knowledge gap by considering the impact of digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and entrepreneurial resilience on SMEs' performance. Entrepreneurial resilience serves as a mediator between digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, environmental dynamism (ED) is used as a moderator between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 453 managers of manufacturing SMEs in Punjab, Pakistan. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling is used for hypothesis testing. Findings Digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation and entrepreneurial competencies have a significant and positive influence on entrepreneurial resilience and SME performance. Entrepreneurial resilience significantly enhances SMEs' performance. Additionally, entrepreneurial resilience significantly mediates the relationships among digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. title: GenAI dependence and team innovation in construction projects: moderated mediation analysis of knowledge integration, team reflexivity and learning goal orientation
abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly embedded in construction project work, yet its implications for project team innovation remain insufficiently understood. Moving beyond a simple adoption or use perspective, this study examines how perceived team-referent GenAI dependence is associated with team innovation in construction projects. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on information processing theory, this study develops a moderated mediation model linking GenAI dependence, knowledge integration, team reflexivity, learning goal orientation and team innovation. Based on survey data from 257 construction project professionals in China, the model was tested using structural equation modeling, supplemented by hierarchical regression and bootstrapped analysis. Findings Based on survey data from the Chinese construction industry, the results show that GenAI dependence is positively associated with knowledge integration and negatively associated with team reflexivity. These two team processes account for opposing indirect associations between GenAI dependence and team innovation. Team learning goal orientation further attenuates the negative association involving team reflexivity, along with the corresponding negative indirect association with team innovation. abstract: This column discusses how text sets focused on systems and power can provoke questions about change, resistance, resilience, and adaptation.

title: A decade review of Indonesia’s PPP project: stakeholder insights on strategic needs and policy adjustments
abstract: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perspectives on institutional governance challenges affecting the implementation of Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) in Indonesia under Presidential Regulation Number 38 of 2015. It further identifies stakeholder-informed policy reform needs to strengthen the national PPP framework. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using semi-structured interviews with nine high-level purposively selected participants representing government institutions, private sector entities, and financial institutions involved in PPP implementation. Data were analyzed through thematic synthesis involving open coding, category development, and interpretive theme construction. Findings The findings identify four institutional governance dimensions influencing PPP implementation: regulatory adaptability and institutional continuity, project preparation quality, financial structuring and risk allocation, and lifecycle governance. Across stakeholder groups, participants consistently highlighted policy inconsistency, limited feasibility study credibility, rigid contractual arrangements, disproportionate risk allocation, and insufficient operational oversight as priority governance concerns. These findings represent expert-based perspectives rather than a comprehensive assessment of Indonesia's PPP system. Research limitations/implica…

Optimization of a Laccase Biosynthesis and Mediator System: A Potential Headway for Sustainable Microplastic Degradation
abstract: Abstract The global accumulation of microplastics has become a critical environmental challenge due to their persistence, widespread distribution, and adverse effects on ecosystems and human health. Although enzymatic degradation has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional physicochemical remediation methods, the practical application of laccase (Lac) remains constrained by low enzyme productivity, limited stability, high production costs, and insufficient activity towards recalcitrant non-phenolic polymers such as polyethylene and polystyrene. Furthermore, current studies are often fragmented, focusing on either enzyme production or degradation performance, while lacking an integrated assessment of catalytic optimization, mediator systems, scalability, and environmental sustainability. This review provides a critical and comprehensive evaluation of recent advances in optimizing Lac biosynthesis and laccase-mediator systems (LMS) for microplastic degradation. Unlike previous reviews, it integrates developments in strain engineering, heterologous expression, protein engineering, omics-guided process optimization, enzyme immobilization, mediator selection, and techno-economic considerations within a single framework. Particular attention is given to how LMS expands the oxidative capacity of Lac towards resistant plastic polymers and to the evidence required to distin…

title: Primary care staff and health policymakers’ perspectives on the Israeli special team management program for complex patients and its further enhancement: a qualitative study
abstract: Abstract Background/aim The healthcare of complex patients is challenging, requiring holistic multidisciplinary teamwork. The targeted Team Management for Complex Patients Program (TMCP) was therefore initiated in Israel and implemented by Leumit Health Services. The aim of the current study was to examine the perceptions and insights of healthcare stakeholders regarding the program implementation and its further enhancement. Methods A descriptive qualitative study using semi-structured remote videoconference interviews was conducted. A purposive sampling of primary care practitioners, managers and policymakers, with operational experience in the TMCP, was employed. Interviewees were categorized into three levels: field staff and service providers, mid-level management staff and high-level policymakers. Results Five main themes were examined amongst the 22 interviewees: detection of complex patients for inclusion in the TMCP; quality and access to healthcare; team function, governance and accountability; and provider experience. These themes were extracted from the three levels of interviewees, all of whom endorsed a broad definition of complexity that integrates clinical, functional, mental and social dimensions and emphasized the critical role of multidisciplinary teamwork in complex patient care. Optimal patient identification combines clinical assessment (“bottom-up”) with …

title: Conservation of heat in the Coupled Arctic Prediction System (CAPS v1.1): comprehensive model evaluation based on the MOSAiC observations
abstract: Atmosphere–sea ice–ocean interactions are vital for understanding past and future changes in the Arctic climate system. Consistent heat-flux exchange across model-component interfaces is essential for investigating these interactions with coupled models on longer timescales. Here, we present the improved version of the Coupled Arctic Prediction System (CAPS), in which heat-flux exchange between the atmosphere (WRF) and ocean–sea ice (ROMS–CICE) components is made consistent across coupling interfaces. A set of pan-Arctic simulations covering the period of Multidisciplinary drifting Observatory for the Study of Arctic Climate (MOSAiC) were conducted with the revised CAPS. The revised coupling substantially reduces interfacial heat-flux residuals and improves the simulation of Arctic sea-ice conditions relative to the original coupling, which produces enhanced winter ice growth and reduced summer ice retreat during the 14-month simulation. CAPS was further evaluated against comprehensive MOSAiC observations of the atmosphere, ocean, snow, and sea ice. The model reproduces the broad evolution of Arctic conditions along the MOSAiC drift, although biases remain, partly associated with errors in simulated synoptic systems and unresolved polar physical processes. The constrained-atmosphere experiment with spectral nudging shows improved agreement with observations in several quantitat…

Austrian pine site indices as a basis for adaptive forest management in southwestern Serbia
abstract: Introduction The site index is the most commonly used indirect indicator of forest site productivity, based on the height-age relationship. The objectives of this study were: (1) to develop a dynamic site index model and (2) to create a site index map for Austrian pine (Pinus nigra) in southwestern Serbia using the Generalized Algebraic Difference Approach (GADA). Materials and methods The modeling was based on data obtained from stem analysis of 56 dominant trees (990 age-height pairs) and was validated using an independent set of 2,835 age-height pairs. In the initial stage, eight nonlinear models were tested, while the subsequent analysis employed the GADA approach to four selected models. Parameter estimation was performed using the Generalized Nonlinear Least Squares (GNLS) method with corrections for autocorrelation (ARMA (2,1)) and heteroscedasticity. The final model selection was based on a combination of statistical and biological criteria. Results The results showed that the Chapman-Richards, Hossfeld IV and Weibull models achieved a high goodness of fit ( R 2 adj ≈ 0.98), while the Gompertz model proved to be less suitable. However, only the Hossfeld IV model within the GADA approach fully satisfied the biological and theoretical assumptions, providing realistic asymptotic values and a biologically logical pattern of height growth. The constructed curves exhibited pr…

title: Less effort, less meaning? Authorship ambiguity and impostor-like experiences in GenAI-mediated knowledge work
abstract: Purpose This study examines how knowledge workers make sense of GenAI-enabled co-production, with particular attention to authorship ambiguity and its implications for competence attribution, self-evaluation and meaningful work. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative approach based on in-depth interviews with 32 knowledge workers who work directly with GenAI tools, combining inductive coding with abductive interpretation. We used the Gioia methodology to analyze participants' reported experiences and interpretations of human–AI collaboration, with sensemaking informing the interpretation of emergent themes and aggregate dimensions. Findings The findings identify authorship ambiguity as a central interpretive challenge in GenAI-mediated knowledge work. When GenAI contributes to ideation, analysis, drafting, coding or other knowledge-intensive outputs, workers may find it difficult to distinguish their own contribution from that of the technology. Participants responded to this ambiguity differently. Some reconstructed their expertise around judgment, validation and contextualization and experienced GenAI as extending their professional capability. Others struggled to internalize successful outputs as evidence of their own competence and reported impostor-like experiences and reduced meaningfulness. The findings suggest that experiences of GenAI-enabled co-produ…

title: The Transnational Power of International Law in a Chaotic World
abstract: Abstract The international legal framework is today under unseen pressure. The principles of sovereignty and respect for international borders are openly rejected by leaders of the most powerful nations. United Nations bodies are being boycotted, and international judges and prosecutors are targeted with sanctions designed for terrorists and criminal organisations. Are we watching the agony of the international law and justice?

title: Legal Culture and Pandemic Management: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: Abstract This article compares the COVID-19 responses of four selected jurisdictions through the lens of legal culture. Legal culture is defined in this article as the interplay of legislation, the infrastructure and behaviour of legal institutions, and the behaviour and legal consciousness of the general population. The four jurisdictions are New Zealand, Taiwan, Germany and mainland China; they bear cross-cutting similarities and differences in terms of legal system, political system and cultural tradition. This article examines how legal culture was revealed in COVID responses and how it in turn shaped COVID responses. It illustrates the legal culture of the four jurisdictions as revealed through their respective pandemic responses. It argues that the three dimensions of legal culture interacted with each other to produce distinct pandemic responses; in other words, pandemic management is to some extent the product of legal culture.

title: Experts' and AI perspectives on the environmental sustainability of tensile membrane structures
abstract: Purpose With increasing demands for sustainable construction, there is growing interest in enhancing the environmental performance of tensile membrane structures (TMS). This study aims to investigate the environmental sustainability challenges and opportunities of TMS across their lifecycle stages by integrating expert insights and advanced AI-generated perspectives. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative methodology was employed using semi-structured interviews with 16 experienced professionals including architects, engineers, contractors, builders, environmental sustainability experts and researchers. To enhance the reliability of findings and address potential gaps, the study also utilised artificial intelligence (AI) tools (ChatGPT and DeepSeek) to compare human expert insights with AI responses. Thematic analysis was conducted to categorise the results into core environmental sustainability themes. Findings Five interrelated themes were identified: (1) material innovation and environmental sustainability, (2) structural efficiency and lightweight design, (3) construction techniques and environmental sustainability alignment, (4) life durability management and (5) accessibility, inclusivity and waste management. These themes highlight critical performance indicators such as energy use, structural behaviour, material optimisation, user experience and maintenance strategie…

title: Integrating ecohydrological modelling and participatory processes to co-design multifunctional forest management
abstract: Mediterranean forests are becoming denser, drier, and more combustible because of natural and human-driven factors. Forest managers report that managing them is increasingly costly relative to its economic returns and requires informed decision-making supported by appropriate tools and dialogue. This study couples the Decision Support System (DSS) CAFE (Carbon, Aqua, Fire and Eco-resilience) with structured participatory processes across four Living Labs in Spain, Morocco, and Italy, representing distinct Mediterranean socioecological systems: semiarid Aleppo pine forests, traditional argan woodlands with goat grazing, and cork-oak silvopastoral systems. The aim was to evaluate whether management co-designed in this way is resilient to climate disturbance while improving ecosystem services (ES). In three rounds of co-design workshops, stakeholders identified priority ES, agreed on the management actions to enhance them, and evaluated alternatives generated by the DSS. Their priorities were remarkably consistent across sites, focusing on wildfire risk, water availability, and biomass extraction. Preferred interventions were ecologically sound and consistent with field evidence. To this end, CAFE was expanded to quantify locally relevant ES that had not previously been modelled, including argan fruit production, cork extraction, fodder availability, and bark regeneration. Model o…

title: C-suite incentive conflict and firm efficiency
abstract: Purpose This article provides empirical support to a long-debated theory in behavioral and organizational management literature regarding how the incentive conflict of firms' executives affects the firm's efficiency. Design/methodology/approach The study employs panel regression techniques, using efficiency measures derived from data envelopment analysis (DEA) and stochastic frontier analysis (SFA) as dependent variables, and a novel measure of C-suite incentive conflict as the independent variable, based on annual data from US companies covering the period 1992–2018. Findings Our results show that incentive conflict improves firm efficiency and thus support the constructive impact of C-suite conflict on firm efficiency. We find that the positive impact of incentive conflict on firm efficiency is weakened when the CEO is more powerful. Our findings provide support to agency theory by documenting that a more diverse board of directors reinforces the positive relationship between incentive conflict and firm efficiency. Research limitations/implications One limitation of this study is that the dataset is restricted to the period ending in 2018, which may limit the ability to capture more recent developments in corporate governance practices and executive incentive structures. Although the findings provide important insights for corporate executives and policymakers, extending the …

title: Do financial analysts improve the quality of earnings forecasting? Evidence from Central Europe, 2014–2024
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether consensus analyst forecasts for annual earnings per share (EPS) are more accurate than a standard random walk (RW) model for companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, the Prague Stock Exchange, the Budapest Stock Exchange and the Bucharest Stock Exchange during 2014–2024. Design/methodology/approach Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS from EquityRT are compared against RW model predictions using mean arctangent absolute percentage error, mean absolute error and mean square error. Wilcoxon and permutation tests assess statistical significance. For the Warsaw Stock Exchange, which provides the largest sample, the analysis is further stratified by analyst coverage intensity, firm capitalization, industry classification, corporate governance structure, institutional ownership composition and dividend orientation. Robustness checks employ alternative error metrics across multiple dimensions. Findings Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS demonstrate no statistically significant differentiation from RW predictions for Poland (excluding 2020), the Czech Republic (excluding 2020 and 2022), Hungary (excluding 2020) and Romania (excluding 2019 and 2022). This finding holds with respect to ownership structures and dividend policies. In the Polish market, for which detailed multi-dimensional analysis is provided, the absence of analyst a…

Artificial neural network-assisted prediction of Ti3C2-GO hybrid nanofluid flow over a curved surface
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the hemodynamics characteristics of nanofluid and hybrid nanofluid over a curved surface. The analysis focuses on momentum and energy transport in the presence of nanoparticles and compares the numerical results with artificial neural network (ANN) results. Design/methodology/approach A Casson blood-based nanofluid (nf) and hybrid nanofluid (hnf) flow model over a curved region is considered. The nf consists of 4% MXene (Ti3C2) nanoparticles dispersed in blood, while the hnf contains 4% MXene (Ti3C2) and 4% graphene oxide (GO) nanoparticles dispersed in blood. The flow is influenced by magnetic forces and Darcy–Forchheimer porous effects, whereas the energy field is affected by radiant heat, ohmic heating and uneven heat-source/sink conditions. The mathematical model is solved numerically by the MATLAB bvp5c problem solver. In addition, an ANN model accomplished with the Levenberg–Marquardt backpropagation procedure is used. The random data split is 70% for training, 15% for validation and 15% for testing to predict the heat transfer rate, and the predictions are validated against numerical results. Findings Results show that hnf significantly improves the heat transfer rate compared with nf taken in this study. Also, the relative change in the magnitude of skin friction is approximately 10%–12% for nf and 22%–25% for hnf when compared wit…

title: CurvEdgeNet: edge feature integration with Ricci curvature for circRNA-disease association prediction
abstract: Introduction Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are important regulatory non-coding RNAs involved in diverse pathological processes and have emerged as promising candidates for disease biomarker discovery. Systematic identification of circRNA–disease associations can help elucidate disease mechanisms and prioritize candidates for biological validation. However, existing computational approaches often rely on conventional similarity networks or node-centered feature learning, which may inadequately capture the non-Euclidean geometry and edge-level interactions of biological networks. Methods We propose CurvEdgeNet, a geometry-enhanced computational framework for predicting circRNA–disease associations. CurvEdgeNet constructs a heterogeneous circRNA–disease network by integrating multiple circRNA and disease similarity measures with known associations. A discrete Ollivier–Ricci curvature-based edge descriptor is incorporated into a curvature-enhanced graph attention mechanism to characterize local network geometry. In parallel, a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) module captures global feature dependencies, while multi-head attention integrates complementary local geometric and global representations for association prediction. Results CurvEdgeNet was evaluated on three public benchmark datasets: CircR2Disease V2, CircRNADisease V2, and CircFunBase. Under five-fold cross-valida…

title: Interpretable linguistic features for multi-trait prediction of english essay scores, and what they do not license a feedback tool to claim
abstract: Automated writing assessment is increasingly proposed for language-learning tools, but the feedback offered is often loosely connected to what the underlying model supports. This study examines multi-trait prediction of English essay scores from interpretable linguistic features, and asks what a feedback tool built on that model may legitimately claim. Working with the released 3,911-essay training partition of the ELLIPSE Corpus of English-language-learner writing, whose six corpus-provided score variables (cohesion, syntax, vocabulary, phraseology, grammar, conventions) are scored 1.0–5.0, we computed 77 linguistic features and evaluated models with nested cross-validation (5 folds × 3 repeats), compared using the Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t -test with Holm–Bonferroni adjustment. Because fold dependence leaves an effective 3.16 independent folds, effect sizes are mean differences with corrected intervals, fold win rates and essay-level probabilities of superiority rather than standardised d z . Ridge regression over these features achieved a mean columnwise RMSE of 0.5271, a 19.3% reduction against a constant-mean baseline, with no detectable difference from TF-IDF representations. Four further findings emerged. First, dimension-specific modelling outperformed a holistic model, but against a base-rate-ranked constant strategy neither single- nor two-variable identific…

title: Reservoir-Scale Heterogeneity in CO2 Geological Storage: A Review of Characterization, Mechanisms, Prediction, and Management with Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract The large-scale deployment of CO2 geological storage imposes stringent requirements on injectivity, subsurface space utilization, and long-term safety, making reservoir-scale heterogeneity a critical constraint on engineering feasibility and storage reliability. However, existing studies have primarily focused on individual heterogeneity elements, localized storage processes, or specific spatial scales, while systematic understanding of the coupling among multiple structural types, cross-scale transfer, and their impacts throughout the storage lifecycle remains limited. Therefore, this study synthesizes experimental, modeling, field, and ML studies, distinguishing their evidence sources and validation limits, to summarize the origins, types, characterization methods, and quantitative indicators of heterogeneity and to compare approaches for geological modeling, probabilistic prediction, and engineering regulation. The reviewed literature indicates the influence of geological architecture and connectivity on preferential migration and plume distribution. Quantitative effects on pressure, capacity, and trapping remain dependent on site conditions and model assumptions. Based on the identified limitations, recommendations are proposed in eight areas: evaluation standards, multisource data integration, structural fidelity, scale correction, probabilistic prediction, dynami…

title: 3D convolutional Dimension Preserved decomposition model integrated with Fourier Transform for traffic data prediction
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to overcome the limitations of traditional deep learning architectures in processing missing and noisy spatio-temporal streaming data. It aims to develop a robust spatio-temporal forecasting framework that can directly utilize incomplete inputs to achieve accurate predictions, thereby preventing catastrophic performance degradation and gradient collapse. Design/methodology/approach An innovative framework, termed FTI3DCDP, is proposed for traffic forecasting with incomplete data without requiring prior imputation. It establishes a dual-domain learning mechanism, where Fourier Transform extracts robust periodic patterns from incomplete signals in the frequency domain, while Dimension Preserved (DP) Decomposition captures low-rank spatial structures. A 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) adaptively integrates these complementary features for end-to-end spatio-temporal forecasting. Extensive experiments on five real-world traffic datasets under varying missing rates demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of FTI3DCDP across diverse traffic scenarios. Findings The results demonstrate that the proposed approach not only maintains forecasting stability under high sparsity but also consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baseline methods. This offers a highly resilient and deployable tool for supporting edge-intelligence solutions in…

title: Hydraulic conductivity and prediction models for clays in Tailan River Irrigation District
abstract: This study examines the permeability mechanism of cohesive soils using the Tailan River Irrigation District in Xinjiang as a case. Laboratory hydraulic conductivity tests and scanning electron microscopy were conducted to analyse the effect of dry density on hydraulic conductivity from both macro and micro perspectives, leading to improved hydraulic conductivity calculations. The results show that: Hydraulic conductivity decreases with increasing dry density, and the strongest correlation is found between porosity and hydraulic conductivity. Four commonly used empirical hydraulic conductivity formulas are modified by incorporating the concept of effective porosity ratio. The modified Kozeny–Carman formula performs the best with an average relative error of 28.16%, which is significantly lower than that of the other modified formulas. Further validation with independent test data from arid cold irrigation districts shows that the error of the modified formula is stably below 35%, indicating sound cross-regional applicability. It can provide reference for the calculation of clayey soil hydraulic conductivity in similar groundwater level regulation projects in arid cold irrigation districts.

title: Effects of egg source and extraction method on physicochemical properties, volatile profiles, and in vitro antioxidant capacity of egg yolk oil
abstract: Egg yolk is rich in lipids, phospholipids and other fat-soluble compounds, which are generally considered to contribute to its nutritional and technological value and have supported its use in flavor bases and functional-food formulations. However, the quality and flavor development of egg yolk oil (EYO) depend on egg source and preparation method. Here, egg yolk oils from conventional chicken eggs and Taihe Black-Bone Silk Fowl eggs were prepared by traditional thermal extraction or ethanol extraction. Physical properties, volatile compounds, and in vitro antioxidant activities were compared to define their flavor characteristics. Both egg source and extraction method influenced oil quality, although extraction method exerted the greater effect on the overall odor profile. Ethanol extraction increased extract yield and reduced viscosity. Thermal extraction produced stronger browning, and aldehydes and furans were the most numerous classes in its volatile profile. In total, 33 volatile compounds were putatively identified across the samples. Ethanol-extracted oils contained relatively higher levels of esters, ketones and pyrazines. Electronic-nose analysis further distinguished the odor fingerprints associated with the two extraction methods. Ethanol extraction of Taihe Black-Bone Silk Fowl egg yolk produced a relatively high extract yield, strong in vitro free-radical-scavengi…

title: Temporal changes in self-reported noncommunicable disease prevention, surveillance, and management capacity among primary care nurses in Binga District, Zimbabwe: A pilot repeated-measures implementation evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims: This pilot implementation study described temporal changes in self-reported noncommunicable disease (NCD) prevention, surveillance, and management capacity among primary care nurses in Binga District, Zimbabwe. Materials and Methods: A prospective repeated-measures implementation evaluation followed eight matched primary care nurses. Baseline data were collected from January 23 to January 24, 2026 after ethics committee approval, followed by midline and endline assessments. Program records listed 36 primary care nurses in the initial concept note and a final target of 40 nurses; exact invitation and refusal counts were unavailable. Study-specific domain scores and an equally weighted self-reported NCD capacity index were expressed on 0–100 scales. Friedman tests with Kendall’s W were exploratory and Holm-adjusted. Results: Five participants were female (62.5%), and the mean age was 40.6 years. The study-specific self-reported NCD capacity index changed from 81.9 at baseline to 89.6 at endline (+7.7). Facility and community readiness changed by +19.8 points, surveillance knowledge by +11.7, prevention knowledge by +8.3, essential medicine availability by +9.4, and nutrition counseling by +5.6; guideline availability changed by −30.0. No comparison remained statistically significant after Holm adjustment. Conclusion: The findings provide pilot descri…

title: Teacher charisma as a mechanism for transforming performance anxiety into creative energy: a case study in vocal education
abstract: Purpose This study explores the potential role of teacher charisma in transforming performance anxiety into constructive creative energy, and identifies strategies of charismatic pedagogical facilitation in vocal and performative arts education. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative pedagogical case-study design, combining conceptual analysis with in-depth, longitudinal observation of two contrasting cases in the vocal classroom of a Ukrainian university specialising in performative arts, over one academic year. The theoretical framework integrates humanistic pedagogy, charismatic leadership theory and the psychology of performance anxiety. Findings Two case-based patterns of performance anxiety were identified – physiological-panic and cognitive-perfectionism – each associated with a different facilitation strategy. In both cases, the teacher's charismatic presence appeared to be one salient factor, alongside other concurrent influences, in the students' movement from anxiety towards greater performance freedom. A preliminary four-mechanism model of this process is proposed as a hypothesis for further, independent empirical verification, rather than as an established finding. Originality/value This study contributes to a still limited body of work by offering an illustrative, case-based account of charismatic pedagogical facilitation as one plausible mecha…

It aims to develop a mechanism linking agent point selection, agent incentives and service quality control. A targeted literature review, comparative analysis and conceptual modelling inform the proposed PostAgent mechanism. The framework jointly considers agent participation, operator costs and customer convenience. Performance indicators and a pilot evaluation procedure are specified. title: Multi-objective Optimization and Experimental Validation of a Drive Neutral Equilibrium Mechanism for Active Structural Control
abstract: ABSTRACT Active structural control systems offer potential improvements in the serviceability of dynamically sensitive bridges. This study experimentally evaluates a Direct-Drive Neutral Equilibrium Mechanism (DNEM) for precision displacement control of a 2.5 m laboratory-scale steel bridge under dynamic loading. The system integrates a rotary-arm-and-tendon actuation mechanism with a composite real-time control strategy (proportional-derivative feedback and harmonic compensation). The 1,000 Hz closed-loop control relies exclusively on LVDT measurements for real-time precision feedback, while a Digital Image Correlation (DIC) system (500 fps) is employed in parallel solely for offline independent spatial validation. Controller gains were optimized using NSGA-II (Kp=42.3 N/mm, Kd=3.7 N·s/mm) within a fixed structural configuration. Experimental results demonstrate a 99.2 % peak displacement reduction under impact loading (6.00–0.05 mm) and steady-state cyclic precision of 0.128±0.0076 mm under a sustained 5 kN moving load. Phase-portrait analysis confirmed stable closed-loop operation without limit-cycle behavior. The close agreement between LVDT and DIC measurements validates the experimental methodology. This study establishes quantitative performance benchmarks for controller tuning, actuator evaluation, and future full-scale implementation of active bridge control technologi…

title: Ionic Liquid-Functionalized CNT Electrochemical Platform Governed by a Dual-Path Sensing Mechanism for Versatile VOC Detection
abstract: Abstract Room-temperature ionic liquids (RTILs) have garnered significant attention as advanced electrolytes for electrochemical gas sensors owing to their negligible volatility and wide electrochemical windows. However, their application in detecting volatile organic compounds (VOCs) is constrained by high viscosity (limiting mass transport) and the sluggish electrooxidation kinetics of most VOCs. Supported ionic liquid phase (SILP) materials, which immobilize RTILs on porous supports to amplify the gas–liquid interface, present a promising yet underexplored avenue for addressing these challenges. Herein, we develop a novel electrochemical platform configured with high-purity semiconducting carbon nanotube (CNT) films serving as both working electrodes and scaffolds to immobilize RTILs to construct a nanostructured SILP electrolyte. This architecture simultaneously maximizes the active gas–liquid interface, minimizes the gas diffusion distance, and ensures efficient charge transport. The platform enables quantitative detection of ethanol and isopropanol, exhibiting well-defined linear responses from 0–800 ppm and 0–600 ppm, respectively, with distinctive non-monotonic patterns at higher concentrations. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the sensing process diverges from conventional faradaic electrochemistry and is instead governed by a dual-path mechanism: competitive ads…

abstract: Метою статті є дослідження інституційного механізму здійснення парламентського та урядового контролю за формуванням та виконанням державного бюджету. У статті використано метод аналізу, а також формально-логічний та спеціально-юридичний методи, які було застосовано під час визначення поняття «публічний контроль за формуванням та виконанням державного бюджету, а також місця органів, що здійснюють парламентський та урядовий контроль у відповідній сфері. Результати дослідження полягають у визначенні сутності інституційного механізму здійснення публічного контролю за формуванням та виконанням державного бюджету, а також у характеристиці окремих елементів інституційного механізму здійснення парламентського та урядового контролю за формуванням та виконанням державного бюджету. В статті обґрунтовується необхідність внесення змін до законодавства, а саме: необхідність доповнення ч. 1 ст. 14 Закону України «Про комітети Верховної Ради України» положенням про аналіз врахування контрольних висновків у бюджетному процесі; ст. 37 Бюджетного кодексу України вимогою про звіт Кабінету Міністрів України щодо врахування результатів публічного контролю у проєкті Державного бюджету України. Обґрунтовується висновок, що інституційний механізм здійснення публічного контролю за формуванням та виконанням державного бюджету є конституційно обумовленою, законодавчо конкретизованою і процедурно пов’язано…

title: Low-carbon control of heavy metals in industrial flue gas
abstract: Heavy metals emitted from industrial sectors represent a class of recalcitrant atmospheric pollutants with severe ecotoxicological hazards even at trace levels. Their control is complicated by temperature-dependent volatilization, chemical transformation, phase redistribution, and interactions with reactive flue-gas components. This Mini Review examines heavy-metal control from the physicochemical basis of release and speciation to gas-phase regulation, interfacial capture, and removal in conventional air-pollution-control devices. Particular attention is given to low-carbon control strategies, which aim to reduce additional energy and material inputs by lowering energy consumption, implementing co-benefit control, and utilizing flue-gas components, while avoiding placing an excessive burden on downstream treatment processes. Controlled cooling, adsorption, catalytic or chemical speciation conversion, wet absorption, and plasma-assisted activation can effectively regulate heavy-metal fate, but their overall benefit depends on energy demand, reagent consumption, and the stability of the resulting metal-containing residues. Current technologies also face three persistent limitations: high energy and material inputs, secondary release from unstable captured metals, and difficulties in resource recovery from complex residues. Future development should therefore couple efficient rem…

title: [68Ga] Ga-FAPI positron emission tomography/computed tomography uptake following liver stereotactic body radiation therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma: two case reports
abstract: Abstract Background [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography have shown high sensitivity for detecting hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI uptake also occurs in benign fibroinflammatory processes, creating a specific challenge for post-treatment surveillance after liver-directed therapies. Case presentation We report two HCC patients who underwent stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) and subsequently developed FAPI-avid hepatic lesions. In Case 1, a 68-year-old man showed focal FAPI uptake in segment VI following SBRT, which Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) characterised as fibrosis (LI-RADS LR-TR non-viable), with stable tumour markers and no clinical progression. In Case 2, a 77-year-old man exhibited FAPI avidity in the treated lesion, with MRI findings suggestive of post-treatment change. In both cases, the increased FAPI uptake was deemed as false-positive and attributed to post-radiation fibroinflammatory changes. Conclusion These cases highlight a critical interpretative limitation of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI PET/CT in post-SBRT HCC surveillance. Fibroblast activation in healing tissues can mimic recurrence; MRI correlation should be done to prevent misdiagnosis. Our report provides novel evidence that SBRT-induced hepatic fibrosis may confound FAPI-based imaging and adds to the evolving understanding of FAPI’s performance in surveillance of li…

Engineering Sustainable Asphalt with Biomass-Derived Surface-Functionalized Biochar through Molecular Conservation and Emission Mitigation
abstract: Abstract Sustainable asphalt technologies are increasingly vital for conserving resources, reducing environmental emissions, and enabling the beneficial reuse of carbon-rich waste materials. Surface-functionalized biochar (SFB) offers a promising strategy to enhance asphalt performance, while providing a sustainable platform for mitigating volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions; however, the roles of environmental humidity and asphalt binder composition in governing SFB’s VOC-mitigation efficacy remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluate SFB-modified asphalt at relative humidity (RH) ≈ 50% and 50 °C using environmental chamber measurements, volatility- and polarity-resolved emission analysis, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations. Across three asphalt binders, SFB reduced total organic emission factors by 94.5%, 84.5%, and 46.7%. Intermediate-volatility organic compounds (IVOCs) and semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) were consistently suppressed by more than 70%, but light-polar VOC emissions showed an increase specifically in one out of the three binders. This in turn demonstrates that mitigation under humid conditions is strongly binder-dependent. Simulations indicate that interfacial water redistributes polar VOCs and competes with them for adsorption sites, weakening SFB–VOC interactions, particularly for small polar compounds. …

title: Beyond Carbon Stocks: Integrating Field Flux Measurements, Land-Use Histories, and Life-Cycle Evidence for Climate-Integrity Accounting in Oil Palm Systems
abstract: Background: Carbon sequestration claims in oil-palm production frequently combine standing biomass inventories, soil measurements, local greenhouse-gas fluxes and product life-cycle estimates without comparable boundaries. Objective: This review evaluates the evidence required to distinguish carbon storage from a net atmospheric sink or verifiable climate-mitigation contribution. Methods: A critical qualitative literature review synthesises fifty-nine peer-reviewed journal articles published from 2020 through 2026, using a Central Kalimantan field briefing as a problem-setting case. Results: Six themes emerge: carbon-pool comparability; land-use history and peat drainage; multi-gas fluxes; complementary measurement systems; management interventions; and baseline and verification integrity. The briefing illustrates a consequential mismatch between forest biomass-only values and plantation vegetation-plus-soil totals. High-frequency sensor transmission similarly does not independently establish accurate annual emissions. Contribution: A six-stage Carbon Integrity Ladder links matched inventories, temporal changes, flux closure, land-use counterfactuals, life-cycle and uncertainty reconciliation, and independent governance. Conclusion: Credible oil-palm mitigation begins with avoiding forest and peat conversion, followed by verified reductions on existing land; individual stock me…

title: Aligning institutions and organizations for sustainable supply chains: the role of digital transformation and low-carbon practices
abstract: Purpose The transition toward carbon neutrality has become a global strategic priority for achieving sustainable development and a green economy. Despite growing interest in digital transformation among scholars and practitioners, achieving a balance between green supply chain performance and carbon performance within the context of carbon neutrality remains underexplored. Drawing on the technology acceptance model and change management theory, this research aims to provide solutions for achieving the zero-carbon target in 2060 through holistic digital transformation, and how institutional pressure and organizational readiness influence green supply chain and carbon performance through digital transformation, low-carbon operations management practices (LCOMP) and the moderating role of environmental proactivity. Design/methodology/approach Data from 442 Chinese manufacturing firms were analyzed using Smart PLS v4 to test the research hypotheses. Findings The results indicate that all three dimensions of LCOMP mediate the relationship between digital transformation, green supply chain and carbon performance. In addition, environmental proactivity strengthens the influence of digital transformation on the three dimensions of LCOMP. Originality/value The findings contribute to the literature by addressing a key gap in sustainable supply chain and digital transformation research, w…

title: Blue carbon stocks and wetland landscape change in the Liaohe Estuary
abstract: Introduction Coastal-wetland carbon assessments can support conservation and restoration monitoring when measured carbon pools are interpreted alongside habitat extent. This study compared carbon stocks in the dominant natural habitats of the Liaohe Estuary and examined landscape change and observations at a restoration site. Methods Natural-habitat aboveground vegetation carbon and 0-100 cm soil organic carbon were compared in a common areal unit. Exploratory Landsat classifications described landscape change during 1985-2020, and four monitoring campaigns characterized vegetation and soil conditions at a Daling River Estuary restoration site. Results Natural Suaeda salsa meadows had higher mean soil organic carbon stocks than Phragmites australis marshes (112.71 ± 49.77 versus 68.56 ± 44.62 Mg C ha⁻¹), whereas P. australis had greater aboveground vegetation carbon. Combined measured soil and aboveground stocks were 114.72 and 73.01 Mg C ha⁻¹, respectively, with soil contributing 98.3% and 93.9%. The mapped natural-wetland area contracted before an apparent increase after 2015; the unvalidated classifications provide landscape context. At the restoration site, aboveground stocks were 0.18048 and 1.833 Mg C ha⁻¹ in November 2020 and July 2022, with corresponding soil stocks of 149.08 and 163.49 Mg C ha⁻¹. Discussion The restoration-site observations differ in season and lack a …

title: Pore development and electrochemical performance of CO 2 -activated polyacrylonitrile-derived carbon nanofibers enabled by shellac
abstract: Abstract Polyacrylonitrile (PAN)-derived carbon nanofibers (CNFs) were fabricated by incorporating shellac, a naturally derived polymer, into PAN precursor solutions, followed by stabilization, carbonization, and CO 2 activation. The resulting shellac/PAN-derived CNFs were characterized for their morphology, pore structure, surface chemistry, and electrochemical performance using a three-electrode configuration. The Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area increased markedly with increasing shellac content, from 214.1 m 2 g −1 for the shellac-free activated CNFs to 771.9 and 1059.8 m 2 g −1 for the samples containing 10 and 20 wt.% shellac, respectively. A corresponding increase in total pore volume was also observed. Despite their lower specific surface area, the shellac-free activated CNFs exhibited the highest specific capacitance of 186.5 F g −1 and the highest energy density of 24.6 Wh kg −1 at a current density of 0.5 A g −1 . These results suggest that a substantial fraction of the surface area generated in the shellac-containing samples was not effectively utilized for charge storage. Nevertheless, the sample containing 20 wt.% shellac exhibited a power density comparable to that of the shellac-free sample and retained 97.7% of the initial capacitance after 1000 charge–discharge cycles. These findings demonstrate that shellac effectively promotes the developme…
