Can agricultural green development policies improve the carbon performance of enterprises? Empirical evidence from listed agricultural enterprises in China
abstract: Introduction Carbon management in agricultural enterprises is deeply embedded in the agricultural industrial ecosystem. The policy of green development in agriculture provides a key path to solve the predicament of carbon reduction in agriculture. Methods This paper, based on the microdata of 245 listed agricultural enterprises in China from 2011 to 2024, uses a dual machine learning model to investigate the impact of agricultural green development policies on the carbon performance (CP) of agricultural enterprises and its mechanism of action. Results The research findings are as follows: First, the green development policy for agriculture has significantly enhanced the CP of agricultural enterprises. Second, mechanism tests have shown that promoting green technological innovation, alleviating financing constraints, and increasing external media attention are the three core paths for agricultural green development policies to enhance the CP of agricultural enterprises. Thirdly, heterogeneity analysis indicates that this policy has a more significant effect on enhancing CP for agricultural enterprises located in the second batch of pilot zones, regions with strong environmental regulations, and those with lower digitalization levels. Fourth, an expansive analysis reveals that there is a significant synergy between the agricultural green development policy and the green finance r…

title: Molecular architecture of surface-active ionic liquids governs protein structural integrity and drug recognition at engineered carbon quantum dot nano–bio interfaces
abstract: Introduction Protein–nanomaterial interfaces are increasingly exploited in biomedicine, yet the influence of ionic liquid (IL) molecular architecture on protein structure and ligand recognition remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the interactions of lysozyme (LYZ) with surface-active ionic liquids (SAILs), SAIL functionalized carbon quantum dots (CQD-ILs), and the subsequent binding of donepezil (DON) to native LYZ and LYZ–CQD/CQD-IL conjugates. Methods SAILs bearing imidazolium (IB) or pyridinium (PB) headgroups with dodecyl (DD) or tetradecyl (TD) alkyl chains were systematically examined using steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy, circular dichroism (CD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, small angle neutron scattering (SANS), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Results and Discussion DON binding proceeded predominantly through a static and spontaneous mechanism, while CQD association enhanced the binding affinity by approximately 1.3-fold. Functionalization with tetradecyl pyridinium (TDPB) produced a further ∼4.7-fold increase relative to native LYZ. Notably, the enhanced ligand recognition did not correlate directly with the strength of LYZ–CQD/SAIL association, indicating that the local physicochemical organization of the IL-modified nano–bio interface, rather than binding strength alone, …

title: Subcooling Controlled Hydrate Crystal Morphology and Aggregate Structure Coupling in Multiphase Flow
abstract: Abstract Deepwater high-pressure and low-temperature environments make oil and gas transportation prone to hydrate blockage. Elucidating the formation and blockage evolution of natural gas hydrates is therefore critical for ensuring energy security. Hydrate crystal morphology provides a microscopic basis for understanding blockage formation. However, previous studies have mainly focused on hydrate crystal morphological evolution in static systems. In this study, a visualized flow loop was developed to investigate hydrate crystal morphology under multiphase flow conditions. The results indicate that increasing subcooling leads to smoother, more elongated, and more fragmented hydrate particles with greater morphological irregularity at the microscopic scale. At the macroscopic scale, the rate of hydrate formation in the system exhibits a nonmonotonic relationship with the subcooling. With increasing subcooling, increasingly fragmented blocklike and elongated rodlike hydrate particles form denser aggregation structures, thereby increasing flow resistance and causing a higher blockage differential pressure. Subcooling regulates hydrate crystal morphology, which governs aggregate compactness and ultimately controls flow resistance and blockage behavior. The findings highlight that hydrate blockage risk cannot be assessed solely based on the formation rate but must consider hydrate c…

title: Numerical investigation on thermal-fluid-solid coupling for afterburner heat shield of aero-engine
abstract: Abstract To address the challenge that it is difficult to accurately predict the evolution laws of the flow field and structural field of an aero-engine afterburner heat shield under high-temperature and high-pressure operating conditions, a numerical simulation study of thermal-fluid-solid coupling for the afterburner heat shield was performed using the ANSYS Workbench software. A periodic sector model of the heat shield was established. The effects of varying the mainstream temperature (750–1,250 K) and coolant mass flow rate (0.15–0.35 kg/s) on the heat shield performance, stress, and deformation were investigated. The simulations showed that raising the mainstream temperature from 750 to 1,250 K barely altered the static pressure in the mainstream passage but reduced the cooling effectiveness of the afterburner heat shield by 4.62 %. Increasing the coolant mass flow rate from 0.15 to 0.35 kg/s significantly raised the static pressure in the coolant passage and improved the cooling effectiveness by 41.18 %. A higher mainstream temperature concurrently increased both the stress and deformation of the heat shield, whereas a larger coolant flow rate decreased the deformation but elevated the structural stress. These findings provide a theoretical basis for afterburner heat shield thermal design.

title: Direction-dependent coherent-dissipative indirect coupling in cavity magnonics
abstract: We demonstrate direction-dependent coherent-dissipative indirect coupling in cavity magnonics. A photon-like self-cavity resonance of a yttrium iron garnet disk first hybridizes with the ferromagnetic resonance to form magnon–photon polaritons. The lower polariton subsequently interacts with the effective cavity response near an interference induced antiresonance formed by adjacent resonances of a two port quadrant-stadium cavity. Under otherwise identical experimental conditions, the same hybridization exhibits level repulsion in forward transmission S21 and level-attraction-like behavior in backward transmission S12, corresponding to coherent-dominated and dissipative-dominated responses, respectively. Independent phase measurements yield distinct directional phase responses, which are directly used as the phase parameters in a hierarchical input-output model. The model captures the principal direction-dependent hybridization features and relates the reversal of the coupling character to the effective phase structure of the polariton cavity port scattering pathway. The resulting nonreciprocity produces compound isolation in opposite directions within two distinct and nonoverlapping frequency windows, providing a route toward multiband nonreciprocal signal processing.

title: Assessing the worthwhileness of efficiency enhancement methods mitigating buoyancy flow in high-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage
abstract: Abstract High-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage (HT-ATES) presents a promising approach for achieving a temporally and spatially balanced, continuous energy supply. A key challenge in HT-ATES systems is the density-driven buoyancy flow, which can result in considerable heat losses and reduced energy efficiency, or thermal recovery efficiency. This study explores two strategies for mitigating the effects of buoyancy flow: adjusting the working fluid’s salinity and modifying the production well screen length, under varying intensities of buoyancy flow. Numerical simulations are employed to evaluate the recovery efficiency and pumping energy requirements across a range of fluid salinities and screen lengths over multiple HT-ATES operational cycles. Under conditions of high intensity of buoyancy flow, the impact of different fluid salinities on thermal front evolution and associated hydrodynamic processes is analyzed. Recovery efficiency exhibits a nonmonotonic response to fluid salinity, with the maximum improvement reaching 36.5% at an increase in salinity of 6%. At a moderate intensity of buoyancy flow, altering fluid salinity proves ineffective due to the formation of a buffering layer, where cooled saline water separates the injected fluid from the surrounding groundwater. Comparatively, modifying fluid salinity is found to be more effective than adjusting the product…

title: Інноваційні педагогічні стратегії формування поліхудожньої обізнаності майбутніх викладачів вокалу на засадах міжмистецької інтеграції
abstract: У статті розглянуто теоретичні засади формування поліхудожньої обізнаності майбутніх викладачів вокалу в процесі професійної підготовки. Методологічну основу дослідження становлять системний, інтегративний, компетентнісний, особистісно-діяльнісний, художньо-інтерпретаційний і культурологічний підходи, реалізовані на основі принципів взаємозумовленості, міжмистецької взаємодії, професійної спрямованості, суб’єктної активності, інтерпретаційної варіативності художнього рішення та культурної контекстуалізації. Уточнено зміст поліхудожньої обізнаності як інтегративної характеристики професійної підготовленості, що охоплює систему знань про різні види мистецтва, розуміння специфіки їхньої взаємодії, здатність встановлювати міжмистецькі зв’язки, здійснювати художньо-образний аналіз і використовувати отримані знання у вокально-педагогічній та творчо-виконавській діяльності. Виокремлено когнітивно-мистецький, інтегративно-аналітичний, інтерпретаційно-творчий і професійно-педагогічний компоненти поліхудожньої обізнаності. Визначено міжмистецьку інтеграцію як системоутворювальний чинник формування поліхудожньої обізнаності та конкретизовано змістовий, аналітичний, творчо-інтерпретаційній та педагогічний рівні її реалізації. title: Influence of Acetic Acid–Based Feed Formulation on Energy and Protein Metabolizability and Growth Performance in Rhode Island Red Chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus)
abstract: The search for alternatives to antibiotic growth promoters in poultry has intensified due to concerns about antimicrobial resistance and food safety. Organic acids, particularly acetic acid, have shown potential in improving gut health, nutrient absorption, and growth performance. This study evaluated the effects of acetic acid–based feed on energy and protein metabolizability, growth performance, and production efficiency in Rhode Island Red chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus). Ninety-six one-week-old chicks were randomly assigned to four dietary treatments in a randomized complete block design: T0 (control, 0% AA), T1 (0.3% AA), T2 (1.65% AA), and T3 (3% AA). Home-mixed starter and grower rations were formulated using Brill Feed Formulation Software and fed ad libitum for ten weeks. Growth performance parameters (BW, ADG, WG, FCR, VFI) were measured, while true metabolizable energy (TME) and true metabolizable protein (TMP) were determined using a force-feeding procedure. Data were analyzed using ANOVA and Tukey’s HSD (p<0.05). No significant differences were observed among treatments for growth performance, TME, or TMP. However, T3 numerically exhibited higher BW, WG, and ADG, and lower FCR. Economically, T3 and T2 had the lowest cost-to-produce (CTP), which was significantly lower than T0 and T1 (p<0.05). Although improvements in growth and nutrient utilization were not sta…

title: Modeling Circularwashing Risk in Renewable Energy Adoption: A Structural Equation Approach for Sustainable Consumption
abstract: Abstract Circularwashing limits eco-friendly consumption by overstating, confusing, or inadequately proving the circular properties of products. While regular greenwashing makes ambiguous claims about the environmental characteristics, circularwashing takes advantage of the complicated nature of resource loops and the quality of the supply chain, causing significant market friction and high information asymmetry. Hence, an unexpected change in information distorts price signals, weakens customer trust, and jeopardizes market transparency by creating a lemon market for real circular goods. The present research presents the idea of circularwashing risk and provides a model to analyze the effect of false claims on the customers’ skepticism, decision-making risk perception, institutional trust, penalties for unreasonable behavior, and post-decision actions. The model is based on the Signaling Theory and the Stimulus Organism Response theory and is verified with the help of the survey data collected from 607 digital consumers in Colombia using the method of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Model (PLS SEM). The measurement properties were assessed through composite reliability, average variance extracted, and heterotrait monotrait discriminant criteria and bootstrap resampling. The findings imply that misleading environmental claims correlate with consumer skepticism, which …

abstract: The paper examines the institutional architecture of public-private partnership (PPP) in the electricity sector of the Republic of Uzbekistan during its market transformation in 2019-2026. The study aims to identify inconsistencies between PPP rules and the emerging institutions of a competitive electricity market and to substantiate ways of resolving them. The methodology draws on new institutional economics, historical-institutional periodization, comparative legal analysis and a matrix of institutional gaps. The reform is shown to have passed through four stages, from establishing basic rules to fiscal ceilings and planned project selection. The project-initiative format ensured a rapid inflow of private capital (solar and wind output rose from 0.43 bn kWh in 2022 to 10.5 bn kWh in 2025) but was accompanied by growing contingent liabilities and limited contract transparency. An approach is proposed that develops the regulatory, organizational and fiscal-contractual contours of PPP in a synchronized way

title: Formation of a giant monoclinic P 2 SiB 6 superstructure by high-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering
abstract: Abstract Silicon hexaboride is a structurally complex boron-rich ceramic whose diffraction response is highly sensitive to processing history and long-range ordering. Nominal SiB 6 ceramics were prepared from elemental Si and B powders by high-energy ball milling for 1 or 10 h, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) between 1,300 and 1,700 °C. Laboratory X-ray diffraction shows that specimens processed at 1,300–1,500 °C retain the established orthorhombic SiB 6 -type framework, whereas the patterns obtained at 1,600–1,700 °C exhibit an abrupt redistribution of intensity and intense low-angle reflections that cannot be described by the orthorhombic cell. The long-period monoclinic metric was first verified by Pawley refinement, after which parent-derived rigid polyhedral motifs were assembled in direct space with PowderSolve. For 1,700-N-1H, the PowderSolve proposal was regularized by diffraction-guided geodesic projection (DGGP), introduced here as an alternating structure-solution strategy. DGGP cycles 1–3 generated a contact-safe connected framework; comparison of coordinated rigid-object alternatives with the experimental low-angle intensities then selected variant A as the definitive cycle-4 reconstruction. title: THE HISTORY OF ENERGY PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN AZERBAIJAN AND THE EUROPEAN UNION IN THE NATURAL GAS SECTOR
abstract: The article presents a comprehensive analysis of the formation and development of the energy partnership between Azerbaijan and the European Union in the gas sector, in the context of the profound transformation of the European energy architecture and global changes in the energy market. Particular attention is given to structural shifts in the EU gas sector, caused by declining domestic production, growing import dependence, price volatility, and increasing geopolitical risks, including the effects of the Russia–Ukraine conflict, which led to a reassessment of energy policy priorities and stimulated the activation of strategies for diversifying gas sources and transit routes. The article examines institutional mechanisms of cooperation, legislative initiatives, and stages of implementation of key infrastructure projects, primarily the Southern Gas Corridor as a system-forming element for transporting Caspian gas to Europe. The significance of its main components—the Trans-Anatolian Pipeline (TANAP) and the Trans-Adriatic Pipeline (TAP)—is highlighted, as they ensured direct access to European markets, enhanced supply reliability, and minimized transit risks. The importance of the Shah Deniz gas field, intergovernmental agreements, and strategic investments in creating a sustainable and long-term export model is emphasized. Restorative Interiors for the Digital Age: A Literature Review on Interior Design Strategies for Digital Fatigue
abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has intensified human interaction with screen-based devices. The demand to remain continuously connected to digital devices across everyday activities has contributed to the emergence of digital fatigue, characterized by mental exhaustion, reduced attention, boredom, and stress. This condition highlights the need to consider the role of the physical environment in supporting recovery processes, particularly the interior environments in which people carry out their activities. This study aims to identify restorative needs associated with digital fatigue and to examine how restorative environmental characteristics can be translated into interior design strategies. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted, with the literature selection process guided by PRISMA. A total of 21 articles were analyzed and grouped into three areas: digital fatigue, restorative environments, and interior design. Attention Restoration Theory (ART) was used as the primary framework for understanding attention restoration, while Stress Reduction Theory (SRT) was used to examine stress recovery. The findings indicate that restorative needs associated with digital fatigue primarily concern attention restoration and stress reduction. Utilization of Digital Immersive Spaces in the Interior Design of Public Spaces in Indonesia: Benefits, Challenges, and Implementation Strategies
abstract: Digital transformation expands the role of interior design from the arrangement of physical elements to the design of responsive, narrative, and participatory spatial experiences. This literature-review article examines the use of digital immersive spaces, including virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), mixed reality (MR), interactive projection, 360-degree video mapping, and digital installations in Indonesian public interior settings. A narrative-critical review of scholarly publications and institutional documents, primarily from 2019–2026, is undertaken with attention to museums, cultural galleries, commercial spaces, and educational environments. The synthesis shows that immersive spaces can enhance psychological presence, visitor engagement, narrative comprehension, atmosphere and scale visualization, curatorial flexibility, and opportunities for cultural preservation and interpretation. These benefits, however, do not arise automatically from adding digital devices. Experience quality depends on the fit between content and spatial context, interaction flow, sensory comfort, accessibility, safety, data privacy, operational capacity, and the sustainability of device life cycles. title: Evaluating gender equality policy alignment and institutional barriers to women’s retention in the Australian construction industry
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate how Australian federal and state government gender equality initiatives align with the key factors influencing women’s retention in the construction industry. Despite an expanding policy landscape, women remain underrepresented, indicating persistent institutional and organisational barriers. Design/methodology/approach A five-step evaluative review integrated a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review, analysis of 30 government initiatives and expert validation involving 12 academics and industry practitioners. Guided by Feminist Institutionalism and the Policy Cycle Model, the analysis assessed alignment with four retention factors: Work Hours and Family Commitment (WHAF), Gendered Culture and Informal Rules (GCIR), Career Opportunities and Available Roles (COAR) and Perceptions of Women’s Ability (POWA). Findings Policy attention to gender equality has increased; however, alignment with women’s retention factors remains uneven. Most initiatives focus on career opportunities and workforce participation, while fewer address workplace culture and informal institutional barriers. Legislative and procurement-based initiatives include stronger accountability mechanisms than voluntary initiatives. Practical implications Improving women’s retention requires policy frameworks that integrate stronger accountability mechanisms with initiatives that…

title: Disrupting gendered task division without achieving equity of parity: a centrality-affective paradox from a design experiment in undergraduate physics labs
abstract: Abstract Prior research has shown that, without careful design, group dynamics in undergraduate physics labs are often inequitable with respect to gendered task division. In this study, we implemented a three-change design experiment: changing lab group size from two-student to up to four-student groups; assigning group members randomly every week instead of allowing students to self-select stable groups for the entire semester; and adding the component of predefined, rotating roles. Through observations, we found that in an algebra-based lab with a majority-women population of bioscience majors, a woman consistently played a central, leading role regardless of role title, and that women assumed the Experimentalist role much more often than they did in two-student mixed-gender groups. However, matched pre and post E-CLASS results show that men do not exhibit any significant change over the course of the semester, whereas women show a significant decline in their attitudes toward experimental physics. These paradoxical results demonstrate that designing equitable learning environments is a complex process, and show that disrupting one pattern of inequity, does not, on its own, produce equity.

Toward a holistic assessment of economic performance in agricultural plant production
abstract: The European Commission reports that 60 to 70% of agricultural soil is degraded, and if current management continues, it is predicted that 90% will be degraded by 2050. Globally, 33% of all agricultural soil is reported as moderately to highly degraded. Ecological economics is guided by three pillars to maintain long-term ecological and economic balance. The pillars are sustainable scale, efficient resource allocation, and fair distribution. If there is a trade-off between maximizing yield and profitability and the overaching soil health, the scaling of management and economic activity is unsustainable. Over time, the system eventually reaches a critical threshold and a possible collapse. This is far from a fair distribution between humans, regarding future generations and non-humans regarding the soil–plant biota as a living ecosystem that also needs a fair share of the dividends we harvest for regeneration. A shift in how we handle the dividends we receive from nature is needed. Our knowledge system about soil–plant biota needs upgrading, followed by new management and economic assessments. In this article, we elaborate on a more holistic assessment of economic performance in agricultural plant production aligned with the three pillars of ecological economics. To illustrate how the pillars can be applied to a practical problem, we refer to a 4-year field trial cultivating org…

Tomato cultivation substrates differ in stage-dependent root zone–rhizosphere coordination and biomass allocation
abstract: Introduction Cultivation substrates are commonly evaluated from their initial properties or final crop performance, leaving the developmental relationships among root-zone conditions, rhizosphere functioning, and plant responses poorly resolved. We examined how contrasting substrates were associated with changes in these components across tomato development. Methods Tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L. cv. “22B”) was grown in greenhouse soil (SL), a composted pinecone residue substrate (PR), or a peat substrate (PS), with corresponding unplanted controls. Independent destructive sampling was conducted at Weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16 after transplanting. Root-zone physicochemical and nutrient conditions, rhizosphere enzyme activities, root traits, and organ dry matter were assessed across development; rhizosphere dehydrogenase activity, aboveground NO 3 -- N, P, and K accumulation and allocation, and yield-related traits were determined at maturity. Results Substrate effects were strongly stage-dependent. PR generally exhibited higher urease and sucrase activities during early-to-middle development. Fluorescein diacetate hydrolase activity was highest in PR at Weeks 4 and 8, but shifted to PS at Weeks 12 and 16. Throughout the growth cycle, PS generally maintained lower bulk density and higher gravimetric water content. It also exhibited the highest rhizosphere dehydrogenase activity at m…

title: Patterns of risk and need in an NHS community-based forensic learning disability and autism service
abstract: Purpose An up-to-date understanding of the needs and risks of adults with learning disabilities and/or autism (LDs/A) who present with forensic needs is essential to ensure policies, research and interventions are well informed. The purpose of this study is to systematically analyse demographic, clinical, forensic and service provision data from referrals to a single community-based forensic LD and autism service. Design/methodology/approach Retrospective case reviews were conducted using a standardised form and procedure. Referrals to the service over a three-year period (July 2022–July 2025) were included, and demographic, clinical and forensic data were collected. Two, 18-month review periods were created (Periods 1 and 2). Chi-square tests for independence were used to explore differences between review periods. Findings In all, 219 referrals were received and 162 progressed to initial assessment (Period 1 = 80; Period 2 = 82). Most of the sample were male (90.1%), White (74.1%) and under age of 34 years (69.1%). Mild LD was most common (24.7%). General interpersonal violence (45.1%) and sexual offending (48.1%) were the most prevalent current risk types. Social care and LD services were the biggest referring agencies. Consultation and direct intervention were the most used pathways. Non-significant trends across time were explored, along with implications for the service, …

title: Overwork climate and ambidextrous academic innovation: the moderating roles of power distance and collectivist values
abstract: Purpose Drawing on social information processing theory, this study examines the association between overwork climate and faculty members’ ambidextrous academic innovation. The study also examines the moderating roles of power distance and collectivist values in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 401 faculty members across five Chinese universities. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings The results show that overwork climate is positively associated with ambidextrous academic innovation. Power distance values are also positively related to ambidextrous academic innovation and strengthen the positive relationship between overwork climate and ambidextrous academic innovation. In contrast, collectivist values are positively related to ambidextrous academic innovation but weaken the relationship between overwork climate and innovation. Originality/value The study extends existing research on overwork and innovation by integrating individual cultural value orientations as boundary conditions of this relationship. These findings contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of overwork climate by showing that its association with academic innovation varies according to how individuals interpret organizational expectations based on their cultural values.

Dual therapeutic potential of plant-derived compounds: From glucose homeostasis to tumor inhibition
abstract: Plants are an abundant reservoir of bioactive compounds that play a vital role in disease prevention and promoting human health. Recent research highlights the therapeutic potential of plant-derived compounds in controlling chronic diseases, particularly metabolic and oncological disorders. Diverse groups of bioactive compounds, including polyphenols, alkaloids, phenolic terpenes, and polysaccharides, exhibit noteworthy anticancer, antioxidant, cytotoxic, hepatoprotective, cardioprotective, immunomodulatory, neuroprotective, and antidiabetic activities. The mechanisms of these bioactive compounds involve modulating insulin sensitivity, inhibiting α-glucosidase, activating AMPK and PPARγ, and suppressing oxidative stress and inflammatory signalling through their antioxidant potential. Moreover, these compounds also regulate various cell death pathways/apoptosis to reduce the probability of cancer cell survival in humans. Emerging evidence highlights mechanistic overlaps between diabetes and cancer, in which chronic hyperglycemia, oxidative stress, and inflammation converge, enabling plant-derived molecules to exert pleiotropic effects. Representative compounds such as trigonelline (TRG), diosgenin (DSG), quercetin, withaferin A, vinblastine, vincristine, carvacrol, eugenol, and many others demonstrate substantial potential as multi-target therapeutic agents. This review summariz…

Energy savings versus thermal comfort in existing Mediterranean office buildings: a case study assessing the effectiveness of low-impact retrofit strategies
abstract: Purpose Energy retrofit strategies based on non-invasive or minimally invasive measures are widely adopted in existing office buildings; however, their effectiveness is often assumed to be transferable across different climatic contexts. This study investigates energy savings and thermal comfort obtained by using commonly applied low-impact retrofit actions in existing Mediterranean office buildings. Design/methodology/approach A dynamic simulation model of an existing office building located in Southern Italy was developed to evaluate the impact of non-invasive retrofit measures, including indoor air temperature setpoint adjustments, daylight saving time strategies and the replacement of conventional boilers with air-to-water heat pumps. Energy performance was assessed in terms of heating, cooling and lighting demand, while thermal comfort was evaluated using Fanger theory. Findings The results show that setpoint adjustments provided the highest individual savings (up to 4.8%), followed by heat pump adoption (4.0%), while their combined application led to a maximum reduction of 7.7%. These savings seem limited since they refer to total annual primary energy consumption, but savings related to heating can reach up to 24–46%, while those related to cooling reach 18%. Moreover, a clear trade-off between energy savings and thermal comfort was identified, particularly during winter…

title: Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry–Derived Body Composition Asymmetry in Pain-Free Adults
abstract: Objective: To characterize body composition asymmetry in asymptomatic adults and examine its associations with age, lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (DD), and physical activity. Design: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans were performed, and lumbar DD grading, and physical activity levels were assessed in clinically asymptomatic adults in this cross-sectional study. Results: Fifty-one participants were included. Asymmetry in trunk fat and lean tissue mass was present in the overall cohort ( P <0.0001), and leg lean tissue mass also differed between sides ( P =0.0178), with right-sided predominance in older participants ( P =0.0094). Trunk lean AI (TLAI) was higher in older than younger participants (6.3±4.9 vs. 3.5±2.6; P =0.012), whereas the corresponding trunk fat AI (TFAI) difference was not statistically significant (8.0±5.9 vs. 5.0±3.6; P =0.085). Greater age was associated with TLAI ( P =0.008), while the trunk fat association was less robust in sensitivity analyses. Signed TFAI and TLAI shifted toward non-dominant-side predominance with greater age ( P <0.05). Lumbar DD and physical activity were not significantly associated with asymmetry. Conclusion: Body composition asymmetry was most evident in the trunk. Trunk lean asymmetry was greater at older ages, whereas the corresponding trunk fat association was weaker. Because functional outcomes were not assessed,…

title: Dispersion characteristics of SH waves in Piezo–viscoelastic structure with dual-uncoupled interface for energy harvesting
abstract: Purpose The transmission of shear-horizontal (SH) waves in piezoelectric–viscoelastic (PEV) composite media has gained great attention due to its potential usage in sensing technologies, energy harvesting and non-destructive evaluation. In this work, the impact of interfacial internal friction on the attenuation and dispersion properties of SH waves in a PEV composite structure is explored. Design/methodology/approach The interface between a viscoelastic (VE) half-space and a PEV layer is modeled using a dual-membrane arrangement made up of a PEV membrane and a VE membrane separated by a classical spring layer, which accounts for frictional energy dissipation at the interface. Analytical formulas are constructed to derive the governing dispersion relation of the coupled system. Findings Parametric studies are carried out to assess the impact of important material and interfacial factors, including density, elastic stiffness, dielectric constants, piezoelectric coefficients and interfacial friction, on wave dispersion and attenuation. Originality/value The results reveal that interfacial internal friction considerably alters wave propagation properties modifying phase velocity. These findings provide important insights for the design and optimization of PEV multilayer composites in wave-based sensing and energy harvesting applications.

title: Post-lithium energy storage selection for the extended sustainable supply chain: a conceptual AHP-based framework illustrated on the Moroccan logistics–energy nexus
abstract: Purpose The paper develops a conceptual framework for selecting post-lithium storage technologies across the heterogeneous nodes of the extended sustainable supply chain, treating strategic sovereignty as a decisional dimension alongside technical, economic and environmental criteria, and illustrates it on the Moroccan nexus. Design/methodology/approach A four-cluster, twelve-sub-criterion analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is instantiated on five alternatives. The instantiation is illustrative rather than survey-based: each pairwise matrix is generated deterministically from published benchmark values for the 2024–2026 window through a Saaty-capped ratio rule, making the demonstration reproducible. Consistency ratios, a ±20 per cent perturbation test and a prospective 2030–2035 re-parameterisation probe its stability. Findings At 2024–2026 benchmark values no technology dominates: the four leading priorities fall within a 0.034 band, and node re-weighting fragments the ranking into four dominant designs – lithium-ion for long-haul transport (0.226), redox flow for stationary storage (0.237), sodium-ion for micro-grids (0.235) and supercapacitor hybrids for intralogistics (0.275). Three hold across the whole perturbation envelope; long-haul is contested. Separately, under the illustrative 2030–2035 re-parameterisation, long-haul shifts toward sodium-ion and solid-state, which dem…

title: Interfacial engineering enables air-stable Li 5 FeO 4 prelithiation additives for long-life LiFePO 4 |graphite batteries
abstract: Abstract Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4, LFP)|graphite (Gr) full cells are widely used for large-scale energy storage because of their safety and long cycling stability. However, irreversible lithium consumption during solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation depletes the limited lithium inventory, causing initial capacity loss and compromising the full cell cycling stability. Lithium-rich lithium ferrite (Li5FeO4, LFO) is a promising cathode prelithiation additive for compensating lithium loss, but its poor air stability and moisture sensitivity restrict practical application. In this study, we introduce an interfacial TiO2 coating strategy to stabilize LFO by constructing a nanoscale protective layer on particle surfaces. The TiO2 coating preserves LFO’s antifluorite structure while suppressing surface degradation and improving electrode processing compatibility. The optimal 1.5% TiO2@LFO maintains structural integrity after 2-h air exposure and effectively mitigates slurry gelation. In LFP|Gr full cells, TiO2@LFO undergoes irreversible delithiation during the initial charge, compensating for SEI-related lithium consumption and increasing the initial discharge capacity from 160 to 175 mAh g−1. Moreover, TiO2@LFO enables stable cycling over 500 cycles at 1C, and LFP|Gr pouch-type cells achieve 60% capacity retention and can still power an LED lamp after 2000 cycles. This …

Beyond Digital Participation: Monitoring and Feedback in WhatsApp-Based Arabic Language Practice
abstract: Digital participation does not by itself establish the quality of Arabic language practice. This qualitative case study examines how digital monitoring and feedback support vacation-period Arabic video assignments at Raudlah al-Lughah al-‘Arabiyah (RLA) Annuqayah, East Java, with particular attention to WhatsApp. Data was collected through interviews with twelve informants (the RLA head, five administrators, and six members) together with observation and documentation. Analysis involved data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, meanwhile source and technique triangulation supported data credibility. The findings identify a connected workflow of assignment completion checks, documentation of WhatsApp Story views, video review, feedback, and recognition of members’ work. Within this workflow, submission records document participation, viewer counts document content reach, and video review provides a basis for feedback on language performance. The study provides a contextual account of digital monitoring and feedback in pesantren-based Arabic language practice rather than evidence of measured proficiency gains. Future research could develop explicit video-evaluation benchmarks and examine changes in speaking performance over time.

title: Open public data and household participation in risky financial markets
abstract: Abstract We study whether government-provided open public data (OPD) platforms alter how households participate in risky financial markets. Exploiting the staggered rollout of provincial OPD platforms across China and five waves of the China Household Finance Survey, we implement a difference-in-differences design to estimate the relationship between OPD access and household portfolio choices. We find that OPD availability is associated with an increase of about 2.5 percentage points in the probability that a household holds risky financial assets, relative to a baseline participation rate of 25%. Risky asset values and risky asset shares in financial wealth rise accordingly. Our mechanism estimates are consistent with three contributory channels: enhanced financial literacy, increased voluntary attention to financial news, and improved household wealth accumulation. The association between information access and financial literacy is stronger for households with more educated heads. Heterogeneity analyses yield larger estimated associations for male-headed households, high-educated individuals, and residents of more developed eastern provinces—a pattern consistent with the knowledge gap hypothesis, wherein early-stage information technology benefits accrue disproportionately to groups with stronger information-processing capacity. Overall, our evidence links public information…

title: Effects of Vacuum and Modified Atmosphere Packaging on Physicochemical and Microbiological Quality of Cooked Squid Stuffed with Sticky Rice During Refrigerated Storage
abstract: Stuffed squid with sticky rice (Tupa Sutong) is a traditional seafood product from southern Thailand with limited refrigerated shelf life because of rapid microbial spoilage and quality deterioration. This study evaluated the effects of atmospheric packaging (AP), vacuum packaging (VP), and modified atmosphere packaging (MAP; 50% O₂, 25% CO₂, and 25% N₂) on the physicochemical and microbiological quality of cooked stuffed squid during refrigerated storage (4 ± 2 °C) for 24 days. Changes in hardness, pH, total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), trimethylamine nitrogen (TMA-N), thiobarbituric acid (TBA), and total viable count (TVC) were determined throughout storage. Storage time significantly affected all quality parameters (p 0.05). Samples stored under AP deteriorated most rapidly, showing faster increases in TVB-N, TMA-N, TBA, and TVC, accompanied by a greater reduction in texture quality. Both VP and MAP delayed quality deterioration by slowing microbial growth and chemical changes during storage. Based on the microbiological acceptability limit, the shelf life of the product was 12, 18, and 21 days under AP, MAP, and VP, respectively. Among the packaging systems evaluated, VP provided the greatest extension of refrigerated shelf life while maintaining the physicochemical and microbiological quality of cooked stuffed squid with sticky rice. These findings provide useful infor…

title: Implementation of Early Warning System (EWS) Feature on Mobile Tower Battery in Realtime to Reduce Mobile Tower Downtime
abstract: Mobile tower network reliability at PT Antareja Mahada Makmur (AMM), Mifa Jobsite, was partially dependent on battery performance. However, the existing monitoring procedures relied on manual inspections, potentially delaying the detection of voltage drops, particularly during shift transitions. This study aimed to design, implement, and evaluate a real-time early warning system (EWS) for mobile tower batteries using an ESP32 microcontroller, applying the eight-step Quality Control Circle (QCC) methodology and the Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA) cycle. Operational records, field observations, team discussions, and cause-and-effect (fishbone) analysis were employed to identify the absence of automated battery monitoring and alert mechanisms as a primary operational issue. The developed system continuously monitored battery voltage and generated automatic notifications when voltage readings fell below 12 V in 12 V operating mode or 24 V in 24 V operating mode. Following implementation, monthly local area network (LAN) availability increased from 92.87% in January 2026 to 99.51% in April and remained at 99.49% in May 2026. Furthermore, no battery-related mobile tower downtime was recorded during the first week of April, compared with documented incidents during the corresponding period in January. These before-and-after findings indicated improvements in operational performance, although…

Indonesia and Australia Cooperation in the Development of the Electric Vehicle Ecosystem in 2023
abstract: Background: As the demand for electric vehicles increases globally, Indonesia one of the world's largest nickel producers has set its ambitions to expand its role in the global electric vehicle supply chain. To achieve its ambition, Indonesia signed a memorandum of understanding with Australia to develop an electric vehicle ecosystem in November 2023. The partnership with Australia is particularly interesting, given that Indonesia previously has established a strategic partnership with South Korea, which is known for its superiority in electric vehicle technology development. Objective: This study aims to identify the factors influencing Indonesia's decision to cooperate with Australia in developing the electric vehicle ecosystem. Result: Based on William D. Coplin's Decision-Making Theory, this study identifies three factors that drive Indonesia to cooperate with Australia in the development of the electric vehicle ecosystem: bureaucratic influence, Indonesia's economic ambition, and global political dynamics. These dynamics include the transition in battery materials from nickel to lithium, the enactment of the United States' Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), and strategic relationship between Australia–Indonesia. Conclusion: There is an overlap between domestic interests and the international context, leading to the agreement between Indonesia and Australia for the development …

The Sociocultural Profile of Puppet Theater Audiences as a Factor in Shaping Development Strategy
abstract: This study examines adult audiences for puppet theater, a group that remains largely on the periphery of existing research in theater sociology and cultural institution management and is rarely examined as a distinct and meaningful audience segment. As competition for urban residents’ attention intensifies, cultural institutions need to move beyond intuitive understandings of their audiences and systematically investigate audience expectations using rigorous research methods. This enables them to translate disparate impressions into a coherent analytical framework and make evidence-based management decisions. The study aims to explore potential audience members’ perceptions and expectations of adult-oriented puppet theater productions and to develop management recommendations for puppet theaters. The empirical data consist of in-depth interviews with participants from five target segments: IT and technical professionals, the creative class, humanities-oriented individuals, urban activists, and volunteers. The data were analyzed using qualitative methods. Puppet theater continues to be perceived by default as a form of entertainment primarily intended for children; however, the prospect of an adult-oriented repertoire generates sustained interest. Respondents expect productions to address complex social and psychological themes, avoid infantilizing approaches, and engage audienc…

abstract: Sektor peternakan melalui teknologi Inseminasi Buatan (IB) telah memberikan konstribusi positif terhadap pendapatan masyarakat di Kabupaten Luwu Timur yang diterapkan pada sapi potong Bali untuk menghasilkan Sapi Jenis Simental, Limosin, PO, Brangus, Madura dan Bali. Hasil Penelitian menjelaskan bahwa faktor eksternal dan internal (IFE-EFE) yang diperlukan adalah peningkatan pengetahuan, dukungan finansial, dan penguatan koordinasi untuk mengatasi hambatan serta memaksimalkan manfaat IB secara sosial dan ekonomi. Strategi pengembangan program IB sapi ternak di Kabupaten Luwu Timur menekankan pada optimalisasi sumber daya dan pemanfaatan teknologi. Strategi ini mencakup peningkatan keterampilan inseminator bersertifikat, pemanfaatan sarana dan bantuan pemerintah untuk mobilitas serta fasilitas kesehatan ternak, dan pengembangan teknologi modern dalam pengolahan pakan dan limbah. title: Agency-in-a-Box: Implications of Full-Stack Ai Agents for VCD Education Strategy
abstract: Rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has shifted from passive, single-prompt-based generative models toward autonomous AI agent ecosystems (agentic AI). "Agency-in-a-Box" phenomenon illustrates the capability of full-stack AI agents, utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) such Claude AI as workflow orchestrators via Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), analyze raw briefs, formulate visual strategies, and invoke external generative modules in an integrated manner. This potential disintermediation within the creative agency value chain poses serious challenges to Visual Communication Design (VCD) curricula that focus on technical instrument mastery. This qualitative research employs exploratory case study approach scenario study and curriculum gap analysis based, alongside structured interviews. Simulation result and interviews demonstrate that AI agents capable of accelerating brief synthesis and multimodal visual draft generation without significant conceptual degradation, critical human boundaries domain contextual empathy, local cultural semiotics, and ethical accountability. Result recommends reconstructing VCD curriculum based on: Meta-Design, Cultural Strategy, and Ethical AI Auditing.

title: Extreme winners, not special memes? No robust evidence of a meme-specific long-run reversal after the 2021 retail squeeze
abstract: Purpose To test whether the long-run reversal of the 2021 meme stocks reflects a meme-specific effect, or simply the reversal that follows any extreme short-run appreciation. The cohort is defined by realized event-window returns, not by any observed measure of social-media activity or retail order flow, so the study characterizes long-run return behavior and makes no causal claim about retail coordination. Design/methodology/approach In a long-horizon event study, we track 44 CRSP common stocks with event-window cumulative abnormal returns above 100% during the January 2021 squeeze through December 2025 (48- and 58-month horizons), via matched-firm buy-and-hold abnormal returns (BHAR) and calendar-time factor models. The primary test is a within-2021 regression of abnormal return on event-window CAR and a meme indicator, with a same-window benchmark, long-short portfolio, squeeze/attention proxies and a cross-decade placebo as robustness. Findings The cohort reverted sharply (median 48-month abnormal return −27.4%; 81.8% underperformed their matched controls). Its multi-year decline is consistent with that of the extreme winners used as comparison groups: the within-2021 meme-threshold coefficient is insignificant (−51 points, t = −1.76), the long-short five-factor-plus-momentum alpha is insignificant (−0.31% per month, t = −0.37) and neither short interest nor turnover predic…

title: Capital Structure, Asset Efficiency, and Firm Performance: The Moderating Role of Transfer Pricing in Indonesian Consumer Sector Firms
abstract: Background: Financing, asset use and affiliated transactions may be associated with accounting profitability, but their relationships can depend on measurement and model specification. Objective: This study examines capital structure and asset efficiency in relation to firm performance and tests interactions with foreign related-party sales intensity. Methods: The reported balanced panel covers 160 Indonesian consumer cyclical and non-cyclical firms in 2023–2024 (320 firm-year observations). ROA is related to debt-to-asset ratio, total asset turnover and foreign related-party sales/equity through moderated regression, controlling for size and liquidity. Pooled, fixed-effects and random-effects estimates are compared. Results: In pooled estimates, TATO is positive (β = 0.0379; reported White p < .0001), whereas DAR is not significant (β = 0.0012; p = .8701). The TATO interaction is positive (β = 0.0761; p = .0027); the DAR interaction is not significant (β = 0.0428; p = .5027). Adjusted R² is 0.4377. Under fixed effects, DAR is significant (β = 0.0774; p = .0092), whereas the TATO interaction is not (β = −0.0349; p = .7191). Conclusion: TATO is the most consistently significant predictor across the reported models. The interaction is estimator-sensitive and cannot establish transfer-pricing effects or mispricing. Accounting overlap, selection and unresolved within-firm dependenc…

title: ANALISIS TEKS DESKRIPSI MENGGUNAKAN MODEL PROBLEM BASED LEARNING BERBANTUAN MEDIA LAGU DI KELAS IX
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) berbantuan media lagu “Selalu Ada di Nadimu” dalam pembelajaran menulis teks deskripsi pada murid kelas IX A SMP Negeri 10 Kota Cirebon. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan subjek penelitian sebanyak 31 murid. Data penelitian diperoleh melalui observasi proses pembelajaran, analisis hasil tulisan murid, dan dokumentasi. Data dianalisis dengan mendeskripsikan pelaksanaan pembelajaran serta karakteristik teks deskripsi yang dihasilkan murid berdasarkan aspek isi, kerincian deskripsi, pilihan kata, penyusunan kalimat, dan ejaan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan lagu “Selalu Ada di Nadimu” menjadi stimulus bagi murid untuk mengenali perasaan, memahami pesan lagu, dan menghubungkannya dengan pengalaman pribadi bersama anggota keluarga. Pengalaman tersebut kemudian dikembangkan menjadi ide dan dituangkan dalam teks deskripsi yang menggambarkan karakteristik, sifat, kebiasaan, serta pengalaman bersama anggota keluarga. Penerapan model PBL memberikan alur pembelajaran yang mendorong murid mengeksplorasi ide, mengembangkan gagasan, dan menyusun teks secara terarah. title: Innovative Learning Media In Physical Education On The Level Of Enjoyment Of Elementary School Students In 3T Areas
abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of using innovative physical education learning media on the level of enjoyment of elementary school students in 3T areas. The background of this study stems from limited learning conditions, both in terms of facilities, infrastructure, and access to technology, so that innovative, simple, and contextual learning strategies are needed. The method used in this study was quantitative with a One Group Prestest-Posttest design. This study involved all twelve students, and data were collected through a 15 item enjoyment level questionnaire. The data were analyzed using the Shapiro-Wilk normality test and paired sample t-test. The results showed a significant increase in the enjoyment scores of students after the application of innovative media, with an increase in the average score from 28 to 47. The results of the paired sample t-test showed a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05), indicating that innovative media for physical education, health, and sports learning had a significant effect on increasing student enjoyment levels. These findings confirm that the use of innovative media in accordance with the characteristics of 3T areas is effective in creating a more interesting and enjoyable learning process for students.
venue: Journal of Physical Education and Sports

title: Legitimacy Boundaries in Crisis: Online Learning Adoption in Ultra-Orthodox Schools During COVID-19
abstract: Abstract The restrictions imposed on the citizens of Israel with the outbreak of COVID-19 forced educational institutions to adopt online channels for distance learning. The ultra-Orthodox society, bound by its suspicious and disapproving approach to the use of media, especially among teenagers and children, had to deal with the new circumstances and decide its course of action to resolve this conflict. The present study investigates whether, and to what extent, online channels were used in ultra-Orthodox educational institutions in their various subsections, and what were parents’ and teachers’ considerations, attitudes, and perceptions regarding the adoption of online learning in either COVID-19 or in any future similar emergencies. The article combines quantitative and qualitative methods based on a survey among a representative sample of parents of primary school-aged children (N=395) and semi-structured interviews (N=45) with parents and teachers in ultra-Orthodox schools. The results show that 14% of all parents in the sample use Zoom for distance learning. Furthermore, significant differences were found between the different sub-currents, with the Chabad stream being the most popular (94%), followed at a large margin by the Sephardic public (15%), Lithuanian (13%), and Hasidic (4%). Differences were also found between the sub-currents in terms of parents’ willingness to …

title: Language learning strategies as antecedents of academic self-concept and achievement: a longitudinal study of beginner CFL character learners
abstract: Abstract Using cross-sectional and cross-lagged panel models, this study examined the concurrent and prospective relationships among language learning strategies (LLSs), academic self-concept (ASC), and academic achievement among Vietnamese Chinese as a foreign language (CFL) beginners engaged in Chinese character writing (CCW). The initial static analyses supported a strategy-driven pathway (LLSs→ASC→Achievement). The longitudinal analyses further reinforced this pattern: initial LLS use positively predicted subsequent ASC and CCW achievement, whereas initial ASC predicted later CCW achievement but did not predict subsequent LLS use. These findings suggest that in persistent, cognitively demanding learning tasks such as CCW, LLS use is positively associated with subsequent ASC and CCW achievement. Moreover, ASC appeared to be more strongly associated with prior LLSs use than predictive of later LLSs use, consistent with self-perception theory. The study, therefore, underscores the importance of prioritizing strategy development to constructively build ASC during the early stages of complex foreign-language learning.
venue: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching

title: Pengaruh Model Pembelajaran Kooperatif Picture And Picture Terhadap Hasil Belajar Matematika Materi Bangun Datar Siswa Kelas II MIS Al-Khoirot Pematangsiantar
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh model pembelajaran kooperatif picture and picture terhadap hasil belajar matematika materi bangun datar siswa kelas II MIS Al-Khoirot Pematangsiantar. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis quasi eksperimen dan desain Non-Equivalent Control Group Design. Sampel penelitian terdiri dari kelas IIA sebagai kelas eksperimen dan kelas IIB sebagai kelas kontrol. Pengunpulan data dilakukan melalui pretest dan posttest. Analisis data menggunakan uji normalitas, homogenitas, Independent sample t-test, dan effect size Cohen’s d. hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata kelas eksperimen sebesar 62,5 dan kelas kontrol sebesar 62,916. Setelah perlakuan, rata-rata posttest kelas eksperimen sebesar 82,708, sedangkan kelas kontrol sebesar 70. Hasil uji hipotesis diperoleh thitung sebesar 3,887 > ttabel sebesar 2,012, sehingga Ha diterima dan Ho ditolak. Hasil effect size memperoleh nilai Cohen’s d sebesar 1,122 yang termasuk kategori besar. Dengan demikian, model pembelajaran kooperatif picture and picture berpengaruh signifikan dan kuat terhadap hasil belajar matematika siswa.

The Influence of Training and Development, Education and Learning, Performance Management, and Career Development on Nurses' Performance
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Training and Development, Education and Learning, Performance Management, and Career Development on nurse performance in the Hemodialysis Unit of Ratu Aji Putri Botung Regional Hospital, North Penajam Paser Regency. The study used a quantitative design with a survey approach, supplemented by qualitative data to obtain a comprehensive understanding. Quantitative data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire from the entire population of 31 nurses, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews and documentation studies. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive analysis and multiple linear regression to test the partial and simultaneous effects of independent variables on nurse performance. The results showed that partially, Training and Development, Education and Learning, and Career Development did not significantly influence nurse performance. Conversely, Performance Management significantly influenced nurse performance. However, simultaneously, all four human resource development variables significantly influenced nurse performance. These findings indicate that in standardized, high-risk clinical work units such as hemodialysis, an objective performance management system, regular evaluations, and consistent feedback are dominant factors in improving performance. Meanwhile, individual development…

title: 2C-LEARNING: INTEGRASI PEMBELAJARAN KREATIF DAN SOSIAL-EMOSIONAL DALAM MENGATASI PERUNDUNGAN ANAK
abstract: ABSTRACT Bullying among children highlights the importance of strengthening social-emotional competencies from an early age, particularly in recognizing bullying behavior, managing emotions, and developing positive relationships with peers. This community service program aimed to strengthen the social-emotional competencies of 15 children exhibiting bullying-related behaviors in Kampung Pelangi, Surabaya, through the Wandersea program, which integrates creative learning and social-emotional learning (SEL) based on the local wisdom values of Trisilas: silih asah (mutual learning), silih asih (mutual caring), and silih asuh (mutual guidance). Wandersea was implemented in collaboration with the Komunitas Pelajar Mengajar Surabaya using the 2C-Learning approach as its learning framework through six activities, including storytelling, role-playing, traditional games, crafts made from seashell waste, and parenting education for parents. Evaluation was conducted descriptively through in-depth interviews at the initial stage, an end-of-program reflection on the Wanderland game using 11 assessment items, and the Sea Hero Card. Analysis of four comparable items between the initial and final assessments using the exact McNemar test indicated an increase of 40.0–80.0 percentage points in expected responses. At the end of the program, all children were able to explain the meaning of bullyin…

title: ENGLISH LEARNING NEEDS, TEACHING PRACTICES, AND PHILIPPINE ESL PROGRAMS IN BEIJING: BASIS FOR TEACHER TRAINING DEVELOPMENT PLAN
abstract: English is a global language, but this is not the only reason why students in Beijing need it. Because of these needs, many families send their children to English training centers outside school. The study determined the English-learning needs of K–12 students in selected English tutoring and training centers in Beijing and assessed how these needs were addressed through existing teaching and learner-support practices. It also examined the respondents’ description of short-term English-learning programs in the Philippines as a means of providing opportunities for English practice and exposure to real-life communication. In addition, the study determined whether a significant relationship existed between students’ English-learning needs and their assessment of existing English teaching practices. The findings served as the basis for developing a Training Development Plan for Chinese English teachers and trainers in selected tutoring and training centers in Beijing. This study used needs analysis and institutional theory as the basis of its conceptual framework. This study also used a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, a methodological approach design to systematically describe the characteristics of a population while examining the statistical relationships that exist among variables without manipulating them. The study was conducted in selected tutoring an…

title: Explainable machine learning for predicting kidney disease progression defined by changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate in type 2 diabetes: a single-centre retrospective study
abstract: Background and objectives Routine clinical data may contain information on the future course of kidney disease in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study assessed the predictive performance and interpretability of seven machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to baseline measurements. Materials and methods This single-centre retrospective study included 382 patients with T2DM evaluated between January 2024 and December 2025. Progression was ascertained at a fixed three-month reassessment and defined according to KDIGO criteria as a decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) category with a fall of at least 25% from baseline or an increase in albuminuria category. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression selected 22 of 52 candidate predictors before repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation, and a sensitivity analysis repeated the selection within training folds. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) were used to interpret the models. Results Progression occurred in 162 patients (42.4%). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.682 for the radial-basis support vector machine (SVM) and 0.671 for LASSO logistic regression; when feature selection was repeated within training folds, the AUCs were 0.603 and 0.640, respectively. LASSO logistic regress…

Lower reward-based reinforcement learning underlying explore-exploit decision making in non-kleptomanic theft recidivists
abstract: Introduction Larceny imposes profound societal and economic burdens; however, punitive judicial measures frequently fail to deter recidivism. The neurobehavioral mechanisms driving habitual offending, whether instrumental or kleptomanic, in theft recidivists remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, we investigated explore-exploit decision-making and underlying reinforcement learning architectures in theft recidivists with a four-arm bandit task while prefrontal cortex (PFC) hemodynamics were continuously monitored using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Results Model-free behavioral analyses revealed that non-kleptomanic theft recidivists (NTR) accumulated significantly higher cumulative regret and made fewer optimal choices compared to control individuals without criminal records (CT), whereas results for the kleptomanic theft recidivists (KTR) remained inconclusive. Model-based analyses through Variational Bayesian Analysis identified Q-learning with decay model as the optimal computational fit. Parameter extraction using the model demonstrated that the NTR group exhibited a lower learning rate than CT and KTR groups, indicating a learning deficit in updating action values following environmental feedback. fNIRS tracking of trial-by-trial latent reinforcement variables revealed that while PFC activity was modulated by these variables, group differences we…

abstract: Мета. Здійснити комплексний теоретико-правовий аналіз поняття правової невизначеності та розкрити його зміст у понятійному апараті загальної теорії права. Методологічну основу дослідження становлять діалектичний метод, структурний і системний підходи, методи аналізу та синтезу, порівняльно-правовий, формально-юридичний та логіко-юридичний методи. Їх застосування дало змогу проаналізувати наукові підходи до розуміння правової невизначеності, виокремити її характерні риси, дослідити співвідношення з правовою визначеністю та сформулювати авторське визначення. Встановлено її характерні риси: об’єктивну зумовленість, багаторівневий характер, біполярність, динамічність та контекстну обумовленість. title: Uncertainty analysis of sphere parameter estimation from NMM-1 point cloud measurements
abstract: Abstract The reliable estimation of sphere parameters is important for precision metrology, calibration, and uncertainty evaluation. This study investigates the effects of the number of measurement points and the sampled region on the uncertainty of sphere parameter fitting using the least-squares (LS) method. Contact surface topography data of a high-precision bearing ball were acquired on the NMM-1 platform using two scanning strategies. Repeated subsampling was applied to evaluate the uncertainty of the fitted parameters under different sampling conditions. The results show that the fitting uncertainty depends not only on the number of measurement points, but also on the geometric coverage of the sampled region. Although increasing the number of points generally improves fitting stability, the gain becomes progressively smaller beyond a certain range. This study therefore provides an experimental basis for the design and selection of sampling strategies for reliable sphere parameter estimation under non-ideal measurement conditions.

Numerical Solution of Optimal Feedback Control for Finite Horizon Optimal Control Problem with Growth Condition
abstract: In this paper, we study approximation of optimal feedback control for the finite horizon optimal control problem with growth conditions for control systems and cost functionals. The optimal control problems with growth conditions are usually applied in practice. In reducing the boundedness for the dynamics function to the growth conditions, we have some difficulty in proving the convergence of the approximation scheme by the Euler scheme. First, we prove comparison principle of unbounded viscosity solution under the growth condition for the dynamics function and prove that the value function is the unique viscosity solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. We then construct a new approximation scheme using Euler implicit scheme for the finite horizon optimal control problem and prove that the approximation value function converges to the viscosity solution of the HJB equation as the discretization step goes to zero. Based on the approximations of the viscosity solution, we construct the optimal feedback controls for the corresponding discrete control systems. We consider an example to show the efficiency of the time-space approximation algorithm by the Euler implicit scheme through computational results.

Optimization of oil production rates under geomechanical stress constraints: a coupled reservoir–geomechanics approach using cascaded artificial neural network surrogates
abstract: Abstract Geomechanical constraints can limit oil production from deep carbonate reservoirs, because depletion raises the effective stress and, with it, the risk of compaction and rock failure. Enforcing such a limit inside a production optimizer is costly, since every candidate rate schedule produces its own pore-pressure field and one coupled reservoir–geomechanical simulation takes about 3 h. This study develops a cascaded artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate to maximize oil production from the MB21 unit of the Mishrif Formation, Buzurgan Oil Field, while keeping the effective mean stress below 11,200 psi. A Pressure ANN predicts the pore-pressure field from the well rates and geomechanical inputs, and a Stress ANN converts the predicted field into effective mean stress. Unlike single-network stress surrogates, which need pore pressure as a known input, the cascade evaluates the stress constraint for the depletion that each proposed rate schedule would itself cause. The networks were trained on 2,446 high-fidelity CMG-GEM coupled simulations and coupled with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to allocate the rates of 18 producers. On independent test scenarios, the Pressure and Stress ANNs reached coefficients of determination of 0.95 and 0.94. PSO produced 42,799.02 bbl/day against 42,592.96 bbl/day for GA (+ 206.06 bbl/day, 0.48%) and reache…

title: Smart Kitchen Counter Innovation for Elderly Users Based on Quality Function Deployment and Internet of Things System
abstract: This study aims to design and develop a kitchen counter product for elderly users by applying the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) technique to address user requirements. The study began with a survey of elderly users’ needs, including design, facilities, usability, product quality, and materials. The collected data was analyzed using the QFD product planning matrix and the design deployment matrix to translate customer requirements into technical design specifications. The results indicated that the participants reported a mean perceived satisfaction score of 4.42 out of 5.00 after observing a demonstration of the prototype and its functions in an actual kitchen environment. The five product attributes with the highest satisfaction scores were lighting within overhead cabinet storage compartments, operational safety, ease of maintenance, structural strength, and electrical outlet safety systems, with mean scores of 4.62, 4.57, 4.56, 4.54, and 4.53, respectively. These findings demonstrate that Quality Function Deployment (QFD) is an effective approach for translating user requirements into product design, particularly in the development of kitchen counter products for elderly users. The resulting design was perceived as having the potential to improve safety and convenience for elderly users during kitchen activities. However, further hands-on usability and long-term field te…

title: MULTI-ACTOR SUPPORT SYSTEM SHAPING UNIVERSITY STUDENT ENTREPRENEURSHIP – A CASE STUDY AT HANOI OPEN UNIVERSITY
abstract: This study investigates how the Multi-Actor Support System (MASS) affects university students’ entrepreneurial skills, motivation, intention, and actions. Using survey data from 2,271 students and a PLS-SEM model, the results show that business and mentor support primarily enhances entrepreneurial self-efficacy. In contrast, support from universities, media, and financial resources tends to boost entrepreneurial motivation. The strong connection between motivation, intention, and behavior shows that motivation is crucial for translating support resources into entrepreneurial activity. The research broadens the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) framework by adding insights from human capital and the university entrepreneurial ecosystem. It also highlights the need for coordinated stakeholder efforts to improve the effectiveness of student entrepreneurship support in Vietnam.

title: FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION IN THE PROCESS OF CONVERGENCE OF THE LEGAL SYSTEM OF UKRAINE WITH THE EU ACQUIS: EUROPEAN STANDARDS, ECTHR PRACTICE AND CHALLENGES OF THE DIGITAL AGE
abstract: Purpose. The purpose of the study is to provide a comprehensive analysis of European standards for protecting freedom of expression in the context of the convergence of Ukraine’s legal system with the European Union acquis. The study also examines the case law of the European Court of Human Rights concerning the exercise of the right to freedom of expression in the digital environment and identifies the main challenges and prospects for improving Ukrainian legislation in the context of digital transformation and European integration. To achieve this purpose, the study pursues the following objectives: to analyse contemporary approaches adopted by the European Court of Human Rights to the interpretation of Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights and to systematise its case law concerning freedom of expression in the digital environment; and to identify the specific features of the convergence of Ukraine’s legal system with the EU acquis in the field of freedom of expression and the implementation of European standards. Methods. The methodological basis of the study is a comprehensive interdisciplinary approach to freedom of expression as a fundamental human right undergoing transformation under the influence of the digitalisation of social relations and Ukraine’s European legal integration. The research draws on human rights theory, constitutional law, European Uni…

title: Effectiveness of Integrated Neuromuscular Inhibition Technique Compared with Local Vibration Therapy on Iliotibial Band Tightness as an Adjunct in the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis
abstract: Abstract Background: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative disorder of synovial joints, leading to knee pain, stiffness, reduced mobility, and impaired quality of life. Iliotibial band (ITB) tightness and associated myofascial pain may further aggravate symptoms in individuals with knee OA. Conventional physiotherapy commonly includes stretching and strengthening exercises. Local vibration therapy (LVT) facilitates muscle relaxation, enhances circulation, and reduces soft-tissue tension through the tonic vibration reflex. Integrated neuromuscular inhibition technique (INIT), which combines ischemic compression, positional release, and muscle energy techniques, has been shown to deactivate trigger points and reduce muscle tightness. However, limited evidence exists comparing the effectiveness of LVT and INIT for managing ITB tightness in individuals with knee OA. Objectives: To compare the effectiveness of INIT and LVT on ITB tightness in individuals with knee OA. Materials and Methods: Forty-six participants aged 50–70 years with knee OA and ITB tightness were recruited and were randomly assigned to the LVT (Group A) and INIT (Group B). Outcome measures included Ober’s test, the visual analog scale (VAS), the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC). Assessments were conducted before and after the interven…
