title: A physically integrated GNN surrogate for microbially-mediated kinetic reactive transport: PHYGNET
abstract: Reactive transport modelling (RTM) is essential for subsurface environmental management but is fundamentally constrained by traditional geochemical solvers. These solvers incur prohibitive computational costs and frequently suffer from numerical instabilities such as convergence failures, particularly in microbially-mediated kinetic reaction systems. While machine learning surrogates offer acceleration, they often lack physical consistency when dealing with stiff biogeochemical dynamics. Here we propose PHYGNET (Physically GNN Network), which maps microbial reaction networks into a directed graph by representing species and reactions as nodes and edges. It embeds Monod-type kinetics within a differentiable physics layer that enforces stoichiometric mass conservation and thermodynamic hierarchies, and incorporates a residual corrector that refines the final outputs at the cost of small deviations from exact mass balance. By successfully coupling with COMSOL, PHYGNET demonstrates the capability to execute full reactive transport simulations. Benchmark tests reveal that, in contrast to the severe super-linear time penalties faced by traditional solvers at engineering scales, PHYGNET maintains stable sub-linear scaling via tensor parallelism. At a scale of 10 5 grid nodes, PHYGNET achieved an acceleration (up to 3588-fold) without numerical crashes. Furthermore, its escalating spee…

title: Harmonious and obsessive passion, cultural identity, and mental health in Chinese students of traditional versus Western music: a national multi-institutional comparison
abstract: Background University music students carry an elevated burden of depression, anxiety, and performance-related distress, yet the motivational processes separating adaptive from maladaptive engagement remain only partly understood, and little is known about how they differ between the traditional Chinese and Western training tracks that coexist in Chinese tertiary music education. Drawing on the dualistic model of passion, we compared the two tracks on passion, cultural identity, and mental health, and tested identity as mediator of the track differences and as buffer of the obsessive passion-distress link. Methods A cross-sectional online survey recruited full-time music majors from 32 institutions across seven regions of China. After attention-check exclusions, 546 students remained (266 traditional, 280 Western; 59.3% women; M age = 20.63 years, SD = 1.33). Participants completed the Passion Scale, an adapted Multigroup Ethnic Identity Measure referencing Chinese cultural heritage, the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21, the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-being Scale, and a brief music performance anxiety scale. Group differences, moderated regression, and bootstrap mediation analyses were estimated. How Resilient Green Logistics drives Sustainable Environmental Outcomes: the multi-mediating role of governance, leadership and work ethos
abstract: Purpose This study looks at how Resilient Green Logistics (RGL) affects Sustainable Environmental Outcomes (SEO) in the Indian dairy sector. It focuses on the roles of Sustainability-Driven Governance (SDG), Eco-Transformative Leadership (ETL) and Pro-Environmental Work Ethos (PWE) as mediators. The research also aims to show how governance, leadership and employee behavior collectively contribute to environmental sustainability in dairy supply chains. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey design was adopted, covering 189 registered dairy companies across Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab and New Delhi. Purposive sampling targeted key supply chain professionals, including senior managers, logistics/supply chain managers and sustainability/environment officers. Of 567 targeted respondents, 407 provided valid responses. The data were analyzed using SmartPLS-SEM 4.1 to examine the proposed relationships. Findings The analysis strongly indicated that RGL directly improves environmental outcomes through business and behavioral mechanisms in the dairy sector's supply chain. Furthermore, the mediating roles of SDG, PWE and ETL have been established, and these mediators strengthen the relationship between RGL and SEO. Among the above-defined mediators, SDG emerged as the strongest, followed by PWE and ETL. Practical implications Adopting and implementing sustainable logistics …

title: Mapping a Quarter-Century of Forensic Nursing Research: A Multi-Database Bibliometric and Science-Mapping Analysis (2000–2025)
abstract: Background Forensic nursing spans interpersonal violence, correctional and forensic mental health, and death investigation, yet its research base has been mapped only in fragments. Aims To map the indexed literature of forensic nursing published between 2000 and 2025, and to identify where its evidence base is thinnest. Methods Performance analysis and science mapping of 1,221 documents (2000–2025), retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science by a 30-term topic query within three defined journal sets, analyzed in bibliometrix. Results Output grew 7.66% annually; one journal carried 47.8% of documents. The United States led production (51.0% of resolvable corresponding addresses) but was the least internationally connected major producer (3.3%), against 9.2% overall. Interpersonal violence dominated the indexed vocabulary; trafficking, exploitation and forensic mental health were concentrated in recent years. Global and local citations identified different documents. Discussion The literature is concentrated in one journal and four countries. Whether its dominant topics define the specialty or reflect uneven research infrastructure cannot be settled bibliometrically; the distribution shows where capacity is thinnest.

Dynamic capabilities perspective on successful technology commercialization: a meta-analysis
abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms' dynamic capabilities shape firm performance in technology commercialization contexts, focusing on the interplay between higher-order dynamic capabilities (sensing, seizing, and reconfiguration) and lower-order dynamic capabilities (technological and marketing capabilities). Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 54 independent samples (N = 16,099), this meta-analysis develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework examining the direct and indirect effects of dynamic capabilities on firm performance, as well as the moderating role of country development. Findings The findings show that sensing and seizing indirectly influence firm performance through technological and marketing capabilities, whereas reconfiguration has both direct and indirect effects on firm performance. Furthermore, country development moderates the relationships between sensing and seizing and technological and marketing capabilities. Originality/value This study advances understanding of dynamic capabilities in technology commercialization by distinguishing the roles of higher- and lower-order capabilities in shaping firm performance. It demonstrates how higher-order dynamic capabilities contribute to performance through technological and marketing capabilities and identifies country development as a boundary condition for these relationships.

title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem and Female Entrepreneurial Growth: Thematic Analysis
abstract: This study evaluates the influence of the entrepreneurial ecosystem on female entrepreneurial growth. Female entrepreneurs face restricted access to finance, growth-oriented capital, venture capital, and business angel funding. These impede the ability of female entrepreneurs to scale up and innovate. The thematic analysis methodology involving the use of juried textual data, from scientific literature was applied to analyze the entrepreneurial ecosystem and female entrepreneurial growth. Findings were extracted using the qualitative analysis of both theoretical and empirical literature in line with the main objectives of this study. The research revealed that female entrepreneurial outcomes are not exclusively based on individual traits. Instead, female entrepreneurial growth reflects the nature of its entrepreneurial ecosystems as it relates to institutional logic and structure, governance, financial networks, dominant values, and social capital within entrepreneurial ecosystems. The entrepreneurial ecosystem is structured and operates in a manner that logically constrains female entrepreneurial growth opportunities. The study recommends that financial institutions within the entrepreneurial ecosystem should deliberately tailor themselves appropriately with the necessary financial tools to assist in the growth of female entrepreneurs. title: The Structure and Evolution of China’s Green Finance Policy Instruments
abstract: China’s green finance policy system consists of many separate measures, and most studies examine them one at a time. This paper describes the system as a whole. It asks which instruments the system contains and how their relative weight changed between the 2016 Guiding Opinions on Building a Green Financial System and 2025. The instruments are grouped into five categories: green credit, green bonds, green insurance, green funds and carbon finance. The description rests on three public sources: green loan statistics from the People’s Bank of China, green bond issuance data from the Climate Bonds Initiative, and the text of the policy documents. Green loans grew faster than total loans over the period, and their share of total loans rose from 6.7% at end-2020 to 16.2% at end-2025. Green bond issuance peaked in 2022 within the period covered and was about 18% lower in 2024 than in 2023. Both patterns need to be read with care, because the green loan statistics were redefined in 2025 and the bond figures come from report editions with different database cut-off dates. Read together with the policy documents, the evidence suggests that direct financial support has been joined by project standards, institutional assessment and risk management requirements. Government direction, market development and risk control are used here as three organising ideas for interpreting that combinati…

title: COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF THE FINANCIAL EFFICIENCY OF TOURISM INVESTMENTS IN AZERBAIJAN
abstract: The study assesses how fixed-capital investment in tourism-characteristic industries in Azerbaijan is transformed into value added and identifies mechanisms for improving the performance of tourism finance. Official annual data for 2014-2024 are analysed using dynamic and comparative methods, investment intensity, a conditional financial-efficiency ratio, a post-pandemic recovery index, compound annual growth, coefficients of variation, and current and one-year-lagged Pearson correlations. Value added increased 2.48 times to AZN 5,973.8 million, while the sector’s share of GDP reached 4.7 per cent. Investment flows were substantially more volatile than value added. For 2016-2024, the correlation between investment and value added was 0.67; with a one-year lag, it was 0.63, indicating that investment outcomes emerge over time. The scientific contribution is an integrated framework combining current financial flows, value added, volatility, time lags and recovery from external shocks. The study recommends performance-based financing, regional project portfolios, a digital investment registry, risk-adjusted financial instruments, public-private partnerships and systematic post-investment monitoring.

title: Contextualizing True Knowledge: Oral Transmission in Balinese Tembang and Hindustani Classical Vocal Traditions
abstract: In classical and traditional vocal music, oral tradition remains a vital epistemology where knowledge is transmitted through direct interaction between teacher and student rather than through written notation. Hindustani classical vocal and Balinese tembang represent this paradigm, where knowledge is understood and sustained through oral transmission within the guru-shishya, or teacher-disciple, relationship. This study aims to understand how oral transmission shapes the meaning of "true knowledge" within the vocal pedagogy of Hindustani classical and Balinese tembang traditions, and how this knowledge is inseparable from the context in which it is taught and practiced. This study uses a qualitative literature-based approach to explore how oral transmission influences teaching, memory, and understanding in Hindustani classical and Balinese tembang vocal traditions. In both traditions, musical knowledge is not simply transferred but developed gradually through imitation, attentive listening, and a trusting relationship between teacher and student. Hence, oral transmission does not merely transmit musical information; it cultivates embodied musical knowledge. This study suggests that sustaining oral vocal traditions requires attention not only to the songs themselves, but also to the relationships and contexts through which musical knowledge continues to be taught, understood, an…

title: From knowledge transmission to competency formation: pedagogical innovation in investigative studies education
abstract: Purpose Competency-oriented reform is a central priority in higher vocational education. This study examines the direct association between pedagogical leadership commitment (PLC) and staff-reported student competency formation (SCF), the mediating role of practice-oriented learning culture (POLC) and the moderating effect of PLC on the POLC–SCF relationship. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to teaching staff and programme leaders involved in the education of investigative studies at higher vocational institutions in China. A total of 312 valid responses were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with WarpPLS to test the proposed direct, mediating and moderating relationships. Findings PLC was positively associated with SCF and strongly associated with POLC. POLC was positively associated with SCF and partially mediated the relationship between PLC and SCF. In addition, PLC significantly moderated the relationship between POLC and SCF. The model showed moderate explanatory power for both POLC and SCF. Practical implications The findings suggest that higher vocational institutions should strengthen leadership support for practice-oriented pedagogy by aligning resource allocation, professional development and curriculum implementation w…

title: Equity Research and Fundamental Analysis of Reliance Industries Limited: Financial Performance, DCF Valuation and Portfolio Relevance for the ABSLI Maximizer ULIP Fund
abstract: The study evaluates Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) using fundamental equity-research techniques and examines the relevance of the company as a core blue-chip holding in the ABSLI Maximizer ULIP Fund. The research problem arises from the need to assess a diversified conglomerate whose businesses differ materially in growth drivers, capital intensity, risk and cash-flow characteristics. Four objectives were addressed: analysis of five-year financial performance and ratios; construction of an FCFF-based DCF valuation; assessment of RIL’s strategic portfolio relevance; and application of practical wealth-management workflows such as goal discovery, risk profiling and consultative product communication. The study uses a descriptive and analytical research design, a purposive single-company case-study approach, and secondary data from RIL financial statements, investor disclosures, regulatory sources and financial databases. Analysis covers FY2022–FY2026, with DCF projections through FY2031. Results show revenue CAGR of approximately 10.6%, PAT CAGR of about 9.0%, OCF CAGR of about 14.8%, improving ROE and ROCE, moderate leverage and strong cash generation. The base-case DCF estimates intrinsic value at about ₹1,080 per share versus an assumed market price of ₹1,275.90, implying approximately 15.3% downside. The study therefore concludes that RIL has strong fundamentals but requir…

title: Echocardiography-led multimodal assessment for pulmonary hypertension in a right heart catheterization-referred cohort: incremental value of ECG and natriuretic peptides
Financial risk and health insurance utilization among older adults in an urban informal settlement in Pune, India: a prospective community-based study
abstract: Background Older adults living in urban informal settlements are vulnerable to financial hardship because of chronic morbidity, repeated healthcare visits, and financial dependence. Longitudinal evidence on healthcare expenditure and financial risk protection in this group remains limited. This study assessed health insurance utilization, out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE), catastrophic health expenditure (CHE), and associated factors among older adults in one urban informal settlement. Methods A community-based longitudinal study was conducted among 116 older adults aged ≥60 years residing in urban informal settlements under an Urban Health Training Center of a medical college in Western India. Participants were followed for 1 year (June 2024 to May 2025) with quarterly assessments. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, morbidity, healthcare utilization, health insurance utilization, and healthcare expenditure were collected using a pre-tested questionnaire and expenditure recording sheets. CHE was defined as OOPE exceeding 10% of household income. Associations were assessed using chi-square, Mann–Whitney U, Friedman and Cochran’s Q tests (pairwise comparisons were Holm-adjusted), modified Poisson regression, multiple classification analysis, and concentration indices. Results Among 116 participants, 70.69% were female, 58.62% lived in joint families, and 64.66% were financi…

title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN RIGHT ATRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND PROGRESSION OF RIGHT HEART FAILURE IN PULMONARY HYPERTENSION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS AND PRIMARY STUDIES
abstract: Introduction: Survival in pulmonary hypertension (PH) is determined by the capacity of the right ventricle (RV) to adapt to a chronically increased afterload, and the right atrium (RA) is the chamber that buffers RV filling during this transition. Phasic RA function can now be quantified with speckle-tracking echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance feature tracking (CMR-FT), but individual cohorts are small and use heterogeneous metrics, units and endpoints. We aimed to quantify the association between RA dysfunction and progression of right heart failure in PH, to characterise RA dysfunction relative to healthy controls and to determinants of RV failure, and to evaluate whether RA function is modifiable by afterload-reducing therapy. Methods: This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov and Semantic Scholar were searched from January 2011 to 3 November 2026, complemented by citation searching. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), comparative studies, cohort studies and case series were eligible. Hazard ratios (HRs) were harmonised to a 1% absolute decrease in RA reservoir strain and pooled with DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models, with Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman (HKSJ) intervals and 95% prediction intervals. Mean differences (MD), standardised mean differ…
venue: The Indonesian Journal of General Medicine

title: BUDGET PLANNING, ORGANIZATION SIZE AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF THE TOP 100 SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN KENYA
abstract: Budget planning is widely promoted as a foundation of sound financial management in small and medium enterprises (SMEs), yet the strength of its payoff may depend on the scale at which an enterprise operates. This study examined the effect of budget planning on the financial performance of the top 100 SMEs in Kenya and determined the moderating effect of organization size on this relationship. The study was anchored on Incremental Budgeting Theory and Activity-Based Costing Theory and adopted a descriptive research design. A census of the 100 SMEs on the Ministry of Trade 2021/2022 list was attempted, with the Chief Accounting Officer of each firm as the respondent. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale, and 83 questionnaires were returned (83.0% response rate). The instrument was reliable in a pilot study (Cronbach’s alpha: budget planning 0.810, organization size 0.731, financial performance 0.713). Data were analysed in SPSS using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and regression with an interaction term. Budget planning was moderately practised (mean = 2.81, SD = 1.054), with strong strategic alignment and budget reviews but weak forecasting accuracy, departmental participation and contingency planning (means below 2.00). Financial performance was moderate (mean = 2.90). Budget planning correlated positively with financia…

title: Climate reporting in public sector organisations: identity construction and changes
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to explore climate change reporting by public sector organisations. In particular, the analysis draws attention to how public sector organisations represent themselves through climate reporting practice to construct and reproduce their identities over time. Design/methodology/approach A comprehensive content analysis of 164 annual and stand-alone sustainability reports produced by 15 public sector organisations listed on the Australian National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting register over an 11-year period from 2014 to 2024 was used for this study. The analysis is informed by Tregidga et al.'s (2014) identity framework of sustainable organisations. Findings The analysis reveals an unbalanced pattern of identity construction in public sector climate reporting, characterised by a strong focus on compliance-oriented reporting, followed by reporting on climate leadership and limited engagement with strategically “good” practices associated with legitimacy seeking. Despite evidence of more substantive climate reporting, disclosures continue to focus predominantly on metrics and statistics reflecting regulatory and policy expectations. The longitudinal analysis reinforces this identity structure, although their climate reporting has developed into a more complex communicative space through which public sector organisations simultaneously constr…

title: Right versus left donor hepatectomy in living donor liver transplantation
Impact of built environment in mountainous aging communities on spatiotemporal behavioural differentiation among older persons: a geospatial analysis
abstract: As demographic aging deepens, the conflict between efficiency of public space resource allocation in mountainous communities and the diverse needs of older persons becomes more prominent. Understanding the adaptability between space and behaviour is crucial for identifying the built environment characteristics associated with the older persons’ outdoor activities for targeted environmental interventions. This study focuses on 42 public spaces in Chongqing, a typical mountainous city in China. From the perspectives of spatial layout and design, it establishes a connection between the public space environment and the characteristics of the older persons’ outdoor activities. Spatial clustering is used to explore the spatiotemporal aggregation of the older persons’ activities, and multiple linear regression models are employed to quantify the associations between environmental factors and the older persons’ behaviours. The results aim to match spatial environments with the activity requirements of older persons, providing evidence for optimising age-friendly built environment upgrades.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Urban Design and Planning

title: TPACK Readiness, Innovative Learning Design, and Digital Entrepreneurship Skills among Indonesian Business Education Students
abstract: Background: Digital entrepreneurship skills are increasingly important for business graduates, but evidence remains limited on how technology-integrated pedagogy is associated with their development. Objective: This study examined the structural associations among TPACK readiness, Innovative Learning Design, and the latent construct Digital Entrepreneurship Skills, including whether Innovative Learning Design carried a significant indirect association. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling. Of 119 responses, two cases met the prespecified extreme-score rule and were excluded, producing an analytic sample of 117 students. Nineteen dimension-level indicators represented the three constructs. Results: The retained measurement model produced standardized loadings of 0.459-0.812 and composite reliability of 0.738-0.863. Model fit improved after two theoretically justified within-construct residual correlations but remained below conventional benchmarks: chi-square (114) = 308.66, p < 0.001; CFI = 0.808; TLI = 0.771; and RMSEA = 0.121. The three direct paths were significant: TPACK-Innovative Learning Design (beta = 0.861, p < 0.001), Innovative Learning Design-Digital Entrepreneurship Skills (beta = 0.451, p = 0.044), and TPACK-Digital Entrepreneurship Skills (beta = 0.464, p = 0.048). The indirect effect was not significa…

title: A compact integrated platform for real-time live-cell imaging and photodynamic therapy: design and experimental demonstration
Visual Question and Answer Educational Game Design for Natural and Social Sciences Learning
abstract: Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) learning in elementary schools is still dominated by lectures, which makes it difficult for students to understand abstract concepts. This study aims to design an educational game based on Visual Question and Answer (VQA) as an IPAS learning medium for fourth-grade students at UPT SD Negeri Papungan 02 and to determine its feasibility. The study employed Research and Development (R&D) with the Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) model consisting of six stages: concept, design, material collecting, assembly, testing, and distribution. The game was built with the HTML5-based Construct 2 engine and integrated with an Express.js backend connected to the Google Gemini API to generate adaptive exam questions based on students' practice scores. Feasibility was measured through black box testing, media expert validation, material expert validation, and a student response questionnaire. The results show that all 22 black box scenarios were successful, and the feasibility percentages were 87% from the media experts, 100% from the material expert, and 91.43% from the student responses, all in the very feasible category. The VQA educational game is feasible as an IPAS learning medium. Future work should add more learning materials, audio narration, and an offline version.

title: Advances in conductive polymer-based composites: Structural design, fabrication strategies, and biomedical applications
Sol-gel based design of lead-free yttrium-doped barium titanate nanocomposites for advanced functional materials
abstract: Abstract Nano-structured pure BaTiO 3 (B-T) and BaTiO 3 doped with different concentrations of yttrium ranging from 1 to 10 mol.%, coded as [BYT-x (x = 0–10)], were prepared using a modified sol-gel process. The study utilized X-ray diffraction (XRD) to illustrate the tetragonal structure of the perovskite BaTiO 3 . The persistence of the tetragonal phase was further verified using a mathematical derivative-based investigation. High resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) were used to examine the morphology of the doped samples. The results indicated that the crystallite size estimated using XRD ranged from 23.36 to 37.84 nm. Two complementary precision impedance measuring instruments were used to properly assess the dielectric characteristics across a wide frequency range (42 Hz to 1 GHz), guaranteeing good measuring accuracy across various regimes. Dielectric characterization of the yttrium-doped BaTiO 3 over such an extended frequency range remains scarcely reported. The dielectric measurements were carried out using a 3532-50 LCR Hi-TESTER and a network impedance analyzer (KEYSIGHT-E4991B), respectively. The pure sample (BYT-0) exhibited a significant permittivity ( ~ 770) and a tangent loss ( ~ 0.076), whereas the doped sample (BYT-9) showed a reduced permittivity (ε′ ~ 95) along with a significantly lower…
venue: Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology

title: In Search of Identity: Rethinking Balinese Product Design through Cultural History
abstract: Balinese product design is often recognized through visual signs such as ornament, material, craft technique, and references to tradition. Yet these signs do not fully explain how a design identity is formed or maintained. This paper revisits the history of Balinese product design through a cultural-historical perspective to examine identity as a process rather than a fixed style. Using literature, historical documents, manuscripts, colonial records, and visual documentation, the study traces recurring relations among local knowledge, patronage, external influence, tourism, and professional design practice. The findings suggest that Balinese design identity has developed through continuity and adaptation: new functions, materials, technologies, and markets have been incorporated without entirely displacing established systems of making and cultural reference. Balinese product design is therefore better understood as a historically negotiated design tradition than as a stable collection of visual attributes.

title: From Transit Space to Third Space: A Critical Regionalist Study of Bus Stop Design in Bali
abstract: Bali has experienced a significant increase in the use of public transportation in recent years. Public transportation systems require supporting infrastructure that functions as transit spaces for users transferring between modes of transportation. Bus stops are understood as transportation infrastructure that serves as temporary transit and waiting spaces. In Bali, bus stops exhibit diverse forms and design characteristics that extend beyond their primary function as transit infrastructure and have the potential to generate varied spatial experiences for users. This study aims to analyze the diversity of forms and design characteristics of bus stops in Bali and to identify their potential as third spaces through the perspective of Critical Regionalism. The study employs a qualitative approach using field observations, visual documentation, interviews with the Dinas Perhubungan Provinsi Bali and document analysis. The collected data are analyzed through three main stages: data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings are expected to demonstrate that the diversity of bus stop designs not only produces variations in architectural form but also contributes to different spatial experiences for users. Bus stops are therefore not merely regarded as transit facilities but also as public spaces capable of fostering aesthetic and social experien…

title: Cost reductions in total hip arthroplasty after DRG payment reform and volume-based procurement in China: a difference-in-differences study
abstract: Background: Between 2021 and 2022, China's health system reforms deployed two overlapping cost-containment instruments in quick succession: diagnosis-related group (DRG) bundled payment and a nationalized volume-based procurement (VBP) programme that cut orthopedic implant prices by 70%−90%. Disentangling their independent contributions to hospitalization costs is both methodologically challenging and policy-critical. We examined whether the January 2021 DRG roll-out in Wenzhou was associated with a differential change in total hip arthroplasty (THA) costs and adverse discharge outcomes across insurance groups, and whether the observed cost reductions are consistent with a larger contribution from either reform. Methods We analyzed 2,518 consecutive THA admissions at a tertiary hospital in Wenzhou (2015–2025). Patients were classified as Social Insurance (NRCMS, URBMI, and UEBMI; n = 2,046) or Other Payment (self-pay, full public-service, miscellaneous; n = 472). A difference-in-differences (DID) framework with year fixed effects and HC3-robust standard errors estimated the group-specific cost change associated with the reform. An event-study design assessed pre-reform parallel trends and traced the year-by-year trajectory of any post-reform divergence. Five sensitivity analyses varied the reform window (excluding 2020–2021, excluding 2021 alone, and a DRG-only window before th…

title: Does comprehensive public hospital reform influence the healthcare costs of inpatients with pulmonary tuberculosis? An interrupted time series analysis in western China
Does environmental judicial reform influence audit fees? Evidence from China's environmental public interest litigation
abstract: Purpose A careful study of the impact of the environmental public interest litigation (EPIL) pilot policy on audit fees would not only make the economic costs of judicial innovation in environmental governance but also the study would make a strong empirical statement about improving the environmental practices of the business community and audit policies. Design/methodology/approach We are working with a quasi-natural experiment in China based on its EPIL pilot program and we apply a difference-in-differences framework. Findings We find that firms in pilot regions pay 4.7% higher audit fees than non-pilot peers, a result robust to parallel-trend checks, placebo tests, propensity score matching and controls for concurrent policies. Mechanism evidence indicates that the EPIL pilot policy elevates auditors' perceived litigation and regulatory risk, leading to higher risk premia in pricing without commensurate increases in engagement hours. Effects are stronger for firms with weaker ESG, greater information asymmetry, higher auditor specialization, lower auditor workload pressure, or strong regional environmental policy enforcement. Further analysis shows that the increase in audit fees associated with the EPIL pilot policy does not lead to an improvement in audit quality. Originality/value (1) Incorporating bottom-up judicial environmental regulation (EPIL) into audit pricing fra…

title: Autocallable ETFs and the Evolution of ETF Market Design: Contractual Architecture, Renewal, and Market Organization
abstract: Autocallable exchange-traded funds provide a setting for examining how the ETF wrapper changes the organization and delivery of structured, state-contingent payoffs. These funds place barrier-based and path-dependent exposures inside a continuing exchange-traded vehicle while the underlying contracts remain finite-lived and may be called, mature, or be replaced. The paper studies the complete U.S. market of 19 autocallable ETFs operating by 5 June 2026, using a hand-collected dataset drawn from prospectuses, regulatory filings, issuer disclosures, holdings, collateral information, fund size, premiums and discounts, bid–ask spreads, and current barrier information where available. A formal contractual framework identifies the common coupon, autocall, maturity, and ETF-level transformation mechanisms, while standardized common-path scenarios illustrate how differences in contractual architecture translate the same reference path into different investor states. The evidence shows substantial variation in reference exposure, barrier placement, contract concentration, renewal, collateralization, income delivery, and disclosure conventions. In the 19-fund cross-section, fund size is negatively correlated with the 30-day median bid–ask spread (Spearman ρs = −0.641; two-sided p = 0.0031), without establishing a causal relationship, while dated TLA holdings document persistence and resi…
venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: Two snapshots of fish diversity and body size in an Amazonian market
abstract: Tropical freshwater fisheries support both biodiversity and human livelihoods, yet long-term fishery characteristics data remain scarce across much of the Amazon Basin. Fish markets offer an opportunity to assess patterns in fish diversity and body sizes from exploited aquatic communities. Fish diversity and body sizes (standard length; SL) of common, locally harvested fish sold in Mercado Belén, Iquitos (Peruvian Amazon), were measured using photographic surveys conducted 11 years apart, in 2008 and 2019. Mean SL of the 10 most abundant species or genera differed significantly between these two years for seven taxa, increasing in five taxa (including Prochilodus nigricans and Plagioscion squamosissimus ) and decreasing in two, notably in a large, predatory Cichla sp. Taxonomic richness and diversity showed small declines between these two years. Minor differences in community composition were observed between years, but the dominant taxa were similar. These two time points serve as a baseline for future comparisons and by themselves do not demonstrate temporal or regional trends. Market surveys provide a useful, low-cost complement to field-based ecological studies in tropical freshwater ecosystems.

title: THE IMPACT OF FINTECH TOOLS ON THE TRANSFORMATION OF THE FINANCIAL INVESTMENT MARKET
abstract: The article examines how FinTech tools transform the structure, accessibility and operating mechanisms of the financial investment market. The study proceeds from the premise that digitalisation is changing not only the technical channel through which an investor buys a financial asset, but also the architecture of intermediation, the cost of investment services, portfolio formation, information processing and the distribution of risks between investors, platforms and regulated financial institutions. The main groups of investment-oriented FinTech tools are systematised: mobile investment platforms, robo-advisory, artificial-intelligence-based analytics, open banking and API infrastructure, distributed-ledger solutions and asset tokenisation. Recent academic evidence indicates that automated advice can broaden access to professional portfolio management, improve diversification for some self-directed investors and reduce the time and fees associated with portfolio management. At the same time, digital investment environments generate new risks related to algorithmic bias, data quality, cybersecurity, opaque decision models, gamification, digital nudging, conflicts of interest and the rapid diffusion of unreliable investment content through social networks. The paper proposes an author's four-contour model of FinTech transformation of the financial investment market. It combines…

title: Perceived Product Quality, Price, and Accessibility in Relation to Purchase Trust and Purchase Decision of Cayenne Pepper Collectors in Kediri Regency
abstract: Cayenne pepper is a perishable horticultural commodity with fluctuating prices, so collectors must weigh several factors when buying from farmers. This cross-sectional study examines how perceived product quality (X1), price (X2), and accessibility (X3) relate to purchase trust (Y1) and purchase decision (Y2) among cayenne pepper collectors in Kediri Regency. Questionnaire data (Likert scale 1–5) from 200 collectors selected by purposive sampling were analyzed with covariance-based Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in AMOS 24. The initial structural model, which fixed the covariances among the exogenous constructs to zero, did not fit (?² = 221.611, df = 83; RMSEA = 0.092). The modified model, which freed these covariances and added four error covariances, met all fit criteria (?² = 95.814, df = 76, p = 0.062; RMSEA = 0.036; CFI = 0.986). In this model, X1, X2, and X3 were positively associated with Y1 (standardized coefficients 0.554, 0.276, and 0.234), and Y1, X1, and X2 were positively associated with Y2 (0.459, 0.255, and 0.246). The association of X3 with Y2 was weakest (0.149; C.R. = 1.915, only slightly above the critical t-value of 1.753). The coefficients were not formally compared with one another, and the cross-sectional design does not establish causality. The findings are conditional on the modified model and on a purposive sample from a single regency.
venue: AJARCDE (Asian Journal of Applied Research for Community Development and Empowerment)

title: CBAM Cost Exposure and Farm Input Price Risk in the Fertiliser Value Chain: A Two-Level Soft-Set and Multi-Criteria Analysis for Türkiye
abstract: The European Union (EU) Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) prices the embedded emissions of imported fertilisers, while nitrogen fertilisers are among the most volatile farm inputs in supplier countries. This study analyses both exposures for Türkiye in two complementary rankings. Stage 1 ranks 21 non-EU suppliers of six CBAM-covered fertilisers from an EU importer’s sourcing perspective; Stage 2 ranks 16 Turkish input groups on descriptive price-risk indicators for January 2020–July 2026 and on base-year index weights. Rankings use the Relational Membership Value Calculation (RMVC), its weighted extension, the Maji–Roy choice value, three compensatory multi-criteria methods and a consensus ranking. Under a 79 €/tCO2e reference price, Türkiye’s modelled 2030 charge equals 32.6% of export value (supplier mean 22.9%), with ammonia, urea and calcium ammonium nitrate carrying 93.9% of it; on the carbon criteria alone Türkiye ranks 18th of 21. Its overall rank (1st to 17th) is driven by market attributes and falls to 9th to 18th when carbon criteria receive half of the weight. Nitrogen fertilisers rank first or second under all twelve full-sample combinations, but their lead weakens after 2023 and under block-bootstrap resampling. RMVC resolves ties, yet with ties handled at fixed cardinality it identifies top alternatives no better than Maji–Roy.

title: Ionospheric TEC forecasting based on CEEMDAN-VMD secondary decomposition and LSTM in the Japan region
Calibrated and Explainable Temporal Forecasting of Psychoemotional Risk from Longitudinal Mobile-Health Data
abstract: Mobile-health systems generate repeated, time-stamped observations, but future-risk forecasts must be reliable rather than merely discriminative. We evaluate Temporal Calibrated Explainable Risk Forecasting (T-CERF) for irregular ecological momentary assessment histories. Study A used 5726 forecasting examples from 542 Corona Health participants, a 56-day history window, and a 28-day primary horizon. On the fixed participant-independent test set, T-CERF achieved a PR-AUC of 0.867, ROC-AUC of 0.946, and Brier score of 0.083. Random Forest matched its ROC-AUC (0.947 versus 0.946), while the Persistence baseline yielded a higher F1-score (0.786 versus 0.761). The PR-AUC difference from the matched current-only model was +0.023, but its paired participant-level bootstrap interval included zero. Across five additional participant-level splits, ΔPR-AUC averaged +0.0106 (SD 0.0262; range −0.0298 to +0.0399), with one split favoring the current-only model. Thus, a consistent discriminative benefit from temporal history was not established. Temperature Scaling improved calibration, while ensemble uncertainty supported selective prediction. A separate HBSC Kazakhstan analysis remains exploratory. T-CERF is therefore presented as a calibrated, uncertainty-aware mobile-health forecasting framework rather than as a hardware or network-level IoT implementation.

title: Air Pollution and Atopic Dermatitis in Children
abstract: Importance Atopic dermatitis is a common inflammatory skin condition that is heavily influenced by environmental factors, and while ambient air pollution has been linked to atopic dermatitis outcomes in adults, its effects in children remain more uncertain. Objective To synthesize the evidence examining the associations between ambient air pollutants and atopic dermatitis prevalence in children. Data Sources MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to February 10, 2026. Study Selection Observational studies of children under 18 years of age that examined the association between at least 1 atopic dermatitis outcome of interest and a pollutant exposure were included. Data Extraction and Synthesis The PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines were used; methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and risk of bias was evaluated using the risk of bias in nonrandomized studies of exposure effects (ROBINS-E) tool. Data were synthesized using random-effects models, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were health care utilization and prevalence, incidence, or severity of atopic dermatitis in relation to predefined ambient air pollutant exposures, including nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), sulfur…

title: Environmental monitoring and forecasting for forest fire in Southeast Asia
abstract: Abstract Forest fires in Southeast Asia, pose persistent environmental challenges with far-reaching consequences. This research investigates the use of advanced environmental monitoring techniques to detect and forecast regional forest fires. Aims to contribute the development of effective, technology-driven for environmental monitoring, fostering a proactive approach to mitigate the impact of fire incidents. These indicators enable real-time monitoring systems, allowing for timely intervention to prevent the escalation of potential fire incidents. The environmental monitoring not only addresses the immediate challenges of forest fires but also aims to forecast potential future fire incidents. The results of research include mapping and plotting fire data from Indonesia and Malaysia.

title: Gay sex and the price of Bildung in John Boyne’s The Heart’s Invisible Furies
abstract: This article explores gay sex and sexuality in John Boyne’s The Heart’s Invisible Furies, a novel that has received very limited scholarly attention. The novel explores the life of its protagonist over a period of 70 years and tracks his development from a young boy in conservative Ireland in the 1940s to an older man in the years directly following the Irish marriage-equality referendum in 2015. While this novel is a Bildungsroman in the conventional sense, I am interested in the curious bifurcated structure of the book. While the first half of the novel maps a rich queer sexual culture, the second half of the novel explicitly disavows and pathologises it. The anonymous hookups and cruising that animate the adolescence and young adulthood of the protagonist in Dublin are replaced by a homonormative project of sexual moralism and a politics of ‘respectability’. In this article, I narrowly argue that the character development of Boyne’s protagonist (the Bildung) becomes inextricably tied to the homonormative rejection of gay sexual cultures, making the novel a Bildungsroman in the most conservative sense of the genre. Contribution: This article offers a close reading of a largely neglected novel to problematise the restrictive and homonormative logics that often constrain depictions of sex within the genre of the gay Bildungsroman.

title: Deep Learning for Wind Energy Forecasting with Emphasis on Complex Terrain: A Structured Review of Automated Architecture Search, Data Fusion, Uncertainty Quantification, and Explainability
abstract: Wind energy forecasting in complex terrain is a critical challenge for reliable power grid integration. This PRISMA 2020-guided structured review examines 134 eligible studies (2018–2026) that apply deep learning (DL) and other neural-network methods to wind speed forecasting, wind power prediction, and wind field downscaling, with particular emphasis on complex terrain. Four methodological pillars are analyzed: automated deep learning (AutoDL/NAS), multi-source data fusion, uncertainty quantification with emphasis on conformal prediction, and explainable AI (XAI). Only 24 studies (18%) explicitly evaluate mountainous, valley, coastal, or urban settings. CNN-based models are the most frequent architecture family, whereas AutoDL/NAS and automated hyperparameter optimization appear in only 11 studies, and no NAS framework has been evaluated in complex terrain. Reported fusion gains are study-specific (from about 13% RMSE reduction to over 50% MAE reduction) and are not directly comparable across datasets, metrics, and baselines. Conformal prediction offers finite-sample coverage guarantees under exchangeability, yet its empirical reliability under terrain-induced non-stationarity has not been evaluated. XAI appears in only five DL studies and is mostly applied post hoc. No study combines three or more pillars. We identify ten challenges and propose ten future directions toward in…

title: КОРРЕЛЯЦИОННО-РЕГРЕССИОННЫЙ АНАЛИЗ И ПРОГНОЗ ПРОИЗВОДСТВА НЕФТЯНОГО БИТУМА В РОССИИ
abstract: The purpose of the study is to identify economic factors associated with changes in the volume of oil bitumen production in the Russian Federation and assess the possibility of using them to predict production output. The information base of the study was compiled by statistical data for 2010-2021, including indicators of oil bitumen production, average product price, dollar exchange rate, foreign trade, oil prices, production capacities, inflation, as well as financing for the repair and construction of highways. The paper uses methods of statistical analysis, correlation analysis, multiple regression and scenario modeling. At the first stage, nine factors are considered, potentially related to the dynamics of production. The calculation of paired correlation coefficients showed the closest positive relationship between the volume of production with the dollar exchange rate (r = 0.87) and the amount of financing for road construction (r = 0.83). For subsequent modeling, the average price of oil bitumen, the dollar rate and the amount of funds allocated for the repair and construction of highways were selected. The constructed linear model has a coefficient of determination R² = 0.944 and is statistically significant in general. Exponential, logarithmic and power forms of dependence are additionally considered. The best values for coefficient of determination, standard error an…

Multimodal CNN-RNN Framework for Ethereum Price Direction Prediction Using Candlestick, Technical, and Sentiment Features
abstract: The increasing adoption of blockchain technology has intensified the need for accurate cryptocurrency price prediction because Ethereum exhibits substantial price volatility and rapidly changing market conditions. This study aims to develop a multimodal prediction model that integrates visual candlestick patterns, technical indicators, and market sentiment to improve Ethereum price direction forecasting. A quantitative experimental approach was employed using daily Open-High-Low-Close-Volume data collected from January 2020 to December 2024 together with news headlines analyzed through Natural Language Processing for sentiment scoring. Candlestick images were processed using a Convolutional Neural Network, while sequential numerical features were modeled using a Gated Recurrent Unit within a hybrid architecture. The dataset was chronologically divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio, and model optimization was performed with the Adam optimizer and early stopping. The proposed multimodal model achieved 91.48% prediction accuracy with balanced precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 91%, substantially outperforming unimodal and bimodal models. These findings demonstrate that integrating heterogeneous information sources significantly enhances prediction reliability, providing an effective and practical framework for cryptocurrency p…

title: A Review of Virtual Power Plants and Adjacent Research from a Decision-Focused Learning Perspective
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) operation commonly follows a predict-then-optimize framework, in which forecasts of generation, demand, and prices feed downstream optimization. However, minimizing statistical forecast errors overlooks cost asymmetry across error directions and periods, and the nonlinear response of decisions. This has motivated decision-focused learning, which incorporates downstream cost, profit, and risk into training or uncertainty representation. This paper reviews VPP and adjacent studies from three perspectives. Market participation benefits from identifying profit-sensitive periods and variables; resource operation requires attention to physical and time-coupled constraints and operational feasibility; and uncertainty handling improves when forecasts are aligned with downstream outcomes. Forecasts should therefore be evaluated using statistical metrics together with economic, operational, and risk implications. We further identify when such approaches are advantageous.

title: Cost-optimized placement of energy storage in renewable networks
abstract: Abstract Massive investments in renewable energy, like solar power, are challenged by the variability of their production, which threatens grid stability. Energy storage is a critical technology for ensuring a reliable supply. This article presents a cost-optimization model for strategically placing storage to minimize total annual costs, encompassing installation, operation, and transmission. A case study in Miskolc, Hungary, reveals that transmission costs are comparable to installation costs, validating the integrated optimization approach for achieving economic viability.

title: Correlation between S–S bond energy and macroscopic properties in inverse vulcanized polymers
abstract: Abstract For a series of polymers obtained by the reaction of d -limonene with various amounts of cyclooctasulfur, the enthalpies of formation and combustion were determined using combustion calorimetry. Furthermore, the average values of the S–S bond energies constituting the oligosulfide bridges were calculated. An exponential decrease in the average S–S bond energy was observed until a minimum value was reached with an increase in the number of sulfur atoms forming the oligosulfide sequences. It has been shown that, in certain cases, the thermal, electrochemical, and physico-mechanical properties of inverse vulcanization products vary systematically with changes in the length of the oligosulfide bridges and, consequently, in the average S–S bond energies. A qualitative correlation is proposed between the distribution of relative signal intensities by m / z value in the LDI mass spectra of the synthesized polymers and the S 8 /(unsaturated monomer) ratio employed in the inverse vulcanization reaction.

title: فاعلية استراتيجية مقترحة قائمة على مهارات التفكير الاستكشافي في اكتساب المَفاهيم الأدبية لدى طلاب الصّف الرابع الأدبي
abstract: يهدف البحث الحالي إلى الكشف عن فاعلية استراتيجية مقترحة تستند إلى مهارات التفكير الاستكشافي في تنمية اكتساب المفاهيم الأدبية لدى طلاب الصف الرابع الأدبي. ولتحقيق هذا الهدف، صاغ الباحث الفرضية الآتية: لا توجد فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية عند مستوى دلالة (0.05) بين متوسط درجات طلاب المجموعة التجريبية الذين يدرسون المفاهيم الأدبية وفق الاستراتيجية المقترحة ومتوسط درجات طلاب المجموعة الضابطة الذين يدرسون المفاهيم نفسها بالطريقة التقليدية في الاختبار البعدي لاكتساب المفاهيم الأدبية. وقد أُجريت الدراسة في إعدادية المرتضى للبنين، التي اختيرت عشوائياً لتمثل عينة البحث، إذ بلغ عدد أفراد العينة (66) طالباً، وُزِّعوا بواقع (33) طالباً في المجموعة التجريبية و(33) طالباً في المجموعة الضابطة. نُفذت التجربة خلال الفصل الدراسي الثاني من العام الدراسي (2025–2026)، حيث بدأ التدريس الفعلي يوم الأربعاء الموافق 18/2/2026 وانتهى يوم الأحد الموافق 19/4/2026. ولغرض جمع البيانات، بنى الباحث أداة تمثلت في اختبار بعدي لاكتساب المفاهيم الأدبية، تألف من (30) فقرة من نوع الاختيار من متعدد. وأظهرت نتائج البحث تفوق طلاب المجموعة التجريبية الذين درسوا وفق الاستراتيجية المقترحة على طلاب المجموعة الضابطة في الاختبار البعدي لاكتساب المفاهيم الأدبية، مما يدل على فاعلية الاستراتيجية المقترحة في تحقيق أهداف البحث.

title: Informality and the Business Environment as Drivers of Carbon Emissions: The Moderating Role of Environmental Regulatory Quality
abstract: ABSTRACT A low‐carbon transition cannot succeed while a substantial share of business activity remains beyond the effective reach of regulation. This study examines how informality and the business environment shape carbon emissions and whether regulatory quality conditions the environmental consequences of informal production. The analysis uses an annual panel of 145 economies over 2005–2020, combining data from the World Development Indicators and World Bank. Informality is measured using dynamic general equilibrium and Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes estimates, while nine disaggregated business‐environment dimensions capture firm entry, infrastructure, finance, taxation, trade and commercial institutions. Standard negative binomial regression constitutes the principal estimator, with Poisson regression, alternative informality measurement and income‐group estimations used for robustness. The results show that informality is consistently associated with lower aggregate CO 2 emissions, with the relationship strongest in low‐income economies and weakest in high‐income countries. This apparent environmental advantage reflects the small‐scale, labour‐intensive and capital‐constrained nature of informal production rather than inherently cleaner business practices. Most business‐environment indicators are associated with higher emissions, particularly in lower‐ to middle‐income…

title: A Chemical-Derivatization Assisted Single-Point Isotopologue Multi-point Calibration Strategy for High-Throughput Quantification of Nitrofuran Metabolites in Aquatic Products by HPLC-HRMS
abstract: Abstract Construction multi-point calibration curves for quantifying nitrofuran metabolites (NFMs) via HPLC-HRMS is crucial and challenging, being laborious, time-intensive, and prone to inaccuracies. This study developed a chemical-derivatization assisted isotopologue multi-point calibration (IMC) strategy. It used 2-chloro-6-fluorobenzaldehyde (ClFBA) instead of 2-nitrobenzaldehyde (prescribed in GB 31656.13-2021) to derivatize NFMs. Owing to Cl’s distinctive isotopic signature, ClFBA derivatization enhanced the M + 1 ∼ M + 4 isotopic abundances of NFMs, facilitating HRMS detection. Integrating single-point IMC with internal calibration, multi-point calibration curves were constructed based on the correlation between the isotopic abundance (reflecting concentration) of ClFBA-derivatized NFMs and HRMS signals, applied to quantify NFMs in aquatic products. All NFMs exhibited excellent linearity (R2 ≥ 0.9991), with LOQs of 0.5 μg/kg. Recoveries ranged from 87.99% to 109.87%, while intra-day RSDs were between 4.19% and 11.88% and inter-day RSDs fell within 2.86% to 8.78%. This methodology holds potential for precise HRMS-based quantification of other amino-containing small-molecule drugs.

title: A Clearer Strategy for Responding to the Ebola Bundibugyo Outbreak Is Needed
abstract: The ongoing Ebola virus disease outbreak caused by Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense (BDBV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo highlights persistent gaps in global outbreak preparedness. Despite decades of experience with Ebola, delayed detection, limited access to care, insecurity, community mistrust, and fragmented response systems continue to hinder effective control and reduce survival. While non-pharmaceutical interventions remain essential, potentially effective medical countermeasures should be considered earlier. Existing vaccines and therapeutics developed against Ebola Zaire, although not licensed for BDBV, could be evaluated through carefully governed investigational or compassionate use alongside rigorous research. Effective response also requires strengthened surveillance, decentralized care, community engagement, and meaningful leadership by local scientists and healthcare professionals. This outbreak underscores the need for an adaptive, locally led, and internationally supported strategy that simultaneously saves lives and generates evidence.

title: Case Report: Low-dose AML therapy with the Brazilian pediatric GELMAI protocol as a bridge strategy during a high-risk pregnancy complicated by severe infection: sustained maternal remission and survival with favorable early developmental follow-up
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) during pregnancy is rare and requires urgent maternal treatment while fetal toxicity and prematurity must also be considered. We report a 17-year-old adolescent diagnosed with AML at 21 weeks and 6 days of gestation, based on first-trimester ultrasonographic dating, after presenting with severe pancytopenia, pneumonia, COVID-19, and septic shock. Bone marrow evaluation showed 73.3% blasts, with an immature myeloid immunophenotype; conventional cytogenetics showed 46,XX[20]. Available molecular testing was negative for CBFB::MYH11, FLT3-ITD, and NPM1, but broader molecular profiling was not available. Based on the studies available, the leukemia was most consistent with AML defined by differentiation under WHO 2022 and AML, not otherwise specified under ICC 2022, while acknowledging that incomplete molecular testing precluded definitive exclusion of genetically defined AML entities. After multidisciplinary counseling, the patient chose to continue the pregnancy. Because of recent septic shock, ongoing pregnancy, and concern for toxicity from intensive induction, treatment was initiated with the low-dose MAG regimen used in the Brazilian pediatric GELMAI protocol (mitoxantrone, low-dose cytarabine, and G-CSF). After MAG I, bone marrow evaluation showed no morphologic evidence of residual leukemia and no measurable leukemic population by multiparameter…

title: Training and Development Outsourcing Strategy and Operational Performance of Commercial Banks in Kenya
abstract: This study examines the relationship between training and development outsourcing and operational performance in commercial banks in Kenya. Commercial banks have grown considerably over the past decade; this has come with sharper competition and mounting pressure on performance, particularly in customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and competitiveness. In response, many banks have turned to training and development outsourcing, engaging external training providers to access specialised expertise and contemporary skills that may not be readily available internally. The study was anchored on Transaction Cost Economics, Resource-Based View, and Systems Theory. A cross-sectional research design was used to analyse and empirically test the relationship between the variables. The target population comprised 38,840 employees of the 38 licensed commercial banks headquartered in Nairobi and selected branches, from which a sample of 385 respondents was selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using structured questionnaires, which were piloted before the main data collection, and reliability was assessed using Cronbach's alpha, yielding a coefficient of 0.78. Analysis was carried out in SPSS version 25.0 using descriptive and inferential statistics: simple linear regression tested the relationship between training and development outsourcing strategy and …

title: A Study on the Integrated Energy Data Platform Architecture for Existing Apartment Complexes Based on a Metering Point Operator
abstract: As services that require high-resolution metering data—time-of-use (TOU) tariffs, residential demand response (DR), virtual power plants (VPP), and municipal carbon monitoring—expand, a reliable data operator for the behind-the-meter (BTM) area of apartment complexes has become essential. This paper proposes an integrated energy data platform based on a metering point operator (MPO) that collects multi-utility data (electricity, water, gas, hot water, and heating) of existing apartment complexes at 15-minute intervals. The platform adopts a two-tier transport security architecture—Transport Layer Security (TLS) between the apartment server (A-EMS) and the central server (MIS), and Virtual Private Network (VPN) tunneling between the MIS and external entities such as the KEPCO meter data management system (MDMS), municipalities, and DR aggregators—together with a pseudonymization roadmap from universally unique identifier (UUID) tokens to keyed hashing (HMAC-SHA-256). The institutional position of the MPO is examined with reference to the Smart Energy Code (SEC) of Great Britain and the Korean Smart Energy Code (K-SEC) under preparation. A one-month field verification across 33 apartment complexes (40,170 households) yielded an end-to-end data integrity ratio of 98.86%, with stage-wise losses of 0.47% (in-complex collection), 0.20% (TLS transmission), and 0.47% (validation). title: Degradation-Aware Participation of Battery Storage in Frequency Regulation Markets
abstract: As data centers make the load on the power grid fluctuate faster, frequency regulation grows more valuable. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are well suited to provide frequency regulation, but providing this service speeds up aging, especially during operation at extreme state of charge (SoC). In the PJM interconnection, the grid operator supplies a regulation signal that a participating BESS is expected to follow, within a capacity that it must bid before the signal is known. Accordingly, we decompose the degradation-aware frequency regulation problem into a bidding layer and an operations layer. For bidding, we propose an adaptive strategy, assuming perfect tracking in which the bid depends on the SoC expected at the start of the bid period by means of choosing basepoints. For operation, the BESS further protects its battery by deliberately giving up a perfect performance score, to keep its SoC away from the extremes. On the PJM regulation signal and prices of 2023, adaptive bids lengthen the battery life by $31\%$ against bidding full capacity, for $2.2\%$ of the revenue. Giving up a perfect score in operation lengthens the battery life of constant bids by $10\%$ to $27\%$, at a change in revenue of at most $0.2\%$.

title: Do Investors Sanction Greenwashing? Selective Market Discipline in Fintech Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate whether stock market investors detect and penalise greenwashing. We draw on media reports of environmental, social and governance incidents at 321 US‐listed fintech firms between 2007 and 2025, within which greenwashing is identified, following RepRisk, as misleading communication about environmental practice. Investors impose no measurable price penalty when firms are publicly implicated in greenwashing, and the sample is large enough to have detected a penalty of the size observed for other conduct. Misleading communication that does not concern the environment is penalised, where cumulative abnormal returns are between 0.4% and 0.6% lower over the 2 weeks following the report, falling further to 0.8% over the 4 weeks before and after, whereas physical environmental damage draws no adverse reaction. The market therefore prices dishonesty, but the sanction depends on the domain of the false claim, and environmental claims by fintech firms fall outside it. Consistent with stakeholder theory, the results suggest that market‐based discipline exists but is selective, so that the truthfulness of environmental claims cannot be presumed to be enforced by investors where regulatory oversight is absent.

title: ЦИФРОВАЯ ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ КАК ФАКТОР СОВЕРШЕНСТВОВАНИЯ ФИНАНСОВО-КРЕДИТНЫХ МЕХАНИЗМОВ ПРЕДПРИЯТИЙ СФЕРЫ УСЛУГ
abstract: В статье рассматривается влияние цифровой трансформации на финансово-кредитные механизмы предприятий сферы услуг Республики Узбекистан. Предприятия сферы услуг, как правило, располагают небольшим объемом материальных активов, пригодных для залога, поэтому традиционная модель кредитования под обеспечение для них малоэффективна. На основе данных Центрального банка Республики Узбекистан и базы Global Findex Всемирного банка за 2017–2025 гг. показано, что число учетных записей в системах дистанционного банковского обслуживания выросло примерно с 20 млн в начале 2022 г. до 79,3 млн к декабрю 2025 г., а доля взрослых, имеющих счет, увеличилась с 34% до 56%. При этом юридические лица и индивидуальные предприниматели составляют лишь около 2% пользователей. В исследовании предложены модель цифрового контура кредитования предприятий сферы услуг на основе электронных счетов-фактур, онлайн-ККТ и эквайринговых данных, а также направления совершенствования финансово-кредитных механизмов.

title: Predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer via artificial intelligence: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND For patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), achieving a pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) creates an opportunity for organ preservation through a “watch-and-wait” strategy, thereby avoiding radical surgery. Artificial intelligence (AI) models applied to medical imaging offer a non-invasive way to predict this response, yet the landscape of available predictive tools remains fragmented. Importantly, pCR is a histopathological endpoint that can only be confirmed after surgical resection, whereas clinical complete response is assessed clinically and used to guide watch-and-wait decisions. AIM To evaluate the diagnostic performance of image-based AI models in predicting pCR (ypT0N0) for patients with LARC following nCRT. METHODS We searched PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL up to May 17, 2026. Studies developing image-based AI or radiomics models predicting pCR were included. Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool, Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-AI, and Radiomics Quality Score were used to evaluate methodological quality, while Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation-Diagnostic Test Accuracy assessed certainty of evidence. A bivariate random-effects model was used to pool sensitivity and specificity, and a hierarchical summary receiver operati…

Managing Students' Physical and Spiritual Conditions Through Classroom Management in Islamic Education: a Study of Coastal Elementary Schools
abstract: This study explores the impact of both physical and spiritual classroom conditions, as well as the accessibility of educational resources, on students' motivation to learn within Islamic Religious Education (IRE) in a coastal elementary school environment located in Lamongan, East Java. Existing research extensively covers classroom management in urban and suburban areas. However, few studies investigate how the socio-cultural dynamics of coastal communities interact with classroom management. Specifically, more research is needed on how spiritual and physical classroom environments operate in rural coastal elementary schools. This study adopted a qualitative field research design. Data were collected through non-participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and document reviews. A total of twelve key informants participated, including the school principal, IRE educators, classroom teachers, and upper-grade students. The key innovation of this investigation is its cohesive framework that connects spatial and physical organization, play-based learning tools, and spiritual practices, specifically designed for the socio-cultural circumstances of coastal learners. The results reveal that a tidy, inviting, and thoughtfully arranged physical environment has a positive effect on students' concentration and emotional health. Additionally, the incorporation of educational games a…

title: Experimental Evaluation of a Hold-State Fuzzy Supervisor for P&O–PSO MPPT in an ESP8266-Based Standalone Photovoltaic System
abstract: Rapid irradiance variation exposes a practical trade-off in photovoltaic maximum power point tracking (MPPT): perturb-and-observe (P&O) is inexpensive to execute but oscillates around the maximum power point, whereas particle swarm optimization (PSO) can recover the optimum after large operating changes but requires more computation. This paper develops a hold-state fuzzy supervisor that assigns duty-cycle calculation to either P&O or PSO according to the normalized power error and its change. Fuzzy logic is therefore used only for mode selection; it does not act as a third MPPT algorithm or directly generate the pulse-width-modulation duty cycle. When the operating point enters a prescribed convergence region, the controller retains the last accepted duty cycle until the measured error indicates a material change. The method was first evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink and then implemented on an ESP8266-based 50 W standalone PV prototype subjected to the same 25 s stepped-irradiance profile. Under the reported test conditions, the supervisor achieved a convergence time of 0.12 s, a settling time of 0.16 s, a tracking efficiency of 99.78%, a steady-state power ripple of 0.48%, and a peak overshoot of 0.82%. The corresponding values for P&O were 0.35 s, 0.42 s, 98.95%, 1.82%, and 2.60%, while PSO achieved 0.18 s, 0.24 s, 99.42%, 0.91%, and 1.35% respectively. The results indicate that…

title: Design and Development of an Information System to Improve Services at Posyandu Dharma Wanita Rawajaya, Palembang
abstract: Posyandu is a community-based maternal and child health service in Indonesia, yet most Posyandu still depend on paper record books that are prone to recording errors, while information on schedules and services reaches parents only through conventional channels. Existing Posyandu information systems are mostly single-platform and do not give parents a view of the data that cadres enter. This study designs and builds an integrated Posyandu Information System for Posyandu Dharma Wanita Rawajaya, Palembang, in which a PHP/MySQL website for cadres and the community and an Android application share one centralized MySQL database through HTTP endpoints that exchange JSON, so that a record or schedule saved by a cadre is available to parents on their next request without re-entry. The system was developed by custom programming after observation and interviews. It covers toddler, pregnant-mother, immunization, and activity management, online activity registration with a unique registration number and a printable proof, and a date-filtered reporting dashboard. Black Box Testing of 26 scenarios in 14 feature groups, run on a pilot dataset of 21 community members, 18 toddlers, 12 pregnant mothers, 33 immunization records, and 12 activities, produced a 100% pass rate (26/26). The results indicate that a shared-database, multi-client architecture is a feasible way to digitalize Posyandu ser…

title: Artificial intelligence in functional gastrointestinal disorders: From symptom recognition to personalised management
abstract: Functional gastrointestinal disorders, now termed disorders of gut-brain interaction, are heterogeneous conditions shaped by psychological, physiological, microbial, and environmental factors. Diagnosis and treatment remain difficult because symptoms overlap, trajectories fluctuate, and no single objective biomarker exists. This minireview synthesises human evidence for artificial intelligence (AI) in symptom classification, digital phenotyping, microbiome and multi-omics prediction, treatment-response estimation, wearable monitoring, and language-based care. Targeted PubMed searches were updated through September 20, 2026. Current studies show feasibility, but most use small, single-centre cohorts, retrospective designs, or internal validation; calibration and prospective impact evaluation are uncommon. The most plausible near-term role of AI is therefore clinical augmentation: Identifying longitudinal patterns, supporting shared decisions, and detecting changes that require reassessment while preserving human oversight and patient autonomy. Large language models may improve education and communication, but disorder-specific evaluations reveal imperfect diagnosis and treatment recommendations with marked overconfidence. Translation requires representative cohorts that include overlapping organic disease, explicit endpoints despite the absence of a diagnostic gold standard, ext…

title: Clinical Supervision in Teachers’ Professional Development: An Integrative Framework
abstract: Clinical supervision has increasingly been positioned as an approach to support teacher professional development; however, previous studies have examined its stages, implementation mechanisms, contextual conditions, and professional outcomes from relatively fragmented perspectives. This study aims to analyze the role of clinical supervision in teacher professional development and to synthesize the relationships among the supervision cycle, developmental mechanisms, implementation conditions, and professional outcomes. This study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with thematic-narrative synthesis following the PRISMA 2020 framework. Relevant literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026 was identified through Scopus, ERIC, Google Scholar, Garuda, and SINTA using keywords related to clinical supervision and teacher professional development. Selected studies were assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Tools and analyzed through thematic coding and cross-study comparison. The findings indicate four interconnected domains: clinical supervision cycle, developmental mechanisms, enabling and constraining conditions, and professional development outcomes. Coherent radio emission at 45 MHz from the nearby planet-hosting star GJ 725A
abstract: Ultralow-frequency (ν<100,MHz) coherent radio emission from exoplanet-hosting stellar systems carries information about planetary and stellar magnetic fields as well as the space weather environment -- information that is difficult to obtain at other wavelengths. We carried out the circularly polarized LOFAR LBA Sky Survey, the most sensitive circularly polarized survey in this frequency range, using the LOFAR low-band antenna system. As part of this untargeted search, we detected a signal in a 1,h observation that is coincident with the quiescent, planet-hosting, solar-neighborhood M,dwarf GJ,725A at a distance of 3.5,pc. The signal has a high circular polarization fraction of 74 =135 between 42,MHz and 50,MHz. It was undetected in the 50--66,MHz range, with a 3σ upper limit of and a peak brightness of B_ I,46 -1 I,58 <48, , corresponding to a drop of at least a factor of ∼3 across 12,MHz and indicating a strong spectral feature or cutoff around 50,MHz. Our detection represents the lowest-frequency confirmed detection of a stellar system. Based on its high estimated brightness temperature (∼10^ -1 14 ,K), transient character, and polarization fraction, the emission is most plausibly attributed to the electron cyclotron maser instability. The available observations are not sufficient to identify the astrophysical origin of the emission. We consider three plausible scenarios: au…
