PEMBERDAYAAN KWT LEBAH EMAS MELALUI INTEGRASI IRIGASI TETES, BUDIDAYA LELE, DAN PEMASARAN DIGITAL
abstract: Kelompok Wanita Tani (KWT) Lebah Emas di Kalurahan Guwosari, Bantul, mengelola sekitar satu hektar lahan produktif, dua puluh petak budidaya, dan beberapa kolam lele. Pengembangannya menghadapi keterbatasan integrasi pengelolaan air dengan budidaya ikan, belum konsistennya perhitungan biaya produksi dan pengemasan, serta belum optimalnya promosi digital. Program pengabdian ini bertujuan memperkuat kapasitas teknis dan usaha melalui pendekatan terpadu yang menggabungkan perencanaan irigasi tetes, budidaya lele, diversifikasi produk, pengemasan, dan pemasaran digital. Pelaksanaan menggunakan metode partisipatif yang mencakup koordinasi dan pemetaan kebutuhan, pelatihan, pendampingan lapangan, pengembangan produk dan media promosi, serta pemantauan. Data diperoleh melalui observasi, diskusi kelompok, dokumentasi kegiatan, artefak produk, dan media digital, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Program menghasilkan pemetaan kolam, jaringan air, dan petak budidaya; pelatihan harga pokok produksi, pengemasan, pembuatan konten, dan promosi daring; penguatan identitas serta kemasan Lele Roy; aktivasi konten Instagram; serta inspeksi teknis kolam buis beton dan jaringan air. Hasil menunjukkan meningkatnya kesiapan mitra mengelola sistem produksi terpadu dan memasarkan produk, sementara pengukuran kuantitatif dampak masih memerlukan monitoring tahap akhir.

title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Low-Cost Autonomous Medical Rescue Robot for Hazardous and Conflict-Affected Environments
abstract: Emergency rescue operations in hazardous, unstable, and conflict-affected environments expose medical teams and first responders to serious risks, including structural collapse, fire, debris, toxic exposure, communication failure, and restricted access to victims. Robotic systems can reduce direct human exposure by performing early reconnaissance, detecting possible human presence, transmitting visual information, and supporting rescue planning. However, many advanced rescue robots are expensive, complex, and difficult to reproduce in low-resource settings. This paper presents the design, implementation, and experimental evaluation of a low-cost autonomous medical rescue robot developed for simulated hazardous-environment rescue support. The proposed prototype integrates an ESP32 microcontroller, HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor, PIR motion sensor, Neo-6M GPS module, ESP32-CAM video-streaming module, L298N motor driver, differential-drive DC motors, servo-actuated robotic arm, and rechargeable battery power system. A reactive autonomous control algorithm was implemented to enable low-speed autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance, human-motion detection, GPS coordinate reporting, live visual monitoring, and basic robotic-arm activation. Experimental testing showed that the robot achieved an average obstacle-response time of approximately 50 ms, distance-measurement accuracy of approx…

Impacto de la educación virtual en el aprendizaje del inglés en estudiantes de básica ecuatoriana [Impact of virtual education on English learning in Ecuadorian basic education students]
abstract: La educación virtual llegó a las escuelas ecuatorianas en marzo de 2020 sin equipos suficientes ni docentes preparados, por cuanto el aprendizaje del inglés quedó sujeto a la conectividad de cada hogar. Es así que el estudio se planteó como objetivo analizar el impacto de la educación virtual en el aprendizaje del inglés en estudiantes de básica ecuatoriana. En este sentido se empleó una metodología descriptiva, documental y comparativa, teniéndose como corpus 25 fuentes (2012-2025) contrastadas mediante matrices por país, nivel, tecnología y resultado. Entre los resultados se obtuvo que las herramientas digitales producen efectos positivos en condiciones planificadas, mientras en Ecuador la falta de dispositivos, la conexión irregular y la escasa interacción limitaron la práctica oral. Entre las conclusiones se estableció que el impacto depende menos de la plataforma que del acceso, la mediación docente y el acompañamiento familiar.

title: Women's Participation in Peacebuilding: A Study of Selected Areas in Taraba State, 1991-2023
abstract: Violent conflicts arising from ethnic, religious, political, land-related, citizenship, and resource-based disputes have shaped peacebuilding needs in Taraba State, Nigeria. This study examined women’s participation in conflict resolution, reconciliation, and peacebuilding in Jalingo, Wukari, and Sardauna Local Government Areas from 1991 to 2023. Using a qualitative approach grounded in documentary and historical evidence, the study analyzed the nature and consequences of violent conflicts and women’s contributions to peacebuilding in the selected areas. The findings indicate that women and children were among the groups most severely affected, experiencing the loss of family members, displacement, property destruction, livelihood losses, economic hardship, and disruption of social relations. Women also played important roles in promoting peace through religious mobilization, including prayer and fasting; community mobilization; women’s associations; peace marches and protests; interfaith engagement; advocacy; dialogue; and informal reconciliation initiatives. Despite these contributions, patriarchal norms, institutional bias, and limited access to decision-making constrained their participation in formal peace and security structures. The study demonstrates the importance of women’s community-based and informal peacebuilding contributions while identifying persistent barriers …

title: Post-Meal Walking as A Strategy for Postprandial Glycemic Control After High-Carbohydrate Meals in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Literature Review of Timing, Duration, & Intensity
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterized by impaired postprandial glycemic control, a condition of particular concern in Asian populations, including Indonesia, where rice serves as the dominant carbohydrate source and carries a high glycemic index. Postprandial exercise, particularly walking, has been proposed as a practical, low-cost, non-pharmacological strategy to attenuate glucose excursions after meals, yet no prior narrative review has specifically synthesized evidence on post-meal walking in relation to high-carbohydrate, rice-based diets. This narrative review aimed to synthesize existing evidence on the effectiveness, optimal timing, duration, and intensity of post-meal walking for glycemic control in individuals with T2DM, and to evaluate its relevance to high-carbohydrate meal contexts. Literature was searched through PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2016 and 2026, yielding ten randomized controlled trials that met the inclusion criteria. Findings showed that post-meal walking consistently reduced postprandial glucose excursions, peak glucose, and area under the curve, with the most consistent benefits observed when walking was initiated within 15-30 minutes after meals, for 10-20 minutes, at light-to-moderate intensity. These effects are physiologically explained by insulin-independent GLUT4 translocation induc…

title: Playing to Teach: SPED Teachers' Experiences in Using Physical and Traditional Games in Teaching Learners with Special Needs
abstract: Background and Aim: Game-based learning has emerged as a promising pedagogical approach in special education, yet existing research has largely examined strategies, challenges, coping mechanisms, and support systems as separate lines of inquiry rather than as an interconnected process, particularly within the Philippine SPED context. This study explored the lived experiences of SPED teachers in using physical and traditional games to teach learners with special needs, examining how their strategies, challenges, coping mechanisms, and support systems interrelate in practice. Materials and Methods: Using a qualitative case study design, this research employed in-depth semi-structured interviews with five SPED teachers from selected schools in District 6, Oroquieta City Division, Philippines. Purposive sampling was used to select participants who had at least one year of experience in special education and actively used game-based instruction, with the sample size guided by the principle of information power and confirmed through the attainment of thematic saturation. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework. Results: Four major themes emerged from the analysis: (1) adaptive game implementation strategies, including game modification, multisensory engagement, and differentiated instruction; (2) multifaceted challenges encompassing…

title: Pan-Cancer Classification in Clinical Applications: A Comprehensive Analysis using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Cancer affects millions of people worldwide, and accurate, timely classification of cancer type is closely tied to treatment selection and patient outcomes — particularly in metastatic disease or Cancer of Unknown Primary, where identifying the tissue of origin directly informs site specific treatment. Multiple clinical and genomic variables, including mutation count, tumor stage, diagnosis age, tumor purity, smoking status and sex are individually associated with cancer behavior, but whether their combined use improves classification across a broad range of cancer types — rather than within a single cancer type, as in most prior work — has rarely been tested directly. This study evaluates four machine learning classifiers — Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, and Artificial Neural Network — on a clinical pancancer dataset spanning 20 cancer types (6,110 patients; 1,222 held out for testing), using ten routinely available clinical and summary genomic covariates. XGBoost achieved the strongestperformance (accuracy 87.0%, 95% CI: 85.0–88.8%; F1-score 0.869; ROC AUC 0.993), with Random Forest close behind; both outperformed SVM and ANN by a margin confirmed as statistically significant through 5-fold cross-validation. title: Exploring Teachers’ Practices in Advocating Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Background and Aim: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education creates opportunities and challenges for teaching and learning. As AI tools become accessible, teachers are essential in guiding students toward responsible, ethical, and effective use. Yet, teacher practices supporting responsible AI use remain underexplored, particularly in the Philippine context. This case study examined how teachers advocate responsible AI use in their classrooms. Materials and Methods: A qualitative case study design was used. Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with fifteen school teachers at Tabina National High School, Tabina District, Division of Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. Purposive criterion sampling selected participants who: (a) taught in basic education, (b) integrated AI tools or AI-related discussions into teaching, (c) demonstrated advocacy for responsible technology use, and (d) had at least three years of teaching experience. Interviews were conducted in Cebuano, transcribed verbatim, translated into English when necessary, and thematically analyzed following Merriam and Tisdell’s (2016) case study procedures. Data were collected from January to June 2026. Results: Four sequential themes emerged: (1) challenges involving student overreliance, absent institutional policies, limited teacher training, and academic integrity; (2) coping mechanis…

title: Vivekananda's Educational Philosophy and Its Relevance to Twenty-First Century Learning
abstract: Background and Aim: India’s education system in 2026 is mid-implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, even as the Indian classroom grapples with digital distraction, uneven policy rollout, and fast AI adoption. Questions remain about the effects on students’ concentration, values, and overall development. This paper examines whether Swami Vivekananda's four core educational concepts — man-making education, concentration of mind, universal access, and character-building — offer a workable framework for analysing this learning crisis, read against NEP 2020 and NCF 2023. Scholarship on Vivekananda’s views on education and the academic discussion on contemporary Indian policy discourse have developed quite independently. There has been very little discussion of the relationship between Vivekananda’s ideas, formulated a century ago, and modern empirical work on attention, equity, and character formation. Materials and Methods: This study uses qualitative, conceptual, and comparative textual analysis and not primary data gathering or statistical testing. The main sources are the speeches and writings of Vivekananda in the Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda. Secondary sources include Indian government documents (NEP 2020, NCF 2023) and articles about policy implementation, digital attention, digital divide, and SEL. Recurring themes in Vivekananda's writings were id…

title: Students’ Perceptions of Homework as a Support for Improving Learning and Knowledge Retention in Vocational Engineering Education: An Action Research Study
abstract: Background and Aim: The inclusion of homework in the engineering vocational curriculum is uncommon, and its effects remain underexplored. To address this gap in the literature, this research focused on students' perceptions of homework to better understand its impact on learning and knowledge retention. To achieve the aim and objectives of this study, both quantitative and qualitative data were collected from 10 learners enrolled at a college in a socioeconomically deprived city in Northern England. The hybrid data collection technique was adopted to ascertain extensively the design and extent to which homework influences learning, based on participants' lived experiences. Materials and Methods: A participatory Action Research (AR) approach adopted in this research began by identifying homework as an intervention to support learning and knowledge retention. This was followed by an evaluation of learners’ perceptions of how homework supported learning and knowledge retention. The evaluation process involved assigning two sets of homework to the selected cohort. Feedback from completing the first set of homework helped redesign the second set. Tasks in both homework sets were problem-based and involved applying and memorizing formulas. title: Negotiating Grade 12 English Textbook Implementation in Nepal: Lived Experiences of Teachers and Students
abstract: Background and Aim: The textbook plays an important role in institutional curriculum policies, in providing a systematic sequence of topics and a logical progression from simpler to more complex concepts. Listening activities, speaking tasks, reading passages, and vocabulary development activities correspond to learning objectives and cultural representation in contemporary English language education. This study explored secondary-level English teachers’ and students’ perceptions of the Grade 12 Compulsory English textbook, centred on the Curriculum Development Centre (CDC) in Nepal. The research focuses on empirical insights, students’ experiences, the textbook’s strengths, limitations, and future policy decisions concerning English language education. Materials and Methods: This study adopted an Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) design to explore participants' lived experiences of using the Grade 12 Compulsory English textbook and their interactions with it to understand challenges, relevance, influence, and usefulness. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with five secondary-level English teachers and three Grade 12 graduates. We obtained detailed accounts of participants’ experiences, interpretations, and perceptions to acquire meaningful information about the use of the Grade 12 Compulsory English textbook. title: The Impact of Conducive Learning Environments on Learners’ Attitudes Towards Geometry: A Null Relationship
abstract: Geometry remains a critical component of mathematics education due to its role in developing spatial reasoning, logical thinking, and problem-solving skills essential for STEM-related fields. However, persistent negative learner attitudes toward geometry continue to hinder achievement and engagement, particularly in under-resourced educational contexts. While existing literature suggests that conducive learning environments positively influence learner attitudes, limited research has explored this relationship specifically within geometry or examined contexts where such relationships may be inconsistent or complex. Therefore, this study investigated the relationship between conducive learning environments and learners’ attitudes toward geometry. Guided by the Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework, the study adopted a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were collected through questionnaires and analysed using chi-square tests and contingency coefficients to determine the strength of association between variables. Qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with mathematics teachers and analysed thematically, with findings interpreted through the lenses of teaching, cognitive, and social presence. The quantitative results revealed a statistically significant and moderately strong relationship between learning environments and learners’ attitudes toward …

title: Motivational Influences of Detective Conan on Thai Undergraduate Psychology Students' Intentions to Pursue Advanced Studies in Forensic Psychology
abstract: Background and Aim: Popular culture may shape students’ academic engagement and career aspirations. This study examined associations between engagement with Detective Conan and undergraduates’ motivation to pursue advanced study in forensic psychology and criminology. Materials and Methods: A questionnaire was completed by 182 psychology undergraduates in Bangkok, Thailand, from 200 invitees (91.0% response rate). Hierarchical cluster analysis using Ward’s method and squared Euclidean distance classified participants into high-, moderate-, and low-engagement groups. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) identified motivational dimensions, while two-way ANOVA compared factor scores by engagement group and academic year. Ethics approval and informed consent were obtained. Results: 90.34% of participants had read or watched Detective Conan, 72.89% reported applying concepts or skills from the series to psychology studies, and 41.67% retrospectively associated the franchise with their interest in forensic psychology. EFA yielded four factors: intrinsic interest in justice, pop-culture-driven motivation, professional advancement, and academic application. Sampling adequacy was confirmed (KMO = .84), and Bartlett’s test was significant, χ² (66) = 915.42, p < .001. title: Machine learning-based classification of type 1 active galactic nuclei
abstract: Quasars and Seyfert galaxies are two prototypes of type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The current view posits that they belong to a uniform population with continuous distributions of the bolometric luminosity and the contribution from host galaxy. Clarifying whether physical differences exist between them would be helpful in improving our understanding of the nature of accretion of supermassive black holes and the co-evolution with their host galaxies. Although the sample sizes and studies of quasars have been growing rapidly recent years, research on Seyfert galaxies continues to be limited. Methods used to select Seyfert galaxies in large surveys or to distinguish quasars and Seyfert galaxies in broad-line AGNs have also received scarce attention in the literature. We aim to provide a machine learning-based method to distinguish type 1 quasars and type 1 Seyfert galaxies based on photometric data, which could be applied to large all-sky surveys. The method can also be used to obtain relatively complete samples of Seyfert galaxy candidates when broad-line AGNs have been selected. A principle component analysis (PCA) was first applied to reduce the dimensionality and visualize the separation between quasars and Seyfert galaxies based on multidimensional data. title: Peran Corporate Governance dalam Meningkatkan Integritas Pelaporan Keuangan: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis atas Dewan Komisaris, Komite Audit, dan Audit Internal
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study aims to examine the role of corporate governance in safeguarding financial reporting integrity, with particular emphasis on the board of commissioners, audit committee, and internal audit function. It seeks to identify the governance mechanisms most consistently associated with financial reporting quality and explain the factors underlying variations in empirical findings. Method: This study employs a limited systematic literature review guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework. A total of 39 records were identified through four search queries, of which 13 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the synthesis. The selected studies were analyzed using a narrative-thematic approach to identify recurring patterns, contextual differences, and inconsistencies in the relationships between corporate governance mechanisms and financial reporting integrity. Results: The synthesis reveals three main patterns. First, the audit committee demonstrates the most consistent association with financial reporting quality, particularly through its independence, expertise, size, and meeting frequency. Second, the effectiveness of independent commissioners is contingent on measurement approaches and regulatory contexts. title: Exploring the Strategies of Secondary English Teachers in Enhancing Students' Literacy Skills: A Case Study
abstract: Background and Aim: Literacy underachievement remains a persistent problem in Philippine basic education, with Filipino learners ranking among the lowest in the 2018 PISA reading comprehension results (Librea et al., 2023). While much existing research quantifies the effectiveness of individual literacy strategies through experimental designs, comparatively few qualitative studies explore how secondary English teachers themselves experience, select, and adapt these strategies within their own classrooms. This case study addresses that gap by exploring the strategies secondary English teachers employ to enhance their students' literacy skills, and the reasoning behind these strategies, within a single Philippine public secondary school. Materials and Methods: A single bounded qualitative case study design was employed, with the case defined as the group of eight English teachers at Tambulig National High School, Tambulig District, treated as one bounded unit of analysis. Participants were purposively selected based on current English teaching assignment, active engagement in literacy instruction, and at least three years of teaching experience. Semi-structured interviews were conducted in Cebuanong Binisaya using a guide validated by three experts, then transcribed, translated into English, and validated through member checking. title: Artificial Intelligence in Predicting Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns: A Machine Learning Approach for Modern Microbiology
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) reduces antibiotic effectiveness and increases morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing remains the clinical standard, but its turnaround time can delay treatment decisions. This review examines advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for predicting resistance patterns in clinical microbiology. It synthesizes literature on the biological mechanisms of resistance, major ML algorithms, clinical and genomic data sources, predictive performance, clinical applications, and implementation challenges. The reviewed studies report high predictive performance for random forests, support vector machines, XGBoost, and deep neural networks applied to genomic and clinical datasets. AI-supported prediction systems could facilitate earlier targeted therapy, strengthen antimicrobial stewardship, reduce unnecessary use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, and support resistance monitoring. However, their implementation is constrained by data quality, limited model explainability, algorithmic bias, privacy concerns, and inadequate infrastructure. The review concludes that AI and ML offer promising approaches to AMR prediction, while their effective clinical use depends on rigorous validation, explainable models, multidisciplinary implementation, and equitable access to digital health infrastru…

title: Analisis Kebutuhan E-LKPD TGT-Joyful Learning Terintegrasi Kearifan Lokal untuk Keterampilan Kolaborasi
abstract: Keterampilan kolaborasi merupakan kompetensi penting dalam pembelajaran fisika. Namun, kondisi di lapangan menunjukkan bahwa keterampilan kolaborasi peserta didik masih rendah, terutama dalam berbagi tanggung jawab dan berpartisipasi aktif dalam kegiatan kelompok, karena belum didukung aktivitas dan sumber belajar yang tepat. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kebutuhan pengembangan Lembar Kerja Peserta Didik Elektronik (E-LKPD) berbasis Teams Games Tournament (TGT) dengan pendekatan Joyful Learning terintegrasi kearifan lokal untuk memfasilitasi keterampilan kolaborasi peserta didik. Penelitian menggunakan metode deskriptif dengan pendekatan kuantitatif dan kualitatif. Data diperoleh dari 31 peserta didik kelas XI F1 dan dua guru fisika di SMA Negeri 3 Batusangkar melalui observasi keterampilan kolaborasi, wawancara, observasi pembelajaran, analisis dokumen, dan angket. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa keterampilan kolaborasi peserta didik berada pada kategori lemah (39%), dengan indikator tanggung jawab bersama memperoleh skor terendah (36%). Pelaksanaan pembelajaran berada pada kategori kuat (66% dan 75%), meskipun partisipasi peserta didik dalam kegiatan kelompok belum optimal. LKPD hanya digunakan oleh satu guru secara tidak konsisten dan berkategori cukup (58%), sedangkan E-LKPD belum pernah digunakan. title: Geometric Transformations and Symmetry in the Panjunan Red Mosque, Cirebon: An Ethnomathematical Study for Culture-Based Geometry Learning
abstract: Historic mosques in Indonesia embody mathematical ideas, yet studies of the Panjunan Red Mosque in Cirebon, built in 1480, have focused on its history and cultural acculturation rather than its mathematical structure. This study aims to identify and map the plane geometry, solid geometry, and geometric transformations embodied in the architecture of the mosque as a source of contextual mathematics learning. A qualitative descriptive design with an ethnographic approach was used. Data were collected through direct observation, a 45–60-minute semi-structured interview with the mosque caretaker, and photographic documentation of eight architectural elements: fence ornaments, roof, pillars, walls, ventilation openings, mihrab, gate, and wall reliefs. The data were analysed with the Miles–Huberman–Saldaña interactive model using inductive open and axial coding, and the transformations were modelled schematically in GeoGebra. The elements contain squares, rectangles, circles, triangles, trapezoids and rhombuses, as well as cylinders, cuboids, a square pyramid and a pyramid frustum. Four transformations were identified: translation in the ventilation openings, approximate reflection symmetry in the mihrab and the split gate, fourfold rotational symmetry in the wall relief (dihedral group D4), and dilation in the concentric square tiers of the gate pillars. title: Dispositional and Contextual Determinants of Informational Leadership: The Mediating Role of Organizational Climate in Thai Private Higher Education
abstract: Background and Aim: Digital transformation has fundamentally reshaped governance structures in higher education, particularly within tuition-dependent private institutions operating under competitive pressures. Informational leadership, defined as the strategic governance of data-driven decision-making, digital strategy implementation, and institutional information systems, has emerged as a critical capability. However, limited empirical research has examined how administrators’ personality traits and organizational climate jointly shape informational leadership. This study investigates the mediating role of organizational climate in the relationship between administrators’ personality traits and informational leadership in Thai private higher education institutions. Materials and Methods: A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed using survey data from 350 administrators across private higher education institutions in Thailand. Personality traits were measured based on the Five-Factor Model, organizational climate was assessed using established climate dimensions, and informational leadership was operationalized within a digital governance framework. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) validated the measurement model. title: تقييم استقرار وكفاءة اختيار الخصائص في أنظمة كشف التسلل متعددة الفئات باستخدام خوارزميات التعلم الآلي
abstract: تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تقييم استقرار وكفاءة خوارزميات اختيار الخصائص في أنظمة كشف التسلل متعددة الفئات باستخدام خوارزميات التعلم الآلي، وذلك من خلال دراسة أثر اختيار الخصائص على استقرار المجموعات المختارة وأداء التصنيف والكفاءة الحسابية. استخدمت الدراسة مجموعة بيانات UNSW-NB15، وتم تطبيق خوارزميتي المعلومات المتبادلة (Mutual Information – MI) واختبار كاي تربيع (Chi-Square) لاختيار أفضل 20 خاصية من أصل 194 خاصية. وتم تقييم استقرار الاختيار باستخدام معامل جاكارد عبر خمس عينات عشوائية، كما تم تقييم أداء التصنيف باستخدام مقاييس Accuracy وPrecision وRecall وF1-score، إلى جانب قياس زمن التدريب والتنبؤ. أظهرت النتائج أن خوارزمية MI حققت أعلى استقرار في اختيار الخصائص بمتوسط معامل جاكارد بلغ 1.0000، مقارنة بـ0.8883 لخوارزمية Chi-Square. كما حققت MI أعلى قيمة لمقياس Macro F1-score بلغت 0.5226، وأعلى دقة كلية بلغت 0.7487. في المقابل، حققت خوارزمية Chi-Square أفضل كفاءة زمنية، حيث بلغ زمن التدريب 326.42 ثانية وزمن التنبؤ 1.09 ثانية. وتشير النتائج إلى أهمية تقييم خوارزميات اختيار الخصائص من جوانب متعددة تشمل الاستقرار وجودة التصنيف والكفاءة الحسابية، وعدم الاعتماد على مقياس واحد لتحديد الخوارزمية الأنسب لأنظمة كشف التسلل متعددة الفئات.

title: General Self-Efficacy and Academic Performance among Female BS Nursing Students: Evidence from College Records
abstract: Self-efficacy is typically linked to academic achievement. However, most of this evidence comes from study-specific measures or from students' own reports of their grades. This study focused on female BS Nursing students and examined whether there is a relationship between general self-efficacy and academic performance in these individuals as reported in college records. A cross-sectional survey was carried out at a nursing college in Sahiwal, Pakistan. A total of 203 students from all four years completed the General Self-Efficacy Scale, and the Examination In-charge recorded each student's CGPA or annual percentage from official records. The scale showed acceptable reliability (α = .79). The correlation between self-efficacy and academic performance was positive but small (ρ = .17, p = .017). Controlling for year of study made little difference to this correlation (partial r = .20, p = .004). Self-efficacy did not differ by year of study, residence, home area or age. Nursing students' academic performance is only mildly related to general self-efficacy. These findings can help nursing colleges decide where support for students' confidence is likely to matter most.
venue: Responsible Education Learning and Teaching in Emerging Economies

title: A Deep Autoencoder-based Adaptive Control Chart Framework under Weak Supervision for Industrial Anomaly Detection
abstract: Nowadays, industrial anomaly detection (IAD) is challenged by multi-dimensional data, nonlinear process behavior, and the lack of reliable fault labels. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Synergistic Machine Learning–Adaptive Control Chart (SML-ACC) framework under a weakly supervised setting for IAD. The framework combines data-driven feature learning with probabilistic supervision and adaptive statistical decision rules. Furthermore, this allows a reliable and interpretable process monitoring without requiring extensively labeled fault data. It is noted that normal process behavior was learned using only fault-free samples. In addition, deviations from normal operation were measured through fused anomaly scores, which are monitored using ACC with dynamically updated control limits. The proposed framework was evaluated using the three public industrial benchmark datasets namely Tennessee Eastman Process, Steel Plates, and SECOM dataset. Thereafter, the performance was analyzed through comprehensive benchmarking against classical statistical process control methods and unsupervised baselines. Notably, systematic ablation studies were conducted to evaluate the contribution of individual framework components. The results indicate that SML-ACC outperforms the tested classical SPC and unsupervised baseline methods in terms of F1 score and AUC value on the TEP and St…

Probabilistic redshift estimation of undetected galaxies from multi-band background light maps
abstract: Accurate knowledge of the redshift distributions of undetected galaxy populations is essential for extracting the cosmological information encoded in the cosmic optical background. We present the first framework for estimating these distributions directly from multi-band maps of unresolved background light, using conditional normalising flows trained on realistic image simulations. For imaging quality comparable to that expected from the survey and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), our model achieves sub-per cent accuracy in both the mean and standard deviation of the flux-weighted redshift distributions when the training and target samples are statistically well matched. Furthermore, the network proves highly resilient to incomplete photometric coverage when combined with tailored data imputation strategies. To address the challenge of statistical mismatches between simulations and real observations, we propose incorporating observational quantities into the target variables, providing a built-in diagnostic to assess model reliability and uncertainty from the predictions themselves. We also demonstrate the feasibility of map-based tomographic analyses, showing that the model retains sufficient pixel-level detail to recover redshift distributions for tomographically defined subsamples with near sub-per cent accuracy across all bins. title: AYOLLAR TADBIRKORLIGI RIVOJLANISHINING HUDUDIY IJTIMOIY-IQTISODIY SAMARADORLIKKA TA’SIRINI KO‘P OMILLI BAHOLASH MODELI
abstract: Ushbu maqolada ayollar tadbirkorligining hududlarning ijtimoiy-iqtisodiy rivojlanishidagi roli hamda uning hududiy samaradorlik ko‘rsatkichlariga ta’sirini aniqlash masalalari ko‘rib chiqiladi. Tadqiqotda ayollar tomonidan amalga oshiriladigan tadbirkorlik faoliyatining iqtisodiy faollikni oshirish, bandlik imkoniyatlarini kengaytirish, yangi ish o‘rinlarini yaratish va aholi daromadlarini oshirishdagi ahamiyatini aniqlashga alohida e’tibor qaratilgan. Tadqiqot davomida hududiy ijtimoiy-iqtisodiy samaradorlikni shakllantiruvchi omillar ularning o‘zaro bog‘liqligi nuqtayi nazaridan guruhlashtirildi hamda ayollar tadbirkorligi rivojlanish holatini tavsiflovchi ko‘rsatkichlar asosida ko‘p omilli baholash yondashuvi ishlab chiqildi. Bunda tadbirkorlik subyektlari soni, moliyalashtirish imkoniyatlari, ayollar bandligi, tadbirkorlikdan olinadigan daromadlar, davlat ko‘magining mavjudligi va biznes infratuzilmasi kabi omillarning hududiy natijalarga ta’siri asosiy mezon sifatida qaraldi. Olingan natijalar ayollar tadbirkorligining rivojlanish darajasi bilan hududning ijtimoiy-iqtisodiy ko‘rsatkichlari o‘rtasidagi bog‘liqlikni tizimli ravishda baholash imkonini beradi.

title: Shale‐Oil Micromigration and Sweet Spot Evaluation of the Shahejie Formation in the Dongying Sag, Bohai Bay Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT Strong heterogeneity of lacustrine shales in China hinders high‐precision shale‐oil sweet spot delineation, whereas the conventional “hydrocarbon generation‐retention” paradigm fails to account for widespread hydrocarbon micromigration. Here we systematically characterize micromigration in the Shahejie Formation shales from the Well NY1 of the Dongying Sag, Bohai Bay Basin, using Rock‐Eval pyrolysis, total organic carbon (TOC), and x‐ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, and establish a micromigration hydrocarbon ( δQ ) evaluation model. Results show widespread micromigration across the studied succession, with δQ values ranging from −523 to 559 mg/g TOC. Hydrocarbon intra‐micromigration (HIM) intervals account for 30.9% of the section and exhibit significantly higher oil content ( S 1 ) and oil mobility (quantified by the oil saturation index [OSI]) relative to hydrocarbon extra‐micromigration (HEM) intervals. Multiple geochemical evidences support micromigration, including suppressed T max values, abnormally elevated production index at low thermal maturity, and selective enrichment of light saturated hydrocarbon fractions in HIM intervals. Carbonate‐rich lithofacies are identified as preferential sites for hydrocarbon charging, whereas intervals with high TOC and high original hydrogen index tend to act as hydrocarbon expulsion zones. Mineral assemblages exert primary con…

title: Religious Identity Matters in Access to the Labour Market in India: Challenges Experienced by Muslims in Search of Livelihood
abstract: This study examines labour market inequalities faced by Muslims in India, highlighting the role of structural exclusion and religious discrimination in shaping employment outcomes. The findings show that Muslims are disproportionately concentrated in self-employment and casual wage labour, with limited access to regular salaried jobs, social security, paid leave, and stable workplaces, contributing to economic vulnerability. Decomposition analysis indicates that discrimination significantly influences labour market disparities, including lower labour force participation, higher informality, and lower wages. The study emphasizes the need for targeted public policies, including anti-discrimination measures, entrepreneurship support, skill development programmes, social security expansion, and gender-sensitive employment initiatives to improve labour market inclusion.

title: Caste and the Division of Laborer’s Linkage in the Indian Labor Market: Special Reference to the Rickshaw Pullers in Lucknow City, Uttar Pradesh, India
abstract: This study attempts to understand the Indian labor market specially the occupation of rickshaw pullers, which is primarily concerned with marginal communities who have been constitutionally identified as Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribe (STs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and religious minorities. In this regard, the essay articulates how a persistence caste system influences the choice of opting for any occupation in the Indian labor market despite constitutional guarantees (see. India’s Article 19 [1] [g]) to practice any occupation, trade or business. To examine the above social issue, this study applies survey method, which was conducted from March 2021 to October 2022 with 350 rickshaw pullers in Lucknow city, India. This present study concludes by examining Ambedkar’s views on caste and occupational preferences, focusing on how occupations such as rickshaw pulling, manual scavenging, cremation-related services, septic tank cleaning, waste collection, leatherwork, barbering, and fishing remain associated with historically marginalised social groups, whose limited access to landownership, education, property, and other assets has weakened their economic opportunities.

title: Integrated Management of Tar Spot of Corn with Organically-Allowed Fungicides in the Midwest United States
abstract: Tar spot of corn, caused by the fungus Phyllachora maydis , has emerged as a major foliar disease that can cause significant yield loss across the Midwest. First identified in the continental U.S. in 2015, P. maydis rapidly spread and is now documented in 20 states and in Ontario, Canada. Currently, there is limited information available on integrated management strategies for organic grain production systems, including the effectiveness of host resistance in organic hybrids and the efficacy of Organic Materials Review Institute (OMRI)-listed foliar fungicides. To fill this gap, field studies were conducted in Indiana and Wisconsin during the 2021, 2022, and 2023 growing seasons. These studies evaluated two organic hybrids (tar spot resistant and susceptible) and the efficacy of OMRI-listed foliar fungicides for tar spot and yield protection. In both Indiana and Wisconsin, tar spot severity varied greatly among years, and hybrid resistance provided the most consistent reduction in tar spot severity, particularly under moderate to high disease pressure. Among the products evaluated, only the conventional fungicide pyraclostrobin + metconazole consistently reduced tar spot and protected yield. Among the OMRI- listed products evaluated, copper oxychloride + copper hydroxide, Streptomycese lydicus , and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens only reduced tar spot severity under specific site-y…

title: Unlocking Rural Agricultural Markets in Adamawa State, Nigeria: Examining Market Access, Smallholder Farmers’ Welfare and Household Food Security
abstract: This study examined agricultural market access, smallholder farmers’ welfare and household food security in Adamawa State, Nigeria. A cross-sectional explanatory research design was adopted across six selected Local Government Areas (LGAs), namely Mubi North, Michika, Yola North, Fufore, Numan and Demsa. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire and complemented with secondary data from the Nigeria Living Standards Survey (NLSS) 2018/19 and relevant official statistical reports. The findings revealed that agricultural market access had a positive and statistically significant relationship with household food security. The research instrument demonstrated good internal consistency, with a Cronbach’s Alpha coefficient of 0.856. The regression model was statistically significant and explained 46.4% of the variation in farmers’ welfare and household food-security outcomes. Agricultural market access, household income, farm size, education, access to agricultural credit and extension services were positively associated with the outcomes, whereas household size was negatively associated with them. The study concludes that improved agricultural market access, supported by adequate financial services, extension support and productive resources, can contribute to enhanced smallholder farmers’ welfare and household food security. The study recommends strengthening rura…

title: Development and Experts Evaluation of a Virtual Laboratory System for Teaching Basic Electricity in Nigerian Technical Colleges
abstract: This article reports the development procedures and expert evaluation of a Virtual Laboratory System (VLS) designed to support the teaching of Basic Electricity in technical colleges in North-West Nigeria. The system was developed within a Research and Development study using the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation (ADDIE) model. Six Educational Technology experts assessed 30 proposed development procedures using a five-point suitability scale and evaluated the completed VLS using a 30-item, ten-point implementation rating scale. The development-procedure instrument and implementation rating scale had pilot-study Cronbach’s alpha coefficients of .902 and .966, respectively. Mean and standard deviation were used to analyse development procedures, while the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) was used to examine consistency among expert evaluations. The five ADDIE phases were all rated suitable; their average mean scores ranged from 4.33 to 4.46, and the overall average mean was 4.42. The developed system integrated digitised instructional materials, circuit diagrams, a virtual workbench using PhET Circuit Construction Kit, practical-report functions and a 25-item computer-based Basic Electricity Test. Expert ratings across the 30 evaluation items ranged from 5 to 10. The average-measures ICC was .863, indicating good reliability of the combined expe…

Abuse of Data-Driven Market Power and Monopsony of Personal Data by Social Commerce Platforms from a Competition Law Perspective
abstract: This study analyzes the abuse of data-driven market power and the monopsony of personal data by social commerce platforms, examined through the lens of Indonesian competition law. Employing a juridical-normative methodology utilizing both statutory and conceptual approaches the research investigates the implications of data concentration for anti-competitive practices. The findings indicate that the exclusive control of personal data by social commerce platforms creates significant barriers to entry for new market participants, reinforces dominant positions through network effects, and facilitates monopsonistic practices that disadvantage both producers and consumers. The deployment of algorithms and the large-scale collection of data lacking transparency trigger market distortions and discriminatory behaviors that are difficult to address using the conventional instruments of Law Number 5 of 1999 concerning the Prohibition of Monopolistic Practices and Unfair Business Competition. Consequently, a reinterpretation of competition law, integrated with personal data protection regulations, is essential to ensure a fair and competitive digital ecosystem.

title: Relative reinforcer efficacy and persistence in extinction are significantly correlated but not clinically actionable
abstract: Abstract Although assessments of relative reinforcer efficacy (RRE) have demonstrated utility for instructional programming, their relevance to informing treatment for challenging behavior is underexplored. Because reinforcer value moderates response persistence, RRE may serve as an index of persistence and could have prescriptive utility for treatment design. We targeted the persistence of arbitrary responses of 90 consenting and compensated adults with disabilities. We assigned participants to one of five baselines in which target responses were maintained on schedules prescribed by demand curve analysis (i.e., elastic‐EO, inelastic‐EO, elastic‐AO, inelastic‐AO, P max ) using reinforcers whose RRE had been quantified by breakpoints obtained during progressive‐ratio analysis. We then placed responding on extinction. Linear regressions revealed significant correlations between breakpoints and various metrics of persistence (i.e., rate, latency, reinforcers missed). These relations, however, were less apparent via visual inspection. Our data suggest progressive‐ratio analysis will not serve clinically useful functions without additional conceptual and validation work.

title: When will your model fail? TreeAlert: a method for predicting extreme forecasting failures
Dynamic machine learning models for the early prediction of acute kidney injury following left ventricular assist device implantation: An explainable AI approach
abstract: The risk of developing acute kidney injury (AKI) following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation is high, making its prediction essential. Current tools are limited by relying on static, preoperative data and “black-box” models. Our aim was to create a transparent prediction tool for AKI that integrates dynamic postoperative laboratory results with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). In a cohort of 138 LVAD patients, AKI was defined using KDIGO criteria within 7 days post-surgery. We evaluated LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost models, using the SMOTE method to manage class imbalance within a stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The LASSO model achieved the best performance with a ROC-AUC of 0.755. SHAP analysis revealed that dynamic postoperative laboratory changes were as important as baseline renal function in predicting AKI. Using risk scores calculated 48 h post-surgery, the model successfully predicted whether day 7 AKI would be “persistent” or “transient.” Accurately predicting post-LVAD AKI is feasible using an interpretable machine learning model that tracks dynamic data. This approach can serve as a reliable tool for early risk assessment, enabling physicians to identify high-risk patients earlier and implement proactive interventions.

Toxic Steam: A Large-Scale Characterization and Prediction of Toxic Users in a Gaming Platform
abstract: Steam is a major digital distribution platform for PC games, and its public game reviews provide a setting for studying toxic discourse. Although message-level toxicity detection has been widely studied, user-level analysis has received less attention, particularly on gaming platforms. This study characterized toxicity across 36.8 million English-language reviews from 14.2 million users. Detector-labeled toxicity was rare (1.86% of reviews, 3.95% of users), with higher rates in competitive game contexts; 57.5% of flagged reviews nonetheless recommended the reviewed game. Building on this characterization, we introduced a prevalence-aware benchmark spanning classical models, fine-tuned transformers, and Large Language Models (LLMs), with primary evaluations at approximately 4% positive prevalence. Text-derived representations achieved higher AUC-PR than profile metadata (up to 0.643 versus 0.070). A leave-toxic-out control retained a weaker signal after removing the reviews that defined each user's label, suggesting that performance depended substantially on direct access to the label-defining text. LLM classifiers obtained lower AUC-PR on their smaller evaluation sample, while narrative generators produced evidence-linked explanations for inspection. Their utility for human-review triage remained unvalidated. These results supported further study of user-level prediction as a t…

DeepCPP: A Deep Learning‐Based Framework for Enhanced Prediction of Cell Penetrating Peptides
abstract: Cell‐penetrating peptides (CPPs) are bioactive molecules characterized by a positive charge, primarily attributed to lysine, arginine, or histidine residues, which enable their traversal across cells’ lipid bilayer membranes. This unique property positions CPPs as promising candidates for intracellular delivery of therapeutic agents. The expanding database of experimentally validated CPPs has facilitated significant advancements in computational modeling, enabling in silico prediction and engineering of established and novel CPPs. Despite progress in this domain, challenges persist in improving the performance of CPP prediction models. This study introduces DeepCPP, a new deep learning‐based framework for efficient CPP prediction. DeepCPP employs a multihead decision‐level late‐fusion approach that uses a trainable weighted fusion mechanism to combine branch‐specific predictions generated by a multilayer convolutional neural network‐guided encoder and a multilayer graph neural network‐guided encoder. These encoders learn evolutionary features from an evolutionary information‐based representation and chemical, topological, and stereochemical features from a molecular graph‐based representation, respectively. Comprehensive experiments conducted on established benchmark datasets reveal the effectiveness of the DeepCPP model, exhibiting performance superior to state‐of‐the‐art mode…

Automated Prediction of Diabetes-Related Foot Ulcer Healing at Initial Assessment
abstract: Background: Diabetes-related foot ulcers (DFUs) that fail to heal within the expected trajectory and become chronic are associated with substantial morbidity. The current clinical standard for identifying chronic DFUs relies on a <50% reduction in wound area over 4 weeks. There is a critical need for tools that can predict wound-healing outcomes at first clinical presentation to enable timely, individualised wound management. We have developed and validated TherMUL, an AI device that analyses the texture of thermal images to predict DFU healing. Methods: Adults with neuropathic DFUs were recruited from 2 specialist foot clinics in Melbourne, Australia. TherMUL, a software-based device, was used to take thermal images during the initial visit. Texture features were extracted using grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) analysis. Wound-healing status at 12 weeks served as the ground-truth label for model training. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier was trained using the images from 44 healed and 24 unhealed DFUs. A separate unseen dataset was used for a preliminary feasibility assessment. Results: The classifier achieved a mean area under the curve (AUC) of 0.635, with a sensitivity of 75.8% for predicting unhealed DFUs, and a specificity of 53% for identifying healed DFUs. In the preliminary evaluation, 5 of 7 predictions correctly matched the 12-week podiatry outcomes. C…

title: Before the Policy: Developing Academic Leaders and Institutional Capacity for the Governance of Agentic AI
abstract: Institutional policies for agentic artificial intelligence are only as good as the leaders and structures that must operate them, yet presidents, provosts, deans, and boards receive almost no systematic preparation for AI governance. This conceptual paper defines the institutional layer of agentic AI governance, explains why senior leaders are its least developed actors, and proposes an institutional AI governance capacity model with three layers: individual governance fluency, structural capacity, and adaptive readiness. Development mechanisms, a board-level readiness diagnostic, and the accountability and ethics of governing the governors are discussed.
venue: Journal of Leadership, Accountability and Ethics

title: Intermittent Fasting Remodels Mitochondrial Morphology and Bioenergetic Capacity in Brown Adipose Tissue of Obese Mice
abstract: ABSTRACT Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a specialized adipose tissue that is associated with thermogenesis, endocrine function, and energy expenditure, characterized by a high mitochondrial density. However, obesity induces profound structural and functional remodeling of mitochondria in BAT, compromising their thermogenic and oxidative capacities. On the other hand, intermittent fasting is a non‐pharmacological approach that can enhance mitochondrial function, thereby contributing to weight loss. Despite this, the effects of intermittent fasting on the morphofunctional aspects of BAT mitochondria are not yet well understood. Thus, we investigated the effects of a chronic 16:8 daily intermittent fasting protocol over 8 weeks on the BAT mitochondria of obese mice. Diet‐induced obesity reduced energy expenditure, increased body weight gain, and adiposity within the BAT. Obesity altered BAT mitochondrial morphology, resulting in smaller, more rounded organelles with disrupted cristae. Conversely, intermittent fasting increased energy expenditure, reduced body weight gain and adiposity within the BAT, increased the UCP1 protein content, and restored browning in the BAT. Remarkably, intermittent fasting promoted extensive remodeling of mitochondrial dynamics protein markers and structural profile in BAT, increasing mitochondrial elongation, total cristae length, and cristae alignment…

Intrinsically Linear and Robust Capacitive Strain Sensors Based on Area‐Variation Mechanism for Soft Machines
abstract: Flexible capacitive strain sensors are essential for soft machines, yet conventional distance‐variation designs inherently exhibit nonlinear responses and limited mechanical robustness. Here we report an intrinsically linear capacitive strain sensor based on an area‐variation mechanism. The sensor employs laser‐micromachined carbon fiber interdigitated electrodes fully encapsulated in polydimethylsiloxane. This yields a highly linear electromechanical response, while experimental deviations in baseline capacitance are attributed to parasitic wire capacitance. For a typical sensor, the electromechanical response exhibits exceptional linearity ( R 2 = 0.9995) and a high sensing accuracy of 0.381% full scale across the entire strain range. The sensor preferentially responds to axial tension with small response of normal compression, while retaining stable performance following over‐range stretching, mechanical impact, and ten water immersion‐drying cycles. When integrated into a smart glove, the sensor enables real‐time, high‐linearity capture of finger‐bending strains for accurate gesture recognition. Embedding the sensor in a cable‐driven soft continuum robot further allows precise monitoring of microstrains in actuation wires, supporting real‐time shape reconstruction with accuracy comparable to that of commercial force sensors. This area‐variation sensing strategy resolves the…

title: The Role of Digital Transformation as A Mechanism to Attract Foreign Direct Investments in The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia: in the light of Vision 2030
abstract: The research aimed to study the relationship between digital economy indicators (network readiness index, Internet service subscription rate index out of the total population, fixed and mobile phone subscriptions, broadband service subscriptions) as independent variables and the business environment and foreign direct investment index as dependent variables during the time period (2006). – 2023) with the application of the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) method and Robust regression in order to avoid the problem of Heteroskedasticity. The study found that there is only a positive and significant relationship between the network readiness index and foreign direct investment, while the index of the percentage of Internet service subscriptions out of the total population and broadband service subscriptions. The results showed the opposite of our expectations, which is negative and significant on foreign direct investment. In addition to this, the indicator of the percentage of Internet service subscriptions out of the total population, mobile phone subscriptions, and broadband service subscriptions have a positive statistical significance on the business environment index.

title: Alchemical Transfer Free Energy Perturbation Simulations Reveal Entropic Mechanism Governing the Binding of a Charged Peptide to a Protein Target
abstract: Abstract We combined alchemical transfer free energy perturbation (FEP) and replica exchange with solute tempering (REST) molecular dynamics to probe the energetics of the binding of a charged peptide to a protein target. For this purpose, we have selected the coreNLS peptide KKPKKE, the conserved fragment from the nuclear localization signal (NLS) sequence in viral capsid protein binding to nuclear transporter importin-α (impα). This peptide binds to impα, natively forming a specific pose similar to that resolved experimentally. The two main outcomes of our work are as follows. First, we further develop the FEP methodology. Alchemical transfer is a rarely used version of FEP, in which an unbound peptide is gradually decoupled, while the bound peptide is coupled. Because the net charge of the system remains unchanged, no charge-related corrections within FEP are necessary. Additionally, our FEP protocol utilizes a “laissez faire” soft-walled flat-bottom spherical restraint, which does not affect a ligand as long as it occupies the major NLS binding site in impα. We showed that combining FEP with REST molecular dynamics affords exhaustive sampling of the binding process and reduces the free energy error down to 0.4 kcal/mol. Second, we found that the coreNLS binds impα with moderate affinity of ΔGb0 = −4.6 kcal/mol. We analyzed the factors contributing to binding energetics. Dir…

Resource‐efficient potato fertilization in acid Inceptisols using a soil‐test crop response framework: Mineral‐input savings, field validation, and screening upstream urea‐manufacturing implications
abstract: Abstract Efficient fertilizer management in acid soils requires decision frameworks that translate soil‐test variability into crop‐specific nutrient demand while minimizing unnecessary mineral inputs. This study developed and field‐validated Soil Test Crop Response (STCR) fertilizer prescriptions for potato under acid Inceptisol conditions in Meghalaya, India. A three‐phase field program conducted during 2022–2024 established fertility gradients, derived crop nutrient‐response parameters, and independently validated STCR‐NPK and integrated plant nutrient supply (STCR‐IPNS) prescriptions at target yields of 100, 125, and 150 q ha −1 . Nutrient requirements for producing one quintal of tubers were 0.56 kg N, 0.26 kg P, and 0.93 kg K. Across the prescription matrix, FYM integration reduced mineral‐N demand by 23.76–23.80 kg N ha −1 and K 2 O demand by 7.0–7.1 kg ha −1 , while realized P 2 O 5 savings ranged from 0 to 32.7 kg ha −1 depending on soil‐test P and target yield. Aggregate realized mineral nutrient‐equivalent savings ranged from 30.76 to 63.60 kg ha −1 . All six targeted‐yield treatments remained within ±10% of prescribed yields, with a mean absolute target deviation of 6.04%, and STCR‐IPNS maintained tuber yield relative to STCR‐NPK. title: A Monotone Rational–Quadratic Spline Driven High‐Fidelity Open Circuit Voltage Modeling for Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable state estimation of Li‐ion batteries in energy applications depends largely on accurate modeling of the open‐circuit voltage (OCV), denoted by V oc , as a function of state of charge (SoC). The V oc –SoC characteristic is conventionally represented using high‐order polynomials or lookup tables stored in the battery management system (BMS). High‐order polynomial models may suffer from numerical issues and generally require numerical root‐finding for inverse mapping, whereas lookup‐table approaches may require a dense set of breakpoints, leading to increased memory usage. To address these limitations, this article proposes a monotone rational–quadratic spline (RQS) framework for V oc –SoC modeling. A greedy knot‐selection algorithm is incorporated into the RQS framework to adaptively select breakpoints along the V oc –SoC characteristic. The proposed approach is validated on test data from six Li‐ion cells with different chemistries, collected at multiple operating temperatures. The proposed method provides a smooth and monotonic representation with analytical invertibility and low computational complexity compared to conventional models. The efficient pseudo‐ V oc ‐based SoC reconstruction suggests the proposed framework's potential suitability for integration into real‐time BMS applications.

title: Experimental Investigation of Phase Change Materials for Enhancing Solar Air Vortex Engine Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar air vortex engines are promising technologies for converting solar energy into clean thermal and kinetic energy. However, fluctuations in solar radiation significantly affect their performance, and their ability to operate continuously during periods of low radiation intensity is limited. This study aims to experimentally evaluate the performance of a solar air vortex engine (SAVE) integrated with a phase‐change material (PCM) to improve thermal stability and extend operating life. Asphalt was used as the phase‐change material and stored in aluminum containers placed inside the solar collector. The experiments were conducted in Kirkuk, Iraq (35.47°N, 44.39°E), under real‐world operating conditions, and the system's performance was compared with and without the phase‐change material. The results showed that incorporating the phase‐change material reduced the maximum air temperature from 72.7°C to 68.1°C and the maximum air velocity from 2.7 to 2.5 m/s during peak conditions, due to thermal energy absorption and storage. Kinetic power and usable thermal energy decreased by 18.3% and 20.8%, respectively, during peak hours. Conversely, the phase‐change material improved system performance during periods of low solar irradiance. Air temperature at the end of operation increased by 17.4%, kinetic power rose from 0.58 to 7.86 mW, and thermal efficiency improved by 54.7%…

title: Mini-review on the production of Primordial Black Holes fromFirst-Order Phase Transitions in the Early Universe
abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) can provide a possible connection between the physics of the early Universeand the dark matter. Among the various PBH formation mechanisms, cosmological first-order phase transitions (FOPTs) can generate PBHs through density perturbations arising from the stochastic nucleation oftrue-vacuum bubbles. In this mini-review, we focus on PBH formation from delayed false-vacuum decayduring slow and strongly supercooled FOPTs. We first review how stochastic bubble nucleation can generate non-Gaussian density perturbations and how these perturbations can lead to PBH formation and anextended PBH mass function. Wethendiscussagaugeinconsistency in the conventional treatment, arisingfrom combining density perturbations and the PBH collapse threshold defined in different gauges, and itsimplications for the predicted PBH abundance. Finally, we discuss delayed reheating and the possibility ofan intermediate early matter-dominated epoch as a potential way to revive PBH formation, and highlightthe remaining theoretical uncertainties and future directions
venue: Progress in High Energy Physics PHEP

title: PoET²S: Folding a digital twin into validator selection for blockchain consensus in peer-to-peer energy trading
abstract: Blockchain platforms for peer-to-peer energy trading often add a digital twin that forecasts each meter's generation and demand. In most designs the twin only raises alarms, while validators are still chosen by stake or computation. The proposed scheme, PoET²S, incorporates the twin's evidence into validator selection: a node's weight is a stake-and-energy term multiplied by its Twin-Trust Score raised to γ = 2.5, so nodes that contradict the physical forecast quickly lose committee seats. A discrete-event simulator compares PoET²S (500 nodes, 15% Byzantine, 30 paired seeds) with seven classical baselines and three design points from recent work: a binary veto, an additive energy-and-trust score, and a linear (γ = 1) reputation weight. Detection is a near-tie: PoET²S catches 91.0% of attackers and the veto 91.7%. PoET²S raises more false alarms per catch by default (13.9 against 9.7) but matches the veto's catch rate at equal false-alarm cost. The malicious committee share is 10.8% under the veto, 3.8% under the linear weight, and 2.6% under PoET²S, and on 100 seeds the gain over the linear weight is 37% (Holm-adjusted p = 7.2 × 10⁻⁹). At 45% Byzantine nodes, the one-third fault bound fails in 64.4% of veto blocks and 2.4% of PoET²S blocks. Simulated commit latency (30.2 ms) is higher than for Proof of Stake and Delegated Proof of Stake, lower than for Practical Byzantine Fault…

title: Explainable AI-Based Vehicle Damage Assessment and Insurance Decision Support System
abstract: Vehicle insurance claim processing still depends heavily on manual inspection by human surveyors, which is slow, subjective, and difficult to scale. Existing deep learning systems largely stop at detecting or segmenting damage, and offer no repair cost estimation, no explanation of their predictions, and no clear recommendation on the claim itself. This paper proposes an Explainable AI-based Vehicle Damage Assessment and Insurance Decision Support System that connects damage detection and segmentation, damage type classification, repair cost estimation, fraud risk assistance, and a claim recommendation with a confidence score into one pipeline. Explainability is built in through Grad-CAM, which highlights the image regions behind a prediction, and SHAP/LIME, which expose the factors that drive the cost and decision outputs. The system finally generates an explainable report for both customers and insurance staff. The design is based on a survey of recent work on vehicle damage assessment and is planned for implementation using YOLOv11, OpenCV, and the CarDD dataset together with a custom vehicle image dataset.
authors: Jeenus C Jino, Devsankar V Babu, Anandhakrishnan
Ashish Krishna, Sudharma G, Anjitha P
