title: How Are Business Strategy and ESG Performance Associated With Stock Liquidity? Global Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether business strategy is associated with stock liquidity and whether environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance conditions this association. Using 58,638 firm‐year observations from 74 countries during 2008–2023, we find no significant association for the continuous strategy score. In categorical analyses, Defender firms exhibit higher illiquidity and Analyzer firms lower illiquidity, both at the 10% significance level, while no reliable average association is found for Prospectors. ESG performance is associated with lower illiquidity in the continuous‐score specification. Marginal‐effects analysis shows that ESG moderates these relationships asymmetrically: higher ESG reduces the Defender illiquidity disadvantage but attenuates the Analyzer liquidity advantage, while the Prospector marginal effect remains insignificant across observed ESG levels. The principal strategy‐specific and interaction patterns are broadly robust across alternative liquidity measures, lagged specifications, crisis‐period exclusions, country‐sample restrictions, log‐transformed illiquidity, and supplementary System GMM estimates.

title: How does a disaster change consumers' belief systems and retail expenditure?
abstract: Abstract Theory of awe suggests that awe elicited by disasters can affect both consumers' belief systems, such as new ecological paradigm (NEP), and their behavioral patterns. In this vein, this research examined how a disaster experience was associated with consumers' NEP endorsement and shopping motivations. It also profiled consumers based on expenditure changes across product categories, comparing pandemic experiences, NEP, shopping motivations, and demographic characteristics. Analysis of responses from 259 U.S. consumers confirmed the NEP as a central mechanism linked to consumption changes and identified four consumer typologies with unique profiles, offering insights for retailers to predict consumer behaviors during future disasters.
venue: Family and Consumer Sciences Research Journal

title: Consumer Innovation Resistance in Green Product Competition: Pricing, Subsidies, and Promotional Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Consumer innovation resistance can persist even when consumers value environmental performance. This study examines how resistance affects green‐product pricing and innovation, and when producer subsidies, consumer subsidies, or private promotion improve market outcomes and welfare. A differentiated duopoly model allows the green firm to choose product greenness before price competition. Explicit equilibrium expressions and boundary comparisons identify economically admissible green‐degree choices. With endogenous greenness, greater resistance reduces innovation except at a knife‐edge cost coefficient, while increasing the green firm's optimized profit; the green‐demand response depends on the unit‐cost coefficient. Producer subsidies increase innovation, but need not increase green demand. Consumer subsidies increase optimized green‐firm profit, while the consumer‐paid price rises when induced innovation exceeds an explicit pass‐through threshold. Private promotion increases demand, effort, and profit on the strict interior branch. For low unit‐cost coefficients, its innovation effect changes sign at an analytical conversion‐efficiency threshold: beyond that threshold, promotion substitutes for product improvement. Welfare comparisons yield environmental‐benefit and public‐funds thresholds rather than a universal ranking of the three channels. Numerical experiments ev…

title: Immediate Marking and Feedback in Higher Education: A Transformational Assessment Strategy Using a Case Study Approach
abstract: Previous research highlights a persistent misalignment between tutor feedback intentions and student understanding, a challenge often intensified by delayed feedback practices in higher education assessment. This study aims to examine the impact of an immediate marking and feedback approach on student engagement, academic performance, and progression within a first-year undergraduate module. Using a case study design, the research evaluates the implementation of a revised assessment regime introduced in 2023, in which a traditional essay with a three-week feedback turnaround was replaced by a skills-focused portfolio assessment. The portfolio was supported through structured, in-class scaffolding and assessed via same-day marking accompanied by individualized, verbal feedback delivered during one-to-one sessions. The findings indicate substantial improvements in student outcomes and engagement. All students who submitted the portfolio achieved a pass (100% pass rate), academic misconduct was notably reduced, and student attendance reached its highest level for the module. In addition, staff reported greater efficiency and reduced marking workload compared to the previous assessment model. The study concludes that immediate marking and feedback can significantly enhance assessment effectiveness by improving feedback clarity, supporting student learning in real time, and strength…

title: Integrating Sustainability and Resilience in Multinational Supply Chains: Evidence From Post‐COVID‐19 Strategic Adaptation in Singapore
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability and resilience have become central strategic concerns in contemporary supply chains, yet their integration remains insufficiently understood in empirical research. Existing studies show that the relationship between resilience and sustainability is neither uniformly complementary nor uniformly conflictive but depends on the practices and decisions under consideration. This study examines how multinational companies in Singapore integrated sustainability and resilience into their supply chain strategies during and after the COVID‐19 disruption. Drawing on sensemaking as the theoretical lens and an abductive grounded‐theory approach, we conducted in‐depth interviews with senior supply chain professionals from multinational companies operating in Singapore. The findings identify five interrelated strategic domains through which firms redesigned supply chains after disruption: supply chain focus and visibility, inventory and sourcing, collaboration and communication, technology integration, and sustainability orientation. Rather than treating sustainability as a separate concern, managers linked it to supplier configuration, nearshoring and local sourcing decisions, information sharing, technology‐enabled visibility, and longer‐term partnership development. At the same time, the evidence indicates persistent tensions between efficiency and buffering, flexibi…

title: Business Responses to Competing Institutional Logics in the Climate Change Field: An Experiment
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine how competing institutional logics shape corporate responses to climate change. We theorize the climate change field as a competitive issue field where a dominant market logic of short‐term profit maximization confronts an emerging environmental logic prioritizing emissions reduction. We model shareholders as carriers of normative and coercive forces and competitors as carriers of mimetic forces, and test four hypotheses through a vignette experiment. Participants predicted the amount an oil and gas manager would invest in reducing emissions. Results show that environmental logic consistently increases expected emissions‐reduction investments relative to market logic. When shareholders' and competitors' logics conflict, participants expect managers to follow shareholders rather than competitors. Adding divestment threats as a coercive force did not produce a statistically detectable incremental effect beyond normative pressure alone. We identify shareholder‐expressed environmental logic as a potentially important lever for organizational decarbonization, creating opportunity for future research to examine its practical impact.

title: Self-Directed Learning among English Majors at Thu Dau Mot University: Strategy Use, Perceived Effectiveness and Challenges
abstract: The increasing demand for English proficiency in Vietnam’s globalised academic and professional contexts raises the question of whether university students use self-learning strategies to strengthen their language skills outside the classroom. This study examined how often English majors at Thu Dau Mot University use self-directed learning (SDL) strategies, how effective they perceive these strategies to be, and what challenges they face when applying them. A descriptive quantitative design was adopted, and questionnaire data from 200 English majors were analysed using descriptive statistics and Cronbach’s alpha. The results show that students used strategies related to motivation, self-monitoring and self-management at a moderate level but rated their effectiveness more highly. Difficulty managing study schedules, procrastination and staying disciplined were the most reported challenges, and many students found it difficult to verify information from digital and AI tools. The findings also suggest that students recognise the value of SDL strategies but do not yet apply them regularly, and that they need support in time management and in the critical use of digital resources.

title: From Expectation to Strategy: Plurilingual Publishing Practices and Intellectual Footprint in Early‐Career Scholarship
abstract: Abstract This qualitative study focuses on early‐career scholars working in francophone institutions in Canada as they negotiate plurilingual research publication practices. Data from four early‐career scholars, collected across two interview rounds over a two‐year period, show how language choice in publishing is a complex process which cannot be understood simply through the lens of linguistic proficiency. Instead, the participants' trajectories reflect strategic and agentive decisions shaped by audience, institutional context, and evolving professional identities. While English was initially viewed as a pathway to scholarly legitimacy, participants increasingly mobilized French, thereby expanding their engagement across communities. The findings also highlight the role of access to resources and geographic positioning in enabling plurilingual publishing practices, alongside a shift toward greater agency in publication decision‐making over time. By documenting how early‐career scholars move from aligning with dominant publishing norms to actively shaping their own dissemination practices, this study contributes to research on English for Research Publication Purposes while foregrounding the importance of plurilingual approaches to scholarly communication. More broadly, the findings position plurilingual publishing as central to promoting more inclusive and context‐responsive …

title: The Interplay of Green Intellectual Capital, Artificial Intelligence, Frugal Innovation, and Triple Bottom Line Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT The study analyzes the critical role of green intellectual capital (GIC) in enhancing SMEs' economic, social, and environmental performance, with frugal innovation (FI) mediating these relationships. The study also investigates the moderating effect of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on the relationship between GIC and FI. The hypotheses were tested using PLS‐SEM. Data were collected from 318 manufacturing SMEs operating in three Pakistani cities. Our findings indicate that GIC significantly influences firms' economic, social, and environmental performance in an emerging economy and that FI mediates these relationships. Furthermore, AI adoption strengthens the relationship between GIC and FI. To our knowledge, no previous study has systematically examined GIC, FI, and AI adoption alongside economic, social, and environmental performance, particularly in the context of manufacturing SMEs in an emerging Asian economy. First, this study examines the mediating role of FI in the relationship between GIC and triple bottom line (TBL) performance. Second, it analyzes the moderating role of AI adoption in the relationship between GIC and FI, highlighting the role of technology adoption in strengthening this relationship. Finally, it extends the resource‐based view (RBV) to a technological context by examining how GIC, FI, and AI adoption affect TBL performance.

title: Thermoregulatory strategy shapes physiological responses to dormancy in animals: A meta‐analysis
abstract: Abstract Dormancy allows animals to persist through prolonged periods of unfavourable environmental conditions by entering states of extreme metabolic depression. However, physiological responses to dormancy vary substantially across taxa and can involve changes in redox balance, immune function and endocrine adjustments. A key unresolved question is whether this variation reflects fundamental differences in how endotherms and ectotherms regulate metabolic depression and subsequent reactivation, with implications for understanding animal life histories and responses to climate change. Here, we conducted a meta‐analysis to test whether physiological responses to dormancy differ between endothermic and ectothermic animals. We synthesised 2464 effect sizes from 106 studies across 57 species, quantifying redox, immune and glucocorticoid status during dormant and arousal states relative to active, non‐dormant state, under cold‐ and heat‐induced dormancy. In endotherms, dormant and arousal states were associated with reduced oxidative damage and reactive oxygen species production, together with increased antioxidant and redox‐regulatory activity, indicating robust maintenance of redox homeostasis across metabolic transitions. In contrast, ectotherms experienced increased oxidative damage during the dormant state under both cold‐ and heat‐induced conditions, with little evidence for c…

title: A Two‐Stage Strategy to Reprogram Cyanine Photosensitizers as Controllable‐Pyroptosis Inducers for Anticancer Phototherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyroptosis, a lytic and inflammatory form of programmed cell death, provides a promising strategy for antitumor immunotherapy. However, controllable modulation of pyroptosis using phototherapeutic agents remains challenging. In this study, we report a two‐stage molecular reprogramming method to rationally design cyanine photosensitizers with tunable pyroptosis‐inducing activity. We first reprogram IR808 into a novel photosensitizer T808, by integrating a tetraphenylethylene unit with IR808, which consequently enhances excited ‐ state features related to intersystem crossing (ISC) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation capability, accompanied by inducing pyroptosis under irradiation. In the second process, T808 is conjugated with poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) chains of varying lengths (M.W. 550, 1000, and 2000 Da) to finely modulate the pyroptotic efficacy. The relationship of PEG chain length with pyroptosis‐inducing activity is in the order of PT550 > T808 > PT1000 >> PT2000. Cellular and in vivo studies show that T808, PT550, and PT1000 treatments suppress tumor growth and induce pyroptosis with occurrence of immunogenic cell death (ICD). Even under a lower intratumoral injection dose (25 µM), T808 and PT550 therapies exhibit remarkable antitumor efficacy with measurable pyroptosis features. This work provides a new insight into reprogramming cyanine photosensiti…

title: Greenhushing as Strategic Adaptation: Net‐Zero Commitment Retreat Among S&P 500 Firms Amid Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Backlash
abstract: ABSTRACT Greenhushing has emerged as a strategic corporate response to political and regulatory uncertainty, yet less is known about how firms recalibrate previously established sustainability signals when external conditions change. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines changes in corporate climate and ESG commitments during the political transition to the second Trump administration. Using qualitative content analysis of corporate disclosures and public communications, we identify 32 large US firms that modified, weakened, or withdrew previously stated commitments between September 2024 and August 2025. Among these firms, 13 (41%) were associated with political or regulatory pressure, 8 (25%) linked changes to rising AI and data‐center demand, and 11 (34%) pointed to profit‐driven refocusing, market uncertainty, or broader regulatory ambiguity. The findings reveal clear sectoral differences in how firms recalibrated sustainability signals. Financial institutions exhibited the most direct and visible retrenchment, particularly through withdrawals from net‐zero alliances and changes in ESG‐related communication. Technology firms more often retained long‐term climate commitments while reducing the visibility, prominence, or certainty of interim targets. Other sectors showed less visible but still consequential forms of retreat, including target modification and the Sc…

title: Factor Structure and Psychometric Properties of the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-12 in Multiple Sclerosis
abstract: Despite the high prevalence of anxiety disorders in multiple sclerosis (MS) and the inherent uncertainty associated with the disease, it is unclear whether current measures of intolerance of uncertainty (IU) are appropriate for people with MS. In this study, we describe the psychometric features of the short-form Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale (IUS-12) in a mixed sample of 2,084 participants (244 MS, 1,840 non-MS controls). A bifactor model best represented the IUS-12 in the MS group. The IUS-12 appeared suitable in MS, demonstrating good construct validity and moderate test–retest reliability over the 6-month survey period. Measurement invariance was found across MS and non-MS participants. Of note, IU scores were comparable between groups, but IU showed stronger associations with anxiety-related pathologies in participants with MS than non-MS controls. Routine assessment incorporating the IUS-12 may help clarify factors underpinning anxiety and inform the development of targeted psychological interventions for people with MS.

title: Financial Sentiment Classification Using Traditional Machine Learning, BERT, FinBERT, and Zero-Shot FLAN-T5
abstract: Financial sentiment classification is a challenging natural language processing task because financial text often combines specialized terminology, implicit sentiment, numerical information, and context that cannot always be captured by simple lexical patterns. This study presents a controlled comparison of five approaches for three-class financial sentiment classification: TF-IDF with Logistic Regression, TF-IDF with a Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM), BERT, FinBERT, and zero-shot FLAN-T5. The experiments use the Financial PhraseBank dataset, which contains 4,846 financial statements labeled as negative, neutral, or positive. The principal experiment uses a stratified 70/15/15 train-validation-test split with random seed 42, and all five models are evaluated on the same test partition. Logistic Regression obtains 73.31% accuracy and a 63.35% macro F1 score, while Linear SVM obtains 74.69% and 68.15%, respectively. BERT reaches 85.01% accuracy and 83.18% macro F1, whereas FinBERT achieves 88.72% accuracy and 87.43% macro F1. Zero-shot FLAN-T5 records 37.69% accuracy and 36.15% macro F1. To provide additional statistical context, bootstrap confidence intervals and exact McNemar tests are applied to the fixed test predictions. A separate three-seed robustness experiment is also conducted for FinBERT using seeds 42, 123, and 2024. Across these runs, FinBERT obtains a mean accur…

title: Countering populist radical-right parties: the institutional foundations of strategic voting, forced mobility, and party coordination in France and Germany
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates how institutional configurations shape strategic voting, forced mobility, and party coordination against populist radical right parties (PRRPs). As PRRPs expand their electoral support across Europe, voters and parties increasingly coordinate to prevent them from gaining power, but the forms and feasibility of such coordination vary across political systems. We argue that electoral systems, party-system structure, and type of democracy jointly shape the incentives and opportunities for electoral coordination and strategic voting. Drawing on France and Germany as theory-building cases, we distinguish strategic voting – the deliberate abandonment of a preferred viable option in a contest involving at least three viable alternatives – from forced mobility in second-round runoffs and party coordination through candidate withdrawals and electoral alliances. In France, two-round legislative elections create repeated opportunities for strategic voting, forced mobility, and party coordination, while the fluid party system and semi-presidentialism facilitate voter realignment. In Germany, the mixed-member proportional electoral system, a more structured party system, and a durable cordon sanitaire around the AfD reduce the need and scope for large-scale strategic voting among voters.

CREATION OF AN UNMANNED AGRICULTURAL TRACKED MOBILE POWER PLANT OF TRACTION CLASS 8 WITH AN ELECTROMECHANICAL TRANSMISSION
abstract: The use of mobile, electrically powered energy systems increases the productivity and operational qualities of machines, reduces their environmental impact, and expands opportunities for digitalization through integration.with digital monitoring, telemetry and autonomous control systems. The purpose of these studies is to develop robotic unmanned transport and technological means with a capacity of about 410 hp and a complex of technological machines for gardening in order to achieve the results of the departmental project "Development of institutes for grant support to researchers, scientific and creative teams" of the state program of the Russian Federation "Scientific and Technological Development of the Russian Federation". The object of the study is agricultural robotic unmanned transport and technological means (RBTTS) with an electromechanical transmission (EMT) with the conventional name "RBTTS-400" and a complex of technological machines for gardening (lifting platform, circular circular pruner, fan sprayer, herbicide sprayer). At this stage, the layout of a tractor with a triangular caterpillar track, its frame, as well as the basic and kinematic circuits of the electromechanical power transmission have been developed.

title: Using AI Effectively in Financial Modeling Modeler Responsibility from Problem Definition to Decision Support
abstract: Artificial intelligence can accelerate financial modeling, but it does not relieve the modeler of responsibility for the model or its conclusions. The central challenge is to use AI effectively without surrendering ownership of the model's purpose, structure, assumptions, logic, and evidence. This article presents the FRAME → DESIGN → BUILD → VERIFY framework as a practical approach to that challenge. FRAME defines the decision, intended user, scope, sources, and required outputs. DESIGN establishes the architecture, economic drivers, assumptions, scenarios, and controls. BUILD implements approved logic in manageable sections that can be understood and tested. VERIFY applies three distinct levels of review: technical verification, financial verification, and decision verification. The framework adds to established modeling practice by defining appropriate AI roles at each stage, identifying evidence of human ownership, and separating technical verification, financial verification, and decision verification. It applies to professional practice and finance education and is illustrated through private wealth management, capital budgeting, and financial forecasting. The modeler remains responsible for the integrity and defensibility of the analysis within the modeler's assigned role, while the decision-maker remains accountable for the decision. The framework does not certify accur…

abstract: تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تقييم الأداء المالي للمصارف التجارية الليبية من خلال تطبيق معيار كفاية رأس المال المعتمد دوليا (معيار لجنة بازل) والتعليمات الصادرة عن مصرف ليبيا المركزي, ولتحقيق هذه الهدف اعتمدت الدراسة على المنهج الوصفي التحليلي لمعالجة الجوانب النظرية إلى جانب المنهج الاحصائي لتحليل البيانات المالية الصادرة عن المصارف التجارية خلال فترة الدراسة. وقد خلصت الدراسة إلى جملة من النتائج كان أبرزها تباين مستوى التزام المصارف التجارية الليبية بالنسب المعيارية لكفاية رأس المال وجود مساهمة لمعيار كفاية رأس المال في تقييم الأداء المالي للمصارف التجارية الليبية وقدرة المصارف على مواجهة المخاطر المحتملة كالائتمانية والتشغيلية وفي ضور هذه النتائج توصي الدراسة بضرورة تدعيم القواعد الرأسمالية للمصارف, وتفعيل أدوات الرقابة المصرفية، والالتزام المستمر بالمتطلبات المعيارية الصادرة عن الجهات الرقابية لضمان سلامة القطاع المصرفي وحماية حقوق المودعين.

title: Frequency-Aware Indexing for Spatio-Textual Data Streams
abstract: Several applications process continuous spatio-textual queries over massive streams of spatio-textual data in real-time, e.g., location-aware ad targeting systems. These queries exhibit several challenges. Besides the fact that the vocabulary of the keywords can be enormous, the frequencies of the keywords can vary across different spatial regions, and can also change over time. This makes the task of adaptively indexing the keywords according to changes in workload – over space and time – very challenging. This paper introduces FAST, a F requency- A ware S patio- T extual index for continuous spatio-textual queries. Unlike existing indexing techniques, FAST does not assume prior knowledge of the entire vocabulary, and adaptively accounts for the variance in the frequencies of keywords across spatial regions. FAST supports continuous spatio-textual range queries and is extended to FASTkNN to support continuous spatio-textual k-nearest neighbor queries. When FAST is compared against state-of-the-art indexes, extensive experimental evaluation using real and synthetic datasets demonstrates up to 3x improvement in performance of spatio-textual range queries as well as 4x improvement in performance of spatio-textual k-nearest neighbor queries. These performance improvements are achieved while using only one third of the memory required by state-of-the-art indexes.

title: A graph-based iterative strategy for solving the all-line transmission switching problem
abstract: Abstract The transmission switching problem aims to determine the optimal network topology that minimizes the operating costs of a power system. This problem is typically formulated as a mixed-integer optimization model, which involves big-M constants that lead to weak relaxations and significant computational challenges, particularly when all lines are switchable. In this paper, we propose a twofold approach: first, using graph theory to derive tighter big-M values by solving a relaxed longest path problem; second, introducing an iterative algorithm that incorporates a heuristic version of the switching problem to efficiently generate low-cost feasible solutions, thereby accelerating the search for optimal solutions in the integer optimization solver. Numerical results on the 118-bus network across 100 demand scenarios demonstrate that the proposed methodology reduces the number of unsolved instances within 1 h by 57% and decreases the average computational time by 44% compared to conventional approaches in the literature.

title: DEMOGRAPHIC PROFILING AND MARKET SEGMENTATION OF SCUBA DIVERS ACROSS MALAYSIAN DIVING DESTINATIONS
abstract: SCUBA diving has shown a notable surge in popularity as a recreational pursuit within the Malaysian context. Tourism Malaysia and Malaysia SCUBA Diving Association highlighted SCUBA diving as one of the essential activities in promoting tourism destinations in Malaysia, and they advocate for SCUBA dive operators to actively promote their products and services to the respective market segments. Nonetheless, the absence of significant statistical data challenges SCUBA diving operators to strategize their marketing initiatives effectively. Thus, the main aim of this study is to identify the segmentation of demographic variables among SCUBA divers across Malaysian diving destinations. The researcher adopted the quantitative method by using an online survey of SCUBA divers who had visited diving destinations in Malaysia. The online survey was distributed via social media and the SCUBA divers’ association. The usable responses were 321, and the data were coded and analysed using descriptive analysis in SPSS software. The implications of the research contribute to the empirical research on SCUBA divers' demographic profile, which helps in providing inputs for the stakeholders. This will also help the stakeholders, such as the government and diving businesses, in planning their marketing strategies and ensuring that these strategies are aligned and suitable with their target market.

title: OPERATING OPTIMISATION FOR A DIRECT-CONNECTED GREEN-ELECTRICITY HYDROGEN-AMMONIA PARK BASED ON MIXED-INTEGER AND CONTINUOUS LINEAR PROGRAMMING
abstract: This paper studies the operation optimisation of a direct-connected wind-photovoltaic hydrogen-ammonia park and evaluates how production flexibility, energy storage and islanded operation affect power balance, renewable-electricity indicators and operating cost. Some applications have been developed for full-load operation, discrete production scheduling, continuous power regulation, islanded dispatch, storage sizing and grid-connected comparison. The park has 40 MW of wind power, 64 MW of photovoltaic power, and hydrogen-ammonia loads for 36 t/d and 72 t/d production. At a 36 t/d full-load baseline, the self-consumption, green-electricity and export ratios are 28.16%, 69.21% and 35.92%, respectively; 54 t/d is the lowest-cost feasible output in discrete scheduling, and the unit cost is 4591.27 yuan/t. The total annual cost of continuous regulation is 1.9005 million yuan, and all three indicators have been achieved in 210 of the 360 weighted days. In islanded operation, 5000 MWh of storage increases the annual output to 25920 t, but the unit cost is still higher than that of grid-connected systems. Flexible production and storage increase the utilisation of renewable energy; however, economic feasibility requires integrated planning of production, storage and grid operation.

title: Tumor-node response heterogeneity: Exploring the “spatial biology” of neoadjuvant therapy response in rectal cancer and its clinical implications
abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy - the combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy administered before surgery - followed by total mesorectal excision is the foundation of treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer. Pathological assessment of the primary tumor commonly uses tumor regression grading, which quantifies the extent of tumor response to treatment and provides prognostic value. However, a growing body of evidence reveals profound inter- and intra-patient heterogeneity in treatment response between the primary tumor and its associated lymph nodes. This review explores the concept of ‘spatial biology’ - the study of how distinct anatomical compartments within a patient, such as the primary tumor site and nodal basins, show unique biological behaviors and distinct responses to therapy. We will synthesize current evidence from single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies, explore the dynamic remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment at the primary site, and contrast this with the unique (and often discordant) response within lymph nodes that may serve as immunological sanctuaries for resistant clones. The combination of a novel lymph node regression grading system, which specifically assesses treatment response in lymph nodes, with traditional tumor regression grading is proposed here to more accurately reflect this spatial variation. abstract: BACKGROUND Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies, and chemotherapy remains the main treatment option for patients with unresectable disease. Reliable prediction of chemotherapy response is therefore critical for individualized treatment planning. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) provides high-resolution, tumor-specific imaging that may be well suited for deep learning-based prediction of chemotherapy response. AIM To develop and validate an EUS-based deep learning model for predicting first-line chemotherapy response in patients with unresectable PDAC, and to evaluate its prognostic value for overall survival (OS) stratification. title: Role of Microstructures on Bubble Detachment and Electrochemical Response in Wicking Electrodes
abstract: Abstract Gas bubble evolution at electrode surfaces reduces the electrode–electrolyte interfacial area and limits the efficiency of gas-evolving electrochemical reactions. While structured electrodes have been widely shown to improve bubble management, the independent contribution of individual geometric parameters to bubble nucleation, detachment, and electrochemical behavior remains poorly understood. Here, bubble-templated electrodeposition is used as a model fabrication platform to systematically vary structural width and height across two morphologically distinct electrode families, stochastic pillar arrays and circular-wall structures, while characterizing double-layer capacitance, current density, bubble detachment diameter, and bubble number density. Three-dimensional wicking architecture is shown to outperform a flat hydrophilic electrode in both electrochemical characterizations and bubble management. At constant height, increasing structural width raises double-layer capacitance but reduces current density and increases detachment diameter─a decoupling attributed to reduced structural unit density and reproduced across both morphological families. title: Structural–Response Consistency Evaluation of a Jiulong Coking Coal Molecular Model Based on Multi-Characterization Constraints
abstract: Abstract The evaluation of coal molecular models commonly relies on individual criteria, such as structural parameter matching, density agreement, or consistency in adsorption behavior. However, these indicators are usually considered independently, and a unified quantitative framework for integrating different evaluation dimensions is still lacking. In this study, an average organic molecular model of Jiulong (JL) coking coal was constructed based on ultimate analysis, 13C NMR, FTIR, and XPS characterization, and a structure–response consistency evaluation framework was established by integrating structural constraints and multiresponse analysis. Based on aromatic carbon fraction, XBP, C–O/C═O ratio, and pyrrolic N/pyridinic N ratio, the molecular formula of the JL coal model was determined as C205H144O30N4. Five indices, including the structural constraint consistency index (SCI), density consistency index (DCI), adsorption response consistency index (ACI), dynamic wetting trajectory consistency index (WCI), and multiresponse consistency index (MCVI), were proposed to quantify structural constraint satisfaction and response consistency. The results indicate that the model effectively retains the structural features derived from multicharacterization, with an (SCI) value of 0.981. title: Design of a Book Sales Management Information System to Support Business Process Digitalization at Sidosari Wunut Tulung, Klaten
abstract: This study aims to design and implement a web-based book sales management information system to support business process digitalization at Sidosari Wunut Bookstore, Tulung, Klaten. Book data, sales transactions, and inventory were previously recorded manually, which limited the accuracy and accessibility of information. The system was developed using the Waterfall method, which comprises requirement analysis, design, implementation, verification, and maintenance. Requirements were identified through observation of the bookstore's operational processes and documented in a Software Requirements Specification (SRS) structured according to IEEE 830-1998, while the Unified Modeling Language (UML) was used to model the system. The system was implemented using JavaScript with MySQL as the database. The main contribution of this study is a documented design and working implementation that integrates book data management, sales transactions, and automatic stock updates in a single web-based system adapted to a small-scale bookstore. The novelty of this study lies in documenting the full path from an IEEE 830-1998 requirements specification and UML models to a functionally tested implementation for a small-scale bookstore, whereas the related studies reviewed focus on online sales, recommendation, or inventory analysis. title: Architectural Dynamics of Fintech Innovations and Digital Financial Services: Empirically Understanding Consumer Trust, Perceived Risk and Financial Inclusion
abstract: Digital financial services and financial technologies have revolutionized the retail banking sector. Payments and intermediation of money has changed dramatically with the advent of these innovations. Many international development organizations have touted the power of digital financial services to promote financial inclusion. However there is still uncertainty if the rapid penetration of digital financial services leads to real financial inclusion or leads to creation of inactive bank accounts. This paper seeks to understand what drives people to adopt digital financial services and convert these services to increased financial wellbeing. Data was collected from 650 individuals across rural, semi urban and urban economies through a questionnaire. Data was analyzed using Pearson Correlations to identify correlations between variables and Multiple Linear Regression to better understand what drives digital financial service use and financial inclusion. Findings reveal that while perceived ease of use and usefulness lead to higher likelihood of adopting digital financial services consumer trust had the highest impact.

abstract: प्रस्तुत शोध अध्ययन नदी (जल) डेटा की राजनीति से संदर्भित है जो चीन की जल डेटा साझा में कमी के कारण भारत और बांग्लादेश की सुरक्षा और आपदा प्रबंधन पर प्रभाव का विश्लेषणात्मक अध्ययन करता है। इस शोध का प्राथमिक लक्ष्य, ऊपर तटवर्ती वाले देशो पर निचले तटवर्ती वाले देशों की नदी (जल) डेटा साझा हेतु निर्भरता को समझना है। भारत और बांग्लादेश, चीन की तुलना में नीचे तटवर्ती अर्थात् दक्षिण एशिया में आते हैं और चीन द्वारा जल डेटा साझा में कमी करने के कारण इन देशों पर बाढ़ जैसी बड़ी प्राकृतिक आपदा का खतरा बना रहता है। ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी बेसिन और इसकी सहायक नदियाँ भारत, चीन और बांग्लादेश से होकर बहती हैं। ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी विश्व की सबसे बड़ी नदियों में से एक है जिसका आरंभिक क्षेत्र चीन है। चीन के द्वारा इन नदियों का डाटा साझा न करने पर भारत के पूर्वी क्षेत्र और बांग्लादेश जैसे निचले तटवर्ती वाले देशों पर विशेषकर मानसून के महीने में नदियों के जल स्तर का कोई भी डाटा उपलब्ध नहीं होता है जिसके कारण अचानक आने वाली बाढ़ से भारत और बांग्लादेश के क्षेत्र में बड़ी हानि पहुँचाती है। इस अचानक आने वाली बाढ़ से भारत और बांग्लादेश दोनों देशों के आपदा प्रबंधन की क्षमता पर नकारात्मक प्रभाव पड़ता है। भारत और चीन के बीच इन नदियों के डेटा साझा करने हेतु 2002 में डवन्े समझौता हुआ इस समझौते के तहत् चीन अपने क्षेत्र से भारत की ओर बहने वाली नदियों का डाटा भारत को साझा करेगा। जिसमें ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी और उसकी सहायक नदियों से संबंधित यह डाटा प्रत्येक वर्ष मई से अक्टूबर तक का देने के लिए चीन ने सहमति जताई। भारत और चीन के बीच हुए इस सम…

title: TALABALARNING IJTIMOIY FAOL KOMPETENSIYALARINI SHAKLLANTIRISHDA KOMMUNIKATIV YONDASHUVNING PEDAGOGIK MEXANIZMLARI
abstract: Maqolada talabalarning ijtimoiy faol kompetensiyalarini shakllantirishda kommunikativ yondashuvning pedagogik mexanizmlari nazariy jihatdan asoslangan. Kommunikativ kompetensiya, kommunikativ harakat, dialogik va hamkorlikda o‘qitish nazariyalarining qiyosiy tahlili asosida ijtimoiy faol kompetensiyaning kognitiv, aksiologik va faoliyatli komponentlarining kommunikativ jihatlari ochib berilgan. Kommunikativ yondashuvning oltita pedagogik mexanizmi - dialogik o‘zaro ta’sir, argumentatsiya va kelishuv, rolli identifikatsiya, hamkorlikdagi faoliyat, tashqi ijtimoiy muloqot va ijtimoiy refleksiya ajratilgan. Mexanizmlarni amalga oshirish bosqichlari, pedagogik shart-sharoitlari va kompetensiyaning kommunikativ jihatlarini baholash mezonlari taklif etilgan.

title: MEASUREMENT OF MUNICIPAL NEW-QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES AND REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
abstract: Guided by the policy of developing new-quality productive forces in light of local conditions, this paper takes panel data (2015-2024) of five core cities in Jiangxi including Nanchang, Ganzhou, Jiujiang, Shangrao and Yichun as research samples. An evaluation system for municipal new-quality productive forces is constructed covering scientific-technological, green and digital dimensions. The entropy-weight improved AHP-TOPSIS model is adopted for comprehensive measurement, so as to analyze its temporal evolution and regional differentiation. The results show that the overall level of new-quality productive forces of the five cities presents a fluctuating upward trend, which can be divided into three stages: steady accumulation, accelerated improvement and adjustment-divergence. Obvious echelon gaps exist among cities. Nanchang takes the lead, Ganzhou ranks second, Shangrao shows strong late-comer momentum, while Jiujiang and Yichun suffer from remarkable fluctuation and decline. Green productivity enjoys sound intra-provincial balance yet meets promotion bottlenecks; inter-city gaps are prominent in scientific-technological and digital productivity. Most cities are confronted with insufficient S&T investment, weak digital industrial foundation and heavy pressure of industrial transformation. title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence in human resource management for sustainable workplaces a bibliometric and literature review
abstract: Abstract This study explores the evolving role of Human Resource Management (HRM) in managing ethical Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in workplace environments. A mixed-methods approach combining bibliometric and literature review was applied to Scopus-indexed literature. The bibliometric component analyzed publication trends, country and institutional contributions, keyword co-occurrence, and co-authorship networks, while the literature review examined conceptual insights and practical directions from the most relevant scholarly publications. The findings revealed an increasing academic interest in the intersection of HRM, AI ethics, and sustainability, with significant contributions from India, China, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Romania. Leading institutional affiliations included the Symbiosis International Deemed University and the University of Delhi. The co-occurrence of key terms highlighted central themes, including human resource management, artificial intelligence, decision-making, ethical technology, and predictive analytics. Co-authorship analysis revealed moderate research collaboration, with emerging networks indicating potential for global cooperation. title: Mathematics for Sustainable Development: Applications, Opportunities and Educational Perspectives
abstract: Sustainable development requires the responsible management of natural resources while ensuring social and economic well-being for present and future generations. Although sustainable development is often associated with environmental science, technology and policy, mathematics plays a fundamental and often under-recognized role in achieving sustainability. Mathematics provides tools for measuring, analysing, predicting and optimizing the use of limited resources. Concepts such as statistics, percentages, ratios, probability, mathematical modelling, optimization, geometry, algebra and calculus can be applied to real-world sustainability challenges including climate change, water conservation, renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, waste management, transportation, population growth and resource allocation. The present paper explores how mathematical concepts can contribute to sustainable development and demonstrates their application through practical examples. It also discusses the role of mathematics education in developing sustainability-oriented thinking among learners. The paper argues that mathematics should be connected with real-life environmental and social problems so that learners understand mathematics not merely as a computational subject but as a powerful tool for informed decision-making and sustainable living. Assessing the Balancing Capability and Grid Integration Performance of Various Solar PV Systems
abstract: Solar photovoltaic energy production fluctuates rapidly due to sunlight and temperature. The fluctuations have to be balanced against the distribution system in which they connect. This paper examines four different types of solar photovoltaic systems; they include monocrystalline roof-top, multi-crystalline roof-top, ground mounted, and battery supported roof-top solar photovoltaic systems. A systematic comparative analysis takes into account balancing and integration indicators. Balancing efficiency is measured using the useful supply, curtailment, conversion loss, and residual imbalance energy. Integration efficiency is assessed based on voltage behavior, ramp control, power factor, controllability, and suitability. Data has been taken from research literature and other accepted references; the analysis has made use of standardized scores and not the actual field data. From the analysis, battery supported photovoltaic systems perform better with a balancing index of 90 and a grid integration score of 91. For the ground mounted systems, it is 79 and 82, respectively, while roof-top systems perform moderately well. While the type of technology affects energy production, system design affected balancing performance significantly. Inverter intelligence, prediction, storage, and coordination improved integration performance.

title: LEAN AND AGILE MANAGEMENT AND WORK ENGAGEMENT AMONG HEALTHCARE EMPLOYEES: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: Healthcare organizations face increasing pressure to improve operational efficiency while maintaining employee well-being and work engagement. Lean and Agile Management have been increasingly applied to address these challenges, yet evidence concerning their relationship with work engagement among healthcare employees remains fragmented. This systematic literature review synthesizes the existing evidence on Lean and Agile Management and work engagement in healthcare settings. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search of Scopus-indexed literature published between 2015 and 2025 identified 26 records. After removal of five duplicate and application of the eligibility criteria, 21 studies were included in the review. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and thematic analysis was conducted to synthesize the evidence. Three themes emerged: patient-centered care, healthcare efficiency, and impact on work engagement. The findings indicate that Lean Management was commonly associated with improved process flow, waste reduction, teamwork, and operational efficiency, although its relationship with work engagement varied across contexts, with some studies reporting increased workload, time pressure, and job strain. title: Socioeconomic Characteristics and Income Inequality among Kinnow Growers: A Comparative Study of Fazilka and Sriganganagar
abstract: This study examines the socioeconomic characteristics of Kinnow growers in Fazilka (Punjab) and Sriganganagar (Rajasthan) using primary data collected during the 2020–21 crop year from 480 growers (240 in each district). Descriptive statistics, cross-tabulation, chi-square tests, Cramér’s V, Lorenz curves, and Gini coefficients were used to compare landholding, demographic characteristics, household conditions, and income distribution. The results show that Kinnow cultivation is concentrated among medium and semi-medium farmers. These categories together account for 87.50% of sampled growers in Fazilka and 86.67% in Sriganganagar. Mean landholding is higher in Sriganganagar (6.85 ha) than in Fazilka (5.34 ha), while landholding inequality is higher in Fazilka (Gini = 0.626) than in Sriganganagar (0.510). Growers in both districts are predominantly middle-aged, married, and formally educated. Mean family size is 6.5875 members in Fazilka and 6.7208 in Sriganganagar. Mean monthly household electricity consumption is also similar at 475 and 474.16 units, respectively. Mean annual income is slightly higher in Fazilka (₹5.8125 lakh) than in Sriganganagar (₹5.525 lakh), whereas income inequality is substantially lower in Sriganganagar (Gini = 0.202) than in Fazilka (Gini = 0.352). Core Muscle Endurance and Side-to-Side Asymmetry in Club-Level Pakistani Fast Bowlers: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Lumbar bone stress injury is the most time-costly injury in cricket, and fast bowlers carry the greatest burden because the delivery stride imposes repeated, asymmetric trunk loading on a spine that is often still maturing. Pakistani club-level bowlers show a high prevalence of poor core endurance ratios, but no Pakistani study has examined core endurance asymmetry in fast bowlers in relation to side dominance, bowling workload, bowling action and low back pain history. Objective: To describe trunk flexor, extensor and side-bridge endurance, endurance ratios and dominant versus non-dominant asymmetry in club-level Pakistani fast bowlers, and to examine their associations with bowling workload, bowling action and low back pain history as potential markers of lumbar injury risk. Methods: This descriptive, multi-club, cross-sectional study will recruit 216 male hard-ball fast and fast-medium bowlers aged 15–25 years from registered clubs and academies in Lahore, Pakistan (194 required plus a 10% allowance). Core endurance will be measured with the McGill Torso Muscle Endurance Test Battery in a counterbalanced Latin-square order with 5 minutes of rest between tests. Bowling action will be classified from two-dimensional video by two independent raters, and workload will be derived from a structured 28-day recall verified against coach or club records. title: Adaptive error management for fault-tolerant quantum computing across hardware-level suppression, system-level diagnosis, and real-time decoding
abstract: Abstract Fault-tolerant quantum computing reached a milestone in December 2024 when Google’s Willow processor demonstrated below-threshold error correction on a superconducting chip, a result since reproduced on neutral-atom and alternative superconducting platforms. Yet the classical decoders needed to sustain this performance face a scaling challenge: noise becomes increasingly structured and correlated as systems grow, while decoders must respond within microsecond coherence windows. This survey asks whether error suppression, noise diagnosis, and decoding are better treated as one adaptive control problem than as three separate research programs. Drawing on a scoping review of 146 records, it organizes the field into a three-layer taxonomy. Layer 1 (Hardware-Level Suppression) integrates protection into the physical substrate; bosonic cat qubits exponentially suppress bit-flip errors, projecting up to 90% overhead reduction versus surface codes. Layer 2 (Diagnosis) employs probabilistic models and computational intelligence to characterize error sources; neuro-fuzzy architectures and the Bias–Entropy decomposition separate hardware drift from logical faults, subject to an identifiability limit that we characterize. Layer 3 (Real-time Decoding) targets the integration of machine learning within strict latency constraints. Hardware acceleration now approaches superconducting …

title: A Study of CSR Practices and Environmental Sustainability Initiatives of Major Industries in Rajasthan
abstract: Rajasthan has some of India’s biggest mining, oil and gas, cement, and textile industries, each having to adhere to the mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) guidelines stipulated in section 135 of the Companies Act of 2013. This study looks at the four leading companies in the industries mentioned above—Hindustan Zinc Limited (Mining), Cairn Oil & Gas/Vedanta Limited (Oil & Gas), Shree Cement Limited (Cement), and RSWM Limited of the LNJ Bhilwara Group (Textile)—in terms of CSR expenditure and environmental sustainability practices. Using the sustainability reports and CSR reports of these companies in addition to literature on the topic, it is observed that the amount spent on CSR varies greatly among the different industries and even within an industry: Hindustan Zinc Ltd reports an expenditure of ₹273.45 crore in FY2024-25 while Shree Cement Ltd spends ₹51.34 crore on CSR in FY2023-24, while Cairn Oil & Gas’s multistate CSR expenditure decreased from ₹25.53 crore in FY2021-22 to ₹10.26 crore in FY2024-25. Similar variations have been seen in environmental initiatives: Sewage treatment and land restoration by Hindustan Zinc, Water positivity and renewable energy by Shree Cement and water conservation by RSWM through its Zero Liquid Discharge project.

title: Financial Knowledge and Financial Attitude in Mutual Fund Investment Decision-Making among Retail Investors in Thiruvananthapuram District
abstract: Financial knowledge and financial attitude are important dimensions of individual financial decision-making, particularly in investment contexts where investors need to evaluate information and make informed choices. Within this context, this study investigates the association between financial knowledge and investor confidence, as well as the relationship between financial attitude and mutual fund investment decision quality among retail investors in Thiruvananthapuram district. To evaluate the relationships between variables, this study gathered primary data from 287 retail mutual fund investors utilising a structured questionnaire through purposive sampling within a quantitative, cross-sectional, and explanatory framework. Data were examined using reliability testing through Cronbach’s alpha, exploratory factor analysis, descriptive statistics, alongside Spearman’s and Kendall’s Tau-b correlations, simple linear regression, and ordinal logistic regression. The results demonstrated a strong positive association between financial knowledge and investor confidence (ρ = 0.584, p < 0.001), where financial knowledge accounted for 34.1% of the variation in confidence. Financial attitude also showed a significant positive association with mutual fund investment decision quality (τb = 0.467, p < 0.001). The ordinal logistic regression model yielded a Nagelkerke R² of 0.286, indicatin…

title: Green Transformational Leadership and Green Innovation: The Sequential Mediating Roles of Green Human Capital Management and Work Behavior
abstract: Organizations seeking environmental improvement need to understand how leaders' environmental priorities are associated with employee capabilities, everyday conduct, and Green Innovation. This study examined the direct and indirect associations among Green Transformational Leadership, Green Human Capital Management, Work Behavior, and Green Innovation, including a sequential mediation pathway. A cross-sectional quantitative survey of 300 purposively selected company employees used a 24-item, five-point Likert questionnaire; the reported data were analyzed with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Green Transformational Leadership was positively associated with Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.406; p < 0.001) and Work Behavior (β = 0.255; p < 0.001), but not directly with Green Innovation (β = 0.041; p = 0.446). Green Human Capital Management was associated with Work Behavior (β = 0.325; p < 0.001) and Green Innovation (β = 0.292; p < 0.001), while Work Behavior was associated with Green Innovation (β = 0.326; p < 0.001). The specific indirect paths through Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.118; p < 0.001), through Work Behavior (β = 0.083; p = 0.001), and sequentially through both mediators (β = 0.043; p < 0.001) were significant. These findings support a statistical explanation in which environmental competency management and work conduct connect leadership orientation with perceiv…

Many-objective reservoir operation optimization using NSGA-III and decision-support analysis: a sustainable management framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India
abstract: Abstract Efficient reservoir operation requires simultaneous consideration of competing goals related to hydropower generation, water-supply reliability, flood management, and storage regulation. However, deriving balanced operating policies becomes increasingly complex when several conflicting objectives are considered concurrently. This study develops a many-objective optimization framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India, considering four objectives: maximization of hydropower generation and minimization of water deficit, spill losses, and storage deviation. The reservoir operation model integrates hydrological inputs, demand characteristics, operational constraints, and reservoir continuity relationships. Five metaheuristic algorithms Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO), Multi-Objective Ant Colony Optimization (MOACO), and Multi-Objective Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (MOTLBO were comparatively evaluated using Hypervolume (HV), Inverted Generational Distance (IGD), and computational performance indicators. NSGA-III achieved an HV of 0.9234 and an IGD of 0.0338, demonstrating effective convergence and diversity for the evaluated solutions. title: राजस्थान के जयपुर रियासत के उपाश्रयी वर्ग का सामाजिक-आर्थिक अ/ययन मीना जनजाति के विशेष संदर्भ में (1920 ई. से 1957 ई. तक)
abstract: प्रस्तुत शोध पत्र का मुख्य उद्देश्य 1920 ई. से 1957 ई. के समयांतराल में जयपुर रियासत के उपाश्रयी ;ैनइंसजमतद / हाशिए पर स्थित) वर्गों की सामाजिक और आर्थिक स्थिति का ऐतिहासिक विश्लेषण करना है। विशेष रूप से मीना जनजाति पर केंद्रित यह अ/ययन उनके पारंपरिक सामाजिक संगठन, प्रशासनिक भूमिकाओं, आर्थिक आधार संरचना तथा औपनिवेशिक व सामंती नीतियों के विनाशकारी प्रभावों को रेखांकित करता है। 1920 के दशक में लागू किए गए दमनकारी ‘जरायम पेशा कानून’ ;ब्तपउपदंस ज्तपइमे ।बजद्ध तथा चौकीदारी प्रथा के सामाजिक-आर्थिक दुष्परिणामों का गहन अ/ययन करते हुए यह पत्र स्वतंत्रता-पश्चात् (1947-1957) हुए सामाजिक सुधार आंदोलनों, पुनर्वास नीतियों, कानून निरसन एवं शैक्षणिक-राजनीतिक चेतना के उद्भव का व्यापक लेखा-जोखा प्रस्तुत करता है। ऐतिहासिक साक्ष्यों और राजस्थान राज्य अभिलेखागार (बीकानेर) के प्रशासनिक रिकॉर्ड्स के विश्लेषणात्मक अ/ययन से यह सिद्ध होता है कि 20वीं सदी के म/य में मीना समुदाय का संघर्ष केवल कानूनी मुक्ति का आंदोलन नहीं था, बल्कि यह औपनिवेशिक-सामंती उत्पीड़न से नागरिक स्वतंत्रता तथा सामाजिक पुनरुत्थान की दिशा में एक युगांतकारी ऐतिहासिक यात्रा थी।

title: Creating satisfaction and loyalty among tourists: the power of experiential tourism
abstract: Abstract The current research examines whether experiential tourism activities in the tourism industry can influence tourists’ behaviour. Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study examines how experience affects travellers’ intentions for satisfaction and loyalty among online travel agents (OTAs). Data were collected from 208 visitors across five travel destinations in India, specifically wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, to examine their lived experiences. The results were analysed using a partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) approach, indicating that experiential tourism indicators have a direct effect on customer engagement. The study suggests that experiential motivation is vital in shaping tourists’ satisfaction and loyalty. The results suggest that tourists are more likely to return to the OTA and recommend it to others if they have positive experiential motivation during their travel encounter. Moreover, the study highlights the importance of co-creation in the tourism industry. In the challenging competitive space, leveraging experiential strategies can help managers gain a competitive advantage. Travel retailers must focus on increasing tourists’ conscious participation and include certain activities that may motivate them and create enthusiasm. This study is one of the few in India to explore the relationship between exp…

title: Cancer therapy-induced intestinal injury: Mechanisms, clinical manifestations, and management strategies
abstract: As cancer treatment advances in recent years, people with cancer are living longer, but the side effects of these treatments on normal tissues remain a major challenge, particularly the intestines. Intestinal injury induced by chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and surgical intervention represents an important factor that limits the effectiveness of cancer treatment. The common symptoms are diarrhea, abdominal pain and malabsorption, which can substantially impair the patients’ quality of life and may lead to severe complications. At present, the clinical strategies for the prevention and treatment of therapy-induced intestinal injury are still relatively scarce. In this minireview, we focus on the mechanisms underlying cancer therapy-induced intestinal injury, including oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and gut microbiota imbalance, and discuss targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at reducing morbidity, improving patient outcomes, and fostering a better quality of life.

title: Analysis of Stock Price Movements of Conglomerate Groups Relative to The Jakarta Composite Index (JCI)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the relationship and influence of stock price changes within conglomerate groups on the movements of the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2019–2025 period. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing secondary data consisting of daily stock price changes and the JCI. The sample was selected using a purposive sampling technique, with the current and former constituents of the Kompas100 Index serving as the screening universe, from which stocks affiliated with conglomerate groups were identified. Based on the research criteria, 18 conglomerate groups comprising 57 companies were selected. The daily stock returns for each company were aggregated by conglomerate group and used as independent variables, while the daily return of the JCI served as the dependent variable. The analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with the assistance of EViews 13. The results indicate that for all annual models throughout the 2019–2025 period, the Prob. (F-statistic) was 0.000, demonstrating that the conglomerate group stock variables are, when taken together, statistically significant in their relationship to changes in the JCI. title: FORECASTING COMPUTING RESOURCE UTILIZATION IN SERVER CLUSTERS USING A LIGHTWEIGHT TRANSFORMER
abstract: The computing resource utilization in server clusters changes dynamically and non-stationarily; thus it is critical to accurately forecast such utilization for effective resource scheduling, auto-scaling, and workload management. Existing forecasting approaches lack abilities to model complex temporal dependencies, while standard Transformers exhibit powerful long-range modeling but incur significant computational and memory overheads. In response, we propose a lightweight Transformer for computing resource utilization forecasting in server clusters. It leverages compact temporal representations and efficient feature interactions to lower computational complexity and enable multi-step forecasts of future resource utilization. We conduct experiments based on real-world server cluster traces, comparing our approach against several representative baselines: LSTM, GRU, DLinear, Transformer, PatchTST, and iTransformer. Both the forecasting accuracy and model efficiency are measured by prediction error, parameter count, computational cost, and inference efficiency respectively. Our result shows that our approach achieves good forecasting performance without significantly increasing computational overhead, which achieves a balanced trade-off between predictive accuracy and model efficiency. Thus, our framework offers an efficient solution for practical resource utilization forecasting…

TRANSMISSION LINE ICE ACCRETION PROBABILITY PREDICTION AND DE-ICING THRESHOLD OPTIMIZATION BASED ON BAYESIAN EXTREME VALUE THEORY AND MONTE CARLO SIMULATION
abstract: Transmission line icing is a rare and severe hazard; therefore, a fixed de-icing threshold cannot account for forecast uncertainty, accumulated long-term risk, and the economic trade-off between de-icing costs and tower collapse losses. Based on 30 years of annual maximum ice-thickness data, real-time weather forecasts and operating cost parameters, this paper builds a probabilistic prediction and de-icing decision model. A generalised extreme value distribution is used to obtain the prior via maximum likelihood estimation, Bayesian updating and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling generate the posterior distribution, a homogeneous Poisson process determines the long-term event frequency, and finally, Bayesian expected loss yields a dynamic de-icing threshold. The fitted GEV parameters are μ=11.95, σ=3.08, ξ=-0.19, and the 50-year and 100-year return levels are 21.5 and 23.9 mm, respectively. Under the given severe-weather condition, the posterior mean is 15.6 mm, and the probability of exceeding 15 mm is 0.84. The probabilities of at least one event within 10, 20, 30 and 50 years are 0.9030, 0.9906, 0.9991 and 0.9999, respectively. The optimal de-icing threshold ranges from 14.2 to 18.6 mm, reducing the expected total cost by about 18.7% compared with a fixed-threshold policy. This report provides verifiable statistical decision support for the construction of a high-probability …

title: The influence of sample size, modelling algorithms, and hyperparameters on bootstrap-based prediction stability in clinical prediction model development: An empirical study using the HOPE dataset
abstract: Abstract Background The stability of clinical prediction models has emerged as an important factor in model development. Models producing unstable or unreliable predictions can ultimately lead to improper clinical decisions and harm patients when applied in clinical practice. Previous studies have highlighted the role of sample size in prediction stability, with larger samples delivering increased stability. However, the role of other modelling decisions remains unclear. This study considered three modifiable factors influencing the stability of predictions: sample size, modelling algorithm (i.e., parametric regression and machine learning algorithms), and hyperparameter tuning. Methods We used the previously published HOPE dataset to develop a prediction model for anxiety at palliative care admission, incorporating 34 candidate predictors. To examine the impact of sample size, we generated seven datasets of varying sizes through random sampling. A total of 21 modelling scenarios were evaluated by combining these datasets with three modelling approaches: LASSO logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost. Models were tuned using cross-validation and assessed for discrimination (AUC) and calibration. Prediction stability was evaluated using a bootstrap-based framework, including the mean absolute prediction error (MAPE) and related instability plots. Results In this clinical …

title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
abstract: Abstract Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through…

Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing
abstract: Abstract Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that OH– forms strong chemical bonds with surface Zr atoms, thereby inducing surface hydroxylation and increasing the diffusion coefficient of Zr atoms. Adsorbed PVP molecules further regulate the softening process and transform the material from a rigid to a softened state. Simulations verify that such softening is essentially a corrosion reaction and predict the corrosion depth and corrosion rate within 60 min. Experiments combining chemical softening and magnetic abrasive finishing (MAF) show that the surface roughness of zirconia specimens decreases from Ra 0.302 to 0.057, and the material removal rate ranges from 2.29 × 10–3 μm/s to 2.93 × 10–3 μm/s. The average error between simulated and measured removal depths is only 17.02%. This composite system enables effective surface softening of zirconia. The simulation can reproduce the experimental trend, providing feasible theoretical support a…

title: FAULT PREDICTION OF FASTENER PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT VIA LIGHTWEIGHT REGRESSION MODELING WITH SCIKIT-LEARN: EVIDENCE FROM THE HAIYAN FASTENER INDUSTRY
abstract: In fastener manufacturing, an unexpected breakdown of a cold heading machine stops the entire production line, yet most small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) still maintain their equipment by rule of thumb. Targeting the SMEs in the Haiyan fastener industry cluster, this paper takes cold heading machines as the object and builds a low-cost equipment fault prediction method based on regression modeling and Scikit-learn. The remaining useful life (RUL) of key components is taken as the prediction target; four models, namely linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting regression tree (GBRT), and support vector regression (SVR), are compared, and grid search is used for parameter tuning. Since such enterprises generally lack usable historical failure data, the method is validated on real degradation data from the public XJTU-SY accelerated life test dataset of rolling bearings, which share the same data form as the key rotating components of cold heading machines. The results show that GBRT performs best (RMSE = 6.25 min, R² = 0.511), that degradation information is concentrated in a few amplitude-type statistical features such as mean amplitude, standard deviation and root mean square, and that in the early-warning replay on two test bearings, alarms are all raised ahead of failure with an average lead time of 8.0 min and no false alarm. abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of price, service quality, promotion, and trust on customers’ decisions to open Hajj savings accounts at Nano Sharia Bank, Jambi Branch, both directly and indirectly through reputation as a mediating variable. In addition, this study examines the influence of each independent variable on the bank’s reputation. This research employs an associative research design with a quantitative approach and a causal nature. Primary data were collected through a questionnaire consisting of 39 research indicators. The determination of sample size followed the minimum requirements for Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis, resulting in 195 respondents as the research sample. The results indicate that, directly, price, promotion, service quality, and reputation do not have a significant effect on customers’ decisions to open Hajj savings accounts. In contrast, trust has a significant effect on customers’ decision-making. Regarding reputation, promotion is found to have a significant influence on shaping the bank’s reputation, while price, trust, and service quality do not show a significant effect. Furthermore, the mediation analysis reveals that reputation does not mediate the effects of price, promotion, trust, and service quality on customers’ decisions to open Hajj savings accounts. title: Epitranscriptomic regulation of the COX-2/PGE2 axis by hnRNPA2B1 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression
abstract: BACKGROUND Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a highly lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic options. Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is frequently overexpressed in ESCC, yet the mechanisms leading to its dysregulation remain poorly understood. Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A2/B1 (hnRNPA2B1), an oncogenic N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, has been implicated in various cancers, but its role in regulating COX-2 expression and promoting ESCC progression has not been defined. AIM To investigate how hnRNPA2B1 promotes ESCC progression through COX-2 regulation. METHODS Expression of hnRNPA2B1 and COX-2 was analyzed in ESCC tissues and cell lines by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Stable hnRNPA2B1 knockdown and overexpression models were established to assess cellular proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth. Bulk RNA-seq, m6A RNA immunoprecipitation-qPCR and RNA immunoprecipitation-qPCR, and actinomycin D assays were used to delineate post-transcriptional regulation of COX-2. Functional and therapeutic relevance of the hnRNPA2B1-COX-2/prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) axis was evaluated using PGE2 supplementation and celecoxib treatment in vitro and in vivo . title: Sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules for the directed biosynthesis of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid in Escherichia coli
abstract: Abstract Bioconversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) confers advantages of mild conditions, high selectivity, and eco-friendliness. However, enzymatic catalysis is expensive and multi-strain microbial catalysis is limited by the transmembrane transport of intermediates between strains, restricting the efficient synthesis of FDCA and generating a byproduct. In this study, we aimed to establish sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules in Escherichia coli to precisely control the expression of hydroxymethylfurfural oxidase (HMFO) and vanillin dehydrogenase (VDH1), enabling the directed one-pot conversion of HMF to FDCA with no detectable accumulation of the measured intermediates and simplifying the operational process. At a 15 mM HMF scale, this strategy achieved a FDCA yield of 100%, significantly higher than the 78.6% yield of the dual-enzyme cascade system established by HMFO and VDH1, and the 56.73% yield from the dual-strain catalysis constructed by two engineered E. coli strains that harbor either hmfo or vdh 1(Student’s t -test, p < 0.0001).
