Tunable Optical-to-THz Frequency Conversion Driven by Localized Surface Phonon Polaritons in LiNbO3 Metasurfaces
abstract: Abstract We demonstrate tunable THz generation by optical rectification in LiNbO3 rod metasurfaces supporting localized surface phonon polaritons (LSPhPs). By varying the rod length, the LSPhP resonance is tuned across the 4–5 THz range, producing a systematic red-shift of the generated THz spectral peak. THz time-domain spectroscopy and numerical calculations show that the emitted spectrum is governed by the geometry-dependent LSPhP response. Although the total far-field emission remains lower than that of the unpatterned film, numerical calculations show that the metasurfaces enhance the volume-averaged mean-square nonlinear current density and strongly localize the generated THz field near the rods. These results establish phonon-polaritonic metasurfaces as compact platforms for spectrally tailoring optical-to-THz conversion and enhancing localized THz fields.

title: Unraveling the Anti-HCV Mechanism of the Ethyl Acetate Fraction of Vitex cofassus via Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
abstract: To address the growing health burden posed by the hepatitis C virus (HCV), the present study employed computational approach to predict the medicinal properties of Vitex cofassus. Liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) analysis of its ethyl acetate leaf fraction identified 37 drug-like compounds. Network pharmacology predicted 201 biological targets, with key proteins such as STAT3, IL6, SRC, AKT1, EGFR, HSP90AA1, and TNF-α being central to the proposed mechanism of action. Functional enrichment analyses pointed to involvement in chemical response, intracellular signaling, stress, and regulated cell death, with molecular functions linked to kinase activity and ATP binding. KEGG analysis further associates targets with key pathways in cancer, viral infection, and metabolic disease. Picrocrocin and flavonoids such as isorhamnetin and apigenin were predicted as potential inhibitors of HCV-related proteins (STAT3 and SRC, respectively). While these in silico findings provide a rational basis for further investigation, the present findings remain predictive and require experimental validation to confirm actual anti-HCV efficacy.

title: BIOFLEXSHIRT: A SMA-DRIVEN SHOULDER EXOSKELETON AND ITS ASSISTED MOTION MECHANISM STUDY
abstract: Loss of shoulder mobility severely impairs upper limb function and reduces quality of life. Here we present BioFlexShirt, a wearable soft exoskeleton driven by shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators, designed to assist shoulder movements across three degrees of freedom. Inspired by the anatomy of major shoulder muscles, BioFlexShirt integrates bionic actuator alignment, a displacement amplification mechanism, and fabric-based modular design to enhance anatomical conformity and assistive performance. A coupled kinematic model was developed based on an ellipsoidal thorax approximation, while dynamic simulations using OpenSim confirmed consistency with natural shoulder–humeral rhythms. Vicon motion capture experiments revealed significant improvements in joint displacement and coordination at the GH, AC, ST, and SA landmarks. All root mean square errors remained below 5 mm, validating the system’s spatial alignment and assistive fidelity. This study demonstrates a viable pathway for SMA-based wearable exoskeletons in rehabilitation, enabling anatomically aligned, lightweight, and efficient upper limb assistance.

AN INTRA-DAY AND DAILY ROLLING ECONOMIC DISPATCHING MODEL FOR ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS IN INDUSTRIAL PARK MICROGRIDS
abstract: Aiming at the electricity-purchase-cost optimization demand of park microgrids equipped with distributed photovoltaics, two sets of energy-storage dispatching models are established for intra-day deterministic dispatching and long-term day-by-day rolling optimization. With the objective of minimizing daily total electricity-purchase cost, the intra-day dispatching model considers power balance, energy-storage charge-discharge power, capacity limits and daily cyclic constraints. Linear programming is adopted to solve electricity-purchase and energy-storage operation strategies under 10-minute time granularity, followed by feasibility verification and sensitivity analysis of key parameters. For long-term rolling dispatching, load forecasting is realized via historical same-week load weighting and deviation damping correction. A safety margin for planned electricity purchase and high-price emergency purchase penalty mechanism are introduced to realize annual-scale optimal operation of microgrid energy storage. Numerical results prove that energy-storage greatly cuts microgrid electricity-purchase expenditure. Charge-discharge efficiency dominates dispatching performance, and a 3% reserved ratio for planned purchase balances economic cost and power shortage risk. This work provides theoretical support for practical engineering dispatching of park-microgrid energy storage.

title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
abstract: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

Energysheds and the Urban Energy Transition: A Method for Assessing Spatial Imbalances in Energy Flow
abstract: Abstract Urban areas are facing the challenges of transitioning toward a low-carbon society as a response to climate change. However, the benefits and burdens of this energy transition are not evenly distributed across cities. To address this disparity, the concept of energy justice has emerged. The issue of urban energy justice can be understood as a manifestation of geographical energy disparities where energy-consuming regions enjoy significant benefits, while energy producing regions suffer from externalities. In this paper, we propose a method that utilizes the notion of “energyshed” to align city energy consumption with power plant energy generation, addressing geographical energy (im)balances. The proposed method maps the spatial supply–demand relationships between regions and power plants without relying on proprietary algorithms or territory-specific cutoff distances. Although spatial imbalance alone does not establish energy injustice, the resulting energysheds provide a diagnostic basis for identifying energy-generating regions that bear disproportionate burdens and for informing a fairer allocation of resources during the energy transition.

Education for a Changing World: Liberal Arts Education and the Case for Structural Integration
abstract: Schools are being asked to prepare young people for economies, technologies and civic conditions that nobody can describe with confidence. Estimates of how automation and generative artificial intelligence will alter work differ widely, yet most of them point in one direction: tasks built on routine procedure are the easiest to hand over to machines, while tasks that call for judgement, explanation and cooperation with others are gaining value. This conceptual paper asks what kind of education answers that situation, and it argues that the long tradition of liberal education offers a better starting point than the narrow, examination-driven specialisation that still governs much schooling in India and elsewhere. The paper first reviews labour-market and policy evidence on the changing demand for skills, drawing on Autor, Levy and Murnane, on Deming, and on Eloundou and colleagues, along with the framing documents of UNESCO and the OECD. It then traces the idea of liberal education from the classical artes liberales, through Newman and Dewey, to Nussbaum's account of democratic citizenship, and sets this history alongside the Indian precedents recognised in the National Education Policy 2020. A review of empirical studies follows. Research from the Wabash National Study and related work links particular liberal arts experiences, such as clear teaching, sustained discussion and f…

title: QR CODE MENU DESIGN AND CUSTOMER SATISFACTION IN MALAYSIAN CASUAL DINING RESTAURANTS
abstract: QR code menus are now standard in Malaysian casual dining, yet little is known about which mobile interface features are associated with diner satisfaction. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model and Menu Engineering principles, this study examines whether digital presentation, strategic item placement and visual digital prompts predict customer satisfaction in independent casual dining restaurants. A cross-sectional online survey was administered to casual dining patrons in Penang, recruited by purposive screening followed by snowball referral and required to have used a QR code menu within the preceding six months; 248 usable responses were retained. Constructs were measured on six-point Likert scales (α = .843 to .867) and analysed by multiple linear regression. The three predictors jointly explained 85.0% of the variance in customer satisfaction, R² = .850, adjusted R² = .849, F(3, 244) = 462.428, p < .001, and each was a significant positive predictor: visual digital prompts, β = .474; strategic item placement, β = .310; digital presentation, β = .178. However, the attributes proved not to be empirically separable: no construct met the Fornell-Larcker criterion, the collinearity condition index reached 37.144, and 92.5% of explained variance was shared rather than unique. Relative weights analysis accordingly returned near-equal contributions of 31.5%, 32.5% and 35.9%.…

title: Towards a competence-behaviour-design alignment for educational robotics kits: a theoretical synthesis and development principles
abstract: Abstract Educational robotics kits (ERKs) are widely used to support competence-oriented technology education, yet their design is rarely grounded in clearly prioritised technological competences and associated learning behaviours. This research, situated in China’s General Technology curriculum, addresses this gap by developing a competence-behaviour-design (C-B-D) alignment for ERKs. The research problem concerns what consistent priority competences and their operationalised learning behaviours are required to guide ERK design. A two-phase mixed-methods approach was adopted. Study 1 used a Delphi-Analytic Hierarchy Process with experienced teachers to prioritise curriculum-defined competences. Materialisation capacity and engineering thinking emerged as highest priorities; within materialisation capacity, ‘knowledge and selection of materials and tools’ and ‘making and processing capability’ were rated equally important, while ‘systems analysis thinking’ was the dominant indicator for engineering thinking. Study 2 undertook document- and artefact-based analysis to identify operationalised learning behaviours corresponding to these competences. Results show that materialisation capacity is predominantly enacted through component selection, modular assembly and basic structural testing, whereas engineering thinking is mainly elicited through functional evaluation, system-level …

De Novo Design of Catalytically Active Salen-Binding Proteins
abstract: Abstract De novo design of catalytic metalloproteins has the potential to generate enzymes that combine the efficiency of natural proteins with the reactivity of synthetic organometallic catalysts. Here, we develop a computational strategy to design enzymes with novel tertiary structures that bind metal salen complexes, classic small-molecule catalysts not found in biology. Six proteins were designed and screened for function; five of six express well, bind a Co-salen cofactor, and catalyze a transition metal hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)-mediated deallylation reaction, representing the first de novo proteins to catalyze this class of transformation. The spectroscopic properties and crystal structure of the most active sequence were in excellent agreement with the design, and the holoprotein retained its structure and activity over a broad range of pH (2–12), temperatures up to 95 °C, and aqueous/organic solvent mixtures. We suggest that the combinatorial space provided by metal ion identity, ligand substitution, and active site structure can be used to generate artificial metalloenzymes that catalyze many chemical transformations.

Solid Lipid Nanoparticles as Delivery Systems for Plant-Derived Phytochemicals in Cancer Therapy: A Systematic Review
abstract: Solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) have been investigated as lipid-based delivery systems to improve the solubility, stability, bioavailability, and delivery of plant-derived phytochemicals to tumors for cancer therapy. However, the available evidence remains heterogeneous and predominantly preclinical. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the formulation strategies, physicochemical characteristics, and therapeutic applications of phytochemical-loaded SLNs in cancer therapy. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Original research articles in English investigating phytochemical-loaded SLNs for cancer therapy were included. Data on formulation composition, preparation methods, physicochemical properties, drug release, in vitro anticancer activity, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and in vivo antitumor efficacy were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE tool for animal studies and an adapted checklist for in vitro studies. Thirty one articles were included in the qualitative synthesis. Most SLNs had particle sizes in the nanoscale range, approximately 50-350 nm, with encapsulation efficiencies of 43-99% and sustained-release profiles. Encapsulation generally improved cellular uptake and in vitro cytotoxicity in several cancer models. However, evidence of improved bioavailability, active tumor targeting, and in vivo antitumor efficacy remained limited …

title: Glycolate oxidase contributes to autophagy-associated antiviral defense against citrus leaf blotch virus
abstract: Abstract Background Kiwifruit is a high-value fruit crop but is increasingly challenged by viral diseases. Citrus leaf blotch virus (CLBV), an important viral pathogen of kiwifruit, causes vein clearing and chlorotic symptoms in leaves, severely impairing kiwifruit yield and fruit quality. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are recognized as pivotal signals in plant antiviral defense, yet the downstream pathway by which virus-induced H₂O₂ accumulation restricts viral infection remains largely unclear. Results Glycolate oxidase (GOX) expression is positively associated with H₂O₂ accumulation and autophagic activity, but negatively associated with CLBV accumulation. CLBV infection in Nicotiana benthamiana was associated with elevated H₂O₂ accumulation and marked upregulation of GOX, a key peroxisomal enzyme responsible for H₂O₂ production. GOX-mediated H₂O₂ accumulation functions as an antiviral barrier against CLBV, as NbGOX silencing enhanced viral infection and kiwi ( Actinidia chinensis ) AcGOX5 overexpression reduced viral accumulation. Further analyses revealed that among the domains in CLBV replicase, the expression of PRO and OTu domains promote H₂O₂ accumulation. Mechanistically, GOX contributes to CLBV restriction and is associated with enhanced autophagic activity and reduced accumulation of the viral movement protein. Conclusions Together, these findings reveal a mechanist…

abstract: Abstract Background Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly integrated into health professions education to address limitations of traditional instructional formats. However, whether VR delivers consistent advantages across different educational constructs remains variable. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of VR-based interventions on objectively assessed learning outcomes compared with traditional instructional methods across health professions curricula. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ERIC, and Cochrane Central from inception through August 28, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing VR with traditional teaching methods. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) were calculated using Hedges’ g via DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models, with outcomes categorized into cognitive/knowledge and procedural/technical domains. Between-study heterogeneity was quantified using the I 2 statistic, and 95% prediction intervals were computed. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane RoB 2, and evidence certainty was graded using the GRADE framework. Results Twenty-three randomized controlled trials (24 independent datasets, 1,202 participants) were included. title: Community Participation in Various Stages of Non-Timber Forest Product Management in the Community Forestry Scheme in Indonesia
abstract: Community participation is a key component of sustainable forest management, particularly in social forestry schemes that utilize non-timber forest products (NTFP). However, empirical evidence on how participation varies across specific operational stages of NTFP management remains limited, especially in Indonesian Community Forest settings. Examining participation at different stages is important because involvement in nursery, planting, maintenance, and harvesting may reflect distinct responsibilities, incentives, and benefit-sharing arrangements. This study therefore aimed to analyze community participation across four operational stages of NTFP management in the Tebing Siring Community Forest, Tanah Laut Regency, South Kalimantan. A descriptive quantitative case-study design was applied to 20 purposively selected members from a population of 65 group members. Participants were selected based on their involvement in NTFP management activities and availability during data collection. Participation was assessed using a four-point ordinal rating scale, with higher scores indicating greater participation. Descriptive analysis showed mean scores of 3.20 for nursery, 2.95 for planting, 2.70 for maintenance, and 2.65 for harvesting. These results suggest greater participation in the first stages and less in maintenance and harvesting. However, the Friedman test found no statistical…

Electric Field Catalysis and the Metabolic Origin of Life
abstract: Abstract Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes. We first overview types of positive feedback relevant to the early evolution of metabolism, the theory of electric field catalysis, and its dominant role in enzyme catalysis. We then examine recent experiments and calculations highlighting the ability of external electric fields to enable nonenzymatic analogues of challenging metabolic reactions in micro- to millisecond reaction times. An underexplored mode of small molecule catalysis (reorientation catalysis) that can only operate in external electric fields is proposed to make positive feedback within prebiotic reaction networks more achievable. By embodying electrostatic catalysis, compartmentalization, and ion concentration gradients, charged aqueous interfaces prepattern three fundamental features of biology, making them a preferred environment for a metabolic origin of life. Computational Compound Prioritization Strategy Incorporating Docking Variability and Interaction Energies Identifies Putative LRH-1 Binders
abstract: Abstract Compound ranking in structure-based computer-aided drug discovery notoriously yields highly ranked false positives due to sampling and, more frequently, scoring errors. We developed a compound prioritization strategy that utilizes sampled docked poses from complementary docking approaches, i.e., targeted physics-based docking and blind docking with a generative model, into multiple conformations of the target protein to train two multilayer perceptron (MLP) models. The MLPs predict binders or activators at the orthosteric ligand-binding pocket of the nuclear receptor Liver Receptor Homologue-1 (LRH-1, NR5A2). Our approach circumvents the reliance on a single docked pose for scoring compounds or individual scoring metrics for compound ranking. In an out-of-distribution compound set, we observed that the MLPs identified compounds that are chemically dissimilar from those in the training set and are sensitive to single scaffold modifications, making the MLPs potential tools for lead optimization. We applied the MLPs on a pilot study prospective drug discovery campaign, which resulted in the identification of four putative LRH-1 binders. We found that a combination of scoring and prediction metrics enriches for hit compounds across library sizes. In all, this work presents a method to leverage structural and experimental data to aid drug discovery for a challenging protein…

title: Human Resource Accounting Information and Investment Evaluation: Evidence from Individual Retail Investors in Karnataka
abstract: Human Resource Accounting Information (HRAI) gives details about an organisation’s human resources and can provide investors with additional information for evaluating investment opportunities. However, its effective use is influenced by investors’ level of knowledge, their perception of its relevance and the ease with which the information can be accessed, understood and evaluated. The present study examines the knowledge, perceived usefulness and hindrances associated with HRAI among NSE-registered individual retail investors in Karnataka. A quantitative descriptive research design was adopted, and data were collected from 287 individual retail investors using a structured questionnaire administered through both online and offline modes. The HRAI items were classified into five dimensions through Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), namely HR Valuation, HR Composition, HR Performance, Employee Benefits and Employee Governance. The responses were analysed using descriptive statistics and one-sample t-tests. The results indicate that investors have a low level of knowledge across all five dimensions, with the mean scores of the individual knowledge items falling below the scale average. In contrast, respondents expressed a high level of perceived usefulness of HRAI for investment evaluation, with mean scores ranging from 4.33 to 4.41. HRAI was particularly perceived as useful for…

title: Digital Transformation of Retail and Distribution Channels in Advanced Manufacturing: An Evidence-Calibrated Framework Applied to Pak Elektron Limited
abstract: Public descriptions of digital transformation often reveal customer interfaces more readily than the systems connecting them to production and distribution. This paper develops the Digital Manufacturing-to-Market Ecosystem (DM2ME), a six-domain architecture for examining those connections while recording capability maturity separately from the evidence supporting it. A bounded documentary application to Pak Elektron Limited distinguishes corporate infrastructure from its Appliances and Power businesses. The 2025 annual report describes current enterprise resource planning (ERP) integration, manufacturing information systems, reporting tools and technology governance; these disclosures support corporate-level classifications that cannot be inferred from customer-facing websites alone. Appliances provides observable retail and service interfaces, while Power has a reported digital transformer lifecycle initiative. Dealer integration, division-specific system coverage, predictive-model use and adaptive feedback remain only partly observable. Classifications represent the highest level supported by the available documents, rather than estimates of the firm's actual capability ceiling. The contribution is a transparent procedure for stating what an external assessment can establish, how business-unit scope affects inference, and which evidence would justify a stronger claim. Projected changes in precipitation and temperature over the KKSD river basin using a machine-learning-based selective CMIP6 multimodel ensemble
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable climate projections are essential for climate-risk assessment and planning. Yet, uncertainty in Global Climate Models (GCMs) and ensemble construction remains a major challenge. This study developed a machine learning-based selective multimodel ensemble framework to project precipitation, maximum temperature (Tmax), and minimum temperature (Tmin) over the Kangsabati, Keliaghai, Silabati, and Dwarkeswar (KKSD) river basin in eastern India. India Meteorological Department gridded observations were combined with statistically downscaled and bias-corrected NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 simulations. Multiple machine-learning algorithms were evaluated, and Extra Trees was adopted because of its strong predictive performance. A parsimonious four-GCM subset was evaluated against conventional multimodel approaches. Future projections for 2025–2098 under different SSP indicate an overall decline in annual precipitation, ranging from approximately −2.45% to −9.16% relative to 1991–2014, along with strong seasonal redistribution characterised by increased winter precipitation and persistent reductions in monsoon precipitation. Annual Tmax increases from approximately 0.39–0.44 °C in 2025–2039 to 1.53, 2.16, and 2.98 °C in 2085–2098 under SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5, respectively, while corresponding Tmin increases reach 1.40, 1.85, and 2.32 °C. THE NEW KITCHEN CLASSROOM: ASSESSING BLENDED LEARNING ACCEPTANCE IN CULINARY ARTS EDUCATION
abstract: Blended learning is a pedagogy that combines practical, hands-on, and online learning and is gaining popularity in TVET education because it offers flexible learning, enhances practical training by integrating theoretical concepts through online classes, and helps build technical and digital workplace skills among TVET graduates. However, the success of this pedagogical integration relies on students' acceptance. In blended learning, a lack of acceptance can reduce learning engagement, academic performance, motivation, and satisfaction, which can widen learning gaps. This research investigates factors such as learning flexibility, openness to new technology, attitude towards online learning, and basic technological skills on students' willingness to adopt blended learning in culinary arts education. A quantitative survey was administered to 253 diploma and degree culinary arts students at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) campuses across Malaysia. SPSS version 29 was used to conduct a hierarchical regression analysis to identify the significant factors that explain students’ acceptance of blended learning. The findings reveal that factors such as openness to new technology play a dominant role in students' acceptance of blended learning. Attitude and basic technological skills are also highly correlated, indicating that students with a positive attitude toward blended learning a…

title: KOMIK DIGITAL DENGAN MODEL PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN LITERASI VISUAL DAN BERPIKIR KREATIF SISWA KELAS VIII
abstract: ABSTRACT Informatics learning, particularly in the topics of functions and data structures, requires instructional strategies that help students understand visual representations while developing creative approaches to problem-solving. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of digital comics integrated with the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model in improving the visual literacy and creative thinking skills of eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 61 Surabaya. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design was employed, involving 60 students divided equally into an experimental class and a control class, with 30 students in each group. The experimental class learned through PBL-based digital comics, whereas the control class received conventional instruction. Data were collected through pretests and posttests and analyzed using descriptive statistics, normality and homogeneity tests, paired-samples t-tests, and independent-samples t-tests. The experimental class’s mean visual literacy score increased from 56.67 to 80.93, while its mean creative thinking score rose from 52.07 to 79.67. Between-group tests revealed significant posttest differences in visual literacy (t = 10.231, p < .001) and creative thinking (t = 7.736, p < .001). DEEP LEARNING BASED DETECTION OF ANOMALOUS INVENTORY FLUCTUATIONS IN INDUSTRIAL SUPPLY CHAINS
abstract: Fluctuations in inventories across industrial supply chains are caused by interplay between demand, ordering, replenishment, and production which makes it challenging to detect anomalies with just one threshold or simple distributional rules. In this paper we introduce an anomaly detection approach based on four synchronized time series (inventory, demand, ordering, and replenishment). Our model captures normal operating patterns through sliding windows and computes the difference between actual and estimated inventory level as an anomaly score. We tested our model over a 240-step simulated sequence including sudden inventory drops and persistent inventory surpluses; for this sequence the multivariate model obtained an F1 score of 0.897 and an AUC of 0.951, surpassing Isolation Forest, LSTM, GRU, and baseline Transformer models. Detected anomalies matched the injected anomaly events. Results indicate potential use of multivariate time-series modeling for inventory anomaly screening, however, further validation is needed on real-world enterprise data.

title: IMPROVING EFL STUDENTS' WRITING SKILLS THROUGH DIGITAL LEARNING PLATFORMS
abstract: Writing is a complex skill for EFL (English as a Foreign Language) learners because it involves grammatical competence, vocabulary knowledge, idea organization, and the ability to convey meaning coherently. Technological developments have introduced various digital platforms that can support writing instruction, particularly through collaborative features, feedback, and assessment tools. This article aims to examine the roles and uses of digital learning platforms in EFL writing instruction based on previous research. This study employed a literature review method involving 15 scholarly publications published between 2021 and 2025. The data were analyzed thematically by categorizing the findings according to the functions of technology in writing instruction. The review identified three major themes. First, Google Docs supports collaborative writing through shared text production and editing, interaction among learners, and engagement in the writing process. Second, artificial intelligence-based technologies, particularly ChatGPT, provide alternative sources of feedback and support for writing revision, although the accuracy and relevance of their outputs still require evaluation and teacher guidance. title: Trichrome-based deep learning for quantitative assessment of steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
abstract: Abstract Aims: This study aimed to develop and evaluate Tri-MASH, a trichrome-based deep learning model for quantitative assessment of steatosis, classic hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis, and to explore their spatial relationships. Inflammatory-cell density was evaluated as an exploratory measure. Methods and results: Tri-MASH was trained using 161 training specimens and internally evaluated on 30 randomly selected, nonoverlapping specimens. External evaluation comprised 39 biopsies independently scored by four pathologists and 524 baseline and week-72 biopsies from 262 clinical-trial participants. Internal-validation F1 scores ranged from 78.9% for inflammatory-cell detection to 99.2% for sinusoidal fibrosis. In cohort 1, associations with median pathologist assessments were very strong for steatosis (Rs = 0.85) and fibrosis (Rs = 0.87–0.88) and moderate for ballooning (Rs = 0.55). In cohort 2, exploratory pooled analyses showed moderate associations for steatosis (Rs = 0.52), ballooning (Rs = 0.54), and total and portal-septal fibrosis (Rs = 0.50); confidence intervals and p values were unadjusted for repeated observations within participants. Inflammatory-cell density correlated poorly with lobular inflammation grade (Rs=-0.01 to 0.14). title: EMBEDDING SDG 12 THROUGH COMPETITION-BASED LEARNING IN VOCATIONAL CULINARY EDUCATION FOR PASTRY STUDENTS
abstract: This paper presents a qualitative case study of how a Diploma in Pastry Arts program operationalises United Nations Sustainable Development Goal SDG 12 through a structured, plant-based competition cooking initiative called the Plant-to-Plate Challenge. Embedded within the “Essential Cookery Skills” course at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Cawangan Pulau Pinang, the initiative unfolds across three progressive stages: plant-based component development, full plant-based meal design, and a judged team competition, followed by digital e-portfolio documentation. Drawing on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) competency frameworks and the literature on competition-based learning and reflective e-portfolios, this paper analyses the pedagogical design and implementation. Respondents were semester one students (n=32) of the March 2026 cohort. As a single-semester, non-comparative case, the findings indicate that the competition format generated short-term but meaningful gains in student engagement, technical problem-solving and understanding of ingredient substitution, while the e-portfolio provided visually mediated documentation of sustainability practice. The paper argues that pastry arts education, historically anchored in animal-derived and refined ingredients and under-represented in sustainability scholarship, can meaningfully advance SDG 12 competencies when experienti…

title: Transforming AI chatbots into metacognitive partners: Culturally grounded mathematics learning in LMS-based environments
abstract: The utilization of AI chatbots in mathematics education is on the rise, with these bots often serving as the primary providers of answers, potentially limiting learners’ engagement in reflective and metacognitive reasoning processes. The present study examines how AI chatbots can function as metacognitive partners within a culturally contextualized mathematics learning framework implemented through a learning management system (LMS). Using an embedded multiple-case study design, the data were collected from 33 preservice teachers enrolled in the Department of Mathematics Education during their seventh semester. The data were collected from several sources: chatbot interaction logs, participatory observations, metacognitive reflective journals, and semi-structured interviews. Four participants were purposively selected for in-depth analysis. Thematic analysis revealed two distinct patterns in the interaction of pre-service mathematics teachers with the AI chatbot when completing assignments: an iterative interaction pattern and a linear interaction pattern. The iterative pattern involves repeated exploration, whereas the linear pattern follows a straightforward path with minimal verification. The two patterns yield different metacognitive outcomes, depending on the degree of regulation. When iterative interaction is well regulated, it fosters metacognitive success; however, when…

title: Reduced attenuation of neural activation during fear extinction learning in patients with anxiety disorders: a delayed fear extinction fMRI study
abstract: Abstract Clarifying the patterns of neural activation during fear extinction in anxiety disorders (ADs) is essential for advancing our understanding of inhibitory learning. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly characterized in large, heterogeneous cohorts of patients. Utilizing a delayed fear extinction fMRI paradigm, this study examined neural responses in 280 patients with ADs — comprising panic disorder, agoraphobia, panic disorder with agoraphobia, social anxiety disorder, and multiple specific phobias — compared to 103 healthy controls (HC). The attenuation of neural activation to conditioned fear (CS+) and safety (CS−) stimuli from early versus late extinction was compared between groups. Subjective ratings of US-expectancy, arousal, and valence were also collected. In a whole-brain voxelwise analysis, patients showed significantly reduced attenuation of neural activation across both CS+ and CS− relative to HC from early compared to late phases of extinction learning. This pattern was observed in a broad network, encompassing the insular cortex (IC) and bilateral supplementary motor area (SMA), among other regions. No interaction between group and stimulus type was observed. Region-of-interest analysis of the left anterior insular cortex confirmed that reduced attenuation in this region represents a robust neural signature of altered extinction learning in ADs…

title: Professional Competence of Madrasah Teachers in the Digital Era: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Develop Islamic Learning Media at MTs Miftahul Jannah
abstract: The development of digital technology, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), requires madrasah teachers to have adaptive professional competence in developing contextual learning media that embody Islamic values. Teachers at MTs Miftahul Jannah still face limitations in digital literacy, understanding of how to use AI, and skills in designing innovative learning media. This community service program aims to describe the process and outcomes of strengthening teachers’ professional competence through training and mentoring in the use of AI to develop Islamic learning media. The activity used a descriptive qualitative approach with a participatory method involving 20 teachers. The implementation stages included observation and needs analysis, training, hands-on media development practice, mentoring, and reflection. Data were collected through observation, interviews, documentation, and analysis of media products, then analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with source and technique triangulation to ensure data validity. The results show changes in three aspects: improved teacher understanding of the wise and ethical use of AI, growing skills and confidence in designing learning media, and the creation of Islamic learning media products that are ready for classroom use. These findings indicate that training based on hands-on practice and continu…

title: Implementing Cooperative Learning to Enhance Fifth-Grade Students’ Science Learning Outcomes: A Classroom Action Research Study
abstract: This study aimed to describe the implementation of the cooperative learning model, students’ learning activities, science learning outcomes, and the challenges encountered, together with the efforts made to address them, in Grade V at UPTD SD Inpres Lasiana, Kupang City. This study employed Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles, each consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 30 fifth-grade students, comprising 17 boys and 13 girls. Data were collected through classroom observations and written tests. The observational data were used to examine students’ learning activities and the teacher’s classroom management, while the written tests measured students’ learning outcomes. The findings revealed an improvement in students’ learning outcomes following the implementation of cooperative learning. The proportion of students achieving the minimum mastery criterion increased from 50% in Cycle I to 90% in Cycle II, representing a 40-percentage-point improvement. Student participation was also reflected in increased engagement in observation, experimentation, and group work, with the frequency of these activities rising from 23 occurrences in Cycle I to 30 in Cycle II. abstract: Aims: This study aims to analyze access to green finance among micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia by identifying structural barriers, enabling factors, and the suitability of green financing instruments for MSMEs’ characteristics and stages of green practice adoption. It also develops a conceptual framework to explain the interaction between MSMEs’ internal readiness, financial institutions’ assessment mechanisms, and policy ecosystem support in expanding access to green finance. Method: This study employs a narrative literature review approach. Relevant literature was retrieved through Google Scholar and GARUDA, while publication metadata were cross-checked through Crossref. A critical thematic analysis was conducted on relevant scholarly articles, regulations, and institutional reports to identify recurring barriers, evaluate the suitability of financing instruments, and synthesize strategies for strengthening MSMEs’ access to green finance in Indonesia. Results: The findings indicate that barriers to green finance access emerge from the interaction of three dimensions. First, the internal MSME dimension includes limited financial and environmental literacy, inadequate financial record-keeping, administrative constraints, and limited capacity to bear the upfront costs of green investment. Second, the financial institution dimension involves collat…

title: Machine Learning-Based Screening and Rationalization for Aromatic Guest Inclusion into MOF Crystals
abstract: Abstract The exploration of metal–organic framework (MOF) properties arising from guest inclusion, particularly for less-volatile molecules incorporated through solution processes, remains time-consuming and data-intensive compared with framework synthesis, leaving much of the existing MOF library unexplored. We report a machine-learning (ML)-based guest screening approach that predicts favorable guests from a library of ∼19,000 aromatic compounds, trained on 42 inclusion experiments for a single MOF. The ML model, constructed using relevant molecular features extracted from feature sets, predicts guest inclusion amounts across low to high values, with performance superior to models containing irrelevant features. The predictions successfully identify suitable guests that can be accommodated through soaking, enabling selective inclusion from mixed solutions and facilitating crystalline sponge analysis. In the absence of inclusion crystal structures, extensive structural search calculations using a neural network potential provide insights into guest alignment and noncovalent interactions, complementing the ML outcomes. This approach substantially reduces the experimental time and cost required to explore guest-inclusion-based MOF properties.

title: Structured Exponentiation Dot Product Attention-based Vision Transformer with Coordinated FuseNet Transfer Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: The number and intensity of cyberattacks have grown exponentially with the explosive growth of cloud computing,Internet of Things (IoT), and high-speed networks. According to recent reports, more than 70% of the contemporary networks intrusions are either stealthy or low-rate intrusions, which are proven to be hard to detect with the traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs). Despite their extensive implementations in signature-based and rule-based IDS, these methods have weaknesses in terms of being slow to adapt to zero-day attacks, a high number of false alarms, and a lack of scalability when dealing with vast data volumes and high-dimensional network traffic data. To overcome these issues, this research proposes a Structured Exponentiation Dot product-based Network Intrusion Detection System (SED-NIDS) to facilitate the determination of accurate and robust cyberattacks. The proposed system is end-to-end, unlike single-model IDS methods, which perform feature learning and decision fusion independently, leading to better generalization of the system to various attack scenarios. The proposed SEDNIDS achieves an accuracy of 98.6%, 93% precision, 94% recall, and an F1-score of 93.5%. The proposed system also displays a reduced false alarm rate of 1.3% indicating how the system is applicable in real-time deployment. SED-NIDS is a precise and robust IDS that will answer the c…

A Comparison of Two Strategies for Converting to Adalimumab Biosimilarsa
abstract: Abstract Purpose We retrospectively compared 2 strategies for adalimumab biosimilar conversion at an academic medical center to better understand the effects of each strategy. Methods The formulary for our institution is managed by physician- and pharmacist-led task forces, in collaboration with our specialty pharmacy and pharmacy benefit manager. We implemented 2 phased strategies to increase adalimumab biosimilar utilization. First, we added preferred biosimilars to the formulary at parity to reference product and relied on prescribers to promote conversion. Second, we added an interchangeable biosimilar and removed reference product from the formulary while leveraging specialty pharmacy workflows for prescription conversions, streamlined facility inventory, and minimized dependence on prescriber workflows. For both strategies, we evaluated prescribing trends, dispensing data, and pharmaceutical spend for all medical center patients, specialty pharmacy patients, and patients with the top 3 specialty pharmacy payers. Results During phase 1 (quarter [Q] 2 of 2023 [2Q23] to 1Q24), reference product dispensing remained largely unchanged (<5% reduction). Phase 2 (2Q24 to 2Q25) resulted in a significant reduction in specialty pharmacy dispenses of reference product, from 95.7% to 19.0%. title: Fostering equitable access to palliative care for people experiencing homelessness and serious illness: a multi-method, citizen science study using a theory of change approach
abstract: Abstract Background In Germany, there are currently over 531,000 people experiencing homelessness (PEH), with a high burden of physical illness, mental illness and substance use, often occurring simultaneously as trimorbidity. PEH face substantial barriers to healthcare and frequently access palliative care (PC) late or not at all. These challenges require approaches that account for complex health and social needs and fragmented care structures. However, co-produced, practice-ready, and transferable approaches remain rare. This study aims to identify current issues and needs in PC provision for PEH in Münster, Germany and to develop a Theory of Change (ToC) to inform future improvements in care. Methods This is an investigator-initiated, multi-method study conducted in Germany. Citizen Scientists and frontline staff co-designed the study, co-facilitated the empirical research and joined analysis and workshops. We hosted a cross-sector World Café ( n = 18) and conducted in-depth interviews ( n = 5) with people living with serious illness and homelessness. World Café material was analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Interviews were analysed using a constructivist Grounded theory informed approach. A ToC was developed iteratively throughout the whole project in recurrent meetings. Results The World Café mapped three dominant problem fields and two enabling conditions. Prob…

abstract: Abstract The hemodynamic effects of end-stage kidney disease and associated pulmonary hypertension may impair right ventricular (RV) function and influence cardiovascular (CV) outcomes after kidney transplantation (KT). We aimed to evaluate the association between pre-transplant echocardiographic RV function parameters, including RV strain, and long-term CV outcomes following KT. In this retrospective cohort study, we included adult KT recipients at a single Midwest academic center from 2015 to 2024 who had adequate-quality pre-transplant echocardiograms and follow-up at our institution. RV function parameters included tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S′), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), fractional area change (FAC), RV index of myocardial performance (RIMP), and RV free wall strain measured by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, heart failure hospitalization, coronary revascularization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmias. Among 371 patients (mean age 53.5 ± 13.1 years; 56% male) followed for a median of 4.9 years (IQR, 3.1–6.4), 79 (21.2%) experienced MACE. On univariable Cox analysis, RIMP and RV strain parameters were associated with MACE, whereas S′, TAPSE, and FAC were not…

abstract: Purpose of Study: This study examined the effect of work-life balance on employee performance in insurance companies in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Specifically, the study assessed the influence of flexible teleworking, wellness programs, family-friendly policies, and reasonable workloads on employee performance, addressing existing knowledge gaps concerning workplace practices and organizational productivity outcomes. Methodology: The study adopted a descriptive research design targeting 520 employees across 65 insurance companies in Nairobi City County, Kenya. A sample of 226 respondents was determined using Yamane's formula. Primary data were collected through semi-structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis to establish relationships between variables. Findings: The findings revealed that work-life balance practices positively and significantly influenced employee performance in insurance companies. The regression model demonstrated strong explanatory power (R² = 0.837), accounting for 83.7% of employee performance variation. Flexible teleworking exhibited the highest unstandardized coefficient (B = 0.462), followed by reasonable workloads (B = 0.378), family-friendly policies (B = 0.376), and wellness programs (B = 0.345). Assessment Reform for Introduction to Sociology from the Perspective of the Field Classroom: A Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Framework
abstract: Assessment reform is central to turning the field classroom from an occasional activity into a durable mechanism of sociological learning. Drawing on the reform of Introduction to Sociology, this article explains how process-based field assignments and summative examination tasks can be aligned around knowledge, competence, and value formation. It then introduces a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation framework whose indicators and weights come directly from the assessment scheme. The framework converts cohort-level score distributions into membership vectors and returns diagnostic evidence to teaching. The reform shows that field-based questioning and assignments help students connect theory with everyday life, strengthen research awareness, and make value-oriented education concrete. Experiential learning, constructive alignment, and transparent evaluation should therefore be designed as one system.

The Determinants of Audit Quality in an Emerging Market: Evidence from Cambodian Auditors
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the impact of auditors’ skepticism, competence, motivation, time budget pressure, and audit tenure on audit quality in Cambodia. It also examines the indirect effects of auditors’ skepticism, competence, and motivation on audit quality, mediated by time budget pressure. Six latent constructs, or unobserved variables—auditors’ skepticism, competence, motivation, time budget pressure, audit tenure, and audit quality—are developed in the Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) using observed or manifest variables. The data are collected from 107 independent auditors in both local and international accounting firms in Cambodia. Path analysis within the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework is utilized to evaluate the influence of these constructs on audit quality, with auditor experience designated as a control variable. The study found that auditor competence and tenure significantly enhance audit quality, while skepticism, motivation, and time budget pressure showed no direct effect. However, skepticism, competence, and motivation significantly influenced time budget pressure. Despite this, it did not impact audit quality and therefore does not serve as a mediating variable. abstract: The increased use of skincare products has raised growing global concerns as regards exposure to heavy metal contaminants andmicrobes. The aim of this research study was to assess microbial contamination, heavy metals and associated health risks in skincareproducts from different market sources. A total of forty skincare products were randomly sourced and analyzed. Microbial contamination was assessed using standard microbiological methods. Heavy metal contaminations were analyzed for manganese, lead, nickel, copper, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, cobalt and zinc using atomic absorption spectrophotometry. Human health risk assessment for skin exposure was conducted using hazard index, carcinogenic risk models and hazard quotients. The result from this study showed variations in microbial counts as regards organism, product type, and source: online products showed high total bacterial counts and the highest reported Salmonella and Shigella counts, supermarket oil had the highest total fungal count, and open-market products showed high coliform and E. coli counts in selected products. All sources contained measurable concentrations of the assessed metals. abstract: This study examines the drivers of sustainable regional economic growth and economic performance through two complementary structural models analyzed using SmartPLS. Model 1 evaluates the role of Green Infrastructure Investment (GII) in influencing Environmental Quality (EQ), Economic Performance (EP), and Sustainable Regional Economic Growth (SREG). Model 2 explores how Regulatory Framework Quality (RFQ), Legal Certainty (LC), and Market Efficiency (ME) affect Economic Performance. A quantitative approach based on Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) is employed to assess both measurement and structural relationships. The results indicate that all constructs demonstrate strong reliability and convergent validity. The structural model demonstrates strong explanatory power, with -square values exceeding 0.98 across endogenous variables in Model 1, and ranging from 0.898 to 0.966in Model 2. In Model 1, green infrastructure investment has a strong positive impact on environmental quality and economic performance, while environmental quality significantly enhances sustainable growth. However, economic performance and the direct effect of green investment on sustainable growth show negative relationships, indicating short-term trade-offs. title: Product Substitution and Comparative Dynamics in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market
abstract: Pharmaceutical product substitution has become a central structural mechanism reshaping pricing, competition, and firm strategy within the Indian pharmaceutical market under an increasingly regulated healthcare environment. This study examines the regulatory, economic, and institutional determinants of generic and therapeutic substitution in India, with particular emphasis on how policy-driven mechanisms shape substitution outcomes across public and private healthcare systems. Using an analytical secondary-data design, the study draws on evidence from the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), Health Management Information System (HMIS), National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM), Competition Commission of India (CCI), and international benchmarks from the OECD and WHO. The findings show that generic medicines account for approximately 97% of pharmaceutical sales by volume in India (AIOCD-AWACS), yet represent only around 38% of total market value, yielding an Effective Substitution Efficiency Ratio (ESER) of 0.39, substantially lower than the OECD average of 0.77. While generic entry results in 30–50% revenue erosion for branded products and generics priced 50–80% lower rapidly gain substantial volume share, economic substitution remains incomplete. title: INSTALLATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SOLAR PANELS AS AN ALTERNATIVE ELECTRICITY SOURCE FOR POWERED SYSTEMS IN AUTOCAD LABORATORY FOR TEACHING, LEARNING AND TRAINING
abstract: Unreliable electricity supply remains a major constraint to practical training in technical education institutions across Nigeria, with the AutoCAD Laboratory a digitally intensive facility being especially vulnerable to power interruptions. This study is on design, installation, and maintenance of a solar panel photovoltaic (PV) system as an alternative electricity source for an AutoCAD Laboratory. An electrical load audit established a total daily demand of approximately 72.2 kWh, against which an 15.44kWp solar array (8 × 580W JA-Solar Panels double side), a 11.7 kVA, 48V/60-battery Leoch Lithium, MPPT charge controllers, and a 5 kVA pure sine wave hybrid inverter were sized, procured, and installed. Postinstallation testing over a two-week period under varied weather conditions showed the system delivering 96.6% of its design output, sufficient to power all computers, lighting, and the projector for a full 8-hour training day without interruption. Cost analysis showed a total installation cost of approximately N6,600,000:00 with a projected payback period of 3-4 years against Ikeja Electricity, Petrol, and diesel-generator alternatives, and an expected system lifespan of 20-25 years. The findings confirmed that solar PV technology is a technically reliable and economically justifiable alternative to grid electricity for powering technical education laboratories in Nigeria. …

Beyond Free Certification: Administrative Burdens and Market Inclusion in Indonesia’s 2026 Halal Transition
abstract: This qualitative documentary study examines how Indonesia’s halal-certification transition distributes administrative responsibilities and subsidized access across micro and small enterprises and public institutions. A purposive case analysis compares enacted regulations, technical decrees, January and April 2026 SEHATI allocation schedules, a dated October government announcement, and relevant peer-reviewed studies. Findings distinguish waived application charges from eligibility checks, documentation, facilitator work, and enforcement review. The original 1,350,000 SEHATI allocation was formally revised to 1,090,891 places on 8 April 2026; these are budgeted facilitation slots, not measured certifications. On 16 October, the government announced an extended compliance schedule for selected categories, but the operative amending government regulation could not be independently authenticated by the evidence cut-off. We propose a bounded burden-incidence framework linking information clarity, procedural usability, facilitation capacity, assurance quality, and reviewability. The evidence establishes policy design and administrative assignments, not applicant costs, realized market inclusion, causal business effects, or equitable provincial access. The contribution is a time-specific institutional diagnosis and an auditable agenda for subsequent firm- and agency-level evaluation.

title: Laser‐Architected Hierarchical Wood Evaporator for Salt‐Resistant Solar Desalination and Dual‐Mode Water–Electricity Cogeneration
abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater scarcity and intermittent solar irradiation motivate the development of technologies for freshwater production and electricity generation. However, salt accumulation limits the long‐term operation of solar interfacial evaporators. A laser‐architected delignified balsa wood evaporator (DBW/LCC) with a 3D cylindrical array and laser‐carbonized surfaces is fabricated through delignification, laser engraving, and in situ laser carbonization. The array enhances light trapping and exposes additional sidewall area. Vertically aligned hydrophilic channels sustain capillary water supply and, together with the hydrophobic top surface, establish asymmetric wettability. DBW/LCC achieves an average absorptance of 99.46% over 250–2500 nm. The wetted surface exhibits a valley–plateau temperature difference of ∼1.2°C. Thermo–solutal Marangoni circulation may contribute to brine redistribution. The evaporator maintains stable evaporation for 150 h in 20 wt.% brine without visible salt deposition. Under 1 sun, it achieves a mass‐loss rate of 5.09 kg m −2 h −1 normalized to its horizontal projected area, with an apparent evaporation efficiency of 99.85% calculated using an effective enthalpy. Coupled with a thermoelectric module, it generates voltages of 86.3 mV under 1 sun and 79.8 mV at a wind speed of 9.6 m s −1 without illumination. This platform offers a route to decentra…

Geographic Pricing and Cross-Market Tariff Spillovers in a Differentiated Bertrand Duopoly
abstract: This paper studies how third-degree price discrimination impacts the Nash equilibrium of a duopolistic Bertrand model in differentiated markets. The model looks at two automobile producers, one based in the UK and the other based in the EU, competing in two different markets–Ireland and Britain market. The European Union producer faces a tariff only in the British market, while the United Kingdom producer faces no tariff in either of the markets. By calculating both firms’ best-response functions, this study compares the equilibrium prices and quantities under geographic price discrimination and a uniform price system. The results show that price discrimination results in the tariff increasing both producers' equilibrium prices in Britain, while leaving prices in the Irish market unchanged. This leaves the cost shock isolated in the British market. Additionally, the tariff increases the British producer’s equilibrium quantity demanded while reducing the EU producer’s quantity demanded. However, under uniform pricing, the tariff results in a cross-market spillover, increasing equilibrium prices in Ireland, set by both producers, despite the absence of a tariff in that market.

Chest pain risk-stratification tools used or trialled in Ambulance Health Service settings: A Scoping Review
abstract: Introduction Patients with chest pain account for a significant proportion of ambulance attendances and Emergency Department (ED) presentations. Rapid identification of life-threatening aetiologies and differentiation from benign causes enables timely interventions and efficient utilisation of healthcare resources. Chest-pain risk-stratification tools are used throughout healthcare; their implementation into Ambulance Health Services (AHS) (i.e. Emergency Medical Services) may support ambulance clinicians with clinical decisions to safely divert patients to alternative care pathways. Objectives This scoping review maps literature describing the use and/or evaluation of chest-pain risk-stratification tools within AHS. It (1) identifies and describes tools used or trialled in adults with chest pain to stratify risk of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or major adverse cardiac event (MACE); (2) reports key characteristics and resource requirements; and (3) describes whether tools have been validated for AHS use. Methods This scoping review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and presented using PRISMA-ScR. Searches of CINAHL, MEDLINE Complete, and Scopus were performed, with grey literature searches through Google Scholar and Trove. Data was extracted using a structured data-charting approach and summarised descriptively, including frequency mapping where…

title: Impact of a pharmacist-led pharmacogenomic service on test capture rates in oncology: A retrospective pre-post cohort study, 2024-2026
abstract: Background Pharmacogenomic (PGx) testing can support clinical decision-making to reduce toxicity associated with commonly used oncology therapies. However, PGx testing remains underutilized in oncology practice due to lack of personnel to coordinate testing. We evaluated whether the implementation of a pharmacist-led PGx service increased PGx testing among oncology patients. Methods We used a retrospective cohort study to compare outcomes from the pre-and post-intervention periods following implementation of a pharmacist-led PGx service within our Duluth oncology clinic, Minnesota-USA. EHR/laboratory data were extracted on adult cancer patients with planned/receiving 5-fluorouracil, capecitabine, or irinotecan between September 1, 2024, and March 31, 2026. The primary outcome was PGx capture, defined as the rate of patients who received PGx testing prior to chemotherapy initiation. Secondary outcomes included tests with actionable results and the proportion leading to therapy modification. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square test, Mann-Whitney U test, and adjusted (age and sex as covariates) logistic regression were used. All analyses were performed using SPSS (IBM 29.0) and RStudio (2025.09.1 + 401) with a statistical significance at ≤0.05. title: Stakeholders Involvement, Project Performance, and Service Delivery in Kenya's Water Flagship Projects: A Three-Construct System, Competing Structures, and Cross-Sectional Versus Temporal Coherence
abstract: Stakeholder involvement, project performance, and service delivery are usually studied as links in a presumed causal chain, but their joint structure, the alternatives to the chain, and the agreement between project-level and portfolio-level evidence are rarely examined. This study analyzes the three constructs as a system in Kenya's water flagship projects.Survey data from 208 usable questionnaires (65.62% response; stratified sample of 317 of 1,804 projects) were analyzed with partial correlations, maximum-likelihood fit of competing three-variable structures with information criteria, Monte Carlo mediation, dominance and commonality analysis, a Gaussian conditional-independence graph for the four constructs including tendering strategy, and a comparison with recorded annual performance and service delivery indices (2015-2019; n = 5) using correlations, first differences, lags, gap series, and a domain cross-correlation matrix. title: Meeting the demand to teach mathematics using technologies – a Cross-Sectional analysis of In-Service and Pre-Service teachers’ Technology-Related professional knowledge
abstract: Mathematics teachers are required to effectively integrate technology into mathematics teaching. Meeting this demand draws on their technology-related professional knowledge. While standards specify competencies teachers should develop, little is known about the extent to which pre- and in-service teachers actually meet such demands. Based on a sample of N = 409 German pre- and in-service secondary mathematics teachers, this study aims (i) to investigate differences between in-service and pre-service teachers regarding their technological content knowledge (TCK) and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPCK), and to characterize the range of teachers’ TCK and TPCK by describing which demands different shares of the sample can meet. Using item-response-theory methods, we found no significant overall differences between pre- and in-service teachers in TCK or TPCK. However, group-specific strengths emerged: in-service teachers performed relatively better on demands involving dynamic geometry software, whereas pre-service teachers showed advantages in spreadsheet-related tasks. Characterizing the range of TCK, demands successfully addressed by 75% of the sample include identifying suitable technology to solve a mathematical task. In comparison, only 25% of the sample demonstrated basic spreadsheet skills. Teachers’ TPCK ranges from knowledge that allows them to identify sin…

title: Pain Characterization: Presentation Patterns, and Multidimensional Assessment in Women with Advanced Gynecologic Cancer in a Palliative Care Service
abstract: Abstract Background Pain in advanced cancer is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon extending beyond intensity to include biological, psychological, and social components. In women with advanced gynecologic malignancies, pain is highly prevalent yet often undercharacterized, particularly in resource-limited settings where disparities in access and delayed integration of palliative care may influence its presentation and management. Objective To characterize multidimensional pain features and identify distinct descriptive pain patterns in women with advanced gynecologic cancer receiving palliative care. Design Observational study. Setting/Subjects Electronic medical records of women aged ≥18 years with advanced gynecologic cancer and documented pain, treated at a tertiary cancer center in Mexico between 2013 and 2023, were reviewed. Measurements Sociodemographic and clinical variables were collected. Pain assessment included location, intensity, time of onset, and characteristics (somatic, visceral, neuropathic, or mixed). Psychosocial factors, including anxiety and depression, were also evaluated. Descriptive statistics were used to explore multidimensional pain patterns. Results A total of 1,015 women were included (median age 56 years; most had≤12 years of education). Cervical and ovarian cancers predominated (43.4% and 32.3%). Pain was mainly pelvic or abdominal (81.0%)…

title: The Effect of Taste, Service Quality, and Omnichannel Experience on customer Satisfaction and Loyalty at Tomoro Coffee Surabaya
abstract: Tomoro Coffee has grown rapidly in Surabaya, but intense competition among coffee shops makes it easy for customers to switch if they encounter dissatisfaction with the product or service. This study focuses on Tomoro Coffee customers in Surabaya and examines the effects of taste, service quality, and omnichannel experience on Customer satisfaction and loyalty. Questionnaire data were collected from 130 respondents and analyzed using covariance-based Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with statistical software, through the stages of measurement model, structural model, and model modification. The study aims to obtain an influence model and its simultaneous equations. The results show that the modified model fits well. The independent variables taste (X1), service quality (X2), and omnichannel experience (X3) have a positive and significant effect on Customer satisfaction (Y1) and Customer loyalty (Y2). Meanwhile, Customer satisfaction (Y1) has a positive but non-significant effect on Customer loyalty (Y2). Taste has the largest total effect on Customer satisfaction, while omnichannel experience has the largest total effect on Customer loyalty. Aging Service Organizational Capacity to Deliver Evidence-Based Depression Programs: A National Survey
abstract: Background Integration of mental health programs within community-based, social or aging service organizations has been recommended to serve more older adults with depression. Objective The purpose of this study was to obtain input from aging service organizations across the United States regarding their consideration and resource needs for implementing a lay-led program for depression ( “Do More, Feel Better,” DMFB). Methods An online survey distributed via email inquired about perceived need and consideration regarding DMFB, existing resources, and resource needs. Results Among 242 respondents across 42 states, perceived need for community-based depression services was high (8.7/10), and almost all reported they would consider implementing DMFB (94%). Most had some resources in place to support DMFB (e.g., technology, staff, experience with other evidence-based programs), but most indicated need for key program-specific resources, with the most critical resource needs being funding, dedicated personnel, and training (e.g., depression identification, DMFB delivery, and emergency management).

title: Exploring Pre-Service Biology Teachers’ Anxiety Levels In the University of Education, Winneba
abstract: This study explored the levels and sources of anxiety among Level 100 pre-service biology teachers at the University of Education, Winneba, Ghana, with a focus on how gender influences anxiety experiences during lessons and assessments. Employing a mixed-methods research design, the study integrated a descriptive survey and a qualitative descriptive design to collect both quantitative and qualitative data. The study involved the entire cohort of 81 level 100 pre-service biology teachers (51 males and 30 females). Data were gathered via a structured questionnaire (adapted from the Betz MAR-S scale, 1978) to measure biology-specific anxiety and semi structured interviews. The quantitative findings revealed that while many students reported low to moderate levels of anxiety, significant anxiety was triggered by conceptual difficulty and cognitive overload rather than test-related stress. Inferential statistical testing revealed that male students reported significantly higher levels of anxiety specifically related to conceptual confusion and cognitive overload, though general test anxiety did not differ by gender. Qualitative data further illuminate the impact of anxiety on academic performance, highlighting themes such as cognitive interference, self-doubt, study avoidance, and reduced classroom engagement. These findings underscore the need for targeted pedagogical interventions…

title: Is the association between Arabic, Somali, and Russian maternal origin and exclusive breastfeeding mediated by health service use and peer support?
abstract: Aims: To examine differences in maternal and child health service utilization between Somali-/Arabic-speaking, Russian-speaking, and Finnish-speaking mothers, and to explore whether health service use and breastfeeding peer support mediate the association between maternal origin and exclusive breastfeeding (EBF). Methods: We used data from the FinChildren 2020 survey. The analysis included 5348 mothers with infants aged 4–5 months: 78 Somali-/Arabic-speaking, 123 Russian-speaking, and 5147 Finnish-speaking mothers. Mediation analysis was used to examine the potential mediating role of health service use and breastfeeding peer support in the association between maternal origin and EBF. Results: Among the infants born to Somali-/Arabic-speaking mothers, 23% had not attended routine child health clinic visits, compared with 1.7% of Russian-speaking and 0.4% of Finnish-speaking mothers ( p < 0.005). Somali-/Arabic-speaking mothers were less likely to be offered postpartum nurse home visits (50% vs. 62% and 72%, respectively; p < 0.005) and to report adequate breastfeeding peer support (50% vs. 57% and 69%, respectively; p < 0.005). In unadjusted mediation analyses, breastfeeding peer support and the offer of a postpartum nurse home visit showed the largest indirect effects (−0.013 and 0.002, respectively). Using child health clinic services showed small effects. After adjustment fo…

Utilisation of diverse healthcare providers: Virtual health service engagement and geographic barriers among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adults with chronic disease
abstract: Background Virtual Health Services (VHS) may improve healthcare access for rural Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, but little is known about whether active engagement is associated with more diverse providers or reduced geographic barriers to primary care. This study examined whether active VHS engagement was associated with provider diversity and moderated geographic distance effects on primary care access. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included 74 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adults enrolled in the Goondir Health Services VHS program in rural Queensland. VHS status (active versus inactive in the past 2 weeks) was the primary exposure, with outcomes being provider diversity across 27 types and visit frequency to 12 services over 12 months. Negative binomial regression, adjusted for sociodemographic, lifestyle and health factors including chronic disease burden examined VHS associations with provider diversity, and interaction terms tested whether active engagement moderated distance effects on Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS) visits. Results Of 74 participants, 47 (63.5%) were active VHS users. After covariate adjustment including chronic disease burden, active users utilised significantly more diverse providers, including specialists (IRR=1.78, 95% CI: 1.12–2.82), allied health professionals (IRR=1.60, 95% CI: 1.04–2.48) and overall providers (IRR…

title: The Taxation of Non-Resident Digital Service Providers Without Physical Presence In Tanzania: Jurisdictional and Enforcement Challenges
abstract: The study examines the jurisdictional and enforcement challenges associated with taxing non-resident digital service providers without physical presence in Tanzania. The rapid growth of the digital economy has enabled non-resident providers to supply digital services to Tanzanian consumers without establishing conventional physical premises in the country, creating challenges for traditional tax rules based on physical presence. The study adopts doctrinal and non-doctrinal legal research methodologies. The doctrinal approach analyses relevant tax legislation, subsidiary legislation, policy documents, international tax materials and scholarly literature, while the non-doctrinal approach draws on empirical information obtained from selected respondents and interviews with Tanzania Revenue Authority tax officials. The study is guided by the Ability to Pay Theory, Benefit Theory and Neutrality Theory. The findings indicate that jurisdictional challenges include difficulties in establishing a taxable nexus, determining the location of digital transactions and consumers, accessing information held outside Tanzania, and exercising taxing authority over providers operating across borders. The study further finds that enforcement is constrained by difficulties in identifying and monitoring non-resident providers, obtaining reliable transaction information, reliance on voluntary complian…
