title: Assessment of the Cybersecurity Posture of the Federal Inland Revenue Service Against AI-Assisted Threats Using NIST, MITRE and ACGF Frameworks
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how attackers target national institutions, yet most cybersecurity assessments still check whether controls exist without asking whether governance can cope with AI-assisted threats. This study assesses the cybersecurity posture of the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) in Nigeria against AI-assisted threats using an integrated model that combines the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the MITRE adversary knowledge base and the AI Cybersecurity Governance Framework (ACGF).

title: Patterns and Factors Associated With Contacting a Children and Young People’s Mental Health Crisis Service
abstract: Background In recent years, there has been a notable increase in the number of children and young people (CYP) experiencing mental health crises. Objective This study aimed to explore the demographic and clinical characteristics of CYP who engaged with a mental health crisis service in Northwest England. Method A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data collected from CYP accessing the crisis service between January 2022 and December 2023. Results A total of 1,940 individuals were identified as having contact with the crisis team. Approximately 75% were female, and nearly half lived in the two most deprived socioeconomic quintiles. The majority were aged between 13 and 15 years. The number of contacts per individual ranged from 1 to 186, totaling 7,711 contacts overall. The primary reasons for contact included self-harm (50%) and suicidality (30%). Notably, 29% were not in education, and 28% were also receiving therapy from CYP mental health services. Contact rates peaked during weekdays and during May, September, October, and November. Conclusions The findings highlight the need for multi-agency preventative interventions, particularly targeting females and those from deprived communities, with attention to times of high service demand.

Comparing self-regulation, anxiety, and willingness to communicate across blended, face-to-face, and online instruction in female EFL learners
abstract: Abstract Technology-enhanced language instruction has expanded the range of instructional options available to EFL learners, yet evidence comparing blended, online, and face-to-face modes across multiple cognitive and affective outcomes remains limited, particularly among advanced EFL learners. This study compared self-regulated learning strategies (SRLSs), foreign language classroom anxiety (FLCA), and willingness to communicate (WTC) in English writing across these three instructional modes. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was conducted with 360 advanced female EFL learners in Iran (120 per group), selected through two-stage cluster sampling from language institutes. Learners participated in 10 instructional sessions delivered through blended, online, or face-to-face modes. Pre-test and post-test measures of SRLS, FLCA, and WTC were collected using self-report questionnaires. One-way ANCOVAs were conducted for each outcome, controlling for the corresponding pre-test score, followed by Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. After adjustment for baseline scores, statistically significant between-group differences were observed for SRLS, FLCA, and WTC. The blended group had higher adjusted SRLS scores than the online and face-to-face groups (partial η² = 0.411) and higher adjusted WTC scores in English writing (partial η² = 0.266), but lower adjusted FLCA scores …

title: Hand-washing frequency, gastric histopathology, and depressive symptom burden in adults undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: a structural equation modeling study
abstract: Abstract Depressive symptoms are common among patients referred for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, but their relation to mucosal pathology is unclear. We examined whether gastric histopathological severity links lifestyle exposures to depressive symptom burden in 442 adults undergoing endoscopy at two tertiary care hospitals in Pakistan, 320 of whom had gastric biopsies. Depressive symptom burden (five DSM-5-derived items) and gastric severity (four Updated Sydney System markers) were modeled as latent variables using structural equation modeling. An abrupt shift in patient characteristics and histology grades during recruitment was identified and adjusted for. In the primary model (CFI = 0.971; RMSEA = 0.040), less frequent hand washing was associated with higher depressive symptom burden (β = 0.23, 95% CI 0.06–0.39) but not with gastric severity (β = −0.11, 95% CI − 0.25 to 0.03). Gastric severity was not associated with symptom burden (β = 0.14, 95% CI − 0.06 to 0.35), and the indirect effect through gastric severity was null. The hand-washing association persisted in all six sensitivity analyses, whereas an apparent hand-washing–pathology association appeared only without adjustment for recruitment period. Depressive symptom burden in these patients was unrelated to mucosal pathology but tracked reduced self-care, supporting symptom screening irrespective of endoscopic f…

title: Frequency of transcalvarial brain matter herniation in depressed skull fractures and its association with clinical, hematological, and injury-related radiological factors
abstract: Objective: To assess the frequency of transcalvarial herniation of brain matter in depressed skull fractures (DSF), and to evaluate the clinical, radiological, and hematological factors associated with such herniation. Methodology: This retrospective observational cohort study included patients who presented with depressed skull fractures between January 2024 and April 2026 at the Department of Neurosurgery, Unit-I, Punjab Institute of Neurosciences, Lahore, Pakistan. Chi-square tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U tests were used to assess the association with transcalvarial brain matter herniation in DSF. Results: Among 60 cases of DSF, brain herniation was present in 36.70% (22). The mean age of the cohort was 25.65±13.11 years, with male predominance (78.30%, 47). The median presenting GCS was 14 (14-15). Radiological signs of raised ICP were present in 51.70% (31). The most common mechanism of injury was road traffic accident (RTA; 78.30%, 47). Brain herniation along the DSF was present in 36.70% (22). The most common locations were frontal (53.30%, 32). In the brain herniation group, the median depth of the fragmented segment was 20.0 (19.7-28.5), and the fractured segment median diameter was 39.5 (30.0-40.0). The presenting Glasgow Coma Scale score (GCS) was higher in patients with transcalvarial herniation (p-value 0.026). Whereas the midline shift (MLS; p…

The transcriptional regulation of specialized terpenoid biosynthesis and its regulation by jasmonic acid
abstract: Abstract All plants produce terpenoids for their general metabolism but most, if not all, also produce terpenoids in their specialized metabolism. These specialized metabolites play an essential role in the interaction of plants with their environment, in particular with other organisms. They are also of great economic value to us as they are used as medicine, in our food and as perfumes. The regulation of terpenoid biosynthesis has received much attention as it is costly for the plants to produce even though they only contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Some terpenoids are constitutively produced but most of them are induced upon biotic stress with a key role for the phytohormone jasmonate-isoleucine (JA-Ile). It has become clear that the regulation is mostly at the level of transcription with an important role for basic-helix-loop-helix (bHLH) and MYB transcription factors in the JA-Ile inducible pathways. This review summarizes recent breakthroughs with examples of specific mono-, sesqui- and diterpenoids, describing the complex molecular network regulating their biosynthesis in certain model systems with other phytohormones involved as well. It also points out that several other avenues of regulation need more attention to understand the fine tuning of the regulation. This will help optimizing the production of these specialized metabolites in our crops.

Molecular Mechanism of Proline-Mediated Regulation of Graphene–Bacterial Membrane Interactions: A Balance between Dispersion Stabilization and Membrane Disruption
abstract: Abstract Graphene nanosheets have attracted considerable attention as antibacterial nanomaterials due to their ability to directly damage bacterial membranes. However, the poor dispersion of graphene in aqueous environments limits its practical applications. Recently, natural amino acids [Mao, T.; et al.Nature2025, 645, 915–921].have been proposed as biocompatible stabilizers for nanomaterials. Nevertheless, how amino acid concentration affects graphene-membrane interactions remains unclear. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the regulation of monomeric proline on graphene insertion into bacterial membranes. Three systems containing 0, 1, and 2 M proline were constructed to reveal the influence of proline on graphene transport behavior, membrane perturbation, and molecular interactions. The results show that graphene can spontaneously insert into bacterial membranes under all investigated conditions, indicating that proline cannot completely eliminate graphene-membrane interactions. However, introducing proline significantly delays graphene penetration by enhancing graphene stabilization in the aqueous environment. The average insertion time increases from 22.3 ± 6.8 ns without proline to 95.3 ± 22.4 ns and 102.7 ± 29.1 ns under 2 and 1 M proline conditions, respectively. After insertion, graphene still induces membrane deformation, alte…

title: Hybrid piezoelectric-electromagnetic energy harvesting from ultra-low-frequency human motion via magnetic frequency up-conversion
abstract: Efficiently harvesting ultra-low-frequency vibration energy from human motion to power electronic devices remains challenging. This study presents a compact magnetically coupled energy harvester (MCEH) that integrates piezoelectric (PEH) and electromagnetic (EEH) modules through a shared reciprocating center magnet. The center magnet simultaneously produces electromagnetic induction and excites the piezoelectric cantilevers through nonlinear magnetic repulsion, enabling dual-path energy conversion and magnetic frequency up-conversion from excitation below 10 Hz. A coupled lumped-parameter electromechanical model was established and evaluated using numerical simulations and experiments, including frequency-response, load-matching, human-motion, and sensor-powering tests. At 6.5 Hz, the PEH reaches an RMS voltage of 3.56 V with magnetic coupling, versus only 0.0383 V for the no-center-magnet reference, showing an approximately 93-fold enhancement. Under the matched loads, the system delivers a total output of 1,147.88 μ W and a normalized power density of 31.89 μ W/ cm 3 . The prototype also powers a temperature-humidity sensor under the tested motion conditions, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed approach for low-power wearable sensing.

title: Sesame Oil Cake as a Partial Soybean Meal Substitute in the Practical Diets of Juvenile Asian Seabass ( Lates calcarifer ): Nutritional Performance, Physiological Responses and Nutrigenomic Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing reliance on imported soybean meal (SBM) in aquafeeds has intensified the search for locally available and sustainable alternative protein ingredients. This study evaluated sesame oil cake (SOC), an underutilized agro‐industrial by‐product in Bangladesh, as a partial replacement for imported SBM in diets for juvenile Asian seabass, Lates calcarife r. Five approximately isonitrogenous and isolipidic diets containing 0%, 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% SOC were formulated with progressive reductions in SBM. Juveniles (4.25 ± 0.27 g) were distributed among 15 tanks, with 20 fish per tank and three replicate tanks per treatment and fed for 60 days. Growth performance remained comparable with the control up to 15% SOC, whereas 20% SOC reduced final weight, weight gain, specific growth rates, and survival rate, while impairing feed conversion and protein utilization. Whole‐body crude protein was significantly lower in all SOC‐fed groups than in control. Higher SOC inclusion reduced haemoglobin, haematocrit and mean corpuscular haemoglobin, although most leukocyte indices remained stable. Fish fed 20% SOC also exhibited lower circulating total protein and lipase activity and elevated cholesterol, triglycerides, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT), indicating altered metabolic and hepatic function. Liver architecture was largely preserved at …

title: Synergistic Crystallization Regulation and Defect Suppression via Dual‐Site Molecular Coordination for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long‐term stability. Herein, (1H‐benzo[d]imidazol‐2‐yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual‐site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH 3 + ) and electron‐rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl‐modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non‐radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy‐level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. title: Regulating Resonance‐Related Dynamic Magnetic Response through In Situ MnO Formation in FeCoNiCr 0.4 Mn 0.6 High‐Entropy Alloy for Low‐Frequency Microwave Absorption
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient microwave absorption in the S–C band requires the strength and frequency distribution of resonance‐related magnetic loss to be regulated while sufficient permeability is retained. The key is therefore to balance control of the resonance‐related dynamic magnetic response with preservation of the magnetic contribution from the ferromagnetic matrix. Here, FeCoNiCr 0.4 Mn 0.6 high‐entropy alloy (HEA) powders were subjected to wet milling and low‐temperature annealing to produce anisotropic flakes while enabling controlled in situ oxidation of the intrinsic Mn. The resulting MnO/HEA interfaces were accompanied by changes in the local strain state and magnetic anisotropy environment of the adjacent ferromagnetic matrix, providing a structural basis for the evolution of resonance linewidth and effective damping. At 300°C, limited MnO formation produced a moderate effective damping state while maintaining relatively high permeability and sufficient ferromagnetic‐phase contribution, enabling effective absorption over 3.2–4.9 GHz at a thickness of 3.5 mm. At 400°C, further MnO formation increased the fraction of the non‐ferromagnetic phase and weakened the microwave magnetic response. These results demonstrate that controlling the oxidation degree of intrinsic alloying elements can balance interfacial regulation, dynamic magnetic relaxation, and ferromagnetic‐phase ret…

title: The Influence of Government Regulation on Tourist Motivation in Indonesia's Religious Tourism: The Mediating Role of Marketing Communication Strategies
abstract: Religious tourism is a significant economic sector in Indonesia, yet how government regulation and marketing communication jointly shape tourist motivation remains underexplored. Grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior, this study treats government regulation as an exogenous antecedent linked to perceived behavioral control and institutional credibility, and marketing communication as the proximal lever acting on attitudes and subjective norms. Government regulation was operationalized through policy implementation, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder engagement; marketing communication through advertising, publicity, word-of-mouth, on-site interpretation, and direct and interactive marketing; and tourist motivation through cultural interest, spiritual significance, and recreational opportunity. An online survey was completed by 402 non-pilgrim visitors who had visited an Indonesian religious heritage site in the previous 12 months; 81.9% reported one of five focal sites (Borobudur Temple, Istiqlal Mosque, Tanah Lot Temple, Uluwatu Temple, and Jakarta Cathedral). Ordinary least squares regression showed that government regulation predicted marketing communication ($\beta = 0.676$, $p < .001$), while marketing communication ($\beta = 0.385$) and government regulation ($\beta = 0.355$) both predicted tourist motivation, together explaining 45.8% of its variance. The Sobel t…

title: Regulation of IL ‐13 Signaling by Retinoic Acid in Airway Epithelial Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Dysregulated vitamin A signaling, characterized by reduced all‐trans retinoic acid (ATRA), is associated with asthma severity, and restoration of ATRA signaling may alleviate asthma symptoms. However, the molecular changes induced by inflammatory cytokines such as IL‐13 that are central to asthma pathology and the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) agonists in airway cells are not well established. This study investigates the effects of IL‐13 and RAR agonists on lung epithelial cells using a mass spectrometry‐based proteomics approach. A549 alveolar and BEAS‐2B bronchial epithelial cells were treated with IL‐13 in the presence of vehicle, ATRA (pan‐RAR agonist), or CD1530 (RARγ agonist). Proteomic profiling revealed significant changes in proteins relevant to asthma pathogenesis in IL‐13‐treated cells. IL‐13 upregulated pro‐inflammatory signaling kinases JAK1 and AXL, cytoskeletal‐associated proteins CLDN2 and ACTN4, and inflammatory proteins CD44 and HLAs in A549 cells. In BEAS‐2B cells, IL‐13 upregulated barrier dysfunction‐related proteins P‐Cadherin and α‐catenin, immune activation marker ICAM‐1, and pro‐fibrosis marker TGF‐β. Notably, IL‐13 significantly reduced ATRA biosynthesis enzymes RDH10 and ALDH1A1 which were accompanied by reduced ATRA levels and reduced ATRA biosynthesis in A549 cells as quantified by liquid chromatography‐multistage‐tandem mass spectrometry. title: Doping in Sport: Health Risks, Psychosocial Drivers, and the Evolving Anti-Doping Response
abstract: Doping in sport is often discussed as a problem of prohibited drugs, positive tests, and sanctions. That framing is incomplete. Contemporary anti-doping governance also addresses prohibited methods and conduct that undermines testing and investigation, while effective prevention must account for health risks, athlete decision-making, team cultures, medical practice, and the commercial pressures surrounding sport. This narrative review synthesizes selected peer-reviewed literature and official anti-doping instruments to examine four connected questions: how doping is defined and regulated; what is known about health consequences; why athletes may consider prohibited performance enhancement; and how detection and prevention can be combined more effectively. The evidence indicates that health risks vary by substance, dose, duration, route, combinations, and the population studied, so findings from non-athlete users should not be generalized uncritically to elite athletes. Research on athlete attitudes identifies perceived performance benefits, social influence, recovery concerns, and financial or career pressures as relevant factors, although attitudes do not directly establish actual use. The World Anti-Doping Code and the annually updated Prohibited List provide a harmonized framework, but testing alone cannot address every source of risk. A more credible response combines risk-…

title: Mechanical Response of EPDM Composites Partially Replacing N550 Carbon Black With FGD Gypsum‐Derived Calcium Sulfate Whiskers: Effects of Replacement Ratio and CSW Characteristics
abstract: ABSTRACT To investigate the potential of FGD gypsum‐derived calcium sulfate whiskers (CSW) as a partial substitute for N550 carbon black in EPDM rubber, CSW were incorporated by mass replacement of N550. The replacement ratio was first evaluated by tensile strength, elongation at break, and Shore A hardness. The highest measured tensile strength was 12.96 MPa at 7% replacement, but it was not statistically different from the 0%, 5%, 9%, 11%, and 13% formulations. At 15% replacement, high‐aspect‐ratio CSW (HRCSW), anhydrous CSW (ACSW), and surface‐modified CSW were compared. HRCSW showed the highest tensile strength (12.68 MPa), while CSW‐Ti1 exhibited the highest elongation at break (489.39%). CSW‐Si and ACSW showed relatively high hardness. Surface modification altered the apparent water wettability and surface chemical environment of CSW without obvious bulk‐phase transformation. SEM observations suggested contributions from whisker bridging, pull‐out, crack deflection, and stress concentration. Overall, the mechanical response depends on the combined effects of replacement ratio, whisker geometry, crystalline state, and surface characteristics.

CD3ε F(ab’)₂ PET imaging captures systemic and intratumoral T-cell response to immune checkpoint blockade
abstract: Abstract Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet only a subset of patients achieve durable responses. Because the spatial distribution of T cells within tumors and lymphoid tissues shapes therapeutic outcomes, noninvasive methods capable of monitoring these populations could improve the evaluation of antitumor immune responses. Here, we report the validation of a CD3ε-targeted F(ab’) 2 positron emission tomography (PET) probe for noninvasive mapping of T-lymphocytes across tumors and lymphoid tissues and characterize its effects on endogenous T-cell biology. Relative to the full-length IgG construct, the F(ab’) 2 format demonstrated more rapid blood clearance, enabled high-contrast imaging within 24 h, produced limited changes in endogenous T-cell populations, and did not measurably impair T-cell activation at imaging-relevant concentrations. CD3ε F(ab’) 2 PET detected tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and lymphocytes within the tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLN) across multiple syngeneic tumor models and in a genetically engineered mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma. In a combination immunotherapy study, tumor uptake distinguished responding from non-responding lesions and detected treatment-associated changes across peripheral lymphoid tissues. These results support CD3ε F(ab’) 2 PET as a noninvasive imaging approach that enables assessment of T-cell distributi…

title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavi…

title: Predictors of Response to Neoadjuvant Systemic Therapy and Survival in Patients with cN1 Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with clinically node-positive (cN1) breast cancer represent a heterogeneous population with evolving axillary management strategies. We evaluated whether extent of axillary nodal involvement is associated with survival in cN1 disease. Methods A retrospective study of patients with cT1-4N1M0 breast cancer and biopsy-proven axillary metastasis (2012–2018) was performed. All patients underwent axillary ultrasound (AUS) prior to neoadjuvant systemic therapy (NST) and again before surgery. Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used for statistical analysis. Results Among 825 patients, most had cT2-3 (75.6%), hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2−; 73%), ductal (89.7%) carcinoma. 64.1% (529) had 1–3 abnormal nodes on pretreatment AUS, whereas 35.9% had > 3 abnormal nodes. Definitive axillary surgery consisted of axillary lymph node dissection in 83.3% and sentinel node biopsy or targeted axillary dissection in 16.7%. Pathologic complete response (pCR) rate (breast and nodes) was 22.7%; breast-only and nodal-only pCR rates were 6.4% and 11.8%, respectively. At median follow-up of 5.6 years, 5-year overall survival, breast cancer-specific survival, and event-free survival were 92%, 94%, and 91%, respectively. Integrating machine-learning-based landslide susceptibility and vulnerability for slope-unit risk assessment
abstract: Landslide susceptibility identifies terrain associated with landslide occurrence, whereas risk prioritization also requires information on the vulnerability of threatened elements. This letter presents a slope-unit framework linking machine-learning susceptibility prediction, SHAP-based interpretation, and vulnerability-based relative risk classification. Four models were evaluated using a regional test dataset, and the selected model was applied to 393 slope units. XGBoost achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.952), followed by random forest (0.904), logistic regression (0.662), and support vector machine (0.600). Paired DeLong tests indicated significant differences between XGBoost and logistic regression (LR) and support vector machine (SVM), but not random forest (RF). SHAP analysis identified slope, relief, and elevation as the leading predictors, accounting for 62.83% of normalized grouped importance. High and very high relative risk occupied 21.34% of the mapped slope-unit area. Of 69 very-high-susceptibility units, only 13 were classified as very high risk after vulnerability integration. The framework supports the identification of priority slope units for targeted field investigation, monitoring, and mitigation planning.

The Power of Behavioral Antecedents in Predicting Supply Chain Performance of Crop Seed Enterprises
abstract: This study examined whether opportunistic behavior, supply chain collaboration, social bonds (supply chain socialization) and human resource practices predict supply chain performance, measured as quality, response time, productivity and financial/cost performance, in crop seed enterprises in Kenya. Guided by social exchange and systems theories, a quantitative survey was conducted of 143 crop seed enterprises registered in Kenya as of 2024. Data were collected from supply chain heads, operations officers or their equivalents in public and private seed companies and analyzed using structural equation modeling, with each driver tested in a separate prediction model. Each hypothesis was partially supported, with one performance dimension significantly related to each driver. Opportunistic behavior significantly lowered quality (b = ?0.40, p = .036). Supply chain collaboration (b = 0.225, p = .040) and human resource practices (b = 0.225, p = .033) were positively associated with productivity, while social bonds were associated with shorter response times (b = ?1.024, p = .034). No driver significantly predicted financial/cost performance at the .05 level. title: Transformación digital en la gestión de cobros electrónicos a través de una aplicación móvil
abstract: La transformación digital representa en una pieza clave para modernizar los procesos que involucran a la gestión de cobros electrónicos dentro de las microempresas. A este respecto la presente investigación tuvo como objetivo desarrollar un proceso para la gestión de cobros electrónicos a través de una aplicación móvil. Para esto se realizó una revisión científica en base de datos recomendados, por consiguiente, se desarrolló una herramienta tecnológica el mismo que se puso a prueba en una cadena de restaurantes en Ecuador y se evaluó mediante la aplicación del instrumento modelo de aceptación tecnológica a dueños de cada negocio. Los resultados arrojaron que la propuesta del aplicativo ayuda a controlar y de mejor manera el registro de los cobros electrónicos brinda confiabilidad al momento de uso y atiende a las necesidades de un negocio.

title: Design and Implementation of a Zero Trust API Gateway for Secure and Risk-Aware API Access
abstract: APIs connect clients, applications, and services, but perimeter-based controls alone do not provide sufficient protection when credentials are compromised or traffic crosses distributed environments. This paper describes the design and implementation of a Zero Trust API gateway developed as an inline policy-enforcement layer for protected services. The prototype is implemented with FastAPI and combines password-based authentication, OAuth sign-in, JSON Web Tokens, time-based one-time-password multi-factor authentication, scoped API keys, refresh-token rotation, and role- and scope-based authorization. Its request pipeline includes IP blocking, request logging, adaptive risk scoring, sliding-window rate limiting, and a rule-based web application firewall. The gateway also provides a reverse-proxy component that resolves registered upstream services, applies destination checks, forwards permitted requests, and records request identifiers and timing information. Additional detection components evaluate behavioral signals, impossible-travel indicators, and per-user anomalies using an Isolation Forest model when the required machine-learning dependency is available. Functional verification covers successful and rejected authentication, authorization boundaries, rate-limit responses, malicious-input detection, and proxy behavior. title: Construction and Empirical Analysis of a Multi-Source Assessment System for Theoretical Mechanics under an Outcome-Based Education Framework
abstract: To overcome the limitations of using a single aggregate score to distinguish differences in knowledge mastery, engineering application, and learning-process performance in Theoretical Mechanics, this study developed a multi-source assessment framework based on outcome-based education (OBE). The framework links course outcomes, assessment components, evidence sources, and instructional improvement. Data were collected from two intact classes of Mechanical Design, Manufacturing and Automation in the first semester of the 2025-2026 academic year and included stage tests, homework, learning-management-system (LMS) quizzes, an integrated project, and item-level final-examination scores. The mean final-examination score was 51.17 ± 22.89. The cohort attainment levels for Course Outcomes 1, 2, and 3 were 0.513, 0.436, and 0.553, respectively. Mean stage-test and LMS-quiz scores showed moderate positive correlations with final-examination performance (r = 0.461 and 0.406, respectively; p < 0.01). Project scores were high with limited dispersion and were not significantly correlated with final-examination scores. The multi-source assessment identified kinematics and multi-step calculation tasks as the main learning bottlenecks and revealed insufficient discrimination in project scoring. Accordingly, tiered learning tasks, an analytic project rubric, and a data-informed diagnostic feedba…

title: QRIS CROSS-BORDER AS DIGITAL SOFT POWER SUPPORTING SUSTAINABLE SHOPPING TOURISM: EVIDENCE FROM BATAM, INDONESIA
abstract: The rapid expansion of cross-border digital payment systems has transformed shopping tourism by enhancing transaction efficiency, convenience, and accessibility for international visitors. This study examines the role of Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) Cross-Border in supporting sustainable shopping tourism in Batam, Indonesia, while exploring its function as an instrument of Indonesia's digital soft power. Employing an exploratory qualitative case study design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 25 purposively selected participants comprising policymakers, tourism stakeholders, micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSME) operators, Malaysian and Singaporean tourists, and Batam residents. The study was further supported by non-participant observations at major shopping destinations and netnographic analysis of publicly available digital content related to cross-border payment experiences. The data were analysed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal four major themes. First, QRIS Cross-Border enhances tourists' shopping experiences by reducing cash dependency, minimising currency exchange concerns, and facilitating seamless transactions. Second, it strengthens MSME competitiveness by improving transaction efficiency and encouraging spontaneous purchases by international visitors. Third, the interoperability of QRIS with regional pay…

Customer Engagement and Lead Conversion in Automotive Retail
abstract: This exploratory research paper examines customer engagement and lead conversion at a private Škoda dealership in Pune, India. The study draws on a confirmed aggregate activity summary of 52 walk-in customers observed during a three-month internship, together with an anonymised 24-record enquiry extract. Of the 52 walk-ins, 45 completed a test drive, six booked within the internship period, and three additional bookings were known to occur later. The enquiry extract shows interest concentrated in the Slavia and Kylaq models, although the extract is not a complete cohort and cannot represent the dealership or market as a whole. Field observations from both authors inform a process-level interpretation of needs discovery, product explanation, test-drive coordination, and follow-up. The analysis is descriptive: it does not estimate causal effects, compare dealerships, or attribute booking outcomes to a single intervention. The findings suggest that a dealership should treat the test drive as an intermediate engagement stage and maintain a consent-aware, structured follow-up process that distinguishes in-period bookings from later conversions. The paper contributes a carefully bounded practitioner account of how customer-journey concepts can be applied to automotive retail while preserving the limits of a small, private operational dataset. Multimodal Emotion Detection in Distributed Data Streams: Deep Transformer Ensembles, Cross-Modal Attention Fusion, and Benchmark Evaluation
abstract: Emotion detection represents a vital frontier at the inter-section of affective computing, artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction (HCI). While traditional uni-modal systems—relying solely on text, speech acoustics, or static facial photographs—have established founda-tional benchmarks, they remain fundamentally fragile in real-world conversational dialogues characterized by lex-ical ambiguity, acoustic sarcasm, and visual occlusions. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end, publication-grade deep learning architecture for Multimodal Emo-tion Detection in Distributed Big Data Streams. Our framework synchronizes three specialized foundation models: a linguistic contextual transformer (RoBERTa-Large), a self-supervised acoustic representation encoder (Wav2Vec 2.0), and a spatiotemporal Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) integrated with Facial Action Unit (FAU) tracking. To resolve temporal granularity discrepancies and inter-modal information imbalance, we formulate a novel Hierarchical Cross-Modal Attention Fusion (HCAF) network. The HCAF module leverages bidirec-tional multi-head cross-attention to project acoustic and vi-sual features into the linguistic latent subspace, selectively attending to emotional cues across communicative chan-nels. To address severe affective class skew (where neutral utterances dominate dialogue corpora), we design a hy-brid multi-task lo…

abstract: The study intends to examine the impact of various customer engagement practices identified with respect to the Hotel location on repurchase intention. The perception of hotel customers towards these practices while assessing and organizing the decisions for repatronizing a hotel. It has been predominantly acknowledged that hotel locations play a significant role in repurchase intention. The study was conducted using a survey method, a structured, closed-ended questionnaire to collect responses from 375 hotel guests, and the calculation of descriptive statistics guided the exploration of the perception of customers towards these practices. Further, a study was carried out with regression analysis to examine the impact of various customer engagement practices on re-purchase intention. The study resulted a strong customer perception towards both natural and non-natural attribute of hotel location based engagement practices, with highest mean value (M=4.49), followed by camp/bonfire practices with vale of (M=3,39), and centralized location with the mean of (M=3.89), study also indicates significant impact of primary customer engagement practices in connection to their overall influence on repurchase intention. title: Did the Removal of Stock-Price Floors Improve Short-Run Price Discovery? An Event Study of the Dhaka Stock Exchange
abstract: This study examines whether the January 2024 removal of stock-price floors improved short-run price discovery and reduced price rigidity in the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE). An event-study technique was applied to 338 securities: 306 firms in the main removal cohort, 20 firms in the second-stage cohort, and 12 firms that retained their floors. Market-adjusted abnormal returns were used as the primary specification, while a market model and complete-window samples were used for robustness. Cross-sectional one-sample t-tests assessed abnormal returns, paired-sample t-tests compared pre- and post-removal zero-return rates and intraday high-low ranges, and Welch tests compared treatment cohorts with the retained-floor benchmark. The main cohort recorded a cumulative average abnormal return (CAAR) of -6.77% over [-5, +5], while the second-stage cohort recorded -18.87% over [-3, +3]. Zero-return rates fell from 49.84% to 5.36% in the main cohort and from 97.85% to 3.50% in the second-stage cohort, while intraday ranges increased significantly. The findings are robust for the shorter event windows but sensitive to sample completeness over the longest window. Abnormal returns, zero-return frequency, and the high-low range are proxy indicators rather than comprehensive measures of market efficiency.

title: Arrival Time Occupancy Forecasting for Electric Vehicle Charging Recommendations Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Queueing Models
abstract: A highway driver choosing where to charge needs to know whether a charger will be free when the car arrives, not whether it is free when the trip starts. Amplyt is a charging advisor built around that need. For each station it forecasts connector occupancy at the predicted arrival time and passes the forecast through a finite-capacity queueing model and an isotonic calibration layer. A data audit early in development showed that the original wait-time target could be rebuilt from availability recorded at the same moment, so the target was redefined and the affected workbook withdrawn. The cleaned corpus holds 463 observations of sixteen stations, and the gradient-boosted model was trained on 724 connector-level trials from thirteen of them. In date-blocked rolling-origin evaluation it scored a Brier of 0.1965 against 0.2183 for a station-hour baseline, but most of the gain comes from quiet stations: at the five busiest the improvement is 1.9 percent and statistically indistinguishable, and leave-one-station-out tests are worse at unseen stations. The end-to-end wait pipeline does not beat an always-zero baseline, so forecast minutes are withheld. Arrival-time availability can be shown honestly as bands with confidence tiers, but the data does not yet support wide deployment. abstract: This study compared traditional time-series and machine-learning methods for the monthly forecasting of government expenditure of Cambodia with dataset. The study employed a natural logarithm of the monthly flows of government expenditure from January 2009 to March 2016. The dataset has 207 observations and was divided into train set, where the general model training took place (80%) and test set out of sample (20%). Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) are the metrics that are used to evaluate forecasting performance. The study compares the benchmark against the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and four machine-learning approaches: Hybrid ARIMA-Random Forest, Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The ARIMA model detects a statistical significant seasonal autoregressive behaviour and a drift, indicating that government expenditure is characterized by long-run growth and seasonal dynamics. Nevertheless, the forecasting accuracy using the traditional method is outmatched by results of machine-learning models in general. In particular, XGBoost outperforms all the other models with the lowest MAE, RMSE and MAPE metrics indicating that it is the best forecasting technique. Longitudinal prediction of biological aging: replication and extension of DunedinPACNI
abstract: Abstract DunedinPACNI is a new brain-based aging biomarker derived from cross-sectional MRI data. This study extended previous work by testing whether DunedinPACNI predicts multisystem composites of biological aging in two midlife cohorts. Replicated results indicated that less education was associated with faster DunedinPACNI in both cohorts; novel findings demonstrated that faster DunedinPACNI was associated with higher biological aging in midlife and with accelerated biological aging over 7–15 years from mid-to-later life.

title: Prediction of Subsequent Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure After a 24-Hour Landmark in Cirrhotic Patients With Variceal Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background: Some cirrhotic patients admitted with variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding experience clinical deterioration during hospitalization and develop acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a critical event strongly associated with short-term mortality. Since ACLF may be reversible in its early stages, risk stratification prior to overt ACLF is clinically important. Methods: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study (2015–2025) involving cirrhotic patients admitted for esophagogastric variceal bleeding. A 24-hour landmark analysis was performed among patients who remained ACLF-free during the first 24 hours after admission, with subsequent ACLF before discharge as the primary outcome. Predictors were identified using LASSO and best-subset selection procedures. Logistic regression and random forest models were developed and compared with the available AIMS65 and Glasgow–Blatchford score (GBS) risk categories. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (AUC), calibration (CITL and calibration slope), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis with integrated net benefit). External validation was performed using an independent cohort. Results: Of 1,787 screened patients, 555 were included in the derivation cohort and 240 in the external validation cohort after application of the 24-hour landmark. title: Development of a Maintenance Management Cost-Effectiveness Prediction Model for Ageing Bridge Infrastructure: A Case of TARURA, Tanga Region, Tanzania
abstract: Bridges managed by the Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA) in Tanga Region are maintained largely reactively. About 78% of the annual bridge maintenance budget of TZS 850 million is spent on emergency repairs that cost 2.5 to 4 times more than equivalent preventive work. Existing bridge prediction models mostly predict condition rather than cost, require long inspection histories or large datasets, and omit institutional factors such as budget adequacy. This study therefore developed a maintenance management cost-effectiveness prediction model for ageing bridges in Tanga Region. It adopted a pragmatic philosophy and a convergent parallel mixed-methods design within a single case study of TARURA Tanga. Data were collected through document review, field observation and a structured questionnaire administered to 80 TARURA staff and contractors selected by stratified random and purposive sampling. Factors were ranked with the Relative Importance Index (RII). A multiple linear regression (MLR) model of annual maintenance cost was then estimated from the records of 80 bridges and benchmarked against a Random Forest. Seven of fourteen candidate factors met the RII threshold of 0.74, led by budget adequacy and allocation methods (0.970) and coastal exposure and corrosion (0.945). abstract: Agricultural productivity in India is strongly affected by weather variability, soil degradation and the over- or under-use of fertilizers. Farmers still tend to rely on personal experience when choosing a crop, estimating its yield and deciding how much fertilizer to apply. This paper presents an integrated, web-based decision-support system that performs three tasks within a single framework: crop recommendation, fertilizer recommendation and crop yield prediction. The system takes soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium), temperature, humidity, soil pH, rainfall, soil moisture, soil type and crop type as inputs. The pipeline consists of data acquisition from public repositories, cleaning and normalisation, correlation-based feature selection, and model training using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Random Forest (RF). Model performance is evaluated with cross-validation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and correlation-based measures. In the reported experiments, the ANN model for yield prediction reached an accuracy of 94.70% and the Random Forest model for fertilizer recommendation reached 93.94%, and the crop recommendation model [insert accuracy] was the best performer for its task. The models are packaged in a Java (JSP/Servlet, Weka, MySQL) web application that lets farmers obtain all three recommendations from one input form..

title: Microbiome‐Informed Genomic Prediction of CH4:CO2 Ratio in Holstein Dairy Cattle Using 16S rRNA Profiles and SNP Markers
abstract: ABSTRACT Ruminant animals produce methane as a by‐product of microbial fermentation in the rumen, with cattle being the largest contributors among ruminants. Methane emissions may be influenced directly by the host's genetics and indirectly through host‐mediated effects on rumen microbiome composition. In this study, we investigated whether modelling both direct and indirect genetic effects could improve the genomic prediction of breeding values for methane emissions. We used genotype, methane CH 4 :CO 2 ratio and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing data (16S), including 16S genus (16S‐G), 16S species (16S‐S) from Danish Holstein cows. A conventional genomic best linear unbiased prediction (GBLUP) model was used as a benchmark and compared with a microbiome‐informed GBLUP approach based on three linked linear mixed models for the prediction of breeding values. In GMBLUP, the first model regresses methane emissions on three random animal effects (archaeal 16S, bacterial 16S and polygenic effects) using corresponding microbiome and genomic relationship matrices. The second and third models separately regress archaeal and bacterial 16S on random animal effects defined by the genomic relationship matrix. We evaluated prediction accuracy using five‐fold cross‐validation. The GBLUP model, which used only genomic marker information, achieved a mean accuracy of 0.20 across the five folds…

title: A Comprehensive Review of AI and IoT-Based Water Pipeline Leakage Detection, Prediction and Monitoring Systems
abstract: Water pipeline leakage is a major challenge in water distribution and supply systems because undetected leaks can result in water loss, infrastructure damage, economic losses, and inefficient water management [5], [13]. Conventional leakage inspection methods often depend on manual inspection, periodic maintenance, or specialized equipment, which may not provide continuous real-time monitoring [5], [13]. Recent developments in the Internet of Things (IoT), sensor technology, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) have created opportunities for automated and intelligent pipeline monitoring [9], [11]. This review presents a study of recent techniques used for water pipeline leakage detection, localization, prediction, and monitoring. Different sensing approaches, including flow, pressure, acoustic, and vibration measurements, are reviewed along with machine-learning and deep-learning methods [1], [3], [4], [8], [12], [13]. Existing research demonstrates that pressure and flow measurements are widely used for hydraulic anomaly detection, while vibration and acoustic measurements can provide additional information about leakage events [5], [6], [7]. KUSp, a novel oral spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma cell line with epithelial-mesenchymal transition features and high invasive capacity
abstract: Abstract Spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma (SpSCC) is a rare and aggressive variant of squamous cell carcinoma characterized by biphasic histopathology and epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated features. The scarcity of well-characterized experimental models, particularly those derived from metastatic lesions, has limited investigation of its biology. Here, we established KUSp, a cell line derived from a cervical lymph node metastasis of oral SpSCC, and characterized its pathological, phenotypic, and functional features. The primary tumor showed conventional squamous and spindle cell components, whereas the metastatic lesion predominantly contained spindle-shaped tumor cells expressing both epithelial and mesenchymal markers. KUSp displayed a pronounced EMT-like phenotype characterized by a spindle-shaped morphology, loss of cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and E-cadherin expression, and expression of vimentin, N-cadherin, and α-smooth muscle actin. Functionally, KUSp showed significantly greater Matrigel invasion than the established oral SCC cell lines examined, including HOC313, together with robust migratory activity. title: Capacity Building and Performance of Agricultural Program in Rural Kenya
abstract: Climate-smart agricultural programs require effective monitoring and evaluation (M&E) systems supported by adequate human capacity to achieve sustainable development outcomes. This study examined the role of capacity building in the relationship between M&E tools and the performance of Climate-Smart Agricultural Programs in Rural Kenya. A mixed-methods approach employing descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational research designs was adopted. Data were collected from 246 respondents drawn from project beneficiaries and staff through structured questionnaires and key informant interviews. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and hierarchical multiple regression analyses were used to analyse the data. The findings revealed that respondents perceived capacity building, measured through level of training, technical skills, and technical competence, as highly implemented (overall mean = 4.24, SD = 0.61). Capacity building exhibited significant positive correlations with program performance, with level of training (r = 0.786, p < 0.001), technical skills (r = 0.753, p < 0.001), and technical competence (r = 0.631, p < 0.001) showing strong associations. Hierarchical regression analysis demonstrated that incorporating capacity building substantially increased the explanatory power of the model from 61.1% to 70.5% of the variance in program performance. From Risk Scores to Decision Value: An Evidence-Governed Business Analytics Framework Under Capacity Constraints
abstract: Organizations increasingly use machine learning to identify customers, transactions, suppliers, and projects that require attention. Yet a high predicted risk does not establish that an intervention will help, that its benefit exceeds its cost, or that the underlying evidence permits action. This paper develops an analytical framework that connects prediction, intervention value, evidence verification, and limited managerial capacity. The framework combines temporally governed data, calibrated risk estimates, bounded intervention effects, constrained optimization, and selective human review. Its central object is a decision record linking each proposed action to the information available at the decision time, the assumptions behind its expected value, and the authority required for execution. Analytical propositions establish when risk ranking agrees with value ranking, how uncertainty changes the intervention threshold, and when additional review has positive expected value. A fully specified six-case worked example demonstrates the distinction. With capacity for two interventions, risk ranking produces an assumed expected net value of −1 unit, whereas value-based selection produces 54 units. title: Is histone H2B deubiquitylation via ATXN7L3-dependent enzymes a new mechanism disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders?
abstract: Abstract Neurodevelopmental disorders are lifelong debilitating conditions that affect cognition and originate during embryonic development. Being heterogeneous and with a variety of etiologies, most of these disorders have no targeted treatment or cures, due to our lack of knowledge on the underlying molecular mechanisms disrupted in their pathogenesis. An emerging epigenetic mechanism recently associated with neurodevelopmental disorders is ubiquitylation of histone H2B. This posttranslational modification controls gene expression during neurodevelopment, where histone H2B ubiquitylation levels are tightly regulated by multiple deubiquitylase protein complexes ensuring correct gene expression. Components of deubiquitylase complexes regulating histone H2B ubiquitylation are the protein scaffolds ATXN7L3 and ENY2, and the deubiquitylating enzymes USP22, USP27X, and USP51. Recent clinical studies have highlighted a potential role of H2B ubiquitylation in human neurodevelopment, including the identification of neurodevelopmental disorders associated with gene variants in the ATXN7L3 , USP27X and USP51 genes. Here, we summarize our knowledge of the functions of deubiquitylase complexes that regulate histone H2B ubiquitylation and their components in neurodevelopment, and describe ATXN7L3 , USP27X , and USP51 -associated disorders, proposing future directions on the required resear…

title: Connecting Patient Preparation to Clinical Dialogue in Digital Shared Decision-Making: A Focused Rapid Review of Reviews With a Mechanism-Informed Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Background Digital tools can prepare patients for decisions, but effects on clinical dialogue are uncertain. We synthesized review-level evidence on shared decision-making and examined the role of timing and workflow. Methods We rapidly reviewed systematic, meta-analytic, and scoping reviews identified through targeted PubMed, publisher-platform, and citation searches to 17 July 2026. One reviewer selected, extracted, and appraised reports and revisited eligibility after extraction. We synthesized outcomes descriptively and developed an interpretive model. Results Eleven reviews were included. Knowledge, decisional conflict, and preparation generally improved; evidence for interpersonal processes was less extensive. Preconsultation aids increased reported decision discussion (68.6% versus 50.2%), whereas separate in-consultation trials, mostly of paper aids, improved observer ratings (mean difference 12.14; 95% confidence interval 8.12–16.16). The trial sets were not directly compared. The five proposed links were decision recognition, patient preparation, clinical visibility, deliberative interaction, and decision closure and follow-through; downstream safety evidence was sparse. Conclusion Digital preparation alone does not establish improved deliberation or safety. The model is interpretive and unvalidated. Comparative studies should test information flow and outcom…

title: Research on the Innovation of Financing Methods and Operation Mechanism of Low-Altitude Economy Enterprises
abstract: As an important carrier of new-type productivity, the low-altitude economy generally faces financing difficulties such as “high R&D investment, lagging profitability, and few collateral assets.” Traditional bank lending, which focuses on fixed asset collateral and stable cash flow as its core evaluation logic, is inherently mismatched with the asset structure of low-altitude enterprises, which is mainly composed of intangible assets such as patents and flight data. This paper takes the “first national low-altitude economy ABS” and the first national dual “cross-border” intellectual property securitization project as core cases to systematically analyze the operation mechanism of two innovative financing methods: financial leasing ABS and intellectual property securitization. The study found that financial leasing ABS, through the transmission chain of “leasing receivables packaging - asset pool construction - structured stratification-exchange listing,” transforms the future cash flow of low-altitude equipment leasing into tradable standardized securities. The first product issued by Science City Leasing reached a scale of 584 million yuan, with a priority A1 tranche interest rate of only 1.9%. MERIT: Mechanism-Driven Model Predicts Drug Outcomes and Nominates Indications for Failed Drugs
abstract: Abstract Drug development depends on efficacy and safety, but many trial-outcome prediction models incorporate trial design, prior development history, or compound identity, enabling compound memorization and inflating apparent performance. We developed MEchanism-Resolved Inference of Trial outcomes (MERIT), a model that predicts trial outcomes from molecular and disease features without using information on similar-compound success. MERIT integrates the disease and drug of interest with large-scale drug–protein, protein–metabolite, and immune interaction maps to link a drug’s intended and potential off-target effects to tissue-specific efficacy and safety. Across 753 small-molecule drugs and 3,133 trials, MERIT achieved an overall AUROC of 0.770 (0.765 for efficacy and 0.784 for safety) under structure-holdout evaluation, outperforming two published methods retrained on the same trials and folds. Scored by a mechanism-fit profiling, MERIT ranked the approved indication above the failed one for 83% (50 of 60) of a preselected set of 60 cohort compounds that failed one indication but are approved for another. Finally, we registered locked, outcome-blind predictions for 55 drug-indication pairs in ongoing phase III trials for prospective evaluation.

title: دعوى بطلان حكم التحكيم باعتباره آلية للرقابة القضائية: دراسة تحليلية في النظام السعودي
abstract: استهدف البحث دراسة الأحكام المنظمة للرقابة القضائية على أحكام التحكيم من خلال دعوى بطلان حكم التحكيم في نظام التحكيم السعودي، عبر بيان مفهوم الطبيعة القانونية لدعوى البطلان وخصائصها وإجراءاتها والآثار المترتبة على الحكم به. بالاعتماد على المنهج التحليلي في دراسة النصوص النظامية، وتم تقسيم البحث إلى مقدمة وأربعة مباحث، ونتائج. المبحث الأول: مفهوم الرقابة القضائية على حكم التحكيم. المبحث الثاني: دعوى بطلان حكم التحكيم: خصائصها وإجراءاتها. المبحث الثالث: أسباب الرقابة القضائية على حكم التحكيم من خلال دعوى البطلان. المبحث الرابع: آثار الرقابة القضائية على حكم التحكيم من خلال دعوى البطلان. وخلص البحث إلى أن الرقابة القضائية على أحكام التحكيم تقتصر على التحقق من سلامة الحكم النهائي في حدود الأسباب التي حددها النظام حصراً، بما يكفل عدم مخالفتها للنظام العام، كما أن دعوى البطلان تعد دعوى مستقلة ذات طبيعة خاصة وليست طريقا تقليديا من طرق الطعن، وأن الأحكام الجزئية أو التمهيدية الصادرة أثناء إجراءات التحكيم لا يجوز الطعن فيها استقلالاً، وإنما تثار أوجه الاعتراضات المتعلقة بها ضمن دعوى بطلان الحكم المنهي للخصومة.

title: The influence mechanism of AIGC-driven “learning-thinking-applying-creating” integrated animation instructional design on college students’ cognitive load and creative thinking
abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence has entered animation classrooms faster than research has been able to describe what it does to learning. This study developed a “Learning-Thinking-Applying-Creating” (LTAC) integrated teaching model built on an open-source AIGC toolchain and evaluated it in a twelve-week quasi-experiment with second-year animation students, two intact classes being allocated to an experimental or a control condition. Cognitive load was measured with a three-subscale instrument adapted from Paas and from Leppink and colleagues, and divergent thinking with an abbreviated Torrance-type battery scored for fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration by two trained raters who worked blind to group and occasion (intraclass correlations 0.86 to 0.91). Data were collected at pretest, mid-test, and posttest. Analysis of covariance indicated that the intervention lowered extraneous load and raised germane load while leaving intrinsic load unchanged. Repeated-measures analysis revealed selective gains: originality and elaboration improved more in the experimental group, whereas fluency and flexibility rose in both. Structural equation modelling was consistent with a differentiated mechanism, in which lower extraneous load predicted fluency and flexibility, germane load related to originality and elaboration indirectly through a deep-processing strategy, a…

title: Modulation mechanism of L-tryptophan and phosphate to the chicken extracellular calcium-sensing receptor via downstream G protein-coupled signaling cascades and their binding modes
abstract: Abstract Laying hens undergo dynamic bone turnover and have a high demand for calcium due to the daily egg-laying cycle. The chicken extracellular calcium-sensing receptor (cCaSR) plays an important role in calcium homeostasis. This study investigated the modulatory effects and mechanisms of L-tryptophan (L-Trp) and inorganic phosphate (PO₄³⁻) on cCaSR-mediated signaling. A stable Flp-In™-293 cell line expressing cCaSR was established and used in a completely randomized in vitro cell culture design. Individual cell culture wells served as the experimental unit, with at least three technical replicates per experiment and at least three independent experiments. cCaSR activation was evaluated using luciferase reporter assays and a cAMP assay to assess Gαq-, Gβγ/Gαi-, Gα12-, and Gαi-mediated signaling. Dose-response curves were fitted by nonlinear regression, and data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s or Tukey’s multiple-comparison test (P < 0.05). L-Trp enhanced Ca²⁺-mediated cCaSR activation, shifting the Ca²⁺ EC50 by 12.88%, 5.18%, and 1.02% in the Gαq, Gβγ/Gαi, and Gα12 pathways, respectively, whereas the Ca²⁺ IC50 for cAMP shifted by 10.15% in the Gαi pathway. The calcimimetic R568 was used to partially substitute for Ca²⁺ to minimize Ca²⁺-phosphate interactions. In the presence of Ca²⁺ and R568, 2 mM PO₄³⁻ inhibited cCaSR responses in the Gαq, Gβγ/Gαi, and Gα12…

Enhanced rock weathering for sustainable carbon capture: advances, challenges, and future prospects in terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) is a carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy that accelerates mineral dissolution in terrestrial systems to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), with the potential for co-benefits across managed and natural ecosystems. This review evaluates ERW’s real-world effectiveness through the lens of measurable carbon fluxes and storage permanence. We synthesize evidence across geochemical kinetics, hydrology, mineralogy, particle size distributions, and biological mediation, showing that the wide range of reported field-scale carbon removal rates (approximately 0 to 9 t CO 2 per ha −1 yr −1 ) reflects diverse site-specific environmental conditions and complex geochemical, biological, and hydrological processes that cannot be explained by intrinsic mineral reactivity alone. Widely used proxies, such as total cation dissolutions, soil pH changes, or crop yield gains, are less reliable indicators of field-scale CDR than alkalinity export or cation mass balance. Furthermore, estimates of net CDR should account for both the efficiency of converting weathering products into durable carbonate storage and full lifecycle emissions. Lifecycle assessments consistently identify energy for grinding and logistics as the dominant sources of cost and emissions, implying an optimal particle fineness for maximizing net removal. A tiered appraisal of modeling…

title: Chitosan-Derived Carbon Dot/Polypyrrole/Hybrid Biomembrane Assembly for Photoresponsive DNA Delivery
abstract: Abstract DNA condensation, extracellular shielding, and intracellular release impose competing requirements on nonviral polyplexes. Here, chitosan-derived cationic carbonized domains, an in situ polymerized polypyrrole phase, and a protein-bearing hybrid biomembrane shell were spatially organized into a hierarchical plasmid carrier. Carbonization and PPy hybridization retained most fluorescamine-accessible amines while introducing intrinsic fluorescence and NIR responsiveness. Membrane coverage progressively reversed the surface charge and reduced model-protein adsorption, with an intermediate membrane/carrier/DNA ratio providing the optimal balance between interfacial shielding and cellular interaction. The resulting HEV-coated assemblies maintained approximately 84% DNA encapsulation and exhibited pH- and NIR-regulated release. Optimized assemblies achieved 93.38% uptake and 56.66% GFP expression in HeLa cells, while excessive irradiation reduced expression through photothermal cytotoxicity. These findings establish a hierarchical structure−property framework for coupling biopolymer-derived DNA-binding domains, a conjugated polymer phase, and a biological macromolecular interface.

title: From Carbon Trading to Transition Finance: Institutional Alignment in Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia’s carbon exchange and sustainable-finance taxonomy evolved along distinct regulatory pathways in 2023–2026. This qualitative documentary study examines when carbon-unit records can corroborate transition-finance disclosures without being mistaken for evidence of taxonomy eligibility. It compares national carbon-pricing legislation, amended exchange rules, the Carbon Unit Registry regulation, and successive Indonesian sustainable-finance taxonomies. Passage-level coding distinguishes binding legal requirements, regulator guidance, institutional announcements, and proposed causal mechanisms. The findings identify separate evidentiary objects: issuance and disposition of carbon units, mitigation-use authorisation, technical screening of financed activities, entity and portfolio classification, and financial disclosure. The July 2026 registry rule differentiates registry functions and carbon-unit uses, while the March 2026 taxonomy update highlights version-specific screening and safeguards. Neither set of instruments establishes successful migration, improved market liquidity, lower verification costs, or financing additionality. The article advances a provisional bounded-alignment framework based on scope-specific traceability, dated classifications, claim reconciliation, and accountable correction. Its economic implications remain testable propositions rather than meas…

Research of robustness of the cluster-variation method for identification of radio emission sources to anomalous and missing measurements in multi-position systems
abstract: A study of the robustness of the cluster-variation method for identifying radio emission sources intended for use in multi-position triangulation systems under conditions of significant a priori uncertainty is carried out. The influence of anomalous measurements, data omissions, asynchrony of observations and unfavorable geometry of direction finders on the accuracy and reliability of coordinate measurement is considered. Quantitative indicators of robustness are introduced that characterize the probability of correct identification of a source, the root-mean-square estimation error and the maximum permissible levels of degradation of measurement information. Based on the results of numerical simulation, the dependences of accuracy on the proportion of gross errors and the number of available channels are obtained. It is shown that the cluster-variation approach ensures operability under conditions in which classical statistical methods become unstable.

abstract: ABSTRACT Developing soft and conformable materials with enhanced charge generation and retention capabilities remains a critical barrier for next‐generation flexible triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). Here, we report a polarization‐coupled tribo‐negative film fabricated by integrating a room‐temperature ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (FNLC) material (FNLC‐1571) into an electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) mat. In contrast to traditional rigid fillers, the optimally engineered ferroelectric nematic phase (N F ) of FNLC‐1571 microdomains assists spontaneous soft polar ordering in the nanofibrous PVDF matrix. This facilitates the integration of dipolar interactions with the fluorinated ends of PVDF, thereby synergistically promoting the crystallization of the electroactive β‐phase, enhancing dielectric behavior, modulating surface potential, improving interfacial charge‐trapping ability, and increasing contact area for superior charge generation while maintaining mechanical flexibility. When paired with a polyethylenimine (PEI)‐coated polyamide‐6 (PA‐6) tribo‐positive counter layer, the optimized 1 wt.% FNLC/PVDF‐based TENG delivers stable electrical output under low‐amplitude mechanical periodic contact‐separation excitation (8N, 10 Hz), with a peak‐to‐peak open‐circuit voltage of ∼395 V, a short‐circuit current of ∼40 µA, and a transferred charge of ∼167 nC. title: Nonlinear Ozone-Phytoplankton-Sea-Ice Coupling Regulates Fine-Scale Gaseous Elemental Mercury Enhancement in the Arctic Marginal Ice Zone
abstract: Abstract Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. Multiscale spatial statistics, machine learning, and quantile regression were applied to MOSAiC in situ observations (June-September 2020). GEM exhibits strong fine-scale spatial autocorrelation at 10 km (Moran’s I = 0.876). Random forest model (R2 = 0.85) with SHAP attribution identified ozone (O3), chlorophyll a (Chla), and open water fraction (OWF) as dominant GEM predictors. Quantile regression revealed that nonlinear coupling among OWF, Chla, and O3 strengthens under high GEM concentrations. By further combining spatial analysis with quantile regression modeling, a GEM-sensitive region was identified (OWF = 0.156–0.404, Chla = 1.17–1.57 μg/L, O3 = 9.2–19.7 ppb); within this region, both the O3 × Chla and O3 × OWF interactions exhibited significant positive correlations. The positive effect of O3 × Chla persists across all regions, while the O3 × OWF coupling varies dynamically with the retreat of sea ice. O3 indirectly favors GEM accumulation via regulating phytoplankton, and sea-ice melt exerts stage-dependent modulation of atmospheric oxidizing capacity. This study identifies O3 as a critical MIZ mercury regulator, and embedding O3-mediated pathways in models improves GEM projections under Arct…

title: RADIAL ONE-DIMENSIONAL HEAT AND MOISTURE COUPLING MODEL FOR THE PREHEATING STAGE OF HOT-AIR DRYING OF CYLINDRICAL MEDICINAL MATERIALS
abstract: This paper focuses on the preheating equilibrium stage in the hot-air drying process of cylindrical medicinal materials. A radial one-dimensional unsteady heat and moisture coupling model is established under the assumptions of axisymmetric and isotropic material. Heat transfer inside the material follows Fourier’s law, moisture migration follows Fick’s law, and the surface exchanges heat and moisture with the drying environment through convective transfer, which is described by third-kind boundary conditions. The measured drying-room temperature and moisture content are processed by piecewise linear interpolation and adopted as time-varying boundary conditions, and the governing equations are solved by an explicit finite difference scheme. During 0–1800 s, the material is heated as a whole while pre-drying occurs mainly in a thin surface layer. At 1800 s, the surface and center temperatures reach 36.79°C and 33.58°C, respectively. The surface moisture content decreases from 2.55 to 1.45 kg/kg on a dry basis, whereas the center moisture content remains close to its initial value. Convergence tests and parameter sensitivity analysis show that the surface temperature is most sensitive to the convective heat transfer coefficient, while the surface moisture content is most sensitive to the convective mass transfer coefficient and the diffusion pre-exponential factor.

title: Meteorological Drivers of Outdoor VOC Exposure at a Repurposed Brownfield Site: Coupling Subsurface Emissions with Atmospheric Dispersion
abstract: Abstract Redevelopment of brownfield sites into open public spaces can expose people to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted from subsurface contamination. Conventional risk assessments rely on low-frequency sampling and static average concentrations, which systematically miss the transient peak-exposure episodes that define the reasonable maximum exposure. To address this gap, we developed a daily resolution, meteorologically driven modeling framework to assess outdoor VOC exposure at a repurposed industrial brownfield site in northern China over a full annual cycle. Simulated VOC concentrations varied by approximately one to two orders of magnitude and were validated against bimonthly field measurements. Results showed that subsurface VOC emission fluxes are governed jointly by soil temperature and soil moisture; once the volatilized vapors reach the ground surface, their atmospheric dispersion and dilution are further controlled by local wind speed. Using the daily resolution record, we then identified distinct meteorological precursor patterns that reliably precede extreme exposure events, and captured them with a logistic regression model built on four forecast-available predictors: air temperature, cumulative rainfall, wind speed, and the 2-day change in wind speed. Preferentially sampling these meteorologically identified episodes can provide representative data for…
