title: Ad libitum eating and reduced exercise resolve impaired bone integrity after prolonged reductions in energy availability in mature female rodents
abstract: Reduced energy availability (EA) results in loss of bone mass and disruption of endocrine regulators of bone integrity, even in very active individuals. Our aim was to determine whether 12 weeks of less exercise and ad libitum eating would enable recovery of deficits incurred during 12 weeks of reduced EA, hypothesizing recovery would be improved in exercising rats. Female rats (n=64, 5 months old) were randomized to sedentary (SED) or exercise (EX) conditions and, within each group, to adlib-fed (ADLIB) or severe energy restriction (SEV-ER). Energy intake was restricted in all SEV-ER rats and exercise volume in SEV-ER EX rats calculated to produce equivalent 30% reductions in EA. After 12 weeks, SEV-ER EX rats exhibited no losses in lean/fat mass and total bone mass (DXA), metaphyseal %BV/TV, and distal femur and femoral neck vBMD (by pQCT), and higher values for osteoblast activity than observed in SEV-ER SED animals. EX did not protect against declines in serum leptin and IGF-I. Half of each group recovered for 12 weeks, eating ADLIB and (in EX rats) reducing running volume by 50%. After 4 weeks recovery, body weight and energy availability for all SEV-ER rats matched those of ADLIB rats. By 12 weeks, there were no significant differences among groups for all variables. These results demonstrate that bone mass/microarchitecture and osteoblast activity observed in SED animals…

title: Differentiated Interfacial Proton Delivery for Durable CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton‐coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high‐rate CO 2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic‐and‐gap‐confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)‐modified Bi (Bi‐PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near‐surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen‐bond environment, while slow‐growth proton‐transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton‐delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to * OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential‐dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate‐related pathway response. Bi‐PDMS‐30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm − 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface‐deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO 2 ‐to‐formate electrosynthesis.

title: Effects of Shading Strategy on daylight illuminance and energy consumption for southern facades of Office Buildings
abstract: This study investigates the effects of exterior shading strategies on annual average daylight illuminance and electricity consumption for the southern façade of a two-story office building in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Using eQUEST, four cases were simulated: a baseline without shading, horizontal overhangs only, vertical fins only, and a combination of overhangs and fins. The results show that all shading configurations reduce electricity consumption compared with the baseline, while horizontal overhangs perform more effectively than vertical fins. The combined strategy achieves the lowest annual electricity consumption and the largest reduction in daylight illuminance. However, excessive shading also reduces the hours during which daylight illuminance remains above the setpoint, increasing electric lighting demand and limiting additional energy savings. The findings indicate that shading design should balance solar heat-gain reduction and daylight availability, with parameters adjusted according to climate, orientation, material, and building conditions.

title: Coordinated Economic Growth and Decarburization in Jiangsu Using an Integrated MOO–CCD Framework
abstract: Economic growth, carbon reduction, and environmental stewardship may all be achieved at once via the use of an optimization technique that takes trade-offs and multiple target progressions into account. Without fully grasping the complex interplay of financial, climatic, environmental, and resource implications, many current regional MOO studies aim for compromise solutions. The creation of a MOO and CCD framework in the Jiangsu Province, China, is the main subject of this study. From 2018 to 2030, we can see potential pathways for energy transition and company reorganization by analyzing eleven indicators: GDP, employment, water consumption, CO2, sulfur dioxide, NOx, PM, CO2, chemical oxygen demand, ammonia nitrogen and solid waste rounding it off. The study's basis is an input-output model with 47 components. Numerous factors are considered, including electricity-related situations, resource and emission coefficients from the past, and more. As a starting point for coordination, CCD ranks and evaluates potential MOO solutions once the optimal-point method has standardized the reduction and maximization objectives. All three scenarios put yearly GDP growth at 6.8%, with the precise number falling anywhere from 6.7% to 7.0%. We need to be more transparent about the moral judgments and assumptions that drive these changes because of the potential impact they have on the environm…

title: Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm −2 . The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.

title: Non‐Planar Chlorine‐Coordinated Activation of Triatomic Ruthenium Sites for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru‐based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen‐containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement‐pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine‐doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru 3 ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru 3 ON 6 Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru 3 ClNC delivers a high alkaline half‐wave potential ( E 1/2 ) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc‐air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru 3 ON 6 Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non‐planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d ‐band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate‐determining step of Ru 3 NC and OH * desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept…

Engineering Intraframework Energy Transfer in Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Luminescent Discrimination of Bisphenol Pollutants
abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent sensing relies on the generation, migration, and dissipation of excited‐state energy modulated by analytes. However, the contribution of intraframework energy transfer processes to sensing performance remains insufficiently studied. Owing to the highly tunable structures and designable energy transfer pathways, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide an ideal platform for dissecting detailed processes. Herein, a series of isostructural lanthanide MOFs were constructed from 2,5‐furandicarboxylic / 3,5‐pyridinedicarboxylic acid, enabling independent regulation of metal‐to‐metal and linker‐to‐linker energy transfer. Direct comparison of chemically integrated frameworks and their physical mixtures using bisphenol pollutants as probes reveals that metal‐to‐metal energy transfer dominates sensing performance, while linker‐to‐linker energy transfer contributes marginally. Mechanistic analyses indicate the impacts originate from the different energetic characteristics. Rigid lanthanide energy levels in Eu‐Tb systems create an “energy reservoir” that strongly regulate luminescence responses, whereas highly environment‐sensitive linker states in mixed‐linker systems give rise to self‐compensating energy transfer, resulting in a diminished influence. title: Entropy Generation Analysis of Unsteady Magnetohydrodynamic Buoyancy‐Driven Nanofluid Flow in a Porous Vertical Channel With Thermal Radiation and Chemical Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates entropy generation in an unsteady magneto‐hydrodynamic nanofluid flow with the influence of buoyancy forces embedded in a vertical porous channel. The simulation is carried out to assess the impact of thermal radiation and chemical reaction; the transport domain is bounded by a left‐cooled plate and a right‐heated plate. The schematic transport field reflects operating conditions commonly encountered in practical thermal and energy systems. The governing equations describing momentum, energy transfer, and nanoparticle concentration are nondimensionalized and solved numerically using a finite‐difference approach (FDA) to ensure stability across the computational domain. The study focuses on assessing the influence of physical parameters on the transport field and the features of the thermodynamic system. The involved parameters are velocity slip at the walls, magnetic field strength, porous medium permeability, thermal and solutal buoyancy parameters, radiation intensity, chemical reaction, Schmidt number, Brownian motion, thermophoretic, Biot number, and effects of viscous dissipation. Detailed analysis is carried out to assess the effects of varying these multi‐physical parameters on nanofluid velocity profiles, energy profiles, concentration profiles, entropy generation, as well as the Bejan number. title: Land Surface Temperature-Aware Optimization of Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Systems for Enhanced Energy Yield: A Comparative Assessment of Metaheuristic Algorithms in Adamawa State, Nigeria
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) energy-yield estimation in thermally variable environments requires consideration of spatial differences in environmental conditions beyond conventional solar-resource assessment. This study developed and comparatively evaluated a land surface temperature (LST)-aware optimization framework for grid-connected PV systems across seven locations in Adamawa State, Nigeria: Yola North, Yola South, Mubi North, Mubi South, Gombi, Numan, and Michika. Global horizontal irradiance, ambient temperature, wind speed, and satellite-derived LST were integrated within a temperature-coupled PV performance model in which LST was treated as a thermal indicator rather than being directly equated with module temperature. PV tilt angle, azimuth orientation, and installed capacity were optimized using Parametric Sweep, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Performance was evaluated using specific energy yield, improvement relative to baseline configurations, convergence behaviour, and solution stability. The optimized configurations exhibited tilt angles of 12–16°, azimuth angles of 165–180°, and installed capacities of 100–108 kWp, demonstrating spatial variation in the preferred PV configuration. title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in the Assessment of Low Energy Availability and Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) in Athletes Without Diabetes: A Critical Narrative Review
abstract: Background: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been proposed to support assessment of low energy availability (LEA) and Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), but its diagnostic value is uncertain. Aim: To critically evaluate CGM evidence relevant to LEA and REDs in athletes without diabetes. Material and methods: Two PubMed searches on 1 October 2026 yielded 145 unique records. AI-assisted assessment informed a purposive narrative synthesis of experimental, clinical, observational and measurement-agreement studies, supplemented by previously identified sources. Results: Severe short-term energy restriction reduced sensor glucose in one experiment, whereas studies of controlled LEA, nutritional intervention and clinically diagnosed REDs did not consistently identify differences in aggregate glucose metrics. Dietary composition, training, recovery and measurement conditions complicated interpretation. No reviewed study established a validated CGM threshold for identifying or excluding REDs. Conclusions: CGM remains an investigational adjunct. Low readings do not confirm LEA or REDs, and an unremarkable profile does not exclude them. Prospective validation must establish whether CGM adds information beyond nutritional and clinical assessment.

title: Living with family discord: a qualitative exploration of anxiety experiences
abstract: Purpose: to explore anxiety experiences among individuals experiencing family disharmony, focusing on emotional manifestations, family-related triggers, impacts on everyday life, and coping strategies. Method: this study used a descriptive qualitative approach with three participants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and non-participant observation, then analyzed using thematic analysis to identify patterns and themes related to participants' anxiety experiences. Findings: revealed that anxiety associated with family disharmony manifested as fear, persistent worry, restlessness, and emotional insecurity. These experiences affected participants' academic concentration, emotional well-being, sleep, and social interactions. Participants used various coping strategies, including emotional expression, personal activities, conflict avoidance, and seeking social support. Implications: the findings highlight the importance of emotional support, healthy family communication, and appropriate coping strategies in addressing anxiety associated with family disharmony. They may also inform the development of more sensitive psychological counselling and support services for individuals experiencing family-related distress. Originality: in-depth exploration of the diverse ways individuals experience and respond to family disharmony, hig…

title: Fully Roll‐to‐Roll Coated Large‐Area Perovskite Solar Modules on Indium‐Free Microgroove Substrates
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low‐cost, low‐carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll‐to‐roll coated, large‐area back‐contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm 2 achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm 2 . The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll‐to‐roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS‐compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x‐ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real‐world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.

Design and Preliminary Performance Evaluation of a SIMON–LWE Hybrid Encryption Scheme for Cloud-Based IoT
abstract: Cloud-based Internet of Things (IoT) networks have transformed data collection, processing and communication across a wide variety of industries, including healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, smart cities, transportation, and environmental monitoring. But, most of the resource constrained IoT devices have limited battery power, memory, storage and processing power, which make it hard to implement conventional cryptographic algorithms such as Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), Rivest–Shaumir–Adleman (RSA), and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) in them. Moreover, standard cryptographic systems are vulnerable to quantum computing attacks. In this work, we propose a resource-efficient encryption framework called SIMON-LBA, combining the SIMON block cipher with a key-generation scheme based on LWE lattice cryptography to achieve quantum resistance and compromise minimal resources. Numerical experimentation with the model was carried out in a simulated cloud-IoT environment using Python in a quantitative experimental approach. Over 100 iterations, the representative sensor data was assessed, such as PM2.5, temperature, and humidity data. Encryption and decryption times, throughput, energy usage, CPU usage and memory usage were measured and compared with a 100 iterations for each of the following algorithms: AES, RSA, ECC, DES, ChaCha20, SIMON, SPECK, Attribute-Based Signcryption…

title: Design and Atmospheric Application of a Large-Volume UV-Irradiated FEP Chamber for Mercury Redox Chemistry Studies
abstract: Abstract Understanding the atmospheric redox chemistry of mercury (Hg) is critical for accurately predicting its global transport, deposition, and environmental impacts. However, large uncertainties remain with respect to reaction mechanisms and oxidation rates that convert elemental mercury (Hg0) to its oxidized forms (HgI, HgII). In this study, we present the design, construction, and characterization of a 40 m3 UV-irradiated fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) environmental chamber developed to investigate Hg oxidation under controlled, atmospherically relevant conditions. The chamber is equipped with a suite of analytical instruments, including a dual-channel Hg analysis system with SI-traceable calibration, a heated Reactive Mercury Active System (RMAS), broadband cavity-enhanced absorption spectroscopy (BBCEAS) instruments, and additional gas analyzers for monitoring oxidants and trace gases. Characterization experiments were conducted to quantify residence time, mixing, and wall loss rates for key atmospheric constituents. The system provides a flexible platform for studying Hg oxidation mechanisms involving compounds such as hydroxyl radical (OH), ozone (O3), and bromine radicals (Br). Vigorous characterization of the atmospheric simulation chamber will allow determination of uncertainties in atmospheric Hg chemistry and improve global chemical transport models.

Reconstructing literary space using artificial intelligence-enhanced architectural representation methods: Georges Perec and the Plassaert Apartment
abstract: Positioned at the intersection of literature and architecture, this study explores how abstract spaces constructed in literary texts can be reconstructed using architectural representation tools and artificial intelligence technologies. The focus of the research is the Plassaert apartment in Georges Perec’s Life: A User’s Manual, which details the space through everyday objects and lists, and the users of this space across different periods. The object-human relationships, hoarding tendencies, and the psychological weight of the space described in the text have been transformed into architectural representations through artificial intelligence (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot). The study’s methodology is based on a spatial accumulation model constructed around the parameters of Actor, Space, and Time. The 5-Level Prompt Model has transformed these literary data into a visual language, producing the spatial counterpart of each actor in their own time. Within the scope of the findings, the layering created by the material concerns, psychological and social states of space users through objects has been concretised through spatial indicators. The narrative structure in Perec’s literature (chess and jigsaw puzzle metaphors) has been represented through conceptual collages. Chromosome-level reference genome assemblies and annotation of four diploid Aegilops
abstract: Abstract Background Aegilops species represent an important reservoir of genetic diversity for agronomic and end-use quality traits as well as resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses for wheat improvement. However, the limited availability of high-quality reference genomes has impeded the effective use of these wild relatives in breeding programs. Results Here, we present chromosome-level reference genome assemblies of four diploid Aegilops species: Ae. comosa , Ae. markgrafii , Ae. umbellulata and Ae. uniaristata . Using a hybrid strategy combining Pacific Bioscience (PacBio) HiFi sequencing, BioNano optical mapping and Hi-C scaffolding, we generated contiguous assemblies ranging from 3.58 to 4.48 Gb characterized by BUSCO completeness score ranging from 97.9 to 98.4%. RNASeq and IsoSeq data from multiple tissues were integrated to facilitate gene annotation. The annotation yielded a total of 47,246 to 51,203 protein-coding genes across the four species, while also characterizing the repeat element composition of these diploid Aegilops . Collinearity analyses identified conserved colinear blocks and revealed multiple intra- and inter-chromosomal rearrangements. Orthogroups shared among the Aegilops and Triticum species were used to perform a phylogenetic analysis that clarified evolutionary relationships among the genomes of this Aegilops/Triticum complex, where the diploid …

title: IDENTIFICATION OF PLANT-SPECIFIC YABBY TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR GENE FAMILY IN FALSE FLAX (CAMELINA SATIVA L.) AND IN SILICO EXPRESSION PROFILING
abstract: Camelina sativa is a hexaploid oilseed crop with remarkable agronomic resilience and industrial value; however, the YABBY transcription factor gene family remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive genome-wide identification and in silico characterization of the YABBY gene family in C. sativa, providing insights into its evolutionary relationships, structural organization, and potential regulatory functions. Seventeen YABBY genes (CsYABBYs) were identified through conserved-domain-based screening and systematically characterized for physicochemical features, evolutionary relationships, exon–intron architecture, conserved motifs, chromosomal locations, cis-regulatory elements, and evolutionary selection pressure. Comparative phylogenetic analysis with Arabidopsis thaliana and Theobroma cacao separated the CsYABBY proteins into five clusters (FIL/YAB3, YAB2, YAB5, CRC, and INO), indicating strong evolutionary conservation and functional similarity in each subfamily. Gene structure analysis showed that exon–intron organization was highly conserved in every clade. In contrast, MEME-based motif analysis identified ten conserved motifs, including the characteristic C2C2 zinc-finger and YABBY domains. Promoter analysis uncovered abundant cis-regulatory elements associated with various regulatory functions, suggesting extensive involvement of CsYA…

Advances and Paradigms in Modern Plant Bioinformatics: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Plant bioinformatics has undergone a paradigm shift from simple gene discovery and sequence alignment to AI-driven multi-omics integration, graph pangenomics, and precision molecular breeding. The intrinsic hyper-complexity of plant genomes—characterized by high polyploidy, extensive heterozygosity, massive repetitive element burdens, and dynamic structural variations—has mandated the invention of specialized assembly algorithms, statistically robust annotation pipelines, and high-dimensional deep learning architectures. This comprehensive review synthesizes core computational methodologies across de novo polyploid sequence assembly (Overlap-Layout-Consensus vs. De Bruijn Graphs), structural and evidence-based functional annotation, epigenomic landscape mapping (WGBS, ATAC-Seq), graph-based pangenomics, single-cell multi-omics resolution, and transcriptomic network modeling. Furthermore, we evaluate state-of-the-art transformer-based Genomic Language Models (GLMs), structural biology integrations (AlphaFold3/ESMFold), and specialized plant databases. Finally, key computational bottlenecks, infrastructure scaling considerations, and actionable computational frameworks for accelerating climate-resilient crop breeding are critically evaluated.

Do floral traits associated with pollination concurrently increase vulnerability to seed predators?
abstract: Abstract Floral traits associated with floral display that likely enhance pollinator attraction may inadvertently increase attractiveness to antagonists such as pre-dispersal seed predators, yet direct tests of this trade-off within closely related species remain scarce. We investigated this relationship in three threatened grass aloes - Aloe albida , A. craibii , and A. chortolirioides - that differ markedly in floral colour, display, morphology, and flowering ecology. We quantified fruit and seed damage, identified predator and parasitoid assemblages, and tested whether independently measured floral and plant traits predicted fruit and/or seed utilisation within each species. Substantial reproductive loss occurred in all three species, with fruit utilisation ranging from 45 to 79% and seed utilisation from 20 to 55%. The chalcid wasp Eurytoma aloineae was the most abundant seed predator across species. Species-level predation was lowest in the smaller, white-flowered A. albida and higher in the more conspicuous A. craibii and A. chortolirioides ; however, within-species model selection provided little support for a general effect of floral display size on predation. In A. craibii , seed utilisation increased with perianth tube depth, whereas the corresponding relationship with fruit utilisation was marginal. These results indicate species-specific associations between floral …

title: Ultra‐High Ionic Conductivity Sulfide‐Based Composite Membranes Paired With Stable Interfacial Layer Enables High‐Energy‐Density All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsic properties of sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SEs) are crucial for achieving all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with high safety and high energy density, yet it is challenging to fabricate high‐performance sulfide SE films in a scalable approach. Furthermore, the inevitable side reactions between sulfide SE and lithium metal anodes exacerbate interfacial incompatibility, causing degradation in the cyclic stability. Here, a high‐performance sulfide SE (Li 5.4 PS 4.4 Cl 0.8 Br 0.8 ) was selected as the base phase to compensate for the loss of electrochemical performance during the dry film‐forming process. It was then combined with Polytetrafluoroethylene binder to prepare a high‐ionic‐conductivity composite membrane (HICCM). To mitigate side reactions between HICCM and the anode, a LiF‐rich interfacial layer forms in situ on the lithium metal surface, and the assembled symmetric cell achieves a high critical current density of 1.3 mA cm −2 and stable cycling for 2000 h (0.2 mA cm −2 ). For electrochemical performance, HICCM exhibits fast ion transport kinetics and electrical insulation, allowing the ASSB configured as FeS 2 //HICCM//LiF‐Li to achieve an energy density of 416.5 Wh kg −1 at a high loading of 3.4 mAh cm −2 . This work demonstrates that by combining HICCM with a stable interface design, ASSBs can achieve longevity and high cell‐level energy densi…

title: Rational Terminal‐Group Engineering of Guest Acceptors for 20.7% Efficient Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy‐level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active‐layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S‐SMA and AS‐SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8‐BO with a weaker electron‐withdrawing 2‐(3‐ethyl‐4‐oxothiazolidin‐2‐ylidene)malononitrile (CN‐Rh) unit. This terminal‐group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8‐BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid‐to‐solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S‐SMA, asymmetric AS‐SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap‐assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8‐BO:AS‐SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. Integrated model of financial literacy, digital trading platforms, and behavioural biases (FL–DT–BB): A comprehensive review of retail investors’ investment decisions
abstract: The rapid digitalisation of financial markets has increased retail investor participation, particularly in emerging economies such as India. However, existing literature largely examines financial literacy, digital trading platforms, and behavioural biases independently, limiting an integrated understanding of their combined influence on retail investors’ investment decision-making. This study examines the investment behaviour of retail investors by synthesising prior research on financial literacy, digital trading platforms, and behavioural biases. Specifically, the study investigates how financial literacy and digital trading platform characteristics interact through behavioural biases to influence retail investors’ investment decision-making and develops an integrated Financial Literacy–Digital Trading Platforms–Behavioural Biases (FL–DT–BB) conceptual framework. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review methodology guided by the PRISMA framework. Academic literature was collected from Scopus, Web of Science, JSTOR, ProQuest, SSRN, ResearchGate, and Google Scholar. A total of 122 records were identified, of which 71 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis after screening. title: Structural Evolution of State-Dependent Kinetics during Potassium Storage in Layered CrSe2
abstract: Abstract Layered CrSe2 reversibly accommodates approximately one potassium (K) per formula unit, but the structural origin of its rate-dependent capacity remains unresolved. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) reveals the sequential P-3m1-R3m-C2/m phase pathway during cycling at different current rates. The P-3m1/R3m transformation exhibits the lattice discontinuity and becomes incomplete when increasing the current rate, as directly observed by operando SXRD. Chemical K deintercalation and state-resolved impedance measurements provide complementary evidence for sluggish kinetics near the fully deintercalated regime. Restricting the upper cutoff voltage will sacrifice some capacity but will improve electrochemical cycling capacity retention. These findings identify a particularly rate-sensitive structural region and show how phase-resolved characterization can guide voltage-window selection for layered potassium-storage electrodes.

title: Element-Selective Surface Reconstruction of Stainless Steel Anodes Governed by the Electrolyte Environment: Insights from High-Throughput Experiments
abstract: Abstract In neutral and mildly alkaline water electrolysis, electrolytes are primarily viewed as media controlling macroscopic solution properties such as pH and ionic conductivity. Beyond this conventional role, electrolyte species can interact with metal ions and dynamically reconstruct electrode surfaces through dissolution and reformation. Although such reconstruction is widely recognized, the extent to which operating surfaces retain the initial oxidation history or are governed by the electrolyte environment remains unclear. Here, a high-throughput electrochemical platform evaluated cell voltages under 108 conditions using 304 stainless steel anodes, independently varying anodic pretreatment, electrolyte pH (9.5, 10.5, and 11.5), phosphate concentration (1 and 3 M), and electrolysis regime. Analysis of variance showed that pH accounted for 70–81% of cell-voltage variation, whereas anodic pretreatment accounted for only 6–7%, demonstrating the dominant influence of the electrolyte environment on the electrochemical response. Surface analyses revealed widespread nickel depletion and heterogeneous chromium-rich films under lower-pH, high-phosphate conditions. Iron behavior was consistent with the equilibrium solubility trend, whereas nickel depletion did not follow the equilibrium solubility trend, indicating the involvement of processes beyond equilibrium thermodynamics. title: Elastic‐Invisibility‐Enabled Metastructure With Mechanically Programmed Nonlinear Resonators for Vibration Attenuation and Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical programming provides a simple way to tune embedded nonlinear resonators without redesigning the host structure. Here, seven magneto‐elastic piezoelectric resonators are integrated into elastically reconstructed openings of a host beam. The removed stiffness, mass, and inertia are restored. The dynamics of the intact beam are therefore recovered over the investigated frequency range. Programming is performed by changing only the spacing between repulsive magnets. Each resonator can be set independently. This creates uniform, nonuniform, and graded combinations of monostable and bistable states. Experiments and simulations show marked changes in both vibration attenuation and harvested power. Different programs favor different functions. One configuration reaches 1.82 times the reference attenuation bandwidth. Another reaches 1.57 times the reference harvesting performance. Assuming nine admissible states per resonator, the seven‐resonator system spans possible configurations. Model‐selected candidates improve both numerical references simultaneously, reaching 1.16 times the attenuation bandwidth and 1.11 times the harvesting metric. The prototype also delivers up to 10.67 of total AC load power near resonance. The result is a structurally integrated platform with programmable nonlinear functionality and largely preserved host dynamics.

title: Natural Beeswax-Seed Oil Coatings for Shell Eggs: Effects on Physicochemical, Functional, and Microbiological Quality during Chilled Storage
abstract: Abstract Shell eggs lose quality rapidly during storage because the porous shell allows moisture and carbon dioxide to escape, allowing air and bacteria to enter. Beeswax is an effective natural barrier against moisture transfer; however, it possesses limited intrinsic antimicrobial activity. In this study, the effectiveness of beeswax-based coatings enriched with cold-pressed sesame oil or black cumin oil at concentrations of 3% and 5% (w/w) was evaluated for preserving the quality and microbial stability of grade A table eggs during 5 weeks of refrigerated storage at 4 °C. Uncoated, water-washed, and pure beeswax-coated eggs were included as control treatments. Quality attributes were assessed at weekly intervals and included weight loss, air-cell height, Haugh unit, yolk index, shape index, component weights, CIE color parameters, albumen and yolk pH, soluble solids content, foaming capacity, and emulsion stability. Microbiological quality was evaluated by enumerating total aerobic mesophilic bacteria, coliforms, and molds and yeasts. Coating treatment significantly affected weight loss, air-cell height, yolk index, albumen and yolk pH, albumen and yolk color, foaming capacity, emulsion stability, and all microbial counts (P < 0.05), whereas Haugh unit, shape index, shell thickness, and yolk weight were not significantly affected. Performance and Security Challenges in Cloud-Based Data Storage Systems: A Secondary Empirical Analysis of Object-Storage Latency, Throughput, Availability, and Cyber Risk
abstract: Cloud-based data storage offers elastic capacity, geographic redundancy, and pay-per-use access, but organizations must balance performance variability with security exposure. This study synthesizes secondary evidence from three performance studies, official reliability documentation from Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, and authoritative threat reports from NIST, the Cloud Security Alliance, Verizon, and ENISA. The analysis examines request latency, throughput, concurrency, durability, availability, misconfiguration, identity and access management, vulnerability exploitation, ransomware, and data exfiltration. In a one-million-request experiment using 1 KiB objects, S3 Standard recorded median read and write latencies of 27 ms and 40 ms, compared with 5 ms and 8 ms for S3 Express, representing reductions of 81.5% and 80.0%. An eight-week object-storage study reported per-object bandwidth of approximately 25–95 MiB/s and aggregate throughput of 75–90 Gbit/s under high concurrency. Security evidence identifies misconfiguration, weak access control, vulnerability exploitation, and ransomware as major risks. The study proposes a performance-security co-optimization framework combining workload-aware storage selection, bounded asynchronous I/O, least-privilege access, encryption, immutable recovery copies, continuous configuration assessment, and centralized …

abstract: The research work describes a unified battery management technique that involves a digital twin-based method that encompasses practically validated theory, data-oriented state evaluation, embedded management, and Internet of Things supervision. The task employs two connected phases of experimentation. The first phase consists in the analysis of a six-cell lithium-ion battery pack 3S2P 18650 in twelve operation modes, which consists of using both 0.5C, 1C, and 2C discharges under ambient temperatures of 25°C, 35°C, and 45°C with dynamic loading. The data obtained in the analysis of the voltage, current, temperature, capacity, and energy indicators will serve as calibration data for a second-order Thevenin equivalency circuit digital twin in MATLAB. Phase II benchmarks Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM models on 9,742 records from the NASA lithium-ion battery dataset and integrates the selected Random Forest model with an ESP32-based BMS prototype. The embedded platform combines dual INA219 current sensors, a 2-channel relay module, local LCD monitoring, MQTT communication, a Flask-SocketIO dashboard, and a staged voltage-protection strategy. The digital twin reproduces the measured voltage response with RMSE below 0.08 V and R² above 0.98 across the reported constant-current validation cases. Coordination Geometry Reconstruction Mitigates α‑Dihedral Angle Restriction of Polyanionic‐Type Cathodes for Ultrafast Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries have attracted extensive attention for large‑scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of sodium resources. However, the near‑coplanar structure geometry of polyanionic‐type cathodes causes in‑plane stress and electrostatic barriers, which lead to blocked Na + transport kinetics and hinder their practical application. Herein, an α‑plane, defined by the transition metal and its coordinating dangling anions, is identified as the critical structural bottleneck for Na + diffusion. By screening and tuning the dangling anions, a coordination geometry reconstruction is achieved that twists the α‑plane into α1‐ and α2‐planes. This twisting behavior breaks α‑plane restriction and relieves the in‑plane stress, thereby lowering the Na + migration barrier. Concurrently, the geometry reconstruction enlarges the Na2‑centered polyhedral volume and increases the Na2 site occupancy from 0.56 to 0.62. Thus, the modified cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 130 mAh g −1 and outstanding rate capability, with 80% retention at 30 C and 83 mAh g −1 at 50 C. It also exhibits excellent wide‐temperature operability (−40°C to 55°C) and stable full‑cell performance. The universality of this strategy is validated on several polyanionic cathodes. This work reveals the α‑plane as a tunable structural parameter, offering a geometry‑electronic synergy para…

title: In Situ Plasma Upcycling of Spent-Battery Graphite into Active WO3/Graphene Oxide Heterointerfaces for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution: Experimental and DFT Insights
abstract: Abstract Converting waste materials into high-value electrocatalysts through advanced synthesis technologies represents a sustainable strategy for resource recycling and clean hydrogen production. Herein, a one-step plasma-assisted electrochemical strategy, followed by ultrasonic dispersion, was developed to synthesize WO3-decorated graphene oxide heterostructures directly from spent battery graphite and tungsten rods. Among the investigated compositions, the optimized catalyst synthesized using one graphite cathode rod and three tungsten cathode rods exhibited excellent hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) performance in 0.5 M H2SO4, requiring an overpotential of 156 mV to achieve 10 mA cm–2 with a Tafel slope of 65 mV dec–1. The superior activity is attributed to strong electronic coupling at the WO3@GO heterointerface, which promotes accessible oxide–carbon interfaces and facilitates interfacial charge transfer. Density functional theory calculations further revealed interfacial charge redistribution, W 5d–O 2p–C 2p orbital hybridization, and increased electronic states near the Fermi level. The catalyst also achieved a Faradaic efficiency of 95% and sustained HER operation for 48 h with only a slight increase in overpotential and minor morphological changes after stability testing. title: Interplay of Janus Polarization and Interfacial Electric Fields Governing Carrier Dynamics in MoS2/MoSSe Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract It is crucial to understand the role of polarization and the built-in electric field in heterostructures of two-dimensional materials, as these factors significantly affect carrier dynamics, interfacial properties, and device performance. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the electronic structure and excited-state carrier dynamics of MoS2/MoSSe heterostructures. We show that the interplay between the intrinsic polarization of Janus MoSSe and the interface-induced electric field strongly modulates interlayer charge transfer. This dual-field coupling drives a transition between type-I and type-II band alignments and switches the dominant carrier relaxation pathways from intralayer recombination to interlayer charge separation. Carrier relaxation is further governed by the interplay between nonadiabatic coupling and phonon-assisted transitions. These results identify polarity reversal as an effective strategy for tuning charge-transfer pathways and excited-state dynamics in van der Waals heterostructures, and provide guidance for designing two-dimensional optoelectronic and photocatalytic materials.

title: Review and analysis of tools for designing autonomous ground vehicle control systems
abstract: For the successful development of self-driving vehicles, as well as advanced driver-assistance systems, specialized programs are required. The purpose of this article is to provide an overview of the main tools for programming and virtual testing of autonomous driving systems for agricultural and road vehicles. Such tools as Autoware Foundation, Baidu Apollo, Siemens Simcenter Prescan, CARLA, MathWorks, Epic Games Unreal Engine, DSpace AURELION, Unity, Foretellix Foretify platform, IPG CarMaker, Cognata, Vector DYNA4, Nvidia Drive Sim, Vires Virtual Test Drive, VehicleSim, LG SVL Simulator are considered. The features and capabilities of each program are described, and a comparison is made according to the following parameters: distribution scheme – contractual or free, full and partial cycle programs, programming and visualization. The available operating systems for each program are listed. Among domestic companies, Sberbank (SberAutoTech) and Yandex (Yandex Self-Driving Group) stand out, which do not offer software as a product.

title: Digitalization of Specialist Modification Workshop Services Through a Customer Relationship Management Approach for Transparency in Vehicle Work Stages
abstract: Digitalization of specialist modification workshop services is needed to address scattered records and limited information regarding vehicle work stages. This study aims to build a web-based information system with a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) approach to integrate customer service and increase transparency of work progress. The study uses an applied research type with a descriptive approach and Prototype development method. Data were collected through observation, interviews, documentation, and literature studies, with owners or admins, mechanics, and customers as informants. The number of samples was not specifically stated. Analysis was carried out through business process identification, needs analysis, implementation of the Acquire, Enhance, and Retain stages, and Black Box Testing. The results show that the system integrates customer data, vehicles, orders, progress, documentation, consultations, complaints, and service history. Testing shows that the tested functions run according to the scenario. This system can support operational digitalization and transparency of workshop services

title: Dual Solar AC Charging System: A Review of Solar Photovoltaic Integration, Power Conversion and Electric Vehicle Charging Technology
abstract: The increasing demand for electric vehicles (EVs) and sustainable transportation has created a need for reliable, economical and environmentally friendly charging infrastructure. Solar photovoltaic (PV) energy provides a promising solution by utilizing renewable solar power for electric vehicle charging. This review paper presents an overview of a Dual Solar AC Charging System, in which two solar photovoltaic sources are integrated to provide electrical power for AC charging applications. The system can be designed with solar panels, solar charge controllers, maximum power point tracking (MPPT), power conditioning circuits, an inverter and suitable protection devices. The paper reviews existing solar-powered EV charging technologies, AC charging configurations, power electronic converters, energy management techniques and the challenges associated with solar energy utilization. It also discusses the possible integration of battery energy storage and grid backup to improve charging reliability during low solar irradiance and nighttime conditions. The dual-solar concept aims to improve solar energy utilization, reduce dependence on conventional grid electricity and support sustainable electric mobility

title: Effects of capacitive-resistive electric transfer therapy integrated with active rehabilitation on pain, sensorimotor function, and functional performance in subacute lateral ankle sprain: A randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Evidence on capacitive-resistive electric transfer (TECAR) applied concurrently with exercise in subacute lateral ankle sprain (LAS) is limited. Objective To evaluate the short-term effects of adding concurrent TECAR to exercise in subacute LAS. Methods Forty-two participants (20–40 years) with grade I-II LAS (10–21 days post-injury) were randomly allocated to exercise plus concurrent TECAR (EG; n = 21) or exercise alone (CG; n = 21). Both groups completed identical 20-min supervised sessions twice weekly for six weeks; TECAR did not extend session duration. Co-primary outcomes were pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale; NPRS) and Y-Balance Test (YBT) composite score ( α = 0.025). Secondary outcomes were joint position error (JPE) and Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM). Results All 42 randomized participants were analyzed; both groups improved on all outcomes ( p < 0.001). Versus exercise alone, TECAR was associated with greater improvements in pain (MD = 1.60, 95% CI 0.84–2.36, p < 0.001; below the 2-point minimal clinically important difference [MCID]), YBT composite (MD = 5.29%, 95% CI 1.44–9.14, p = 0.009), JPE (MD = 2.58°, 95% CI 2.03–3.13, p < 0.001), FAAM-ADL (MD = 10.39, 95% CI 7.72–13.06, p < 0.001), and FAAM-Sports (MD = 13.24, 95% CI 8.50–17.98, p < 0.001). Directional YBT differences did not survive multiplicity correction. Conclusion Adding TECAR was associ…

title: Almost-decoupling active control of in-wheel motors-driving 5DOF vehicle via complementary acceleration-difference feedback force control strategy
abstract: By incorporating the vertical–pitch dynamic coupling, the primary mechanism underlying motion sickness mitigating, we propose an almost-decoupling active control framework for a five-degree-of-freedom (5DOF) semi-vehicle powered by in-wheel motors (IWMs) grounded in frequency response analysis. A novel complementary acceleration-difference feedback (CAF) force control strategy is theoretically derived to suppress pitching angular acceleration and achieve almost-decoupling between vertical and pitch motions. The CAF force control law synthesizes suspension force from spatially differentiated vertical acceleration measurements acquired at the chassis–front and chassis–rear suspension interfaces. Root-mean-squared (RMS) values and frequency responses of key performance metrics, including vehicle-body acceleration, pitch angular acceleration, and related dynamic quantities are evaluated for the IWM-equipped 5-DOF semi-vehicle model subjected to stochastic road excitation conforming to ISO 8608 Class C. Results demonstrate that, across the speed range of 5–50 m/s, the proposed CAF force control strategy reduces the RMS pitch angular acceleration by up to 47.8% and attenuates its dominant frequency-domain peak amplitude by up to 41.1% at 20 m/s. The novelty of the proposed CAF force control strategy lies in its practical realizability and underlying almost-decoupling framework, not i…

title: Cation-Effect-Driven Modulation of Interfacial Solvation Structures Enables Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes. With benzyltriethylammonium serving as a model cationic regulator, we show that it accumulates near the polarized graphite surface and forms a cation layer that alters the local electric field. This cation-mediated interfacial regulation promotes PF6– accumulation at the interface, redirects early solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation toward anion-derived pathways, mitigates solvent decomposition, and accelerates Li+ desolvation and transport. As a result, graphite-based pouch cells deliver ∼88.2% state of charge within 6 min, maintain stable cycling for 2000 cycles with ∼71% capacity retention, and provide ∼218.2 Wh kg–1 with 10 min charging. Beyond LiPF6-based electrolytes, this cation effect also promotes reduction of the anions in other lithium-salt systems. This work bridges electrocatalytic cation effects and battery interfacial chemistry, offering a prac…

title: Data-centric Simulation Model for Electric Vehicle Charging Station Load Profiling and V2G Controls
abstract: The Electric Vehicle (EV) ecosystem significantly benefits from simulations that provide precise operational insights grounded in real-world data. This research proposes a data-centric simulation paradigm to generate 24-hour load profiles of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS). Specifically designed to serve as high-fidelity inputs for real-world simulators and digital twins, these profiles model charging execution, queuing delays, user responses to varying conditions, EVCS operational metrics, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) interactions. The paradigm utilizes an engineered real-world dataset derived from public charging operations within the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) grid regions. The framework integrates five interdependent stochastic modules: (i) an extended Non-Homogeneous Poisson Process (NHPP) utilizing cubic spline-interpolated thinning to model continuous diurnal arrival variations; (ii) a capacity-constrained M / G / c queuing system incorporating balking and reneging mechanisms to model user decisions better; (iii) an hourly method-of-moments bounded log-normal formulation preserving charging dynamics, time-sensitive variations, and skewness with greater fidelity than static fits; (iv) an empirical power rate formulation constrained by EVCS capacities for Grid to Vehicle (G2V) charging ; and (v) introducing scenario based V2G control models enfo…

title: Oficina educativa de primeiros socorros para estudantes: estratégia interprofissional nas escolas
abstract: Objetivo: descrever o processo de desenvolvimento de uma Tecnologia Educativa (TE) do tipo oficina de aprendizagem em Primeiros Socorros (PS) para estudantes no contexto escolar. Método: estudo metodológico, composto das seguintes etapas: revisão da literatura, diagnóstico situacional e desenvolvimento da TE, abrangendo a universidade, escola pública de Ensino Fundamental e o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU). Resultados: a TE constituiu-se em uma oficina composta por quatro matrizes: programática, conceitual, metodológica e operativa, as quais estruturaram a abordagem aos temas apontados pela pesquisa: PS e acionamento do SAMU; parada cardiorrespiratória; quedas, queimaduras e engasgo. A TE desenvolveu um modelo de competências baseado em conhecimento, habilidades e atitudes visando que os estudantes reconheçam as principais situações de urgência/emergência, executem ações básicas de PS e acionem a equipe especializada para a realização de manobras básicas de atendimento. Conclusão: o processo colaborativo, interprofissional e interinstitucional entre os sistemas de saúde e educação envolveu técnicos, docentes e acadêmicos na proposição de práticas de educação em saúde sobre um tema complexo, como os PS, com potencial impacto para sua replicação na rede escolar, por meio da implementação da TE.

title: Multiplex Determination of Pathogens via a Dual-Mode Microfluidic Platform Integrated with a Universal Sensing Strategy
abstract: Abstract Multiplex determination of pathogens is crucial for precise medical treatment of infectious diseases. To address this challenge, here we propose a CRISPR/Cas-assisted microfluidic multiplex sensing platform (CAMMSP) based on a nucleic acid amplification-free, universal, and modular sensing strategy. This strategy leverages the synergistic action of Cas12a and nanoporous materials to construct a target-responsive indicator release/enrichment system and achieve cascade signal amplification without nucleic acid amplification. By virtue of the programmability of the CRISPR system, this strategy is readily extended to different targets by replacing crRNA only. With the aid of a spatially divisional microfluidic platform, four common reproductive tract pathogens were synchronously detected as a proof-of-concept. The signal property of the methylene blue indicator was utilized to achieve electrochemical and optical signal cross-validation, guaranteeing the detection reliability at the readout level and offering flexible options for different scenarios. The developed CAMMSP exhibits broad linear ranges across 6 orders of magnitude and sub-femtomolar detection limits, with outstanding specificity in complex samples. Clinical sample analysis further validates its potential for practical applications, establishing a promising laboratory proof-of-concept and reliable technical fou…

title: Teachers’ Perception of Learning Action Cell (LAC) as a Strategy for Continuous Professional Development in Elementary Schools
abstract: This study examined teachers’ perceptions of the LAC as a strategy for continuous professional development in elementary schools during the 2025–2026 school year to inform a professional training plan. A descriptive survey research design was employed to describe teachers’ perceptions of LAC implementation before, during, and after sessions, their level across variables, and the challenges encountered. Using total enumeration, all teachers from selected elementary schools in Dumanjug District II participated, and data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and standard deviation based on an instrument adapted from the DepEd LAC Policy. Findings revealed that teachers perceived LAC implementation across three phases as fully implemented. In terms of specific areas, LAC was fully implemented in learner diversity and student inclusion, content and pedagogy, and assessment and reporting, but only implemented in 21st-century skills and ICT integration, as well as curriculum contextualization, localization, and indigenization. Challenges were generally slightly serious, with time constraints due to heavy workload identified as the most critical concern affecting participation. It is concluded that teachers have a positive perception of LAC as an effective professional development strategy that strengthens instructional practices, although improvements are needed in…

title: AYURVEDA AS A COMPLEMENTARY STRATEGY AGAINST ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF EVIDENCE, MECHANISMS INSIGHTS, AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
abstract: Introduction: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) a growing worldwide concern for health, requires an alternative and mechanistically heterogeneous treatment approaches. Ayurveda with its broad spectrum of therapeutic herbs and phytoconstituents, is a potent alternative to antibacterial and resistance-modulating treatments. Methodology: Research and review articles published from 2015 to 2026 were selected through PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Using Rayyan, 90 records screened of which, 13 duplicates were removed and 13 Articles were excluded and 64 articles were included in the qualitative synthesis. Results and Discussion: As per the reviewed evidence Ayurvedic plant phytoconstituents demonstrate an antibacterial, antibiofilm, antivirulence, resistance-modulating, and antibiotic-adjuvant effects against clinically relevant resistant pathogens. Several substances such as thymol, carvacrol, cinnamaldehyde, piperine, and quercetin, may increase the therapeutic value of conventional antibiotics by using complimentary processes. However, formulation variability, poor standardization, mechanistic gaps, a lack of pharmacokinetic and safety evidence, possible drug-herb interactions, and regulatory heterogeneity contribute as a barrier to clinical translation of ayurvedic formulation. Conclusion: Rather than taking the place of traditional antibiotic medication, Ayurv…

title: Práticas Integrativas e Complementares em Saúde como estratégia de promoção do bem-estar e autonomia dos idosos
abstract: As Práticas Integrativas e Complementares em Saúde (PICS) são ofertadas no Sistema Único de Saúde a uma população que envelhece, mas a evidência sobre bem-estar e autonomia da pessoa idosa está dispersa. Esta revisão integrativa, com dados públicos e abertos, sintetizou estudos de 2021 a 2026 sobre PICS em idosos. Seguiu o PRISMA 2020, com questão PICO, lista do Joanna Briggs Institute e níveis de evidência de Melnyk e Fineout-Overholt. As buscas de 31 de outubro de 2026, em motor de busca acadêmico e páginas de periódicos, retornaram 83 registros, e 18 estudos foram incluídos (seis de nível I, cinco de V, seis de VI e um de VII). Emergiram três categorias: práticas corpo-mente e exercício terapêutico (n = 7); música, dança e aromaterapia (n = 7); e políticas, serviços e visões panorâmicas (n = 4). Metanálises indicam benefício de Tai Chi, Qigong, ioga e musicoterapia sobre depressão, ansiedade, sono e função física, com certeza baixa a muito baixa e alta heterogeneidade; estudos brasileiros qualitativos apontam pertencimento e prazer, e um estudo com Lian Gong não mostrou efeito sobre o medo de quedas. Nenhum estudo avaliou a autonomia com instrumento específico, e o relatório nacional de monitoramento não apresenta dados por faixa etária. Propõe-se o modelo AURORA-PICS, teórico e não validado, e uma agenda de pesquisa. As bases indexadas não foram consultadas.

title: A General Strategy to Control Lifetime-Resolved Polarity Quantification of Push−Pull Fluorophores
abstract: Abstract Cellular polarity is important for physiological and biological conditions. Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) provides a quantitative approach for resolving microenvironmental polarity in living cells, and a variety of fluorophores have been developed for lifetime-based sensing. However, achieving tunable and quantitative polarity responses in fluorescence lifetime remains challenging, particularly when the range of polarity changes is wide. Herein, we establish a molecular design strategy that enables push−pull fluorophores to exhibit a linear response of their lifetime to environmental polarity in a wide range of polarity variations (dielectric constants from 5.30 to 32.70 or to 70.85). Theoretical calculations demonstrated that the tetrahydroquinoxaline−piperidine (THQP) unit exhibited an appropriate twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) tendency, enabling effective modulation of the excited-state dynamics associated with environmental polarity. This strategy provides broad applicability across multiple push−pull fluorophores including coumarins, difluoride-boron complexes, rhodols, and boranil-derived fluorophores. Notably, THQP−coumarin probes enable quantitative mapping of polarity variations in proteins and subcellular compartments both in vitro and in living cells via FLIM. Owing to their high brightness and photostability, these probes fu…

title: Research on the Financing Status, Dilemmas, and Optimization Paths of Low-Altitude Economy Enterprises under the Digital Economy
abstract: As a vital carrier of new quality productive forces and a nationally strategic emerging industry, the low-altitude economy is entering a critical window of scale-up development; however, its financial supply system significantly lags behind the pace of industrial expansion. Against the backdrop of deep integration between the digital economy and the low-altitude economy, this paper adopts a mixed-methods approach combining literature review, policy text analysis, and semi-structured interviews to systematically examine the financing status of low-altitude economy enterprises, analyze their dilemmas and underlying causes, and propose optimization paths. The study finds that the financing of low-altitude economy enterprises exhibits a structural feature of “debt-financing dominance, insufficient direct financing, and high policy dependence.” The mismatch between asset-light structures and collateral logic, the absence of rights confirmation, valuation, and disposal mechanisms for data assets, and the dual uncertainty of policy and technology jointly constitute the core causes of financing constraints, while the financing pain points of the three enterprise types—R&D-oriented, operation-oriented, and infrastructure-oriented—show significant heterogeneity. title: Germinate-to-Exterminate: Precrop Stimulation of Verticillium dahliae Microsclerotia Germination by Root Exudates as a Novel Strategy for Sustainable Control of Verticillium Wilt
abstract: Verticillium wilt (VW) is an important soilborne disease caused by Verticillium species. VW has been reported in nearly 400 plant species from various families, including but not limited to Solanaceae, Brassicaceae, Cucurbitaceae, Fabaceae, Rosaceae, Caprifoliaceae, Malvaceae, Lamiaceae, and Sapindaceae. Potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.), belonging to the Solanaceae family, is one of the most important staple crops globally and can be greatly impacted by VW, resulting in more than 40% yield losses in heavily infested commercial fields. VW in potatoes can be caused by infections with Verticillium dahliae (the most damaging species), V . albo-atrum , V . tricorpus , and others. V. dahliae produces microsclerotia (MS), resting structures that can persist in the soil for more than 10 years, even without a host crop, making effective field management challenging. Additionally, the incidence and severity of VW can be increased when root-lesion nematodes and V. dahliae coinfect potato crops. Root exudate metabolites facilitate plant-microbial communication, which is also essential for the pathosystems adaptation to environmental change. These can also provide important signals to plant pathogens; for example, to facilitate stimulation of V. dahliae MS germination. title: Ukraine’s digital heritage diplomacy in China and Indonesia: Soft power visions in comparative perspective
abstract: This article addresses gaps in scholarship on Ukraine’s digital cultural diplomacy in Asia by examining how Ukraine’s Embassies communicate its national identity and heritage in China and Indonesia, major actors in the region and the world. The study asks how the Embassies of Ukraine in China and Indonesia communicate Ukraine’s national identity and cultural heritage through digital diplomacy, and how these communications align with or diverge from the soft power visions of their host countries. The analysis draws on data collected from the Embassies’ digital platform between January and May 2025, encompassing Ukraine’s Cultural Diplomacy Month. Focusing on Ukraine’s digital diplomacy towards China, the findings show that almost half of the Embassy’s heritage communication simultaneously documents Russia’s actions against that heritage, challenging depoliticised local media framing. Focusing on Ukraine’s digital diplomacy towards China, the findings show a strategic communication priority assigned to the narratives of Ukraine’s heritage destruction by Russia, challenging depoliticised local media framing. Bilateral cultural positioning is largely absent, while strong Weibo engagement reflects visibility within, but not influence over, a highly controlled information environment. In the case of Ukraine’s digital diplomacy with Indonesia, by contrast, the Embassy of Ukraine focus…

title: A Firefly‐Inspired Biomimetic Multispectral Cascade Framework for Transient Thermal Mitigation and Tissue Protection in High‐Power Laser Surgeries
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐power laser systems remain indispensable in modern clinical surgeries owing to their superior cutting precision and structural blood occlusion capabilities. However, collateral thermal damage manifesting as rapid localized carbonization, tissue scarring, and secondary peripheral cell death remains a major complication due to unmitigated macroscale heat accumulation. Traditional mechanical methods, such as air‐flow cooling or liquid cryogen sprays, suffer from structural latency and block critical intraoperative visualization fields. To resolve this photothermal bottleneck, this study introduces a novel theoretical framework: an active, firefly‐inspired biomimetic coaxial optical buffering shielding engine designed for transient millisecond‐scale spatial–temporal thermal mitigation. By engineering a hardware‐native cascaded energy transport model, localized high‐energy thermal photons generated during target tissue cutting are captured by a peripheral spectral absorption layer. This system dynamically shifts the localized photon energy across a multispectral cascade grid, mimicking the cascading energy transfer topologies observed in bioluminescent mechanisms to dissipate structural thermal waste as nondestructive, minimized‐thermal luminescent output. Multiphysics numerical co‐simulations demonstrate that this biomimetic cascading network restricts peripheral tiss…

The Power of Collective Efficacy: Sources, Interventions, and Outcomes for Diverse Students
abstract: Although self-efficacy theory has emphasized individuals’ beliefs in their capabilities, collective efficacy may operate through similar processes. Understanding these mechanisms may be particularly important for promoting equitable pathways into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) careers among students from underrepresented groups. Using a deductive qualitative analysis approach, this study examined how the four sources of self-efficacy (i.e., performance accomplishments, vicarious experiences, social persuasion, and physiological and emotional states) contribute to the development of collective efficacy during collaborative STEM learning. Focus groups with diverse eighth-grade students and semistructured interviews with their teachers explored students’ experiences working collaboratively on a multimedia STEM project. Findings indicated that all four sources of self-efficacy contributed to students’ shared belief in their groups’ ability to accomplish collective goals. Furthermore, proximal contextual supports, including peer collaboration and teacher support through problem-solving, modeling, and tolerance for mistakes, helped students navigate barriers, facilitating persistence toward shared goals and skill development. Findings extend the application of self-efficacy theory and social cognitive career theory by highlighting collective efficacy as a po…

title: Retail Sales Promotion and Consumer Conversion of Wellness-Oriented Food Products: An Exploratory Field Study of Nutrica at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi
abstract: Purpose: This study examines how point-of-sale promotion and need-based personal selling are used to engage shoppers and support purchase conversion for Nutrica wellness-oriented food products at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi. It focuses on the practical selling process, customer questions and objections, and the role of product knowledge in retail interactions. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts an exploratory, descriptive single-site case-study design based on a two-month sales internship conducted from 1 June to 31 July 2026. Evidence comprises the trainee’s field observations, customer-facing selling activities, an internship activity diary and a summary of outlet-level records supplied in the source report. No structured questionnaire, probability sample or controlled experiment was reported. Findings: The field account indicates that concise, customer-centred communication, active listening, product familiarity and responses tailored to specific objections were central to the selling process. The source report records 247 customer interactions and 192 conversions. If these counts use consistent definitions and refer to the same observation period, the implied descriptive conversion ratio is 77.7%; this should be treated as provisional because the underlying transaction-level records and operational definitions were not included. The report also lists 1,014 L as units sold…

title: O SILÊNCIO COMO ESTRATÉGIA NARRATIVA EM VARANDAS DA EVA DE MILTON HATOUM: LACUNAS, AMBIGUIDADES E A IMAGINAÇÃO DO LEITOR
abstract: Este estudo acadêmico se dedica à narrativa curta Varandas da Eva (2009), escrita por Milton Hatoum, com objetivo de dar atenção especial ao uso do silêncio e das omissões narrativas como estratégias estéticas indispensáveis. Entende-se que Hatoum, uma figura do cânone da literatura brasileira contemporânea, utiliza o não dito para gerar tensão, aumentar a profundidade psicológica dos personagens e envolver ativamente o leitor no processo interpretativo de construção de significado. A pesquisa analisa o silêncio corporal de figuras como Tarso e da Mulher Anônima, assim como as elipses temporais e as ambiguidades que marcam a narrativa. A partir das teorias formuladas por pesquisadores como Hans Robert Jauss e Wolfgang Iser, a crítica visa esclarecer de que modo as indefinições textuais incitam o leitor a interagir imaginativamente com os vácuos, colocando-os, portanto, como coautores da obra literária. A metodologia é adotada de uma abordagem bibliográfica qualitativa e parte dos pressupostos teóricos dos autores citados. A conclusão é que, o silêncio, em Varandas da Eva, vai além da simples ausência; ao contrário, ele se manifesta como uma presença potente que aprimora a experiência estética e a natureza polissêmica do texto.

Engineering Acid Adaptability of Zearalenone Lactonase Guided by an Integrated Structural and Computational Strategy
abstract: Abstract Zearalenone (ZEN) lactonases are promising biocatalysts for detoxifying ZEN-contaminated food and feed. However, their poor activity and stability under acidic conditions limit practical applications. Here, we establish an integrated computationally/structurally guided hydrophobic microenvironment engineering as a paradigm for improving the acid adaptability of ZEN lactonases. Constant pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) simulations revealed that acidic conditions suppress proton abstraction by altering catalytic-residue protonation and destabilizing key structural regions. Structure-guided engineering introduced Pro and Phe residues to stabilize acid-sensitive regions, while hydrophobic microenvironment engineering promoted substrate repositioning and the formation of near-attack conformations. The engineered M4 mutant exhibited a 111.7-fold enhancement in acid stability. Validation with 5Z-7-oxozeaenol supported a hydrophobic gating mechanism, in which the hydrophobic microenvironment governs substrate positioning, aligns catalytic residues, and stabilizes reactive conformations. M4 degraded approximately 70% of ZEN under simulated gastrointestinal pH conditions, demonstrating its potential for ZEN detoxification.

title: Anxiety Experience and Coping Strategies of Students Facing Test-Based University Entrance Exams: A Phenomenological Study
abstract: Anxiety when facing university entrance selection remains a persistent issue in Indonesia, even as the selection scheme has changed name from SBMPTN to UTBK-SNBT and undergone several structural revisions. Most existing studies rely on quantitative-correlational designs and tend to focus on prospective test-takers, leaving the lived experience of those who have already passed through the process underexplored. This study aimed to understand university students' experiences of anxiety when facing test-based university entrance exams and the coping strategies they used to manage it. A qualitative phenomenological design was employed, with data analyzed using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis. Five informants who had previously taken the exam were selected through purposive sampling and interviewed using a semi-structured, in-depth approach. Findings revealed that anxiety stemmed primarily from fear of failure linked to the absence of alternative plans, alongside negative self-evaluation of preparedness, further shaped by contextual factors such as access to learning facilities. To manage this anxiety, informants combined problem-focused strategies, such as additional study efforts, with emotion-focused and social strategies, such as cognitive reframing and peer support. These findings enrich phenomenological understanding of entrance-exam anxiety and remain relevant for cu…

abstract: Objective: Mapping learning preferences at entry into the MBBS course may help faculty design teaching sessions that are more responsive to learner diversity.The present study aims to evaluate the VARK learning preferences among first-year MBBS students. Methods: This cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among 235 first-year MBBS students The VARK questionnaire version 8.02 was administered using an online Google Form. The data was analysed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square/Fisher’s exact test, Mann–Whitney U test, Friedman test and Spearman’s correlation. Results: Of the 238 students recorded, 164 (68.9%) were females and 74 (31.1%) were males. The mean age was 19.30±1.41 years. Complete VARK data were available for 235 students. Multimodal learning was predominant [157/235 (66.8%)], with bimodal learning being the single most frequent mode [85/235 (36.2%)]. The distribution of learning modes did not differ significantly by gender (p=0.983).
